67339.title: Maamar Basi LeGani - I Have Come to My Garden
67339.description: A chassidic discourse based on the Previous Rebbe’s discourse of the same title.
path: Maamar Basi LeGani - I Have Come to My Garden

67342.title: “Niggun Simcha”
67342.description: A joyous Chabad song. The Rebbe encourages the singing, while motioning to some to say L’chaim.

67349.title: On the Money
67349.description: U.S. currency states, “In G-d we trust.” Trust is much higher than belief.

68008.title: Rabbi Paldi
68008.description: The Rebbe Introduces Rabbi Chaim Yehuda Paldi from “The Committee for a Complete Nation,” who speaks for a few minutes.

68009.title: The Correct JudgmentJudge Joseph Fisch
68009.description: A good judge is one who can cause the prevention of crime.

68013.title: Torah Study
68013.description: The importance of Torah study on a daily basis – even for the layman.

68016.title: Farbrengen
68016.description: A vintage color-film of a Farbrengen. The Rebbe encourages the singing, and motions to some to say L’chaim. After the Maamar, the Rebbe takes a tractate in Chalukat Hashas. At the conclusion, the Rebbe stands up and vigorously encourages the Niggun.

68020.title: A Toast to the Holy Land
68020.description: The Rebbe sends Mashke to Jerusalem, Kfar-Chabad, and Nachlat-Har-Chabad. A special bottle is sent to the Georgian immigrants living in Nachlat-Har-Chabad.
path: A Toast to the Holy Land

68024.title: The Belzer Rov visits the Rebbe
68024.description: The Belzer Rov, Rabbi Yisochor Dov Halevi Rokeach, visits the Rebbe in his office. After conversing for approximately an hour, the Rebbe escorts him to the door.
path: The Belzer Rov visits the Rebbe

72751.title: Continuing Inspiration
72751.description: After visiting Germany on Shlichus, it is necessary to continue the connection by sending holiday greetings and provisions.

72754.title: Purim in the Rebbe’s Home
72754.description: The Rebbe leads the Morning Prayers on Purim, including ‘V’al Hanisim,’ the special Purim prayer, receives an Aliya, and listens in to the Megilla reading.

72755.title: Federation of Central N.J.
72755.description: It is not necessary to fear when going on a trip to Israel, it is a safe place. When going, one should publicize the trip.

72758.title: Machne Israel Development Fund
72758.description: After meeting with the members of the Machne Israel Development Fund, the Rebbe leaves the Shul. The Rebbe asks for the partitions to be moved so he can see the Ark. On the way to his room he addresses the Shluchim.

72759.title: Medical Advice
72759.description: It is advisable to go through with a medical procedure as long as the doctor is a competent and professional in especially this field. When doing so, the sooner the better.

75180.title: A Blessing for Life
75180.description: A blessing for life until one hundred and twenty.

75183.title: Birthday Present – Vladimir & Gregory Dashevsky
75183.description: At the Rebbe’s 75th birthday Farbrengen, 2 Russian artists present the Rebbe with a painting of himself. The Rebbe thanks them and blesses them to follow “in the spirit of the picture.”

75188.title: Standing Strong!
75188.description: Happy Pesach to all of Israel, and a message to Mr. Arik Sharon to remain strong in his beliefs, and not to be swayed.

75189.title: V’hee She’amda
75189.description: From the Hagaddah, this Nigun emphasizes the perseverance of the Jewish people throughout the ages, with G-d’s help.

75190.title: “I” – But Only For G-d
75190.description: Ethics of our fathers: “If I am not for myself, who is for me?” A person must know that G-d created each person as an entity unto himself, however this must be used to serve G-d.

75191.title: Prayer
75191.description: The Rebbe takes part in the morning prayers on Purim.

75192.title: Build Now!
75192.description: Do not wait for all the money to erect a Shul. As soon as you have enough money to begin, do so!

75193.title: Ki Bsimcha Teitzeiu
75193.description: “You shall go out in Joy,” a lively Chasidic Nigun, which was sung at the conclusion of the Rebbe’s Farbrengens.

76494.title: End of Parade
76494.description: At the conclusion of the Parade, the singing turns into dancing, the Rebbe encourages the dancing, and encourages the onlookers to join.

76495.title: A Mission in U.S.
76495.description: The Rebbe does not want to leave America, since there are many Jews living there, and many moving there from Russia.

76504.title: Nigun “Al Achas”
76504.description:
“...How much more so should we be grateful to the Omnipresent One for the doubled and
redoubled goodness that He has bestowed upon us...” (From the Passover Haggadah)

76512.title: Ki Elokim
76512.description: As the children sing at the Pesach rally, the Rebbe vigorously encourages them.

80025.title: Chasidic Discourse
80025.description: On the eve of Shavuot, the Rebbe recites a Chasidic discourse on the Ten Commandments.

80027.title: V'samachta
80027.description: "And you shall rejoice with your Festivals," A lively Holiday classic.

80030.title: “God’s Messengers”
80030.description: The Rebbe's Shluchim receive their strength from G-d Almighty, and it is transmitted through the Rebbe.

80033.title: Early Morning Chat
80033.description: The Rebbe converses with photographer Levi Freidin outside the Rebbe’s house on President Street.

82200.title: Visiting the Ohel
82200.description: The Rebbe visits the Ohel, resting place of his father-in-law and predecessor Rabbi Yosef Yitzchok of Lubavitch, in the Sir Moses Montifiore Cemetery in Queens, New York.

84131.title: Young Role Models
84131.description: A child going to camp, and saying Modeh Ani, can be a role model for the other children in his/her city.

84138.title: A Good Year
84138.description: The Rebbe finishes an address to children returning from summer camp, and directs them to declare “Ketiva V’chatima Tova” for all Jewish people.

84140.title: Nigun Simcha
84140.description: A very lively Chabad classic, being sung during the distribution of Kos Shel Brachah. The Rebbe puts down his cup and vigorously encourages the Niggun.

84143.title: Naming the Baby
84143.description: Naming a baby is done exclusively by the parents. Blessings and L’chaim to the Brit - ritual circumcision.

87269.title: Tefillin in Prison
87269.description: United States law allows an inmate to put on Tefillin.

87272.title: Kesiva VaChatima Tova
87272.description: The importance of wishing one another a good upcoming year. While distributing dollars for charity, the Rebbe wishes each person to be inscribed and sealed for a good year.

87276.title: Erev Rosh Hashanah
87276.description: A Farbrengen on the eve of Rosh Hashanah. At the conclusion the Rebbe says, “we shall leave this year with all of its sorrows,” and starts “Ki Bsimcha.”

87277.title: Never be Satisfied
87277.description: One should never be satisfied with previous accomplishments, and must continuously increase.

87281.title: Jewish Livelihood
87281.description: An increase in Torah Study and giving Tzedaka will increase Parnassa, livelihood.

91139.title: Machneh Israel
91139.description: The Rebbe meets members of the Machne Israel Development Fund, and briefly addresses the Shluchim, between Rosh Hashanah and Yom Kippur.

91140.title: New Year's Blessings
91140.description: Blessings for a good year in all aspects, physical and spiritual.

91141.title: Avinu Malkeinu
91141.description: The Rebbe leads the morning prayers on the Yartzeit of his mother, Rebbetzin Chana. Avinu Malkeinu is sung with the tune that is attributed to the Alter Rebbe.

91145.title: Nigun Simcha
91145.description: A lively Niggun, to which the words “Ketiva Vachatima Tova” were later added. During the singing, the Rebbe motions to the photographers to say L’chaim.

91151.title: “Yaakov Went On His Way”
91151.description: At the conclusion of “Kos Shel Brachah,” the Rebbe announces, “as we each embark on our individual ways, may it be with joy and peace.”

91153.title: Hallelu Es Hashem
91153.description: A part of the Hallel prayer, “may all the nations praise G-d,” during a Farbrengen, this Niggun is strongly encouraged by the Rebbe.

91156.title: Studying Rambam
91156.description: The Rebbe is presented with a Kapach edition of the Rambam. The Rebbe thanks the compilers, and requests to receive the future volumes as well. As for a recommendation-letter, use the one that was sent for the first volume.

91157.title: “Fourteen are the books of the Rambam”
91157.description: The Rebbe vigorously encourages the Russian version of “Who Knows One?” especially the reference to the fourteen books of the Rambam.
path: “Fourteen are the books of the Rambam”

96297.title: Seeing off the Guests
96297.description: The Rebbe stands on the steps of 770 to see off the Tishrei guests.

96301.title: Shacharit
96301.description: The Rebbe prays the Morning Prayers. When the Chazan says “Birkat Kohanim” the Rebbe gazes at the Chazan.

96303.title: Kemofet Hayiti
96303.description: This lively Niggun was one of several composed in honor of the Rebbe’s seventieth birthday.

96306.title: Lubavitcher
96306.description: Lubavitch work belongs to all, knowingly or not, and everyone can participate.

96314.title: IDF – Physically and Spiritually Strong
96314.description: Physical strength is not sufficient for the safety of Eretz Yisrael, there must be spiritual strength, as well.

96319.title: Samach Tesamach
96319.description: During the distribution of Kos Shel Brachah, the Rebbe encourages the singing of “rejoice beloved friends…” a verse from the Seven Marriage Blessings.

96325.title: The Chanukah Campaign
96325.description: Following Mincha, the Lighting of the Menorah, and Maariv, the Rebbe turns to the waiting audience, directing them to spread the Chanukah miracle.

96331.title: Haneiros Hallalu
96331.description: A rare clip of “Haneirot Hallalu,” the text said after lighting of the Menorah, being sung at a Farbrengen.

96337.title: Morning Prayers
96337.description: The Rebbe participates in the morning prayers on a Fast Day. The Rebbe is called to the Torah.

96338.title: Who Owns Your Name?
96338.description: If he wants, he can combine his given name and his used name.* Before private audiences are featured, permission is obtained.

96341.title: Distributing Charity
96341.description: On the way out of 770, the Rebbe sits down in the car and distributes nickels to the children to give to charity.

96342.title: Rambam Nachas
96342.description:
20 Teves is the Rambam’s Yahrtzeit.
Rabbi Hurwitz presents the Rebbe with his most recent work on the Rambam. The Rebbe encourages him to continue, and blesses him with “Rambam Nachas.”

105082.title: Mincha
105082.description: The Rebbe takes part in the Mincha Services. As he enters, the Rebbe distributes Tzedaka to children.

105084.title: A Lively Niggun
105084.description: A vintage clip of this lively Niggun, as the Rebbe claps his hands to encourage the singing.

105086.title: Farbrengen
105086.description: A vintage film of a Yud-Tes Kislev Farbrengen. The crowd sings a heartfelt Chassidic melody; the Rebbe says a Maamar; the Rebbe encourages the lively singing.Before the end of the Farbrengen, the Rebbe selects his tractate of the communal Talmud study.

105092.title: Nyet Nyet Nikavo
105092.description: The Rebbe begins this Russian Niggun, “There is none other than You.”

111019.title: Keren Chomesh
111019.description: The Rebbe founded a fund to help institutions that are named after the Rebbetzin. During the distribution of “Dollars”, the Rebbe announces that requests for funding should be made to the fund, and that these institutions must be legitimate, with a confirmation from the local rabbinate or the Rebbe’s secretariat.

111023.title: Tzedaka to Children
111023.description: On his way to hear the Torah reading, the Rebbe distributes coins to children for them to give to charity.

111024.title: Just Choose Peace
111024.description: It is imperative to remain strong, and not to give in to pressures, when it comes to the security of Israel.

111027.title: Selichot Prayers
111027.description: The Rebbe leads special “fast day” prayers for Taanit Esther in his home several weeks after the passing of his wife, the Rebbetzin ob”m.

130762.title: Every Minute Counts
130762.description: The Rebbe encourages someone who finished his pre-conversion learning and preparation to quickly move on to the actual conversion.

130765.title: Boy's Choir at Kos Shel Brachah
path: Boy's Choir at Kos Shel Brachah

142979.title: "Just as His Children Are Alive, So Too, He is Alive"
142979.description: If you observe the conduct of his children, his students, and you find that "his children are alive," his influence still vital with an infectious vitality, then "he too, is alive."
path: "Just as His Children Are Alive, So Too, He is Alive"

142980.title: I'll Mention It At The Ohel
142980.description: The Rebbe responds to individuals who wrote requesting blessings that he reads the letters at the Ohel of his father-in-law and predecessor, the Previous Lubavitcher Rebbe.
path: I'll Mention It At The Ohel

160591.title: You must increase, not only continue
path: You must increase, not only continue

160597.title: Living the Torah
160597.description:
Our Sages teach us that we should view the Torah as being new every day, not
merely renewed. How do we resolve this statement with the reality that lies
before our eyes, a world that appears to be the same on awakening as it was
yesterday?

160598.title: Havdalah
160598.description:
Following a Farbrengen which began on the Festival, the Rebbe reads from a
prayerbook, reciting Havdalah, which concludes the Festival. The cup of wine is
filled and refilled until the wee hours of the morning. The wine is distributed to
young and old of all backgrounds.

160599.title: A Truly Big Blessing
160599.description:
Is Kaddish being recited for the grandmother? A blessing to have only good news.
Blessings to the Rebbe apply to all those around him as well. G-d can live up to
the challenge of filling even such a big blessing.

160600.title: Tzomo Lecho Nafshi
160600.description: Song lyrics: “My soul thirsts for You, my flesh longs for you; (as one) in a desolate and dry land without water, so (I thirst) to see You in the Sanctuary, to behold your might and glory.” This song was first taught by the Rebbe on 28 Nissan, 5714 – 1954.

160601.title: Making Ink From Grass!
160601.description: After the passing of his mother, Rebbetzin Chana Schneerson, in 1964, the Rebbe began holding a farbrengen, chassidic gathering and public address, on the date of her yahrzeit. This gathering would be dedicated to her legacy, and to the mission of the Jewish woman.

160602.title: Main Synagogue
160602.description: The Esrog lies on the prayer stand as the Rebbe is called to the Torah, looks on as the Torah is raised and touches it affectionately on its departure. Musaf for the Holiday is then recited.

160603.title: A Heavenly Case
160603.description: Blessings for success in the practice of law. Every Jew has to prepare their case at this time to be presented before the Heavenly Court on Rosh Hashanah.

160604.title: V’somachta - Children’s Rally
160604.description: Children sing the song v’samachta. English translation “And you shall rejoice in your Festival… and you will be only happy.” (Deuteronomy 16:14, 15)

160606.title: Main Synagogue
160606.description: The congregation circles while reciting the Hosha’anos on Hoshanah Rabah. The Hosha’anos are recited while holding the Lulav and Esrog to the heart. The Rebbe counts out the five willows, then strikes them on the ground.

160607.title: A New Year Blessing
160607.description: Lekach for the birth of a baby. To bring Moshiach, check your Tefilin and Mezuzos. Spread Yiddishkeit by showing an example and through pleasant words.

160608.title: Nye Zhuritzi Chloptzi
160608.description:
This melody was often sung by the Chassidim of the Mitteler Rebbe as they traveled to Lubavitch to visit him. The words allude to their hopeful yearnings. When they reach Lubavitch, they will drink from “the well of Torah and Chassidism,” and will lack nothing.
The Rebbe taught this song during the Festival of Simchas Torah 1956.

160609.title: Maimonides’ Universal Acceptance
160609.description:
1985 marked the first Siyum Harambam, closure of the yearly cycle of studying the Mishne Torah, the magnum opus of Maimonides. This project was initiated by the Rebbe to unite all Jews in study, and for the benefit of studying the entire body of Jewish law, as compiled by Maimonides.
The universal acceptance of Maimonides is evidenced by his headstone, which is engraved with the words “From (the first) Moses to Moses (Maimonides) there arose none like Moses.” Through the time of the Judges, the Prophets, the Kings and the Sages, the Mishnah and the Talmud, and all of the subsequent Jewish sages, no one could compare to Moses – until Maimonides!

160610.title: The Rebbe’s Sukkah
160610.description: Distribution of Lekach, honeycake, with wishes for a sweet New Year. This is an age-old tradition on Hosha’ana Rabah. The Rebbe hands Lekach to men, women and children of all walks of life.

160611.title: Winning Over the Opposition
160611.description: Thanks to the children who danced and sang. Money for charity in Israel and participation in the efforts to spread Yiddishkeit. The wife should help the husband and vice versa. Do not be afraid of opposition, for it brings out greater effort. Redemption will come in merit of righteous women.

160612.title: Sheyibone
160612.description:
“May the Temple be rebuilt speedily in our days, and give us our portion of your Torah.”
This song was first taught by the Rebbe on 28 Nissan, 5714 – 1954.

212426.title: A Month that Lasts a Year
212426.description: The following talk, as others in its genre, was meant as encouragement for the underground Russian Jewish movement. Some of these talks or their translation into Russian would be broadcast on Radio Free Europe, reaching the oppressed peoples of the Soviet Republics.
path: A Month that Lasts a Year

212427.title: Farbrengen’s End
212427.description: At the conclusion of the Farbrengen, the Rebbe nods, says L’chaim and encourages as the crowd sings. Dollars are distributed to the “Mitzvah Tankists”. After a reminder to say the After-Blessing and a few final words, the Rebbe leaves the Synagogue.

212428.title: Business and Owner
212428.description: The owner should live in the same city as the business. Miami has proper Jewish necessities: education, Kosher food, etc. Moving is best done in the summer.

212429.title: Niggun Yosisu
212429.description: “Let all those seek You rejoice and delight in You, and let those who love your deliverance say always, ‘May G-d be exalted!’” (Psalms 70:5) Although the tune of the Niggun is much older, the words were added in honor of the Rebbe’s sixty-ninth birthday.

213518.title: A Nation Under G-d – Farbrengen
213518.description: One of the Patriarch Avraham’s great first deeds was not only the promotion of monotheism, but the credo that G-d is “Master of the World.” G-d is the Master of the World in the occupational sense; this is what he does constantly. He fills the entire world with His presence and guidance.

213519.title: Children’s Rally – Main Synagogue
213519.description: The Rebbe enters the synagogue, touches the Ark and gives charity before ascending the podium and prays Minchah with the children. After the children say the Torah passages, they are addressed by the Rebbe.

213520.title: Surgery
213520.description: On three different occasions, the Rebbe recommends placing a charity box in the hospital room and gives blessings for surgeries. G-d is in the hospital room as well.

213521.title: Didan Notzach
213521.description: The words Didan Notzach (We will be victorious!) had been added to this older tune to express the hope that the Rebbe and Chassidim would win the court case to keep the books of the Previous Rebbe in the hands of the Lubavitch Movement. A month prior, on 5 Teves, Lubavitch won the case.

214337.title: Children of Avraham
214337.description: Judaism demands ethics of all ages; children as well as adults. The demands are much greater than the not cheating or lying; we must refrain from even approaching a seller to underbid or somehow get an item that another child or person wants. It would be frustrating and spiteful if it were done to us, therefore we should not do it to another.

214338.title: Chanukah Gelt
214338.description: The Rebbe distributes Chanukah Gelt to men and women on Chanukah.

214339.title: Debt Reduction
214339.description: Increasing the enrollment in a school is the best source for additional donations.

214340.title: Al Tirah
214340.description: “Do not fear sudden terror, nor the destruction of the wicked when it comes. Contrive a scheme, but it will be foiled, conspire a plot, but it will not materialize, for G-d is with us.” These words conclude every prayer service.

217047.title: This World is Not a Jungle
217047.description: What prevents anyone with financial, military or academic power from doing as they please? G-d is ultimately the Master of this world, and His wish will prevail. This is not a question of religious belief, but a matter of fact.
path: This World is Not a Jungle

217048.title: Grace After Meals
217048.description: At the end of the Farbrengen the Rebbe washes his fingertips and leads the Grace After Meals. The wine is then distributed as Kos Shel Brachah in large glass bottles. Cake and Challah are given out.

217049.title: Bank Leumi
217049.description: Bank Leumi should fulfill its literal meaning and be a bank for the entire Jewish nation. Every branch should have a charity box.

217050.title: Niggun Hisvaadus
217050.description: The Chasidim sing one of many inspirational niggunim commonly sung at Chasidic gatherings.

218746.title: The Ripple Effect
218746.description:
The International Conference of Shluchim takes place every year on the last weekend of Cheshvan. The Rebbe’s address to these emissaries was its highlight.
The International Conference of Shluchim contains a two-fold idea: that it is worldwide, encompassing the entire globe; and that the entire world resides within the heart of every Jew. Whether one is a child, a reserved person, or active in one’s community, his behavior as prescribed by the Torah helps you to convert every detail of the world into one illuminated with G-dliness.

218747.title: Completion of Torah Scroll
218747.description: A Torah Scroll for Morocco is completed. The Shluchim dance. In the evening, the Rebbe speaks and then distributes a booklet.

218748.title: Opening the Doors to Goodness
218748.description: The recipient of a key takes possession of the entire property. Therefore everything in the properties must follow the Code of Jewish Law. These keys will be used to lock out all negative things and lock in Judaism, Torah and Mitzvos.

218749.title: Nyet Nyet Nikavo
218749.description: A song in Russian: “G-d is One, His name is One, besides Him there is no one.”

219309.title: The Purpose of Evil
219309.description: The seminal book of Chasidic philosophy, the Tanya, teaches that each Jew has two inclinations within themselves. One is good, advising him to follow the Torah and perform Mitzvos, and the other is the opposite.

219310.title: Highlights
219310.description: The Rebbe enters the Farbrengen, responds to L’chaim, a personal conversation, a Chasidic discourse is recited.

219311.title: Jewish Congress, Jewish Unity
219311.description: A Congress brings people together, and should promote Jewish unity.

219312.title: Halelu Es Hashem
219312.description: From the section of Psalms known as “Hallel”, or praise, the Chasidim sing “Praise G-d all peoples, extol Him all the nations.” Commonly sung on festivals when the Hallel prayer is recited.

222945.title: Confined Potential
222945.description:
On the tenth of Kislev, 5587, December 10, 1826, the second Lubavitcher Rebbe Rabbi Dovber, known as the Mitteler Rebbe, was released from prison after being falsely accused of treason.
The many outreach activities demanded by the Rebbe may not be used as an excuse to not pay attention to one’s own spiritual needs.

222946.title: Anniversary Blessings
222946.description: Outside the Rebbe’s study, Chasidim offer the Rebbe blessings on the occasion of entering the 60th year from his wedding. The Rebbe responds: Those who give blessings will themselves be blessed from ‘Alef’ to ‘Tof’; from Ahavas Yisroel, love for a fellow Jew, to Torah, Teshuvah (repentance), Tefilah (prayer) and Tehilah (praise).

222947.title: Visit by a Sephardic Leader
222947.description: A blessing for a new building for the teaching of Kabbalah. It should affect the entire globe, and be an immediate predecessor to the building of the third Holy Temple and the coming of Moshiach.

222948.title: We Want Moshiach Now
222948.description: The children should sing ‘We Want Moshiach Now,’ and he should truly come now!

222952.title: Sacrifice of the Great
222952.description: On the 19th of Kislev 5559 (November 27, 1798) the founder of Chabad Chasidism was released from prison after being falsely accused of treason. A Jewish leader sacrifices his own standing to find every Jew in need of guidance and ensure that they receive it.

222953.title: Farbrengen’s End
222953.description: Appeal with opportunity to ask for blessing. A bottle is given to Russian Jews to be distributed for L’chaim. A bottle is given for Jerusalem to be distributed. The Challah is given away, last L’chaims are said, after-blessing is recited, and the Rebbe leaves, taking along the notes for blessing.

222954.title: Vote for Torah
222954.description: There are still three months until the elections, and until then the vote must be for Moses the servant of G-d, his Torah and his Mitzvos.

222955.title: Niggun of Four Stanzas
222955.description: A Niggun composed by the Alter Rebbe. The song has four stanzas, and each raises the singer and listener to the next spiritual realm.

235109.title: The Chanukah Battle Continues
235109.description:
The Chanukah battle and victory were immortalized by the Sages. The candles evoke the memory of the small group of Jews who fought those who had opposed the Torah.
Today, we each battle our own evil inclination as well. Our victories, as well, will be eternally remembered.
Our current mission and battle is for the coming of Moshiach, as we request three times a day during prayer. Although we only request his coming three times a day, we yearn for him “all day”!

235110.title: Chanukah for Children
235110.description: At a children’s rally the Menorah is lit, the children sing the prayer after the lighting and recite the 12 Torah passages. The Rebbe tells the children to “listen to what the candles have to tell us.”

235111.title: Increasing Light
235111.description: The first time putting on Teffilin and lighting the Shabbos candles should be a good beginning. Increase in these mitzvos, just as we increase the amount of Chanukah candles. An investment in the Israel Electric Company. We must always increase light.

235112.title: V’ata Amarta
235112.description: God’s promise to Jacob: “I will do good to you, and I will make your offspring as the sand of the sea which is too numerous to count.” (Genesis 32:13)

239245.title: The Purpose of Obstacles
239245.description:
Following the victory in Federal Court which resulted in the return of the books and objects of the Previous Rebbe, the Rebbe explains.
Josef sets the example for the aftermath of hardship or tragedy. The pain and trouble are not incidental. We must search for the lesson and G-dliness within challenges. They allow us to make the world into G-d’s dwelling place.

239246.title: Chanukah with Seniors
239246.description: The Rebbe enters and distributes coins for charity, the Chanukah candles are lit, and the prayers after lighting is sung. The Rebbe addresses the crowd and distributes dollars for the seniors present.

239247.title: They Bear Your Name
239247.description: Mr. and Mrs. Mel Landow are told that as the Yeshiva bears their name, every student carries their name as well. Blessings for achievement, health, and business together.

239248.title: Ach Tzadikim
239248.description: The conclusion of every prayer service: “Indeed, the righteous will extol Your Name; the upright will dwell in Your presence.”

239250.title: True Living in Egypt
239250.description: The third Lubavitcher Rebbe, the Tzemach Tzedek, once asked his grandfather, the Alter Rebbe: Why do we say that our forefather Jacob not only dwelled in Egypt for seventeen years, but those were his best years? Egypt was a very immoral land; how could this be?

239251.title: Torah Reading
239251.description: The Rebbe receives the Torah scroll and brings it the Bimah to be read. Later he receives the last Aliyah, recites the blessings, and after the Torah is wrapped, recites the Haftorah.

239252.title: Standing Firm for a Safe Israel
239252.description: Mr. and Mrs. Lieberman are told to insist that the leaders of Israel protect the residents, as they are under great pressure to do the opposite. Do so peacefully, persistently and with strength, as you go with the strength of Torah.
path: Standing Firm for a Safe Israel

239253.title: Yifrach Beyomov
239253.description: “In his days may the righteous flourish, with much peace until the moon is no more.” (Psalms 72:7) Chassidim sing a niggun composed for the Rebbe’s seventy-first birthday.

239255.title: Leadership Despite Opposition
239255.description:
There are many similarities between Maimonides and the Alter Rebbe, the Founder of Chabad Chassidism. 
They both faced extreme opposition to their teachings, yet the opposition fell away. Eventually, their detractors became ardent disciples.

239256.title: Communal Talmud Study
239256.description: The Rebbe announces the opportunity for everyone to join the communal study of Talmud by accepting the study of one Tractate within the coming year. Paper and pen are passed around. The Rebbe, as well, writes his own commitment. The Rebbe then encourages the singing.

239257.title: Maimonides’ Precision
239257.description: Maimonides used three distinct signatures depending on the subject matter of the writing. From this, one can learn of Maimonides’ extreme attention to detail.

239258.title: Aimosai
239258.description:
“When will the Master come?”
This question was asked of Moshiach by the Baal Shem Tov, founder of Chassidism, during a visit to his chamber On High.
“When your Wellsprings (of Chassidism) will spread to the outside,” was Moshiach’s response.

247479.title: The True Beauty of Torah Study
247479.description: King Solomon writes in Proverbs, “Charm is false and beauty is naught, a G-d-fearing woman is the one to be praised.” The Midrash explains that this is a parable for Torah study: The lofty Torah study of Moses and Joshua’s generations, which appear to be “charming” and “beautiful,” are considered “false” compared to the learning of those Jews who cling to Torah with “fear of G-d” in times of persecution.
path: The True Beauty of Torah Study

247480.title: Yahrzeit Services
247480.description: The Rebbe leads the evening services on the occasion of the Yahrzeit of his father-in-law and predecessor.

247481.title: To Benefit a Third Jew
247481.description: When two Jews meet, the outcome should be good for a third Jew.

247482.title: Oheiv Hashem
247482.description: “The Lord loves the gates of Zion more than all the dwelling places of Jacob” (Psalms 87:2). The Chassidim sing a Niggun composed for the Rebbe’s eighty-sixth birthday.

249776.title: Self Sacrifice
249776.description:
A story with a lesson.
The Previous Rebbe, Rabbi Yosef Yitzchak, was dispatched to Petersburg by his father Rabbi Sholom Dovber. His mission was to avert a decree against the Jewish people, in his father’s words “at any cost.”
When he discovered that the Interior Minister of Russia was the man instigating the decree, the Rebbe contacted the Minister’s mentor for help. The mentor helped him enter the Minister’s office building, a highly restricted area, where the Rebbe stole into the Minister’s office, stamped the decree “void” and returned home safely.

249777.title: Parade
249777.description:
A vintage film.
Children gather at 770 for a Lag B’omer parade. The Rebbe addresses the children, and reviews and encourages their march up the road.

249778.title: May Israel Do Her Part
249778.description: Israel is the safest country. El-Al signifies to strive for higher, Israel should do so as well in Torah and Mitzvos. Every plane should have a charity box, and I will give one dollar for each plane to help cover the cost of the charity boxes.

249779.title: E Vadye (Russian)
249779.description: A lively niggun sung during the times of the Soviet Jewish resistance. “Water will not drown us and fire will not burn us”.

253998.title: It’s a Beautiful World
253998.description:
The Previous Rebbe wrote a discourse that served as his last teaching. Its title quotes the verse where G-d says, “I have come to My garden, My abode.”
By choosing those powerful words, the Rebbe taught his generation and future generations, that beneath all its outer appearances, this world is G-d’s own garden and dwelling place. No matter how strong the urge to give in to cynicism or despair, no matter how bad things may appear, this teaching shows and empowers us to search out and reveal the essential goodness and G-dliness of the entire creation.

253999.title: Personal Torah Delivery
253999.description: The Rebbe distributes a booklet, containing newly published teachings of his father-in-law, the previous Rebbe, to men and women.

254000.title: More Wisdom, More Activities
254000.description: With greater challenges in business comes the ability to understand and overcome them. Blessings for success, good health, Chabad activities, and the partnership of husband and wife.

254001.title: Veyaidu Ki Atah
254001.description: “And they will know that You, whose Name is the L-rd, are alone, Highest over all the Earth” (Psalms 72:7) The Chassidim sing a niggun composed for the Rebbe’s eighty-third birthday.

254003.title: Tu B’Shevat: Celebrating the Potential
254003.description:
On Tu B’Shevat, the 15th of Shevat, we celebrate the New Year for Trees. It falls in the middle of the winter, when the sap is just beginning to flow.
If the fruit is not yet growing, why do we celebrate the occasion by eating fruit?
By enjoying fruit on Tu B’Shevat, we celebrate the potential within the tree. We also commit ourselves to bring out this potential by nurturing the tree through the spring and summer, until it brings its fruit.
The human being is compared to a tree. We must recognize the wonderful potential within every person and every event, and we must commit ourselves to bringing out that potential.

254004.title: Fruits of Blessing
254004.description: The Rebbe gives Rabbi J.J. Hecht platters of fruit to distribute the following day at a children’s rally, and then begins a lively song.

254005.title: Great Cities in Israel
254005.description: The Mayors of Ashkelon and Lod, Israel, are told their cities should be great in every sense. The New Year of trees applies to man as well. Charity for their cities.

254006.title: Hu Elokainu
254006.description: “He is our Lord, He is our Father, He is our King, He is our Salvation”, from the Shabbat morning services. The Rebbe taught this song to the Chasidim on Simchas Torah 5724-1963.

257011.title: A Tribute to the Rebbetzin
257011.description: “Thank you to those who have begun new projects and institutions in the Rebbetzin’s memory…The Rebbetzin was educated by her father, the Rebbe, Rabbi Yosef Yitzchak Schneersohn. She merited that many Jewish girls carry her name and are educated in her spirit and by her example.”

257012.title: Message to the Yeshiva Students
257012.description: The Rebbe departs 770 and tells a photographer to give the students a message.

257013.title: Ambassador for the Holy Land
257013.description: Be an ambassador to publicize everywhere that Israel is the Holy Land. Interpretation of a dream – the hand of G-d bringing the true and ultimate redemption.

257014.title: Ana Avda
257014.description: “I am the servant of the Holy One, blessed be He, before whom and before whose glorious Torah I bow at all times.” From the prayers preceding the Torah reading.

257016.title: Making This World a Sanctuary for G-d
257016.description: When G-d wanted the Tabernacle to be built, He showed Moses a completed Tabernacle, made of fire. G-d was saying to Moses, “Everything already exists spiritually, but in order for My Essence to be revealed on earth, the Tabernacle must be of this world and its physical materials.”
path: Making This World a Sanctuary for G-d

257017.title: Funeral
257017.description: The Rebbe attends the funeral of his brother in law, Rabbi Shmaryahu Gurary.

257018.title: The Best Blessing – Help the Shluchim!
257018.description: A blessing for a dinner. Helping the Shluchim makes the Rebbe’s life more peaceful.
path: The Best Blessing – Help the Shluchim!

257019.title: Sheyiboneh
257019.description: “May it be Your will, Lord our G-d and G-d of our fathers, that the Temple be speedily rebuilt in our days, and grant us our portion in Your Torah.” From the daily prayers.

257021.title: The Secret of the Jewish Leap Year
257021.description: The solar year is longer than the lunar year. The seasons are determined by the movement of the sun. But the Jewish people set their months and festivals by the moon. Every few years, we add a thirteenth month to synchronize the two cycles.
path: The Secret of the Jewish Leap Year

257022.title: The Blizzard of 1969
257022.description: The New York Blizzard of 1969. The Rebbe enters 770 using the path prepared by the Yeshiva students.

257023.title: Rebuilding Hebron, the Channel for Our Prayers
257023.description: A blessing for success in rebuilding Hebron, through which all prayers ascend.
path: Rebuilding Hebron, the Channel for Our Prayers

257024.title: Ki Elokim
257024.description: “G-d will redeem Zion and build the cities of Yehuda and they will dwell there and possess it. The descendants of His servants will inherit it and those who love His name will establish themselves there.” (Psalms 69:36, 37)

257026.title: Small, Yet Great
257026.description: Torah emphasizes the advantage of “smallness”: Jacob was “the small one.” And we are all preparing to greet Moshiach, son of David, and “David is the smallest.” On a leap year we celebrate a ‘Small Purim’ As well as a ‘Small Shushan Purim’.

257027.title: Kiddush Levana
257027.description: The Rebbe recites Kiddush Levana and Kaddish for the Rebbetzin.

257028.title: Increasing Love
257028.description: “D’Amato,” in Italian, means that you are permeated with love for the people around you. Lubavitch means ‘City of Love.’ We must go from strength to strength in all things and in a way which is permeated with love for all people.

257029.title: Kemofet Hayiti
257029.description: “I am a wonder to many; but You are my strong refuge.” (Psalms 71:7) The Chassidim sing a Niggun composed for the Rebbe’s seventieth birthday.

263345.title: Two Halves Equal One
263345.description:
By creating Adam alone, G-d teaches us that every individual is like a whole world.
But this is only half the story. When the Torah requires a donation from every single Jew to connect us all as one to the work of the Holy Temple, it tells each to bring precisely a half-Shekel.

263346.title: Gerrer Visit
263346.description: The Rebbe receives Rabbi Yaakov Alter, son of the Gerrer Rebbe, who later became the Rebbe of Ger.

263347.title: Model of the Holy Temple
263347.description: Presentation of a model of the Holy Temple. The altar ramp seems to be too short. Blessings for success and to actually see the rebuilding of the Third Temple.

263348.title: Uforatzta
263348.description: From G-d’s blessing to Yaakov, “And you shall spread forth to the west, to the east, to the north and to the south.” These words became a slogan for the Rebbe’s call to reach every Jew, wherever he may be.

263350.title: Joy Reaches Highest
263350.description:
King David, in his songs of prayer and praise, writes, “Serve G-d with joy.”
It is not only the service in prayer that must be joyful, but all of our activities. These means that our study of Torah — our Jewish intellectual life — and our acts of kindness — our Jewish communal life — must also be infused with joy.

263351.title: Officiating at a Wedding
263351.description: The Rebbe presides over the marriage of two young Chassidim and recites the seven blessings over a cup of wine.

263352.title: Katan – Small, but Great
263352.description: ‘Katan’ means small, but is also a name for the Jewish People. Your achievements should certainly not be small at all!

263353.title: Yidelalch Shreit Ad Mosai
263353.description:
“May it be Your will, Lord our G-d and G-d of our fathers, that the Temple be speedily rebuilt in our days, and grant us our portion in Your Torah.”
The song expresses the hope that the Beis Hamikdosh will be speedily in our days, and ends off, “Jewish People cry out Ad Mosai – how much longer must we remain in Golus?!”

263355.title: Moses and the Simpleton
263355.description: The unique traits essential for a true Torah student.

263356.title: Meggilah
263356.description: The Rebbe prays Shacharit and reads the Meggilah on Purim.

263357.title: Bringing Judaism to the Soviet Union
263357.description: A conversation in Russian. Through your newspaper, you must reach out to every Jew and encourage them to increase their observance of Torah and Mitzvot. Teach them about the commandment of charity.
path: Bringing Judaism to the Soviet Union

263358.title: Vayehi Bimei
263358.description: “And it was in the days of Achashverosh, the Achashverosh who ruled from Hodu to Kush, one hundred and twenty seven lands.” (Esther 1:1)

263360.title: Awakening
263360.description:
Haman, bitter enemy of the Jews, said of their misdeeds, “the Jewish nation is slumbering.”
Even their worst enemy perceived that a Jew’s heart is inseparable from G-d. The Jew is merely asleep sometimes, and his heart’s true desire cannot be expressed through our sleeping body.

263361.title: Distributing L’chaim
263361.description: The Rebbe distributes L’chaim at a Purim Farbrengen.

263362.title: Spreading Judaism through Torah Study
263362.description:
It is important to arrange Torah classes for all members of the Sephardic community, and that will bring success in all matters, including plentiful livelihood.
Blessings for a Jerusalem development adjacent to the Temple Mount, which is being built with the necessary permits.

263363.title: Ashreinu
263363.description: How fortunate are we, how goodly is our part, how pleasant is our destiny, how beautiful our inheritance!

269462.title: Seeing Divine Success
269462.description: The Jewish nation’s wandering through the Sinai Desert is a metaphor for exile. Yet it was in this sanctuary, built by human hands in exile, that G-d chose to dwell even more than in the heavens.

269463.title: Gan Eden Hatachton – Ante-chamber of the Rebbe’s study
269463.description: The Rebbe gives his Siddur to a groom to use on his wedding day and distributes coins for charity to those assembled outside his office, before praying Mincha.
path: Gan Eden Hatachton – Ante-chamber of the Rebbe’s study

269464.title: Faith in G-d’s Gift
269464.description: G-d provides financially for the entire world. Surely He will not lack when it comes to providing the funds to print a Torah book. Give to those around you, and G-d will give to you.

269465.title: Hoshia Es Amecha
269465.description: “Deliver Your people and bless your heritage; tend them and exalt them forever.” (Psalms 28:9).

269467.title: Safeguarding Mother, Baby and Doctor
269467.description: According to Jewish custom, the Shir Lama’alot psalm is posted beside a newborn baby’s crib. This was commonplace when Jewish women gave birth in the atmosphere of their own homes. Nowadays, when most children are born in hospitals, it is vital to encourage Jewish mothers everywhere to have this Psalm in the delivery room and to post it in the room where the baby stays afterwards. This will help ease the birth process, strengthen the baby, and prepare the baby for a life of holiness.

269468.title: Distribution of Tanyas
269468.description: Tanyas are distributed by members of the Kolel, as representatives of the Rebbe.

269469.title: Media’s Role – To Spread Goodness
269469.description: A blessing for special success in the reporter’s special mission, of spreading goodness.

269470.title: Al Achas
269470.description: “Thus, how much more so should we be grateful to the Omnipresent One for the doubled and redoubled goodness that He bestowed upon us, for He has brought us out of Egypt.” From the Passover Haggadah.

269472.title: The Jewish Woman – Royal Benefactor
269472.description:
We begin the Seder by announcing, “Whoever is hungry come and eat; whoever needs come celebrate Passover.”
It is admirable to give money to someone who hungers, but even greater to provide prepared food so he need not exert any effort before quieting his hunger. Although we give money to the needy so they may acquire their Passover needs, we go further to invite them to our prepared Seder meal; all they must do is come in and they will immediately be able to eat!

269473.title: A Maamar – Chassidic Discourse
269473.description: The introductory niggun for a maamar is sung. The Rebbe recites a discourse on the topic of Passover Matzah (on the eve of Bedikas Chometz).

269474.title: Painting the Redemption
269474.description: An artist presents the Rebbe with his progress in painting the way the world will look when Moshiach comes.

269475.title: Niggun of Four Stanzas
269475.description: This Niggun, composed by the Alter Rebbe, is sung only on special, holy occasions.

269477.title: Constant Growth
269477.description: The United States prides itself on its work ethic. Yet, somehow, it has cultivated the idea that one’s useful work life is over by age fifty or sixty. When one is no longer as strong and energetic, one is given the right to decrease in the activities relevant to his mission in life. The Torah instructs us that as long as we are alive, our mission is alive and we must do no less than previously.

269478.title: Selling the Chametz – Erev Pesach
269478.description: In his home, the Rebbe sells the chametz before Passover.

269479.title: Happy Birthday, Rebbe!
269479.description: Adults and children wish the Rebbe a long life, a happy Passover and a happy birthday!

269480.title: Hupp Cossack
269480.description: “Jump, Cossack, Jump”. Rabbi Aryeh Leib of Shpoleh, the “Shpoler Zeide” danced to this song in competition against a cossack to gain the freedom of a poor, Jewish innkeeper.

275261.title: Why the Exact Moment of Exodus Matters
275261.description: The Torah does not tell us the exact times when many important events occurred. Nevertheless, we are told that Pharoah commanded the Jews to leave Egypt exactly at midnight on the 15th of Nissan. Further, the Torah narrates the exact moment they actually left: The next day, precisely at noon – not delaying even for the “blink of an eye”.
path: Why the Exact Moment of Exodus Matters

275262.title: Motzaei Yom Tov Pesach
275262.description: The Rebbe wishes everyone a “Gut Moed!” We are required to have joy on Chol Hamoed also, so we should sing “V’somachta b’chagecha.”

275263.title: Asking the Questions, Giving the Answers
275263.description: The Rebbe encourages children to ask the four questions at the Seder, and reminds their parents to prepare the answers.
path: Asking the Questions, Giving the Answers

275264.title: We Want Moshiach Now
275264.description: “Jewish nation have no fear, Moshiach will be here this year. We want Moshiach now, we don’t want to wait!” At a children’s rally, the children sing the Tzivos Hashem Anthem.

275266.title: Ethics Based on Torah
275266.description:
Wisdom and Torah are not identical. The Rabbis tell us that wisdom may be found in the world at large, but not Torah.
When ethics come from G-d, they are unalterable. Only this formula, based on Torah, G-d’s wisdom, can make true ethical life possible. Every person must then perpetuate that life by “raising many students” — continuing to make true morality known so that all may live in true peace and harmony.

275267.title: Kos Shel Brachah
275267.description: At the conclusion of Passover, the Rebbe distributes Kos Shel Brachah, “Cup of Blessing.” Some individuals receive full bottles of wine.

275268.title: Thank You for Your Book
275268.description: Lis Harris, author of Holy Days, receives a blessing for her book and encouragement for her future writing.

275269.title: Sisu V’simchu
275269.description: “Rejoice and exult in the joy of Torah.” The Chassidim sing this Niggun in honor of the first annual Conclusion of Rambam, which the Rebbe had finished immediately prior to this song. From the Simchas Torah prayers.

275271.title: Every Moment Is Precious
275271.description:
The mitzvah of counting the Omer is to count the days from Passover until Shavuos, when the Omer offering was brought in the Temple.
Each day has a purpose. Whether it leads up to the Omer offering or it is an ordinary day of life, we must look at the clock, and ask ourselves, “Am I using my time properly, to fulfill my mission in this world?”

275272.title: Lag B’omer
275272.description: The Rebbe distributes coins for children to give to charity. The Rebbe departs 770 on his way to the Ohel, resting place of the Previous Rebbe.

275273.title: Even Better in the Future
275273.description: A U.S. Senator, the President of the JDC and an accomplished Actor and Singer receive the Rebbe’s blessings for increased involvement in the future.

275274.title: Al Hasela
275274.description: “He struck the rock and water flowed.” The verse tells how, in the desert, G-d commanded Moses to hit the rock with his staff. Water flowed forth from it to satisfy the thirst of the Jewish people. From the Prayer for Rain.

275276.title: Love Your Fellow As Your Fellow Needs
275276.description: The mitzvah to “love your fellow as yourself” raises a dilemma. What should you do when your needs are different from your friend’s? If you are thirsty while your friend is hungry, it would be un-loving to offer him a drink instead of food. If you have time for Torah study while your friend is struggling to make ends meet, it is wrong to help him learn Torah but ignore his need for help earning a livelihood.
path: Love Your Fellow As Your Fellow Needs

275277.title: Lag B’omer Parade
275277.description: A grand Lag B’omer parade. After the crowds arrive and the 12 Pesukim are recited, the Rebbe addresses the children. The parade goes by the Rebbe with marching bands, U.S. soldiers, marvelous floats and happy children.

275278.title: Advocate for the Good
275278.description: A good lawyer should judge all people favorably. Success in one endeavor must inspire you to take on new and greater responsibilities.

275279.title: Shamil
275279.description:
Composed by a cossak who was arrested and yearned for his home and his freedom, this Niggun expresses the yearning of the soul to be where it belongs, close to Hashem.
Taught by the Rebbe on Simchas Torah 5719.

281311.title: G-d is With Us in Exile
281311.description: Exile is a state when the world does not fully endorse the truth. Throughout history, Jews have risen above many attempts to discredit and hinder their devotion to G-d, and so must we do.
path: G-d is With Us in Exile

281312.title: Lag B’omer Fair
281312.description: The Rebbe drives by the Lag B’omer fair and waves to the many joyous children.

281313.title: Take Responsibility
281313.description: The Rebbe speaks with Mr. Shlomo Gazit, former Head of Israeli Military Intelligence. Merely negotiating to give away any part of the Land of Israel is dangerous. Everyone must take responsibility when the government does so.

281316.title: Counting Up to the Greatest Treasure
281316.description:
Exile is a state when the world does not fully endorse the truth. Throughout history, Jews have risen above many attempts to discredit and hinder their devotion to G-d, and so must we do.
We must learn from the self-sacrifice of Jews in countries of oppression who struggle to educate their children Jewishly. One day those lands will see legions of Jewish boys and girls who are proud of their Jewishness. Knowing their struggles must inspire us to appreciate and improve the Jewish education of our children in free countries.
path: Counting Up to the Greatest Treasure

281317.title: N’shei Chabad Jewish Women’s Convention
281317.description: The Rebbe participates in the Annual N’shei Chabad convention. “You are the righteous women of the last generation of exile, and you will be the righteous women of the first generation of redemption.”

281318.title: Light Up the Exile
281318.description: Presentation to the Rebbe of a beautiful silver gift. “Thank you for your thoughtfulness and may you light up the entire exile!”

281319.title: Va’anachnu Amcha
281319.description: “And we, Your people, the flock of Your pasture, will thank You forever; for all generations we will recount Your praise.” (Psalms 79:13) Chassidim sing a nigun composed for the Rebbe’s 78th birthday.

281321.title: The Torah – G-d’s Wisdom, for Every Jew
281321.description: In ancient Egypt, the study of wisdom was limited to an intellectual elite – the sorcerers and astrologers. Ordinary people had no independent access to wisdom. When the Jews left Egypt, however, G-d commanded them to journey to Sinai and receive the Torah. G-d revealed the Ten Commandments, which included the entire Torah, directly to three million Jewish men, women and children together.
path: The Torah – G-d’s Wisdom, for Every Jew

281322.title: Torah Completion
281322.description: A Farbrengen in conjunction with the upcoming Torah completion in Kfar Chabad, Israel, honoring the Rebbe’s 50th wedding anniversary and 30 years of leadership. “May you make many more Torah crowns and fulfill everything in the Torah!”

281323.title: Every Jew Yearns for Judaism
281323.description: “When a Jew feels restricted in his observance of Judaism his desire for it becomes ever greater!”

281324.title: Atah V’chartanu
281324.description:
“You have chosen us from among all the nations; You have loved us and found favor with us. You have raised us above all tongues and made us holy through Your commandments. You, our King, have drawn us near to Your service and proclaimed Your great and holy Name upon us.” From the Festival Prayers.
The Rebbe taught this song on Simchas Torah 5721 – 1960.

281326.title: The Woman’s Three Special Mitzvot
281326.description:
There are three fundamental mitzvot entrusted to every Jewish woman.
Separating challah “from the first of your dough” shows that before benefiting from anything in this world, we “set aside an offering for G‑d.” By knowing that the beginning of everything is for G‑d, the entire home becomes a dwelling place for Him.

281327.title: Ride to 770
281327.description: The Rebbe offers photographer Levi Freidin a ride to 770.

281328.title: Publish More Torah
281328.description: Double your achievements by publishing more Torah and emulate your grandfathers.

281329.title: Ech Ti Zimlak
281329.description:
The famous song “Who knows One?” sung in Russian.
Honoring the Rebbe’s campaign to study Maimonides’ Mishna Torah, the singer adds a fourteenth stanza, “Fourteen are the Books of Rambam!”

291219.title: Foundations In Education
291219.description: Proper education means giving our children a delicate balance. They must know Torah’s unwavering fundamentals, which are, “our life and length of our days“ – principles which cannot change, regardless of the circumstances. At the same time, however, the child is told to continually grow, and be innovative in his life’s mission. Just as his body constantly grows, so must his soul grow, every single day.

291220.title: Refusenik’s Visit
291220.description: Upon seeing the Rebbe for the first time, a newly-emigrated refusenik recites the Shehechiyanu blessing. “We must all learn from his and his wife’s self sacrifice for Yiddishkeit.”

291221.title: From Strength to Strength
291221.description: You should be a living example for men and women, how to behave when G-d gives you the ability to go higher and higher.

291224.title: Peace Upon the Land
291224.description:
The Israeli government must set its priorities in Operation “Peace for Galilee.”
From the outset, the military experts made it clear that casualties could be minimized on both sides of the conflict by a swift operation, which could be over in days. Even the President of the US did not pressure Israel to do otherwise. But some politicians became afraid of their own inner insecurities.

291225.title: Yechidus in French
291225.description: A private audience in French, just after Yud Beis and Yud Gimmel Tammuz.

291226.title: Victory Without War
291226.description: Security for Israel can be achieved by being so strong that the enemies will be too afraid to consider hostility. We already have this strength, but to keep it hidden away and guarded so no one knows of it, defeats its entire purpose.

291227.title: Becho Hashem
291227.description: “I have taken refuge in You, O Lord; I will never be shamed.” (Psalms 71:1) Chassidim sing a nigun composed for the Rebbe’s 70th birthday.

291229.title: Passing of a Tzaddik – Turning Pain into Growth
291229.description:
A person’s passing seems to be a time of sorrow, not happiness. Yet, we gather on the Rebbe’s Yahrzeit, to increase our energy, enthusiasm, and joy in fulfilling our life’s mission.
Torah teaches that, “a greater light comes from darkness.” Torah instructs us to take apparent negativity and darkness, and find in it G-d’s glory, goodness and light.
path: Passing of a Tzaddik – Turning Pain into Growth

291230.title: The Previous Rebbe’s Yahrzeit
291230.description: The Yahrzeit of a Rebbe is a day of blessing. A Tzaddik never abandons his flock, and even after his passing, beseeches G-d, Who bestows blessings for everything we need.

291231.title: Every Jew, A Shliach
291231.description: “Shliach” and “Moshiach” share the same Hebrew letters and numerical value. The supporters are Shluchim as well. We will soon greet Moshiach with all the Shluchim, their families, and their students.

291232.title: The Niggun of Four Stanzas, Nye Zhuritzi
291232.description: A Niggun attributed to the Alter Rebbe, sung on special occasions.
path: The Niggun of Four Stanzas, Nye Zhuritzi

291234.title: Like a Lion
291234.description: The 12th and 13th of Tammuz celebrate Rabbi Yosef Yitzchak Schneersohn's redemption from Soviet exile. But why does good often come only after hardship? Could G-d not have caused all the benefits resulting from the Rebbe’s liberation, without a painful and restrictive imprisonment?

291235.title: Farbrengen
291235.description: President Zalman Shazar of Israel participates at the Rebbe’s Farbrengen honoring 12 Tammuz.

291236.title: A Living Example
291236.description: The most peaceful and effective way to bring your children closer to Judaism is to show a living example.

291237.title: Aimosai
291237.description:
“When will the master come? When your wellsprings spread to the outside.”
This exchange took place between the Baal Shem Tov and the soul of Mashiach on Rosh Hashanah, 5507, 1746. From a Letter of the Baal Shem Tov to his brother in law, Rabbi Avraham Gershon of Kitov.

297059.title: Selfless Prayer
297059.description:
In the Holy Temple, a Korban Olah, a Burnt sacrifice, was offered up twice daily, in the morning and at dusk. Our Sages teach that while we are in exile, “the prayers were established in place of the daily offerings.”
‘Korban,’ offering, shares the same Hebrew root as ‘Kiruv,’ closeness. The purpose of an offering is, that through it, we become closer to G-d. True closeness to G-d can be achieved when our prayers, like the Burnt Offering, are in order to connect with G-d, not for personal gain.

297060.title: Public Fast Day
297060.description: The Rebbe is called to the Torah on the 17th of Tammuz fast day. The Rebbe speaks after the prayers: "May these days been transformed into days of joy with the immediate Redemption!"

297061.title: Publishing The Rebbe’s Works
297061.description: Printing the Rebbe’s works should be done with permission from Kehot. Much success in printing new Torah insights.

297062.title: Sheyiboneh
297062.description: “May it be Your will, L-rd our G-d and G-d of our fathers, that the Holy Temple be rebuilt speedily in our days, and grant us our portion in your Torah.” From the Daily Prayers.

297178.title: Living and Growing
297178.description: Every morning, we thank G-d for giving us life. But there are many different levels of life. Physical growth and energy are much more apparent during childhood than in adulthood. Since body and soul are closely connected, clearly, a child’s soul, as well, develops rapidly during the formative years.

297179.title: Kiddush Levana
297179.description: The Rebbe recites Kiddush Levana, Sanctification of the Moon, in front of his home on President Street.

297180.title: The Rebbe’s Advice
297180.description: Delay your business venture until your uncertainties are resolved. It is incumbent upon you to increase in your observance, since your employees will emulate you.

297181.title: Ho’aderes V’hoemunah
297181.description: This mystical hymn, attributed to Rabbi Yishmael ben Elisha Kohen Gadol, lists the praises of G-d. It was sung at the Rebbe’s Farbrengen to the tune of La Marseillaise, the French National Anthem. By converting its anthem into a Chassidic Nigun, the Rebbe explained, the nation is elevated.

297183.title: A Preferred Home
297183.description: During the three weeks between the 17th of Tammuz and the 9th of Av, we mourn the loss of both Holy Temples in Jerusalem. The Torah tells us, however, that when we study the laws of the Temple’s construction, we are already rebuilding it.

297184.title: The Rebbe’s Camp
297184.description: The Rebbe visits the first Gan Israel overnight camp and addresses its campers.

297185.title: Thank You
297185.description: You can help me in doing G-d’s work!

297186.title: Tziyon Bamishpat
297186.description: “Zion shall be redeemed with justice, and they that return of her, with righteousness.” (Isaiah 1:27)

297188.title: As One
297188.description: G-d dispersed the Jewish people for their own sake. This ensured that Jewish communities would always thrive somewhere in the world, even when others, G-d forbid, would be oppressed. This also ensures that we can join together once again, back in our homeland, when “a great congregation will return there.”

297189.title: Tisha B’Av Morning Prayers
297189.description: The Rebbe recites the Haftorah and Kinos for the Tisha B’av fast day.

297190.title: Territorial Compromise – A Problem, Not A Solution
297190.description: All of Israel belongs to the Jews. No one can give away the property of the entire Jewish people. Our enemies wish to do us harm, regardless of how Israel tries to appease them. Giving them land will not help the situation.
path: Territorial Compromise – A Problem, Not A Solution

297191.title: Nyet Nyet Nikavo
297191.description: A song in Russian: “G-d is One, His name is One, besides Him there is no one.”

302760.title: Only Loving Words
302760.description: In the course of our spiritual development we may sometimes experience a pause in our personal growth. One can advance only so far before facing the boundaries of human limitation. But by humbling oneself, one becomes a vessel – able to receive G-d’s infinite blessings which uplift one to new spiritual heights.

302761.title: Siyum Sefer Torah
302761.description: The Rebbe participates in the celebration of completing a Torah scroll from Israel.

302762.title: Double Your Achievements
302762.description: Being happy with one’s lot is a good trait – but only in mundane matters. When it comes to spreading goodness and holiness, however, one must always be on the look-out for ways to double past accomplishments.

302763.title: Hoshia Es Amecha
302763.description: “Deliver Your people and bless your heritage; tend them and exalt them forever.” (Psalms 28:9).

302765.title: Unwavering Jewish Courage
302765.description: The Rebbe’s father, Rabbi Levi Yitzchak Schneerson, was the Chief Rabbi of Dnepropetrovsk, Ukraine, at a time when Jewish leaders were persecuted for preserving Judaism. Rabbi Levi Yitzchak, however, was defiant; publicly declaring that he would not be coerced into submission.

302766.title: Yahrtzeit of Reb Levik
302766.description: The Rebbe leads the morning prayers on the 45th Yahrtzeit of his father, Rabbi Levi Yitzchak Schneerson.

302767.title: Regards from Almaty
302767.description: A special blessing for the caretaker of the resting place of the Rebbe’s father. May all the Jews of Alma Ata have only good news until the coming of Moshiach.

302768.title: Reb Levik’s Nigun – Blessing of the Sun
302768.description: This lively, Simchas Torah Nigun, was a favorite of the Rebbe’s father, Rabbi Levi Yitzchak. Here, it is sung at Birkat Hachamah, the Blessing of the Sun.
path: Reb Levik’s Nigun – Blessing of the Sun

302770.title: Expecting Moshiach Today
302770.description: The Previous Rebbe was once approached with the following dilemma: You profess to expect Moshiach’s coming “immediately.” Yet, at the same time, you make long-term plans, as if expecting exile to continue for the foreseeable future?

302771.title: Children’s Rally
302771.description: The Rebbe participates in a children’s rally with children returning from camp at the summer’s end.

302772.title: Mayoral Matters
302772.description: When the Rebbe gives a blessing it is genuine. G-d knows what is best and He appoints the most suited official.

302773.title: V’yaidu
302773.description: “And they will know that You, Whose name is the Lord, are alone, most High over all the earth.” (Psalms 83:19) Chassidim sing a Nigun composed for the Rebbe’s 82nd birthday.

302775.title: The Loving King
302775.description: Elul is a time for building a deeper, more loving relationship with G-d. The Alter Rebbe teaches that, at this time, G-d is like a great king who leaves his palace and his city, and goes out to the fields to be near the common-folk of his kingdom. All the townspeople joyously gather to welcome him, and he looks upon each one with a smile and a gracious countenance. He lovingly listens to their needs, and the people then escort their beloved king back to his capital city.

302776.title: Erev Rosh Hashanah
302776.description: On his way from 770 to the Ohel, the Rebbe distributes coins to children to be given to charity.

302777.title: Boomerang Back to Judaism
302777.description: Influence other Jews to return to their heritage. May the Jews of Israel go from strength to strength in peace of mind and with no fear at all.

310843.title: The Upper Hand
310843.description: The Torah states, “When you go out to war upon your enemies, and the L-rd, your G-d, will deliver him into your hands...” This is not merely an introduction to the laws discussed; it is an assurance that when a Jew fights in service of G-d he will be victorious.

310844.title: Annual Pre-Rosh Hashanah Address to Women
310844.description: The Rebbe distributes coins and dollars to be given to charity. The annual Pre-Rosh Hashanah address to Jewish women. “This is a special opportunity to wish each other and every single Jew to be ‘inscribed and sealed for a good and sweet year.’”
path: Annual Pre-Rosh Hashanah Address to Women

310845.title: Awaiting Moshiach, Unconditionally
310845.description: Don’t dwell on prerequisites for Moshiach’s arrival. He should come today – literally!

310846.title: Ki Elokim
310846.description: “G-d will redeem Zion and build the cities of Judah and they will dwell there and possess it. The descendants of His servants will inherit it and those who love His name will establish themselves there.” (Psalms 69:36, 37)

310849.title: Chassidus – The Crown Jewel
310849.description: The mystical secrets of Torah were always studied by the Jewish people, but during most of Jewish history they were guarded and only accessible to a scholarly elite. In later generations these teachings were disseminated to a wider extent, but even then, they were only comprehensible to the initiated; the spiritual illumination of these teachings reached the outside world through those who studied them.

310850.title: Torah Reading
310850.description: The Rebbe is called to the Torah in the upstairs synagogue at 770. Visitors recite the “Hagomel” blessing after arriving from overseas.

310851.title: An Island for Judaism
310851.description: Israel has many people working to strengthen Judaism. Stay in Hawaii where you will be a source of inspiration and Judaism for the Jews there.

310852.title: We Want Moshiach Now
310852.description: “Jewish nation have no fear, Moshiach will be here this year. We want Moshiach now, we don’t want to wait!” Chassidim sing the Tzivos Hashem anthem.

310854.title: Rosh Hashanah – Day of the Jewish Mother
310854.description: On Rosh Hashanah, we are reminded of the Jewish mother’s dedication and self-sacrifice in fostering our nation’s deep commitment to G‑d.
path: Rosh Hashanah – Day of the Jewish Mother

310855.title: Hataras Nedarim
310855.description: On Erev Rosh Hashana, the Rebbe recites Hataras Nedarim, the Annulment of Vows. “May you be inscribed and sealed for a good and sweet year.”

310856.title: A City to be Emulated
310856.description: May your city be a shining example to all other cities in Israel. Stand strong for the wholeness of Torah, which also depends on the wholeness of the Jewish people and the wholeness of the Land of Israel.

310857.title: Yifrach
310857.description: “In his days may the righteous flourish, with much peace until the moon is no more.” (Psalms 72:7) Chassidim sing a Niggun composed for the Rebbe’s 71st birthday.

310859.title: Individual Teshuvah, With the Community
310859.description: Teshuva requires that a person make an honest assessment of his spiritual standing. To do this, it would seem ideal to isolate oneself from all distractions, to focus on one’s past deeds. Why do we see, that on Yom Kippur – the main day for Teshuvah of the whole year – we spend the entire day in a public place, in synagogue, together with so many others?

310860.title: Panim – Erev Rosh Hashanah
310860.description: On Erev Rosh Hashanah, the Rebbe collects “Panim”, petitions for blessings for the New Year.

310861.title: Ultimate Trust Fund
310861.description: Increase your trust in G-d and you will receive even more blessings from Him. Study the chapter, The Gate of Trust in G-d from the book, Duties of the Heart.

310862.title: The Tune of Ashreinu
310862.description: The Rebbe encourages the singing of a lively Chassidic Niggun.

318989.title: Sharing the Season of Joy
318989.description: The Yahrzeit of the Rebbe Maharash falls just before Sukkos, when every Jew busily prepares for the upcoming festival. In recalling his life’s work, we see how the Rebbe Maharash gave up his personal comforts, and worked tirelessly to improve both the spiritual and physical lives of Russian Jewry.

318990.title: Funeral of Rebbetzin Chana
318990.description: The funeral of Rebbetzin Chana Schneerson, the Rebbe’s mother.

318991.title: Leverage the Admiration
318991.description: Admiration for Lubavitch should be used to benefit all.

318992.title: Rabbi Shmuel of Lubavitch's Melody
318992.description: This melody was a favorite of the Rebbe Maharash and is known today as Lechatchila Ariber. Its tune and its name represent his famous adage on dealing with challenges: "The world says, 'If you can't crawl under an obstacle, try to climb over,' but I say, 'At the outset, one should climb over!'"

318994.title: Tzivos Hashem – G-d’s Army – An Inaugural Speech
318994.description: Every Jewish child is a soldier in “Tzivos Hashem – G-d’s Army.” He or she is given the strength to overpower his own evil inclination. But success in this mission depends on careful adherence to the army’s basic rules of conduct.
path: Tzivos Hashem – G-d’s Army – An Inaugural Speech

318995.title: Distributing the Four Species
318995.description: The Rebbe inspects Lulavim and distributes the Four Species to a number of distinguished individuals. The Rebbe receives a Kvitel sent by Rabbi Yekusiel Yehudah Halberstam, the Klausenburger Rebbe. A blessing to those present: “May we draw down all spiritual blessings and have good and joyful tidings throughout the year.”

318996.title: Partnership for a Jewish Environment
318996.description: Much success in restoring the natural environment. I take you as a partner to spread Yiddishkeit all around you.

318997.title: V’samachta
318997.description: “And you shall rejoice in your Festival… and you will be only happy.” (Deuteronomy 16:14, 15)

318999.title: Children – Fruitful Trees of Life
318999.description: On the third day of creation, when G-d created plant life, all the nourishing produce of the fields sprouted forth, and every single tree bore fruit, becoming a source of delectable pleasure.

319000.title: Hoshana Rabba
319000.description: For Hoshana Rabba, the Rebbe gives out “Lekach,” honey cake, from the door of his Sukkah.

319001.title: Every Jew is Close
319001.description: There is no such thing as a Jew who is far from G-d. Reaching out to other Jews simply means bringing even closer, those who are already close to G-d.

319004.title: Go Out of Your Ark
319004.description: In the ark, Noah focused entirely on serving his Creator. After the great flood, G-d commanded Noah, “Go out from the Teivah—the ark.” He was commanded to leave this ideal environment and reenter the world.

319005.title: Yechidus Klali
319005.description: At the conclusion of the month of Tishrei, the Rebbe addresses a group of overseas guests, prior to their return home after the holidays.

319006.title: Opposition as Inspiration
319006.description: May you raise a surplus of money for your projects so you can make additions to your plans. Opposition to your good work should only increase your enthusiasm to do more.

323914.title: The Power of Jewish Pride
323914.description: Vacationing at sea, a successful Jewish businessman was diligent to recite his daily prayers and inquired of the captain which direction was eastward. The captain asked, “Why your sudden interest in the boat’s navigation?” The businessman explained that our prayers ascend through Jerusalem, and a Jew faces there three times a day to beseech G-d.

323915.title: Funeral of Rabbi Yitzchak Isaac Kleinberg
323915.description: The funeral of Rabbi Yitzchak Isaac Kleinberg, a distant relative of the Rebbe.
path: Funeral of Rabbi Yitzchak Isaac Kleinberg

323916.title: Look Forward to New Accomplishments
323916.description: Don’t postpone the completion of your present project. There is much more to accomplish when you are finished!

323917.title: “Niggun Simcha”
323917.description: A Lively Chassidic Niggun atributed to Reb Michoel Dvorkin.

323919.title: Maimonides – A Light Unto the Nations
323919.description: Maimonides is celebrated as a master of Jewish law and philosophy. Not only do we learn from his scholarly writings, but from the life he led as well – a life dedicated to the physical and spiritual welfare of all people.
path: Maimonides – A Light Unto the Nations

323920.title: L’chaim for the Yeshivos
323920.description: The Rebbe distributes L’chaim to the directors of Tomchei Temimim Yeshivos from around the world, to be given out to their students.

323921.title: Yeshivah – A Preparation for Life
323921.description: It is important to take a break from planning your career, to devote at least one year to full-time Torah study. This will help you decide how to proceed.

323922.title: Niggun Hachono
323922.description: Chasidim sing a nigun that is attributed to the Rebbe Rashab as preparation to the Alter Rebbe’s niggun (Daled Bavos).

323924.title: Keeping Warm in a Cold World
323924.description: The Previous Rebbe related that one extraordinarily cold Russian night, he was returning from a meeting to help the Jews of Russia. Even with his fur coat, which ordinarily sufficed, he was forced to find shelter for warmth.
path: Keeping Warm in a Cold World

323925.title: Address to Shluchim
323925.description: The Rebbe addresses a group of Shluchim after a meeting of the Machne Israel Development Fund: “When a Shliach utilizes all ten powers of his soul, he adds a ‘Yud – ten’ to the word ‘Shliach – emissary,’ equaling the numerical value of ‘Moshiach.’” The Rebbe distributes dollars to be given to charity.

323927.title: Whoever Blesses, is Blessed
323927.description: G-d promises that whoever blesses a Jew is blessed by G-d Himself, according to G-d Almighty’s infinite abilities.

323928.title: Uforatzta
323928.description: “And you shall spread out westward and eastward and northward and southward.” (Genesis 28:14) This lively Niggun was composed to honor the Rebbe’s campaign to spread Torah Judaism to all four corners of the globe.

323930.title: Mankind – Nature’s Keeper and Nurturer
323930.description: G‑d created plants and animals with the ability to procreate – to perpetuate themselves and reflect G‑d’s own Infinitude. Man, too, was granted the remarkable ability to reproduce, but was additionally blessed with the ability to harness and expand the infinite powers hidden within the rest of nature.

323931.title: Dollars for the Lubavitch Women’s Organization
323931.description: The Rebbe distributes dollars to the Lubavitch Women’s Organization, to be given out at the Torah Completion Ceremony in memory of Rebbetzin Chaya Mushka. “’A messenger is considered like the sender himself,’ even as ‘Supernal Man,’ and this applies to Jewish women and girls, as well.”
path: Dollars for the Lubavitch Women’s Organization

323932.title: Irish Insistence to Benefit All
323932.description: May you be successful and insistent for the benefit of all New Yorkers and for all the citizens of the United States.

323933.title: Va’anachnu Amcha
323933.description: “And we, Your people, the flock of Your pasture, will thank You forever; for all generations we will recount Your praise.” (Psalms 79:13) Chassidim sing a Niggun composed for the Rebbe’s 78th birthday.

335480.title: Two Prayers for World Peace
335480.description:
To counter escalating conflicts in the world, the Rebbe requests that all Jews add in prayer for world peace and tranquility:
It is crucial for all Jews, without exception, to begin their daily prayers by declaring, “I hereby accept upon myself the Mitzvah to ‘Love your fellow as yourself.’” This not only prevents quarreling in general; it will bring an end to the exile, itself caused by a lack of love for others. (19 Kislev, 5744 • November 24, 1983)

335481.title: Hoshana Rabba
335481.description: On Hoshana Rabba, the Rebbe davens Mincha in the upstairs shul in 770.

335482.title: Blessing Jews Every Day
