don’t you rely on G-d – after all, He’s the one Who sent us into Exile in the first place!”
path: You Have to Ask for Moshiach

1224747.title: The Ohel
1224747.description:
The Rebbe visits the resting place of his father-in-law and predecessor, Rabbi Yosef Yitzchak
Schneersohn of Lubavitch.

1224748.title: G-d Bless You
1224748.description:
“May G-d grant the wishes of every single man, woman and child — especially on the Rebbe’s
Yahrzeit, when his entire life’s work is elevated and he ‘effects salvation in all the land.’”

1224749.title: 16 Years
1224749.description:
A special film in honor of the Rebbe’s 16th Yahrzeit, and highlighting his instruction that all
Jews record and publish their memoirs about the Rebbes and the Chassidim of generations
past.

1224752.title: Not Alone
1224752.description:
The events of the Previous Rebbe’s liberation on the 12th of Tammuz raise a fundamental question: How
is it that one solitary individual was able to stand against a tyrannical world power?

1224754.title: Never Forget
1224754.description: “You say you knew my father-in-law, the Rebbe. Just make sure never to forget him!”

1224755.title: Torah Education in Israel
1224755.description:
Rabbi Menachem Porush was born in Jerusalem in 1916. A seventh-generation Jerusalemite,
he devoted his life to championing Torah values and Torah education in Israel.
A story about the Previous Rebbe, Rabbi Yosef Yitzchak of Lubavitch.

1224757.title: Hold the Gates
1224757.description:
17 Tammuz, 5743 · June 28, 1983 
In Jewish tradition, a communal fast day is an auspicious time On High. This Divine favor
then manifests itself in this world below, and can be intensified by man’s deeds. Maimonides
writes that fasting is one of the paths of repentance, and hastens G-d’s promise: “These fast
days will be transformed into days of joy and festivity.”

1224758.title: Haftarah
1224758.description: The Rebbe recites the Haftarah for communal fast days.

1224759.title: Jewish Law in Russian
1224759.description:
Chief Rabbi of Tel Aviv, Rabbi Yisroel Meir Lau, presents the Rebbe with the Russian edition
of his book on Jewish law, translated soon after the fall of the Soviet Union.

1224760.title: The Kollel Student, Part 1
1224760.description: Rabbi Chaim Brovender was founder and Rosh Yeshiva of Yeshivat Hamivtar in Efrat, Israel. As a young, non-Chassidic, Kollel student in Jerusalem during the late 1960s, he and his wife had a private audience with the Rebbe.

1224763.title: Rescue at Entebbe
1224763.description:
From time to time, G-d grants us the opportunity to observe in this physical world how quality
prevails over quantity, how the soul prevails over the body, and how the soul of the world rules
over the veil of physical reality.

1224764.title: L'chaim for Distribution by Russian and Georgian Guests
1224764.description: The Rebbe distributes bottles of L’chaim at a Farbrengen at 770.
path: L'chaim for Distribution by Russian and Georgian Guests

1224765.title: Budding Philanthropist
1224765.description:
Give this dollar to charity for your young son. Educate him so that when he grows up he should
have a special desire to give charity on his own.

1224766.title: The Kollel Student, Part 2
1224766.description: Rabbi Chaim Brovender is founder and Rosh Yeshiva of Yeshivat Hamivtar in Efrat, Israel. As a young, non-Chassidic, Kollel student in Jerusalem during the late 1960s, he and his wife had a private audience with the Rebbe.

1248280.title: The Day of Eternal Sabbath
1248280.description: It is customary to hold a Siyum each day of the nine days, to diminish the sorrow of exile through the joy of Torah. Watch the Rebbe conclude Tractate Tamid on Rosh Chodesh Av.

1248282.title: Painting for Judaism
1248282.description:
Jewish Artist Raphael Nouril visits the Rebbe:
May G-d Almighty bless you to always paint good things and have good results in spreading
Judaism around you.

1248283.title: The “Art” of Jewish Outreach
1248283.description:
Mr. Rafael Nouril is an acclaimed Jewish artist. The Rebbe encouraged him on numerous
occasions to spread Judaism through his art.

1248286.title: Dressed for Redemption
1248286.description:
Before the Jewish People entered the Land of Israel, the Torah says that G-d “signed the
letters of His holy Name upon them.” Our Sages explain that His main purpose was to vouch
for the women: Although they had been in Egypt for 210 years, the Jewish women did not
emulate the qualities, behaviors and styles of the Egyptian women, and when it came to their
personal conduct, “they did not change their manner of dress.”

1248287.title: Tisha B’av Nidcheh
1248287.description: Morning Prayers on Tisha B’av, at the Rebbe’s house on President Street.

1248288.title: Seven Steps to Moshiach
1248288.description:
Israeli Journalist Motti Eden asks the Rebbe when Moshiach is really going to come: “When I find out, I’ll call you right away! Until then we must expect Moshiach every day.”
A BBC Journalist asks the Rebbe for his message to the non-Jewish world: “My message is that world peace is achievable through observing the Seven Noahide Laws.”

1248289.title: When G-d Sends a Curveball
1248289.description: When Mr. Bentzion Rader came to the Rebbe seeking advice concerning a serious and complex business problem he was facing, he got down-to-earth counsel as well as spiritual advice.

1248291.title: Wise Jewish Child
1248291.description: The Code of Jewish law rules that from the 15th of Av and on, as the days grow shorter and the nights longer, a Jew should increase his Torah study each night.

1248292.title: Morning Prayers
1248292.description:
The Rebbe leads the Morning Prayers at 770 on the Yahrzeit of his father-in-law and
predecessor, Rabbi Yosef Yitzchak Schneersohn of Lubavitch.

1248293.title: Enough Miracles!
1248293.description:
Mayor of Ariel Israel, Mr. Ron Nachman, visits the Rebbe:
“Israel has had enough miracles. From now on, within nature itself there should be success.”

1248294.title: The 4:00 AM Jew
1248294.description:
Rabbi Mendel Baumgarten was a student at 770 during the 1940s. He was 17 years old in
1944 when the Rebbe’s father, Rabbi Levi Yitzchak, passed away in Soviet-imposed exile.

1248296.title: “My Father Stood Up to the Soviets”
1248296.description: The Rebbe speaks on 20 Av, the anniversary of his father's passing.
path: “My Father Stood Up to the Soviets”

1248297.title: “Reb Levik’s Niggun”
1248297.description: A lively Niggun that was a favorite of the Rebbe’s father, Rabbi Levi Yitzchak Schneerson.

1248298.title: Iron Curtains Wide Open
1248298.description:
Rabbi David Hollander discusses with the Rebbe developments in reaching out to Soviet Jewry,
soon after the fall of the Iron Curtain.

1248299.title: The Man with the Information
1248299.description:
In 1956, Rabbi David Hollander became one of the first American rabbis to visit the Soviet
Union. On that visit, and on each of his many subsequent visits, he would come to be briefed
by the Rebbe before leaving, and would report back to him upon his return.

1264759.title: The Sin-Monger
1264759.description: The Rebbe explains the best way to rebuke a fellow who is seemingly guilty of sin.

1264760.title: Niggun
1264760.description: The Rebbe asks new Jewish immigrants from the Soviet Union to start a Chassidic Niggun.

1264761.title: Government for the People
1264761.description:
“With these two dollars for charity, may you go “From strength to strength” both before and
after the upcoming elections. But don’t pay me back, give back to the people!”

1264762.title: Rabbinic Ordination
1264762.description:
Rabbi Yechiel Yaakov Weinberg, author of the Halachic work Sridei Eish, served as director of
the Hildesheimer Rabbinical Seminary in Berlin from 1924 to 1938.
After the war, he opened a Yeshiva in Montreux, Switzerland. Rabbi Gershon Mendel Garelik,
the Rebbe’s Shliach to Milan, Italy was invited to speak at the Yeshiva's opening ceremony.
Before travelling to the ceremony, the Rebbe gave Rabbi Garelik specific guidance.

1264765.title: Jewish Entrepreneurs
1264765.description: An address to the supporters of the Machne Israel Development Fund.

1264766.title: Niggun “Sheyiboneh”
1264766.description:
“May it be Your will, Lord our G-d and G-d of our fathers, that the Holy Temple be speedily
rebuilt in our days, and grant us our portion in Your Torah.” (From the Amida Prayer)

1264767.title: Every Living Thing Must Grow!
1264767.description: “I’m not satisfied for my work to ‘continue’ – it must increase! Every living thing must grow!”

1264768.title: Two Lions
1264768.description:
Rabbi Avrohom Pinter’s father, Rabbi Pinchas Pinter, was a recognized Torah scholar who
studied at the same time as the Rebbe with the famous Torah Sage, Rabbi Chaim Heller.

1264770.title: Jewish Entrepreneurs
1264770.description:
An address to the supporters of the Machne Israel Development Fund
G-d’s foremost commandment is to give charity. Each of you no doubt maintains a separate
account for charity, so that you will not have to stop and ponder from which account to
write the check when you are approached for a donation.

1264771.title: Niggun “Rachamana”
1264771.description:
“May the Merciful One, Who answers the poor, answer us. May the Merciful One, Who
answers the broken-hearted, answer us.” (From the Selichos liturgy) This Niggun was taught
by the Rebbe on Simchas Torah, 5720 — 1959.

1264772.title: Charity on the Seven Seas
1264772.description:
“See to it that charity is given on board your Kosher cruises. And I hope that before your
next cruise Moshiach will come, and then we will speak about the cruise in the Land of Israel.

1264773.title: “I Think His Name is Schneerson”
1264773.description:
In 1940, along with thousands of other Jewish refugees fleeing the Nazi advance into
Belgium, Reb Aharon Noach Blasbalg and his family escaped to Southern France.

1264776.title: Called to Duty
1264776.description:
One of the purposes for which the Jewish children’s organization, Tzivos Hashem, was
founded is to gather Jewish children together outside of school where they will be impressed
with the message that they are soldiers in G-d’s Army.

1264777.title: Panim
1264777.description:
Jews from all walks of life line up outside 770 to hand the Rebbe petitions for blessing for the
New Year.

1264778.title: The Jewish Key to Success
1264778.description:
The Rebbe is presented with honorary keys to various cities and enterprises in Israel:
“According to Jewish law, when you give over a key you also give over ownership of all that
the key opens. This means to say, that all the activities there must be in accord with Torah.”

1264779.title: My Chassid, the Lawyer
1264779.description:
After earning his law degree, Mr. Bentzion Bernstein decided to change his career plans and
go into Jewish education instead. But the Rebbe had other plans for him… (1961)

1280178.title: A Rosh Hashanah Meditation
1280178.description:
Once, after Rosh Hashanah prayers, the Alter Rebbe asked his son, the Mitteler Rebbe, “With
what meditation did you pray this Rosh Hoshanah?” He replied, “With the verse, ‘All mankind
shall prostrate themselves before You’.” Then the Mitteler Rebbe asked his father, “With what
meditation did you pray?” The Alter Rebbe responded, “I prayed with my lectern.”

1280179.title: Farbrengen
1280179.description: A collage of the Rebbe’s Farbrengen on Erev Rosh Hashanah, 1972.

1280180.title: It’s All About Your Readers
1280180.description:
“Trying to interpret the debates of the Talmud regarding the Halachic nature of “time” based
on the Theory of Relativity and Quantum Physics may raise questions in matters of Jewish
faith. Better utilize your talents in writing about subjects that won’t raise any doubts.”

1280181.title: It’s in G-d’s Hands
1280181.description:
Dr. Avraham Lorber was training at Guy’s Hospital in London, England, when a young baby
was brought in with a severe congenital heart defect. After the medical team recommended
immediate surgery, the family flew to New York to see the Rebbe for a second opinion (mid-1980's).

1280183.title: Holistic Living
1280183.description:
The Code of Jewish Law rules: “All your actions should be for the sake of Heaven” and “In
all your ways, know G-d.” This instruction is not referring to the commandments of the Torah
or of the Sages. “Your actions” means the personal activities that you choose to do, and
“Your ways” means the personal path you choose in life. Even these pursuits have a deeper
intent and purpose, in the words of the Mishna: “I was created only to serve my Maker.”

1280184.title: Erev Yom Kippur
1280184.description: On his way to Afternoon Prayers on Yom Kippur Eve, the Rebbe places coins in all the charity boxes set out in 770. On his way to Kol Nidrei, the Rebbe blesses the students of Tomchei Temimim. (Collage)

1280185.title: Make it a Family Affair
1280185.description:
“Although your wife is the one arranging everything for the Jewish women’s dinner, surely
you don’t hold yourself back from helping her. You and all your children should give charity
for the success of the dinner.

1280186.title: “He Thinks I Don’t Know”
1280186.description:
Reb Hirshel Chitrik used to visit the Rebbe’s mother, Rebbetzin Chana, after she moved to
New York. On one occasion, Rebbetzin Chana let Reb Hirshel in on a little family secret (early 1960s).

1280189.title: Two Jews, One Opinion
1280189.description:
G-d created human nature in a way such that no two people think alike. Nevertheless, He
expects them to reach harmonious agreement.

1280190.title: Choosing the Four Species
1280190.description: The Rebbe chooses palm branch, willows and myrtles for his set of Four Species for Sukkos.

1280191.title: Dreams
1280191.description:
“If you had a disturbing dream, have it in mind over the coming Festival during the Priestly
Blessing . May all your dreams be fulfilled in a good way.”

1280192.title: To Israel’s Labor Party, With Love
1280192.description:
Rabbi Menachem Hacohen served as a member in Israel’s Knesset for 15 years. At the time
of his first private audience with the Rebbe in 1959, he was serving as Rabbi of Israel’s
Moshav settlement movement, Rabbi and executive member of the Israeli Trade Union, and
Chief Editor of Machanayim, the official publication of the IDF Rabbinate.
path: To Israel’s Labor Party, With Love

1280195.title: “Order of the Year”
1280195.description:
The year is divided into twelve months. But Torah tells us that there are special years which
have an additional month – changing the entire year into a Jewish “Leap Year.”

1280196.title: Hallel, Hoshanos
1280196.description:
During the Morning Prayers on Hoshana Rabba, the Rebbe waves the Four Species during
Hallel and circles the Bimah for Hoshanos.

1280197.title: Charity-Competition
1280197.description:
“Certainly you’re not upset that your son-in-law is your ‘competition’ and he gives charity in
the same style as you. May you be able to outdo him!”

1280198.title: New Blood
1280198.description:
Rabbi Dovid Edelman is the Rebbe’s Shliach in Springfield, Massachusetts since 1950. During
Hakafos at 770 on Simchas Torah 1973, he was standing right beside the Rebbe and was
privy to a converation between the Rebbe and an Israeli military representative.

1317504.title: The New World
1317504.description:
Although Columbus “discovered” America, obviously these lands and their inhabitants existed
before he arrived. They were just unknown to those living on the other side of the globe.

1317505.title: Kos Shel Brachah
1317505.description: At the conclusion of Simchas Torah, the Rebbe distributes wine from the cup of the Afterblessing.

1317506.title: Holy Land
1317506.description: The mayors of various cities in Israel visit the Rebbe.

1317507.title: Faith and Reason: Evolution
1317507.description:
Rabbi Dr. Moshe Tendler is a senior Rosh Yeshiva and a professor of biology and of medical
ethics at Yeshiva University in New York. He shares from his encounter with the Rebbe in 1970.

1317509.title: Predestination
1317509.description:
When G-d made His covenant with Abraham, He decreed: “Your children will be enslaved and
oppressed for 400 years. But the nation that enslaves them, I will punish.”
How could G-d punish the Egyptians for something He decreed upon them to do?

1317510.title: Tune of “Zol Shoin Zein Di Geulah”
path: Tune of “Zol Shoin Zein Di Geulah”

1317511.title: Sons and Daughters of Abraham
1317511.description:
“As a Jewish convert, you are especially beloved by G-d — even more so than myself or the
rabbi that converted you!”
“May your conversion be a good start for a new life, and go from strength to strength.”

1317516.title: Schools or Jails
1317516.description:
Government is responsible to use its authority to promote the rule of law and protect the
welfare of its citizens. Ultimately, law and order can be maintained when people fear the
government. But relying on fear tactics means that otherwise there would be chaos.

1317517.title: "Rostover Niggun"
1317517.description: Chassidim sing the Rostover Niggun as a prelude to the Rebbe’s Chassidic discourse.

1317518.title: Noahide Law
1317518.description:
Chief Rabbi of Tel Aviv, Rabbi Yisrael Meir Lau, reports to the Rebbe on his efforts to
promote the Seven Noahide Laws around the world.

1317519.title: Who Knows Who
1317519.description:
Dr. Yitzchak Block is Emeritus Professor of Philosophy at the University of Western Ontario.
He earned his PhD in Greek Philosophy at Harvard University in 1958.
In his book, however, it was the Rebbe who made him a “great philosopher.”

1317522.title: The Greatest Job
1317522.description:
Our sages state in Ethics of the Fathers: “Any Torah study that is not combined with work,
will not endure.” Elsewhere the Talmud maintains that man was not born to toil in work, but
rather to toil in Torah. So if one has the ability to study Torah exclusively, why “work” at all?

1317523.title: The Rebbe Sings “Tzomah Lecha Nafshi”
1317523.description:
“My soul thirsts for You, my flesh longs for You; (as one) in a desolate and dry land without
water, so (I thirst) to see You in the Sanctuary, to behold Your might and glory.” (Psalm 63)
This Niggun was first taught by the Rebbe on 28 Nissan, 5714 – 1954.

1317524.title: Judaism on Wheels
1317524.description:
The Rebbe is presented with the picture of a new “Chabad House on Wheels” for Miami,
Florida, along with a special proclamation from the mayor of Miami Beach.

1317525.title: Incognito
1317525.description:
Rabbi Mottel Zajac studied at 770 from 1950 to 1956. He recalls some fascinating anecdotes
about some of the Rebbe’s attempts to ‘hide himself’ from the public eye.

1339417.title: Unconditional Love
1339417.description:
Someone once asked my father-in-law, the Rebbe: “Jewish Law describes certain types of
Jews that one should shun. Why, then, do you treat all Jews equaly with love?”

1339418.title: Morning Prayers
1339418.description:
The Rebbe is called to the Torah the morning after the first International Conference of
Shluchim.

1339419.title: Regards to the Shluchim
1339419.description: The Rebbe sends his blessings to various Shluchim around the world.

1339420.title: The Chicken Race
1339420.description:
In 1945, the Previous Rebbe appointed Rabbi Hershel Fogelman to head Chabad’s Hebrew Day
School in Worcester, Massachusetts. A few years later, when adversaries challenged
Chabad’s presence there, he turned to the Rebbe for advice.

1339423.title: International Mission
1339423.description:
An address to the International Conference of Shluchim:
It truly is a global mission, for it includes also the non-Jewish nations of the world. They have
the responsibility to make this world a civilized place through the Seven Noahide Laws.

1339424.title: Sunday Dollars
1339424.description: The Rebbe distributes dollars at his home on President Street.

1339425.title: Dream Come True
1339425.description:
Israeli Artist Michael Ende presents the Rebbe with a watch depicitng Jacob’s dream.
“In his dream, Jacob saw ‘Angels of G-d, ascending and descending.’ So should it be with all
matters relating to Jerusalem and the Holy Land.”

1339426.title: Heart to Heart
1339426.description:
In 1961, Rabbi Shmuel Lew spent a Shabbos with the university students at Penn State. One
of the students had plans to marry a non-Jewish girl. A few weeks later, the student had a
heart-to-heart talk with the Rebbe.

1339428.title: Architects of Peace
1339428.description:
Tractate Brachos in the Jerusalem Talmud concludes with the passage: “Torah scholars
increase peace in the world, as the verse states, ‘All your children shall be disciples of the
L-rd, and your children’s peace shall increase.’”

1339429.title: “The Mittler Rebbe’s Ensemble”
1339429.description:
At a Farbrengen on the Yahrzeit of Rabbi Dovber of Lubavitch, the Mittler Rebbe, the Rebbe
requests a Niggun that was sung by the Mittler Rebbe’s court choir.

1339430.title: Even-Yisrael: Stone of Israel
1339430.description:
Rabbi Adin Even-Yisrael Steinsaltz visits the Rebbe
Perhaps you should change your Yiddish family name, ‘Steinsaltz’, to a Hebrew one. The
Hebrew form of ‘Steinsaltz’ would be “Even-Melach.’ But it’s up to you and your wife to do
as you see fit.”

1339431.title: Condensed Matter
1339431.description: Rabbi Adin Even-Yisrael Steinsaltz is a world-renowned Jewish scholar. Here, he shares some of the Rebbe’s guidance to him in his own life’s work.

1339433.title: My Dear Child
1339433.description:
The elder Chassid, Reb Michoel of Nevel, used to give his students the following parable:
A simple villager once received a letter from afar. Since he did not know how to read, he took
the letter to his son’s tutor. The letter unfortunately told that the villager’s father had passed
away. When the tutor read the letter aloud, the villager fainted…

1339434.title: Printing Tanya
1339434.description:
Tanyas have recently been printed in many cities in honor of my birthday. This deserves a
special ‘thank you’ from myself, in addition to the ‘thank you’ which Tanya’s author, the Alter
Rebbe, gives. And if you become aware of a community of Jews who are lacking in their lives
the blessing that comes with having had a Tanya printed in their vicinity, print one there also.”

1339435.title: Share Your Charity Work with Your Children
1339435.description:
“You and your husband have sponsored the publication of numerous Jewish books in Russia.
In due time, make sure your own children read the books that you sponsored.”
path: Share Your Charity Work with Your Children

1339436.title: Turn Up the Light
1339436.description:
Len Weksler was a 22 year-old college student when he had a private audience with the
Rebbe in 1952. His career aspirations — and the Rebbe’s — were the topic of discussion.

1367222.title: You Rule the Exile, the Exile Doesn’t Rule You
1367222.description:
The Evil Inclination is tricky and cunning. He comes to the Jewish child with an argument: “I
know you belong to Tzivos Hashem and you must obey the orders of G-d, the Commander-in-
Chief. But you are in exile! G-d assumes that since you’re a smart child you will figure out on
your own that for the time being you should hold off on your prayers, Torah study and Jewish
observance until Moshiach comes and builds the Third Holy Temple.”
path: You Rule the Exile, the Exile Doesn’t Rule You

1367223.title: Menorah Lighting
1367223.description: The Menorah is lit at 770 and Chassidim sing Niggun “Haneiros Halalu.”

1367224.title: Remain Faithful at the Front
1367224.description:
“The Jews living in the Holy Land must continue there. As for those living in the Diaspora,
there are some whose role is to specifically stay in the Diaspora to guard the physical and
spiritual welfare of every Jew wherever in the world they may be.”

1367225.title: Texas Minds
1367225.description:
In 1972, the Rebbe sent Rabbi Shimon Lazaroff on Shlichus to Houston, Texas. A year later,
he brought his first group of Jewish-Texan college students to the Rebbe — in cowboy hats!

1367227.title: A Chanukah Message for All Ages
1367227.description:
Chanukah reminds every Jew that it is G-d’s eternal mandate to carry the torch of His
“Mitzvah-candle and Torah-light.” With most Mitzvos, the “candle” and “light” are not
physically visible. But with the Chanukah candles we see how fulfilling the Mitzvah creates
actual physical light that illuminates all one’s surroundings.
path: A Chanukah Message for All Ages

1367228.title: Chanukah Gathering
1367228.description: The Rebbe joins a special Chanukah gathering at 770 for senior citizens.

1367229.title: The Boychik Scouts
1367229.description:
Jewish Boy Scout Troop 611 visits the Rebbe:
“May G-d bless each of the boys to be scouts for Judaism – to find G-dliness everywhere.”

1367230.title: The Rebbe on Extremism Among Arab Youth
1367230.description:
Motti Eden is director of Israel’s Channel One television. In 1980, while working as a
broadcast journalist for Kol Yisrael Israeli radio, he had a private audience with the Rebbe,
which he recorded and later broadcast on Kol Yisrael.
path: The Rebbe on Extremism Among Arab Youth

1367232.title: Solutions, Not Blame
1367232.description:
The Talmud in Tractate Megillah relates: “Rabbi Eliezer says we do not read Ezekiel 16
publicly, for it recounts the undesirable behavior of the Jewish people in Jerusalem. In practice, we do not follow Rabbi Eliezer’s opinion. Why, then, did the Talmud record this?

1367233.title: The Previous Rebbe’s Library
1367233.description: Fifth anniversary of the US District Court’s verdict ordering the return of books from the Previous Rebbe’s library in 770.

1367234.title: Print More Torah
1367234.description:
The Rebbe blesses and encourages numerous authors in the publication of their Torah
writings.

1367235.title: If I Forget Thee, Oh Jerusalem…
1367235.description:
Geulah Cohen is a renowned journalist for the Israeli newspaper Maariv, who also served on
its editorial board from 1961 through 1973. In 1974, she was elected as a member of the
Knesset, where she served for five terms until 1992.
path: If I Forget Thee, Oh Jerusalem…

1367238.title: On Learning Rambam
1367238.description:
The Mishneh Torah was not written only for great Torah scholars. Maimonides himself writes
that he composed it in a clear unambiguous style for all Jews – “for small and great alike.”

1367239.title: The Melody of “V’Harikosi Lachem Brachah"
1367239.description: The lyrics of this Chassidic melody are “And I shall pour out to you such blessing that there will be no room to suffice for it.” (Malachi 3:10).

1367240.title: What Should My Name Be?
1367240.description: Numerous visitors ask the Rebbe to give them a Jewish name.

1367241.title: Journalism – A G-dly Mission
1367241.description:
Moshe Ishon served as a representative for Israel’s Jewish Agency in New York from 1977 to
1980. In 1981, he became the chief editor of the Israeli newspaper HaTzofe, a position which
he held until 1997.

1393810.title: What Came First, the Torah or the Jew?
1393810.description:
The Midrash asks: “Torah and the Jewish people both preceded creation. But which of the
two came first?” The Midrash concludes that in G-d’s Divine plan, the Jewish People came
first...
path: What Came First, the Torah or the Jew?

1393811.title: Mitzvah Tankists
1393811.description:
The Rebbe gives dollars to those who spread Judaism on the Mitzvah Tanks. The Rebbe seeks
Israeli train conductor and Mayor of Kfar Chabad, Israel, Rabbi Shlomo Maydanchik.

1393812.title: Forces of Darkness Spreading Light
1393812.description:
Professor Herman Branover presents the Rebbe with a new Tanya printed in Vilna in the
original building and facilities of the Widow and Brothers Romm Printing House
“More important that having been printed in the original Romm building, is the fact that now
the communists themselves are printing works of Chassidism!”

1393813.title: “In All Your Ways, Know Him”
1393813.description:
During the 1940s, the Rebbe was instructed by his father-in-law, the Previous Rebbe, to Farbreng
every Shabbos Mevarchim. Rabbi Leibel Posner recalls two “out of the box” talks from that time.

1393815.title: When the Son Outshines the Father
1393815.description:
How is it possible for a Jew, a true believer and recipient of Torah, to entertain the notion
that “It is my strength and skill that has caused my success”?
path: When the Son Outshines the Father

1393816.title: Niggun “Hu Elokeinu”
1393816.description:
“He is our G-d; He is our Father; He is our King; He is our Deliverer. He will soon again save
and redeem us, and in His mercy will let us hear, in the sight of every living thing: ‘Behold, I
have redeemed you from this final exile as from the first, to be your G-d.’”
(The Musaf Prayer)

1393817.title: Good News
1393817.description: The Rebbe counsels various news journalists about the special mission of their field.

1393818.title: Jewish Boys at the Front - Tour in Korea
1393818.description:
Mr. Bernard Cytryn arrived in the United States in 1946. Having been liberated from the
concentration camps by US soldiers, he wished to repay the kindness, and enlisted in the US
Army. Before shipping off to Korea in 1950, he had a private audience with the Rebbe (1950-1951.
path: Jewish Boys at the Front - Tour in Korea

1393821.title: United Nations
1393821.description:
A Jew is responsible not only to teach Torah to Jews, but also to teach the Seven Noahide
Laws to non-Jews.

1393822.title: Niggun “Nye Zhuritsi Chlopsi”
1393822.description: The Rebbe rises from his chair and leads the assembled in a lively Niggun.

1393823.title: Family of Nations
1393823.description:
“As army chaplain, may you influence your Jewish soldiers in performing the 613 Mitzvos,
and the non-Jewish chaplains and soldiers in the Seven Noahide Laws. May G-d bless you,
your family, your large family of Jewish soldiers, and the larger family of non-Jewish
soldiers.

1393824.title: Jewish Boys at the Front - Safe and Secure
1393824.description:
After meeting with the Rebbe in 1950, Private Bernard Cytryn shipped off to the Korean
warfront with his US Battalion. From there, he continued to correspond with the Rebbe.
path: Jewish Boys at the Front - Safe and Secure

1393826.title: Joint Mission
1393826.description:
Excerpts from the address when the Rebbe formally accepted the leadership of the Chabad-Lubavitch movement: “The leaders of Chabad demanded that their disciples take personal action—not to rely upon
the rebbe, and certainly not to rely upon a rebbe’s son-in-law . . .”

1393827.title: 40th Anniversary
1393827.description:
The Rebbe leads the Evening Prayers and addresses the Chassidim on the 40th Yahrzeit of his
father-in-law and predecessor, Rabbi Yosef Yitzchak Schneersohn of Lubavitch.

1393828.title: Forty Years of Leadership
1393828.description:
In honor of his 40th anniversary of leadership of the Chabad-Lubavitch Movement, the
Borough Presidents of Manhattan, Brooklyn, Queens and the Bronx visit the Rebbe.

1393829.title: The Physician’s Prayer
1393829.description: Dr. Ira Weiss served as the Rebbe’s chief cardiologist from 1977 to 1994.

1418735.title: “She Speaks with Wisdom”
1418735.description:
The Sages say: “Who is a worthy wife? One who does the will of her husband.” Chassidism
explains that the Hebrew word, ‘Oseh – does’ also means ‘creates.’ Therefore, “Who is a
worthy wife? One who creates the will of her husband.”

1418736.title: End of Kaddish
1418736.description:
The Rebbe leads the Afternoon Prayers on the last day of Kaddish for his wife, Rebbetzin
Chaya Mushka Schneerson, of blessed memory.
“When we complete this stage and begin the new one, it is not merely a ‘next step,’ but rather
a quantum leap to an entirely new level, new in the realm of good.”

1418737.title: Her Name Was “Life”
1418737.description:
“My wife’s name was ‘Chaya — Life.’ She will continue to radiate life until the Resurrection.
Those who try their best to emulate and fulfill her wishes will bring the greatest gratification
to her soul and to the one who survives her.”

1418738.title: Shlichus Dimensions - Part 1
1418738.description:
Mrs. Reba Sharfstein and her husband were sent by the Rebbe on Shlichus to Cincinnati, Ohio,
in 1954. Here, she discusses various instructions they received from the Rebbe.

1418741.title: Brothers
1418741.description:
The Jews trapped behind the Iron Curtain are living in the lowest spiritual circumstances
possible. But specifically for this reason they have G-d’s promise for an even greater ascent,
far beyond that attainable by Jews living in free lands.

1418743.title: Endeavors of Her Own
1418743.description:
“Thank you for all you are doing at the State Assembly in Albany. And a special thank you
to your wife for all that she does. She certainly has endeavors of her own!”

1418744.title: Shlichus Dimensions - Part 2
1418744.description:
Mrs. Reba Sharfstein and her husband were sent by the Rebbe on Shlichus to Cincinnati,
Ohio, in 1954. Here, she discusses some advice the Rebbe gave her on being a mother.

1418746.title: The Holiest Altar
1418746.description:
The verse in Parshas Tetzaveh states: “The Altar is holy of holies, all that touches it shall become sanctified.”
Chabad Chassidic teaching explains that the Holy Altar corresponds to the heart of every Jew.

1418747.title: Rashag's Shiva
1418747.description:
Afternoon Prayers held in the apartment of the Rebbe’s brother-in-law, Rabbi Shmaryahu
Gurary, on the day after his passing.

1418748.title: Television with a Soul
1418748.description: “Don’t underestimate your influence as a television director in Israel. Utilize it to disseminate Judaism, until the Land of Israel will be Jewish not only in name, but also in practice.”

1418749.title: On the Mark
1418749.description: Rabbi Raphael Pelcovitz shares a personal discussion he had with the Rebbe in the late 1950s.

1418751.title: Secure Your Borders
1418751.description: The Code of Jewish Law rules that if non-Jews mobilize to besiege a Jewish border town – even in the time of Exile, and even in the Diaspora – we are obligated take up arms, even on the Shabbat.

1418752.title: Niggun “Utzu Eitzah”
1418752.description: Song lyrics: “Do not fear sudden terror, nor the destruction of the wicked when it comes. Contrive a scheme, but it will be foiled; conspire a plot, but it will not materialize, for G-d is with us.” (From the Daily Prayers)

1418753.title: Jewish Law Says It All
1418753.description: “Likud means ‘consolidate.’ Your party should consolidate every Jew and all Jews together through Torah and Mitzvos. You need not ask me for additional clarification on what Israel’s defense policy should be. Look it up in the Code of Jewish Law, it’s all crystal clear!”

1418754.title: Security from a Higher Source
1418754.description: Rabbi Binyomin Klein, a member of the Rebbe’s secretariat, tells the story behind an improptu talk of the Rebbe in 1990 on a global terrorist threat.

1441932.title: Say It Like It Is
1441932.description: Rashi states on Torah’s very first verse: “It could happen that gentiles will claim the Jews stole the Land of Israel from them. Therefore, G-d related His mighty works in the Book of Genesis to show that it was He Who created the Land of Israel and gave it to the Jewish People.”

1441933.title: Nigun “Utzu Eitza” & “Sheyiboneh”
1441933.description:
Unfortunately, there are those who stubbornly insist on giving away the Land of Israel. To
nullify this stubborness, let us sing the verse: “Contrive a scheme, but it will be foiled; conspire
a plot, but it will not materialize, for G-d is with us.” (Isaiah 8:10)

1441934.title: The Strong Jew
1441934.description:
Likud Party member Mr Abraham Sharir visits the Rebbe:
“Israel must stand stong against all pressures to relinquish land. Our father Abraham was also called: “Eitan – the Steadfast One,” for he stood strong against all opposition. So too, when people see you they should think of you not only as Abraham, but as “Eitan.”

1441935.title: Drug War
1441935.description: The late 1970s saw the rise of drugs in Israel’s school system. Dr. Eliezer Shmueli served as Director General of Israel’s Ministry of Education at that time.

1441937.title: More Than You Need
1441937.description:
An address to the members of the Machne Israel Development Fund
A Jew starts the day reciting Modeh Ani: “I give thanks to You, living and eternal King, for
returning my soul with great mercy.” G-d returns our souls invigorated, refreshed and robust
so that we may have a healthy day in all ways, both physically and spiritually. And He does
this with “great mercy.” Even if it would just be G-d’s “ordinary” mercy we would obviously
receive everything we need. But when we emphasize that G-d gives with “great mercy,” it
means that G-d gives even that which one doesn’t feel a need for.

1441939.title: Jewish Business in the Orient
1441939.description: “Jews from around the world are now traveling to Hong Kong. When you are there on business, part of your ‘business’ should also be to influence them so that when they return back home, they will go with more Judaism than with which they came.”

1441940.title: Something Is Funny Here
1441940.description:
Rabbi Pinchas Weberman, President of the Orthodox Rabbinical Council of South Florida, and
founder of congregation Ohev Shalom in Miami Beach, relates a “Baal Shemske Maaseh” (1967).

1441942.title: Torah Revolution - Epic Transformation
1441942.description:
The Talmud relates that Haman cast lots in order to decide which month to implement his
evil plot against the Jews. When the lot fell out on the month of Adar he was overjoyed, for
Moses, the Redeemer of Israel, passed away on the seventh of Adar. But Haman did not
realize that 7 Adar is also Moses’ birthday, and his birthday is a rectification for his passing.

1441943.title: Niggun “Ub’yom Simchaschem”
1441943.description: The translated lyrics to this song: “And on the day of your rejoicing... you shall sound the trumpets over your burnt-offerings and over the sacrifices of your peace-offerings.” (Numbers 10:10)

1441944.title: Bring On the Competition
1441944.description: “The Sages state that ‘He who has 100, wants 200.’ This applies to every Jew – even the greatest rabbi. The “Rashba” instructs that you must publicize those who perform a Mitzvah, because when others will try to compete it will increase Torah wisdom.”

1441945.title: Love of Torah
1441945.description:
Rabbi Chaim Ciment studied at 770 in the late 1940s. He recalls some of his impressions of
the Rebbe from that time.

1441949.title: Torah Revolution - Comrades
1441949.description:
The Sages list 48 qualities that one must possess in order to acquire true Torah knowledge.
Among them are: “companionship with colleagues” and “discussion with students.” This
means that you cannot be satisfied to be passionate in your own Torah study, rather you must
engage everyone you can reach in the excitement of Torah, as well.

1441950.title: Fast of Esther
1441950.description: The Rebbe reads the Haftarah during Afternoon Prayers on the Fast of Esther.

1441951.title: Torah Vodaas
1441951.description:
Rabbi Moshe Wolfson, Mashgiach of Yeshiva Torah Vodaas, visits the Rebbe:
“I see from your writings that you qualify for the blessing given by Moshiach to the Baal Shem Tov: ‘May your wellsprings spread outward!’”

1441952.title: Mamish Geshmak!
1441952.description: Reb Ben Zion Shenker is a world-renowned composer of Jewish music. He first heard about the Rebbe during the 1940s, while studying in Beis Medrash at Yeshiva Torah Vodaas.

1467868.title: The Silly Bird and the Wily Fox: Two Purim Parables
1467868.description: The Midrash gives a parable for the story of Haman’s plot against the Jews...
path: The Silly Bird and the Wily Fox: Two Purim Parables

1467869.title: Megillah Reading
1467869.description: The Book of Esther is read on Purim at the Rebbe’s house on President Street.

1467870.title: Jewish Media
1467870.description: The Rebbe blesses and advises various people in the field of Jewish media.

1467871.title: Matters of Principle - Part 1
1467871.description:
Rabbi Hershel Feigelstock served as principal of the Lubavitch Yeshiva in Montreal for forty
years. He recalls a time when he was on the verge of calling it quits...

1467873.title: Starting from the End
1467873.description:
One should search for ways to bring another Jew to the study of Maimonides’ Mishneh
Torah. One way is to celebrate the conclusion of Mishneh Torah...

1467874.title: Siyum HaRambam
1467874.description: Upon the conclusion of the 4th daily study cycle of Maimonides’ Mishneh Torah, the Rebbe discusses the significance of celebrating the occasion.

1467875.title: Israelis Making Aliyah
1467875.description:
“Aliyah is a two-fold ascent, both physical and spiritual. In that case, the Jews in Israel can
also make ‘Aliyah.’ Maimonides concludes his code of Jewish law describing the era of
Moshiach with the verse: ‘For the knowledge of G-d will cover the land.’ In Torah, ‘the Land’
refers first and foremost to the Land of Israel, and afterwards to all other lands.”

1467876.title: Matters of Principle: Through Children’s Eyes
1467876.description:
Rabbi Hershel Feigelstock served as principal of the Lubavitch Yeshiva in Montreal for forty
years. In 1960, he began to take the High School students to New York once a year for a
private audience with the Rebbe.
path: Matters of Principle: Through Children’s Eyes

1467878.title: A Birthday Meditation
1467878.description:
My father-in-law, the Rebbe, writes that on one’s birthday one should recall and contemplate
his past experiences and make resolutions to improve for the future. But if it is called a
“birthday” one must also contemplate the very concept of birth.

1467879.title: Mayim Shelanu
1467879.description: The Rebbe draws water from a well outside 770, to be used for baking the Passover Matzos.

1467880.title: Extra-Strength Mitzvah
1467880.description:
“The Alter Rebbe extols the greatness of charity given to the Holy Land. All charity hastens
the Redemption, but in Israel even more so.”

1467881.title: What a Rebbe Is
1467881.description: For many years, Rabbi Tzvi Greenwald worked at the “Chasam Sofer Home for Boys,” under its Director, Rabbi Akiva Sofer. Rabbi Sofer once shared a story with the boys about an encounter he had with the fifth Lubavitcher Rebbe, Rabbi Sholom Dovber.

1467883.title: The Season of Freedom--Preaching and Practicing
1467883.description: Education comes in many forms: First and foremost is to provide a living example. The best way to influence someone is by practicing what you preach. As we approach Passover, the call of the hour is to seek out those who cannot afford the holiday expenses and provide all that they need.
path: The Season of Freedom--Preaching and Practicing

1467884.title: Prayer – Hoaderes v’Hoemunah
1467884.description: Special moments with the Rebbe in prayer, accompanied by a special recording of the Niggun, “Ho’aderes V’Hoemunah.”

1467885.title: World Cruise
1467885.description:
The Rebbe is presented with a new volume of Likutei Sichos, by the book’s patron: “May you have abundant wealth in cruzeiros, the currency of your country. ‘Cruzeiros’ also 
means ‘to cruise.’ The holy books, too, circulate and ‘cruise’ around the entire Jewish world.”

1467886.title: Birthday Observance
1467886.description: As a student, Rabbi Sholom Chaskind was present at the Rebbe’s first “birthday Maamar” (1952).

1490990.title: Four Sons, One Family
1490990.description: At the very start of the Seder, the Haggadah makes clear that “The Torah speaks of four sons” – a Jew is commanded to gather around his table not only the wise son, but also the simple son, the uneducated son, and even the wicked son.

1490991.title: Biur Chametz
1490991.description: The Rebbe burns the Chametz on the Eve of Passover and distributes Matzah for the Seder.

1490992.title: “And I Will Bless Them”
1490992.description: The Rebbe encourages Kohanim to bestow the Priestly Blessing in synagogue on the Festivals.

1490993.title: The Four Answers
1490993.description: On Passover night, before conducting his own Seder, the Rebbe would visit the Seders at a number of educational institutions in Crown Heights. Rabbi Moshe and Mindy Feller, Shluchim to Minnesota, would lead the Seder at the Machon Chana Yeshiva for Women (circa 1978).

1490997.title: Redemption and the Real World
1490997.description: The Evil Inclination comes to a Jewish child – or any Jew – and says: You can sit in the synagogue or the study hall and ‘Await Moshiach every day’…But the world seems to show an entirely different reality!”

1490998.title: Niggun “Al Achas”
1490998.description:
Song lyrics: “How much we must be grateful to the Omnipresent One for the doubled and redoubled
goodness He has bestowed upon us; for He has brought us out of Egypt...” (The Haggadah)

1490999.title: Much Nachas
1490999.description:
Between talks at the Yud Shevat Farbrengen in 1972, the Rebbe gives special blessings to a
grandfather on the birth of his granddaughter, and to a father on the Bar Mitzvah of his son.

1491000.title: No-Brainer
1491000.description:
Reb Chaim Meir Minkowitz of Montreal recalls some surprising business advice he and his
wife received from the Rebbe, and how it helped spell their success (1958).

1491002.title: Faith After the Holocaust
1491002.description: A sword or gun, or fire or water, can affect only the physical body or the soul’s connection to the body, but never the soul itself . . .

1491003.title: Niggun “Ani Maamin”
1491003.description:
Song lyrics: “I believe with complete faith in the coming of Moshiach; and even though may tarry, I await
his coming every day.” (Maimonides’ Thirteen Principles of Faith, Principle 12)

1491004.title: Moshiach Must Comfort Us
1491004.description: “After everything that has befallen the whole Jewish people in our generation, we cannot fathom the tragedies… The only thing that can be said is that it must reinforce our demand for Moshiach, who must answer all the questions.”

1491005.title: We Need Justice!
1491005.description: Renowned Nazi-hunter Tuvia Friedman reveals the Rebbe’s role in his life’s work (circa 1970).

1491008.title: Unethical Experiments
1491008.description: There is a school of thought that in order to bring close “alienated” Jews we must go to them with an abridged and reformed version of Torah. But others have tried this approach before them...

1491009.title: Niggun “L’chatchila Ariber”
1491009.description: At a children’s rally, the children sing a favorite Niggun of Rabbi Shmuel, the Rebbe Maharash.

1491010.title: Never Too Powerful to Learn
1491010.description: “As a member of Israel’s Ministry of Education, you must not only educate Israel’s youth, but even its government. They pay no attention when you give them ‘orders,’ but ‘good advice’ they will take from anyone, especially from someone who is himself part of the government.”

1491011.title: A Chassid in Berlin
1491011.description: Mr. Uri Metzner’s father, Reb Menachem Mendel Metzner, studied at the Hildesheimer Rabbinical Seminary and the University of Berlin in the early 1930s. During that time, he and his colleagues heard two fascinating accounts about the Rebbe’s private ways (1930-1933).

1515866.title: Finding What You Didn't Lose
1515866.description: The “Second Passover” sacrifice was offered as a makeup for the paschal sacrifice, for someone who was ritually impure or too far away from the Temple at the time of Passover. On the other hand, the commentaries explain that the Second Passover is also a celebration in its own right.

1515867.title: Niggun Simcha
1515867.description: Chassidim sing a lively chassidic melody.

1515868.title: The ‘Rabbi’ of the Supporters
1515868.description: “Your Shliach is succeeding because he has the cooperation of the people around him. You can become a ‘rabbi’ of the supporters for the purpose of communal activities” (5750 -- 1989-1990).

1515869.title: The Real Maimonides
1515869.description: Rabbi Marvin Tokayer is a prolific writer and speaker. As a young college student in 1960, he came to the Rebbe to discuss some of his theological questions (1960).

1515871.title: G-d Is Guarding His Children; You Can Help
1515871.description:
An address at the 1967 Lag BaOmer Parade, less than a week before the Six-Day War.
G-d is protecting your brothers and sisters in the Holy Land, but you have the unique privilege to help them . . .
path: G-d Is Guarding His Children; You Can Help

1515872.title: "Lag BaOmer Parades"
1515872.description: A collage of Lag BaOmer parades spanning five decades, accompanied by a special recording of the niggun “Hinei Mah Tov.”

1515873.title: Ladder to Sinai
1515873.description:
Rabbi Simcha Ashlag presents the Rebbe with a volume of the Zohar Im Peirush HaSulam
“The word ‘Sulam – Ladder’ is numerically equivalent to ‘Sinai.’ May it form ‘a ladder
reaching the heavens for living souls.”

1515874.title: Scholar in Residence: Exchanging Kabbalah for Alef-Beis
1515874.description: Over the course of the Rebbe’s three-month stay in Paris, he was asked to speak publicly on numerous occasions. Rabbi Nachum Avraham Yakobovitch was 20 years old at the time, and was present at a number of these events (1947).
path: Scholar in Residence: Exchanging Kabbalah for Alef-Beis

1515876.title: Torah Scholarship: Not for Men Only
1515876.description: In this day and age, women and girls–even very little girls–study parts of the Torah which in the past they’d rely on their husbands or brothers to know.
path: Torah Scholarship: Not for Men Only

1515877.title: Address to Women
1515877.description: The Rebbe delivers his annual pre-Shavuos address to women.

1515878.title: Renewing the Vows on Shavuot
1515878.description: The Giving of the Torah on the holiday of Shavuot is G-d’s marriage to the Jewish People.

1515879.title: Scholar in Residence: “A Waterfall of Torah!”
1515879.description: Rabbi Nachum Avraham Yakobovitch continues his account of the the Rebbe’s public addresses in Paris in 1947.
path: Scholar in Residence: “A Waterfall of Torah!”

1515881.title: How You Can Attain Infinity
1515881.description: Jews must “conquer” the world through increased Torah study – each person according to his own level.

1515882.title: Cup of Blessing
1515882.description: The Rebbe distributes wine from the cup of the After-Blessing at the conclusion of Shavuos. Cantor Tzvi Hirsh Tzatzkis sings a song he composed honoring the Rebbe’s call in 1987 to build housing in Jerusalem in anticipation of a great exodus of Jews from the Soviet Union.

1515883.title: No, You Are!
1515883.description: Chief Rabbi of Haifa, Rabbi Shar Yashuv Cohen, has an interesting exchange with the Rebbe, with each arguing that the other has the power to bestow Divine blessing.

1515884.title: Drawing with the Rebbe
1515884.description: In 1959, Mrs. Esther Mentz brought her toddler to a private audience she had with the Rebbe. When the child could not be made to sit quietly, the Rebbe took matters into his own hands.

1547901.title: G-d’s Only Daughter
1547901.description:
When G-d commanded Moses to count the Jews, the “greatest” among them counted as one,
and the “simplest” among them counted as one. Every Jew is an equal son or daughter of G-d
Himself, and is beloved to Him much more than an only child is loved by a father and mother.

1547902.title: The Rebbe's Sensitivity to Five Year Old Girl
1547902.description: Chassidim sing the Russian version of “Who Knows One?” as the Rebbe distributes wine from the cup of the After-blessing. When a young girl sings along into the microphone, he gently reminds her to clap rather than sing, and stops the line of visitors to clap along with her.
path: The Rebbe's Sensitivity to Five Year Old Girl

1547903.title: The Rebbe on Jewish Beauty
1547903.description: The 1991 “Miss Israel” winner visits the Rebbe: “Torah says: ‘Beauty is false.’ But the verse continues: ‘A G-d-fearing woman is to be praised.’ The commentaries explain that if a woman is G-d-fearing, she uses her beauty for beautiful endeavors in Torah and Mitzvos. Good tidings, and please relay this message to your friends.”

1547904.title: Speechless
1547904.description: Around 1970, a young teenage girl who had inexplicably lost her voice emerged from the Rebbe’s room speaking again! Now a healthy mother of eleven, she tells “the rest of the story.”

1547906.title: Planning for a Family
1547906.description: Torah’s first commandment is: “Be fruitful and multiply; fill the earth and conquer it.” This is not just a physical command, but a spiritual one: When it comes to building a family, one must conquer all the concerns that stem from the ‘earth’ — from worldly, materialistic considerations...

1547907.title: Niggun “Sheyiboneh”
1547907.description: At a children’s rally, the Rebbe asks for the Niggun “Sheyiboneh” to be sung — for the first time in 770.

1547908.title: Not Just One Life
1547908.description: “May G-d bless you to continue to convince women not to opt for abortion. Every child that is added to the Jewish people is a big help for Jews everywhere, even in Israel.”

1547909.title: If You Could Have Anything in the Whole World…
1547909.description: Rabbi Yitzchok Meir Gurary is Mashpiya of the Lubavitcher Yeshiva in Montreal. His father, Rabbi Zalman Gurary, a devoted Chassid and financial supporter of the Rebbe’s work, once made a deal with the Rebbe that he could ask for a blessing in anything he wanted...(circa 1959)
path: If You Could Have Anything in the Whole World…

1547911.title: A Golden Lining
1547911.description:
Talmud Tractate Chagigah concludes with a discussion about the coating of the Golden Altar.
Although the gold plating is extremely thin, it protects the wooden vessel inside it from being
consumed by fire; and even though the gold is considered secondary to the wood,
nevertheless Torah calls it: “The Golden Altar.”

1547912.title: 50 Years in America
1547912.description: Chassidim celebrate the 50th anniversary of the Rebbe and Rebbetzin’s safe arrival on American shores in 1941, and fifty years of the Rebbe’s public service in America.

1547913.title: It’s All in the Name
1547913.description: The Rebbe derives personal messages for various individuals based on the meaning of their Hebrew names.

1547914.title: Sweet Deal
1547914.description: Mr. David Mintz is founder and Chief Executive Officer of Toffuti. He shares one of many occasions when the Rebbe literally saved his business (circa 1987).

1547916.title: Jewish Leadership Defined
1547916.description:
The verse states: “He gave his own bread to the destitute.” The Talmud explains that this
refers to Moses giving the Torah to the Jewish people. But every word of the verse is precise..

1547917.title: The Ohel
1547917.description: Hours before Rosh Hashanah, the Rebbe brings petitions for blessing to the Ohel, resting place of his father-in-law and predecessor, Rabbi Yosef Yitzchak of Lubavitch.

1547918.title: Faithful Shepherd
1547918.description: “One reason I do not visit Israel is that I have not found sufficient Halachic grounds to allow me to leave Israel and return to America. I cannot abandon American Jewry. Even if I could return, my return itself could be interpreted as a ‘preference’ for America over the Holy Land.”

1547919.title: Be a Man
1547919.description: In the summer of 1968, Rabbi Moshe Feller was invited to be a visiting scholar at Bnai Brith’s Youth Leadership camp in Pennsylvania. When some of the teenagers asked him to Farbreng with them in honor of Yud Beis Tammuz, he reluctantly agreed, giving up his chance to enjoy the Rebbe’s Farbrengen in New York. Or so he thought...

1558540.title: Bostonian in a Faraway Land
1558540.description: My father-in-law, the Rebbe, instituted “Merkos Shlichus,” whereby Yeshiva students volunteer each summer to visit remote Jewish communities in order to raise awareness of Torah, Mitzvos and Judaism.

1558541.title: Torah Publications
1558541.description: On the 50th Anniversary of the Previous Rebbe’s liberation from Soviet incarceration, the Rebbe is presented with various new Torah publications.

1558542.title: Keep On Your Toes
1558542.description: “Thank you very much for supporting your local Shliach. And don’t let him be satisfied by his achievements – by showing him that you are also not satisfied by your achievements.”

1558543.title: Kostroma
1558543.description: In 1927, the communist authorities sentenced Rabbi Yosef Yitzchak of Lubavitch to exile in Kostroma, a small city over 400 miles away from his headquarters in Leningrad. During his time there, he stayed with the family of the local Shochet, Reb Yerachmiel Kugel.

1558545.title: G-d's Chosen Home
1558545.description: When Maimonides discusses the biblical commandment to build a Sanctuary for G-d, he quotes the verse “Build for me a Holy Temple.” Accordingly, he should have called the section of his code that deals with the Temple “Laws of the Holy Temple.” Why does he instead call them “Laws of the Chosen House”?

1558546.title: Selichos
1558546.description: The Rebbe leads Selichos on the Fast of Tammuz, at his home on President Street.

1558547.title: Bibi Netanyahu
1558547.description: “Tell Bibi Netanyahu in my name to continue to hold on to the hardline. And if the occasion arises to stand even stronger, he will certainly find that strength within himself.”

1558548.title: Religion and Politics
1558548.description: Dr. David Luchins is Chair of Political Science at Touro College. For 20 years he served on the staff of US Senator Daniel Patrick Moynihan, during which the Senator visited the Rebbe on several occasions.

1558550.title: The Wagon Driver’s Lesson
1558550.description:
An address to the children of Camp Gan Israel of New York:
Camp ‘Gan Israel’ is named after Rabbi Israel Baal Shem Tov, founder of the Chassidic movement – for through studying and living by his teachings, the Baal Shem Tov lives on.

1558551.title: Torah Reading
1558551.description: The Rebbe joins the morning Minyan upstairs at 770, to hear the Torah reading.

1558552.title: Strengthened by the Opposition
1558552.description: “According to Jewish law, so long as a legal contract is not contested, it is not fully authenticated. Only after it stands up to a challenge is its authenticity fully confirmed. Now that you have overcome your opposition, you will proceed even stronger than before.”

1558553.title: Completely Unwarranted Love
1558553.description: The Sages teach that the Holy Temple was destroyed on account of unwarranted hatred, and will be rebuilt through unwarranted love. Rabbi Pinchas Weberman recalls a private audience in 1973 where the Rebbe explained just how literal this teaching is.

1558555.title: “For My Children? Only the Best!”
1558555.description:
Parents are never satisfied to provide their children with the minimum, or even the average.
For their own needs a father or mother might settle for less, but for their children they want only the greatest and the best they can provide. If this is so with food and clothing, which are quite temporary, how much more so when it comes to a child’s spiritual education, which impacts the rest of his or her entire life.

1558556.title: We Want Moshiach Now
1558556.description: Campers from Gan Israel New York attend the Rebbe’s Farbrengen.

1558557.title: The Educator’s Huge Responsibility
1558557.description: The Rebbe offers insight and blessings to Jewish educators.

1558558.title: All for the Cause
1558558.description: In 1968, Mr. Moshe Salzberg founded a new Jewish elementary school in Montreal, Canada, despite the existence of a local Chabad school. What did the Rebbe think of that?

1586466.title: Make it Stop!
1586466.description:
The Jerusalem Talmud states: “If the Holy Temple is not rebuilt in your lifetime, it’s as though
it were destroyed in your lifetime.” The commentaries learn from this that the Temple’s destruction is an ongoing event. On Tisha B’av, we do not mourn events that occurred 1,900 years ago… The destruction of the Temple takes place every single day – and a Jew is expected to cry out for Redemption as if he has witnessed that destruction today!

1586467.title: Afternoon Prayers and Haftorah
1586467.description: Afternoon Prayers on Tisha B’av at 770. The Rebbe recites the Haftorah.

1586468.title: Stones of Jerusalem
1586468.description: “Thank you for donating the stone façade for the front wall at 770. May you and your family merit to take part in building the Holy Temple in Jerusalem.”

1586469.title: Don’t Worry, the Money will Come
1586469.description: In 1979, Mr. Chaim Bialik-Chacham was appointed senior aide to Israel’s Minister of Finance. While on assignment in New York, he got an out-of-the-blue phone call that the Rebbe wished to see him.
path: Don’t Worry, the Money will Come

1586473.title: What Goes Down Must Come Up
1586473.description: The Talmud states in Tractate Taanit: “Never were there more joyous days for the Jewish people than the 15th of Av and Yom Kippur,” listing five or six joyous events that occurred on 15 Av throughout history. What is it about the energy of the 15th of Av that attracts so much joy?
path: What Goes Down Must Come Up

1586474.title: L’chaim
1586474.description: The Rebbe distributes L’chaim to various individuals.

1586475.title: The Chassidic Masters and Tu B’av
1586475.description: ”Rabbi Chaim Elazar of Munkatch teaches that beginning on the 15th of Av – Tu B’av – one starts to wish others a good New Year. Perhaps he received this teaching from Rabbi Levi Yitzchak of Berditchev, but regardless of where he got it from, it’s a good thing.”
path: The Chassidic Masters and Tu B’av

1586476.title: Light at the End of the Tunnel
1586476.description: Mr. Murray Dalfen recalls how the Rebbe’s words got him through some of the darkest financial moments of his career (1989).
path: Light at the End of the Tunnel

1586478.title: Tears
1586478.description: The Arizal writes that the numerical value of ‘Dimah–Tears’ is 120, which in Torah signifies full life.

1586479.title: Niggun “Stav Ya Pitu”
1586479.description: Chassidim sing a Russian Niggun, taught by the Rebbe on Simchas Torah 5722 – 1961.

1586480.title: Operation Esther: Saving Yemenite Jewry
1586480.description: “Rescuing the Jews in Yemen and relocating them to Israel is truly a matter of life and death. Regarding your work to keep the Land of Israel whole – it would more conducive to live in Israel and work from there; otherwise people will wonder why you traded the good and holy Land of Israel for the ‘gold-paved streets’ of America.”

1586481.title: Reb Yitzchok the Schochet
1586481.description: Rabbi Mordechai Goldschmid’s father, Reb Nochum, grew up with the Rebbe in Dniepropetrovsk, Ukraine. His grandfather, Reb Yitzchok, was the local Shochet.

1586485.title: Aspiring Levites
1586485.description:
An address to the campers returning from Camp Gan Israel Detroit:
Torah says of the Tribe of Levi: “G-d is their inheritance” – G-d provides for all their needs. We
see this idea with children as well...

1586486.title: Off to Work
1586486.description: The Rebbe leaves his home on President Street for 770 (September, 1983).

1586487.title: Double-double-double-double!
1586487.description: “Tell the restaurants that use your ventilation system that ‘double charity’ is only my minimum program, and only as a beginning. After that, their appetite should grow – along with all the eating – and, in turn, they will demand your product double-double-double-double.”

1586488.title: “Where were you?!”
1586488.description: After giving birth to triplets prematurely, Mrs. Esther Glauberson and her parents waited helplessly while the newborns’ lives hung in the balance. In the middle of it all, her mother suddenly vanished into thin air…

1600156.title: Shaatnez – A Lesson for Life
1600156.description: Torah commands a Jew not to wear Shaatnez – wool and linen woven together. What is the inner meaning of this Mitzvah?

1600158.title: Mitzvos in Los Angeles
1600158.description: Thirteen dollars in honor of growing your beard, which draws down G-d’s Thirteen Attributes of Mercy. Checking your Tefillin and Mezuzos will help the psychiatric patients who come to you.

1600159.title: The Logic of Joy
1600159.description: The importance of joy in one’s life and in one’s G-dly service is central to Chassidic teaching. In one of his private meetings with the Rebbe (in 1961), Mr. Bentzion Bernstein asked how such joy was humanly possible.

1600161.title: How a Father Acts
1600161.description: A Jew is instructed to give rebuke, as the verse commands: “You shall surely rebuke your fellow.” Nevertheless, you can deliver the rebuke joyfully, good-naturedly, and gently.

1600162.title: Family Tree
1600162.description: The Rebbe is presented with a book listing the descendants of the Alter Rebbe.

1600163.title: Reformed Ways
1600163.description:
An ex-Reform rabbi informs the Rebbe that he is returning to Orthodox Judaism.
"To go in the way that you have chosen means you must be very strict to fulfill all the instructions of G-d Almighty as they are recorded in the Code of Jewish Law. Influence your pupils to do the same, and that will fortify yourself as well."

1600164.title: Testing the Waters
1600164.description: In 1956, Rabbi Eitan Greene had a two hour audience with the Rebbe, in which he asked many questions on Talmud and Jewish philosophy.

1600166.title: "I Am My Beloved's, My Beloved Is Mine"
1600166.description: The sages teach that “Elul” is an acronym for the verse in Song of Songs: “I am my Beloved’s and my Beloved is mine.”
path: "I Am My Beloved's, My Beloved Is Mine"

1600167.title: Selichos Prayers
1600167.description: The first night of Selichos at 770.

1600168.title: Never Be Satisfied
1600168.description: “To be satisfied with one’s lot” is a great thing in general, but when it comes to Torah and Mitzvos there must always be growth. To be satisfied with the past is fine – it’s good to be a happy Jew. But aside from that, one must increase many times over.

1600169.title: Baba Sali Stories
1600169.description: Rabbi Machluf Krispin is married to the granddaughter of the Moroccan Torah sage, Rabbi Yisrael Abuchatzeira, famously known as “Baba Sali.” At his first private audience with the Rebbe, he related a fascinating story of his grandfather.

1600171.title: New Year’s Blessings from A to Z
1600171.description:
Many High Holiday prayers follow the order of the alphabet. In this spirit, may it be:
A year of “Orah – light.” A year of “Brocha – blessing.” A year of “Gedula – greatness...”
path: New Year’s Blessings from A to Z

1600172.title: Dollars for Shluchim
1600172.description: The Rebbe distributes dollars to the Shluchim and Shluchos who brought their supporters to the meeting of the Machne Israel Development Fund.

1600173.title: Make them Smile
1600173.description: People are not happy when they hear about unhappy things. Speak only about the positive blessings and rewards of living a Jewish life, not about Divine punishment… When people are smiling, and you are smiling, they accept it more – “smiling.”

1600174.title: A Higher Network
1600174.description: In 1987, Mr. Jerry Levine was working as an anchorman for Miami’s Channel 10 News when he was asked to get involved in Chabad’s outreach activities. When he wrote the Rebbe to ask his guidance on the matter, the response he got back seemed somewhat . . . silly.

1638109.title: Find and Seek
1638109.description: Regarding the Ten Days of Repentance between Rosh Hashanah and Yom Kippur, Isaiah the Prophet states: “Seek G-d when He is found, call to Him when He is near.”

1638110.title: Erev Yom Kippur
1638110.description: The Rebbe bestows the Priestly Blessing following Afternoon Prayers on Erev Yom Kippur.

1638111.title: Infinite Teshuva
1638111.description: “To renounce Judaism for another religion is the worst sin. The fact that you think you’re happy now only reveals how unhealthy your situation is... May G-d bless you to become healthy – and the main thing: to become a Jew openly, and proclaim to all the people around you that G-d has so much mercy that He forgives even the biggest sin that can be done.”

1638112.title: “Someone’s Praying for Him”
1638112.description: Rabbi Shabsi Alpern is a senior Shliach in Brazil. In 1976, a member of his community funded the building of a new synagogue and Mikveh, after which he suffered a serious accident...

1638115.title: Swords into Palm Branches
1638115.description: An address to children on Sukkos: Unlike other nations, who parade with a rifle, a Jew parades with a lulav. And instead of bullets, a Jew arms himself with an esrog. Instead of brandishing daggers or swords, a Jew carries hadassim (myrtles) and aravos (willows).

1638116.title: The Four Species
1638116.description: Hallel during the Morning Prayers on Chol Hamoed Sukkos.

1638117.title: Kick Up a Fundraising Storm!
1638117.description:
“A fundraising campaign done with humility will have very little money coming in... You must
conduct the fundraiser like it’s a ‘Desert Storm,’ as they called it during the Gulf War.”

1638118.title: Picking the Rebbe’s Lulav
1638118.description: For many years, Rabbi Yitzchak Maier Gurary and his father-in-law, Rabbi Mordechai Altein, would provide the Four Species to the Rebbe for Sukkos.

1638120.title: Four of a Kind
1638120.description: The Midrash teaches that each of the Four Species on Sukkos represents one kind of Jew and concludes: “On Sukkos, all four Jews must join together, for each one completes the others.”

1638121.title: Hoshana Rabba
1638121.description: Reciting the Book of Psalms on the Eve of Hoshana Rabba.

1638122.title: Cure for Arrogance
1638122.description: “The word ‘Esrog’ forms an acronym for the verse: ‘Let not the foot of arrogance overtake me.’ This is especially pertinent to a successful doctor, that he should never claim: ‘My own strength has brought me my success.’”

1638123.title: Damascus
1638123.description: In 1973, at the time the Yom Kippur War broke out, Mr. Aryeh Morgenstern was director of the Torah Department of the World Zionist Organization in the United States.

1638125.title: G-d, the Homemaker
1638125.description:
A good homemaker is missing nothing in her home, but she also has nothing extra. Extra
possessions in one’s domain make clutter, they’re a distraction. So too, in the words of the
Talmud: “G-d did not create even one detail in His world in vain.” If an intelligent human being
avoids both deficiency and excess, then surely G-d, Who is the ultimate perfection, did not
create any detail in vain.

1638126.title: Farewell
1638126.description:
At the conclusion of the festive month of Tishrei, the Rebbe sees off the guests who travelled
in to Crown Heights from overseas.

1638127.title: The Joy of Yiddish
1638127.description: “I’m glad you enjoyed my Yiddish. Until now, when I’ve addressed the supporters of the Machne Israel Development Fund, I’ve spoken in English. But today I made a change and spoke in Yiddish, because Yiddish is always better – even than my Pidgin English.”

1638128.title: G-d-Given Talents
1638128.description: At the time Avraham Zigman was starting out on the path of Teshuva, he was working as a music radio host. He consulted the Rebbe as to what his next step on the path should be (1979).

1663535.title: Too Good for G-d?
1663535.description: It happened once on Shabbos that in the midst of prayer, the Alter Rebbe removed his Tallis and went to the edge of the town. There, he found a woman who had just given birth. The Alter Rebbe had sensed that she needed help...

1663537.title: Noahide Law in the Knesset
1663537.description: “Bring all Jews under the wings of G-d’s Divine Presence, including the ministers of the Knesset — even the non-Jewish ministers, who are obligated in the Seven Noahide Laws.

1663538.title: What Did They Teach You?!
1663538.description: Rabbi Mottel Zajac grew up in Brazil. In 1947, he was sent to New York to study at the Lubavitcher Yeshiva in Crown Heights, and later at 770 (from an encounter with the Rebbe in 1960).

1663540.title: Responsibility Doesn’t Disappear!
1663540.description: There is a long standing edict that in every Jewish community – without exception – there be one person who acts as the community’s Chasidic mentor, before whom the people can pour out their spiritual ailments, and whose task it is to guide others in the ways of Chasidism and provide each one with an individualized path in the service of G-d.

1663542.title: Israel’s Aerial Gateway
1663542.description: The city of Lod connects the Holy Land to the world – through the airport. As mayor of the city, you have a responsibility to two parties: the Holy Land, and the rest of the entire world.

1663543.title: Vote of Confidence
1663543.description: Born into a secular Jewish family, Rabbi Michoel Kanterovitz returned to Judaism on his own at the age of 7. Over the course of his rabbinic career, he served Jewish communities in Canada, England and Australia. But it was the Rebbe who got him his first rabbinic post (1967).

1663545.title: Defend Your Parents!
1663545.description: When the outrageous suggestion was made by a Jew to officially divide the Cave of the Patriarchs in half, a Muslim stood up and made a commotion: “The structure around the cave was converted into a mosque over 1,300 years ago...

1663546.title: “Giving and Giving”
1663546.description: A photo collage of various gifts handed out personally by the Rebbe, accompanied by a special recording of the Niggun, “Shir Mizmor.”

1663547.title: Did You Light Shabbat Candles?
1663547.description: The Rebbe, Rabbi Menachem Mendel Schneerson, of righteous memory, encourages Jewish women and girls to light Shabbat candles.

1663548.title: Healing Light
1663548.description: A miraculous account of the power of the Shabbos lights (1957).

1663550.title: “Fill the World and Conquer It”
1663550.description: “Fill the world and conquer it.” This commandment is directed to every Jew: Do not think that only when you’re in the synagogue or Yeshiva are you on a mission from G-d, to study Torah and fulfill Mitzvos...

1663551.title: Conference of Emissaries - 1989
1663551.description: The Rebbe joins the Shluchim and their supporters for Afternoon Prayers at 770 on the final day of the Second International Conference of Shluchim.

1663552.title: Think Even Bigger!
1663552.description: See to it that your Chabad House building is even bigger than you need for your activities now. That way it will challenge you every day: Why have you not yet filled the entire building with activities?!

1663553.title: “There Are No Jews in Madagascar”
1663553.description: Rabbi Yosef Wineberg worked for the central Lubavitcher Yeshiva, and traveled on numerous missions for the Previous Rebbe and the Rebbe over his 60 years of service. In 1955, the Rebbe asked him to visit Madagascar in search of fellow Jews.

1686483.title: Your Deeper Mission
1686483.description: My father-in-law, the Rebbe, charged each individual with a specific mission designed to strengthen Judaism. One must keep in mind however, the words of the Zohar: “One layer of shell covers another layer of shell…”

1686484.title: Niggun “Rosh Chodesh Kislev”
1686484.description: Chasidim sing a joyous Niggun, as the Rebbe distributes dollars to the Mitzvah Tankists.

1686485.title: His Chasidim Need Him
1686485.description: An assistant to the Gerer Rebbe requests a blessing for the Gerer Rebbe’s health. “Tell him he needs to be well for the Jewish People’s sake. His activities for them will increase his health. You need not come to me... Chasidim must demand it of their own Rebbe himself.”

1686486.title: Tools of the Trade
1686486.description: Before setting out to their post as the Rebbe’s Shluchim to the state of Minnesota in 1962, Rabbi Moshe Feller and his wife, Mindy, had a private audience with the Rebbe.

1686490.title: All of Talmud in One Year
1686490.description: The Alter Rebbe instructed that every Jewish community should study the entire Talmud each year. Therefore, it is customary on Yud Tes Kislev to divide up the study of Talmud.
path: All of Talmud in One Year

1686491.title: Sheva Brachos
1686491.description: Sheva Brachos are held at the Rebbe’s Farbrengen in honor of the marriage of Dr. Larry and Molly Resnik.

1686492.title: Only Simchas!
1686492.description: The Rebbe blesses a family’s bride and Bar Mitzvah boy.

1686493.title: Chasidus for Kids
1686493.description: Rabbi Mordechai Goldschmid’s father, Reb Nochum, grew up with the Rebbe and his brothers in Dnepropetrovsk, Ukraine (circa 1917).

1686495.title: Chabad: What Is Chassidus?
1686495.description:
After his liberation from Czarist prison on the 19th of Kislev, 1798, the Alter Rebbe
recounted that the souls of his masters, the Baal Shem Tov and Maggid of Mezritch, had
visited him in prison, explaining that his ordeal on earth was the result of a decree against him in Heaven above, because of his widespread dissemination of Chasidic teachings. When he asked if he should stop teaching, his masters replied: “On the contrary. Your liberation from prison will be the Heavenly sign that you must not only continue, you must increase!”

1686496.title: Tanya Distribution
1686496.description: The Rebbe distributes Tanyas in honor of Yud Tes Kislev, “Rosh Hashanah of Chasidus.”

1686497.title: 192 Years of Chabad Chasidus
1686497.description: The Rebbe is presented with 192 Tanyas, newly-printed in different locations.

1686498.title: Perceiving the Roots
1686498.description: Rabbi Binyomin Klein was a member of the Rebbe’s secretariat for 30 years. He shares two stories of the Rebbe’s unique ability to see to the root of things.

1686501.title: Children’s Rally
1686501.description: A special Chanukah Rally bringing together Jewish Yeshiva and public school children.

1686502.title: Chanukah, the Day After
1686502.description: “After the eighth day of Chanukah we stop lighting the candles. But as far as Mitzvos are concerned, the ninth day must bring an added Mitzvah, and the tenth day another new Mitzvah — constantly increasing and growing.”

1686503.title: On the Borderline
1686503.description:
Rabbi Meir Schlesinger is the founder of Yeshivat Sha’alvim in Israel, where he served as Rosh
Yeshiva for over 30 years (reflections from the 1960s).

1720319.title: The Chicken and the Egg
1720319.description: Maimonides rules in his Laws of Partnerships: If one person owns eggs, and another has chickens, and the two enter into a partnership for the latter’s chickens to warm the eggs until they hatch, the eventual profits are to be divided between them. Until then, the egg-owner must provide food and compensation to the chicken farmer.

1720321.title: One People, One Torah
1720321.description: A discussion in English about a common standard for conversion, and Ben-Gurion’s vision of a united Jewish people living in the Land of Israel.

1720322.title: Look for the Unifying Force
1720322.description: Rabbi Shmuel Lew recalls a simple, yet powerful, formula for Jewish unity, taught to him by the Rebbe (in the year 1974).

1720324.title: What Every Jewish Community Needs
