1720324.description: It is imperative that in every Jewish community a library be established – a place where books of Torah can be found — simple books for those with a basic knowledge of Judaism, as well as deeper ones for those at an advanced level of Torah study.

1720325.title: Didan Notzach
1720325.description: Chasidim celebrate the ruling of the US Court of Appeals, upholding Agudas Chasidei Chabad’s ownership of the Previous Rebbe’s library.

1720326.title: Keep the Presses Running
1720326.description: The Rebbe encourages the publishing of Torah books.

1720327.title: Torah to the People
1720327.description: Rabbi Meir Wunder was a senior librarian at Hebrew University’s National Library. During the 1960s, he managed the extensive Torah library at the Ponevezh Yeshiva in Bnei Brak, which inspired him to help found a central organization for Torah libraries (from a 1970 encounter).

1720330.title: The Road to Peace: Part 1
1720330.description: Code of Jewish Law, Laws of Shabbos, Chapter 329: If non-Jews besiege a Jewish border town—whether in the Holy Land or in the Diaspora—stating that they come only to pilfer straw, Jews are obligated to arm themselves for war, even on Shabbos, because such an intrusion opens up the entire Jewish land to attack.

1720331.title: Moshiach Now
1720331.description: In 1987, the Rebbe spoke about the need for Jews to demand of G-d that it is high time for Moshiach to arrive. The next day, a group of rabbis, led by Rabbi Yehuda Kalman Marlow of the Crown Heights Beis Din, present a halachic ruling on the matter.

1720332.title: The “Minchas Elazar”
1720332.description: Various discussions surrounding the personality of Rabbi Chaim Elazar Shapira of Munkatch, author of the Halachic work, “Minchas Elazar.”

1720333.title: The Rebbe Discusses Israeli Aviation
1720333.description: In 1977, while training in the United States together with a group of fellow IAF pilots, Mr. Herzl Makov visited the Rebbe.

1720335.title: The Road to Peace: Part 2
1720335.description: The nations of the world are watching and waiting: “When will Jews begin to say what they’re really thinking about the Land of Israel?” When a Jew starts talking diplomatic jargon, begging the nations to take more and more land, thinking that in this way he’ll find favor in their eyes – the non-Jew doesn’t believe him, because he’s not talking like a Jew.

1720336.title: Nigun “Kol Dodi”
1720336.description: The translated lyrics of this chassidic melody are: “Hark! My beloved is knocking: Open for me, my beloved, my dove, my perfect one.” (Song of Songs 5:2)

1720337.title: A Land of Only Good
1720337.description:
Rabbi Simcha Ashlag visits the Rebbe:
“It is impossible for there to be any ‘bad’ in the Land of Israel. May there be revealed and obvious good, with peace of body and mind to study Torah’s revealed and inner dimensions.”

1720338.title: Once a Leader, Always a Leader
1720338.description: Israeli Major-General Yehoshua Sagi served as director of AMAN, Israel’s Military Intelligence, from 1979 to 1983. His first audience with the Rebbe took place in the early 1980s.
path: Once a Leader, Always a Leader

1744431.title: Rabbeinu Tam Tefillin
1744431.description: According to the Arizal, donning Rabbeinu Tam Tefillin is a law, not a custom. The question of “custom” is only whether to don them after Rashi Tefillin or at the same time, but the Arizal holds that all Jewish men are obligated to don both pairs.

1744432.title: Talis and Tefillin
1744432.description: The Rebbe in Talis and Tefillin, during Morning Prayers.

1744433.title: Like an Engine
1744433.description: A human is like an engine – if you overdo it you can burn it out, but if you underuse it, it gets sluggish. Never be satisfied just with past accomplishments – but don’t let the fact that you are not satisfied affect your health.

1744434.title: Rabbeinu Tam Tefillin
1744434.description: Rabbi Leibel Schapiro is Rosh Yeshiva of the Yeshiva Gedolah of Miami. He recalls some of the Rebbe’s special instructions to him when he first started to don Rabbeinu Tam Tefillin (in 1965).

1744436.title: Mission of the Generation, Part 1: “Yosef”
1744436.description: Rachel named her son ‘Joseph,’ as a prayer: “May G-d add to me a different son.” The Tzemach Tzedek explains: Rachel prayed that Joseph have the ability to transform someone “different” – someone far from G-dliness, into a “son” – someone righteous, like himself.

1744437.title: 20th Yahrtzeit: Vintage footage of 10 Shevat, 5730 (1970)
1744437.description: Vintage footage of the Rebbe’s Farbrengen in honor of the 20th Yahrtzeit of his father-in-law and predecessor, Rabbi Yosef Yitzchak Schneersohn of Lubavitch.

1744438.title: Super-Connected
1744438.description: If someone is autistic, it doesn’t mean that they don’t relate to anyone. They might not relate well to people, but to G‑d they relate as well as everyone else, and even more. Place a charity box in his room. This will benefit him, and he’ll remind his visitors that they must give charity.

1744439.title: Never Give Up On a G-dly Spark
1744439.description: Professor Reuven Feuerstein, a world-renowned Israeli clinical and developmental cognitive psychologist, discusses some of the Rebbe’s influence on his life’s work.
path: Never Give Up On a G-dly Spark

1744442.title: Mission of the Generation, Pt. 2: “Yitzchak”
1744442.description: The Previous Rebbe’s lifelong tireless efforts for Jewish youth are well-known. First in Eastern Europe, then in America, he succeeded in drawing the hearts of the younger generation back to their age-old Jewish heritage.

1744443.title: New Year for Trees
1744443.description: The Rebbe distributes fruits at a Farbrengen on Tu B’Shevat, New Year for Trees.

1744444.title: A Fruitful Tu B’Shevat
1744444.description: “Take back all the ‘good fruit’ from the New Year of Trees, for all of Australia. May it ultimately be ‘A land of wheat and barley and grapes and figs and pomegranates, a land of olive oil and honey’ – with all the spiritual connotations.”

1744445.title: Plant Your Vineyard
1744445.description: Rabbi Nachman Bernhard served the largest Jewish congregation in South Africa for over three decades. Before taking the job, he had actually planned to leave the rabbinate. That was when he had his first private audience with the Rebbe…(in the year 1964)

1744448.title: In Loving Memory
1744448.description: On the eve of the first Yahrzeit of his wife, Rebbetzin Chaya Mushka Schneerson, of blessed memory, the Rebbe distributes dollars at his home on President Street.

1744449.title: Blessings to the Shluchos
1744449.description: Blessings to the Shluchos who came in from around the world in honor of the first Yahrzeit of the Rebbe’s wife, Rebbetzin Chaya Mushka Schneerson, of blessed memory, and to attend the N’shei Chabad Jewish women’s convention in New York.

1744450.title: The Jewish Performing Arts
1744450.description: Mrs. Leah Gniwisch lives in Montreal, Canada. Each year from 1963 to 1974, she directed a Jewish musical for the women and girls of the community.

1775201.title: 20/20 Foresight
1775201.description: It’s a dangerous mistake to entrust Israel’s security to surrounding Arab governments. Their leadership structure is entirely unstable.

1775202.title: Nigun “Hosheia Es Amecha”
1775202.description: Melody lyrics (English translation): “Deliver Your people and bless your heritage; tend them and exalt them forever.” (Psalms 28:9)

1775203.title: Uniting Jews in Israel Saves Jews Worldwide
1775203.description: “One supernatural way to help Jews trapped in hostile countries is to ‘consolidate’ all Jews in Israel around the cause of Torah and Mitzvos. This will unite them to greet Moshiach and to receive all good tidings, and it will hasten the success of all your efforts.”
path: Uniting Jews in Israel Saves Jews Worldwide

1775204.title: Secret Weapon
1775204.description: Rabbi David Bouskila translated the Tanya into Arabic thinking that he would enable Jews from Arabic-speaking countries to learn about G-d. Little did he know, he was stepping into the middle of an age-old cosmic battle and turning the tides of the war... (1980)

1775206.title: Redemption, a Process
1775206.description: Maimonides rules in his Laws of Kings about the times of Moshiach: “Do not think that the world will undergo miraculous changes. The world will continue according to the natural order. And prophecies such as, ‘The wolf shall dwell with the lamb,’ are metaphors.”

1775207.title: First Siyum HaRambam
1775207.description: Completion of the first study cycle of Maimonides’ code of Jewish law, the Mishneh Torah.

1775208.title: Home is Where the Heart Is
1775208.description:
“The Baal Shem Tov teaches: ‘Wherever a person’s thoughts are, that’s where he is present.’
In the Laws of Eruv Techumin, the Techum is established based upon where you have in mind, not necessarily where you physically stand. Although you are here in America, your thoughts are, no doubt, in the Land of Israel. Draw Israel’s holiness upon the people here in the Diaspora.”
path: Home is Where the Heart Is

1775209.title: To Be Connected
1775209.description: In the early 1970s, Rabbi Meir Tzvi Gruzman sought the Rebbe’s advice on motivating the students of his Tomchei Temimim Yeshiva in their study of Talmud.

1775212.title: A Jew is a Jew
1775212.description: There are some who believe that by hiding their Jewishness they will be protected from anti-Semitism. The Megillah teaches us a lesson: When Haman persuaded King Achashverosh to issue the decree against the Jewish people, he argued that...

1775213.title: Chasidic Medley
1775213.description: At the end of the Purim Farbrengen, the Rebbe requests a medley of lively Chasidic Nigunim.

1775214.title: To Life
1775214.description: “Frame your grandfather’s will and hang it in your bedroom. It will remind you of his good deeds and help you increase your own good deeds as well.”

1775215.title: So Far, Yet So Close
1775215.description: Rabbi Shmuel Chefer, director of the Beis Rivkah Teachers’ Seminary in Kfar Chabad, Israel, recounts a heartwarming story about what it truly means to be “close” to the Rebbe (1968).

1775217.title: A Higher Standard of Writing
1775217.description:
If a person has been blessed by G-d with the talent and ability to write a book, no matter what
the book’s storyline is, it must communicate to the reader the awareness that “There is a
Master of this palace” – that Someone is in charge of this turbulent world.

1775219.title: Profits, Not Opinions
1775219.description:
“Taking money from outside investors definitely helps, but only if they will not have a say in
running the actual business. If they share in some of the profits that’s okay, but do not
relinquish any control of the business itself.”

1775220.title: Returning a Lost Art
1775220.description:
In 1964, Baruch Nachshon had his first private audience with the Rebbe. An aspiring artist
who had recently returned to his Jewish roots, the Rebbe commissioned him with the historic
task of reviving an ancient “art form.”

1804971.title: Parent and Protector
1804971.description:
The fact that a parent feeds and clothes a child does not mean he may do with the child
whatever he wants… The parent himself is a possession of G-d; how much more so their child,
who is only entrusted to the parent for safekeeping. There is only one path – the straight path,
the path of life: to educate them and raise them to Torah, marriage and good deeds.

1804972.title: Machne Israel Development Fund
1804972.description: A meeting with the members of the Machne Israel Development Fund.

1804973.title: Tel Aviv
1804973.description:
Spring is the beginning of growth for the entire year. “Tel Aviv,” however, reflects the “Tel –
Heights” of “Aviv – Spring.”

1804974.title: Hiding and Seeking
1804974.description:
Reb Chonye Morosow served as a personal secretary to the fifth and sixth Lubavitcher Rebbes
in Russia. His son, Reb Mendel, was born in 1916, and recalls two episodes in the Rebbes’
homes.

1804976.title: Publishing “Hemshech Ayin Beis”
1804976.description:
The fifth Chabad Rebbe’s Chasidic discourses from the year 5672 to 5676 (1912–1915) are renowned to
Chasidim as ‘Hemshech Ayin Beis – The 5672 Series.’

1804977.title: The Mitzvah Tankists
1804977.description: The Rebbe distributes dollars to the Mitzvah Tankists at the conclusion of a Farbrengen.

1804978.title: Hoping for a Shorter Passover
1804978.description: “Thank you for your book on the Laws of Passover. Moshiach should come; then you won’t need to write anymore about the laws that apply in the Diaspora.”

1804979.title: Working Through Others
1804979.description: Rabbi Don Yoel Levy is director of the OK Kosher Certification. During the early 1960s, his father, Rabbi Berel Levy, was privy to the Rebbe’s methods of working with other Jewish movements.

1804981.title: Celebrate with Humility
1804981.description: Arrogance is the root of all undesirable traits. How, then, can we allow people to gather here in order to honor an individual?

1804982.title: Birthday Blessings
1804982.description: Chasidim bless the Rebbe on his 86th birthday.

1804983.title: Budgets Shouldn’t be Smooth
1804983.description: “In the United States it’s a healthy sign when there’s a problem with the budget. When the budget is too smooth, it means there are no activities... May G-d Almighty bless you to see the situation differently, with joy, and that will bring much more success also.”

1804984.title: How the Rebbe Bought Us Passover Dishes
1804984.description: Where is a young couple to turn when they can’t afford their Passover expenses? Mrs. Esther Mentz tells a heartwarming story of kindness and sensitivity (in the year 1957).
path: How the Rebbe Bought Us Passover Dishes

1804986.title: "Why Am I Different?"
1804986.description: The Passover Seder begins with the child’s question: “Why is this night different from all other nights?” Fundamentally, the question bothering the child is: “Why am I different from children of all other nations?”

1804987.title: Nigun “V’hi Sheomdah”
1804987.description:
Song lyrics: “This is what has stood by our fathers and us! For not just one alone has risen against us to
destroy us, but in every generation they rise against us to destroy us; and the Holy One, blessed be He, saves us from their hand!” (The Passover Haggadah)

1804988.title: Got Shmura?
1804988.description: “Even if someone eats ordinary Matza in his own home, still you should not offer him non-Shmura Matza at your table. Try to influence them so that even after they return home, they continue to eat Shmura Matza all Passover round.”

1804989.title: Balanced Rebuke
1804989.description: Rabbi Yisroel Gordon’s father, Reb Yochanan Gordon, studied at the Tomchei Temimim Yeshiva in Lubavitch, Russia, in the early 1910s. His father would recall an insightful lesson he was taught by the Yeshiva’s director, the future Sixth Rebbe, Rabbi Yosef Yitzchak (circa 1912).

1827326.title: G-d’s Law for All People
1827326.description: Maimonides rules that a non-Jew must keep the Seven Noahide Laws, not because he agrees with them intellectually, but because they were commanded to him by G-d, through Moses at Sinai.

1827327.title: Farewell Yechidus
1827327.description: Farewell audience for guests who travelled from abroad to spend Passover with the Rebbe.

1827328.title: One Hundred and One Percent
1827328.description: “When it comes to educating Jews, ‘trying’ is not enough. You must ‘try’ at least 101 times!”

1827329.title: We Checked Already!
1827329.description: What does it mean when the Rebbe gives you the same advice three times in a row? And how many times must you check your Mezuzos anyway? (1992)

1827331.title: Life on the Edge
1827331.description: When a person is involved in Torah study, he need not be cautioned to avoid unholy preoccupations. But when it comes to a Jew’s mundane affairs, on the surface they are activities that non-Jews engage in as well. Here, the Jew must know that Torah draws a line of distinction – and this is a total, absolute divide.

1827332.title: Nigun “Lechatchila Ariber”
1827332.description: Chasidim sing a favorite Nigun of Rabbi Shmuel of Lubavitch, the Rebbe Maharash

1827333.title: “The Land Which G-d’s Eyes are Upon”
1827333.description: “The Land of Israel is ‘The Land which G-d’s eyes are upon from the beginning of the year until the end.’ I tell everyone that it is safe to travel there. Someone who is already there is forbidden by Jewish law from leaving. And those who planned to travel there, but cancel their plans, will be perceived by others as having violated Jewish Law.”
path: “The Land Which G-d’s Eyes are Upon”

1827334.title: The Highest Calling
1827334.description: Rabbi Avraham Leizerson is chairman of Chinuch Atzmai, the independent religious education system in Israel (1992).

1827336.title: Nature and Nurture
1827336.description: Every child has natural inborn traits, some positive, some negative. These often become apparent in the earliest stages of childhood. It is the parent’s sacred duty to caution the child against the negative ones and to teach him discipline

1827337.title: Nigun “Ki V’Simcha”
1827337.description: The Rebbe starts a lively Nigun at the conclusion of a Farbrengen.

1827338.title: Never Too Late
1827338.description: “The Second Passover teaches us that ‘It’s never too late.’ The holiday was given for those who were unable to offer the original Passover sacrifice in its proper time. They thought that it was too late, and yet they were told that there is a solution. So too, in any area of life, if there are things you should have done in the past but did not, it’s never too late to make them up now.”

1827339.title: The Joy of Children, Part 1
1827339.description: Just three days before her wedding, a bride declares her wishes to call off the marriage... (circa 1957)

1827341.title: Rabbi Shimon’s Joy
1827341.description: On Lag B’omer, Rabbi Shimon ben Yochai proclaimed: “This is the day of my rejoicing!” He also requested every Jew to share in his joy, so his own delight is increased when he sees many Jews rejoicing together.

1827342.title: Lag B’omer Parade
1827342.description: Vintage footage of the 1957 Lag B’omer Parade in front of 770.

1827343.title: Architecture with Soul
1827343.description: “Much success in your building project near the monument of Rabbi Shimon ben Yochai in Meron, Israel. Your work to establish a Sephardic Studies program at Yeshiva University is also ‘building’ — not of stones, but of souls.”

1827344.title: The Joy of Children, Part 2
1827344.description: The doctors promised her she would never have a single child. The Rebbe promised her she would have many! (circa 1957)

1854584.title: Living the Torah
1854584.description: Torah is “Our life, and the length of our days.” It is not possible for something to be called ‘living’ if it’s alive only at certain times of the day, week or year. Life is constant at all times, and without pause.

1854585.title: L'chaim!
1854585.description: During a lively nigun at the Yud Beis Tammuz farbrengen, the Rebbe invites the JEM camera crew to join in saying L’chaim.

1854586.title: Blessing Within the Natural Order
1854586.description: “You have my blessing for your product to be approved by the city council. But a committee is composed of human beings. If someone there will be acquainted with your project beforehand, it will probably help make the approval process easier and more speedy.”

1854587.title: Judaism in Color
1854587.description: In 1973, Mr. David Stauber accompanied his wife and father-in-law to an audience with the Rebbe. Although he thought he had no personal interest in the meeting, he came out a new Jew.

1854589.title: You Are What You Eat
1854589.description: The food a person eats transforms into his very flesh and blood. One’s character is therefore shaped by what he allows into his mouth. Consuming the meat of a predatory animal, for example, ingrains the trait of cruelty into one’s chemical makeup.

1854590.title: Aliyah
1854590.description: The Rebbe is called to the Torah at 770.

1854591.title: Healthy Living
1854591.description: “May G-d bless you by healing all your patients. Then you can focus on practicing preventive medicine for healthy people. Instruct your patients about kosher diet and lifestyle, which will bring them G-d Almighty’s blessings.”

1854592.title: Healthy Soul, Healthy Body
1854592.description: Rabbi Yekusiel Farkash is a prominent halachic authority living in Jerusalem, Israel. An amazing story of how the Rebbe’s advice saved his doctor-friend’s wife from fatal illness, through a change of diet (circa 1975).

1854595.title: The Day the Heavens Opened
1854595.description: The Jewish people studied Torah and observed its precepts long before they actually became obligated in them at Sinai. Moreover, the Ten Commandments were composed largely of laws already commanded to the non-Jewish world. What, then, was so important about the giving of the Torah at Sinai?

1854596.title: Kiddush Levanah
1854596.description: Sanctification of the New Moon outside the Rebbe’s home on President Street.

1854597.title: Holy Ads
1854597.description: “Much success in your international Torah contest. The Torah booklets you distribute also have advertisements inside them, so you must add cautionary notes throughout the publication to remind the reader that it is a holy book and must be handled respectfully.”

1854598.title: Healthy Soul, Healthy Body
1854598.description: Rabbi Yekusiel Farkash relates a sequel to the story of his friend’s wife’s miraculous healing (circa late-1970s).

1854600.title: Shabbat & Blessings for Livelihood
1854600.description:
We live in a time of great freedom and prosperity for Jews. However, we must always keep
in mind that it is not the “Strength and might of my own hand which has earned me this
wealth,” but rather, “It is G-d’s blessing that brings riches.”

1854601.title: Kos Shel Brachah
1854601.description: The Rebbe distributes wine from the cup of the After-blessing, as chasidim sing a nigun honoring the Tefilin and Shabbos-candle campaigns.

1854602.title: Charity and Shabbos in the Financial Sector
1854602.description:
Install a charity box at your bank, and place my dollar inside it. May G-d Almighty bless you
to have many other banks imitate your bank’s charity box and observance of Shabbos.”
path: Charity and Shabbos in the Financial Sector

1854603.title: Ten Hour Flight, One Hour Mission
1854603.description: Rabbi Israel Haber, a decorated former U.S. Air Force chaplain, was stationed in Alaska during the 1970s. In 1980, two years after making aliyah with his family, the Rebbe asked him to visit Alaska again, “at least for one hour.” (circa 1980)
path: Ten Hour Flight, One Hour Mission

1878839.title: Fundraising Manifesto
1878839.description: Jewish Federations play a valiant role in the collection of funds for Jewish causes worldwide. With this comes the enormous responsibility of allocating the funds appropriately.

1878840.title: Children’s Rally
1878840.description: Rabbi JJ Hecht leads the children in bestowing the Priestly Blessing upon the Rebbe, followed by the singing of the Tzivos Hashem song, We Want Moshiach Now!

1878841.title: Do Not Fear
1878841.description: “There are Jews who are frightened about going to Israel, and they are frightening others as well. Publicize that you’re going and that there is nothing to fear. It is actually the safest place because it is the location of the Holy Temple.”

1878842.title: The Shlichus Will Find You
1878842.description: Rabbi Yitzchok Sufrin is an administrator of the Lubavitch Foundation in the United Kingdom. His dream, however, was to be a Shliach, battling on the front lines for Yiddishkeit...

1878844.title: Climbing the Rungs, Side by Side
1878844.description: The customs associated with a yahrzeit are intended to help elevate the soul of the departed. But how does this apply to the soul of a tzaddik, which achieves continuous spiritual elevation on its own merit?
path: Climbing the Rungs, Side by Side

1878845.title: Sunday Dollars
1878845.description: The Rebbe distributes dollars to be given for charity, at his home on President Street, during the year of mourning after his wife, Rebbetzin Chaya Mushka Schneerson, of blessed memory.

1878846.title: All Together
1878846.description: “Thank you for your blessings. Most important, however, is that they include the entire Jewish people.”

1878847.title: A Shabbos Afternoon in Mexico
1878847.description: Professor Shlomo Eckstein is the former President and Rector of Bar Ilan University in Tel Aviv. He shares an insight the Rebbe gave him in his youth, which he has carried with him throughout his lifelong career in education (circa 1953).

1878849.title: Connected
1878849.description: One might assume that after a tzaddik has ascended on high and experienced unlimited Divine revelation, he would no longer concern himself with matters of this physical world. For the Rebbe, however, such calculations don’t apply.

1878850.title: The Ohel
1878850.description: The Rebbe brings petitions for blessing to the resting place of his father-in-law and predecessor, Rabbi Yosef Yitzchak Schneersohn of Lubavitch.

1878851.title: The Sky is Not the Limit
1878851.description: “The main partnership of every Jew is in spiritual activities, spiritual business; in addition to that, one can also have a partnership in material business. But Jews’ partnership together must be total and complete — I’m not happy when I hear Jews describe that they are partners with each other ‘to a certain extent.’ Even the sky is not the limit!”
path: The Sky is Not the Limit

1878852.title: The Basics
1878852.description: With all the complex challenges of life, it’s easy to search for complex solutions, overlooking the basics of success. Reb Aaron Dalfin shares two illuminating interactions with the Rebbe (the early 1960's)

1878854.title: “Vine of Israel”
1878854.description:
After the Rebbe’s liberation from Soviet-imposed exile, he delivered a Chasidic discourse
expounding the verse: “You caused a vine to journey out of Egypt; You expelled nations and implanted it.” The Sages explain that just as a vine is uprooted from its place and replanted elsewhere in order to grow more plentifully, likewise, when G-d moves a Jew to a new location, it is only in order to increase his success.

1878855.title: “Ech Ti Zimlak”
1878855.description: The Rebbe asks Cantor Tzvi Tzatzkes to sing the Russian version of “Who knows One.”

1878856.title: Persecution in the Past; Unity Today
1878856.description: “Jews and Blacks both suffered great persecution in history. From now on, may every one of us, and all the population of the United States, have only good news and healthy news, in all matters of goodness and kindness.”
path: Persecution in the Past; Unity Today

1878857.title: Leningrad On the Line
1878857.description:
Professor Herman Branover is a world-renowned physicist. Living as a refusnik in Leningrad in
1972, he found the phone number to 770 in the inside page of a Jewish prayer book...(circa 1972)

1900545.title: Rebuild it, and They will Come
1900545.description: The prayers for the fast of 17 Tammuz begin: “Permit G-d no silence, until He sets and establishes Jerusalem as the praise of the earth." The Rebbe asks 'How can we challenge G-d?'
path: Rebuild it, and They will Come

1900546.title: Fast Day Haftarah
1900546.description: The Rebbe recites the Haftarah during Afternoon Prayers of the Fast of Tammuz.

1900547.title: Unity Politics
1900547.description: “America must not only become stronger, it must become more united, as emphasized by its very name: The United States. May G-d Almighty bless you to be active in this direction, not only among Jews, but among non-Jews as well.”

1900548.title: A Visit to the Sick
1900548.description: Rabbi Nissen Mangel recalls a story about his father-in-law, to whom the Rebbe paid a personal visit in the hospital (circa early-1970's)

1900551.title: Creatures of Holiness
1900551.description: The Sages instruct us in Ethics of Our Fathers: “Be of the disciples of Aaron the High Priest.” Aaron was the holiest Jew. Yet, which of his qualities do the Sages instruct us to emulate? “Love peace and pursue peace; love all creatures and draw them close to Torah.”

1900552.title: Nigun “Yehi Ratzon”
1900552.description:
“May it be Your will, L-rd our G-d and G-d of our fathers, that the Holy Temple be rebuilt
speedily in our days, and grant us our portion in Your Torah.” (From the Amida Prayer)

1900553.title: Rebbe of Rebbes
1900553.description: Visits by Rabbi Yosef Dovid Teitelbaum, Sossover Rebbe of Israel, and by Rabbi Ben Zion Hager, Zobeltover Rebbe.

1900554.title: Jewish Nationalism
1900554.description: An excerpt from a recently discovered 1969 recording of Prime Minister Ariel Sharon describing his second private audience with the Rebbe.

1900556.title: The Charity Campaign
1900556.description: We live in a time when many Jews – due to no fault of their own – are not aware of Judaism. Therefore, a campaign was launched to ensure that every Jewish home should have a charity box. In this way, even a person uneducated in Judaism who encounters this unfamiliar object will ask what it is about. This will lead him to discover the commandment of charity, which, in turn, will lead him to fulfill many more Mitzvos.

1900557.title: Coins to Children
1900557.description: On his way to visit the resting place of his father-in-law and predecessor, the Rebbe distributes coins to children to be given for charity.

1900558.title: Chicago’s Loop of Blessing
1900558.description: Blessings and directives to a supporter of Chabad of “The Loop” in Chicago.

1900559.title: Mezuzah Delivery
1900559.description: Reb Chaim Meir and Faige Minkowitz recall the tribulations of her four-day labor, and the Rebbe’s unorthodox “medical” advice (circa 1952).

1900561.title: Prerequisite to Torah Study
1900561.description: It was taught in the school of Elijah the prophet: “Anyone who studies Jewish law every day is assured a place in the World to Come, as the verse says ‘halichos olam lo’ – the ways of the world are his;’ do not read it ‘halichos – ways of the world,’ but rather ‘halachos – Jewish law.’” – Making Jewish law your own makes the Next World yours as well.

1900562.title: Nigun “Tzomah L’cha Nafshi”
1900562.description:
Song lyrics: “My soul thirsts for You, my flesh longs for You; (as one) in a desolate and dry land without
water, so (I thirst) to see You in the Sanctuary, to behold Your might and glory.” (Psalm 63)

1900563.title: Yerushalayim Post
1900563.description: The publishers of The Jerusalem Post visit the Rebbe: “May G-d Almighty bless you to be successful in reporting real news, not only from ‘Jerusalem, ’but ‘Yerushalayim, the Holy City.’ And may you announce in The Jerusalem Post when Moshiach arrives there.”

1900564.title: A Symbiotic People
1900564.description: Yitzchak Rabin served as Israel’s ambassador to the United States from 1968 to 1973. In 1972, Ambassador Yehuda Avner accompanied Rabin to pay Israel’s respects to the Rebbe in honor of his 70th birthday.

1923538.title: "In a Place Devoid of Men, Strive to Be a Man"
1923538.description: My father served as chief rabbi of Dnipropetrovsk, a major city in Ukraine, which supplied wheat to large parts of Russia. When the time came to prepare flour for matzah, people flocked from the surrounding areas seeking flour that was certified kosher for Passover.
path: "In a Place Devoid of Men, Strive to Be a Man"

1923539.title: Yahrzeit Prayers
1923539.description: The Rebbe leads the Morning Prayers at 770 on the 19th yahrzeit of his mother, Rebbetzin

1923540.title: Forty Years of Torah
1923540.description: Ashkenazic Chief Rabbi of Mexico, Avraham Hershberg, discusses the Rebbe’s newest campaigns, and ways to honor the Rebbe’s father on his 40th yahrzeit.

1923541.title: You Will Survive
1923541.description: Mr. Israel Adamski grew up in Dniepropetrovsk, Ukraine, and attended underground Torah classes taught by the Rebbe’s father, Rabbi Levi Yitzchok Schneerson. Here, he recalls Reb Levik’s prophetic words to him shortly before the outbreak of World War II.

1923543.title: Big Business
1923543.description: An address to the entrepreneurs of the Machne Israel Development Fund: The word ‘development’ does not describe the process of creating something from scratch; it means taking that which already exists and maximizing it to its fullest potential.

1923545.title: Not for the Honor of Flesh and Blood
1923545.description: “For G-d A-lmighty there are no problems. May you have good news all year round. And your increased pledge to charity should be in honor of G-d Himself, not me.”
path: Not for the Honor of Flesh and Blood

1923546.title: The Place Where All Worries Melt
1923546.description: Mrs. Rochel Pinson, head Shlucha of Tunisia since 1960, recalls how the Rebbe was sometimes the lone source of calm amidst the challenges.
path: The Place Where All Worries Melt

1923548.title: Spiritual Motherhood
1923548.description: The Talmud teaches: “Let that man be remembered for good, and Rabbi Yehoshua ben Gamla is his name. Until he came, only children with fathers had the opportunity to study Torah, whereas orphans did not. But Rabbi Yehoshua established Torah schools in every province and city for all children, even as young as six and seven.”

1923549.title: Jewish Women’s Convention
1923549.description: The Rebbe addresses the annual pre-Rosh Hashanah Jewish women’s convention at 770.

1923550.title: Don’t Lose Sight of Your Blessings
1923550.description: “Although your yeshivah is experiencing financial difficulties, this is certainly no time to downsize. On the contrary, your students are your greatest help from Above!” (December, 1990)
path: Don’t Lose Sight of Your Blessings

1923551.title: Quantity is Quality
1923551.description: Rabbi Shmuel Chefer, director of the Beis Rivkah Teachers’ Seminary in Kfar Chabad, Israel, shares a fundamental perspective of the Rebbe on building a successful educational institution (circa 1960).

1923553.title: The Palace and the Field
1923553.description: The Alter Rebbe gives a parable concerning the month of Elul: Throughout this month, G-d, so-to-speak, is like a king who stands in the field outside his royal city, where he greets all his subjects with a loving countenance.

1923554.title: Rostover Nigun
1923554.description: Chasidim sing a favorite nigun of the fifth Rebbe of Chabad, Rabbi Sholom Dovber Schneersohn, in preparation for the Rebbe’s delivery of a new chasidic discourse.

1923555.title: Increase in Love
1923555.description:
US Senator Alfonse D’Amato visits the Rebbe shortly after the Crown Heights riots
“Much success in all your endeavors for the peace and security of all the people of the United
States. ‘Amato’ means ‘love’ in Italian. Proceed in your work with inner love, and the entire
population of New York will respond to you and your colleagues with true love as well.”

1923556.title: The Soul Hears
1923556.description:
uring the 1980s, renowned podiatrist Dr. Elliot Udell would treat the Rebbe and Rebbetzin at
their home on President Street. One time, he shared with the Rebbe an experience he had of
a Chabad Shliach’s outreach efforts, which he expected would displease the Rebbe...(late 1980s)

1940869.title: Chasidic Coal Miners
1940869.description: My father-in-law, the Rebbe, gives a parable for what it means to be a Chabad Chasid: A miner digs deep into the ground for coal, which provides warmth and light.

1940870.title: Children’s Rally
1940870.description: The Rebbe participates in a rally at 770 for children returning home from summer camp.

1940871.title: Chasidic Teachings within the Curriculum
1940871.description: The Belzer Rebbe, Rabbi Yissachar Dov Rokeach, visits the Rebbe “Your newspaper recently began to include chasidic teachings. If you are now providing the laymen with regular doses of chasidus, perhaps it’s also time to provide the yeshivah students with regular study sessions in chasidus. Many important innovations have been introduced in our generation, for when new ‘illnesses’ arise, new ‘medicines’ must be administered.”

1940872.title: 200 Years of Hindsight
1940872.description: Detractors to chasidism still point to the Vilna Gaon’s opposition as the basis upon which they rely. But would the Vilna Gaon count himself among them today? (from a 1963 encounter)

1940874.title: The Blessing within the Curse
1940874.description:
The Alter Rebbe would read the Torah in public. One year, he was away during the Torah
reading of Ki Savo, and his young son and future successor, Rabbi Dovber, heard someone else read the portion, which includes G-d’s severe rebuke of the Jewish people. The son became so distressed that he fainted, and weeks later it was still questionable whether he’d be able to fast on Yom Kippur. The chasidim later asked him: “In previous years you didn’t faint; what happened this year?” The boy responded, “When father reads it, I don’t hear curses.”

1940875.title: Selichos
1940875.description: The first night of Selichos at 770.

1940876.title: California Telethon
1940876.description: Several supporters receive the Rebbe’s blessing for the annual telethon by Chabad of the West Coast in Los Angeles, California (Elul, 5750 · September, 1990).

1940877.title: L’chaim, To a Healthy Birth!
1940877.description: When the doctors keep threatening that the baby will be born with a defect, it’s hard not to be terrified, even with the Rebbe’s assurances again, and again, and again, and again... Miriam Haber shares her personal story.

1940879.title: Ten-Day Journey
1940879.description: The prophet Isaiah declares: “Seek G‑d when He can be found, call to Him when He is near.” The Talmud explains: “This refers to the Ten Days of Repentance between Rosh Hashanah and Yom Kippur.”

1940880.title: Hatoras Nedarim
1940880.description: The Rebbe recites the Annulment of Vows on the Eve of Rosh Hashanah.

1940881.title: Facing the New Year with Joy
1940881.description: Rabbi Gavriel Zinner presents the Rebbe with a new book he authored on the Laws of Sukkos.
path: Facing the New Year with Joy

1940882.title: By the Grace of G-d
1940882.description: The importance of two little letters at the top of every page (circa 1967).

1940884.title: One Day, One People
1940884.description:
At the very beginning of Yom Kippur, before Kol Nidrei, we declare: “With the sanction of the
Omnipresent, and with the sanction of the congregation, by authority of the Heavenly Court, and by authority of the earthly court, we hereby grant permission to pray with those who have transgressed.” All agree that on this day, there are no differences between Jews; they all stand united as one in the presence of G-d.

1940885.title: Motzaei Yom Kippur
1940885.description: Havdalah at 770 upon the conclusion of Yom Kippur.

1940886.title: When G-d is Close
1940886.description: “The Talmud explains that one must seek G-d all year round, but during the Ten Days of Repentance, the merit of one single individual is amplified. G-d only asks him to ‘seek’ and to ‘call’ Him, and He will surely grant one’s requests.”

1940887.title: Rosh Hashanah Heirloom
1940887.description: Rabbi Leibel Raskin shares several heartwarming anecdotes from his family’s interactions with the Rebbe’s mother, Rebbetzin Chana Schneerson, of blessed memory.

1974184.title: Just Get it Done!
1974184.description: Of all the Rebbes of Chabad, the fourth Rebbe, Rabbi Shmuel, known as the Rebbe Maharash, was especially known for his supernatural approach to worldly matters – as his famous adage goes: “The world says if you cannot crawl under an obstacle, then try climbing over it. And I say, L’chatchila Ariber! – in the first place go over!”

1974185.title: Nigun “Lechatchila Ariber”
1974185.description: Chasidim sing a favorite nigun of Rabbi Shmuel of Lubavitch, the Rebbe Maharash.

1974186.title: Time to Clean Up
1974186.description: “If the business you are involved in is in the black market, then you should not continue in it. If you cannot get out of it immediately, then do it gradually until you are entirely out.”

1974187.title: Why the Rebbe Snuck Over the Wartime Border
1974187.description: Rabbi Menachem Teichtel was a refugee student in Vichy France during the war. He recounts just how far the Rebbe was willing to go to uphold a Jewish custom during wartime (circa 1940).
path: Why the Rebbe Snuck Over the Wartime Border

1974189.title: Let the World Know
1974189.description: Chabad philosophy teaches that the sukkah—which represents the clouds of glory that sheltered the Jewish people in the desert—is also the revelation of the incense cloud that blanketed the Holy of Holies on Yom Kippur. On Sukkos it is revealed for all to see, even non-Jewish passersby.

1974190.title: The Four Species
1974190.description: During Chol Hamoed Sukkos, the Rebbe shares his Four Species with the Chasidim.

1974191.title: Torah Keeps You Young
1974191.description: “When one studies the Torah of Moses, then, like Moses, one’s ‘vigor does not abate, nor do his eyes dim’ — even to the age of one hundred twenty!”

1974192.title: At the Rebbe’s Table
1974192.description: Rabbi Tuvia Blau is a renowned author and educator. In 1967, he managed to work his way into the Previous Rebbe’s apartment upstairs at 770, and observe the Rebbe’s Simchas Torah meal with the elder Chasidim.

1974195.title: Soldiers on Parade
1974195.description:
In an army, there are certain times when the soldiers are intensively involved in training and
active duty, while at other times they are granted time to rest.

1974196.title: Cup of Blessing
1974196.description: At the conclusion of Simchas Torah, the Rebbe distributes wine from the cup of the Afterblessing.

1974197.title: Education, an Honor and a Responsibility
1974197.description: “Great responsibility brings with it great powers from Above. May you succeed to ‘Educate the child according to his way...’ and merit to see the promise ‘...even as an adult, he will never stray from it.’”
path: Education, an Honor and a Responsibility

1974198.title: Extended Family
1974198.description: Rabbi Dr. Israel Drazin served for over three decades as Assistant Chief of Chaplains of the US Army. The Rebbe taught him that being a Jewish chaplain is not only about ministering to Jews (circa 1986).

1974200.title: The Women First
1974200.description: The Jewish woman plays a crucial part in G-d’s plan for mankind. When Torah was first given, G-d instructed Moses to speak to the women first and explain to them its greatness, thereby strengthening the rest of people’s acceptance of it as well.

1974201.title: Farewell
1974201.description: At the conclusion of the month of Tishrei, the Rebbe bids farewell to the guests from abroad (Tishrei, 5736 · September, 1975).

1974202.title: A Modest Queen
1974202.description:
Bess Myerson, winner of the 1945 Miss America pageant, visits the Rebbe
“Always remember that you are a queen. May G-d Almighty bless you to always have good news and healthy news – and to show a good example for the tznius, the chastity, of all Jewish women and girls.”

1974203.title: Of Love and Marriage
1974203.description: Reb Sholom Goldshmid was a student at 770 during the late 1940s and early 1950s. When it came time to start thinking about dating and marriage, it was the Rebbe who gave him the most important advice of all (c. 1951).

2018698.title: Every Moment Counts
2018698.description: “G-d did not create even one detail of His creation in vain.” The talents and opportunities G-d grants a person in life are meant to be utilized and maximized to the fullest; if one doesn’t do so, the entire order of creation suffers…

2018699.title: Nigun Hachana
2018699.description: Chasidim sing a nigun that is attributed to the Rebbe Rashab as preparation to the Alter Rebbe’s niggun (Daled Bavos).

2018700.title: Don’t Wait for Others
2018700.description: “In the meantime, you’re the leader in the efforts to handle the halachic issues introduced by the influx of Russian immigrants into Israel. Do the best you can and you will inspire others to emulate you.”

2018701.title: Prognosis: Positive
2018701.description: When it’s three doctors against one rabbi, who would you believe? (1973)

2018703.title: The Power of One
2018703.description: “I multiplied Abraham’s seed, and gave him Isaac.” How is the birth of one son the fulfillment of G-d’s promise to multiply Abraham’s seed?

2018705.title: Melt the Ice
2018705.description: “Much success to you and your husband in working together to spread Judaism in Alaska. Don’t grow accustomed to any spiritual ‘coldness’ up there. On the contrary, warm it up!”

2018706.title: Be Sensitive to the Other
2018706.description: When Mrs. Sarah Karmely chose to return to Jewish observance, her husband was resistant. She turned to the Rebbe for guidance (Mid 1980s).

2018708.title: With Every Shliach, Together
2018708.description: The Bible relates that King David coronated his son, Solomon, during his own lifetime. King David, however, continued to rule until his own passing. How can two kings rule simultaneously, especially in light of Torah’s teaching: “There is only one leader to a generation, not two”?

2018709.title: Blessing the Shluchim
2018709.description: After meeting with the members of the Machne Israel Development Fund, the Rebbe blesses the Shluchim who brought their supporters, in the antechamber to his office.

2018710.title: The Special Role of Lay Leaders
2018710.description: The Rebbe encourages lay-leaders of various backgrounds and fields to partner with their Shluchim as exponents of Judaism. 5750 - 5751 (1990 - 1991)
path: The Special Role of Lay Leaders

2018711.title: The Missing Farewell
2018711.description: Rabbi Shabsi Alpern and his wife were among the first to answer the Rebbe’s call to leave Crown Heights for lifelong Shlichus in far-off lands. But when they stopped at 770 on their way to the airport, the Rebbe didn’t show up to say good-bye... (1961)

2018713.title: Love and Unity, the Best Medicine
2018713.description:
The Rebbe speaks from his office, two nights after suffering a massive heart attack:
For certain reasons this talk was delayed until after the Festival... It is, however, being heard now even by fellow Jews who are distant physically, but close spiritually – for the spiritual is what Jews consider most important, especially when this unity is forged through Torah.
path: Love and Unity, the Best Medicine

2018714.title: The Rebbe is Gezunt!
2018714.description: A special presentation in honor of the 35th anniversary of the Rebbe’s recovery from a heart attack in 1977.

2018715.title: A Single Party
2018715.description: The Rebbe discusses with Knesset Member Avraham Werdiger the need for a single united religious front in Israel.

2018716.title: Source of Healing
2018716.description: During Shemini Atzeres hakafos in 1977, the Rebbe suffered a massive heart attack. Dr. Moshe Feldman was a member of the medical team that treated the Rebbe at 770.

2048386.title: Brick and Mortar
2048386.description: Torah relates that the Egyptian exile involved hard labor of “chomer u’leveinim” – mortar and brick. Whatever spiritual refinement G-d intended for the Jewish people through that exile could only be acquired through mortar and brick – otherwise, G-d would never have put them through it.

2048388.title: Bridge the Divide
2048388.description:
Rabbi of the Ashkenazic community in Panama visits the Rebbe
“Panama joins North America to South America. You have the opportunity to join them through Torah!”

2048389.title: On a Tight Schedule
2048389.description: “Knock, knock.” “Who’s there?” “Tefillin delivery from the Lubavitcher Rebbe.” (1961)

2048391.title: Three Innovations, Three Accusations
2048391.description: The Alter Rebbe relates that he was informed of his release from prison as he was reciting the verse in Psalms, “He redeemed my soul in peace from the battle that came upon me, because of the many who were with me.”

2048392.title: Farbrengen
2048392.description: Vintage footage of a 1960s Yud Tes Kislev farbrengen.

2048393.title: The Riches Will Come Along
2048393.description: “Continue to give much charity. And I hope we will finally convince G-d to take us all to Israel. Then we will take all our money there, and give charity there as well.”

2048394.title: The Answer with No Question
2048394.description:
Rabbi Tuvia Blau, a prominent Chabad Chasid, was born into a family of distinguished nonchasidic
origins. After discovering Chabad Chasidism as a student in yeshiva, he wrote to the Rebbe asking for clarification on a number of theological questions. In his response, the Rebbe added the answer to a question Tuvia hadn’t even asked – which turned out to be perhaps the most important answer of all.

2048396.title: Two States of Exile
2048396.description: Joseph had two dreams foretelling his ascendancy over his brothers. Both dreams came true: the ten brothers – including Benjamin – prostrated themselves to Joseph when they went down to Egypt the second time; and they prostrated again later after Jacob and Bilha joined them there.

2048397.title: Children’s Rally
2048397.description: The Rebbe participates in a children’s rally at 770 during Chanukah.

2048398.title: Spiritual Buildings
2048398.description: “Continue to build — physically and spiritually. The verse states that every Jew is ‘G-d’s inheritance’ – he belongs to, and is a part of, G-d Almighty. And since G-d has no limits, when one connects to G-d there is no limit to the good he or she can accomplish.”

2048399.title: Chanukah in July 1979
2048399.description: During the first summer of the Iranian Hostage Crisis, Chief Rabbi of Mexico Abraham Hershberg was selected by the United Nations to visit the Jewish hostages. Before leaving, the Rebbe gave him an important instruction: “Be sure to light the Chanukah menorah with them.”

2048401.title: Shining Examples
2048401.description: The festival is called, “Chanukah – dedication” for it recalls the rededication of the Holy Temple after the Macabees’ victory over the Greeks. The Temple was purified and made holy, and the Jewish people renewed its service with greater love and passion than before.

2048402.title: Didan Notzach
2048402.description: Two weeks before Chabad’s victory in “The Book Trial,” Chasidim sing “Didan Notzach — Victory is Ours,” as the Rebbe distributes dollars to the Mitzvah Tankists.

2048403.title: Capitalize on the Blessings
2048403.description: “The Talmud and commentaries explain that the word ‘bracha – blessing’ comes from the expression “one who bends a grapevine.” A blessing is certainly a good thing, but it requires the person’s involvement as well, to ‘sow,’ ‘plow,’ and ‘harvest’ its fruits.”

2081428.title: The Questions Remain
2081428.description:
An address after the tragic murder of wife and mother, Mrs. Pesha Leah Lapine:
Everything that occurs in this world is by Divine plan; how much more so when a Jewish life is given in sanctification of G-d’s Name. But that doesn’t make the pain any easier to bear…

2081429.title: Haftarah
2081429.description: The Rebbe reads the Haftarah during Afternoon Prayers on the Fast of Teves.

2081430.title: Restoration Work
2081430.description:
Chief Rabbi of Warsaw, Rabbi Menachem Joskowicz, visits the Rebbe:
“When Moshiach comes, the Fast of Teves will be transformed into a day of ‘gladness, rejoicing, and festivity.’ Obviously, then, the day itself already brings an extra measure of blessing. Poland was once the base of Jewish life for the entire world. May you revive it, and return it to its glory of old, with joy and happiness.”

2081431.title: The Decree is Over, Part I
2081431.description: After a horrific car accident, three-and-a-half year old Yaacov Orimland was left in a coma, with doctors giving him just hours to live. His father, Reb Gimpel, turned to the Rebbe for advice and a blessing (1963).
path: The Decree is Over, Part I

2081434.title: A World of Pain, or of Pleasure?
2081434.description: In a letter to one of his disciples, Maimonides describes the taxing daily schedule he endured as court physician to the sultan of Egypt. It not only drained him to the point of exhaustion, it also left him nearly no time to pursue the true joy of his life: Torah study.
path: A World of Pain, or of Pleasure?

2081435.title: Nigun “We Want Moshiach Now”
2081435.description: The Tzivos Hashem anthem is sung at a children’s rally in 770.

2081436.title: Higher and Higher
2081436.description: “May your son, who has returned to Jewish observance after three generations of communist oppression in Russia, continue to grow in all matters of Judaism – as the famous Russian song goes: ‘Higher and higher.’”

2081437.title: The Decree is Over, Part II
2081437.description: Part two of last week’s incredible story...
path: The Decree is Over, Part II

2081439.title: Hearing the Cry of a Child
2081439.description: Once, in the middle of the night, one of the Mitteler Rebbe’s children fell out of bed. Entirely engrossed in his studies, he did not hear the child’s cries. However, his father, the Alter Rebbe, heard the cries, closed his Torah books, and went to comfort the child. The Alter Rebbe later said to his son: no matter how deeply immersed you are in holy pursuits, when a child cries you must hear it; you must stop what you’re doing and soothe their pain.
path: Hearing the Cry of a Child

2081440.title: Tanya
2081440.description: The Rebbe distributes a special edition of Tanya printed by Chasidim in honor of the 40th anniversary of his leadership.

2081441.title: Please Write
2081441.description: “Not only are you qualified to issue rulings in Jewish law, you’re also a descendant of the Alter Rebbe. It has been over three years since you’ve published any new Halachic innovations... This dollar will obligate you, because it will be waiting to be redeemed.”

2081442.title: On the Front Line
2081442.description: During the 1982 Lebanon War, Rabbi Aharon Eliezer Ceitlin was part of a group of Chasidim instructed by the Rebbe to print the Tanya in various Lebanese cities — including the capital, Beirut, itself.

2081444.title: True Giving
2081444.description:
Historically, Jews treated their wisdom in a vastly different way from other nations. In Egypt,
for example, knowledge and scientific progress were the exclusive domain of an intellectual elite. The masses obeyed them with blind action. By contrast, immediately when the Jewish people became a nation, G-d’s first action was to give the Torah to all the Jews, of all generations, equally.

2081445.title: Sanctification of the Moon
2081445.description: Kiddush Levana behind the Rebbe’s house on President Street.

2081446.title: Return on Investment
2081446.description: “When G-d sees a person using his earnings to increase in giving charity, He blesses that person with even more, expecting him to give even more. May G-d give you more, and may you give more.”

2081447.title: Chasid in Camouflage
2081447.description:
Rabbi Benjamin Blech is a world-renowned Modern Orthodox author and lecturer, and a professor of Talmud at Yeshiva University in New York.
One day, he received a surprising phone call from Chabad world headquarters...

2111297.title: In the Moment
2111297.description: One time, my father-in-law, the Rebbe, was scheduled to travel from Leningrad to Moscow on secret business concerning his underground network. Such a journey was fraught with peril, especially because his movements were closely monitored by the communist authorities.

2111298.title: Yahrtzeit
2111298.description: The Rebbe leads the Evening Prayers on the 15th yahrtzeit of his father-in-law and predecessor, Rabbi Yosef Yitzchak Schneersohn of Lubavitch.

2111299.title: Collective Effort
2111299.description:
“To bring Moshiach cannot be achieved by one person alone. It must be accomplished through the collective effort of all Jews together.”
“As an additional aid to finding his soulmate, your brother should study the laws of daily living in the Code of Jewish Law.”

2111300.title: A Few Blocks Away
2111300.description: Rabbi Herschel Feigelstock, an elder Chasid of the Montreal Lubavitcher community, recalls details of the Previous Rebbe’s funeral in the winter of 1950 and instructions he received from the Rebbe concerning the mourning and the visitation to the Previous Rebbe’s resting place.

2111302.title: Split at the Sea
2111302.description:
When the Jewish people was surrounded by the Egyptians at the sea, four opinions were
voiced on how to respond: 1) Jump into the sea – better to give one’s life in sanctification of G-d’s Name than to transgress His will; 2) Return to Egypt – perhaps they had not completed their spiritual mission there; 3) take up arms and fight – for to extinguish their own lives or return to Egypt would both transgress G-d’s will; 4) Pray to G-d.

2111304.title: Tu B’Shevat
2111304.description: “With Tu B’Shevat, the New Year of the Trees, upon us, gather your students together for a farbrengen, give them good fruits, and share with them good words.”

2111305.title: Seeing is Believing
2111305.description: Rabbi Yitzchak Dovid Grossman is a recipient of the Israel Prize, his country’s highest honor. In 1985, his daughter developed a severe eye condition that confounded all the experts... The Rebbe’s diagnosis: “Check the mezuzahs.”

2111308.title: Celebrate the Differences
2111308.description: The brain and heart are equally central to the body’s health and homeostasis. Nevertheless, each has its own function. Similarly, man and woman are equal in importance and in their contribution to Jewish life and continuity. But they have different roles.

2111309.title: Yahrtzeit
2111309.description: At the conclusion of the Afternoon Prayers on the 3rd yahrtzeit of his wife, Rebbetzin Chaya Mushka, the Rebbe recites mishnayos and kaddish at his home on President Street, followed by the distribution of dollars.

2111310.title: Attending to the Rebbetzin
2111310.description: A doctor of the Rebbe’s wife, Rebbetzin Chaya Mushka Schneerson, and a household attendant of hers, visit the Rebbe after her passing.

2111311.title: How Are You?
2111311.description: As an Israeli college student studying in London, England, Mrs. Orah Jurawel befriended a local Chabad family. When she subsequently traveled to visit New York, they asked her for a small favor: to deliver a gift to the Rebbe’s wife, Rebbetzin Chaya Mushka. (1974)

2111313.title: Grab the Bull by the Horns
2111313.description:
According to Jewish tort law, the first three times an ox gores another animal, the owner pays
only half damages, for he cannot be expected to foresee and control the ox’s sudden rage. After three times, the owner must pay full damages, for the animal’s violent nature has been established and the owner should have taken proper precautions. Maimonides rules, however, that if a violent ox is sold or given as a gift to a new owner, the ox is given a fresh clean slate.
path: Grab the Bull by the Horns

2111314.title: Nigun “Ech Ti Zimlak”
2111314.description: Chasidim sing the Russian version of “Who knows one?”

2111315.title: Marketing Torah
2111315.description: Rabbi Pinchas Menachem Alter visits the Rebbe. As brother of Rabbi Simcha Bunim Alter, the Gerer Rebbe who established the daily study cycle of the Jerusalem Talmud, the Rebbe discusses the importance of publicizing the success of this study movement, to inspire others.

2111316.title: Gas Mask in the Yom Kippur War
2111316.description: During the Yom Kippur War, Reb Efraim Mol was stationed at Israel’s southern border with Sinai, when intelligence came in about a possible imminent chemical attack by the Egyptians. Ordered to shave his beard in preparation to don a gask mask, Efraim convinced his superiors to allow him to consult the Rebbe first.
path: Gas Mask in the Yom Kippur War

2139945.title: Be Your True Self
2139945.description: The Megillah recounts how Haman’s evil decree was reversed. Here is how it happened.

2139946.title: Taanis Esther
2139946.description: The Rebbe leads selichos on the Fast of Esther at his home on President Street.

2139947.title: A Reason to Rejoice
2139947.description: “Rabbi Moshe Isserles writes in his glosses to the Code of Jewish Law: ‘One who has a cheerful heart is always feasting.’ Be an example to your students of how a Jew is always rejoicing with his good fortune to be Jewish.”

2139948.title: Risky Business
2139948.description: In 1962, the Rebbe’s warning to Meyer Zajac to stay away from stock market investing saved him from enormous losses. A decade later, after buying $100,000 worth of shares as a favor to a friend, his portfolio fell by 95% to $5,000! Meyer flew to New York to see the Rebbe...

2139951.title: What Makes Purim Unique
2139951.description: What makes Purim unique from all other Jewish holidays?

2139952.title: Nigun “Ih v’Vodeh Mi Ne Utonem”
2139952.description: The Rebbe strongly encourages a lively tune, traditionally sung to Russian lyrics: “No water can drown us, no fire can burn us.”

2139953.title: Making Up for Lost Time
2139953.description: “Thirty days before Passover — at Purim time — one should already be starting to distribute charity for Passover, not starting to fundraise for it. There’s no point in crying over the past, but see to it now to give double.”

2139954.title: Keep It Simple
2139954.description: Expecting for the first time, Dr. and Mrs. David Lazerson requested a blessing from the Rebbe to raise their child to be a “G-d-fearing, righteous, scholarly, Chasid.” The Rebbe’s response on how to achieve this was a little simpler than they’d expected (1973).

2139956.title: Quality Time
2139956.description: When Torah takes a census of the Jewish people, it always counts them “according their households.” The Jewish people is only as strong as its families.

2139957.title: Governor’s Yechidus
2139957.description: 1950’s footage of New York Governor W. Averell Harriman’s visit to the Rebbe (circa 5716 - 1956).

2139958.title: Instilling Self-Confidence
2139958.description: “If you are concerned about your son’s move from a Jewish Day school to a more rigorous yeshivah, it would be advisable to find someone to tutor him once or twice a week. Boost his self-confidence by explaining to him that he is changing schools because he has become older and wiser, and is now capable of greater things.”

2139959.title: Our Friend, the Grand Rebbe
2139959.description: New York City councilman James E. Davis, rest in peace, founded the non-profit organization, Love Yourself, Stop the Violence, dedicated to halting inner city gun crime and drug abuse. His brother, Geoffrey Davis, retells the original inspiration behind his brother’s life work. (late-1970’s)

2139962.title: Constant Connection
2139962.description: “And they shall build for me a Sanctuary and I will dwell within them.” The Sages explain: “within them” – within the heart of every single Jew.

2139963.title: Nigun “Tzomah Lecha Nafshi”
2139963.description: Song lyrics: “My soul thirsts for You, my flesh longs for You; (as one) in a desolate and dry land without water, so (I thirst) to see You in the Sanctuary, to behold Your might and glory.” (Psalm 63)

2139964.title: Don’t Be Happy with Your Lot
2139964.description: “You generally speak to the public in a reserved manner, but a rabbi must be more demanding! To be ‘happy with one’s lot’ is very worthy for others, but if a rabbi is happy with his lot, it’s a pity on his congregation… You have my partnership and a double portion of benediction.”
path: Don’t Be Happy with Your Lot

2139965.title: “They will be Successful”
2139965.description: Mr. Nash Kestenbaum, president of the National Council of Young Israel at the time of the Yom Kippur War, was instrumental in securing the Nixon Administration’s weapons airlift to Israel. His son, Dovid Kestenbaum, recalls his father’s interactions with the Rebbe at the time.

2169748.title: Daily Miracles
2169748.description: One of the 613 commandments is to recount the Exodus from Egypt every single day. It is imperative for the success of a Jew’s daily mission to live with the consciousness that today he is witnessing G-d’s miracles of redemption.

2169749.title: Nigun “Yehi Ratzon”
2169749.description:
Song Lyrics: “May it be Your will, L-rd our G-d and G-d of our fathers, that the Holy Temple be rebuilt
speedily in our days; and grant us our portion in Your Torah.” (From the Amidah Prayer)

2169750.title: Birthday Wishes
2169750.description:
Visiting dignitaries extend their good wishes to the Rebbe at a farbrengen in honor of his 80th
birthday.

2169751.title: Special Delivery
2169751.description: Dr. Abraham Luchins was a world-renowned Orthodox Jewish psychologist who was close to both the Previous Rebbe and the Rebbe. When he was appointed by Washington to lead the American delegation to the World Psychology Convention in Moscow, the Rebbe tasked him with a secret mission.

2169753.title: When You Least Expect It
2169753.description: After being elevated to second in command of Egypt, Joseph saved the entire region by storing grain during the seven years of plenty, in preparation for the seven years of famine. The Talmud records that the wealth Joseph accumulated for Pharaoh from the sale of that grain filled three treasure houses, bolstering Egypt’s position as a world superpower.

2169754.title: Matzah Distribution
2169754.description: On the Eve of Passover, the Rebbe distributes matzos for individuals and communities to use at the seder.

2169755.title: Charity for Israel
2169755.description: “Charity increases merit in all areas. Even when it comes to the Land of Israel, which already has tremendous merit of its own, charity magnifies it even more.”

2169756.title: A Timely Message
2169756.description: Reb Nochum Partzovitz, the beloved head of the Mirer Yeshivah in Jerusalem, had a private audience with the Rebbe in the early 1970s. His student, Rabbi Yosef Yitzchak Havlin, recounts the details of that meeting as related to him by Reb Nochum (1972).

2169758.title: Pay No Attention
2169758.description: An address to children: On the fourth day of the Exodus, Pharaoh’s emissaries reminded the Jews that they had only been granted a three-day pass to worship in the desert; it was time to return to Egypt as slaves.

2169759.title: Nigun “Al Achas”
2169759.description:
Song Lyrics: “How much we must be grateful to the Omnipresent One for the doubled and redoubled
goodness He has bestowed upon us; for He has brought us out of Egypt...” (The Haggadah)

2169760.title: Be Strong
2169760.description: “As a member of Israel’s Consolidation Party, the Likud, you should ‘consolidate’ all the Jews around you, standing even stronger than you have until now.”

2169761.title: Engine Trouble
2169761.description: For over sixty years, Rabbi Yosef Wineberg traveled the globe fundraising on behalf of the central Lubavitcher Yeshiva. The Rebbe would often entrust him with personal missions during these travels. A story out of the Jewish heart of Africa (1950s).

2169763.title: Changing with the Times
2169763.description: A Jew must “always increase in holiness.” He or she must not only grow constantly in their Jewish observance and Torah study, but also innovate in their service of G-d.

2169764.title: Sefiras Haomer
2169764.description: The Rebbe leads the Counting of the Omer after Evening Prayers at his home on President Street.

2169765.title: The Merit of Mishnah
2169765.description: “The Alter Rebbe writes that in the merit of the study of Mishnah we will be redeemed from exile. May you bear good tidings in your project to encourage Mishnah study in memory of those who perished in the Holocaust.”

2169766.title: The Right Diagnosis
2169766.description: Shortly after becoming pregnant with their first child, Reb Meshulom Weiss’s wife was diagnosed with the rare Weber-Christian Disease. But even after the diagnosis was confirmed by a top expert in the field, the Rebbe insisted on his own ‘third opinion.’ (Late 1950s)

2189970.title: Torah Defense, Part I
2189970.description: Recent generations have witnessed a paradigm shift in the art of warfare. Whereas it used to be the quantity of one’s soldiers and weaponry that deterred war or proved victory in the battlefield, today it is the quality of one’s arsenal that matters most. One technologically advanced weapon outweighs vast quantities of enemy manpower.

2189971.title: Nigun “Lechatchila Ariber”
2189971.description: Chasidim sing a favorite nigun of Rabbi Shmuel of Lubavitch, the Rebbe Maharash.

2189972.title: A Time for Loving
2189972.description:
Ashkenazic Chief Rabbi of Israel Avraham Shapira and Sefardic Chief Rabbi of Israel Mordechai Eliyahu visit the Rebbe during the Days of Sefirah between Passover and Shavuos.
A discussion about the students of Rabbi Akiva and the mitzvah to love one’s fellow man.

2189973.title: Bird’s Eye View
2189973.description: During the Yom Kippur War, Israeli fighter jets from 1967 faced cutting-edge Russian-made surface-to-air missiles. Shortly after the war, Israeli Air Force engineer Mr. Yitzchak Rappaport was sent to America on a mission to update the IDF’s technology for the future.

2189976.title: Lag B’omer Carnival
2189976.description: On his way to the Ohel, the Rebbe’s car passes the Lag B’omer carnival on Empire Boulevard.

2189977.title: Better Than a Doctor
2189977.description: Dr. Efraim Meltzer of Shaarei Tzedek Hospital and Israeli Chief Justice Yehuda Cohen, chairman of the board of Ezrat Nashim Hospital, visit the Rebbe.

2189978.title: Keep Looking
2189978.description: Rabbi Mordechai Einbinder is a Chabad emissary in Tarzana, California. When one of his congregants was facing financial ruin, they wrote to the Rebbe in hope of a miracle. Following the Rebbe’s advice, the man discovered the solution to his problem in his own backyard... (Late-1980's)

2189980.title: The Tanners' Market
2189980.description:
Rabbi Elazar son of Rabbi Shimon ben Yochai taught: “G-d promises the Jewish people in
exile: ‘I shall never reject them or abhor them to break My covenant with them.’ This is like a man whose bride lives in a leather tanners’ market, where everything reeks. Were she not there, he would never have entered. But because she is there, it smells to him like a spice market, the most beautiful scent in the world.”

2189981.title: Lag B’omer Parade
2189981.description: The Rebbe participates in the 1970 Lag B’omer parade in front of 770.

2189982.title: Keep it Warm
2189982.description: “May G-d bless you with increased wealth and much nachas from your children. California is a warm place. Warm it up spiritually as well, with Judaism.”

2189983.title: Showing Appreciation
2189983.description: Rabbi Shneur Zalman Vilenkin served as the Rebbe’s childhood teacher in Yekaterinoslav (Dnepropetrovsk), Ukraine. Vilenkin’s grandson, Rabbi Yehudah Leib Schapiro, describes the extraordinary honor the Rebbe accorded his grandfather years later in New York.

2189985.title: Holy Futures
2189985.description: That which a child is exposed to, even at the youngest age, has far-reaching effects on him, physically and spiritually. Modern science has also reached this conclusion, even concerning infants who are too young to understand what is going on around them. Therefore, it is important to surround a Jewish child with only holy sounds and images. Even if their minds do not understand it, their souls do.

2189986.title: Nigun “Hinei Mah Tov”
2189986.description: Song lyrics: “Behold how good and how pleasant it is when brothers dwell together.” (Psalm 133:1)

2189987.title: Halachic Ruling
2189987.description: Rabbi Menachem Mendel Mendelsohn of Moshav Komemiut asks a blessing for the neighboring Chabad yeshiva in Kiryat Gat to be able to pay off its debts.

2189988.title: Stories of Tzadikim
2189988.description: Mrs. Chana Arnold is a veteran educator. She recalls a simple instruction she received from the Rebbe, advising her how to instill love and respect of G-d in the hearts of children. (1977)

2222306.title: Trustees of Torah
2222306.description: Shavuos celebrates the Giving of the Torah at Sinai. Jews in every generation gather to hear the reading of the Ten Commandments, for on this day they receive renewed strength in their mission to brighten G-d’s world.

2222307.title: “Reb Levik’s Nigun”
2222307.description: The Rebbe asks the Chasidim to sing the joyous Simchas Torah nigun of his father, Rabbi Levi Yitzchak Schneerson, of righteous memory.

2222308.title: Priestly Blessings
2222308.description: “Consult a rabbi, explaining to him your doctor’s opinion about the surgery, and proceed as he advises. As a kohen, be sure to bless to congregation on Shavuos, as the priestly blessing draws down Divine healing as well.”

2222309.title: First Fruits in Brooklyn
2222309.description: Mr. Amram Malka served for a time as an assistant in the Rebbe’s household. One time, he was asked to assist in organizing the Rebbe’s office, and he came across a drawer with family pictures of Chasidim sent to the Rebbe from around the world. This gave Malka an idea...

2222311.title: Torah Defense, Part 2:
2222311.description: In past generations, the numbers of one’s armies determined the outcome of war. Today, the quality of one’s forces far outweighs the significance of its numbers. This is true with regard to the technological superiority of weaponry, but, and even more so, the superiority of the soldiers themselves.

2222312.title: Blessings to Bride and Groom
2222312.description: The Rebbe blesses several couples on their wedding days.

2222313.title: Make Your Mazel Shine
2222313.description: “Lighting Shabbos candles causes one’s mazel to shine. Every girl, even before marriage, should light Shabbos candles, and should give charity beforehand.”

2222314.title: The Bar Lev Line
2222314.description: Mr. Yisroel Katzover is senior military correspondent who covered the IDF for numerous Israeli newspapers and media channels. (year 1970)

2222316.title: On Isolationism
2222316.description:
Isolationism is not a moral or sustainable path for the United States.
A civilized nation must be built upon solid moral foundations. This means that no matter what the immediate situation may be, the country stands by its principles, even if it appears that compromising on principles could bring material gain.

2222318.title: G-d is on Your Side
2222318.description: New York City Mayor-hopeful Rudy Giuliani visits the Rebbe.

2222319.title: A Practical Gift
2222319.description: Rabbi Zalman Aaron Grossbaum is executive director of Chabad Lubavitch of Ontario, Canada. He recalls the Rebbe’s advice for the “perfect gift” to present to Canada’s Prime Minister. (Early-1980s)

2222322.title: America is No Different
2222322.description: Materially-speaking, Jews today have it better than any other time in history. Whereas for most of their two thousand year sojourn in exile, huge numbers of Jews lived in dire poverty, today, even the poorest among them lead comfortable lives.

2222323.title: Family Visit
2222323.description: The Jaffe family of England greets the Rebbe as he leaves 770 on his way home before Shabbos.

2222324.title: In the Right Direction
2222324.description: “Don’t emphasize the fact that a Jew is only now beginning to don tefilin, so, calling attention to the fact that he hasn’t done so in the past. Emphasize what he is doing now and for the future.”

2222325.title: A 365-Day Jew
2222325.description: Mr. Dennis Eckstein grew up as what he calls a “three-day-a-year-Jew.” But twenty five years ago that changed, thanks to one thoughtful act of the Rebbe. (year: 1989)

2243606.title: The Power of Thought
2243606.description: Sometimes, quite out of the blue, we can experience thoughts of repentance, of growing spiritually, and of bettering ourselves. Far from random, the Talmud relates that such thoughts are the soul’s response to a call which issues daily from Heaven.

2243607.title: At the Rebbe’s Resting Place
2243607.description: The Rebbe visits the resting place of his father-in-law and predecessor, Rabbi Yosef Yitzchak Schneerson, to read requests for blessings from across the world.

2243608.title: Become a Member
2243608.description: “The term ‘supporter of Chabad’ implies that while you may be supporting it, you remain separate. It would be much better if you would support yourself by becoming a part of it!”

2243609.title: Think of Me, and I’ll Think of You
2243609.description: Reb Mendel Futerfas, imprisoned in a Soviet gulag and unable to communicate with the outside world, composed a unique letter in his mind and “sent” it off to the Previous Rebbe. Reb Mendel’s wife was shocked to receive a letter from the Previous Rebbe in reply to her husband’s “telegram.”
path: Think of Me, and I’ll Think of You

2243623.title: On Jewish Identity
2243623.description: In a public letter written after his liberation from Soviet imprisonment in 1927, Rabbi Yosef Yitzchak Schneerson wrote that the release was not his alone, but a redemption for every Jew, even one for whom the title “Jew” may seem irrelevant.

2243624.title: Farbrengen
2243624.description: A farbrerngen held in the courtyard adjacent to 770, in honor of Rabbi Yosef Yitzchak Schneerson’s release from Soviet imprisonment.

2243625.title: Prevention is Better than Cure
2243625.description: New York City Police Commissioner Mr. Lee P. Brown visits the Rebbe.

2243626.title: For The Sake of Torah
2243626.description:
Rabbi Mayer Plotkin was a student in Yeshiva Torah Vodaas, when he heard a former faculty
member recount that the Previous Rebbe boldly kept the doors of the Yeshiva open during a
financial crisis in the late-1940s.

2243628.title: No Words of Their Own
2243628.description: Bilam, a non-Jewish prophet, was summoned by the King of Moab to curse the Jewish people. He consented to go, but warned him that he can do nothing and say nothing outside of what G-d instructs him. In the end, Bilam prophesied the future glory of the Jewish people instead.

2243629.title: Nigun
2243629.description: This nigun was sung by Reb Michoel Dworkin, a prominent chosid, upon the Release of Rabbi Yosef Yitzchak Schneerson from Soviet imprisonment in 1927.

2243630.title: Enough is Never Enough
2243630.description: The Rebbe responds to a startling question: “When does one finally have enough?”

2243631.title: Don’t Give Up!
2243631.description: Rabbi Yaakov Biderman, director of Chabad-Lubavitch in Austria, discovered that he was not the first shliach to Vienna. Over two decades before his arrival, the Rebbe sent Mrs. Marguerite Chajes to pay a visit to Doctor Viktor Frankl, the founder of logo-therapy and author of Man’s Search for Meaning.

2243633.title: A Love of the Land
2243633.description: The Torah relates that Tzelofchad left no sons to inherit his portion in the Land of Israel. Driven by their love of the Land, his five daughters overcame their sense of modesty and appeared before Moses with a claim that they should be their father’s heirs.

2243634.title: Distribution of Dollars
2243634.description: At the conclusion of a farbrengen, the Rebbe distributes dollars to the “Tankists” – who shared the Mitzvah campaigns and manned the Mitzvah Tanks.

2243635.title: One Good Deed
