2243635.description: “My father-in-law, the Rebbe, declared that one good deed is worth a thousand sighs.”

2243636.title: Sweet Medicine
2243636.description: Mrs. Rochel Fogelman led a group of women from Worcester, Massachusetts, on a visit to New York and to an audience with the Rebbe that went down in history. (year 1953)

2264992.title: A True Diagnosis is Half the Cure
2264992.description: The value of a Temple offering brought when a Jew was unsure whether or not he sinned, was far greater than that brought for a definite sin, when he was certain of his sin.
path: A True Diagnosis is Half the Cure

2264993.title: Nigun B’cho Hashem Chosisi
2264993.description: A melody composed in honor of the Rebbe’s 70th birthday and set to the first verse of chapter 71 in Psalms.

2264994.title: Moses Who Loves Them Shall Rebuke Them
2264994.description: “Rebuke comes in two ways. One is to focus on the wrong, proceeding to correct it. The other is to focus on the good that one is capable of. The wrong will then take care of itself.”
path: Moses Who Loves Them Shall Rebuke Them

2264995.title: Does the Rebbe Know You?
2264995.description: Rabbi Shimon Lazaroff, director of Chabad-Lubavitch of Texas, traveled to New York to resolve a personal issue. While there, he was astonished by the special attention he received from the Rebbe during a farbrengen, especially in light of preceding events. (1980s)

2264997.title: A Work in Progress
2264997.description: The Midrash relates that at the beginning of the Babylonian exile, seventy years before the Jews’ return to Jerusalem, G-d instructed Ezekiel to teach them the dimensions of the Holy Temple, because when they engage in its study, G-d considers it as though they built it.

2264998.title: Tisha B’av Prayers
2264998.description: The Rebbe recites the morning prayers on Tisha B’av. His secretary, Rabbi Hodakov, leads the services.

2264999.title: Rebuilding Shilo
2264999.description: The Rebbe reassures a delegation from Shiloh, Israel: “You need not wait for my response in a letter. You’ll receive a response through G-d’s blessings!”

2265000.title: The Facts of Life
2265000.description: Mr. Yaakov Schiffman joined his family in an audience with the Rebbe when his father was terminally ill. The Rebbe proceeded to teach him a page of Talmud, and a lesson that changed his life. (1975)

2265002.title: Burning the Midnight Oil
2265002.description: Our sages declare that the night was created for girsa – Torah study. They chose their words carefully: Girsa denotes a cursory type of study, intended to cover ground in Torah. It is not necessarily deep. Yet, the sages maintain that nighttime was created specifically for this type of study.

2265003.title: President Shazar Visits the Rebbe
2265003.description: On his first presidential visit to the United States, President Zalman Shazar of Israel visits the Rebbe.

2265004.title: Rejoicing on the Fifteenth of Av
2265004.description: Blessings for joy and healing in the days approaching the fifteenth of Av, an auspicious day on the Jewish calendar.
path: Rejoicing on the Fifteenth of Av

2265005.title: Presidential Visit
2265005.description: Mr. Dan Patir served as advisor to several Israeli leaders. He accompanied President Shazar on a historic visit to the Rebbe in 1966.

2265007.title: Giving of Oneself
2265007.description: The Rebbe’s father, Rabbi Levi Yitzchok Schneerson, whose passing is marked on the 20th of Av, was imprisoned and exiled to Kazakhstan for his stance against Soviet efforts to uproot Jewish learning and practice.

2265008.title: Rabbi Levi Yitzchok’s Hakofos Nigun
2265008.description: Children returning from summer camp sing this nigun at a rally.

2265009.title: Charity Begins at the Bank
2265009.description: “By offering a special discount to anyone opening a charity account, you will provide an incentive for people to do so faster.”

2265010.title: A Jew Just Like You
2265010.description: Mr. Israel Adamski lived in Dnepropetrovsk, Ukraine, where Rabbi Levi Yitzchok Schneerson, the Rebbe’s father, served as rabbi. He recalls Rabbi Levi Yitzchok performing an underground wedding, and inviting a communist informant to be the tenth man. (Late 1930’s)

2289712.title: Returning the Hearts of the Fathers
2289712.description: Although parents have a duty to educate and guide their children, it can sometimes be that the parents need direction themselves.
path: Returning the Hearts of the Fathers

2289713.title: Children’s Rally
2289713.description: The Rebbe participates in a lively Tzivos Hashem rally in 770.

2289714.title: Climbing the Ranks
2289714.description: A proud member of Tzivos Hashem shows the Rebbe his “passport.”

2289715.title: Lasting Impressions
2289715.description: Rabbi Norbert Weinberg was becoming despondent when all of his hard work as a Hebrew school principal was becoming undone by his students’ parents. Fortunately, the Rebbe cast a new light on the situation. (Late 1950s)

2289717.title: Who You are Today
2289717.description: Maimonides teaches that “genuine” repentance is when the “Knower of Secrets,” G-d himself, can attest that a person will never commit the same sin again. Yet practically, Jewish law judges a person only by his current, observable deeds and not by what he has in his heart, or what the future may hold.

2289718.title: Meeting of Machne Israel Development Fund
2289718.description: Participants meet the Rebbe and receive honey cake for a sweet new year.
path: Meeting of Machne Israel Development Fund

2289719.title: Already Jewish
2289719.description: “Being a Jew is not contingent on one’s deeds.”

2289720.title: On Keeping Resolutions
2289720.description: As a student in yeshiva, Rabbi Yitzchok Meir Gurary received important guidance from the Rebbe. (Early 1950s)

2289722.title: Fighting the Inner War
2289722.description: The evil inclination is a master at its craft and will bring all sorts of proofs to justify its cravings. It will even claim that what it wants is natural and healthy.

2289723.title: Celebrating the Founding of the Chabad Yeshivah in 1897
2289723.description: In connection with the 85th anniversary of the founding of Yeshiva Tomchei Temimim, the Rebbe calls for a farbrengen to be held in the yeshiva, and sends L’chaim to be shared with participants.
path: Celebrating the Founding of the Chabad Yeshivah in 1897

2289724.title: Continuing Education
2289724.description: “You should not suffice with being an alumnus. Strive to remain a student.”

2289725.title: "But Where Is G-d?"
2289725.description: Mr. Elliot Lasky had returned from a concert tour with a famous band when he experienced an unexpected spiritual awakening and began to reexamine his lost faith. (1973)

2289727.title: On the Offensive
2289727.description: When fighting a spiritual war, it is insufficient to simply ward off enemy attacks. One must go out and capture ground, constantly growing in Jewish observance.

2289728.title: Nigun of Three Movements
2289728.description: This melody was composed by the Baal Shem Tov, the Magid of Mezritch, and the Alter Rebbe.

2289729.title: A Claim to Fame
2289729.description: “Being a descendant, you should act in a way that will make the Baal Shem Tov proud!”

2289730.title: Letters to Camp Pickett
2289730.description: When Mr. Mendel Greenbaum was conscripted into the U.S. Armed Forces after the outbreak of the Korean War, he sought the Rebbe’s advice and began a correspondence. (1952)

2316178.title: Bribing G-d
2316178.description: The Torah mentions the prohibition against judges taking bribes several times, also relating that the Almighty Himself, “does not show partiality nor take a bribe.” Yet we find it stated explicitly that repentance, prayer and charity can sway G-d’s judgment. How can we reconcile these two points?

2316179.title: “Panim”
2316179.description: The Rebbe receives “panim”, petitions for blessing, before the new year.

2316180.title: Precisely Worded Blessings
2316180.description: “The translation of my Rosh Hashana message can be found in the High Holiday prayer book.”

2316181.title: Lost in Translation
2316181.description: After Mr. Naftali Deutsch financed the construction of a Jewish school, the Rebbe used the High Holiday prayer book to reassure Mr. Deutsch that he had made the best investment possible. (Late 1970s)

2316183.title: Strength in Numbers
2316183.description: During the days between Rosh Hashana and Yom Kippur, known as the ten days of repentance, every individual has the power of a minyan, a quorum of ten: That which at any other time of year requires the combined effort of ten, can be achieved by the individual during these ten days.

2316184.title: The Nigun “Ki Anu Amecha”
2316184.description: Song lyrics: “For we are Your nation and You are our G-d.” The melody to these words from the High Holiday liturgy was first taught by the Rebbe on Simchas Torah, 5717 – 1956.

2316185.title: Keep the Peace
2316185.description: “The meaning of ‘Anash,’ an acronym for the Chabad community, is ‘people of our peace.’ It means that you must all be at peace with one another.”

2316186.title: Urgent Message
2316186.description: A year after visiting an isolated group of Jews in Sweden, Rabbi Dovid Weitman discovered that the Rebbe did his own outreach, sending one of them an urgent telegram just a few days before Rosh Hashana. (1974)

2316188.title: Open Invitation
2316188.description: The Talmud relates that the entire Jewish people could dwell in one sukkah.

2316189.title: Maariv
2316189.description: The Rebbe leads evening services in 770 on the yahrzeit of his mother, Rebbetzin Chana Schneerson.

2316190.title: A “Big” Mitzvah
2316190.description: “You should not suffice with being an alumnus. Strive to remain a student.”

2316191.title: A Promise Fulfilled, Part 1
2316191.description: Reb Gimpel Orimland took the Rebbe’s advice to move to Florida and take on a new business venture. When he later made a commitment to charity which he couldn’t afford, the Rebbe assured him he’d be able to give many times that amount the following year. (Late 1960s)

2316193.title: The Properties of Water
2316193.description: When the Holy Temple stood in Jerusalem, wine was poured on the altar daily, but on the festival of Sukkos there was an additional water libation after the morning service.

2316194.title: Intermediate Days of Sukkos
2316194.description: A vintage scene from morning services in 770 during the festival of Sukkos. (5720s - 1960s)

2316195.title: Dance for Joy!
2316195.description: “For a speedy recovery, you should dance for the joy of the Torah.”

2316196.title: A Promise Fulfilled, Part 2
2316196.description: Almost a year had passed since the Rebbe had assured Reb Gimpel Orimland that he’d return to 770 and be able to give many times more than his previous pledge to charity. Several weeks before his return to 770, however, the fulfillment of the Rebbe’s blessing was yet to be seen. (Late 1960s)

2349202.title: The Small Luminary
2349202.description: The book of Genesis relates that on the fourth day of creation G-d created the two luminaries; the great luminary, the sun, to shine by day, and the small luminary, the moon, to shine by night.

2349203.title: Kos Shel Brachah
2349203.description: The Rebbe recites havdalah at the conclusion of Simchas Torah and distributes kos shel brachah.

2349204.title: Three Times Three
2349204.description: “This year there was a chazaka, an auspicious series of three two day festivals followed by Shabbos in a row.”

2349205.title: Never Too Small
2349205.description: Rabbi Immanuel Schochet was a prominent scholar and author. On two occasions, he was surprised to discover just how much the Rebbe paid attention to the needs of his chasidim. The Rebbe seemed to keep track of even the very small ones.

2349210.title: Mutual Defense Pact
2349210.description: The Talmud relates that King David and his general, Yoav Ben Tzeruya, supplemented each other. David was immersed in the study of Torah, while Yoav went out to battle.

2349211.title: Farewell Audience
2349211.description: Guest who came to spend Tishrei with the Rebbe hand the Rebbe a petition for blessing and receive a dollar for charity to be given upon their return home.

2349212.title: City of Abraham
2349212.description: “Be’er Sheva is the city of our forefather Abraham. This brings a special merit to its residents, along with a responsibility.”

2349213.title: Exceptional Soldiers
2349213.description: Mr. Yosef Lautenberg was injured in the battle for Jerusalem in 1948, and among the founders of the IDF Disabled Veterans Organization. In 1976 he led the Israeli delegation, made up in large part of injured IDF veterans, to the Paralympics in Toronto, and decided to bring the group to New York to visit with the Rebbe.

2349215.title: “Land for Peace?”
2349215.description: The Code of Jewish Law rules that if our enemies set out to besiege Jewish cities, then even if they come for a seemingly benign purpose such as “gathering straw and stubble,” they must be fought off, even at the cost of desecrating the Sabbath.

2349217.title: Keeping Brooklyn Safe
2349217.description: New York City Mayor John Lindsay comes to visit the Rebbe in 770 to discuss crime and social issues in the Crown Heights community.

2349218.title: Waiting for an Answer
2349218.description:
Rabbi Boruch Zaichyk was serving as a rabbi in Johannesburg, South Africa, when a
congregant fell critically ill and called the Rebbe’s office for a blessing and advice. When an answer did not arrive, Rabbi Zaichyk decided to take matters into his own hands. (1970s)

2349220.title: The Idealism of Youth
2349220.description: One of the virtues of youth is that they have not yet become inured to the limitations and “realities” of daily life. This, coupled with their enthusiasm and energy, allows them to stand behind the truth without compromise.

2349221.title: Nigun “Ach Du”
2349221.description: A lively nigun composed by Chazan Shmuel Kontaroff.

2349222.title: “Young” Israel
2349222.description: “Make sure to maintain the vigor of youth in the Council of Young Israel.”

2349223.title: Time for Ice Cream
2349223.description: When Rabbi Mordechai Gutnick was told by the Rebbe to enter the rabbinate, he sought to prepare himself through study and a rabbinic apprenticeship. Yet his greatest lesson lay in the Rebbe’s attitude to a request from a young girl. (1974)

2371378.title: Food for Thought
2371378.description: In some U.S. states, public schools begin their school day with a moment of silence, a time during which students can reflect. This presents a perfect opportunity for students to think about a Higher Authority.

2371379.title: Teaching Charity
2371379.description: Entering the main synagogue in 770, the Rebbe stops to distribute coins to little children to be given to charity. (Fall, 1979)

2371380.title: A Comptroller Can Pull Strings
2371380.description: In anticipation of New York City mayoral elections, the Rebbe asks then comptroller and mayoral candidate, “Why do you want to be mayor – who’s the actual boss of New York City, the mayor or the comptroller?”

2371381.title: All Shall Come to Know God
2371381.description:
Rabbi Chaim Druckman was a young man involved in the Bnei Akiva Youth Movement when the Rebbe told him that the main focus of the curriculum, even in formal schools, should be the fear of Heaven.
Many years later, the Rebbe added that the imperative to bring people closer to G-d applies not only to Jews, but to all mankind.
path: All Shall Come to Know God

2373036.title: Mission Accomplished?
2373036.description: The Torah relates that when the Jewish people were preparing to enter the land of Israel, Moses sent spies to scout out the city of Ya’azer and its environs, which the Jews would have to cross in order to enter the Holy Land.

2373037.title: Kinus Hashluchim
2373037.description: Distribution of a chasidic discourse followed by a lively celebration at the conclusion of the International Conference of Shluchim.

2373038.title: The Best Method
2373038.description: “The most effective way to bring Jews of Sephardic descent back to Judaism is by setting up Torah classes.” (Collage)

2373039.title: What Happens When You Help Others
2373039.description: Rabbi Shlomo Riskin, rabbi of Efrat, Israel, comes to the Rebbe with a concern about one of his children and ends up with a life-lesson from the super-rational commandment of the red heifer. (1991)
path: What Happens When You Help Others

2373053.title: Part of a Whole
2373053.description: In 1980 the Rebbe initiated a campaign for every Jewish child to own a letter in a Torah scroll.

2373054.title: Dedication of a New Torah
2373054.description: A lively celebration of the dedication of a Torah scroll written in honor of the Rebbe and the Rebbetzin.

2373055.title: A New Crown
2373055.description: The Rebbe personally accepts a crown for the Torah written in his and the Rebbetzin’s honor three years prior.

2373056.title: Tuned In
2373056.description: Standing amongst the crowd in 770, Mr. Michoel Hazan discovers the extent to which the Rebbe understands his personal situation – a yeshiva student from Gibraltar who wants to adopt Chabad customs. (Late 1970s)

2373064.title: Women's Rights
2373064.description: There is a prevalent misconception that in order to demonstrate their equality, women need to imitate men. But the need to imitate someone else implies an inferior self-perception.

2373065.title: Farbrengen
2373065.description: Two young men approach the Rebbe for a blessing and L’chaim in the days before their weddings.

2373066.title: The Month for Weddings
2373066.description: “The month of Kislev is an auspicious time to get married – so you still have a few weeks to find a bride!”. (Collage)

2373067.title: Mandate for a Woman
2373067.description: Rabbi Yekusiel Farkash and his wife arrive for an audience with the Rebbe, but receive a private talk on the requirement for women to study chasidic teachings, with a special directive for Mrs. Farkash.

2403932.title: Rising To the Challenge
2403932.description: The nineteenth of Kislev marks the release of Rabbi Shneur Zalman of Liadi from imprisonment in Czarist Russia. He was imprisoned as a result of his efforts in spreading chasidic teachings, but it was only after this that he was able to continue his work without hindrance, and with greater success and intensity.

2403933.title: A Farbrengen
2403933.description: Recently restored footage of a farbrengen marking the release of Rabbi Shneur Zalman of Liadi from Czarist imprisonment.

2403934.title: The Chabad Path
2403934.description: “The Patriarchs, Abraham, Isaac and Jacob, represent wisdom, knowledge and understanding in the service of G-d.”

2403935.title: The Soul of Torah
2403935.description: Rabbi Nissen Mangel, a prominent author and scholar, was a yeshiva student in Montreal, Canada, when he brought a friend from a non-Chabad background to spend Shabbos in Crown Heights and have an audience with the Rebbe. (Late-1950s)

2403955.title: Three Celebrations, One Message
2403955.description: Imprisoned in Czarist Russia, the Alter Rebbe’s case was at the mercy of the hostile officials of the most powerful country in the world. Miraculously, his acquittal was ordered by the Czar himself, and he was freed on the nineteenth of Kislev.

2403956.title: Chanukah Live 5750/1989
2403956.description: The first internationally televised Chanukah rally.

2403957.title: Happy Chanukah!
2403957.description: “The idea of Chanukah is to make sure that the light of the menorah reaches those around us.”

2403958.title: A Sure Cure
2403958.description: As a young child, Rabbi Psachya Korf arrived in an emergency room after a terrible house fire. Doctors scrambled to airlift him to a special treatment center and warned his parents that his prognosis was not too optimistic. That’s when his father, Rabbi Pinchas Korf, rushed to the Rebbe for a blessing. (1989)

2403963.title: Good Times, Bad Times
2403963.description: The lives and challenges of our forefather Isaac and his grandson Joseph were very different. Isaac lived out his entire life in the Land of Israel amidst physical prosperity. Joseph spent most of his life in Egypt where he was sold into slavery and ultimately became a powerful ruler.

2403964.title: End of a Long Journey
2403964.description: Almost a year after the U.S District Court ordered that books taken from the Chabad Library be returned to Agudas Chasidei Chabad, they were finally brought back.

2403965.title: On Printed Matter
2403965.description: “A published work will not only affect the masses, it will influence future generations!”

2403966.title: A Sign of Things to Come
2403966.description: When Rabbi Moshe Weiss’ father would not give him the prayer book the Rebbe had sent him as a gift, he asked his teacher for paper and decided to write his own. The Rebbe saw this as a sign of things to come. (Late 1960’s)
path: A Sign of Things to Come

2403980.title: Claim Your Inheritance
2403980.description: In Deuteronomy, the Torah is referred to as “the inheritance of the congregation of Jacob,” of which every Jew is a member.

2403981.title: Nigun Rachamana
2403981.description: A verse from the slichos liturgy set to a melody composed by the Rebbe’s grandfather. The Rebbe first introduced this nigun in 1959.

2403982.title: Scholars and Laymen
2403982.description: “Whereas laymen may come to ask questions of the rabbi, scholars often come to ask questions on the rabbi.”

2403983.title: A Message from Tashkent
2403983.description: Rabbi Bentzion Vishedsky relates that when his sister was in the former USSR, her father in law, Reb Simcha Gorodetzky, was overjoyed to receive word from the Rebbe that she and her husband would soon be allowed to leave the Soviet Union. (1966)

2432362.title: On Going Mainstream
2432362.description: During the slavery of the Jewish people in ancient Egypt, Pharaoh’s harshest decree was that every male child born, be drowned in the Nile.

2432363.title: Walking to Shul
2432363.description: Vintage footage of the Rebbe walking to 770 during the intermediate days of Sukkos. (Fall of 5725, 1965)

2432364.title: Making a Living
2432364.description: “G-d is responsible for making a living, you just need to make sure to collect it.”

2432365.title: Sensitivity in Code
2432365.description: When Mrs. Shulamis Saxon wrote a letter to the Rebbe just days before her bat mitzvah, instead of simply asking for a blessing, she decided that she would bless the Rebbe as well.

2432502.title: Three Partners, One plan
2432502.description:
The Talmud explains that that there are three partners involved in the creation of a child –
the father, the mother, and G-d.

2432503.title: Nigun of Four Parts
2432503.description: Chasidim sing a nigun composed by Rabbi Shneur Zalman of Liadi, the Alter Rebbe.

2432504.title: Print on the Double
2432504.description: “You blessed me with long life; it means I’ll be able to continue to demand even more of you!”

2432505.title: Name Him Yosef Yitzchak
2432505.description:
Dr. Yechiel Lasri is the mayor of Asdod, Israel, and a former member of the Knesset. After
his mother lost her first three children within hours of their being born, the family sought the
advice and blessing of the Rebbe.

2432507.title: Neither Famine nor War
2432507.description: The Rebbe concludes the yearly study cycle of Maimonides’ Mishneh Torah in his home on President Street, Brooklyn. In the very last law, Maimonides describes the future redemption.

2432508.title: Farewell Gathering
2432508.description:
Rabbi Yosef Yitzchok Scheersohn, the Previous Rebbe, attends a farewell gathering before
his return to Europe after his first visit to the United States.

2432509.title: Rambam is for Everybody
2432509.description: “The study of Maimonides’ Mishneh Torah is not just for yeshiva students, it is universal.”

2432510.title: How to Inspire a Generation
2432510.description: Upon accepting his first pulpit, Rabbi Sholom Ber Gordon consulted Rabbi Yosef Yitzchak Schneersohn, the sixth Lubavitcher Rebbe, on how to bring his new congregation to deepen their Jewish observance.

2432523.title: Tending G-d’s Garden
2432523.description: The last discourse that Rabbi Yosef Yitzchok Schneersohn, the Previous Lubavitcher Rebbe, published before his passing commences with the verse “I have come into My garden.” The Previous Rebbe explains that this refers to our world, the innermost dwelling place of G-d.

2432524.title: Histalkus
2432524.description: The funeral of Rabbi Yosef Yitzchak Scheersohn, the sixth Lubavitcher Rebbe, took place outside his residence and synagogue, 770 Eastern Parkway, Brooklyn.

2432525.title: A Twofold Blessing
2432525.description:
“I mention you at the resting place of my father-in-law, the Rebbe, and he gives you his
blessing.”

2432526.title: Feeling the Connection
2432526.description:
After having made numerous trips to New York to see the Rebbe, Rabbi Avrohom Michoel
Halpern, the rabbi of Givat Tzarfatit in Jerusalem, tells the Rebbe that he still feels no change
in their connection.

2462172.title: A Stumbling Block Before the Blind
2462172.description: Maimonides rules that every Torah teaching, even a legal ruling, is intended “to set our hearts straight and rectify our character traits.”
path: A Stumbling Block Before the Blind

2462173.title: The Rebbe Leads Services
2462173.description:
Newly discovered and restored footage of the Rebbe leading morning services in 770 on the
occasion of his father’s yahrtzeit.

2462174.title: Without Compromises
2462174.description:
It is easier to maintain the integrity of Torah today, without any modifications or
compromises, than it was in previous years.

2462175.title: Making a Mess
2462175.description: On two separate occasions when their shlichus seemed in trouble, Rabbi Yossi Groner’s wife wrote to the Rebbe. When she received the Rebbe’s encouragement and experienced unanticipated outcomes, one of her congregants noticed and decided to try the same.

2462187.title: Life-Giving Water
2462187.description:
Our sages teach that in the merit of Miriam’s righteousness, a miraculous well accompanied
the Jewish people throughout their wanderings in the desert and provided them with water.

2462188.title: The Beinoni Nigun
2462188.description:
Chasidim sing this melody, associated with Rabbi Yosef Yitzchak Schneersohn, the sixth
Lubavitcher Rebbe, at a farbrengen marking his passing.

2462189.title: Bringing Blessing into the Home
2462189.description: Place a charity box on the table before your class begins. That way people will not only study, but will also have an opportunity to give charity.

2462190.title: A Class of Their Own
2462190.description: When Mrs. Alice Zlotnick’s husband, Professor Dov Zlotnick, told the Rebbe about the success of his Talmud class in Riverdale, New York, he received an unexpected challenge, which he duly passed on to his wife.

2462192.title: Thirteen Months of the Year
2462192.description: Addressing children in 770, the Rebbe sheds light on the significance of the leap year and the special lesson that can be gleaned the extra month of Adar.

2462193.title: The Morning Service
2462193.description:
The Rebbe prays in the home of his brother-in-law, Rabbi Shmaryahu Gurary, on the third
floor of 770, the day after his funeral.

2462194.title: No Need to Fear
2462194.description:
The verse guaranteeing God’s protection over the Holy Land is well-known. The people of
Israel need only to be joyful, especially since we find ourselves in the month of Adar.

2462195.title: The Chancellor of the Exchequer
2462195.description: Mr. Bentzion Rader, a registered accountant for almost forty years, was surprised to learn that the financial advice he gave to an acquaintance who wanted to increase his contributions to charity was vetoed by the Rebbe. As events unfolded, he realized that the Rebbe must have his own sources.

2462206.title: Message from Behind the Iron Curtain
2462206.description: Rabbi Yehuda Leib Levin, Moscow’s chief rabbi, was sent by the Soviet government to the United States to assure the West that Soviet Jewry faces no discrimination and is free to practice its religion.
path: Message from Behind the Iron Curtain

2462207.title: News from the Inside
2462207.description:
An excerpt from a recorded meeting between the Rebbe and Rabbi Yehuda Leib Levin, the
Chief Rabbi of Moscow, during his visit to the United States.

2462208.title: A Covert Operation
2462208.description: Shortly after Mrs. Ella Skoblo arrived in New York, she had an audience with the Rebbe. While she knew that her grandfather, Rabbi Yehuda Leib Levin, the Chief Rabbi of Moscow during the Soviet era, had met with the Rebbe during his visit in 1968, she was surprised to discover that he was also part of a covert operation orchestrated by the Rebbe.

2489366.title: The Previous Rebbe's Dangerous Speech in Moscow, 1927
2489366.description: He spoke about the imperative to provide Jewish children with an authentic Torah education, even under communist rule.
path: The Previous Rebbe's Dangerous Speech in Moscow, 1927

2489367.title: Purim Katan Children’s Rally
2489367.description: The Rebbe participates in a lively children’s rally on Purim Katan in 770.

2489368.title: Effective Education
2489368.description: The great merit of teaching Jewish children Torah and performance of mitzvos will surely bring blessings.

2489369.title: The Rebbe’s Response on Sepharadim and Ashkenazim
2489369.description: Rabbi Hillel Zaltzman was active in the Soviet Jewish underground. When faced with hard times and tough decisions, he recalls secretly consulting his “zeide” in America. The word may simply mean “grandfather” in Yiddish, but to Rabbi Zaltzman and his comrades, it was the code name for “Rebbe.” (1960s)
path: The Rebbe’s Response on Sepharadim and Ashkenazim

2489384.title: The Infinite in the Finite
2489384.description: The world was created by G-d, Who is infinite. It follows then, that in every single creation there must be evidence of the artisan who created it. It must contain some resemblance to its Creator’s infiniteness.

2489385.title: Distribution of Dollars
2489385.description: A special selection of encounters with the Rebbe during his Sunday distribution of dollars for charity.

2489386.title: A Needle in a Haystack, Part 1
2489386.description: Rabbi Pinchas Woolstone, who served as rabbi of the Jewish House Crisis Center in Sydney, Australia, was on a trip to New York when he was approached for assistance in finding a girl from Brooklyn who had run away to Australia. Not knowing where to start, Rabbi Woolstone decided on his first step: to consult the Rebbe. (1980s)
path: A Needle in a Haystack, Part 1

2489390.title: How Can Divine Forgiveness Be Purchased?
2489390.description: In the Book of Exodus, the Jewish people are instructed to contribute a half-shekel coin towards the building of the tabernacle as “atonement for their souls,” and the commentaries explain that it atoned for the grievous sin of the golden calf.
path: How Can Divine Forgiveness Be Purchased?

2489391.title: Nigun Hisvaadus
2489391.description: Chasidim sing a rousing melody at a farbrengen marking the passing of Rabbi Yosef Yitzchak Schneersohn, the Previous Rebbe.

2489392.title: Months of Joy
2489392.description: Your wedding date falls out at just the right time to “increase in joy,” since there are sixty days of Adar this year.

2489393.title: A Needle in a Haystack, Part 2
2489393.description: When the Rebbe instructed Rabbi Pinchas Woolstone to take a trip to Brisbane, Australia, he was unsure of what he was expected to do there. He set out on his mission anyway, and by the time he arrived, he knew exactly what had to be done. (1980s)
path: A Needle in a Haystack, Part 2

2489406.title: When G-d Is Hidden
2489406.description: A deeper look at the heroine of the Purim story, whose very name means “hidden” in Hebrew.

2489407.title: America Is No Different
2489407.description: An excerpt from a new JEM film featuring the films of Rabbi Yosef Yitzchak Schneersohn, the sixth Rebbe, with original commentary and first-hand interviews.

2489408.title: A Custom Blessing
2489408.description: You already have G-d’s blessings, without the need for an intermediary!

2489409.title: Seeing the Connection
2489409.description: Rabbi Zalman Sudakevitch was living in Paris when the Rebbe traveled to France to escort his mother to the United States, three years before he assumed leadership. He recalls meeting the Rebbe for the first time in the Rebbe’s hotel room, and learning a lesson about the connection of a chosid to his Rebbe. (1947)

2523739.title: Dare to Be Different
2523739.description: The Book of Esther relates that when King Achashverosh made a great feast, he provided every guest with whatever food and drink they desired.

2523740.title: Purim Morning Service
2523740.description: Early colored footage of the Rebbe participating in the morning prayers and megillah reading on Purim in 770. (5720s – 1960s)

2523741.title: An Entertaining Line-Up
2523741.description: Since you make your living by making Jews laugh, may G-d make you joyful, many times over.

2523742.title: Downfall of a Modern-Day Haman
2523742.description: Rabbi Yoel Kahn, a leading authority on Chabad Chasidic thought, recalls being present at a Purim farbrengen in 770 when the Rebbe told a very unusual story. But even more unusual, were the events which unfolded soon after. (1953)

2530636.title: A Solid Foundation
2530636.description: Those responsible for allocating communal funds must make some difficult decisions about how the money should best be spent.

2530637.title: Kos Shel Brachah
2530637.description: The Rebbe distributes wine from the Havdalah ceremony following Simchas Torah. A group of children from Morocco are heard singing among the crowd.

2530638.title: Four Times the Wisdom
2530638.description: The Talmud relates that one who comes from the Holy Land has twice the wisdom, and one who goes to the Holy Land gains twice the wisdom. You are doing both.

2530639.title: Getting Out of Debt
2530639.description:
When the rand suddenly collapsed, Rabbi Nachman Bernhard recalls that Lubavitch Foundation of South Africa stood to lose the property which housed its growing school. After receiving an unsolicited message from the Rebbe, Rabbi Bernhard wasted no time in
putting the advice to use. (1980s)

2530651.title: On Harmony in Marriage
2530651.description: In the 1970s the Rebbe issued a call for a campaign to strengthen and promote the observance of Family Purity among all segments of the Jewish community.

2530652.title: Mayim Shelonu
2530652.description: Chasidim look on as the Rebbe draws water outside 770 to be used the next day for baking matzo for Passover.

2530653.title: Fresh News
2530653.description: Unlike mayim shelonu, water drawn the night before matzo baking, your newspaper, Yisrael Shelonu, should report fresh news!

2530654.title: A Mikvah for Whom?
2530654.description: Rabbi Moishe Engel was among the shluchim in Long Beach, California, who dreamt of opening a kosher store or starting a Hebrew school to help boost the community’s Jewish infrastructure. They were astonished when a call arrived from the Rebbe’s office with a blessing for a new mikvah. (1971)

2530657.title: Give It All You've Got!
2530657.description: When the Temple stood, certain offerings were based on a person’s means. A poor person could bring an offering of lesser value, while a wealthy person who brought the same offering had not fulfilled his obligation. Since G-d had blessed him with wealth, more was expected of him.

2530658.title: Farbrengen
2530658.description: Newly discovered footage of a farbrengen marking the Rebbe’s seventy-fifth birthday.

2530659.title: Through the Eyes of Children, Part I
2530659.description: A special selection of clips featuring children receiving dollars from the Rebbe.
path: Through the Eyes of Children, Part I

2530660.title: Birthday Blessings
2530660.description: Rabbi Aron Eliezer Ceitlin would write monthly reports to the Rebbe when he was a senior yeshiva student in Tzefat, Israel. Approaching the month of Nissan, he decided to include a birthday blessing for the Rebbe in the name of the entire administration. Not knowing how his superiors would react, he sent off the report and hoped for the best. (1980)

2552678.title: War on Ignorance
2552678.description: The Haggadah lists four sons at the Passover Seder table. The child ‘who doesn’t know to ask’ is listed last amongst the four sons, following not only the ‘wise son’, but also the ‘wicked’ one. This offers insight and an important lesson in our calling to action in these times.

2552679.title: Burning the Chametz
2552679.description: Burning the chametz in the basement of 770 before Passover.

2552680.title: Educating New York
2552680.description: Mr. Sandy Harman, New York Board of Jewish Education

2552681.title: Sensitivity at Midnight
2552681.description: Rabbi Yisroel Shmotkin, as a yeshiva student had the good fortune to attend the Rebbe’s seder for a number of years in the 1960s.

2552696.title: Chasidic Discourse: “As in the Days of the Exodus”
path: Chasidic Discourse: “As in the Days of the Exodus”

2552697.title: Distributing Matzah
2552697.description: The Rebbe distributes matzah to shluchim to be used at communal seders.

2552698.title: No News is Good News
2552698.description: New York City Comptroller Harrison J. Goldin. Jay Goldin served as comptroller of New York City. In the 1970s, he was active in the struggle for Soviet Jewry.

2552701.title: The Simple Jew vs. the Bandits
2552701.description: Thousands of years ago, an international coalition denied the right of the Jewish people to dwell in the Holy Land, claiming it was stolen land. A simple man rebuffed their assertions with a simple quote from the Torah.
path: The Simple Jew vs. the Bandits

2552718.title: Humility’s Role in Warfare
2552718.description: The advantage of quality over quantity in deterring the enemy, and in the battle of the spiritual over the physical.

2552721.title: Permission Granted
2552721.description: While Professor Evsey Nemoytin served as dean of Kazakh State University, his parents ran an underground mikvah. In the 1970s, the Rebbe arranged their eventual exit from the Soviet Union. Professor Nemoytin recalls the Rebbe’s valuable advice, as well as his delight at learning that the Rebbe understood his field of research. (Includes footage filmed by Rabbi Berel Levy to be smuggled out to the Rebbe.)

2579729.title: Second Chances
2579729.description: The Mishna states that every Jew is righteous. Yet how can it be expected of every Jew, regardless of circumstances or the education he received, that he conduct himself “righteously” in every aspect of his life?

2579730.title: Hippocratic Oath
2579730.description: As a doctor, you should heal as many Jews as possible, and non-Jews, as well. Best would be to have healthy patients, and to earn your livelihood from preventative medicine.

2579731.title: A Special Year
2579731.description: Rabbi Shlomo Zarchi shares some recollections of 770, where he was a student in the mid- 1960s. He recalls the Rebbe’s mother’s passing in 1965, as well as one particular morning prayer that became seared into his memory.

2586146.title: Lag B’omer, Day of Unrivaled Joy
2586146.description: Rabbi Avraham HaLevi, a disciple of the Arizal, had the custom of reciting Nachem, a prayer of mourning for Jerusalem, every single day.
path: Lag B’omer, Day of Unrivaled Joy

2586147.title: Lag B’omer Parade
2586147.description: Celebration of Lag B’omer, 5744, as captured by the lens of Sholom Ber Goldstein.

2586148.title: Relying on Rabbi Shimon
2586148.description: A collage of interactions about Lag B’omer and Rabbi Shimon Bar Yochai.

2586149.title: Desperate Measures
2586149.description:
After Mrs. Leah Englander’s three year old son was rushed to the hospital, the doctors
informed her that the boy would be at least partially paralyzed for life.
When she contacted her brother, Dr. Levi Reiter for help, he was left with only one option to help his nephew: To ring the bell at the Rebbe’s home on President Street, in the middle of the night.

2586163.title: A Head Start
2586163.description: The food that a child eats and the air that he breathes have an important impact on a child. Likewise, the actions of parents have an effect on the child. Here, however, we learn that even the parents’ conduct before the child is born play an important role in the child’s development.

2586164.title: Farbrengen
2586164.description: A joyous chasidic melody sung at a Farbrengen with the Rebbe.

2586165.title: Walk, Don’t Run
2586165.description: You don’t have to run for government, you can walk. The main thing is to get there.

2586166.title: I Did My Part
2586166.description: Before her marriage, Mrs. Chana Arnold received a letter from the Rebbe outlining the rewards a woman receives for covering her hair with a wig. Six years later, Mrs. Arnold kept the Rebbe to his word.

2586173.title: High Expectations
2586173.description: The Mishna states that every Jew is righteous. Yet how can it be expected of every Jew, regardless of circumstances or the education he received, that he conduct himself “righteously” in every aspect of his life?

2586174.title: Havdalah
2586174.description: A rare film of the Rebbe performing the Havdalah ceremony at the conclusion of Shavuos and Shabbos, and subsequent distribution of kos shel brachah, wine from the “cup of blessing.”

2586175.title: Inscribed in a Book
2586175.description: When Rabbi Yosef Minkowitz suggested that a certain verse might have a connection to the Rebbe’s “Letter in the Torah Scroll” Campaign, he never expected the Rebbe’s reaction. At a subsequent rally for children, some heavenly force seems to have altered the weather forecast.

2606410.title: Every Home a Temple
2606410.description: The Torah calls the Jewish people “a kingdom of priests.” Here is what it means to you…

2606411.title: Farbrengen
2606411.description: After a lively nigun, the Rebbe instructs visiting rabbis to say L’chaim in order to hasten the redemption.

2606412.title: Jews Like all Others
2606412.description: Given their unique hardships, Jews in the former Soviet Union are especially deserving of Gd’s blessings.

2606413.title: A Change of Heart
2606413.description: When Israel’s future President, Zalman Shazar, requested that Chabad send someone to assist the Israeli author Eliezer Steinman in writing about the movement, Rabbi Chanoch Glitzenstein approached the mission cautiously. Given the writer’s sacrilegious bent, Rabbi Glitzenstein decided to request the Rebbe’s advice.

2615416.title: Making the Most of Vacation
2615416.description: For children, summer vacation is a welcome break from school. For parents and those responsible for their Jewish education, it is an opportunity not to be missed.

2615417.title: Tzivos Hashem Rally
2615417.description: At a rally for children, they sing before the Rebbe a new song of Tzivos Hashem.

2615418.title: A Noble Cause
2615418.description: When people see that you are a count and still a Torah observant Jew, it will influence them to be more observant themselves.

2615419.title: A Timely Letter
2615419.description: When Rabbi Chanoch Glitzenstein discovered that his acquaintance, the Israeli author Eliezer Steinman, had fallen seriously ill, he sent an urgent telegram to the Rebbe requesting a blessing. To his surprise, no response was forthcoming.

2618575.title: The Heart of the Nation
2618575.description: The verse in the Torah which addresses the Jewish people, divides them into ten categories, from “the heads of your tribes” to “your water drawers.”

2618576.title: Nigun Simcha
2618576.description: A lively nigun often sung at the Rebbe’s farbrengens.

2618577.title: Getting Back to Work
2618577.description: Tell your father to get well soon – remind him that he still has lots of work to finish!

2618578.title: A Triple Blessing
2618578.description: After five years of marriage and numerous visits to doctors, Yocheved and Yehuda Daphna were yet to have children. At the urging of a friend, they sought the Rebbe’s blessing..

2618589.title: Eternal Bond
2618589.description: The Jerusalem Talmud notes that one verse in the Book of Judges states that Samson judged Israel for forty years, while another says he judged them for twenty years.

2618590.title: A Jewish Leader
2618590.description:
Presented for Gimmel Tamuz, the twentieth anniversary of the Rebbe’s passing.
Precious scenes of the Rebbe captured on film, accompanied by selections from a talk
delivered on 12 Nissan, 5741.

2618591.title: A Good Beginning
2618591.description: The proof of a good beginning is that it leads to increased action every single day.

2618592.title: Just the Person to Talk To
2618592.description: After Rabbi Dr. Tzvi Hersh Weinreb had earned his Ph.D. from the University of Maryland, he was faced with a variety of decisions that would shape the course of his life. Not knowing where to turn, he decided to place a call to the Rebbe. In the end, he received his counsel from a different person entirely.
path: Just the Person to Talk To

2635602.title: From the Mouths of Infants
2635602.description: The twelfth and thirteenth days of Tammuz mark the release of Rabbi Yosef Yitzchak Schneerson, the sixth Lubavitcher Rebbe, from Soviet imprisonment, which was the result of his efforts in strengthening Torah and mitzvah observance among Soviet Jewry.

2635603.title: Dollars Distribution
2635603.description: The Rebbe distributes dollars for charity at his home on President Street.

2635604.title: Keep the Memories
2635604.description: Why must you worry the patient by calling it a “difficult surgery.” Call it an “easy surgery!”

2635605.title: The Unforgotten Jew
2635605.description: When Mr. Yitzchok Nemes was about to travel to Guyana, the Rebbe gave him an extra dollar for charity “to pass on to a Jew living there.” Although he could not find any Jews in Guyana, Mr. Nemes took his mission very seriously, and did not give up until he delivered the dollar to its intended recipient. (Late 1980s)

2635614.title: Behind Closed Doors
2635614.description: The release of Rabbi Yosef Yitzchak Schneerson from Soviet Russia was more than a victory for an individual. The approach which proved to be successful in lobbying the Soviets to agree to his release was one of quiet yet forceful diplomacy, far away from the public arena.

2635615.title: Nigun
2635615.description: The Rebbe instructs Cantor Tzvi Tsatskis to sing a lively Russian song at a farbrengen.

2635616.title: Citing the Sources
2635616.description: I take care to cite my sources because even if someone doesn’t agree with my words, he can look up the sources and study the subject in greater detail.

2635617.title: Quiet Activism
2635617.description: When Irina Markish became active in the protests and demonstrations calling for the release of Soviet Jewry and on behalf of her husband, David Markish, in particular, her advocacy led her to a surprising and fruitful meeting with the Rebbe. (1972)

2635624.title: Dressing Modestly in the Summer
2635624.description: The laws of modesty apply to men and women. Still, there is a difference stemming from the distinct virtue which women possess.

2635625.title: Farbrengen
2635625.description: This newly uncovered film of a farbrengen in the summer of 1976 is the only known recording of the event.

2635626.title: New Inventions
2635626.description: When you finish writing this book, you should make the time to write a Torah book also. Toil and you will succeed.

2635627.title: Worth the Risk
2635627.description: Rabbi Mordechai Dubinsky readily agreed to host a young couple from Israel who came to the United States seeking treatment for the wife’s heart condition. What he didn’t expect was to also be involved in the birth of their first child. (1970s)

2635634.title: Unity in Purpose
2635634.description: There are many activities that can bring people together. Eating, drinking, and working together for a common goal are just a few examples.

2635635.title: Kiddush Levana
2635635.description: Sanctifying the new moon outside 770 on the second night after Yom Kippur.

2635636.title: Not So Impossible
2635636.description: Try to answer at least one of your grandfather’s Talmudic questions, it’s not as impossible as you may think.

2635637.title: Where is Moshiach?
2635637.description: Rabbi Moshiach Chudaitov and his family were active in the Jewish underground in Samarkand, Uzbekistan during Soviet times. When they succeeded in leaving the Soviet Union, they received some unexpected attention from the Rebbe, together with a very special blessing. (Early 1970s)

2660915.title: Kabbalah for Kids
2660915.description: The fifth of Av marks the passing of Rabbi Yitzchak Luria, known as the Arizal, who was a foremost scholar of Jewish mysticism and the father of his own school of Kabbalah

2660916.title: Havdalah
2660916.description: At the conclusion of the fast of Tisha B’av, the Rebbe listens to havdalah being recited in 770.

2660917.title: Daily Blessings
2660917.description: The Arizal taught that in the times of the redemption the Levites will become Kohanim. Although you are a Kohen and your grandson is a Levite, your family will still remain in the priesthood.

2660918.title: On My Shoulders
2660918.description: Shortly after his Bar Mitzvah, the Rebbe assured Rabbi Mordechai Einbinder’s parents that he would see to the well-being of their son in a yeshiva far away from home. Decades later, Rabbi Einbinder discovered just how serious the Rebbe was about his word.

2660930.title: Destroying to Rebuild
2660930.description: The Ninth of Av commemorates the destruction of both the first and second Temples in Jerusalem. It also commemorates many other calamities which befell the Jewish people throughout their exile. Marked by a fast, it is the saddest day on the Jewish calendar.

2660931.title: Afternoon Prayers
2660931.description: Newly uncovered film of the Rebbe taking part in the afternoon prayers on Tisha B’av.

2660932.title: A Good Report
2660932.description: The verse “Honor G-d with your property,” can also be read as “Honor G-d with your voice.” This is especially appropriate for a cantor such as yourself.

2660933.title: What Makes a Marriage Endure?
2660933.description: After becoming observant in college, Rabbi Meilech Leib DuBrow asked the Rebbe about marrying someone whom he had known during his student years. In an unusually long audience, he received the answer to his question, as well as advice on the basics of a Jewish marriage. (1971)

2660937.title: A Positive Emotion
2660937.description: The twentieth of Av marks the passing of Rabbi Levi Yitzchak Schneerson, the Rebbe’s father. Reflecting on the passing of a loved one is seldom joyous and often brings up feelings of sadness and even bitterness.

2660938.title: Nigun
2660938.description: Hop Kazak, a lively melody attributed to the prominent chasidic master, Rabbi Aryeh Leib of Shpola, known as the Shpoler Zeide.

2660939.title: A Holy Task
2660939.description: Thank you for taking care of my father’s gravesite in the past and for your help in the future, as well.

2660940.title: Saying Thank You
2660940.description: Mr. Evsey Neymotin recalls his father’s efforts in assisting Rabbi Levi Yitzchak and Rebbetzin Chana Schneerson, the Rebbe’s parents, when they arrived in Almaty, Kazakhstan, as well as the Rebbe’s expressions of gratitude when the Neymotins arrived in the United States many decades later.

2660953.title: You Don't Have to Be a Rabbi
2660953.description: In our daily lives we come into contact with a variety of people, whether family, friends, coworkers or employees, and our interaction with them is often limited by the way we perceive them.
path: You Don't Have to Be a Rabbi

2660954.title: Children’s Rally
2660954.description: The Rebbe participates in a rally for children returning from summer camp.

2660955.title: Double the Amount
2660955.description: When you decide to take on a good deed, G-d will ensure that you’ll succeed.

2660956.title: A Spiritual Business
2660956.description: Mr. Meir Zeiler, the proprietor of a textile factory in Israel, was encouraged by the Rebbe to take part in European trade shows. His reports that the shows were not profitable did not deter the Rebbe, and Mr. Zeiler began to suspect that the tefillin booth he would set up as part of his display had something to do with it.

2684095.title: Speaking the Truth
2684095.description: Rashi comments on the very first verse in the Torah: “It could happen that gentiles will claim that the Jews stole the Land of Israel from them. Therefore, G-d related His mighty works in the Book of Genesis to show that it was He Who created the Land of Israel and it was he who gave it to the Jewish People.”

2684096.title: Nigun
2684096.description: To “counter the stubbornness of those who insist on giving away the Land of Israel” the Rebbe initiates the signing of the nigun Utzu Eitza, based on the verse: “Contrive a scheme, but it will be foiled; conspire a plot, but it will not succeed, for G-d is with us.” (Isaiah 8:10)

2684097.title: The Closest Time, the Dearest Place
2684097.description: Despite events in the Middle East, the days leading into Elul should not be viewed as “difficult days.” To the contrary - at this time of year, G-d is even closer to every single Jew, especially those in the Holy Land.
path: The Closest Time, the Dearest Place

2684098.title: The Essence of Things
2684098.description: Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu of Israel shares the enduring message which he received in his first meeting with the Rebbe during his tenure as Israel’s Ambassador to the United Nations. (1984)

2684110.title: Peace Upon the Land
2684110.description:
The Israeli government must set its priorities in Operation “Peace for Galilee.”
From the outset, the military experts made it clear that casualties could be minimized on both sides of the conflict by a swift operation, which could be over in days. Even the President of the US did not pressure Israel to do otherwise. But some politicians became afraid of their own inner insecurities.

2684111.title: Farbrengen
2684111.description: The Rebbe asks several senior Rabbis to address the Farbrengen and issue Halachic rulings that the Land of Israel belongs to the Jewish People.

2684112.title: Israel and the U.S.: Friendship through Strength
2684112.description: The only approach which has succeeded so far is when Israel makes clear to the United States through its actions that it will not compromise on security issues, and that the US needs a strong partner in the Middle East.
path: Israel and the U.S.: Friendship through Strength

2684113.title: The Nation That Dwells Alone
2684113.description: Yitzchak Rabin was prime minister of Israel, and served as Israel’s ambassador to the United States in the early 1970s. In 1972 he was sent to convey Israel’s blessings to the Rebbe in honor of his 70th birthday, and left with a challenging message. (1972)

2684115.title: Land for Peace?
2684115.description: The nations of the world are watching and waiting: “When will Jews begin to say what they’re really thinking about the Land of Israel?” When Jews start talking diplomatic jargon, begging the nations to take more and more land, in order to curry favor in their eyes – the non-Jew doesn’t believe them, because they’re not speaking as Jews should.

2684116.title: Visit by Israel’s Prime Minister
2684116.description: Israeli Prime Minister, Menachem Begin, visits the Rebbe.

2684117.title: Wake Up Call
2684117.description: Motti Eden is Director of Israel’s Channel One television. In 1980, while working as a broadcast journalist for Kol Yisrael Israeli radio, he had a private audience with the Rebbe, which he recorded and later broadcast on Kol Yisrael. (1980)

2684130.title: Morale in the IDF
2684130.description: In past generations, the numbers of one’s armies determined the outcome of war. Today, the quality of one’s forces far outweighs the significance of its numbers. This is true with regard to the technological superiority of weaponry, but, and even more so, the superiority of the soldiers themselves.

2684131.title: Nigun Ata Vechartanu
2684131.description: A nigun based on the words from the festival prayers, “You have chosen us from among all the nations.” The Rebbe taught this song on Simchas Torah, 5721, 1960.

2684133.title: Exceptional Soldiers
2684133.description:
Mr. Yosef Lautenberg was injured in the battle for Jerusalem in 1948, and was one of the founders of the IDF Disabled Veterans Organization.
In 1976, he led the Israeli delegation, made up in large part of injured IDF veterans, to the Paralympics in Toronto, and decided to bring the group to New York to visit with the Rebbe. (1976)

2715105.title: Where the Penitent Stands
2715105.description: A Talmudic passage about marriage helps us gain a deeper understanding of the journey of teshuva, repentance.

2715106.title: Nigun Avinu Malkeinu
2715106.description: Chasidim sing Avinu Malkeinu, one of the ten nigunim composed by the Alter Rebbe.

2715107.title: In the Way of Our Fathers
2715107.description: Double what you’ve done until now. If you triple it, I’ll be happy, and so will you!
path: In the Way of Our Fathers

2715108.title: Are There 'Secular' Soldiers in the IDF?
2715108.description: When Shmuel Blizinsky served in the Israel Defense Forces in the early 1950s, he was only able to find twelve religious soldiers on his entire base. As it turned out, the Rebbe was able to find three thousand. (1951)
path: Are There 'Secular' Soldiers in the IDF?

2719716.title: Rabbi Shmuel and Spreading Sukkot Joy
2719716.description: The yahrzeit of the Rebbe Maharash, the fourth Chabad Rebbe, falls just before Sukkos, a time when Jews busily prepare for the upcoming festival. In recalling his life’s work, we see how the Rebbe Maharash gave up personal comforts, working tirelessly to improve the spiritual and physical lives of Russian Jewry.
path: Rabbi Shmuel and Spreading Sukkot Joy

2719717.title: Distributing the Four Kinds
2719717.description: The Rebbe inspects lulavim and distributes them to a number of distinguished individuals, concluding with a blessing for good and joyful tidings throughout the year.

2719718.title: Don’t Rely on My Blessing!
2719718.description: The very fact that you mention this issue to me is an indication that you can do more.

2719719.title: Secret Mission
2719719.description: Elimelech Leiman relates that when the Rebbe heard about his father’s upcoming trip to the Soviet Union to visit family, he requested to see him. Handing him a bag of esrogim and a secret code, the Rebbe stated, “This mission will be good for them and good for you.”

2725117.title: One Sukkah, One Lulav, One People
2725117.description: The two central mitzvos of Sukkos, the sukkah and the Four Kinds, have at their core the theme of Jewish unity.
path: One Sukkah, One Lulav, One People

2725118.title: Hallel – Chol Hamoed Sukkos
2725118.description: Reciting Hallel with the Four Kinds during the intermediate days of Sukkos. (October, 1978)

2725119.title: Fourteen Honored Guests
2725119.description: My father-in-law, the Rebbe, revealed that in addition to the seven ushpizin, or supernal guests that visit the sukkah on each night of the festival, there are also seven chasidic ushpizin. In Lubavitch we have fourteen!

2725120.title: A Helping Hand
2725120.description: When things became tough financially, Rabbi Yossi Groner decided to travel to the Rebbe for a blessing before Simchas Torah. Before he could say anything, the Rebbe blessed him with improvement in his finances, and even secured a donation. (1991)

2725133.title: Playing the Fool
2725133.description: “Ech Ti” is a chasidic nigun first taught by the Rebbe on Simchas Torah 5718 – 1958. Its words, in Hebrew and Belarusian, revolve around a fool who travels to a market, but doesn’t actually buy or sell anything.

2725134.title: Speak Up!
2725134.description: One must take responsibility for the direction one’s students are headed. One must at least make sure they are able read their teacher’s writings!

2725135.title: Practically Speaking
2725135.description: Rabbi Mordechai Gutnick relates that his father, known as a powerful orator, once confided in the Rebbe that he wonders how much he is actually accomplishing with his speeches. The Rebbe’s advice to his father is something Rabbi Gutnick still uses today.

2741416.title: Answering to a Higher Authority
2741416.description: In 1985, the U.S. Supreme Court heard a case about an Alabama law allowing public school teachers to start each day with a moment of silence for meditation or voluntary prayer.

2741417.title: Farbrengen
2741417.description: The Rebbe calls an unscheduled farbrengen after receiving word that his special request to conduct hakafos in Hebron and Jerusalem after Simchas Torah has been fulfilled.

2741418.title: All of Humanity Included
2741418.description: Reach out to the non-Jewish members of Knesset, as well, by promoting the Seven Noahide Laws which were given to all mankind.

2741419.title: Isaac Herzog, President-Elect of Israel
2741419.description: Firsthand recollections of his visit to 770 one Simchat Torah with his father, Chaim Herzog, who was then Israel’s Ambassador to the United Nations. (1977)

2741436.title: A Matter of Choice
2741436.description: A Jew shares a relationship with G-d on two levels, that of the soul and that of the body. While the Tanya relates that the soul is “a veritable part of G-d above,” and its relationship to G-d is like that of a parent and child, the value of the body is often overlooked.

2741437.title: Vintage Scenes
2741437.description: Unique scenes from the “small shul” in 770, which served as the main synagogue for many years. (1960's)

2741438.title: Rain of Blessings
2741438.description: In Israel, the prayers for rain begin on the seventh of Cheshvan. May we have the type of rain which brings blessings in tow, especially the blessing of the final redemption.

2741439.title: The Rebbe’s Prescription for a Paralyzed Arm
2741439.description: Soon after Dr. Levi Reiter purchased his own pair of tefillin, he found himself in a doctor’s office with a paralyzed arm. Neurologists gave him three possible prognoses, but the Rebbe reduced it to one.
path: The Rebbe’s Prescription for a Paralyzed Arm

2755532.title: Be a Lamplighter
2755532.description: When a chassid asked the Rebbe Rashab, “What is a chassid?” the Rebbe Rashab answered him, “A chassid is a lamplighter.” He has an obligation to ignite the spark in his fellow Jew’s G-dly soul.

2755533.title: Dollars Distribution
2755533.description: The Rebbe distributes dollars for charity in honor of the birthday of Rabbi Sholom DovBer of Lubavitch, the Rebbe Rashab.

2755534.title: An Occasion for Joy
2755534.description: The twentieth of Cheshvan marks the birthday of the Rebbe Rashab. It’s an auspicious day on the chasidic calendar and provides an opportunity to cultivate joy.

2755535.title: The Rebbe’s Word
2755535.description: Reb Velvel Konikov relates that when his father, Reb Chaim Tzvi Hersh, was drafted into the Russian army, he sought the blessing of the Rebbe Rashab.

2755548.title: Be Like a Redwood
2755548.description: The Code of Jewish Law rules: “All your actions should be for the sake of Heaven” and “In all your ways, know G-d.” This instruction is not referring to the commandment. “Your actions” means the personal activities that you choose to do, and “Your ways” means the personal path you choose in life. Even these pursuits have a deeper intent and purpose, in the words of the Mishna: “I was created only to serve my Maker.”

2755549.title: Nigun Hoaderes V’hoemuna
2755549.description: The Rebbe instructs chasidim from France to sing the nigun Hoaderes V’hoemuna to the tune of the French national anthem.

2755550.title: Good for the Bank
2755550.description: When the director has a happy family life, it’s also good for business.

2755551.title: Construction and Destruction
2755551.description: Professor Aaron Ciechanover, a Nobel Prize winning scientist, relates the conversation he shared with the Rebbe when his research was in its early stages, as well as the lesson he learned. (1977)

2765489.title: A Global Mission
2765489.description: Whenever Jews gather, the Divine Presence rests upon them. How much more so here, when this gathering is for the sake of bringing G-d’s Torah to every Jew across the globe.

2765490.title: International Conference of Shluchim
2765490.description: During the International Conference of Shluchim, and the day before the seforim return to 770, the Rebbe is greeted by an excited crowd as he enters the afternoon prayers.

2765491.title: On Their Heads
2765491.description: Those who support the shluchim must also make sure they fulfill their obligations!

2765492.title: A Wedding and a Mission
2765492.description: As a student in yeshiva in his early twenties, Rabbi Yossi Baumgarten asked the Rebbe for a blessing on route to a friend’s wedding in Italy, and ended up with a mission. (Early 1970s)

2765504.title: A Drink on the Way
2765504.description: Nye Zhuritzi was a song sung at farbrengens by chasidim of Rabbi Dovber, the second Chabad Rebbe.

2765505.title: Seventy Languages
2765505.description: It is important that you’ve translated the Abridged Code of Jewish Law into Hungarian. Moses showed the way by translating the Torah into seventy languages.

2765506.title: Saving Three Lives
2765506.description: Dr. Harold Serebro was surprised when the rabbi of his synagogue walked into his practice holding a file of x-rays belonging to a fellow congregant. The rabbi’s dilemma: doctors were insisting on immediate surgery, but the Rebbe was of an entirely different opinion. (Early 1980s)

2765510.title: The Making of a Chasid
2765510.description: The nineteenth of Kislev marks the liberation of Rabbi Shneur Zalman of Liadi from Czarist imprisonment for his efforts in spreading chasidic teachings.

2765511.title: An Auspicious Day
2765511.description: Rabbi Zalman Gurary, an elder chasid, blesses the Rebbe on the occasion of his wedding anniversary on behalf of the entire community.

2765512.title: Wedding in Warsaw
2765512.description: Much success in continuing your father’s dynasty and charity work. It’s possible that the Radziner Rebbe was at my wedding in Poland, but to remember every guest is too much to expect.

2765513.title: Everybody Counts
2765513.description: Mrs. Dena Horn, who lost her father at a young age, recalls the special attention the Rebbe showed her family when they moved to the neighborhood. (1950s)

2765526.title: Evolution of Torah
2765526.description: In 1984, the Rebbe initiated a campaign for the daily study of Maimonides’ seminal work, the Mishneh Torah, with the aim of completing the fourteen volumes over the course of a year.

2765527.title: Farbrengen
2765527.description: A unique glimpse at preparations for a farbrengen in 770.

2765528.title: Celebrating Study of Rambam
2765528.description:
Rabbi Shmuel Butman recalls the day the Rebbe called him to his house, requesting that he publish a book commemorating the worldwide celebrations of the annual completion of the Mishneh Torah.
His due date? Three weeks. (1980s)

2803065.title: Looking Back, Moving Forward
2803065.description: During a rally for children, the Rebbe teaches a lesson from the Torah portion of Miketz, which is usually read during Chanukah, and contains the story of Joseph’s brothers going down to Egypt to buy grain during the famine.

2803066.title: Chanukah Rally
2803066.description: Newly acquired film of a rally for children, held on the second day of Chanukah and attended by participants from all over New York.

2803067.title: Chanukah Gifts
2803067.description: This dollar is for the Menorah you made. It is really worth much more, but I cannot pay its true value!

2803068.title: Stay the Course
2803068.description: When Avraham Infeld agreed to accompany an Israeli dignitary to a meeting with the Rebbe, he had no intention of meeting the Rebbe himself. Little did he know that the trip would not only change his life, but the lives of thousands. (Late 1960s)

2808268.title: The Sun Sets, the Sun Rises
2808268.description: The Chanukah lights are kindled after sundown. In a chasidic discourse delivered in the form of a talk, the Rebbe explains the deeper significance of this custom:
path: The Sun Sets, the Sun Rises

2808269.title: Maariv
2808269.description: Evening prayers held at the Rebbe’s home on President Street during his year of mourning for the Rebbetzin.

2808270.title: Shine Like the Sun
2808270.description: May G-d bless you to irradiate your entire environment with Judaism and prosperity.

2808271.title: The Educator’s Secret
2808271.description: Rabbi Moshe Naparstek, who serves on the faculty of Yeshiva Tomchei Temimim in Kfar Chabad, Isreal, was surprised when during an audience, the Rebbe volunteered advice on the correct approach to education. More than just sound advice, it was a solution to his dilemma. (1960's)

2815188.title: Weapons of Peace
2815188.description: Addressing members of Israel’s Defense Mission in the audience, the Rebbe explains the importance of Israel maintaining a large defense arsenal.

2815189.title: Farbrengen
2815189.description: Yosef Ciechanover, head of Israel’s Defense mission to the United States, shares an exchange with the Rebbe at a farbrengen.

2815190.title: Transformative Vision
2815190.description: When academic and artist, Mel Alexenberg, was considering giving up his position at New York’s Columbia University and relocating to Israel, he and his wife were looking to do something out of the box. As it turned out, the Rebbe had just the idea. (1977)

2815201.title: When the Alter Rebbe Chopped Wood
2815201.description: In the early 1980s, the Rebbe began to speak on the importance of raising awareness about the Seven Laws of Noah among non-Jews.
path: When the Alter Rebbe Chopped Wood

2815202.title: Nigun Daled Bavos
2815202.description: The Nigun of Four Stanzas, composed by the Alter Rebbe.

2815203.title: Make Him Proud
2815203.description: If you remember your forbear, the Alter Rebbe, by acting in a way that makes him proud, he will remember you in return.

2815204.title: Medical Referral
2815204.description: Rabbi Hershel Slansky recalls that when his mother-in-law was diagnosed with a painful condition, and doctors were recommending disfiguring surgery, he encouraged her to go to 770 to see the Rebbe. Expecting a blessing, she returned with a referral instead.

2823541.title: Why Did G-d Punish the Egyptians?
2823541.description: When G-d made His covenant with Abraham, He decreed: “Your children will be enslaved and oppressed for 400 years. But the nation that enslaves them, I will punish.”
path: Why Did G-d Punish the Egyptians?

2823542.title: Farbrengen
2823542.description: Some moments from a newly-acquired silent film of a farbrengen in the summer of 1961, with supplementary audio from the same event.

2823543.title: Making a Tumult
2823543.description: Let the other side make a ruckus; we must make a tumult in Torah and mitzvos – that’s the best way to bring about peace.

2823544.title: Keep the Land
2823544.description: Moshe Ishon, chief editor of the newspaper Hatzofeh in Israel, recalls an audience he had with the Rebbe in the wake of the Six Day War. (1971)

2823559.title: You Can Tip the Scales
2823559.description: Maimonides writes that a Jew must view himself and the entire world as equally balanced between good and evil, and that his every word, thought, and action can have a tremendous impact. In reality however, remaining mindful of this at all times and not losing oneself for even a moment, is a tremendous feat.

2823560.title: Visit of Zalman Shazar, President of Israel
2823560.description: President Zalman Shazar visits the Rebbe in the winter of 1973. The meeting in the Rebbe’s office lasted for over five hours.
path: Visit of Zalman Shazar, President of Israel

2823561.title: Song of Devorah
2823561.description: May you always have a song of praise to sing to G-d for His revealed good.

2823562.title: The Right Question
2823562.description:
Rabbi Joseph Telushkin recalls that when his father, who served as the accountant for Chabad Lubavitch, was hospitalized after a stroke, he received daily phone calls from the Rebbe’s office, inquiring about his progress. Shortly after his father came out of his coma, he received another
call from the Rebbe’s office. This time, it was an accounting query. (1986)

2823568.title: Into the Depths of the Earth
2823568.description: Quoting his father-in-law, Rabbi Yosef Yitzchak Schneerson, the Rebbe declares that our mission today is to reach out to our fellow Jews who are “being held captive” by the forces of assimilation.
path: Into the Depths of the Earth

2823569.title: Nigun – Becho Botchu
2823569.description: At a farbrengen, the Rebbe sings the nigun Becho Botchu, with the words from Psalm 22.

2823570.title: Lasting Impressions
2823570.description: May your memories of my father-in-law, the Rebbe, have a good impact on you. You should make him proud.

2823571.title: In the Beginning
2823571.description: Reb Moshe Chaim Sapochkinsky recalls traveling to New York in honor of the first yahrzeit of Rabbi Yosef Yitzchak Schneerson, the Previous Rebbe. He was present at the historic event when a group of elder chasidim petitioned the Rebbe to accept the leadership of ChabadLubavitch, which the Rebbe had previously declined to do. (1951)

2823584.title: How the Alter Rebbe Gave Away His Dowry to Jewish Farmers
2823584.description:
When the match was proposed between the Alter Rebbe, the founder of Chabad Lubavitch, and Shterna, the daughter of one of the wealthiest Jews of his day, the Alter Rebbe set a tough precondition: His dowry was to be used to help settle poor Jews on the land, and help them earn
a livelihood.
path: How the Alter Rebbe Gave Away His Dowry to Jewish Farmers

2823585.title: Morning Prayers
2823585.description: The Rebbe leads morning prayers on the fourth yahrzeit of his wife, Rebbetzin Chaya Mushka

2823586.title: Everlasting Bond
2823586.description: At a wedding, we hear it said that a marriage is “an everlasting edifice.” This holds true even in the face of a tragedy which seems to contradict it.

2823587.title: She Taught Us to Appreciate the Mainstay of the Home
2823587.description: Louise Hager, who developed a close relationship with the Rebbe’s wife, Rebbetzin Chaya Mushka, recalls speaking about her for the first time in public, and relates some important lessons the Rebbetzin taught her. (1991)
path: She Taught Us to Appreciate the Mainstay of the Home

2858761.title: Unethical Experiments
2858761.description: There is a school of thought that in order to bring close “alienated” Jews we must go to them with an abridged and reformed version of Torah. But others have tried this approach before them.

2858762.title: Distribution of Dollars
2858762.description: The Rebbe distributes dollars to participants in the International Conference of Shluchos.

2858764.title: We are Together
2858764.description: Rabbi Noson Gurary shares two unique and candid audiences he had with the Rebbe after he and his wife set out on shlichus and established the Chabad Student Center near the campus of New York State University, Buffalo. (1970s)

2858778.title: The Inner Moses
2858778.description: The seventh of Adar marks the birth of Moses, which came in the wake of Pharaoh’s decree that all newborn Jewish boys be cast into the Nile. It was not only a decree against the Jews as a whole; it was a decree targeted specifically against Moses himself.

2858779.title: Farbrengen: Georgian Song
2858779.description: The Rebbe asks a recent emigrant from Georgia to sing a traditional song of the Georgian Jews.

2858780.title: Our Family in Georgia
2858780.description: Geographically, the Jews of Georgia may be far-away, but they are closer to the Holy Land then we are.

2858781.title: Old Traditions in a New Land
2858781.description: Rabbi Avraham Alashvili relates that when his father, Rabbi Rafael Alashvili, emigrated from his native Georgia to Israel, he travelled to New York to seek the Rebbe’s guidance on adjusting to his new life in the Holy Land, and returned to Israel a changed man. (1973)
path: Old Traditions in a New Land

2858784.title: Why Does Purim Have a Persian Name?
2858784.description: The names of the Jewish festivals and other dates on the Jewish calendar are all in Hebrew, the Holy Tongue. There is, however, one exception: The festival of Purim.
path: Why Does Purim Have a Persian Name?

2858785.title: Nigun Shoshanas Yaakov
2858785.description: The Rebbe instructs chasidim to sing Shoshanas Yaakov, a nigun with words traditionally recited at the conclusion of the Megillah reading.

2858786.title: Chief Profession
2858786.description: You may indeed have a career, but your chief profession is being a Jew and spreading Judaism in your home and all around you.

2858787.title: Bringing it Together
2858787.description: When Rabbi Michael Paley was a physics student at Brandeis University and found himself surrounded by many doubts, a friend and a mentor advised him to see the Rebbe. The short encounter left its impression on the remainder of his life. (1951)

2858799.title: Torah Revolution: Comrades
2858799.description: The Sages list forty eight qualities that one must possess in order to acquire true Torah knowledge. Among them are: “companionship with colleagues” and “discussion with students.” This means that you cannot be satisfied to be passionate in your own study, rather you must engage everyone you can reach in the excitement of Torah, as well.

2858800.title: Purim Farbrengen (Vintage Video)
2858800.description: Unique glimpses of a Purim farbrengen from a newly acquired silent film, with supplementary audio from the same event.

2858801.title: Staying Independent
2858801.description: In order to maintain Israel’s strength and integrity, there must be the resolve to do so by its own government.

2858802.title: We Tried Everything to Have a Child
2858802.description: Dr. Shelli Menachemson and her husband had tried everything they could to have a child, including infertility treatment and a blessing from the Rebbe, but there seemed to be no success. After another failed pregnancy, they reluctantly turned to the Rebbe again. (1989)
path: We Tried Everything to Have a Child

2889241.title: An Important Reminder
2889241.description: At the conclusion of every farbrengen, the Rebbe would remind those present that whoever is obligated to recite an after-blessing, should make sure to do so.

2889242.title: Making an After-Blessing
2889242.description: A collection of scenes through the years where the Rebbe reminds chasidim to recite the afterblessing.

2889243.title: An Auspicious Month
2889243.description: May you share joyous news – the month of Adar brings especially good fortune, as does the following month, Nissan.

2889244.title: Remembering the Law
