2889244.description: Jacob Abramczyk recalls being present at a Purim farbrengen when the Rebbe suddenly turned to the distinguished rabbis seated behind him and asked a question in Jewish law, the answer to which almost no one seemed to remember. (Early 1960s)

2889257.title: The Rebbe’s Example
2889257.description: Rabbi Menachem Mendel of Lubavitch, known as the Tzemach Tzedek, lived at a time when the Jews of the Russian Empire faced many anti-Semitic decrees at the hands of the czars.

2889258.title: Sending Matzos to Israel
2889258.description: The Rebbe separates challah from baked matzos and oversees as they are packed and sent off to the Holy Land.

2889260.title: No, There is Hope! - Part One
2889260.description: When one year old Amina Schochet was badly burned, doctors were in doubt whether she would survive the day. When her father turned to the Rebbe, he offered a more positive prognosis and instructed the family to make a kiddush that Shabbos. (1951)
path: No, There is Hope! - Part One

2889262.title: Is There a Right Time to Retire?
2889262.description: On the occasion of his eightieth birthday, the Rebbe gives spirited advice to those approaching the age of retirement.
path: Is There a Right Time to Retire?

2889263.title: Farbrengen
2889263.description: Newly discovered film of a farbrengen on the occasion of the Rebbe’s seventy-fourth birthday shows chasidim and well-wishers presenting gifts to the Rebbe.

2889264.title: The Rebbe’s Shliach
2889264.description: Rabbi Schneier of Park East Synagogue tells the Rebbe of his encounter with a young “Chabad representative” in Moscow.

2889265.title: No, There is Hope! - Part Two
2889265.description: When one year old Amina Schochet sustained critical burns, her family followed the Rebbe’s advice and, with heavy hearts, prepared a kiddush on Shabbos. Later, when little Amina suffered another setback, the family again turned to the Rebbe. (1951)
path: No, There is Hope! - Part Two

2889280.title: An Eternal Covenant
2889280.description: Torah sources relate that when G-d took His people out of Egypt and split the sea for them, the prosecuting angels objected. How were the Jewish people any more worthy of redemption than their pursuers? Had not both served idols in Egypt?

2889281.title: Passover 1962
2889281.description: Newly acquired film of the Rebbe distributing matza the day before Passover, and the morning prayers during the intermediate days of the festival. Rabbi Ahron Goldstein, who was present, and whose father filmed these scenes, provides a running commentary. (1962)

2889282.title: Dispelling Fear
2889282.description: Tell your brother to continue the tradition of the great sages who lived in Bnei Brak – they were not afraid of the Romans!

2889283.title: At the Rebbe’s Seder
2889283.description: Rabbi Yosef Yitzchak Offen recalls being present at the Rebbe’s Passover seder, and describes how the Rebbe recited the Haggadah. (Late 1960s)

2920436.title: Redemption and the Real World
2920436.description: The Evil Inclination may approach a Jew and claim, “You’ve been busy studying Torah and doing mitzvos – but I’ve been out there in the real world. There are so many other nations, so many influences which oppose Torah study and Jewish observance. You can sit in the synagogue or the study hall and ‘await his coming every day’… But the world seems to show an entirely different reality!”

2920437.title: Nigun Al Achas
2920437.description: Chasidim sing a song with words from the Passover Haggadah at a farbrengen in honor of the Rebbe’s seventy-fourth birthday.

2920438.title: His Real Life
2920438.description: You should publicize Professor Lieberman’s work so that his students will see that his real passion was in Torah and mitzvos.

2920439.title: A Double Portion of Blessing
2920439.description: When Shraga Jameson and his wife experienced a personal tragedy, they decided to travel to the Rebbe in search of some solace. After a seemingly uneventful first encounter, they decided to write the Rebbe about their troubles. (1990)

2920452.title: Grabbing the Opportunity
2920452.description: Rabbi Shmuel of Lubavitch, the Rebbe Maharash, would travel extensively throughout Europe and the Russian Empire to advocate for his fellow Jews in Russian lands.

2920453.title: Evening Prayers
2920453.description: On the occasion of the birthday of the Rebbe Maharash, the Rebbe delivers a talk and distributes dollars after evening prayers in his home.

2920454.title: Charity for All
2920454.description: You should encourage everyone you encounter at the hospital to give charity. There is an opinion in the Talmud that the non-Jews are also obligated in this commandment.

2920455.title: Trouble in Tanzania
2920455.description: Ephraim Katz recalls a hapless business trip he took to Tanzania to purchase gemstones. Luckily, it turned out to be very lucrative – but only thanks to the Rebbe’s blessing and guidance along the way. (1980's)

2920459.title: The Greatest Job
2920459.description: The Mishna states in Ethics of the Fathers: “Any Torah study that is not combined with work will not endure.” Elsewhere, the Talmud asserts that man was created for toil in Torah.

2920460.title: Nigun Hinei Mah Tov
2920460.description: Chasidim sing a nigun with words from Psalm 133: “Behold how good and how pleasant it is when brothers dwell together.”

2920461.title: Nothing to Fear
2920461.description: It turned out that all the fears were unfounded. If only people had such fear of God!

2920462.title: A Joint Effort
2920462.description: Stanley Abramowitz frequently traveled to North Africa on behalf of the Joint Distribution Committee, where he found himself working side by side with Chabad. Impressed, he decided to meet the man behind the operation. (1950s)

2920474.title: Spiritual Sustenance
2920474.description: After the Talmudic sage Rabbi Shimon Bar Yochai committed the Zohar to writing, he was informed by Heaven: “With this book of yours the Jewish people will be sustained.”

2920475.title: On the Study of Chasidus
2920475.description: An excerpt from the visit of Rabbi Yissachar Dov Rokeach, the Belzer Rebbe.

2920476.title: The Start of a Career
2920476.description: When Rabbi Immanuel Schochet became engaged to be married, he decided to drop college to pursue a business opportunity. “If there is no livelihood, there is no Torah,” he reasoned. The Rebbe had a different plan. (1960's)

2943733.title: Rabbi Shimon’s Joy
2943733.description: On Lag B’omer, Rabbi Shimon ben Yochai proclaimed: “This is the day of my rejoicing!” What was it that made Rabbi Shimon so joyful?

2943734.title: Parade and Fair
2943734.description: A newly acquired film showing a rare glimpse of the Rebbe visiting the Lag B’omer fair in Prospect Park.

2943735.title: Thirteen Channels of Blessing
2943735.description: When Reb Berel Wiess, a successful businessman, asked the Rebbe for a blessing to have both wealth and Torah knowledge, the Rebbe told him that this particular blessing requires a special vessel which Reb Berel was yet to acquire. (1980's)

2946204.title: It’s Up to G-d!
2946204.description: The Sotah woman is estranged from her husband, like the Jewish people during our long exile.

2946205.title: N’shei Chabad convention
2946205.description: The Rebbe addresses the annual convention of the N’shei Chabad women’s organization in 770, and distributes dollars to participants.

2946206.title: The World was Created for You
2946206.description: Me’or Enayim, the name of your yeshiva, is connected to the giving of the Torah. So the festival of Shavuos has special meaning for you.
path: The World was Created for You

2946207.title: Missing in Action
2946207.description: During his year as a student in 770, Amram Malka was often enlisted to help in the Rebbe’s secretariat, and assisted at the Rebbe’s table during all festival meals – except for the second night of Shavous. (1966)

2946219.title: Speak Like a Chasid
2946219.description: The Talmudic tractate Pirkei Avos is a guide to higher ethical conduct. It does not deal with the basic tenets of Jewish law. Pirkei Avos is concerned with matters that go beyond the letter of the law.

2946220.title: Motzaei Shavuos Farbrengen
2946220.description: A rare film featuring a Shavuos farbrengen filmed after nightfall from the women’s gallery. This is the only known recording of this farbrengen.

2946221.title: A Small, Strong Government
2946221.description: As a member of Likud, you are probably aware that I have always favored a narrow, strong government.

2946222.title: Sing Your Way to Success, Part 1
2946222.description: When Cantor Berel Zaltzman first arrived from the Soviet Union, the Rebbe asked him to sing numerous times during his distribution of wine at the conclusion of Rosh Hashanah. At his first audience, Rabbi Zaltzman finally understood the Rebbe’s intentions. (1970's)
path: Sing Your Way to Success, Part 1

2946224.title: Life on the Edge
2946224.description: When a person is involved in Torah study, he need not be cautioned to avoid unholy preoccupations, his Torah protects him – he is in the “Holy Land”. But when it comes to a Jew’s mundane affairs, he must know that Torah draws a line of distinction:

2946225.title: Nigun
2946225.description: Chasidim sing a nigun with words from the Rosh Hashanah liturgy at a farbrengen in 770.

2946226.title: Standing Together
2946226.description: May the mere knowledge that the Anti-Defamation League supports our community be enough to deter those who may wish to hurt us.

2946227.title: Sing Your Way to Success, Part 2
2946227.description: Cantor Berel Zaltzman was too busy adjusting to his new life in Israel and struggling to make a living to realize that the Rebbe had already given him the key to his success. (1970's)
path: Sing Your Way to Success, Part 2

2969752.title: A Call for Unity
2969752.description: At the Exodus from Egypt the Jews experienced true unity. The experience at Sinai caused them to become one. In order to order bring this into practical reality today, in a way that even a child can appreciate, it needs to involve something tangible.

2969753.title: Torah Reading
2969753.description: The Rebbe is called up to a new Torah scroll written for Chabad of Springfield, Massachusetts.

2969754.title: A Gift that Keeps Giving
2969754.description: When you donate a Torah scroll, whenever it is read, wherever it is read, it is done so in your merit.

2969755.title: The Power of a Letter – Part I
2969755.description: Rabbi Shmuel Greisman recalls some of the special instructions he received from the Rebbe as he began to direct the new campaign for Jewish children to own a letter in a Torah scroll. (1981)
path: The Power of a Letter – Part I

2971924.title: Chassidic Coal Miners
2971924.description: The Previous Rebbe gives a parable for what it means to be a Chabad chasid.

2971925.title: Public Audience
2971925.description: A farewell audience for guests that came to spend Shavuos with the Rebbe.

2971926.title: Ask for Your Needs
2971926.description: You know what your needs are, and G-d knows what your needs are, so He will certainly fulfill them.

2971927.title: The Power of a Letter – Part II
2971927.description: Rabbi Shmuel Greisman relates that after initiating the campaign for the children’s Torah scroll, the Rebbe urged all Jews to participate in signing up as many children as possible. Speaking about the campaign on numerous occasions, the Rebbe and stressed that a display of unity would help avert a threat over the Jewish people. (1981)
path: The Power of a Letter – Part II

2971939.title: A Shepherd of Israel
2971939.description: The definition of a true Jewish leader is not his lofty personal level, as the head and soul of the people. Rather, that he is able to descend and relate to “the body,” to each of his students and followers on their own level.

2971940.title: Being a Part of the Story
2971940.description: A special presentation in honor of Gimmel Tammuz, the anniversary of the Rebbe’s passing.
path: Being a Part of the Story

2971944.title: Never Too Young
2971944.description: Long before his bar mitzvah, the Previous Rebbe was already preoccupied with doing acts of kindness. At age eleven he established a free-loan fund, allowing him to help the needy in a dignified manner.

2971945.title: Beinoni Nigun
2971945.description: Chasidim sing the Beinoni Nigun at a farbrengen marking the liberation of Rabbi Yosef Yitzchak, the sixth Lubavitcher Rebbe, from Soviet imprisonment.

2971946.title: Good Beginning
2971946.description: May all of your achievements until now serve as a good start.

2971947.title: Together in Thought
2971947.description: Rabbi Pinchos Baumgarten relates that the Rebbe asked his father to visit Jews scattered in rural Argentina and Brazil. Finding himself alone on the anniversary of the Previous Rebbe’s release from Soviet imprisonment, a day celebrated by chasidim, he decided to send the Rebbe a telegram. (1950's)

2996474.title: Soaring Letters – Part I
2996474.description: When Moses descended Mount Sinai and saw the people worshipping a golden calf, he shattered the Ten Commandments.

2996475.title: Reading of the Fast-Day Haftarah
2996475.description: The Rebbe recites the Haftorah for fast days during the afternoon prayers.

2996476.title: Unbroken Tablets
2996476.description: Now is an auspicious time for the Jewish people. We are in the forty days after Moses descended from Mount Sinai.

2996477.title: On the Straight and Narrow
2996477.description: Mrs. Mariashi Groner, now the co-director of Lubavitch of North Carolina and director of the Charlotte Jewish Day School, recalls turning to the Rebbe during a difficult time in her teens. (1976)

3002752.title: Soaring Letters – Part II
3002752.description: At the sin of the golden calf, only three thousand Jews actually sinned. The vast majority of the Jews did not participate. Why did G-d hold the entire people responsible for what transpired, and deserving of punishment?

3002753.title: A Visit to Remember
3002753.description: Newly discovered film of the Rebbe’s third visit to Camp Gan Israel in Swan Lake, New York, accompanied by an interview with Rabbi Tzvi Telsner, who was a camper at the time.

3002754.title: Going to Camp
3002754.description: To a camp nurse: Take this dollar for your work, and may G-d bless you to have no patients!

3002755.title: The Beginning of Camp
3002755.description: When Rabbi Moshe Lazar was a yeshiva student in his late teens, he wrote to the Rebbe with the idea of opening a Chabad summer camp for Jewish children – an initiative the Rebbe embraced. (Mid 1950's)

3002770.title: The Root of the Problem
3002770.description: When one looks at the world today, one sees increasing crime as well as unprecedented friction between various segments in society.

3002771.title: We Want Moshiach Now!
3002771.description: Chasidim sing the lively song, “We Want Moshiach Now!” at a farbrengen.

3002772.title: Preparing for Moshiach
3002772.description: Of the days between the Seventeenth of Tammuz and the Ninth of Av it is written, “Zion will be redeemed in judgment, and its captives with tzedaka,” so charity is very timely.

3002773.title: A Niche Market
3002773.description: When Mr. Bernard Perrin was having trouble with his fur business, he followed the advice of a friend and wrote to the Rebbe, only to receive a most unexpected response.

3002775.title: Rebuilding the Temple
3002775.description: The Jerusalem Talmud states: “If the Holy Temple is not rebuilt in your lifetime, it’s as though it were destroyed in your lifetime.” The commentaries learn from this that the Temple’s destruction is an ongoing event.

3002776.title: Tisha B'Av
3002776.description: Scenes from Tisha B’Av services conducted in the Rebbe’s home. In 1988 the fast was observed on the tenth of Av, as the ninth was Shabbos.

3002777.title: Following Instructions
3002777.description: Did you ask for your doctor’s approval of before deciding to set off on your trip?

3002778.title: The Full Picture
3002778.description: When Rabbi Shlomo Jakobovits was a student at Yeshiva University, he asked the Rebbe a series of questions in an audience which lasted over two hours. (1953)

3024077.title: Giving of Oneself
3024077.description: The passing of the Rebbe’s father, Rabbi Levi Yitzchok Schneerson, is marked on the 20th of Av. He was imprisoned and exiled to Kazakhstan for his stance against Soviet efforts to uproot Jewish learning and practice.

3024078.title: Chof Av Farbrengen With the Rebbe
3024078.description: During a farbrengen marking the passing of the Rebbe’s father, Rabbi Levi Yitzchak Schneerson, the Rebbe accepts pledges to a charity fund established in his name.
path: Chof Av Farbrengen With the Rebbe

3024079.title: No Reason to Fear
3024079.description: There is no need to scare the patient with a negative prognosis. Seek out a doctor who is caring, but not emotionally involved.

3024080.title: Unbroken Spirit
3024080.description: Reb Gedaliah Mazal shares his memories of the arrival of Rabbi Levi Yitzchak Schneerson, the Rebbe’s father, in Alamty, Kazakhstan. Reb Gedaliah’s father became close to Rabbi Levi Yitzchak, and was present at his passing. (1940's)

3028552.title: A Higher Form of Giving
3028552.description: When the Jewish people returned from their exile in Babylon, there was a shortage of wood for the altar in the Holy Temple.

3028553.title: The Rebbe Distributing Charity
3028553.description: A special collage featuring unique scenes of the Rebbe distributing charity.

3028554.title: Closing Shop
3028554.description: Ami Pykovski, the proprietor of a large clothing store in downtown Los Angeles, found himself grappling with the idea of closing his store on Shabbos. Torn between his business and a growing commitment to Judaism, he decided to write to the Rebbe. (1980s)

3033238.title: Consecrating the Inner Self
3033238.description: The Torah provides a strict warning that offerings may not be brought outside the Holy Temple. Among the rituals performed in the Temple were the placing of the blood and fat of an offering on the Altar.

3033239.title: Nigun
3033239.description: A lively scene of a nigun being sung at a farbrengen, featuring never-before-released footage.

3033240.title: Gate of Redemption
3033240.description: The Zohar alludes that Tractate Bava Basra, “The Last Gate,” is connected to the final redemption.

3033241.title: Atomic Energy
3033241.description: Overwhelmed by mounting questions about his work in the rabbinate and Jewish outreach, as well as in his business, Rabbi David Lapin sought advice from the Rebbe.

3033256.title: The Apple of His Eye
3033256.description: The month of Elul is a time for repentance and introspection before the coming of Rosh Hashanah. Yet there are some who use this time of year to chastise their congregations instead of inspiring them.

3033257.title: Tishrei with the Rebbe
3033257.description: An excerpt from the JEM film, Tishrei with the Rebbe, Volume I, featuring inspiring scenes from the month of Elul.

3033258.title: A Sacred Task
3033258.description: A shochet has the opportunity to draw his fellow Jews closer to Judaism. The Hebrew word “shochat – slaughter,” also means to “draw close.”

3033259.title: Fomenting Revolution
3033259.description:
After calling for revolution at an anti- Vietnam War rally, Larry Caroline lost his position as a philosophy professor at the University of Texas, and his academic career. After making his journey to Judaism and reporting the events to the Rebbe almost a decade later, he was encouraged to
remain a radical.

3046516.title: Full Time Study
3046516.description: Torah describes the symbiotic relationship between the sea-faring tribe of Zevulun and the scholarly tribe of Issachar. Zevulun supported the Torah study of Issachar, and shared in the merit of that study.

3046517.title: Niggun Ribono Shel Olam
3046517.description: Chasidim sing the rousing melody, Ribono Shel Olam, at a farbrengen.

3046518.title: Your Alma Mater
3046518.description: You were a student in the Tomchei Temimim yeshiva. May its effect on you remain strong and shine through in all your work.

3046519.title: Time for Prayer
3046519.description: Rabbi Meir Tzvi Gruzman taught a class of adolescent yeshiva boys. When he noticed that his encouragement of “chasidic prayer” was not always having the desired results, he decided to bring the issue up in an audience with the Rebbe.(1960's)

3046545.title: Changing History
3046545.description: The Alter Rebbe assures us in Tanya that the efforts of those who follow in his ways, inspiring their fellow Jews to return to G-d, will have an “eternal” effect.

3046546.title: Selichos
3046546.description: Scenes of selichos, a series of penitential prayers recited in the days leading up to Rosh Hashana.

3046547.title: Moving Forward
3046547.description: We have a promise from G-d Almighty that one who comes to be purified receives the assistance he needs to be able to do so.

3046548.title: A Vote of Confidence, Part I
3046548.description: Rabbi Simon Jacobson recalls the visit of the controversial Israeli writer, Natan Yellin-Mor, to his home one Rosh Hashanah, and the fateful exchange the writer shared with the Rebbe at the conclusion of the festival.(1977)
path: A Vote of Confidence, Part I

3046550.title: The Jewish Mother: Partners with G-d
3046550.description: The Haftorah of the first day of Rosh Hashanah relates the story of Chana, a childless woman who entreated G-d for a son at the Tabernacle in Shiloh. Eventually she gave birth to a son who would become the prophet Shmuel.
path: The Jewish Mother: Partners with G-d

3046551.title: Erev Rosh Hashanah, 5736
3046551.description: Morning prayers on the day preceding Rosh Hashanah, followed by the ceremony for the Annulment of Vows.

3046552.title: A Good Cantor
3046552.description: It is more important to consider the cantor’s feelings when he prays, than the quality of his voice.

3046553.title: A Vote of Confidence, Part II
3046553.description: Rabbi Simon Jacobson relates that a few years after his father introduced the writer Natan Yellin-Mor to the Rebbe, he received an envelope from the ailing writer. Inside was a request that its contents be published after the writer’s death.(Early 1980s)
path: A Vote of Confidence, Part II

3046567.title: A Holy Assembly
3046567.description: When the Temple stood in Jerusalem, every seven years all Jewish men women and children would ascend the Temple Mount to hear the king of Israel read the Torah in fulfillment of the verse, “Assemble the people, men, women, and children… in order that they learn to fear G-d and do all the words of his Torah.”

3046568.title: Erev Yom Kippur, 5747
3046568.description: The Rebbe delivers his blessing to the students of the Tomchei Temimim yeshiva before the onset of Yom Kippur.

3046569.title: One Prayer for All
3046569.description: The High Priest on Yom Kippur would utter one prayer and affect every Jew – including those not aware of its contents.

3046570.title: A Heartfelt Prayer
3046570.description: Rabbi Yossi Baumgarten would often seek out the company of a newcomer to 770, a basketball coach by the name of Abe Sacks. As it turns out, the Rebbe shared his affinity for this Jew.(1970's)

3077583.title: Swords into Palm Branches
3077583.description: In an army, soldiers are given special tents, designated living quarters. They possess special weaponry so they can carry out their mission effectively and win their battles. And when they want to demonstrate their victory, they parade around and display all their weaponry.

3077584.title: Sukkos Gathering
3077584.description: The Rebbe addresses a special gathering for New York public school children from the Released Time program in the sukkah outside 770.

3077585.title: Begin Rejoicing Now
3077585.description: Now is the time to begin rejoicing, and when Sukkos arrives you should increase in joy.

3077586.title: When the Time Comes
3077586.description: Sam Friedland recalls that when he suggested making changes in the family business to his father, he was instructed to ask the Rebbe for his opinion. Aware of the Rebbe’s saintliness and scholarship, he could not help but wonder what the Rebbe could possibly know about his father’s small company. (1980's)

3077600.title: The Humble Willow
3077600.description: The seventh day of Sukkos is known as Hoshana Raba, during which we fulfill the custom of making seven circuits around the bima while holding the Four Species and reciting prayers for blessing and prosperity in the coming year.

3077601.title: Distribution of Lekach
3077601.description: A special collage featuring scenes of the Rebbe distributing lekach, or honey cake, for a sweet new year.

3077602.title: Where Everything seems Right
3077602.description: Leah Aizenman arrived in New York from Tel Aviv to discover that her sister’s home served as a stop for guests coming from all over the world to spend the High Holidays with the Rebbe. On Hoshana Raba, after feeding an endless flow of people, she ran to 770 toward the end of the Rebbe’s distribution of honey cake for a sweet new year. Fortunately, she was too late. (1976)

3077604.title: What Is Our Right to the Land?
3077604.description: Torah is replete with references about the special connection of the Jewish people to the Land of Israel. Yet Rashi, the foremost commentator of Torah, sees it in the very first words of the book of Genesis: “In the beginning G-d created the heavens and the Earth.”
path: What Is Our Right to the Land?

3077605.title: Farbrengen
3077605.description: Scenes from a farewell farbrengen held in honor of guests from around the world who came to spend the month of Tishrei with the Rebbe.

3077606.title: True Protection
3077606.description: If the Israel Defense Forces are to live up to their name, they must also be active in defending the fabric of Jewish life –Torah and mitzvos.

3077607.title: Speaking the Truth
3077607.description: Rabbi Mordechai Piron recalls that when he served as chief rabbi of the Israel Defense Forces, he faced a moral dilemma and sought the Rebbe’s advice. He knew in his heart that the guidance he was hearing seemed right on the mark, but to what extent, he would only realize when he returned to Israel. (Early 1970's)

3077621.title: Why Does G-d Make It Hard?
3077621.description: We are presented with many opportunities to partner with G-d in creation. Some of these opportunities lie in our most difficult challenges, which serve as reminders that G-d created a world which is in need of perfection.
path: Why Does G-d Make It Hard?

3077622.title: Walking to 770
3077622.description: Unique vintage scenes of the Rebbe walking to 770 from his home on President Street. (1960's)

3077623.title: Toil and You Shall Find
3077623.description: You have had to overcome many difficulties; may you now see much success.

3077624.title: Focus on Healing
3077624.description: When Arnold Dalfen was told by his doctor that he would not be able to have children, the Rebbe referred him to another specialist. When that doctor arrived at the same conclusion, the Rebbe asked him to simply focus on the healing. (1950's)

3107135.title: Nature and Nurture
3107135.description: Every child has natural born traits, some positive, some negative. As the child grows and develops, it is the parent’s sacred duty to reinforce the positive ones, and address the negative ones.

3107136.title: Nigun Simcha
3107136.description: Chasidim sing a lively nigun at a farbrengen in honor of Yud Tes Kislev.

3107138.title: A Sign Upon Your Arm, Part I
3107138.description: When Rabbi Shimon Lazaroff discovered that Dr. Milton Nirken, the pediatrician that treated his children, had suffered a sudden paralysis of his left arm, he assured the doctor that he would seek a blessing from the Rebbe on his behalf. (1970s)
path: A Sign Upon Your Arm, Part I

3107152.title: The Power of One
3107152.description: In the book of Joshua, G-d declares, “I multiplied Abraham’s seed, and gave him Isaac.” Yet how can Isaac, one son, be seen as the “multiplication of seed” promised by G-d?

3107153.title: Walking to the Library
3107153.description: Rare footage showing the Rebbe distributing coins to children before the onset of Shabbos, as he walks to the Chabad library housed next door to 770, where he would spend Shabbos.

3107154.title: City of Abraham
3107154.description: Be’er Sheva is named for the covenant Abraham made there with Abimelech. Just as then, the Jewish people in Israel need not relinquish anything to secure peace.

3107155.title: A Sign Upon Your Arm, Part II
3107155.description: When neurologists could do nothing about his paralysis, Dr. Milton Nirken turned to Rabbi Shimon Lazaroff, who then turned to the Rebbe for a blessing. After receiving a phone call from the Rebbe’s office late one night, he called Dr. Nirken to relay the Rebbe’s words. Dr. Nirken, however, had news of his own. (1970s)
path: A Sign Upon Your Arm, Part II

3107159.title: This Is No Time for Prayer
3107159.description: Three days after leaving Egypt to receive the Torah, the Jewish people found themselves trapped between the Red Sea and Pharaoh’s army, which was fast approaching.
path: This Is No Time for Prayer

3107160.title: Morning Prayers
3107160.description: The Rebbe takes part in morning services on Rosh Chodesh Kislev, including scenes of Hallel.

3107161.title: God’s Blessings
3107161.description: Being a community leader yourself, I don’t have to tell you that the best service you can do for a Jew is to develop his potential.

3107162.title: Encouraging Words
3107162.description: Rabbi Yehoshua Gordon relates that when he and his family were facing a difficult challenge in their work as Chabad emissaries, his wife wrote to the Rebbe for advice and blessing. To this day, the words of the Rebbe’s response hang framed in Rabbi Gordon’s office.

3107177.title: You Can Be a Hakhel Jew
3107177.description: The Rebbe points out that every one of us must be a clarion call for gathering, just like every priest was to herald Hakhel in the Temple.
path: You Can Be a Hakhel Jew

3107178.title: Children’s Rally
3107178.description: The Rebbe takes part in a rally for children returning from summer camp, just before the end of the year of hakhel.

3107179.title: Be Active in Hakhel
3107179.description: Distribution of dollars after a general audience for guests who had arrived to spend the month of Tishrei with the Rebbe.

3107180.title: Assembling the Nation
3107180.description: When Rabbi Tuvia Blau told the Rebbe that he hoped that his wife and children would have the experience of meeting him, the Rebbe suggested that he bring his family in for hakhel. This was not an easy feat for a family of seven from Israel, in the 1970s

3137538.title: Good Beginnings
3137538.description: When the Mitteler Rebbe was a young child about to begin his Jewish education, the Alter Rebbe, his father gave specific instruction to his teacher on how to proceed with the very first lesson.

3137539.title: Nigun Podoh B’sholom
3137539.description: The Rebbe requests chasidim to sing the song Podoh B’sholom in honor of the Mitteler Rebbe’s birthday and anniversary of passing.

3137540.title: Promoting Torah
3137540.description: Simply publishing a Torah book is not enough today. In our times, you need to advertise it and publicize its contents.

3137541.title: You are with Us
3137541.description: Israel Adamski grew up in Dnepropetrovsk, Ukraine, where the Rebbe’s father served as Rabbi. Although the Rebbe was married in faraway Warsaw, Mr. Adamski remembers the celebration that took place the night of the wedding in the Rebbe’s parent’s home. (1928)

3144757.title: By Natural Means
3144757.description: Although the Alter Rebbe was known for his piety and greatness in Torah, he also gained a reputation as a miracle worker.

3144758.title: Farbrengen
3144758.description: Vintage color footage featuring scenes from the conclusion of a farbrengen in honor of Yud Tes Kislev.

3144759.title: Differences Aside
3144759.description: Since Chabad chasidim befriended your ancestor despite their differences, you should befriend Chabad chasidim.

3144760.title: A Chapter a Day
3144760.description: Rabbi Nissen Mangel recalls that shortly after the Rebbe sent him to Lakewood, New Jersey, to teach chasidic philosophy in a non-chasidic yeshiva, he was approached by an impatient student eager to study Tanya – at one o’clock in the morning. (Late 1950s)

3144773.title: Spreading the Light
3144773.description: Bread, water, wine, and oil represent various dimensions in Torah.

3144774.title: Chanukah Live - 5751-1990
3144774.description: Scenes from a “Chanukah Live” celebration which was telecast simultaneously all over the world.

3144775.title: A Year of Light
3144775.description: May the miracle of Chanukah serve as a precedent for bringing light into the entire year.

3144776.title: At Just the Right Time
3144776.description: Rabbi Yechezkel Sofer relates that when he tried convincing his father to write a letter to the Rebbe, his father was skeptical that he would receive a response. When Rabbi Sofer finally succeeded but no reply was forthcoming, he couldn’t help but wonder whether his father was right. (Mid 1960s)

3144778.title: Chanukah Fun and Games
3144778.description: It is customary on Chanukah to organize special gatherings for children. It is also the custom to make family gatherings which include activities such as playing dreidel, staging plays and distributing Chanukah gelt.

3144779.title: Farbrengen
3144779.description: Scenes from a farbrengen held in honor of Chanukah.

3144780.title: Living with Miracles
3144780.description: The miracle of Chanukah lasted eight days, but its message must accompany the Jewish people all throughout the year.

3144781.title: Positive Thinking
3144781.description: Rabbi Avraham Rottenberg recalls that when he received word from Israel that his father had suffered a heart attack, the Rebbe insisted that he take the oldest medicine in the book, and to good effect. (Late 1950s)

3169841.title: Preparing for Famine
3169841.description: In an address to children, the Rebbe encourages every Jew, wherever he may be, to take the example of Joseph during his exile in Egypt. Joseph had the foresight to collect and store the country’s grain during the seven years of plenty not only in order to save Egypt, but to supply grain to all the neighboring lands during the seven years of famine which followed.

3169842.title: Selichos
3169842.description: An audio recording of the Rebbe reciting penitential prayers on the Fast of the Tenth of Teves. Commentary by Rabbi Shlomo Zarchi who was a yeshiva student at the time.

3169843.title: Doing the Impossible
3169843.description: “You have done so many impossible things, why not do one more?”

3169844.title: A Bright Future
3169844.description: During a polio outbreak in the United States in the 1950s, Rabbi Yechiel Ziskind contracted the dreaded disease and found himself paralyzed in an iron lung. While doctors were losing hope, the Rebbe had bright plans for the future. (Mid 1950s)

3177249.title: The Best Defense
3177249.description: The Talmud teaches, “If someone rises to kill you, rise up to kill him first.” The Rebbe explains that this dictum of our sages is the only way for Israel to deal with its enemies who seek its destruction.

3177250.title: Street Scene
3177250.description: Rare film of people approaching the Rebbe for blessings as he leaves the mikvah on Union Street. Mo Gelber, who filmed the scene, recalls the story behind it in his commentary. (Winter 1989)

3177251.title: Safe for Travel
3177251.description: Simply tell your parents that you wish to spend Passover in Israel because it is a Holy Land and a Jewish land.

3177252.title: A Global Responsibility
3177252.description: When Ovadia Eli met the Rebbe shortly after his appointment as the Deputy Defense Minister of Israel, he was surprised to hear the Rebbe say that all of the world’s Jews are under his watch, not just those living in the Holy Land. As it turns out, the Rebbe’s words had far reaching effects. (1991)

3177269.title: Two Luminaries
3177269.description: There are many similarities between Maimonides and the Alter Rebbe, the Founder of Chabad chasidism. They both issued decisions on Jewish law that guide all later generations.

3177270.title: Nigun
3177270.description: Recently restored film of the Rebbe leading chasidim in the lively song, Nye Zhuritze Chloptzi, originally sung by the second Chabad Rebbe’s chasidim on the way to Lubavitch.

3177271.title: The Other Wellsprings
3177271.description: Much success in spreading the chasidic wellsprings. This includes Jewish law, not just philosophy. (June 1989)

3177272.title: An Unexpected Letter
3177272.description: Rabbi Avraham Chaputa recalls a fateful audience he had with Rebbe when he was the dean of a fledgling yeshiva in Tel Aviv. The consequences of that audience only became clear to him many decades later. (1973)

3177276.title: A Sense of Entitlement
3177276.description: The book of Genesis relates that “the heart of man is evil from his youth,” and when one looks around at the world today, it seems to confirm this verse. Yet Torah assures that as a person matures, the good within him develops and he can overcome negative character traits by following God’s commandments.

3177277.title: Nigun Ashreinu
3177277.description: Chasidim sing the joyous song, Ashreinu, at a farbrengen.

3177278.title: Spreading the Peace
3177278.description: This dollar is for your parents, who raised a daughter to do what you are doing.

3177279.title: The Rebbe's Plan to Calm the Streets of New York
3177279.description: Jacob Worenklein, who was an intern at the office of the president of the New York City Council, recalls arranging a meeting between City Council President Francis X. Smith and the Rebbe at a time when New York City was facing a surge in crime. (1969)
path: The Rebbe's Plan to Calm the Streets of New York

3200156.title: On Jewish Leadership
3200156.description: The verse states: “He gave his own bread to the destitute.” The Talmud explains that this refers to Moses giving the Torah to the Jewish people. But every word of the verse is precise:

3200157.title: Evening Prayers
3200157.description: The Rebbe leads evening prayers on Yud Shevat, the anniversary of the passing of his father-in-law and sixth Lubavitcher Rebbe, Rabbi Yosef Yitzchak Schneersohn.

3200158.title: The Blessings Continue
3200158.description: I see that my father-in-law, the Rebbe’s, blessing succeeded. May it continue to succeed for many healthy years.

3200159.title: Twice Blessed
3200159.description: Rhoda Friedland recalls receiving a blessing for children from Rabbi Yosef Yitzchak Schneersohn, the Previous Rebbe. After the Previous Rebbe’s passing, with the blessing yet to materialize, she turned to the Rebbe for help. (Early 1950's)

3206564.title: The Pleasure Principle
3206564.description: The Fifteenth of Shevat celebrates the New Year for Trees and the marks the beginning of a new fruit-bearing cycle in the Holy Land.

3206565.title: Farbrengen
3206565.description: Chasidim sing a lively melody known as a Nigun Rikud Nikolayev during a farbrengen in honor of the New Year for Trees.

3206566.title: Growing in Torah
3206566.description: An increase your study of Torah will bring with it success in other endeavors.

3206567.title: The Heart of the Matter
3206567.description: As a young serviceman in the Israeli Air Force, Moshe Tzur was moved by Chabad’s outreach work. Almost a decade later, when he had a chance to give back to the movement that changed his life, he was even more moved by what he heard from the Rebbe in a private audience. (1970's)

3212656.title: First Defenders
3212656.description: Jewish girls are equal members in Tzivos Hashem. Even though in Torah the “army” is not a place for women, when it comes to a battle of life and death – and the battle against the evil inclination is a battle of survival – the law is different. In that case, even a bride must go from her wedding to take part.

3212657.title: Distribution of Dollars
3212657.description: A collage featuring scenes from the distribution of dollars in the Rebbe’s home on the twenty-ninth of Shevat, a day after the conclusion of shiva for Rebbetzin Chaya Mushka Schneerson. (1988)

3212658.title: In the Merit of Righteous Women
3212658.description: You and I leaving exile is dependent on your wife, along with all Jewish women, in whose merit the Jewish people will be redeemed.
path: In the Merit of Righteous Women

3212659.title: Words of Encouragement
3212659.description: As a young woman, Sarah Rifkah Sassonkin was sent by the Rebbe to be a teacher in Milan, Italy, where her sister and brother-in-law served as shluchim. Overwhelmed by her new responsibilities, she wrote an emotional letter to the Rebbe. (1960)

3212674.title: Serving with Distinction
3212674.description: Soldiers spend most of their time training and carrying out missions. Periodically, they assemble at a parade, where their performance is checked, and medals are awarded.

3212675.title: Machne Israel Development Fund
3212675.description: During a year of hakhel, the Rebbe addresses participants in one of his first meetings with members of the Machne Israel Development Fund.

3212676.title: Don’t Look to Solve Every Issue
3212676.description: To avoid conflict, don’t press to find a solution to every issue. We can leave something for Moshiach to resolve.
path: Don’t Look to Solve Every Issue

3212677.title: Hakhel State of Mind
3212677.description: Rabbi Chaim Benyamini established and headed the Yeshiva in Petropolis, Brazil, for over 30 years. He shares a perplexing encounter with the Rebbe that left him with a penetrating lesson about just how “hakhel-conscious” a Jew can be. (1987)

3226536.title: Thought for the Day
3226536.description: The Ba’al Shem Tov teaches that “a person is where his thoughts are.”

3226537.title: Niggun
3226537.description: Chassidim sing an upbeat Russian nigun during the Rebbe’s distribution of wine at the conclusion of Simchas Torah.

3226538.title: The Properties of Energy
3226538.description: May you succeed in producing so much energy, that you’ll be able to double, triple, and quadruple what you’ve done up until now.

3226539.title: Your Action Is What Counts
3226539.description: Rabbi Chaim Shneor Nisenbaum is a Chabad representative in Paris, France. As a young Rabbi, he approached the Rebbe with a sincere concern; while he felt productive in his work, he was concerned about it inflating his ego. The Rebbe’s clear and direct response shaped the remainder of Rabbi Nisenbaum’s life. (1970s)

3226553.title: Small, Yet Great
3226553.description: According to the Jewish calendar, a second month of Adar is added in a leap year. While Purim is usually celebrated in Adar, during a leap year it is postponed until the second Adar, and we mark Purim Katan—“the small Purim”—in the first month.

3226554.title: Unveiling Ceremony
3226554.description: Scenes from the unveiling ceremony for Rabbi Shemaryahu Gurary, the Rebbe’s brother-in-law.

3226555.title: For Clarity of Mind
3226555.description: It would be good idea to check the mezuzahs in your home. The mezuzah has an affect on one’s thoughts and peace of mind.

3226556.title: Hear O Israel
3226556.description: Soon after they moved to Alabama, Rabbi Stern’s young daughter suffered damage to her ear which resulted in loss of hearing. After going through two surgeries which failed, the Sterns decided to ask the Rebbe for his advice and blessing. (1969)

3226560.title: The Secret to Staying Young
3226560.description: Youth have an important advantage over their older peers. While older people spend much time deliberating over the merits and demerits of ideas, it is the young people that are driven to concrete action.

3226561.title: Niggun Simcha
3226561.description: Chassidim join the Rebbe in singing a joyous melody known a nigun simcha.

3226562.title: Beyond Possibilities
3226562.description: One has to do more than what is possible. Settling for what is possible is within the natural order, but why should a Jew be limited by nature?

3226563.title: A Mission Accomplished
3226563.description:
Rabbi Yoseph Itzhak Gurewitz was part of a delegation sent by the Rebbe sent to study in Israel.When Purim arrived, the Rebbe requested that they bring the joy of the festival to soldiers stationed on bases across Israel.
As the group neared their destination, they came to a makeshift roadblock where they were confronted by a mob of Arab youths. Motivated by their mission and the Rebbe’s words, they forged on with their assignment. (1976)

3226578.title: Hakhel in Our Times
3226578.description: When the Holy Temple stood in Jerusalem, every seven years the entire nation would gather there to hear the Torah read by the king and be inspired in the service of G-d. While the Temple may no longer stand in Jerusalem, it continues to exist spiritually within the heart of every Jew.

3226579.title: Torah Reading
3226579.description: The Rebbe is called up to the Torah during a weekday Torah reading in the small prayer hall in 770.

3226580.title: Your Responsibilities
3226580.description: Cantillation is your expertise. May you have a year of success in doing what the Jewish kings did – reading the Torah before all of Israel.

3226581.title: A Mission Accomplished Part II
3226581.description: Part of a special group charged with visiting soldiers serving in the IDF on the festival of Purim, Rabbi Yosef Yitzchak Gurewitz recalls risking involvement in a dangerous situation in order to carry out his mission. An event the Rebbe used as a lesson in life. (1976)

3256477.title: Joy Reaches Highest
3256477.description:
King David writes, “Serve G-d with joy.”
Our study of Torah, our Jewish intellectual life, our acts of kindness, and our Jewish communal life, must all be infused with joy.

3256478.title: Purim Farbrengen
3256478.description: The Rebbe converses with individuals while chassidim are singing during a Purim farbrengen.

3256479.title: A Joyful Increase - Collage
3256479.description: In general, one should be happy with his lot. But when it comes to charity, and matters of Torah and mitzvos, he should make sure to increase from time to time. The greater the increase, especially if done with joy, the more praiseworthy it is.

3256480.title: On the Other Hand
3256480.description: Rabbi Yisroel Shusterman is left handed. Since mitzvos are usually to be done with the right hand, as a young man, he asked the Rebbe for direction in this matter and about the ramifications of being a lefty. At the time, the Rebbe sent him to the local Rabbinic authority and Rabbi Shusterman all but forgot about the story. Imagine his surprise when the Rebbe made reference to this so many years later. (Early 1970s)

3256503.title: Two Days of Purim
3256503.description: When king Achashverosh gave permission to the Jews fight off their enemies, he allowed an extra day for those in Shushan. The day after Purim, called Shushan Purim, is celebrated to mark this special phenomenon. In a sense this is more than just an historical commemoration; it celebrates the ability in general, to add to good in a meaningful way.

3256504.title: Nigun - Hop Kazak
3256504.description: During a lively Purim farbrengen, the Rebbe enthusiastically encourages the singing of “Hop Kazzak” - a nigun attributed to the “Shpoleh Zeida”.

3256505.title: In Esther’s Merit - Collage
3256505.description: Surely, your wife knows that the savior of all the Jewish people was also named Hadassah. Queen Esther had a second name - Hadassah.

3256506.title: To Every Single Child
3256506.description: Rabbi Yaakov Roth is an educator and teacher Miami, Florida. From time to time, he would have his young students send letters to the Rebbe. The Rebbe’s thoughtful responses were touching and inspiring. (Early 1970s)

3256517.title: Children of Redemption
3256517.description: The festival of Purim has a special connection to young children.

3256518.title: Post Purim Children’s Rally
3256518.description: The Rebbe participates in a lively children’s rally, held just a couple days after Purim.

3256519.title: True to Sephardic Tradition
3256519.description: May all your father’s matters be performed with increased joy. But until then, he should not allow anyone to make decisions for him in a way that does not fit with his will and desire.

3256520.title: Preventive Psychology
3256520.description: Mr. Mordechai Reich is a psychologist practicing in Efrat, Israel, where he lives with his wife and their five children. In the summer of 1974, during a visit with the Rebbe, he asked for advice on what career path he should pursue. The Rebbe’s answer gave him new insight into both psychology and education, and their effect on our society at large. (1974)

3256534.title: The Birthday Campaign
3256534.description: The Previous Rebbe taught that a birthday is a time for introspection, a time to account for the past and make resolutions for the future. It is a most propitious time, for on one’s birthday his “mazel”—his “fortune”—radiates with extra strength.

3256535.title: Cause for Celebration - Collage
3256535.description: Make a gathering; a party in honor of your birthday, and make it large. Remember to give tzedaka at your time of celebration.

3256536.title: House Visits
3256536.description: Dr. Alan Newmark merited to attend to Rebbetzin Chaya Mushkah, the wife of the Rebbe. In this clip, he recalls and shares some of the most memorable conversations that he had with the Rebbetzin, illustrating her sensitivity and care. (1980s)

3296314.title: Seeing the Good
3296314.description:
The Baal Shem Tov teaches that every single Jew is cherished by G-d. This is even more so during exile, when the Jewish people is “afflicted.” When one reaches out to a Jew who is distant and reveals that he, too, is an “only child” of G-d, then G-d’s kindness and compassion for
the entire people become aroused.

3296315.title: The Rebbe Distributes Matzos
3296315.description: The Rebbe personally sends matzos to be used at public Passover Seders around the world.

3296316.title: Spreading the Word
3296316.description: Visitors will be coming, some just before Passover. In addition to organizing a public Seder, you need to ensure that people actually know about it in advance.

3296317.title: Soviet Exodus Part I
3296317.description: Rabbi Gershon Ber Schiff was active in the Jewish underground in the Soviet Union. When he heard that his relative was visiting Moscow from beyond the Iron Curtain, he was torn about whether to put himself and his activities in danger in order to meet - until he heard a message from the Rebbe. (1969)

3296335.title: All Are Welcome
3296335.description: The Haggadah relates that “Torah speaks to four sons”. Although they are all different they are placed one beside the other to emphasize the innate value of each.

3296336.title: Nigun Vehi She'amda
3296336.description: At a farbrengen, chasidim sing Vehi Sheomdo, a melody from the Haggadah taught by the Rebbe in 1955.

3296337.title: Asking the Four Questions
3296337.description: A collection of scenes of the Rebbe encouraging children to recite the Mah Nishtana, or Four Questions.

3296338.title: Soviet Exodus Part II
3296338.description: When Gershon Ber Schiff finally emigrated from Russia, he was excited to be spending Passover with the Rebbe. When the Rebbe called an unscheduled farbrengen on the first day of the festival, he realized just how much it meant to the Rebbe, too. (1971)

3296341.title: Lasting Freedom
3296341.description: Although Passover is called the Season of Our Freedom, when the Jewish people were redeemed from Egypt there was no mention of the matter. Instead, they were told by Moses that they are leaving Egypt to serve G-d.

3296342.title: Morning Prayers
3296342.description: The Rebbe takes part in morning prayers during the intermediate days of Passover. (Chol Moed Pesach, 5736 - Passover, 1976)

3296343.title: Birthday Blessings
3296343.description: Asking the Four Questions is a focal point of the Passover Seder.

3296344.title: Passover in Wartime
3296344.description:
Rabbi Fabian Schonfeld describes the Rebbe’s efforts to obtain matzo of the highest kosher
standard during the Second World War, for his own use and for others.

3296361.title: Counting Down
3296361.description: When counting the fifty days between Passover and Shavuos, instead of counting “Today is the first day of the Omer” and so on, we count, “Today is one day of the Omer.” This isn’t just semantics. The days of the Omer correspond to the days which led up to the giving of the Torah.

3296362.title: Kos Shel Brachah
3296362.description: The Rebbe distributes wine at the conclusion of Passover. Chasidim are led in the singing of lively melodies by the Tzatzkis brothers, who had emigrated from the Soviet Union.

3296363.title: Awaiting Moshiach
3296363.description: When we pray that “we hope for your salvation all day”, it does not mean that we hope he will arrive the day after tomorrow, rather, we await “all day” that he will arrive now - today.

3296364.title: With Conviction and with Love
3296364.description: Rabbi Sidney Katz was a chaplain and Rabbi in South Africa. His son, Rabbi Michoel Katz, recalls the Rebbe’s answer to his parents when like many, they were thinking of leaving the country. (1972)

3317684.title: Jewish Fundamentals - Part 1
3317684.description: In 1976, as part of his campaign for Jewish education, the Rebbe selected twelve fundamental Torah passages for every Jewish boy and girl.

3317685.title: Nigun L’chatchila Ariber
3317685.description: Chasidim sing the nigun L’chatchila Ariber, which was attributed to the Rabbi Shmuel of Lubavitch, the Rebbe Maharash.

3317686.title: Property of God
3317686.description: The Talmud relates that Torah scholars become weak from their rigorous study, but this is not inevitable; Maimonides rules that the body is the property of God, which one is required to take care of.

3317687.title: When the Nurse Blinded Our Newborn
3317687.description: Like all parents, the Landbergs were very excited by the birth of their son. Their joy, however, was short lived when their child was blinded by a nurse’s negligence. Given the frightening prognosis, their doctor offered a surprising referral.(1973)
path: When the Nurse Blinded Our Newborn

3323931.title: Jewish Fundamentals, Part 2
3323931.description: In 1976, as part of his campaign to educate every Jewish child, the Rebbe selected twelve fundamental Torah passages to be learned by every Jewish boy and girl.

3323932.title: Morning Prayers and Torah Reading
3323932.description: Scenes from morning prayers in 770. The Rebbe ia called to the Torah.

3323933.title: House of Healing
3323933.description: You work at the hospital in Tel HaShomer, which means ‘“Hill of the Guard.” May you watch over those around you in this spirit.

3323934.title: Patient Empowerment
3323934.description: Dr. Mordechai Shani is an Israeli physician and medical Professor. Intrigued by the Rebbe’s words to him one Simchas Torah, he decided to follow up with a private audience. The meeting, which discussed developments in healthcare, continues to impact him today. (1976)

3323946.title: Gathering with a Purpose
3323946.description: The stories related in the Torah are more than historical events. They offer guidance and direction for the way we live our lives. When we find ourselves in a year of hakhel, it’s not enough to merely recall how it was marked in the Holy Temple, we must search for ways to make it relevant in our lives, today.

3323947.title: Lag Ba’omer
3323947.description: Unique scenes of the Rebbe participating in the Lag B’omer parade of 1967, which was a year of hakhel.

3323948.title: Hakhel, Why Now?
3323948.description: Experience has shown us that whenever Jews gather for a holy purpose, something good is bound to come out of it.

3323949.title: Research Results
3323949.description: Hans Morgenthau was a major twentieth-century figure in the study of international politics. In 1991, while researching his life for a dissertation, Dr. Benjamin Mollov came to 770 to interview Rabbi Yehuda Krinsky about his subject’s relationship with the Rebbe. As it turned out, Dr. Mollov, developed a relationship of his own. (1991)

3323952.title: A Message of Hope for Russian Jewry
3323952.description: Addressing Jews who had recently arrived from the Soviet Union at a Lag B’omer parade, the Rebbe explains that they demonstrate, for all to see, the steadfast commitment to Torah and Judaism that the Jewish people have, despite adversity.
path: A Message of Hope for Russian Jewry

3323953.title: Lag B’omer Farbrengen
3323953.description: Scenes from a farbregen held in honor of Lag B’omer, which commemorates the passing of Rabbi Shimon Bar Yochai .

3323954.title: Women of Chabad
3323954.description: Raise your daughter with the awareness that she is a member of N’shei Chabad, the Chabad women’s organization.

3323955.title: Darkness to Light
3323955.description: Mrs. Riva Ceitlin runs Chabad programs for women in Montreal, Canada. When her son, Rabbi Aaron Eliezer Ceitlin, heard his mother speaking about the pressures of her position, he decided to ask the Rebbe for some encouragement. (1980's)

3346480.title: What Time Is It for G-d?
3346480.description: The world consists of various time zones. Consequently, commandments which are dependent on time take place at different times in the various places where Jews live. One region can be celebrating Shabbos, while another is busy at work.
path: What Time Is It for G-d?

3346481.title: Counting the Omer
3346481.description: An audio recording of the Rebbe counting the twenty-sixth day of the Omer while leading evening prayers.

3346482.title: Across Time Zones
3346482.description: A traveller should try to avoid crossing the International Date Line during the days of the Omer Count, since doing so will complicate the count.

3346483.title: Crossing the Line
3346483.description: When Rabbi Yoel Kahn discovered that his Shabbos guest had crossed the International Date Line during the Omer Count, he realized that for him, that Shabbos was already the fiftieth day of the Omer, and the festival of Shavuos. Uncertain of what his guest should do, he advised him to consult the Rebbe. (1961)

3356124.title: Torah 101
3356124.description: Understanding is required to fulfill one's obligation in studying the Oral Torah, but exceptions apply if comprehension is beyond one's control.

3356125.title: Niggun
3356125.description: The Rebbe requests that chasidim sing this lively Russian song at a farbrengen.

3356126.title: All Mountains Lead To Sinai
3356126.description: All mountains are connected to Mount Sinai. This is especially relevant this time of year. May God “raise His banner over the mountains,” with the true and complete redemption.

3356127.title: Musical Interlude
3356127.description: When Shmuel Katan came to spend Simchas Torah with the Rebbe, he didn’t expect to becomethe center of attention. But hearing of his musical talent, chasidim urged him to play his violin while the Rebbe distributed wine after the conclusion of the festival. To his surprise, the Rebbe offered three pointers on his technique. (1968)

3360372.title: Make It Your Own
3360372.description: The Kabbalah states that when the sages of the Talmud ruled on a matter of law, it was a reflection of how the law was applied in the upper realms.

3360373.title: Graduation
3360373.description: The graduating class of Beth Rivkah High School receive a blessing from the Rebbe for a healthy summer and continued success in their endeavours.

3360374.title: Personal Prayer
3360374.description: The Prayer books which you distribute begin with the prayer of “Modeh ani – I give thanks.” May you always merit to thank G-d for all good things.

3360375.title: Slowly, But Surely
3360375.description: Rabbi Joseph Karasick was president of the Orthodox Union from 1966 till 1972. One day during his tenure, he received an unexpected call from the Rebbe’s office inviting him for a meeting with the Rebbe. In the course of their conversation about his organization, Rabbi Karasick asked the Rebbe an unrelated question. The Rebbe’s answer has been with him, and shared with others, to this day.(1967)

3366032.title: Why It's a Mitzvah to Sleep
3366032.description: Although he may not feel it, every journey in a Jew’s life is ordained by his Creator and part of his Godly mission.
path: Why It's a Mitzvah to Sleep

3366033.title: Farewell Audience
3366033.description: A collection of scenes from a farewell audience for departing guests who had visited the Rebbe for Shavuos.

3366034.title: Match Made in Heaven
3366034.description: On the advice of her father, Chaya Cohen would often turn to the Rebbe for advice and guidance in her life. When the Rebbe advised her to start visiting friends for Shabbos meals, she knew something good would follow. (1970)

3371583.title: The Right Approach
3371583.description: Through a welcoming and uplifting approach, a Rebbe is able to kindle one’s soul, and bring him closer to God. This ability to uplift, to inspire confidence and potential, doesn’t disappear with a Tzaddik’s passing. After his passing, as during his lifetime, he’s able to affect and inspire the Jewish nation, injecting joy and commitment in their service of the Eternal.

3371584.title: The Best Thank You
3371584.description: The best way to repay me, is to raise your children in the same spirit. May you have much good Nachas from your children, not in the same manner, but in an even greater way.

3371585.title: Praying for His People
3371585.description: Rabbi Chaim Yehuda Krinsky served in various positions of Chabad's administrative staff since 1954, and as a personal secretary and press director for the Rebbe. In this presentation, he recalls some of the most memorable moments and details of when the Rebbe would visit the gravesite of his father-in-law and Rebbe, Rabbi Yosef Yitzchok Schneerson.

3377058.title: A Leader Defined
3377058.description: More than just the period of time in which he lived, each generation is essentially intertwined with, even defined by, its spiritual leader. This ccentuates the tremendous responsibility of those who merited to live in the same generation as a Rebbe. This extends also, to those who did not see him during his lifetime, or were born after his passing. If one studies his Torah teachings, and fulfills his directives, then he is bound to the Rebbe, and all that he represents. And this bond must transcend merely being connected; it should define and express his entire identity.

3377059.title: The Shachris Prayers
3377059.description: Scenes from the morning prayers with the Rebbe in 770, in 1992

3377060.title: Planting the Seed
3377060.description: If you'll try to begin to go in the right direction, it will have a big effect on your children. If they’ll see that you have changed, it will encourage them to reconsider their life ahead of them. They are still in the stage of preparing for independent life, and like with a seed, every small change in their attitude now, can make a tremendous impact in their life ahead. (1972)

3377061.title: Matters of the Heart
3377061.description: In 1991, Naftoli Feldman was confined to the hospital suffering from cardiovascular issues. As each treatment that he tried failed to bring positive results, he asked his wife to go to the Rebbe to seek a blessing. The Rebbe’s advice, and his subsequent care and attention, is something that left an indelible impression. (1991)

3377074.title: The Meaning of Sacrifice - Part 1
3377074.description: In Sefer Hasichos 5702, the Previous Rebbe relates some of the struggle that Chassidim endured in the Soviet Union. Warned against practicing Judaism under threat of danger to their lives, the Previous Rebbe gathered his closest Chassidim and made a pact. They swore not to be deterred from their mission, in spreading and promoting a life of Torah.

3377075.title: Niggun - Mi Armia
3377075.description: Cantor Berel Tzatzkis leads Chassidim as they sing a Russian Niggun about the dedication of Chassidim to follow the Rebbe in battling for the furtherance of Judaism.

3377076.title: A Jew in Secret
3377076.description: Those trapped in the Soviet Union face a tremendous test. They have been in a predicament in which there was never a calm moment in matters of Judaism, yet they have never been deterred from their commitment to Judaism.

3377077.title: Opening the Doors to the Soviet Union
3377077.description: After promising to maintain secrecy and informing the Rebbe of his plans, he was given some contacts by the Rebbe. (1960's)
path: Opening the Doors to the Soviet Union

3377079.title: The Meaning of Sacrifice - Part 2
3377079.description: As Jews, we’re painfully familiar with the term “self sacrifice”. Throughout the course of our history, so many Jews have chosen to give up their lives for Judaism to endure. But serving G-d with self sacrifice need not be limited to such dire circumstances. Each of us are face regularly with tests of character and attitude, and it’s up to us to rise to the challenge and overcome it. So next time you need to choose between helping yourself or those around you, have some self sacrifice and serve the greater good.

3377080.title: Niggun - Yehi Ratzon
3377080.description: The Rebbe asks Rabbi Mordechai Dov Teleshevsky to lead the Chassidim in singing the prayer for the Temple to be rebuilt - speedily in our times

3377081.title: Not only in Russia
3377081.description: May God grant you good tidings to report from every place you visit. If Judaism can flourishing under oppression in the USSR, how much more so should it flourish here. Those who are here; who don’t face all these challenges, should hear it from you.

3377082.title: Seeing Potential
3377082.description: As a young man, Rabbi Fishel Jacobs came with his mother for a private audience with the Rebbe. In his innocence, he brought along a tape recorder to record the meeting. Listening to the recording brings back powerful memories of the Rebbe’s care and concern for his personal life - both spiritually and materially. (1981)

3391961.title: All Year Round
3391961.description: When it comes to educating young children, how could yeshivas or Jewish schools shut down for the summer? Torah is our life-source, so how can one stop learning for even one day of the year?!

3391962.title: Farbrengen
3391962.description: At the conclusion of a farbrengen, the Rebbe hands a small bottle of vodka to Rabbi Dovid Raskin, and instructs him to use its contents toward a farbrengen in Crown Heights, and to have some of it sent to camp Gan Yisroel for a farbrengen there as well.

3391963.title: Swiss Air
3391963.description: As Rabbi in Switzerland, ensure that people come there for spiritual purposes as well, not just the fresh air.

3391964.title: Not a Scratch!
3391964.description: Rabbi Yisroel Shemtov was a sixteen year old student in 1956. He recalls the Rebbe’s visit to Camp Gan Israel that summer, and the farbrengen the Rebbe held there. During the gathering, news arrived of a terrible accident that had involved a busload of people on their way to the camp. The Rebbe’s reaction to the news was wholly unexpected, and seemingly miraculous. (1956)

3391976.title: Two States of Being
3391976.description: The soul of every Jew is an “actual part of God” to which God wishes to grant the ultimate good. This unparalleled opportunity for metamorphosis is possible only when the soul descends into a body, into an environment which is hostile to spirituality.

3391977.title: Farbrengen
3391977.description: On the 17th of Kislev in 1980, the Rebbe held a farbrengen in the afternoon. Following this unusual occurrence, the Rebbe addressed chasidim as they prepared for the afternoon services.

3391978.title: Abandoning Ship
3391978.description: I hope you haven’t forgotten about your responsibility as a professor. May you continue to have the desired impact on your students.

3391979.title: A Healer’s Job
3391979.description: Uriel Ash was riding his bike one day when he was hit by a car and knocked unconscious. After putting him through various tests in the hospital, the doctors despaired and gave up on trying to save his life. In their desperation, the Ashes asked the Rebbe for advice and blessing. While seemingly unremarkable, it was a few words from the Rebbe, which guided the young boy to a miraculous recovery. (1987)

3403339.title: Engineering Light
3403339.description: The windows in the Temple were designed to be narrow on the inside and wide on the outside, representing the fact that its purpose is to shine outward and share the light with the rest of the world. The goblets in the Temple Menorah also symbolize this idea.

3403340.title: Tisha B’av
3403340.description: Scenes from the morning prayers on the fast of Tisha B’av, which that year fell out on Shabbos and was observed on Sunday.

3403341.title: Rebuilding the Temple
3403341.description: In the spirit of building a replica of the Temple, may you merit to help in building the third Temple with Moshiach.

3403342.title: Summer in the Caribbean
3403342.description: In 1959, the Rebbe sent Rabbi Shmuel Pesach Bogomilsky to the caribbean Islands, to help strengthen the local Jewish community. Upon landing at the airport in Barbados, he met an estranged Jew who sought to develop a relationship with the Rebbe. Little did he know, that this one small connection would lead to some very big achievements.

3403355.title: The Rebbe's View on Incarceration
3403355.description: The Torah considers denying a human being the ability to impact the world through incarceration as inhumane. Instead, we are responsible to help rehabilitate criminals to contribute productively to a moral and just society. We must ensure that prison acts not just as a punishment, but as an opportunity for positive growth.

3403356.title: Dollars
3403356.description: The Rebbe distributes dollars on the anniversary of the passing of his father, Rabbi Levi Yitzchok Schneerson

3403357.title: The Aleph Institute
3403357.description: Rabbi Sholom Lipskar and the staff of the Aleph Institute. May you merit to be an Aleph; a leader. But don’t stop at Aleph; move onto Beis, then Gimmel, until Taf.

3403358.title: The Greatest Custom
3403358.description: While visiting from France, Rabbi Yaakov Spitetzky was confused as to why the Rebbe seemed to ignore him during one of their meetings. It was some information that he later received from the Rebbe’s secretary that touches and inspires him till this day. (1968)

3413899.title: How a Father Acts
3413899.description: The verse commands: “You shall surely rebuke your fellow.” Nevertheless, one must deliver the rebuke joyfully, good-naturedly, and gently.

3413900.title: Children’s rally
3413900.description: Children returning from summer camp recite the Twelve Torah passages before being addressed by the Rebbe.

3413901.title: A Month for Inspection
3413901.description: During the month of Elul it is customary to check one’s tefillin and mezuzos. Be sure to get yours checked and have a sweet new year.

3413902.title: West Meets East – Part 1
3413902.description: Rabbi Marvin Tokayer recalls the life changing audience in which the Rebbe brought the plight of the Jewish community in Japan to his attention, along with the suggestion that he might hold the solution to their problem. (1960's)

3413916.title: The King Awaits
3413916.description: The Alter Rebbe offers a parable illustrating G-d’s closeness to every Jew during the month of Elul

3413917.title: Niggun - T’raneina S’fosai
3413917.description: Scenes of chasidim singing a lively nigun with words from Psalm 71 at a farbrengen.

3413918.title: Judaism in Japan
3413918.description: Contact the current rabbi in Tokyo and enquire about the state of Judaism there. The mere fact of your inquiry will encourage an even greater effort on his part.

3413919.title: West Meets East – Part 2
3413919.description: After agreeing to serve as rabbi in Japan for a period of two years, Rabbi Marvin Tokayer was thinking of backing out when his father suddenly passed away. The Rebbe’s guidance and advice turned his challenge into the most rewarding experience of his life.(1960's)

3413921.title: How to Be a Good Teacher
3413921.description: Throughout the summer months, it is customary to study Pirkei Avos - Ethics of Our Fathers. In this talk to women and girls entering the field of education, the Rebbe uses the first mishna of the tractate to lay the foundation for success as a teacher.
path: How to Be a Good Teacher

3413922.title: Niggun Darkecha Elokeinu
3413922.description: This melody was taught by the Rebbe to words from the High Holidays liturgy describing how G d forgivingly overlooks our faults.

3413923.title: Not the End of the World
3413923.description: The 25th of Elul marks the the day that G-d began to create the world. Surely, the Creator of the entire world will be able to provide for your needs as well.
path: Not the End of the World

3413924.title: Attention to Detail
3413924.description: Rabbi Yitzchok Wolf, who serves as director of Chicago's Cheder Lubavitch Hebrew day School, recalls the Rebbe’s request that schools test students and send the results to his office. After sending in a box of notebooks, he was surprised to receive a telephone call from 770. (1987)

3413963.title: Chassidism - What? When? Why?
3413963.description: There are many explanations given to define the contribution of Chassidism.

3413964.title: Farbrengen - 18 Elul
3413964.description: Highlights of a farbrengen celebrating Chai Elul, the birthday of the Baal Shem Tov and the Alter Rebbe, with original narration by photographer Levi Yitzchak Freidin.

3413965.title: In the Merit of Our Fathers
3413965.description: May you always remember from whom you are descended, the Alter Rebbe. Study and practice what he wrote in the Code of Jewish Law
path: In the Merit of Our Fathers

3413966.title: No Time to Quit
3413966.description: After some difficult first years as a shliach in New York City, Rabbi Shlomo Kugel was ready to throw in the towel, and sent a letter of resignation to the Rebbe’s secretariat just before Rosh Hashana. The Rebbe’s refusal to accept his resignation continues to drive him further each day. (1980's)

3445182.title: This Is the Time to Say Nice Things!
3445182.description: Elul is a month of reflection, introspection, and repentance. Some in the rabbinate, in their desire to lead their fellow Jews to improve during this auspicious time, tend to focus on the negative.
path: This Is the Time to Say Nice Things!

3445183.title: Elul with the Rebbe
3445183.description: A collection of unique images of some of the most memorable moments with the Rebbe during the month of Elul.

3445184.title: Torah Leadership
3445184.description: Excerpts from the visit of the Rebbe of Gur, Rabbi Simcha Bunim Alter, known as the Lev Simcha.

3445185.title: A Touching Apology
3445185.description: Mrs. Asya New remembers the care that the Rebbe showed her family when her father, Rabbi Isser Kluwgant, took ill. Not only did the Rebbe provide indispensable advice, he requested a daily report on Rabbi Kluwgant’s progress. (1981)

3445198.title: Greater Returns
3445198.description: Reshis Chochmah quotes Rabbi Moshe Cordovero, and the opinion of Rabbi Yonah of Gerona, that the days between Rosh Hashana and Yom Kippur are like the intermediate days of a festival.

3445199.title: Eve of Rosh Hashana
3445199.description: On the day before Rosh Hashana, Jews from all walks of life line up outside 770 to hand the Rebbe petitions for blessings for the coming year.

3445200.title: Chosen People
3445200.description: Do not be concerned. If G-d Almighty can take care of all the people in the world, he can certainly take care of his chosen people, you included.

3445201.title: Path to Success
3445201.description: As a young boy, Baruch Wilhelm suffered an accident causing damage to his ears, and requested the Rebbe’s blessing to regain his hearing. While he may not have received what he was hoping for, he received was a deep and impactful lesson to apply throughout his life. (1980)

3445203.title: A Heartfelt Cry
3445203.description: There are many details and rituals connected to the various obligations of a Jew. Even when it comes to matters of the heart, such as prayer and repentance, there are many laws and requirements.

3445204.title: Eve of Yom Kippur
3445204.description: Vintage film featuring rare scenes from the day preceding Yom Kippur

3445205.title: Taste of Things to Come
3445205.description: The Rebbe blesses members of the Machne Israel Development Fund with a healthy, happy, and sweet new year.

3445206.title: My Spiritual Compass
3445206.description: Elie Wiesel, an author, Nobel Prize laureate, and Holocaust survivor, recalls seeing the Rebbe for the first time, and the profound impact it had on the rest of his life. (1960's)

3445218.title: Let the World Know
3445218.description: The sukkah is a testament to G‑d’s protection over the Jewish people. Like the clouds of glory in the desert, which it represents, the sukkah brings the nations of the world to respect the Jewish people and to recognize that this world has one true Master, G‑d Almighty. Thus, the coronation of G‑d which the Jewish people initiated on Rosh Hashana also reaches its apex on Sukkos, as all the nations of the world recognize G‑d’s dominion.

3445219.title: Farbrengen
3445219.description: Archival film providing a rare glimpse into a farbrengen during the intermediate days of Sukkos in the sukka adjacent to 770.

3445220.title: Everyone Needs a Sukka
3445220.description: As we celebrate the festival of Sukkos, it is important to think of those that don’t yet have a sukka.

3445221.title: When It Rains on Sukkot
3445221.description: Rabbi Binyomin Silberstrom recalls asking the Rebbe, “How can we spread joy during the festival Sukkos when it won’t stop raining? The Talmud clearly states that rain is a sign of God’s displeasure.” The quick reply to his question was was a revealing example of the Rebbe’s unique perspective. (1975)

3466300.title: The Humble Willow
3466300.description: During the festival of Sukkos, the Torah commands us to take a citron, a date palm frond, a myrtle branch, and a willow twig and bring them all together. The Midrash adds that each of these represents a different kind of Jew.

3466301.title: Morning Prayers
3466301.description: Unique scenes from the morning services during the second of the intermediate days of Sukkos. (1991)

3466302.title: The Four Kinds
3466302.description: The Rebbe gives instructions to Rabbi Dovid Raskin on putting together the Four Kinds before the festival of Sukkos.

3466303.title: A Fateful Blessing
3466303.description: Hanan Caspi recalls attending Simchas Torah celebrations in 770, as well as a private audience he had as a child, when his father served as the Consul General of Israel in New York. It was then that he heard the words that would give him the strength he so much needed many years later in life. (Early 1970s)

3477412.title: “Fill the Earth and Subdue It”
3477412.description: The first commandment in the Torah is to have children.
