When G-d created Adam and Eve, He blessed them and said: “Be fruitful and multiply and fill the earth and subdue it, and rule over the fish of the sea and over the fowl of the sky and over all the beasts that tread upon the earth.”

3477413.title: Farewell to Guests
3477413.description: The Rebbe bids farewell to guests who arrived for the month of Tishrei, watching them depart from the steps of 770.

3477414.title: Name Play
3477414.description: Your name Noach means “comfort.” May your activities proceed in similar manner.

3477415.title: Seizing the Moment
3477415.description: Rabbi Mayer Plotkin recalls the unusual scene that unfolded as he approached the Rebbe to request a blessing for an ailing acquaintance the night after Simchas Torah, as the Rebbe was distributing wine. (1971)

3482589.title: Founded on Faith
3482589.description: In the United States, there is much debate about the separation of government and religion.

3482590.title: Nigun
3482590.description: Chasidim sing a melody attributed to Rabbi Meir Shlomo Yanovsky, the Rebbe’s maternal grandfather.

3482591.title: Spiritual Healthcare
3482591.description: May you have a speedy discharge from the hospital, but as long as you are there, use your time to influence those around you to do good.

3482592.title: Message for the World
3482592.description: Ari Goldman, then a reporter for The New York Times, recalls several encounters that he shared with the Rebbe, as well as an unexpected telephone call shortly after one particular visit. (Late 1980s)

3482608.title: The Land of Our Inheritance
3482608.description: The open miracles that G-d has shown the Jewish people in the Holy Land in our own times are a powerful reminder of its importance and centrality to the entire nation.

3482609.title: Rare Scenes
3482609.description: The Rebbe is seen speaking to photographer Levi Freidin outside his home on President Street. The conversation continues into the car, and ends at the entrance to 770.

3482610.title: Covenant of Abraham
3482610.description: There is no need to persuade a Jew to become circumcised; he surely desires to do so on his own.

3482611.title: Preventative Medication
3482611.description: As a young man, Mottel Feiglin suffered from painful migraines. On the advice of friends, he decided to ask the Rebbe for a blessing. He expected the blessing, and even advice, but not the prescription. (1971)

3507811.title: Today’s Front: Outreach
3507811.description: From the beginnings of the Chasidic movement, there has been an effort to disseminate “the wellsprings of Chassidism to the outside.” After the Alter Rebbe’s release from prison in 1798, this endeavor increased in an even greater way.

3507812.title: Distribution of Discourse
3507812.description: The Rebbe distributes a Chasidic discourse written by the Rebbe Rashab in 5678 – 1918.

3507813.title: Actions Speak Louder
3507813.description: While sitting Shiva for his wife, Rebbetzin Chaya Mushkah, the Rebbe is visited by Rabbi Simcha Elberg. They discuss the burial of our matriarch Sarah.

3507814.title: Nothing Wrong
3507814.description: In 1981, Dr. Leslie Rosenthal was suddenly struck by a severe headache during the Rosh Hashanah services. Further tests indicated that he was suffering from an aneurysm behind his eye. Running out of options, his rabbi convinced him to write to the Rebbe detailing his ailments. The Rebbe’s answer startled him, as well as his doctors. (1981)

3507831.title: Soul Purpose
3507831.description: Our sages teach that “one who saves a single Jewish life is as if he saved an entire world.”

3507832.title: Nigun
3507832.description: At a farbrengen honoring the Mitteler Rebbe, the second Rebbe of Chabad, Chasidim join the Rebbe in singing “We Want Moshiach Now.”

3507833.title: Month of Miracles
3507833.description: We must do even more than we have up until now to make it abundantly clear that Israel is a Jewish country. Living in Israel, you can accomplish more in this direction than I can from here.

3507834.title: On the Rebbe’s Mind
3507834.description: Rabbi Shlomo Matusof was one of the first Chabad shluchim and a pioneer of Jewish education in Morocco. His son, Rabbi Yosef Yitzchak Matusof recalls an episode highlighting the Rebbe’s care and concern for his emissaries around the world. (1957)

3513079.title: Bar-Mitzvah Lessons
3513079.description: At the Previous Rebbe’s Bar Mitzvah, following a custom passed down through the generations, he asked his father a question.

3513080.title: Rostover Nigun
3513080.description: At a farbrengen, Chasidim sing the Nigun Hachanah, customarily sung before the recital of a Chasidic discourse. This nigun was often sung by the fifth Rebbe of Chabad, Rabbi Sholom Dovber Schneersohn.

3513081.title: Becoming a Man
3513081.description: The Rebbe blesses Bar Mitzvah boys to grow up to be chasidim, G-d-fearing, and a Torah Scholars.

3513082.title: No Shortcuts
3513082.description: Rabbi Shlomo Majeski recalls an audience that he had with the Rebbe on the occasion of his Bar Mitzvah. After asking him to share the words of Torah that he would speak at his Bar Mitzvah, the Rebbe offered some words of his own. (1963)

3520885.title: On Harmony in Marriage
3520885.description: In the 1970s the Rebbe began a campaign to promote the observance of Family Purity in the Jewish community.

3520886.title: The Wedding Day - Collage
3520886.description: Standing under the wedding canopy is an auspicious time for the groom and bride to have their prayers answered.

3520887.title: Late Notice
3520887.description: Rabbi Shmuel Lew recalls that his father-in-law, Zalman Jaffe, tried every angle he could in an effort to convince the Rebbe to officiate at his daughter’s wedding, a practice that the Rebbe had ceased several years earlier. (1963)

3527515.title: Three Innovations, Three Accusations
3527515.description: The Alter Rebbe was informed of his release from prison as he was reciting the verse in Psalms, “He redeemed my soul in peace from the battle that came upon me, because of the many who were with me.”

3527516.title: Elul with the Rebbe
3527516.description: On the birthday of the Tzemach Tzedek, the Rebbe distributes a pamphlet containing the notes on Tanya from the Tzemach Tzedek, the third Rebbe of Chabad.

3527517.title: Classic Reprint - Collage
3527517.description: Various prints of the Tanya are presented to the Rebbe at Sunday Dollars.

3527518.title: The Bilingual Tanya
3527518.description: Mr. Bernard Perrin lives in Manchester, England. In the 1970’s the Rebbe commissioned him for an important project in the dissemination of Chassidism to the wider world. (1970's)

3536259.title: Twilight
3536259.description: The Chanukah Menorah is kindled at twilight. “Twilight” represents a dual state: on the one hand, there is darkness; but at the same time, the sun is still fully there, albeit obstructed.

3536260.title: Children’s Chanukah Rally
3536260.description: On the fourth night of Chanukah in 1976, the Rebbe participates in a rally for children in honor of the holiday.

3536261.title: A Bright Month
3536261.description: Kislev is a special month for weddings; we light candles and everyone is happy.

3536262.title: Family Time
3536262.description: In 1976, Rabbi Shmuel Gurewicz brought his family with him for an audience with the Rebbe. Relating to each child in a unique and personal manner, the Rebbe’s special interaction with the children was a beautiful expression of his love for every Jew. (1976)

3544308.title: Joseph's Two Dreams
3544308.description: Both of Joseph’s dreams came true: Eleven brothers prostrated themselves to Joseph, and they bowed again after Jacob and Bilha joined them.

3544309.title: Chanukah Gelt
3544309.description: The Rebbe distributes coins to the Yeshiva students on Chanukah. It’s customary to give out money on Chanukah, in what’s known as “Chanukah Gelt.”

3544310.title: Patron of the Arts
3544310.description: The Rebbe blesses Israeli artist Baruch Nachshon. “Much success in all of your new paintings.”

3544311.title: An Exhibition in Brooklyn
3544311.description: Baruch Nachshon is a famed artist from Chevron, Israel. In 1979, he brought some of his art with him when he came to visit the Rebbe. After suggesting to him to make an art exhibit, the Rebbe came and gave comments which were subtle, yet very profound. (1979)

3544324.title: Polishing the Buttons
3544324.description: The Previous Rebbe gave us a mission: "Stand ready to greet Moshiach." "Everything is already prepared, all that remains is to 'polish the buttons.'"

3544325.title: Slichos, Asara be’Teves
3544325.description: The Rebbe leads the congregation in the Recitation of slichos during the year of mourning for his wife, Rebbetzin Chaya Mushka.

3544326.title: Definition of Charity
3544326.description: “To the poor person it makes no difference where the money comes from. The main thing is that he receives it.”

3544327.title: A Place in the Sun
3544327.description: Rabbi Avraham Shalem hailed from a long line of Sephardic rabbis. In the 1960’s, after being offered two different rabbinic posts, he was conflicted as to what to do. Seeing no way to solve his dilemma on his own, he turned to the Rebbe for advice. (1960's)

3556609.title: Be Like Abraham
3556609.description: Abraham broke his natural tendencies to follow G-d. We can (and must!) do the same.

3556610.title: Russian Nigun
3556610.description: Chasidim sing a song with words in Russian; “We will not drown in water, and in fire we will not burn,” as the Rebbe distributes L’chaim to Jews who have recently arrived from the Soviet Union.

3556611.title: Remaining in Russia
3556611.description: I am pleased that the Chasid, Reb Getzel, is not leaving Russia. He still has much to accomplish there.

3556612.title: The Work Must Go On
3556612.description: Rabbi Eliezer Nisilevitch recalls the dangers his family faced in the Soviet Union as members of the Jewish underground, and the strength and direction they received from the Rebbe even after they had succeeded in emigrating to Israel. (1971)

3564320.title: A Joyful Connection
3564320.description: Chasidism places much emphasis on serving G-d with joy. In truth, this is not something that a Jew must search too far to find. It is a natural expression of the awareness of G-d in all facets of life, and of the Jew’s recognition of what lies within him.

3564321.title: Nigun of Four Stanzas
3564321.description: On the eve of 24 Teves, the Rebbe conducts a special farbrengen in honor of the 150th year since the passing of Rabbi Schneur Zalman of Liadi, the founder of Chabad Chasidism.

3564322.title: Study What You Print
3564322.description: May you report good tidings and go from strength to strength, not just in printing the Tanya, but in studying from it as well.

3564323.title: A Weight off His Shoulders
3564323.description: When Meir Moss returned to his Jewish roots and decided to attend a yeshiva in his teens, his father, a holocaust survivor who had become alienated from Judaism, decided to take it up with the Rebbe. He travelled to all the way to New York from Melbourne, Australia but forgot to lodge his complaint with the Rebbe. (1970's)

3570927.title: The Most Important Partner
3570927.description: The Talmud teaches that there are three partners in the creation of a child; the father, the mother, and G-d Himself. And while G-d entrusts the parents with the ability to make a very special contribution, He never removes Himself from the equation.

3570928.title: Through the Eyes of Children
3570928.description: A heartwarming collection of scenes of the Rebbe interacting with children.

3570929.title: The Stray Kitten
3570929.description: Shavi Slodowitz grew up in Brooklyn, New York, where she attended Bais Rivkah High School. Being a somewhat difficult student, she lacked the motivation she needed to grow. In the most unusual way, the Rebbe channeled her passions into personal growth and academic success.

3570937.title: Focus on the Individual
3570937.description: In 1927, Rabbi Yosef Yitzchak Schneersohn, the sixth Lubavitcher Rebbe, was arrested for his efforts to save Judaism from being stamped out in the face of Soviet repression.

3570938.title: Evening Services
3570938.description: The Rebbe leads the evening prayers on the anniversary of the passing of his father-in-law, Rabbi Yosef Yitzchak Schneersohn, the sixth Lubavitcher Rebbe.

3570939.title: A Leader Needs Followers
3570939.description: For me to lead successfully I need your input. We must work with urgency – Moshiach will be arriving very shortly.

3570940.title: What the Rebbe Was Thinking About
3570940.description: Rabbi Asher Zeilingold recalls spending 10 Shevat, the anniversary of the passing of Rabbi Yosef Yitzchak Schneersohn, the sixth Lubavitcher Rebbe, in 770. After observing the Rebbe during evening services, he could not help but wonder how the Rebbe would spend the remainder of such an auspicious day. To his surprise, an answer was short to follow. (1958)
path: What the Rebbe Was Thinking About

3584380.title: Seeing the Potential
3584380.description: 15 Shevat, the New Year for Trees, is when the sap is just beginning to flow, and the trees awaken from their winter sleep. But if the fruit is not yet growing, why do we celebrate the occasion by eating fruit?

3584381.title: Farbrengen: L’Chaim and Singing
3584381.description: At a Farbrengen held in honor of 15 Shevat, the Rebbe encourages Chassidim as they sing.

3584382.title: Fruits of the Garden
3584382.description: Dr. Marvin Shuster presents the Rebbe with fruits from his garden.

3584383.title: Memories of 15 Shevat, 1941, in Marseille
3584383.description:
In 1941, the Rebbe travelled to Marseilles, France, to obtain entry visas to the United States for himself and his wife, Rebbetzin Chaya Mushka. While there, the Rebbe maintained his characteristic low profile, but at a gathering in honor of the New Year for Trees, he gave those
present a taste of things to come. (1941)

3591569.title: Women Lead the Way
3591569.description:
The Midrash teaches that the sin of the Golden Calf was enabled by the men, as opposed to the women who refused to partake in it. Moreover, when it came to contributing materials to build the tabernacle in the desert, it was the women who were first to step up to the task,
followed by the men.

3591570.title: Kaddish - 22 Shevat
3591570.description: The Rebbe leads the prayers on the Yahrtzeit of his wife, Rebbetzin Chaya Mushka.

3591571.title: Visiting Family
3591571.description: I heard that your husband studies Tanya with your son every night in yeshiva. May they have even more success going forward.

3591572.title: Family Medicine
3591572.description: A relative of the Rebbe’s family, Shem Rokeach describes the warm friendship his mother and grandmother enjoyed with Rebbetzin Chaya Mushka, and recalls a time when the friendship helped save his mother’s life. (1970's)

3591585.title: The Strength of Our people
3591585.description: At the first possible opportunity, we begin teaching our young about their precious heritage. And while the obligation to educate our children only begins once they reach the age of five or six, there is much we can teach them even before then.

3591586.title: Maamar Distribution
3591586.description: The Rebbe distributes booklets of a Chassidic discourse famously known by its title, Ve’atah Tetzaveh.

3591587.title: The King’s Choice
3591587.description: The Rebbe discusses the concept of free choice during an audience with the Ashkenazic and Sephardic chief rabbis of Israel.

3591588.title: On Taking Charge
3591588.description: Rabbi Yaakov Lieder recalls making the decision to become an emissary of the Rebbe in Sydney Australia. In what he thought was a noble sense of dedication to the Rebbe’s vision, he asked the Rebbe to send him wherever he saw fit. The Rebbe’s answer – or the lack of it – contained a powerful lesson. (1970's)

3605428.title: America is No Different
3605428.description: When the Rabbi Yosef Yitzchak Schneerson, the sixth Lubavitcher Rebbe, miraculously arrived on the safe shores of America in 1940, he declared: “America is not different”.

3605429.title: Evening Prayers
3605429.description: The Rebbe joins Evening Prayers the night after the passing of his brother-in-law, Rabbi Shmaryahu Gurary.

3605430.title: First Supporters
3605430.description: The Rebbe tells Milton Kramer, whose family was instrumental in the arrival of Rabbi Yosef Yitzchak Schneersohn in America, to always remember the traditions of his family.

3605431.title: The Second Blessing
3605431.description: Rabbi Fabian Schonfeld, former president of the Rabbinical Council of America, recalls receiving a blessing from the Rebbe for his daughter to find a suitable match. After waiting a year for the blessing to materialize, he returned to 770 to take the issue up with the Rebbe. (1990's)

3614875.title: The Subconscious Revealed
3614875.description: Judaism puts great emphasis on maintaining a frame of mind conducive to serving G-d. It’s odd then, that we’re taught to get drunk on Purim - even to a point of not be able to distinguish between Haman and Mordechai!

3614876.title: Purim 5751
3614876.description: Scenes of the Megillah reading on the night of Purim in 770.

3614877.title: Purim Conversations
3614877.description: The Rebbe speaks with a number of individuals during a joyous farbrengen held on Purim 5732 - 1972.

3614878.title: That’s Nothing?
3614878.description: Rabbi Sholom Geisinsky recalls that when his father moved from New York to Cleveland, Ohio, the Rebbe personally assisted him in securing a new rabbinic position. While he was very grateful to the Rebbe for his help, he was especially touched when the Rebbe’s persistent questioning reminded him of a personal matter. (1951)

3614895.title: The Red Heifer Lives On
3614895.description: Fundamentally, the commandment of the red heifer—sprinkling its ashes upon the impure to purify them—is most unusual. One of its laws, however, expresses an important and powerful lesson. When the ashes of a new red heifer are prepared, the ashes of the new cow are mixed with the old ones. This was done with all the red heifers—from the first red heifer of Moses to the heifer to be prepared by Moshiach in the near future.

3614896.title: Niggun Yifrach Beyamav
3614896.description: Chasidim sing the lively niggun, Yifrach Beyamav, during a Purim farbrengen.

3614897.title: Our Capital
3614897.description: Jerusalem is the capital of Israel. When the capital benefits, the other cities benefit too. This is true of cities both near or far, even those outside of Israel.

3614898.title: The Power of Charity
3614898.description:
Rabbi Dovid Shochet recalls a most amazing story that took place following a lecture he had
given to students in Buffalo, New York. During his talk, he related a story which took place with a miser who was later revealed to be the secret benefactor of his entire town. After concluding his speech, Rabbi Shochet was approached by a young priest in the audience. Little did he know the impact of the story he had told. (1960's)

3629127.title: A Sense of Pride
3629127.description: Our small Jewish nation, dispersed among many, sometimes seems too small to matter to the rest of the world's peoples. Occasionally, it may even feel appropriate to try blending in; to compromise on our own unique traditions and blend in with those who surround us.

3629128.title: Distribution of Dollars
3629128.description: Sights and scenes of the Rebbe distributing dollars to be given to Charity.

3629129.title: Laws for Humanity
3629129.description: I’m very pleased to meet the senator from Brazil. US President Reagan published two declarations regarding the importance of the Noahide Laws, but Brazil should try to even surpass the US in its commitment to them.

3629130.title: Billing the Rebbe
3629130.description: Rivkah Zakutinsky recalls the inspiration she gained from traveling with her class to visit the Rebbe. Motivated by the Rebbe to be proactive in spreading Judaism, she decided to begin a Shabbos group for the local Jewish children. She had everything in place to begin, except the necessary funds, until she reached out to the Rebbe.

3637137.title: Passover Preparations
3637137.description:
All important things need preparation, and education is certainly no exception. We need not wait to respond to our children; by being proactive, we can be sure that they’re properly engaged. This is especially true by the Passover Seder. Much of the ritual that surrounds the Passover Seder
involves the participation of our children. By properly preparing, all our children, no matter their personalities, can feel welcome and involved.

3637138.title: Birthday Blessing
3637138.description: Rabbi Zalman Gurary and Rabbi Yitzchak Hendel are joined by a delegation of Rabbis to bless theRebbe on the occasion of his birthday.

3637139.title: Do It Yourself
3637139.description: Don’t wait until the Rabbi comes to help you. You have your own mission in the place you live to influence people. You can perform a great deal of good, even by yourself.

3637140.title: Keeping the Focus
3637140.description:
Rabbi Laibl Wolf recalls being sent by the Rebbe to run a Chabad House at the University of
Madison, Wisconsin. In the weeks before Passover, wanting to grab the attention of the students, he put an advertisement in the local student newspaper. As with all of his work, he sent it to the Rebbe for review. The Rebbe’s feedback wasn’t just to the point; it has continued to guide him in
all his projects since. (1970)

3644167.title: A Quantum Leap
3644167.description: Each individual fulfils a different role within his or her community, facing diverse challenges in different areas. Some individuals might dedicate themselves to a life of Torah study, while others might enter the world of business and philanthropy, but the one thing that unites us all is our commitment to Torah.

3644168.title: Matzah Distribution
3644168.description: Just a few days before Passover, the Rebbe distributes matzah to shluchim to be shared with their guests at the Seder.

3644169.title: Passover Haste
3644169.description: Passover requires fast and meticulous work to ensure that no leaven is overlooked. May your other endeavors also be quick to succeed, then you can go on to do even more.

3644170.title: Faith is Contagious
3644170.description: David Chase, a prominent businessman and philanthropist, recalls how one little request from the Rebbe had far-reaching effects on his life and the lives of others. (1983)

3644183.title: Reward of the Struggle
3644183.description: As G-d testifies Himself, He came personally to redeem us from our slavery in Egypt to serve Him as His chosen people. But if we’re really God’s chosen people, why does serving Him require such effort and struggle?

3644184.title: Distribution of Wine
3644184.description: At the conclusion of Passover, the Rebbe distributes wine from the Havdalah ceremony.

3644185.title: A Tenth for Charity
3644185.description: Place a charity box in your business and give at least ten percent from your net income to charity. But don’t be too exact – give at least one dollar beyond the ten percent.

3644186.title: Tithes to Riches
3644186.description: Ami Pykovski recalls introducing designer Maurice Sasson to the Rebbe. Despite a successful career in the clothing business, Sasson was not seeing the returns from his work and turned to the Rebbe for help. (1990)

3655616.title: Focus on Growth
3655616.description: On the sixteenth of Nissan, the second day of Passover, we begin counting down the days until the festival of Shavuos, a practice with origins in the Jewish people’s redemption from slavery. As soon they left Egypt, the Jews began to eagerly count down the days until G-d would give them the Torah at Sinai.

3655617.title: Farewell Audience
3655617.description: Scenes from a public audience for guests who had come to spend Passover with the Rebbe

3655618.title: To Learn and to Serve
3655618.description: Your son’s primary focus now is to study Torah – at this stage, even involvement in activities to benefit the good of the community are a distraction.

3655619.title: Ask Again
3655619.description: Winnie Gourarie remembers the story of when her husband got sick with appendicitis. Their uncle, Zalman Gurarie went to the Rebbe to ask for some urgent counsel. It took lots of faith to carry through with the Rebbe’s advice before they found out the real diagnosis. (1950's)

3660447.title: How One Little Candle Changed a Family
3660447.description: A girl spoke in a non-religious school in Israel about the Mitzvah of Shabbos candles. She taught them the blessings, and gave them candles and candlesticks to take home.
path: How One Little Candle Changed a Family

3660448.title: Audience
3660448.description: In a rare film, the Rebbe holds a private conversation with Rabbi Binyomin Gorodetski at the conclusion of a public audience. Rabbi Gorodetsky served as a Chabad emissary in Europe and North Africa for over four decades.

3660449.title: Lighting the Shabbos
3660449.description: Although your wedding will take place after Shabbos, you should nevertheless begin lighting one candle this Friday. Then next Friday you can light two candles, for you and for your new husband.

3660450.title: Three More Lights
3660450.description: Yehudah Clapman recalls arranging a private audience with the Rebbe for his cousins. After asking the girls in the family to light their own Shabbos candle, the Rebbe offered them a special gift to help them get started. When they tried to thank the Rebbe as they left, it was the Rebbe who thanked them instead.

3667951.title: The Common Thread
3667951.description: Through the years of the Rebbe’s leadership, he launched a total of ten campaigns which encouraged and promoted the observance of various commandments. Each campaign had a clear and obvious mission, yet the Campaign of Ahavas Yisrael -- love of one’s fellow, had not been clearly defined. Here the Rebbe explains why.

3667952.title: Nigun - Yemin Hashem
3667952.description: The Rebbe encourages chasidim as they sing a nigun of the third Rebbe of Chabad, the Tzemach Tzedek, during a farbrengen marking his passing.

3667953.title: Second Passover
3667953.description: During a visit from the Nadvorner Rebbe, Rabbi Yaakov Yisachar Ber Rosenbaum, the Rebbe discusses “Pesach Sheni” and the unique status of the commandments: that they prepare us for the arrival of Moshiach.

3667954.title: The Teacher from Tekumah
3667954.description: Henny Karniel is a veteran educator living in Kfar Chabad, Israel. In 1975, as she was about to return to work after taking time off on maternity leave, she was approached with a particularly challenging job offer. After the Rebbe encouraged her to go ahead, she accepted the position. She saw immediate results, but it was only many years later that she found out what a big difference her efforts had made.

3679514.title: Counting Up
3679514.description: When the Jews were redeemed from Egypt, they eagerly counted down the days until the giving of the Torah at Mount Sinai. Today as well, we count the days and weeks from Passover as we gear up to receive the Torah anew on Shavuos.

3679515.title: Lag B’Omer Parade (1987)
3679515.description: Highlights from the Lag B’Omer Parade of 1987.

3679516.title: Day of Rabbi Shimon
3679516.description: May the merit of Rabbi Shimon whose Yahrtzeit we celebrate on Lag B’Omer bring you success.

3679517.title: Lag B’omer Mint
3679517.description: Rabbi Chaim Yehuda Krinsky served in various positions of Chabad’s administrative staff and as a personal secretary to the Rebbe. In 1990, just days before the grand Lag B’Omer parade, the Rebbe asked him about the possibility of minting a batch of special coins commemorating the event. A seemingly impossible task to pull off in such short time, Rabbi Krinsky all but gave up. But after hearing how the Rebbe blamed himself for the last minute notice, he concluded that failure wasn’t an option. The coins were ready in time…

3679534.title: Jerusalem: The City of Oneness
3679534.description: From all the cities of the world, Jerusalem was chosen as the capital of the Land of Israel. The Talmud relates, that when Jews would arrive in Jerusalem, they all “became united as one.” Indeed, in Psalms, it is called “the city in which all are joined together.” And as we pray today for our true return to Jerusalem the arrival of Moshiach, forever, Jerusalem remains important and meaningful, uniting each and every Jew, man, woman, and child.

3679535.title: Coins for Charity
3679535.description: Vintage footage of the Rebbe distributing coins to be given to charity on his way into the Synagogue (Sivan, 5740 - May, 1980).

3679536.title: G-d’s Capital
3679536.description: A conversation during the Gulf War: Your daughter studying in Jerusalem is in G-d’s capital and shouldn’t even consider leaving. This is true for all Jews since we’ll all be going there soon with Moshiach.

3679537.title: One Short Telegram
3679537.description: In 1967, Rabbi Shlomo Schwartz was part of a delegation of students sent by the Rebbe to revitalize the Toras Emes Yeshiva in Jerusalem. The group was in Israel on the cusp of the Six Day War. As the war drums were being beaten across the Arab world, many American Yeshiva students were leaving Israel in fear. After asking the Rebbe whether to stay or leave, the response that they got would make headlines in the Israeli Press and boost the morale of the country ahead of the war.

3684725.title: Root Cause
3684725.description: Much like the rest of the Written Torah, the Ten Commandments are stated very concisely. And yet, despite their brevity, the Rabbis teach that the Ten Commandments contain all the fundamental tenets of Judaism within them. Moreover, each of the commandments have their root in the very first Commandment: I am the L-rd your G-d.

3684726.title: Farbrengen Erev Shavuos
3684726.description: Chasidim sing a joyous nigun at a farbrengen in the days leading up to the festival of Shavuos.

3684727.title: Ten Commandments
3684727.description: My father-in-law, the Previous Rebbe would bless Jews before Shavuos to receive the Torah with joy and inner meaning. May this blessing truly come to fruition.

3684728.title: Restaurant Status
3684728.description:
In 1988, as a restaurant owner living in the Flatbush section of Brooklyn, Naftali Feldman was on
the dinner committee of Colel Chabad, the oldest operating charity in Israel. When the invitation for the dinner was sent to the Rebbe, it was his name – and restaurant – which the Rebbe inquired about. Wanting to only give the Rebbe positive news, he committed to bringing his establishment
up to standard.

3697603.title: Give It Your All
3697603.description:
Torah insists that nothing in this world is extra; everything was created with a specific purpose.
In fact, just by virtue of having been created, G-d has declared you an irreplaceable asset in bringing his world closer to a state of perfection. In a fascinating analysis of the Parsha, the Rebbe draws a crucial lesson in the life of a Jew: To achieve your full potential, use your every ability in the service of your Creator.

3697604.title: Kos Shel Brachah
3697604.description: On the Shabbos following the holiday of Shavous, the Rebbe held a surprise farbrengen before Marriv, followed by distribution of Kos Shel Brachah.

3697605.title: Commissioned Articles
3697605.description: Mr. Shaul Schiff of the Israeli “Hatzofeh” neswpaper visits the Rebbe: The impression I get from your recent writing is that your work is not decreasing, G-d forbid, but is also not increasing. You must double your achievements! This dollar is not a bribe for you to write more about me, but to write more on all the other Jewish matters…

3697606.title: Try to Remember
3697606.description: When Mr. Shaul Schiff handed his note to the Rebbe during a private audience in 1971, the Rebbe recognized his handwriting, but Mr. Schiff had no recollection of ever writing to the Rebbe before.

3706098.title: Why We Need to Ask for Moshiach
3706098.description: Can't we just rely on G-d to bring it at the appropriate time?
path: Why We Need to Ask for Moshiach

3706099.title: Nigun ‘We Want Moshiach Now’
3706099.description: Children lead the crowd in singing ‘We Want Moshiach Now’.

3706100.title: Campaign Results
3706100.description: The Rebbe gives words of encouragement to different people who recently began putting on teffilin (Collage).

3706101.title: The Full Picture
3706101.description: Not long after the Rebbe launched the tefillin campaign, Mr. Bentzion Rader asked the Rebbe, “Why tefillin?”. The answer the Rebbe gave him, was only understood seven years later (1967).

3706104.title: The Woman’s Three Special Mitzvot
3706104.description: There are three fundamental Mitzvos entrusted to every Jewish woman. Separating Challah “from the first of your dough” shows that before benefiting from anything in this world, we “set aside an offering for G-d.” By knowing that the beginning of everything is for G-d, the entire home becomes a dwelling place for Him.

3706105.title: Children’s Rally
3706105.description: The Rebbe attends a special children’s rally held for the Released Time children from NY public schools.

3706106.title: Neighborhood Memories
3706106.description: The Rebbe’s neighbors from the 1950’s, reminisce about their early encounters with the Rebbe (Collage).

3706107.title: Early Impressions
3706107.description: Yitzchak Popack recalls his memories from when the Rebbe and Rebbetzin arrived to the United States in 1941.

3706119.title: Nothing Has Changed
3706119.description:
The Talmud states that Samson ruled for forty years, yet the verse states that he only ruled for
twenty? In answer to this apparent discrepancy the Talmud declares: He influenced them for twenty years after his passing, thus extending the years of his leadership of the Jewish nation. In this passionate talk delivered at a farbrengen celebrating the liberation of his father-in-law from
prison, the Previous Rebbe, the Rebbe explains why our circumstances aren’t so different today.

3706120.title: A Rebbe’s Connection
3706120.description: At a farbrengen commemorating the passing of his father-in-law, the Rebbe spoke about the difference between a Rebbe and a leader.

3706121.title: Global Connection
3706121.description: People from different communities around the world greet the Rebbe by Sunday Dollars. (Collage)

3706122.title: A Few Realistic Words
3706122.description:
As a young teenager, Charles Ramat would sometimes chauffer his teacher from time to time. Once, when his teacher had an audience with the Rebbe, Charles took the opportunity to ask the Rebbe’s advice in regards to his mother’s terminal illnes. The Rebbe’s realistic prognosis helped
him deal with the eventual outcome. (1968)

3719791.title: Not Alone
3719791.description:
12 Tammuz marks the anniversary of the Previous Rebbe’s release from Soviet prison where he was jailed for the “crime” of promoting Judaism. Far from retreating under pressure from the Communist regime, Rabbi Yosef Yitzchak fought the Jews’ oppressors and with a small group of
devoted Chassidim, succeeded in keeping Judaism alive in Russia. But his amazing and inspiring story raises a fundamental question: How is it that one solitary individual was able to stand against a tyrannical world power?

3719792.title: Farbrengen - 13 Tammuz, 5736
3719792.description: Scenes from a farbrengen celebrating the 12th of Tammuz, the anniversary of the Previous Rebbe’s release from Soviet prison where he was jailed for the “crime” of promoting Judaism.

3719793.title: Good Reports
3719793.description: Rabbi Dovid Hollander visits the Rebbe and discusses returning to Soviet Russia to help the Jews being oppressed under the Communist regime.

3719794.title: A Message for the President
3719794.description: Rabbi Shimon Lazaroff is the regional director of Chabad-Lubavitch of Texas. In 1973, when President Zalman Shazar of Israel was in Houston, Rabbi Lazaroff was among the local Jewish leaders invited to meet him at the airport. On the Rebbe’s advice, Rabbi Lazaroff took up the invitation and reminded President Shazar of his roots in Chabad.

3724942.title: Better Than a Vacation
3724942.description: Most of us see the summer months as an opportunity to relax with time off from work or school. Not so the Previous Rebbe, Rabbi Yosef Yitzchak Schneerson. In fact, far from relaxing, he launched a special program to take advantage of the vacation.

3724943.title: Afternoon Prayers on Tammuz 17
3724943.description: The Rebbe reads the Haftarah during the Mincha services on the fast of the 17th of Tammuz.

3724944.title: Good Things Come with Hard Work
path: Good Things Come with Hard Work

3724945.title: It’s Who You Are
3724945.description: Rabbi Tzvi Grunblatt is the regional director of Chabad-Lubavitch in Argentina. In this account from 1976, he recalls his first shot at promoting the teachings of Judaism and Chassidism. After complaining to the Rebbe about what he felt was his lack of success, the Rebbe rejected this notion. The Rebbe’s answer, beyond inspiring him, is sure to remind of our own privileges and responsibilities.

3724960.title: A Love of the Land
3724960.description: The Torah relates how after Tzelafchad died without leaving any sons, his daughters appeared before Moses with a claim that they should be their father’s heirs. G-d agreed and commanded Moses to write this into Jewish law.

3724961.title: Farbrengen
3724961.description: The Rebbe asks that a bottle received from a farbrengen which took place in Beirut during the Lebanon war, be distributed at the farebrengen and in Camp Gan Israel.

3724962.title: Knesset Matters
3724962.description: Eitan Bar Eliyahu, the Sergeant-at-Arms of the Knesset in Israel visits the Rebbe. He presents the Rebbe a picture of the Knesset in session during a speech by Prime Minister Shamir.

3724963.title: A Painful Solution
3724963.description:
Eliezer Shefer serves as chairman of the World Organization of Orthodox Communities and Synagogues in Israel and the Diaspora. In 1971, he and two of his colleagues had an audience with the Rebbe.
At the time, Jerusalem was dealing with friction between segments of its community. Pained about the goings-on on both sides of the fighting, the Rebbe suggested a practical solution to try to tamp down the hostilities.

3732819.title: From Sea to Sea
3732819.description: “May he rule from sea to sea, and from the river to the ends of the earth.” The commentaries on the verse explain that these words in Psalms refer to Moshiach. But being that all the revelations we’ll experience in the times of Moshiach will reflect our effort before his arrival, as it turns out, we need not wait to begin actualizing this verse.

3732820.title: Nigun Yifrach
3732820.description: Chassidim sing a lively Nigun at a farbrengen on 12 Tammuz in 1973. This Nigun was introduced at the farbrengen on Nissan 11, 5733, commemorating the 71st birthday of the Rebbe.

3732821.title: Hastening the Redemption
3732821.description: The Talmud says that each new Jewish home, hastens Moshiach's arrival, and that the birth of every Jewish child hastens his coming (Collage).

3732822.title: Yours Faithfully
3732822.description:
Esther Solomon is a veteran educator living in Israel. In 1969, she was diagnosed with an inability to give birth. Desperate for her own children, she and her husband flew to New York and arranged an audience with the Rebbe. After reprimanding them for not placing more faith in G-d, the Rebbe
gave the couple a blessing. But the story only reached its conclusion many years later.

3740136.title: Above the Exile
3740136.description: It is through teshuva, returning to G-d, that we can fix the root-cause of exile, and bring it to an end. The Midrash teaches that the exile truly began when the Jewish children were exiled. In this regard, the Jewish children play an important role in resolving the situation and ushering in the arrival of Moshiach.

3740137.title: Tisha B’av 5747
3740137.description: The Rebbe participates in the reading of the Book of Lamentations on the eve of Tisha Ba’v. On this day we mourn the destructions of the first and second Holy Temples.

3740138.title: May it be Rebuilt
3740138.description: The Rebbe advises Kohens and Levites to prepare to serve in the third Holy Temple, which with Gd’s help, will be rebuilt very soon. (Collage)

3740139.title: Help from Above
3740139.description: Moshe Mandelbaum is a professor of economics and former Governor of the Bank of Israel. In 1967, while working to defend his thesis explaining the nature of Israel’s economy, he had an audience with the Rebbe. The Rebbe’s suggestion to him was eventually passed into law, and the cryptic statement the Rebbe left him with, helped him succeed in completing his thesis. (1989)

3747189.title: When the Nights Get Longer
3747189.description: We see that the more necessary something is for survival, the more available it is. For example, a house can be expensive, clothing is more affordable, food even more, and air which we need to breathe, is free. The same is true with Torah and commandments. While commandments have their limitations in time and other requirements, Torah study is something which can always be done, pointing to how necessary it really is for our survival.

3747190.title: Nigun Bnei Heicholo
3747190.description: The Rebbe instructs chasidim to sing the nigun “Bnei Heichala”. Customarily sung at the conclusion of Shabbos, it’s one of the ten nigunim of the Alter Rebbe.

3747191.title: Two Worlds
3747191.description: You say that you wish you had more time to study Torah. I was never elected to any office so I don’t know what it’s like, but surely if you try you can find the time to do both.

3747192.title: Music for the Mind
3747192.description: Michael Tabor is an educator and musician. In 1970, as a student at the London School of Economics, he had an audience with the Rebbe. After a conversation with the Rebbe about music and the arts, he learned an important lesson that has remained with him ever since.

3752479.title: “My Father Made the Ultimate Sacrifice”
3752479.description: Rabbi Levi Yitzchak Schneerson, the Rebbe’s father, dedicated himself to the impossible task of providing true leadership to Soviet Jewry stuck in the USSR. He may have ended up paying for his efforts with his life, but his legacy has far outlived that of his oppressors.

3752480.title: Reb Levik’s Nigun
3752480.description: Chasidim sing a lively nigun, a favorite of the Rebbe’s father, Rabbi Levi Yitzchak Schneersohn. The Rebbe enthusiastically encourages the singing.

3752481.title: Take it to Print
3752481.description: It is a sound idea indeed to spend the summer in Jerusalem, and when Moshiach arrives, we will all join you.

3752482.title: A Son’s Obligation
3752482.description: In 1970, Mordechai Gorelik was granted permission to leave the Soviet Union. His parents and brother, Rabbi Elozor Gorelik, remained there, trapped behind the Iron Curtain. During his first audience with the Rebbe, he presented the Rebbe with a photograph of the resting place of the Rebbe’s father in Almaty, Kazakhstan.

3752495.title: Heart and Mind
3752495.description: The source of violence, disorder and crime stems from the unhealthy balance of the head and the heart. The mind knows what is wrong, but isn’t able to control over the heart’ desires. The solution must come from a higher source: tefillin can help master our emotions and lead them towards good.

3752496.title: Refusenik’s Visit
3752496.description: Upon seeing the Rebbe for the first time, a newly-emigrated refusenik, a Jew who was previously trapped behind the Iron Curtain of the Soviet Union, recites the shehechiyanu blessing.

3752497.title: From Strength to Strength
3752497.description: May you be a living example for all, showing everyone how to behave when G-d gives you the ability to go higher and higher.

3752498.title: A Wish Granted
3752498.description: Rabbi Yosef Mendelevitch is a Rabbi and teacher living in Jerusalem, Israel. He is famous for his struggles in Soviet Russia where he was imprisoned for almost a decade for his public attempts to immigrate to Israel from the Soviet Union. It is the Rebbe’s care and direction, however, which led him down the path on which he finds himself until this day.(year 1980)

3765585.title: Point of Pride
3765585.description: In the Book of Exodus, G-d calls the Jewish people a “kingdom of priests and a holy nation.” A story in the Talmud demonstrates how we could fulfill this verse and inspire the respect of the nations that surround us.

3765586.title: A Russian Song
3765586.description: The Rebbe instructs Reb Hirshel Chitrik to sing the Russian version of “One is Hashem”.

3765587.title: Russian Connection
3765587.description: Thank G-d for saving you from danger by increasing in Torah study and observance. Give this to charity for all the Jews in Russia, and please send them my regards. (Collage)

3765588.title: The Rebbe’s Care
3765588.description: Rabbi Yitzchak Kogan serves as the director of the Bronnaya Synagogue in Moscow. He is a former refusenik and leading figure in the Soviet Jewish underground. Although he later had numerous encounters with the Rebbe, as a young child, all he knew was what he heard from his mother. (1981)

3770383.title: Seeing the Light
3770383.description: Like sunglasses which block the powerful light emanating from the sun, our physical bodies cover and conceal the precious light of our souls. But surely, this was orchestrated by G-d for a purpose. Our mission, we are told, is to bring forth the concealed light of the soul. Through following in the ways of Torah, and elevating ourselves with the performance of its commandments, we will illuminate our surroundings, and expose the divinity that lies within.

3770384.title: Post Camp Rally
3770384.description: The Rebbe participates in a rally for children of Camp Emunah.

3770385.title: The Greatest Calling
3770385.description: May all of your students be educated in a manner befitting the Holy Land. To educate others you need to be healthy -- both mentally as well as physically. (Collage)

3770386.title: Give and Take
3770386.description: Zlata Hertzel is a veteran educator living in Israel. In the early 1970s, she had an audience with the Rebbe. Being both a young mother and a committed teacher meant that she found most of her earnings going towards childcare for her young children. Asking the Rebbe if she should quit her job evoked a response that has inspired her since.

3770399.title: No Jew Left Behind
3770399.description: For centuries, being engaged with Torah meant being of an exceptional mind and travelling to study under the tutelage of a rabbi and sage. However, the Baal Shem Tov, and the Rebbes who followed, showed us a different way. By traveling to and visiting many Jewish communities, they brought the beauty of Torah to those who otherwise didn’t know of it.

3770400.title: Called to the Torah
3770400.description: The Rebbe is called to the Torah in the synagogue upstairs in 770.

3770401.title: The Main Message
3770401.description: What’s most important is that each and every Jew should be inscribed and sealed for a good year. Everything else I said was an introduction.

3770402.title: Double Tipping
3770402.description: Rabbi Avraham Yitzchak Kiss is a restaurant manager and caterer living in Brooklyn, New York. As a young boy in the early 1960s, he had had an after-school job delivering groceries. As one of his customers, he merited to to deliver to the home of the Rebbe’s mother, Rebbetzin Chana Schneerson. Once, when he knocked at her door, he was surprised to see who opened.

3789068.title: Turn Up the Light
3789068.description: A Jew’s purpose is to illuminate all the world around him. To “illuminate” does not mean to change the order of creation; rather, light enables one to discern the true nature and purpose of what already is there.

3789069.title: Excerpt from Tishrei with the Rebbe
3789069.description: The Rebbe recites the annulment of vows, traditionally done on the eve of Rosh Hashanah.
path: Excerpt from Tishrei with the Rebbe

3789070.title: In Our Power
3789070.description: Every single Jew has the ability to crown the Almighty as King on Rosh Hashana, the Jewish New Year. With the Shofar, we elevate a physical and otherwise mundane object to the lofty level of coronating the Creator.

3789071.title: A Special Invitation
3789071.description: Rabbi Ezra Schochet serves as dean of Yeshiva Ohr Elchonon Chabad in Los Angeles, California. In 1976, he was on a visit to New York with his wife and two children. When they arrived, he never thought he’d have a chance to meet with the Rebbe privately. But then he got an exciting message from the Rebbe’s secretary.

3796942.title: No Need to Wait
3796942.description: When it comes to Jewish education, some parents ask, “What’s the rush? When our child learns right from wrong, and matures a little, then we’ll teach him about his heritage. It can wait until he is at least able to understand that he is part of the chosen people, and different to others.”

3796943.title: Lekach
3796943.description: The Rebbe distributes honey cake for a sweet New Year.

3796944.title: Common Bond
3796944.description: After spending a month at his ill father’s bedside, Dr. Stuart Ditchek had the unique privilege of meeting privately with the Rebbe. The Rebbe brought to light a common connection the two of them shared, and gave him an open invitation to visit. (1986)

3801471.title: Move Into G-d’s Barracks
3801471.description: During their sojourn in the desert, G-d protected the Jewish people against danger and the elements with the Clouds of Glory, which the Torah refers to as “sukkahs.” To commemorate this, He commanded us to observe the holiday of Sukkos, when we spend a week in temporary huts.

3801472.title: Havdalah
3801472.description: The Rebbe listens as Rabbi Yehudah Keller recites Havdalah following Yom Kippur.

3801473.title: A New Beginning
3801473.description: “The New Year is time to elicit new blessings, with new resolutions and new beginnings.” (Collage)

3801474.title: Esrogim in Kfar Chabad
3801474.description: In the late 1950s, When Rabbi Nachman Elbaum raised the issue of using an esrog from a tree that had been grafted, the Rebbe gave him a solution and a mission. The result was a new orchard in the village of Kfar Chabad, Israel.

3801494.title: Why the Willow Need Not Grow Near Water
3801494.description: The Four Species taken on Sukkos represent four types of Jews, from the citron which has both flavor and fragrance, and represents the Jew who studies Torah and fulfills its commandments, to the willow which is neither tasty nor fragrant, represents the simplest of Jews, who lacks both Torah and good deeds.
path: Why the Willow Need Not Grow Near Water

3801495.title: Hoshanos
3801495.description: The Rebbe takes part in the services of Hoshana Rabbah.

3801496.title: As G-d is Simple
3801496.description: “My father-in-law would not refer to uneducated Jews as ignorant, but would call them ‘simple Jews,’ explaining that they are simple just like G-d is simple.

3801497.title: Spreading the Joy
3801497.description: Mendel Greenbaum recalls how the Rebbe waited to begin the Simchas Torah celebrations until the last of the Chasidim who had gone out on the Rebbe’s directive to spread the joy of the festival, had returned to 770. (1954)

3801501.title: What Is the Purpose of Creation?
3801501.description: According to the statement of the Midrash, G-d created the world because he desired to have a “dwelling in the lower realms.” Yet a verse in Song of Songs refers to G-d’s world as His garden. A deeper look at the descriptions “dwelling” and “garden” provide an insight into the very nature and purpose of creation.
path: What Is the Purpose of Creation?

3801502.title: A Blessing for Success
3801502.description: “May the Almighty bless you to progress in all matters of holiness; and success in your business will follow.”

3801503.title: A French Revolution
3801503.description: Rabbi Chaim Shneur Nisenbaum recalls his visit from France to Brooklyn to spend the High Holidays with the Rebbe, and the surprise that awaited him and his entire group. (1973)

3821439.title: Young Teachers
3821439.description: Much has been written and taught about the education of our own children in the ways of the Almighty. But as a light unto the nations, we must help educate their children as well.

3821440.title: Interacting With Children
3821440.description: “Give this to charity for your doll.” (Collage)

3821441.title: Think for Yourself
3821441.description: In the late 1960s, Rabbi Mottel Krasnjasnki was a child growing up in the Crown Heights section of Brooklyn. (circa 1975)

3826408.title: Praying for Children
3826408.description: The Torah relates the story of how Chana persevered in her prayers and was finally granted a son. But more than just a biblical tale, it’s a lesson for us in our responsibility to the future generations.

3826409.title: Afternoon Prayers
3826409.description: The Rebbe enters the synagogue at 770 for the afternoon Mincha prayer.

3826410.title: Be a Leader
3826410.description: “Abraham was called “A father to multitudes.” You cannot suffice with your own Judaism; you need to be a leader to many peoples;

3826411.title: Four Miracles
3826411.description: After six years of unsuccessfully trying to start a family, Fay Flood and her late husband, Vic, turned to the Rebbe for help and advice. (1978)

3833925.title: Good Times, Bad Times
3833925.description: The lives and challenges of our forefather Isaac and his grandson Joseph were very different. Isaac lived out his entire life in the Land of Israel amidst physical prosperity. Joseph spent most of his life in Egypt where he was sold into slavery and ultimately became a powerful ruler.

3833926.title: Nigun Hachana
3833926.description: Chasidim sing the nigunHachana, attributed to the Rebbe Rashab.

3833927.title: A New Look
3833927.description: “You should enjoy your beard as much as I am enjoying it.” (Collage)

3833928.title: Peaceful Solution
3833928.description: Kasriel Oliver lives in Melbourne, Australia. In 1975 after becoming acquainted with Lubavitch, he came to spend the summer in 770. While there he had an audience with the Rebbe.

3840610.title: The Woman’s Miracle
3840610.description: The Midrash relates the miracles that G-d would perform for Sarah and Rebecca. A beautiful story highlighting the greatness of our matriarchs, it holds a poignant lesson for us today and the special role of a woman to bring G-d’s light into the home.

3840611.title: Kuntres Eitz Chaim
3840611.description: The Rebbe distributes Kuntres Eitz Chaim, a discourse by the Rebbe Rashab.

3840612.title: Shining Light
3840612.description: “It would be good for her to begin lighting candles. Yes, even before her marriage.” (Collage)

3840613.title: The One Mitzvah That Kept My Kids Jewish
3840613.description: In the 1970s, Charles Ramat had a number of audiences with the Rebbe. During one of these meetings, he asked the Rebbe about something he was struggling with.
path: The One Mitzvah That Kept My Kids Jewish

3847818.title: Don’t Pass the Buck
3847818.description: The Talmud states that when two people lift a load together, they have significantly more than twice the strength of one. This is most certainly the case when the efforts of many are combined. When we all work together, our true abilities are much greater than we can ever imagine.

3847819.title: Recalling the Rebbe’s 1977 Heart Attack and Miraculous Recovery
3847819.description: A beautiful video surrounding the story of when the Rebbe suffered a severe heart attack on the night of Shemini Atzeres in 1977.
path: Recalling the Rebbe’s 1977 Heart Attack and Miraculous Recovery

3847820.title: Visiting Doctors
3847820.description: On the night of Shemini Atzeres in 1977, the Rebbe suffered a severe heart attack. This is a video collage showing the Rebbe in conversation with the doctors who treated him at the time. (Collage)

3847821.title: A Life’s Mission
3847821.description: Rabbi Yossi Gordon is a teacher in Yeshiva College in Melbourne Australia, and the director of Chabad of Tasmania. After hearing from the Rebbe about the greatness of serving Jews in remote places, he volunteered to assist in the Rebbe’s efforts to bring Judaism as far as Tasmania. A paper the Rebbe gave him before leaving keeps him inspired until this day.

3855287.title: In a Strange Land
3855287.description: The Torah relates how our forefather Jacob behaved when he dwelled with Laban. Overcoming all the challenging circumstances he found himself in, he remained loyal and true to serving G-d despite them. While this steadfastness was a clear demonstration of where Jacob’s true allegiance lay, it still wasn’t the true fulfilment of his potential.

3855288.title: Mitteler Rebbe’s Kapelya
3855288.description: Chasidim sing during a farbrengen marking 9 Kislev, the birth & passing of Rabbi Dovber of Lubavitch.

3855289.title: In the Mitteler Rebbe’s Merit
3855289.description: Please give this to charity in honor of your ancestor, Rabbi Dovber of Lubavitch, known as the Mitteler Rebbe. (Collage)

3855290.title: Musical Harmony
3855290.description: Jeanne Zaidel-Rudolph is a composer, conductor, and professor of music at University of the Witwatersrand in Johannesburg, South Africa. As she and her husband became more observant, they travelled to New York for an audience with the Rebbe. Throughout their discussions, personal and professional, it was the Rebbe’s care that struck them most. (1981)

3861905.title: Cause for Celebration
3861905.description: On the fourteenth of Kislev in 1928, the Rebbe married Rebbetzin Chaya Mushka, the middle daughter of the Previous Lubavitcher Rebbe, Rabbi Yosef Yitzchak Schneerson.

3861906.title: Sheva Brachos
3861906.description: A Sheva Brachos ceremony is held for a newly married couple during a farbrengen at 770 in 1979.

3861907.title: Golden Jubilee
3861907.description: This is for congratulations for your fiftieth wedding anniversary. My apologies for always mixing into your affairs, but I hope you’re making a gathering for this occasion.

3861908.title: Two Halves of a Whole
3861908.description: In 1950, Rabbi Leibel and Thirza Posner became engaged to be married. The Rebbe, who was yet to officially accept leadership of Chabad after the passing of Rabbi Yosef Yitzchak Schneerson, granted them a private audience. During the meeting, the Rebbe shared with them the secret of what makes a marriage so special.

3871126.title: Pursuit of Peace
3871126.description: The Alter Rebbe’s release on 19 Kislev was so surprising that even government ministers were awed by the course of events. The same ministers who ordered his arrest and forbade the dissemination of Chassidism, gave him freedom and allowed him to continue spreading Torah.

3871127.title: Nigun Podoh V’sholom
3871127.description: During a farbrengen celebrating the Alter Rebbe’s liberation from Czarist imprisonment on 19 Kislev, chasidim sing the nigun, Podoh V’sholom.

3871128.title: They Bear Your Name
3871128.description: Be a good example for all the people around you. There are several establishments that are named after you. Landow Yeshiva has many students, and everyone has the name that he is a student in Mel Landow’s Yeshiva.

3871129.title: From Tennis to Tefillin
3871129.description: In 1970, Rabbi Sholom Ber Lipskar was sent as a Chabad emissary to Florida, where he serves as rabbi and director of The Shul in Bal Harbor. A member of his community, a champion tennis player, invited him to meet his wealthy friend. Bringing his Tefillin to the tennis courts began a relationship that lasted well beyond that first encounter. In fact, the impact of that meeting is still felt by hundreds of children today.

3880672.title: A Light in the Darkness
3880672.description: On the 19th of Kislev, Rabbi Schneur Zalman, the first Rebbe of Chabad, was released from prison after being arrested by Czarist authorities on false charges of providing aid to the Turkish Sultan.

3880673.title: Niggun - Haneiros Halalu
3880673.description: Chassidim sing Haneiros Halalu after the lighting of the Menorah on the fifth night of Chanukah in 1990.

3880674.title: Think Big
3880674.description: Dr. Larry Resnick treated the Rebbe after he suffered a heart attack in 1977. Here, he brings his family to visit the Rebbe.

3880675.title: Doctor and Chasid
3880675.description: On Shmini Atzeres in 1977, the Rebbe suffered a massive heart attack during the dancing. For the next five weeks, Jews around the world prayed for the Rebbe’s health and wellbeing. Rabbi Mendel Groner, whose father was a personal secretary of the Rebbe, was a student at 770 at the time. Here, he recalls the joy that Chassidim felt when the Rebbe finally returned home

3889801.title: The Hidden Good
3889801.description: On the tenth of the Hebrew month of Teves, Nebuchadnezzar and the armies of Babylon laid siege to the holy city of Jerusalem. This led to the eventual destruction of the first Holy Temple on the ninth of Av.

3889802.title: A Movement on Trial (Excerpt)
3889802.description: Scenes from JEM’s landmark film "A Movement on Trial".

3889803.title: I’ve Waited Too Long
3889803.description: You saved me energy; I was going to reprimand you for not publishing your book yet. I’m happy to hear that it’ll be published soon. (Collage)

3889804.title: Bringing the Rebbe Joy
3889804.description: In 1985, important books and manuscripts were discovered missing from the Previous Rebbe’s Library. Following a surveillance operation, the culprit was found, leading to a long court battle over the ownership of the library itself. Throughout the battle, the Rebbe frequented and prayed at the resting place of his father-in-law and predecessor, the Previous Rebbe. Rabbi Mendel Azimov was a yeshiva student at the time, whose father, Rabbi Shmuel Azimov, was the Rebbe’s emissary to France. At one point, Rabbi Shmuel Azimov led an initiative in the Rebbe’s merit.

3892581.title: The Rebbe and the Best-Selling Author
3892581.description: The Rebbe vocally and repeatedly called for every individual to utilize his or her unique talents and abilities to help promote a spirit of G-dliness in the world.
path: The Rebbe and the Best-Selling Author

3892582.title: Author’s Visit
3892582.description: Award-winning author Chaim Potok visits the Rebbe. The Rebbe encourages him to use his platform to promote Judaism.

3892583.title: The Cast and Crew
3892583.description: Individuals involved in the film-making business visit the Rebbe. The Rebbe encourages them to use their platform for good. (Collage)

3892584.title: A Risky Business
3892584.description: In the late 1980s, Rabbi Shlomo Schwartz was a Chabad emissary in Los Angeles, California. He recalls having a great idea to pitch to producers in Hollywood. It was just after Rabbi Yitzchak Kogan got out of the Soviet Union, and writing a script about his story would be a great way to draw attention to the plight of the Jews that were stuck there. But after he asked the Rebbe for his blessing, all his plans were changed.

3902044.title: The Mystical Meaning of the Name Schneur
3902044.description: The twenty-fourth of Teves marks the passing of Rabbi Schneur Zalman of Liadi, the founder of Chabad Chassidism. He is famous among Jews today as the author of both the Tanya and a version of the Code of Jewish Law. His name, Schneur, hints to his unique ability to teach and expound on both the revealed and the more esoteric parts of the Torah.
path: The Mystical Meaning of the Name Schneur

3902045.title: Niggun - Tzomoh Lecho Nafshi
3902045.description: Chassidim join together in singing this soul stirring melody as the Rebbe leads the Niggun during a Farbrengen celebrating his birthday in 1981.

3902047.title: Fulfilling an Obligation
3902047.description: Rabbi Henry Isaacs served as rabbi on Bangor, Maine, for close to forty years. In 1958, he was a rabbinical student at Yeshiva University, and was engaged to be married. He had plans to enter the Armed Forces and join the Air Force. His father wouldn’t agree and unsure how to proceed, he turned to the Rebbe. The Rebbe’s advice on that night was more far-reaching than he could have ever imagined at the time.

3908661.title: Standing Up for Our Future
3908661.description: Faced with the prospect of their baby boys being killed by the Egyptians, the Jews in Egypt followed the lead of Amram, the father of Moses, in flouting Pharaoh's decrees and continuing to have children. These young boys would become the generation to leave the bondage in Egypt and perceive revealed G-dliness at the splitting of the Red Sea.

3908662.title: Nigun - Zol Shoin Zein Di Geula
3908662.description: Chasidim sing a lively nigun during farbrengen. The nigun is of our urgent request of the Almighty, to send us Moshiach now.
path: Nigun - Zol Shoin Zein Di Geula

3908663.title: Guarding Her Beauty
3908663.description: Much success with the concert, and may it take place in a modest manner. As a female singer, you should sing joyfully for the Jewish people, but only for female audiences. (Collage)

3908664.title: A Change in Career
3908664.description: Meir Bastomski wasn’t raised in a Lubavitch family, so as he began to look and dress more like a Chabad Chassid, he also began to worry about any upset it might bring to his parents. It became so uncomfortable, that he was reluctant to return home for fear of causing friction in his relationship with them. Unsure of the best way to proceed, he asked the Rebbe for advice. (1967)

3914303.title: Tending G-d’s Garden
3914303.description: The last discourse that Rabbi Yosef Yitzchak Schneersohn, the Previous Lubavitcher Rebbe, published before his passing commences with the verse “I have come into My garden.” The Previous Rebbe explains that this refers to our world, the innermost dwelling place of G-d.

3914304.title: 10 Shevat - 5747
3914304.description: Special footage of the morning services on the 10th of Shevat, the anniversary of the Previous Rebbe’s passing and the day on which the Rebbe formally accepted leadership of Chabad one year later.

3914305.title: The Garden Above
3914305.description: The Midrash explains that G-d’s abode is called His garden. May you reach true Ramat – heights, and may it be a true Gan – garden. And may it be so with joy and happiness.

3914306.title: Everything in Its Time
3914306.description: Michael Allouche is an aerospace engineer from France. He asked the Rebbe numerous times about the prospect of making Aliya with his family and moving to Israel, yet he was always somewhat disappointed when the Rebbe discouraged them from doing so. When the Israeli Air Force embarked on a project to build their own fighter jet, it seemed like a most opportune time for him to relocate with his family. Yet for some reason, the Rebbe wouldn’t give them his blessing for the move. (1982)

3914326.title: A Modern Day Moses
3914326.description: Like the human body, a nation comprises of a “head” which guides their direction and “feet” to do the lifting and lead them towards it. The Zohar teaches that in every generation there’s an individual, who like Moses, serves as the head of the Jewish nation, injecting life and vitality into all those connected to him.

3914327.title: Nigun Beinoni
3914327.description: Chasidim sing the Beinoni, a song attributed to Rabbi Yosef Yitzchak Schneersohn, the Previous Lubavitcher Rebbe.

3914328.title: Making of Leaders
3914328.description: The word nasi means to lift up, and a nasi, a Jewish leader, needs to elevate every single Jew, both spiritually and physically.

3914329.title: A Community of Individuals
3914329.description: Nochum Stilerman grew up in the Crown Heights area of Brooklyn in the years following World War ll. It was in this immigrant community that his father decided to open a Kosher grocery store. Challenging all the naysayers, they managed to keep the store afloat and served many prominent customers in the process. Nochum would help his father with the deliveries, but was embarrassed by his menial work when he became of marriageable age. On one of his delivery stops, he asked the Rebbe for some advice. (1960s)

3920843.title: No Matter Where You May Roam
3920843.description: There’s a lot we can learn from the order and sequence of stories in the Torah. In this week’s Torah portion, we begin with the story of Jethro and go on to read about the Ten Commandments, encompassing all the fundamentals of the Torah.
path: No Matter Where You May Roam

3920844.title: The Rebbetzin (Excerpt)
3920844.description: A special presentation highlighting the greatness and modesty of the Rebbe’s wife, Rebbetzin Chaya Mushka Schneerson.

3920845.title: No Better Time
3920845.description: It would be appropriate to perform good deeds in memory of the Rebbetzin. Her first name was Chaya, meaning “life.” That applies even after the life of the person, until the Resurrection. I hope it will be very soon.

3920846.title: Sharing the Experience
3920846.description: Eliot Sovronsky is a videographer who was commissioned to film the Rebbe’s farbrengens in the 1970s. He was very pleased to hear that the Rebbe appreciated his concern for the Rebbetzin, the Rebbe’s wife, to be able to view the farbrengens on video.

3936069.title: Women of Honor
3936069.description: The tasks of the Jewish people are divided between Torah study and engaging in the physical world. The rule, however, is that commandments don’t override Torah study. Nevertheless, a mitzvah that cannot be done by others does override Torah study; it actually takes priority.

3936070.title: Dollars for Shelichut
3936070.description: Scenes of the Rebbe distributing dollars to emissaries of Chabad from all around the world.

3936071.title: Mainstay of the Home
3936071.description: The Talmud says that livelihood comes in the merit of one’s wife. She gives you the merit of a better livelihood, so give this to charity for your wife, the mainstay of the home. May the Almighty bless you with blessing and success. (Collage)

3936072.title: Getting to Work
3936072.description: Shortly after getting married, Gittel Eidelman moved with her husband to Morocco as emissaries of the Rebbe. Having grown up in England, Morocco wasn’t exactly a natural place for her to end up living. It was an interesting place for them to have ended up, but with the Rebbe’s guidance, they succeeded in having a real impact on the community there. (1959)

3936085.title: Children Lead the Fight
3936085.description: The Megillah relates that everyone, from young to old, was included in Haman’s decree. Similarly, the Evil Inclination, also wants to, G-d forbid, influence the Jewish people, starting with Jewish children, to weaken their strength and pride.

3936086.title: Nigun Simcha
3936086.description: A Chassidic Nigun traditionally sung to the opening verse of the Purim Megilah: Vayehi Bimei Achashveirosh.

3936087.title: Generations of Success
3936087.description: May you have much success in the Rabbinate and with all your students in the entire yeshiva. (Collage)

3936088.title: A Picture Tells a Thousand Words
3936088.description: Rabbi Shimon Elituv is a rabbi in Mevaseret Zion and a member of the Chief Rabbinate Council. As a young boy, he sent his first letter to the Rebbe, beginning a relationship that has lasted since. Here, he remembers the help that the Rebbe provided to him and his family during difficult times. And it was the Rebbe’s guidance and inspiration that set him on his career path until this day. (1957)
path: A Picture Tells a Thousand Words

3947491.title: Stop Living in the Past
3947491.description: The Baal Shem Tov explains the Talmudic statement, “One who reads the Megilah backwards, does not fulfill his obligation.” He interprets “backwards” to mean that one can read the Megilah following all the laws, with all the proper intentions, but at the same time, he might think “This is ‘backwards,’ it’s irrelevant.

3947492.title: Megilah Reading
3947492.description: Scenes from the Megilah reading on Purim in 5749 - 1989.

3947493.title: A Healthy Purim
3947493.description: May God bless you with many healthy and successful years. Happy Purim for all Jews. For now, get rid of one of your walking sticks, and keep the other. In time, you’ll get rid of the second one too.

3947494.title: Seeking in Bangladesh
3947494.description: Max Cohen is a businessman from Manchester, England who was scheduled to make a trip to Bangladesh in April of 1991. Shortly before his trip, a powerful cyclone had struck the Chittagong district of southeastern Bangladesh, killing 138,000 people and leaving over ten million homeless. He was very worried about the safety of travelling there as more cyclone warnings were still in effect in that area. But a message he received from the Rebbe made him reconsider cancelling.

3947513.title: On False Humility
3947513.description: Chassidism requires us to fulfil our G-dly mission proudly regardless of how it might affect our own growth. In fact, spreading G-dliness to those around us will most certainly impact us positively as well. It’s our responsibility to do what is required of us to transform the world positively. As for the sense conceit that it can possibly impart in us along the way, that can always be rectified through the fire of Torah and mitzvos.

3947514.title: Walking to 770
3947514.description: Vintage footage of the Rebbe walking to 770 in the morning, during the 1960s.

3947515.title: No Need to be Meek
3947515.description: There is a difference between humility, which means that you recognize your abilities but it doesn’t affect your ego, and meekness, which means you don’t recognize your value at all. Humility will be enough.

3947516.title: Any Further Questions?
3947516.description: Yehudis Fishman had an audience scheduled with the Rebbe late in the evening. The long wait outside the Rebbe’s room gave her time to think about some different questions that we wished the Rebbe would answer, and she was pleasantly surprised when the Rebbe afforded her that opportunity. Here, she remembers some of the questions that she asked. (1960s)

3967185.title: A Birthday Meditation
3967185.description: In 1988, one month after the passing of his wife, Rebbetzin Chaya Mushka, the Rebbe launched the Birthday Campaign in her memory. At a farbrengen marking his own birthday in 1983, the Rebbe explained the significance of the occasion.

3967186.title: Farbrengen
3967186.description: A video clip of recently discovered footage that was filmed during a farbrengenin the early 1970s.

3967187.title: Mr. Manchester
3967187.description: A rare recording of a private audience that the Jaffe family from Manchester merited to have with the Rebbe. The audience outside the Rebbe’s study was held in honor of the Bar Mitzvah of one of Mr. Jaffe’s grandchildren.

3967188.title: When Three Girls Left a Letter for the Rebbetzin
3967188.description: Devora Caytak heads the Jewish Youth Library in Ottawa, Canada. In 1978, after making her way back to Judaism, she was a seminary student at Machon Chana in the Crown Heights section of Brooklyn. Feeling alone, she and her friends decided to write a letter to the Rebbe’s wife, Rebbetzin Chaya Mushka. The Rebbetzin’s surprising response is a lesson that Devorah has implemented in her own life until this day.
path: When Three Girls Left a Letter for the Rebbetzin

3972401.title: Confused Souls
3972401.description: Every soul descends to this world to fulfill a mission that’s unique from any other. The Evil Inclination, however, cunningly tries to mislead a person from his true path by distracting him with other seemingly virtuous tasks.

3972402.title: Nigun Rostov
3972402.description: Chasidim sing the Rostover nigun, usually sung in preparation for a Maamar, a Chasidic Discourse. This nigun is often associated with the fifth Rebbe of Chabad, the Rebbe Rashab.

3972403.title: Source of Healing
3972403.description: May your primary work as a doctor be in preventive medicine. But since there are those who, for now, need to be healed, may you merit to utilize G-d’s permission for a doctor to cure, in a good and successful manner. (Collage)

3972404.title: No Appointment Necessary
3972404.description: Rabbi Yaakov Shpitzer was director of the Sanz-Klausenberg institutions in Israel before becoming the chief gabbai of the Imrei Shefer community in Jerusalem. In the early 1980s, his niece was suffering from a particularly aggressive cancer that doctors said left her with slim chances for survival. During an audience with the Rebbe, he raised her plight and left the meeting with specific instructions of what to do.

3980078.title: Why Is this Night Different?
3980078.description: The themes of the month of Nissan, and especially of Passover, comprise the fundamentals of Judaism. Accordingly, the Exodus from Egypt, and the messages of the holiday, must be applied not just once a month, but during every single day of a Jew’s life.

3980079.title: Burning Chametz
3980079.description: Film of the Rebbe during the burning of the chametz on the eve of Passover in 1987.

3980080.title: Closed for Shabbos
3980080.description: Put a charity box in your place of business, and run the business according to the laws of Shabbos. Being meticulous in your observance of Shabbos and the festivals will bring you financial success in all your endeavors. (Collage)

3980081.title: Closed for Business
3980081.description: Today, Harvey Milstein is a businessman living in Israel. As a child, however, he grew up in the Crown Heights section of Brooklyn where his father owned a pharmacy. While his father was a respected member of the religious community, he still struggled with the idea of closing his business on Shabbos and Jewish holidays. But a letter from the Rebbe finally convinced him to change his mind. (1960)

3985003.title: A Personal Exodus
3985003.description: In a Chassidic discourse distinguished by its tone and rhythm, the Rebbe draws parallels between the Exodus from Egypt, and the journey of the soul. Just like there were many stages to the Exodus, in which as each boundary was breached another needed to be overcome, our lives are very much the same.

3985004.title: Distribution of Matzah
3985004.description: Film of the Rebbe distributing Matzah to Shluchim who are leading public Seders on Passover of 1987.

3985005.title: The Rebbe’s Matzos
3985005.description: Have a good new year, with much success in baking Matzos, the “bread of healing” and “bread of faith.” (Collage)

3985006.title: Straight to the Top
3985006.description: Rabbi Efraim Schmuckler has served as rabbi of the Geriatric Center in Montreal, Canada for over thirty years. In 1970, during an audience with the Rebbe, he asked for a blessing that his uncle succeed in leaving Soviet Russia. The Rebbe gave him a blessing, but made it conditional on him keeping it secret. He was elated to have received assurances from the Rebbe, but was dismayed when he failed to live up to the condition the Rebbe had set.

3986026.title: It Means You
