3986026.description: In recent decades, we have experienced a level of liberty that our grandparents could have only dreamed about. Of course, this level of freedom brings about its own challenges as we try to dedicate ourselves towards the service of our Creator.

3986027.title: Kos Shel Brachah
3986027.description: Following the Havdalah ceremony after Passover, the Rebbe distributes wine from his cup, known as Kos Shel Brachah - Cup of Blessing.

3986028.title: Leaving Egypt After Passover
3986028.description: The Naroler Rebbe visits and brings the Rebbe a Haggadah with glosses of the Koidanover Rebbe, compiled by his son-in-law, a great-grandson of the Koidanover Rebbe.

3986029.title: A Gift for Your Father
3986029.description: Menasheh Janashvilli lives in Lud, Israel. As a teenager in the 1970s, he travelled to the United States to study at the United Lubavitcher Yeshiva in Brooklyn, New York. The Rebbe’s words to him after Pesach made him wonder if everything was okay with his father back in Israel. It was only after he finally reached his father on the telephone that he began to appreciate the full story.

3986041.title: Back to the Fundamentals
3986041.description: The world seems to be so unstable these days. Time and again, the news is filled with stories of senseless violence in schools and on the streets. The politicians continue to debate on an appropriate response, but in the meantime, a generation of children is missing out on experiencing life to the fullest.

3986042.title: Post-Passover Yechidus
3986042.description: A public audience in which the Rebbe addresses the guests who had come to spend the holiday with him at 770.

3986043.title: Where Are the Results?
3986043.description: You need to be more active. You’re working and working, but where are the results? May you have blessings and success and report good tidings.

3986044.title: A Torah of Truth
3986044.description: Rabbi Sholom Rephune is an educator and community activist. In the early 1970s, while serving as principal of Manhattan Day School, he made an appointment to see the Rebbe. It was an important meeting for him, as he had a long list of questions that he wished to ask the Rebbe about reconciling science with the Torah.

3996750.title: Searching for Pearls
3996750.description: The Previous Rebbe, Rabbi Yosef Yitzchak, compared chassidic teachings to pearls and coal. Pearls, he explained, are found in the depths of the sea, while coal is found deep in the earth.

3996751.title: Nigun - Becha Hashem
3996751.description: Color footage that was filmed for a television program, featuring Chassidim singing a lively nigun composed for the Rebbe’s 70th birthday, B’cha Hashem.

3996752.title: X-Ray Vision
3996752.description: In radiology, you work on revealing something hidden, something that is not on the surface. May G-d Almighty bless you to reveal the 'Penimiyus', the inner soul, of every Jew that you come into contact with.

3996753.title: A Teenager’s Dream
3996753.description: Golda Jacobs is a career counselor and consultant. As a teenager growing up in Chicago in the 1960s, she had a strong desire to travel on Zim Lines, a shipping company that offered rides to Israel. After her father heard her plans to travel alone with another female friend, he raised concerns about their safety. Golda wasn’t willing to let go of her dream so easily, and decided to ask the Rebbe what to do.

4012526.title: Deeper Bonds
4012526.description: The Lag B’omer rallies and parades outside 770 drew thousands of Jews from all walks of life and backgrounds. The gatherings attest to the fact that despite all our differences in language and culture, there is a single unifying force that keeps all Jews together as one family. But what is that glue that binds us together, and how do we maintain it throughout the rest of the year as well?

4012527.title: Sheyiboneh
4012527.description: Cantor Moshe Teleshevsky leads the crowd at a Lag B’omer rally in a rendition of the classical Jewish Niggun, Sheyiboneh.

4012528.title: Onboard Charity
4012528.description: There is probably a charity box onboard your Mitzvah Tank. Put this dollar in there. Good tidings and much success. (Collage)

4012529.title: Different Strokes for Different Folks
4012529.description: Rabbi Raphael Aron is the director of the Gateway family Counseling Centre in Melbourne, Australia. In 1974, while running the Lubavitch Youth Organization in Melbourne, he had an audience with the Rebbe. At the time, he was looking for a way to deal with the opposition they were receiving for the rambunctious nature of their Mitzvah campaigns. The Rebbe’s response was somewhat surprising, and has remained with him since.

4019311.title: Earning Respect
4019311.description: As Jews, we can be plagued by feeling different from those around us, leading us to compromise on the integrity of our own values in a bid to gain acceptance. In a talk to women and girls, the Rebbe highlights a quote in Maimonides that teaches us how to really earn respect.

4019312.title: Lively Nigun
4019312.description: Chassidim join together at a farbrengen in singing a lively Chabad nigun.

4019313.title: Medical Advice
4019313.description: Don’t predict what will happen in a year from now, you are not a prophet. Ask a doctor who is active with new developments. If there will be a good development, they will probably change their minds and give a better prognosis for the future. May you have good tidings. (Collage)

4019314.title: More Than a Donation
4019314.description: In 1975, Rabbi Yekusiel Yehudah Halberstam, the Sanz-Klausenburger Rebbe, opened a not-for-profit hospital in Netanya, Israel. He appointed Rabbi Gershon Lieder to oversee the project while it was still in the early stages of development, and as the eventual director of the hospital. As part of their effort, the fundraising committee decided to visit the Lubavitcher Rebbe in Brooklyn, to ask for his assistance and advice.

4020988.title: Faith Comes First
4020988.description: To many, Judaism represents intellectualism, analysis, study, and questioning. While it’s true that as Jews, we place great emphasis on a critical education, there’s another necessary ingredient before we’re ready for any of that.

4020989.title: The Rebbe’s Aliyah
4020989.description: The Rebbe is called to the Torah for an Aliyah during the morning services.

4020990.title: The Path to Success
4020990.description: The first thing you should do is observe Shabbos. G-d commanded us to keep Shabbos when he gave the Torah, in the Ten Commandments, and every Jew must keep it, throughout the ages.

4020991.title: The Start of a Campaign
4020991.description: Rabbi Chaim Jacobs and his wife Sora, have been the co-directors of Lubavitch of Scotland for more than four decades. In 1967, the Rebbe launched the now famous Tefillin campaign. A Yeshiva student at the time, Rabbi Jacobs began an initiative for students to visit the local Jews and help them don Tefillin. He remembers the Rebbe’s warm responses to the work they were doing.

4032879.title: Seize the Days
4032879.description: In ancient times, thousands of Jews with offerings in hand would make the pilgrimage to Jerusalem for the festival of Shavuot. For those who weren’t able to bring their offerings in the Temple on the holiday itself, some more time was allotted afterward, known as the days of Tashlumin.

4032880.title: Kos Shel Brachah
4032880.description: The Rebbe pours Kos Shel Brachah from his cup following the holiday of Shavuos.

4032881.title: Securing All Jews
4032881.description: Much success in protecting the Land of Israel, as well as protecting the spiritual integrity of the Land of Israel. May the Jews in the Holy Land be protected, and by extension, the Jews all over the world. Good tidings, and happy holiday. (Collage)

4032882.title: A Rising Threat
4032882.description: Shlomo Shamir is a journalist and political analyst. He was the New York correspondent for the Israeli daily, Haaretz, for over thirty-five years, and a long time columnist for the Algemeiner Journal. He met and corresponded with the Rebbe on numerous occasions over the years, but it was an indirect message that he received from the Rebbe that led him to send the Rebbe an apology. (1979)

4040747.title: Charity Begins at Home
4040747.description: Each year, in the days around the holiday of Shavuos, the Rebbe would deliver a special address to members of the N’shei Chabad Women’s group. Here, we present an excerpt from the Rebbe’s talk at this gathering in 1991.

4040748.title: N’shei Chabad
4040748.description: Vintage footage of the Rebbe receiving petitions from the N’shei Chabad women’s group in the days before Shavuos.

4040749.title: Women Will Bring Moshiach
4040749.description: To spread the wellsprings of Judaism outwards, you need to be outside; otherwise you won’t be able to spread Judaism there. It all depends on you. You need to watch over yourself. Don’t focus on the “outside,” focus on the “wellsprings.”

4040750.title: Help Your Friend First
4040750.description: Mrs. Rochel Fogelman and her husband, Rabbi Hershel Fogelman, of blessed memory, have been Chabad emissaries in Worcester, Massachusetts since 1947. She remembers asking the Rebbe repeatedly for a blessing for her sister to find her match. Her sister seemed so choosy, it almost looked like there wouldn’t be anyone who’d meet her qualifications. The matter was on her mind again when she brought a group with her to the Rebbe from Worcester, Massachusetts in the 1950s. Thankfully, she finally received the blessing she was seeking when the Rebbe asked her to help someone else.

4047338.title: How Jews Support Large Families
4047338.description: Judaism teaches us that each and every child born is a cherished blessing for its parents and the Jewish people as a whole. But where can parents gain the confidence to take on the financial burden of raising a large family? The real answer is that your success was never in your hands anyway.

4047339.title: Children’s Rally
4047339.description: Vintage footage of the Rebbe taking part in a rally for Jewish children on the 13th of Sivan in 5740 – 1980.

4047340.title: Spread the Love
4047340.description: The Lelov dynasty is renowned as lovers of Israel. Give this to charity in the Holy Land, and may you merit to bring good tidings for all of Israel. (Collage)

4047341.title: This is for Your Child
4047341.description: Rabbi Simcha Krakovsky is a community activist and served as a secretary of the Lelover Rebbe in Bnei Brak, Israel. When he and his wife struggled to have children, a friend of his, Mordechai Werdiger, invited Rabbi Krakovsky to visit the Rebbe and ask for a blessing. (1989)

4050170.title: Nobody Gets a Pass
4050170.description: All too often, it’s those with the most to contribute that are complacent when it comes to securing a future for the Jewish people. Here, the Rebbe expounds on a passage from Maimonides’ book of Jewish law to show that when it comes to the battle for Jewish continuity, nobody gets a pass.

4050171.title: Invited to a Farbrengen
4050171.description: On the 28th of Sivan in 1941 the Rebbe arrived in America with his wife, Rebbetzin Chaya Mushka. On the anniversary of this day, chasidim are invited to a celebratory farbrengen.

4050172.title: Achieving Quick Success
4050172.description: It is often overlooked, but the Rogatchover Gaon was also a very quick person. Whether in studying, writing or speaking, and even eating, he accomplished everything very quickly. Beginning with study...

4050173.title: A Rebbe, A Mentch
4050173.description: Rabbi Chaim Zev Bomzer was a longstanding member of the Rabbinical Council of America, and Rabbi of Young Israel of Ocean Parkway for more than forty years. It was during the sixties that over the course of his travels to Israel, he developed a relationship with the chief chaplain of the Israeli Army, Rabbi Shlomo Goren. Once, when Rabbi Goren was in New York, he asked Rabbi Bomzer to take him to see the Rebbe.

4052875.title: Even More Than Before
4052875.description: The third day of Tammuz marks the passing of the Rebbe. Citing Jewish history and texts, the Rebbe demonstrates that a true Jewish leader is always present, and will never leave his flock.

4052876.title: We Want Moshiach Now!
4052876.description: Newly recovered footage from 10 Shevat in 5741 of the Rebbe leading chasidim in singing the now famous song, We Want Moshiach Now.

4052877.title: Conveying G-d’s Blessings
4052877.description: Thank you very much for giving me the possibility to bless a Jew. May G-d Almighty bless you to do even better, and have good news. The main thing is that the blessings should be fulfilled. May G-d bless you that you will thank Him at age 120. (Collage)

4052878.title: They Need to Spread Outside
4052878.description: Rabbi Tzvi Greenwald was an educator living in Kfar Chabad. In the 1960s, he was involved in the “Evening with Chabad” outreach program, visiting kibbutzim across Israel. After receiving criticism for his approach toward the attendees and the atmosphere at the events, he decided to ask the Rebbe how to continue his activities.

4057734.title: Despite the Odds
4057734.description: On the 12th of Tammuz in 1927, the Rebbe’s predecessor and father-in-law, Rabbi Yosef Yitzchak Schneerson, was released from Soviet imprisonment.

4057735.title: 12 Tammuz Niggun
4057735.description: On the 12th of Tammuz in 1927, the sixth Rebbe of Chabad, Rabbi Yosef Yitzchak Schneerson was released from soviet imprisonment after being arrested for his activities in spreading Judaism across the USSR. At a farbrengenmarking this day, chasidimsing a niguncomposed by R’ Aharon Charitonov to mark the release.

4057736.title: Good Memories
4057736.description: Many good and long years, and many more years of leadership. May all these good memories of the Previous Rebbe bring about many good things. May we all meet very soon in the Holy Land.

4057737.title: Spiritual Extravagance
4057737.description: Rabbi Sholom Spalter is on the faculty of the Rabbinical College of America in Morristown, New Jersey. Before his Bar Mitzvah, his father wrote to the Rebbe. The Rebbe’s memorable response changed his Bar Mitzvah, as well as those of his children. (1967)

4069628.title: A Breach of the Wall
4069628.description: The 17th of Tammuz is a fast day that marks the beginning of a period of mourning over the destruction of the Holy Temples in Jerusalem. But as a matter of fact, this day bore tragedy for Jews even before the walls of Jerusalem were breached. Indeed, there are famously five tragic events which befell the Jewish people on this day. It’s strange then, that so much emphasis is put on the Jerusalem walls.

4069629.title: Haftorah
4069629.description: During the Mincha services on the 17th of Tammuz, the Rebbe is called to the Torah and recites the haftorah.

4069630.title: Visiting Family
4069630.description: After the Three Weeks of mourning the destruction of the Holy Temples pass, good tidings follow – may it be so in this matter also.

4069631.title: Living to See Nachas
4069631.description: In 1974, Rabbi Shimon and Goldie Feld became engaged. But while they were making plans for their wedding celebration, they were also receiving worrying news from the doctors who were treating Goldie’s father for a cancer that he was battling. When some Chassidim suggested that they ask the Rebbe for a blessing for him to be able to attend the wedding, they grabbed the opportunity.

4074478.title: Bonds of Love
4074478.description: Our sages teach that the Holy Temple was destroyed because of the baseless hatred that Jews harbored towards one another. It follows then, that rectifying that problem will be the catalyst for rebuilding it. And Speedily.

4074479.title: Rally for Public School Students
4074479.description: The Rebbe takes part in a rally for Jewish children studying at New York public schools. (July, 1976)

4074480.title: A Spark of Moshiach
4074480.description: The Rambam writes, “May they be immediately redeemed”. The Rambam is a book of law, so this must be a law as well! That we must be immediately redeemed.

4074481.title: A Healthy Diet
4074481.description: Rabbi Yosef Yitzchak Gurewitz serves on the faculty of Yeshiva Tomchei Temimim in Migdal Haemek, Israel. He remembers how when his wife was expecting, she started feeling severe pains which impacted her breathing. After receiving a diagnosis, they were strongly urged by her doctor to go ahead with surgery. After asking the Rebbe a number of times about how to proceed, they finally received an answer - albeit not one that they or their doctor were expecting. (1979)

4074494.title: A Modest People
4074494.description: The fashion and glamor of the wider world can look most alluring. Why, the logic goes, should I stand out like a sore thumb among the rest of society? To that end, dressing in a way that is different to that of the society around us can be a real challenge.

4074495.title: “To Love a Fellow Jew”
4074495.description: Chassidim join together in singing the Jewish children’s classic “To Love a Fellow Jew” as the Rebbe distributes wine at the conclusion of Passover.

4074496.title: Hold on to a Good Thing
4074496.description: Perhaps you can sell a portion of your company, but the money you receive should be invested back into the company. It needs to remain active, since G-d needs you to continue giving charity, a lot of charity, as you’ve been doing until now.
path: Hold on to a Good Thing

4074497.title: If at First You Don’t Succeed
4074497.description: David Mintz is the founder and CEO of Tofutti Brands. In the early 1980s he was the proprietor of Mintz’s Buffet, a kosher catering business in New York. With an eye on expanding his catering business, he asked the Rebbe for a blessing. The answer he received was unequivocal: he should not pursue this opportunity. Instead, the Rebbe encouraged him to continue his experimentations with creating frozen tofu desserts. Looking back, it almost seems obvious. But at the time, it took a great level of trust to heed the Rebbe’s advice.
path: If at First You Don’t Succeed

4089232.title: The Greatest of Holidays
4089232.description: Kabbalistic teachings explain that if G-d ever allows for a descent in goodness and holiness, it can only be for the purpose of achieving something even greater. This concept, in fact, sheds light on a peculiar statement in the Mishnah. An address about the unique holiday marked on the 15th of Av.

4089233.title: Havdalah
4089233.description: At the conclusion of the fast of Tisha B’av, the Rebbe listens to havdalah being recited in 770.

4089234.title: In Moshiach’s Times
4089234.description: In Moshiach’s time there will also be wealthy people. So you’ll have what to do then too. May you go from strength to strength, and may we very soon gather together with all Jews in the Holy Land. You will take the money along with you, so there is no need to worry. (Collage)

4089235.title: Surgeon Without Surgery
4089235.description: Dr. Leonard Lovitch is a general surgeon in Whittier, California. Originally members of a Conservative temple in North Hollywood, he and his wife were first introduced to Chabad in the mid-1970s. At one point, still in the beginning of his career, he was stepping on an unstable stool when he slipped and injured his eye. The prognosis wasn’t good, and he decided to ask the Rebbe for advice. He did, in fact, get an answer from the Rebbe, but it had no apparent connection to the injury of his eye. (1982)

4093161.title: The Golden Years, Part 1: Non-Retirement
4093161.description: At an age when most people retire, the Rebbe initiated an unprecedented expansion of the Chabad Lubavitch movement, and called for seventy new institutions to open their doors. Here the Rebbe shares his thoughts on putting one’s golden years to use.

4093162.title: Afternoon Prayers
4093162.description: The Rebbe leads Mincha, the Afternoon Prayer, on the occasion of his father’s yahrtzeit.

4093163.title: Forget About It
4093163.description: “I don’t believe in retirement…strength comes from G-d Almighty." (Collage)

4093164.title: Documenting History
4093164.description: Rabbi Naftali Tzvi Gottlieb was an author and biographer living in Betar Illit, Israel. Bothered by the fact that so little was known about the Rebbes’ father, he decided to write a book about him. (1960s)

4098681.title: The Golden Years, Part 2: Making Every Moment Count
4098681.description: During a gathering in 1980 marking the passing of his father, Rabbi Levi Yitzchak Schneerson, the Rebbe announced that it was high time that seniors start using their time more productively. He went on to establish a network of institutions to help them do just that. It was called Kolel Tiferes Zkeinim, Levi Yitzchak.
path: The Golden Years, Part 2: Making Every Moment Count

4098682.title: Scenes of a 1976 Farbrengen
4098682.description: Newly acquired film of a farbrengen in honor of the yahrzeit of the Rebbe’s father, Rabbi Levi Yitzchak Schneerson.

4098683.title: In My Father’s Name
4098683.description: “The synagogue carries my father’s name, so it has a connection to me, also.”

4098684.title: Never Stuck
4098684.description: Stranded in an airport away from their families, Miryam Swerdlov recalls the phone call made to the Rebbe. The Rebbe’s response was a life lesson for all Jews. (1967)

4098700.title: Yes, You Can Meet G‑d This Coming Month
4098700.description: The month of Elul is a time of introspection and preparation for the Days of Awe. In an address to children, the Rebbe teaches how we can all infuse these days with greater meaning.
path: Yes, You Can Meet G‑d This Coming Month

4098701.title: Nigun 'Kesivah'
4098701.description: During the distribution of dollars for charity at the conclusion of a children’s rally, chasidim sing a song with the words of “May you be inscribed and sealed for a sweet New Year”.

4098702.title: Shatnez and Redemption
4098702.description: “May G-d help, that we are soon able to use shatnez in the Temple service.”

4098703.title: To Each in His Way
4098703.description: Rabbi Nochum Cohen is an educator and rabbi serving the needs of diverse Jewish communities across Israel. During a trip to the United States in the 1970s, he had an audience with the Rebbe.

4098707.title: How to Build a Jewish Home
4098707.description: How did newlyweds of yesteryear get their new home ready prior to marriage?
path: How to Build a Jewish Home

4098708.title: Nigun 'Asher Bara'
4098708.description: Chasidim sing a song with words from the wedding liturgy.

4098709.title: A Foundation for Life
4098709.description: “This will be a receptacle for G-d Almighty’s blessings, for the preparation of the wedding itself.” (Collage)

4098710.title: Like a Father
4098710.description: Rabbi Tzvi Abba Lerman recalls the special attention the Rebbe gave him in the early 1950s, in connection to his wedding.

4114808.title: The Crown Jewel
4114808.description: The eighteenth of Elul marks the birth of two leaders that revolutionized the Jewish world. The Baal Shem Tov, founder of the Chasidic movement, and the Alter Rebbe, founder of Chabad. Yet if their teachings are so vital, why did they come so late in Jewish history?

4114809.title: Afternoon Prayers
4114809.description: Mincha Prayers in the Rebbe’s home.

4114810.title: Spreading the Study of Tanya
4114810.description: Be sure to give charity before the class, because the study of Torah and charity are connected. (Collage)

4114811.title: Gaining Approval
4114811.description: Rabbi Gad Bouskila has served as rabbi of Congregation Netivot Israel in Brooklyn, New York, for over three decades. Originally from Morocco, he was a yeshiva student in Lakewood, New Jersey, in 1980.

4121883.title: Everything in Focus
4121883.description: The goal of Jewish life should undoubtedly be spiritual – growth in the study and observance of Torah. If after this simple test, one sees that this isn’t the case, then the month of Elul is the perfect time to get things in focus.

4121884.title: Slichos
4121884.description: Reciting of Slichos in the week leading up to Rosh Hashana.

4121885.title: Settling the Land
4121885.description: Establish it this year, before the new year begins.

4121886.title: An Effort to Innovate
4121886.description: Rabbi Yitzchok Sufrin is an administrator of the Lubavitch Foundation in the United Kingdom. In 1962 he was a student at the Central Lubavitch Yeshiva in Brooklyn, New York, and engaged to be married.

4127313.title: Who Is G-d's Partner in Creation?
4127313.description: In a Jewish household, the wife and mother is called the mainstay of the home. But when it comes to the month of Elul, every Jew should strive to fulfill this role.
path: Who Is G-d's Partner in Creation?

4127314.title: Nigun
4127314.description: The Rebbe begins the nigun Nyet Nyet Nikavo.

4127315.title: New Year for All
4127315.description: God Almighty bless you, and thank you for your protection.

4127316.title: Sounding the Shofar
4127316.description: Rabbi Sholom Tenenbaumis an educator living in Brooklyn New York. Beginning in the early 1950s his father, Rabbi Yosef Menachem Tenenbaum, would sound the Shofar on Rosh Hashanah in 770.

4127343.title: Repentance with Joy
4127343.description: “Seek G-d when he is found, call Him when He is near.” Our sages teach that this verse refers to the Ten Days Between Rosh Hashanah and Yom Kippur, when our repentance is especially effective and accepted immediately by G-d.

4127344.title: Kos Shel Brachah
4127344.description: The Rebbe distributes wine from his cup of blessing, following Rosh Hashanah.

4127345.title: Protecting our Interests
4127345.description: May G-d grant that the rulings of the consulate should be in a manner that the Jewish nation will be happy to fulfill them.

4127346.title: Sound Advice
4127346.description: Rabbi Avraham Tanzer has served as head of Yeshiva College and spiritual leader of the Glenhazel Hebrew Congregation in Johannesburg, South Africa, for over five decades. In 1966, he had an audience with the Rebbe.

4127350.title: Closer Than You Think
4127350.description: The Torah reading of Ha’azinu consists of a song delivered by Moses on the last day of his life. In it he exhorts the Jewish people to be faithful to G-d, and calls upon the heavens and earth to bear witness.

4127351.title: Sukkos
4127351.description: A group of Chassidim representing Chabad communities around the world, along with members of the Rebbe’s secretariat, are invited into the Rebbe’s study, to choose for themselves the Four Species for the upcoming Festival. (Late 1970s)

4127352.title: Season’s Greetings
4127352.description: “It might be a new year, but the esrogim were planted two or three years ago…” (Collage)

4127353.title: Matters of Faith
4127353.description: Yosef Shandling reconnected to his Jewish roots as a senior in college. In 1970, as a student in Yeshiva Hadar Hatorah in Brooklyn, New York, he had an audience with the Rebbe.

4127355.title: The Properties of Water
4127355.description: When the Holy Temple stood in Jerusalem, wine was poured on the altar daily, but on the festival of Sukkos there was an additional water libation after the morning service. The seven nights of Sukkos were spent celebrating the drawing of this water, which was collected daily at daybreak from a valley below the Temple. Water may lack all the sophistication of wine, but it is for this reason that our sages associate it with Torah, unity and joy.

4127356.title: Lekach
4127356.description: Distribution of honey cake on Hoshana Rabba for a sweet new year. (1980s)

4127357.title: Offerings of Joy
4127357.description: “…Your name is Simcha – joy, may you be joyful all year round.”

4127358.title: Waiting for an answer
4127358.description: Rabbi Shmuel Rodal has served as a Chabad emissary, educator, and rabbi of the Beth Shlomo Synagogue in Milan, Italy, for close to fifty years. In the mid-1960s he was a student in Yeshiva Tomchei Temimim in Kfar Chabad, Israel.

4127361.title: Making Room for Creation
4127361.description: In the Beginning G-d created the heavens and the earth. But in order to make room for a finite world, the Kabbalah teaches that G-d who is infinite, had to limit some of His own light.

4127362.title: Farewell Audience
4127362.description: Special audience for guests who came for the month of Tishrei.

4127363.title: Accelerating Redemption
4127363.description: “Every additional mikvah is accelerating the arrival of our righteous redeemer.”

4127364.title: Mystery Solved
4127364.description: Rabbi Yechiel Michel Stern is a prolific author and rabbi of the Ezrat Torah neighborhood in Jerusalem. In the early 1980s, he served on Israel’s ministry of religious services, supervising numerous mikvahs in Jerusalem and across Israel.

4127366.title: Investing in Talent
4127366.description: Chasidic teachings instruct us to serve G-d with every fiber of our being. That is why we are each created with unique talents and abilities. The key is to actually put them to use.

4127367.title: Nigun Hu Elokeinu
4127367.description: Chasidim sing the nigun Hu Elokeinu.

4127368.title: Prayers for Rain
4127368.description: “Surely their fast was accepted by G-d, and rain will fall.” (Collage)

4127369.title: A Grounding Experience
4127369.description: Michoel Muchnik is a foremost Jewish artist living in Brooklyn, New York. In the early 1970s, he was a student at the Rabbinical College of America, in Morristown, New Jersey, when he had an audience with the Rebbe.

4166719.title: Why Do Jews Celebrate Circumcisions?
4166719.description: We spend our whole lives trying to elevate ourselves above and beyond the mundaneness of day-to-day material wellbeing. In fact, it’s such an important part of being a Jew, that we demonstrate our commitment to it in the first days of our life.

4166720.title: Nigun Hachanah
4166720.description: At a farbregnen marking the Rebbe Rashab’s birthday, the Rebbe instructs the chasidim to sing the Hachana Nigun, which is attributed to the Rebbe Rashab.

4166721.title: Worthy Endeavor
4166721.description: ”Arranging a Bris or Bar Mitzvah for someone who has not yet had one is a very worthy endeavor, and it deserves a lot of time and energy. We are promised, “Toil and you will be succeed.”

4166722.title: The Right Balance
4166722.description: Rabbi Chaim Moshe Bergstein serves as the director of Chabad of Farmington Hills, Michigan. As a student in Yeshiva in Israel, he internalized the lessons of his rabbis in Yeshiva about refraining from materialism and physical desires. But he couldn’t reconcile this idea with living a happy life. With this seeming contradiction in mind, he resolved to write to the Rebbe. (1969)

4171602.title: Creating a Perfect Past
4171602.description: The Torah is replete with the stories of our forefathers and foremothers. Highlighting their righteous and saintly behavior, it’s supposed to inspire us to emulate their ways. But are such lofty heights really achievable for any of us? And what if we’ve already messed up in the past?

4171603.title: Birthday of the Rebbe Rashab
4171603.description: The Rebbe distributes a Chasidic discourse in honor of the 127th birthday of Rabbi Sholom Dovber, the Rebbe Rashab.

4171604.title: A New Start
4171604.description: Now that you have returned to the Jewish fold, forget about the mistakes of the past. May you live many long, good, Jewish years.

4171605.title: All in the Right Time
4171605.description: Rabbi Menachem Mendel Gluckowsky serves as rabbi of the Chabad community in Rechovot, Israel. He was part of a special delegation of emissaries sent by the Rebbe to Israel, where he married and raised a family. When his newborn son had jaundice, he feared that he would not be able to have the Bris on time. He asked for a blessing from the Rebbe, but only later discovered the care and attention the Rebbe had given him. (1989)

4175164.title: If You Really Cared
4175164.description: In a culture of “live and let live” you might convince yourself that another person’s religious commitments are none of your business. But ask yourself what you’d do if you truly cared about your fellow’s welfare. And why should someone’s spiritual needs be any less important than their physical needs.

4175165.title: Evening Prayers
4175165.description: The Rebbe leads the Evening Prayers in his home. This day marks the Rebbe’s recovery from a heart attack in the winter of 5738 – 1977.

4175166.title: Costa Rica
4175166.description: Give this to charity for success in the work of you and your family in Costa Rica. Have good news and go from strength to strength - and don’t be satisfied with what you’ve done in the past.

4188710.title: Never Too Many Blessings
4188710.description: The very first command of the Torah is: “Be fruitful and multiply.” Rashi explains: You might think that having one child is already being “fruitful,” so Torah adds “and multiply.” And to remove all doubt, the verse continues, “fill the earth and conquer it.”

4188711.title: Two Dollars
4188711.description: Following the Afternoon Prayers, the Rebbe distributes two dollars to all those present, to be given to charity.

4188712.title: A Wish Come True
4188712.description: A video montage of individuals requesting and receiving blessings from the Rebbe for children. (Collage)

4188713.title: Ask the Rabbi
4188713.description: Rabbi Moshe Havlin serves as the Ashkenazi Chief Rabbi of Kiryat Gat in Israel, where he lives with his family. After his wife gave birth to two sons and a daughter, she suffered a number of miscarriages. When doctors recommended an operation, they decided to ask the Rebbe for advice and blessing. (1981)

4197982.title: A Vision of Peace
4197982.description: On the 10th of Kislev, the second Rebbe of Chabad, Rabbi DovBer was liberated from prison. He was freed just nine days before Chasidim would celebrate the release of his father, Rabbi Schneur Zalman. Both the Alter Rebbe and the Mitteler Rebbe connected their release from prison to the verse in Psalms, “my soul was redeemed in peace,” a verse that will be fully realized with the ultimate arrival of Moshiach. The lesson for us: A Jew should always be permeated with the idea that every person can bring redemption to the world.

4197983.title: Nigun Podoh V’sholom
4197983.description: Chasidim sing the nigun Podoh V’sholom, at a farbregnenmarking the yartzeit and liberation of the Mitteler Rebbe.

4197984.title: A Reason to Dance
4197984.description: May we very soon prepare for the marriage of the Jewish people with G-d. Midrash Rabbah says that until Moshiach, our relationship is like an engagement, and in the future, it will be a complete marriage.

4197985.title: In the Moment
4197985.description: Dovber Klein lives in Manchester, England, where he teaches in a boy’s school. As a student who was reconnecting to his Jewish roots he asked the Rebbe a wide range of questions, ranging from black magic to how much one should sleep at night. (1970s)

4199229.title: A Celebration for All
4199229.description: The Alter Rebbe was arrested due to a heavenly decree against his dissemination of the Torah’s secrets in an intellectual manner. The Alter Rebbe spread these teachings in a manner that allowed it to be understood just like the revealed parts of the Torah, such as Talmud. But it was the self-sacrifice of Jews, that caused the Heavenly decree to be torn apart. This is the lesson of the 19th of Kislev: We need to know that the Jewish people aren’t divided into factions. This is no more than an illusion of the evil-inclination who fears unity among Jews.

4199230.title: Nigun Four Stanzas
4199230.description: At a farbrengen marking the liberation of the Alter Rebbe, chasidim sing the nigun of Four Stanzas composed by the Alter Rebbe.

4199231.title: You Included
4199231.description: It’s the 19th of Kislev today. The Alter Rebbe promised the chasidim victory, and you’re included in that. You’re included in the victory of the chasidim.

4199232.title: A Time for Everything
4199232.description: Rabbi Zalman Gopin is a mentor at the yeshiva in Kfar Chabad, Israel. As a student, he once asked the Rebbe about how to best deal with the mood swings a person experiences. He would have expected the Rebbe to say that sadness is a bad thing, unequivocally. To his surprise, the Rebbe’s answer was much more unpredictable. (1960s)

4205395.title: You Can Be a “Hillel” Menorah
4205395.description: There are two approaches to Judaism, increasing the good or decreasing the bad. On Chanukah, and particularly on the fifth night of Chanukah, we emphasize the former by adding an extra light on each new day.

4205396.title: Chanukah Rally
4205396.description: A Chanukah Rally on the first day of Chanukah, held especially for children.

4205397.title: A Warm Chanukah
4205397.description: Happy Chanukah to you. Chanukah means lighting all the streets around your house. It is summertime in Australia, may it be a summery Chanukah over there. (Collage)

4205398.title: Who Is a Chasid?
4205398.description: Professor David Weiss was issued a special passport by the Soviet Union that allowed him to reach Jews that others couldn’t. At one point, the Rebbe asked him to come for a meeting to discuss the state of Jewish affairs in the USSR. in this interview, he recalls some of the points that were addressed at that meeting. (1965)

4210602.title: Chanukah and Chasidism
4210602.description: Chasidism is often challenged based on the fact that it’s a relatively new path in the service of the Almighty. But the laws of Chanukah actually provide an important answer for this question. The Torah and Mitzvos are our best weapon against the darkness of the world around us. As we get closer to the end of this exile and the darkness increases, it’s also necessary to add more light as a counterbalance. Jewish observance has minimums set by Jewish Law. Then there’s going beyond these minimums, to “beautify” it, which can be done in various ways. The lesson of the Chanukah lights for the year ahead is to strive to be the best Jews we can possibly be.

4210603.title: Chanukah Live
4210603.description: The 1991 "Chanukah Live" international satellite hookup that united Chanukah celebrations held across the globe in New York, Paris, Moscow, Melbourne, Hong Kong and Jerusalem.

4210604.title: A Victory for Chasidim
4210604.description: We are approaching the 19th of Kislev, may the Chasidim be victorious. May God bless you to resemble the medieval sage Ralbag. He wrote widely on philosophy, but his rulings in Jewish law are very good.

4210605.title: Living in the Present
4210605.description: Rabbi Avraham Glick was a shliach in Worcester, Massachusetts when he was asked to join the Chabad Representatives in Melbourne, Australia. The Rebbe approved of his move but advised him not to move right away but to wait a while. Feeling like he was in limbo, he wasn’t sure about how to proceed with his Chabad activities. But upon mentioning his feelings to the Rebbe, he was given an entirely new perspective. (1970)

4231278.title: It’s in Our Hands
4231278.description: On the Tenth of Teves in the year 425 BCE, Nebuchadnezzar, king of Babylon, laid siege around the holy city of Jerusalem. The siege lasted over two years, eventually culminating in the breach of the city’s walls and the destruction of the Holy Temple with all the calamities that followed. But in fact, this wasn’t the first time the holy city was besieged. Years earlier, Sennacherib, king of Assyria, led a massive army against the Jews and intended to penetrate Jerusalem’s walls. But that time, it ended very differently.

4231279.title: Mincha: Tenth of Teves
4231279.description: The Rebbe joins the Chasidim for the afternoon services on the Tenth of Teves fast and is called upon to read the Haftarah.

4231280.title: Blessing and Success
4231280.description: The Tzemach Tzedek explains that Joseph’s success was above the natural order. Success transcends order, whereas blessing serves to “pull or draw” something from one place to another, from a concealed state to a revealed one, showing that it is rooted within nature.

4231281.title: Success in All You Need
4231281.description: Daniel Finkelman is a producer and filmmaker living in Brooklyn, New York. In the late 1980s he was a young child growing up in Jerusalem when he contracted a severe eye condition that made it very difficult for him to see. When his family moved to the United States, a family friend urged his father to seek the Rebbe’s blessing - a blessing that has since been fulfilled in more than one way.

4237496.title: Take Us Out!
4237496.description: The Torah teaches us that Jacob’s best years were while living in Egypt during the final part of his life. Nevertheless, Jacob insisted on being taken to be interred near his parents and grandparents in the city of Hebron.

4237497.title: Nigun Ech Ti Zimlak
4237497.description: The Rebbe asks the Russian Chasidim to sing a Russian Nigun in honor of the Alter Rebbe’s liberation from Czarist prison. But it needs to be a Nigun with which everyone else can join in.

4237498.title: A Russian Connection
4237498.description: We need to find a solution for printing the Tanya in Russia. If you go on your own, the communists will probably interfere and get in your way. It would be better if in each location, you found someone connected to the authorities, to the officials there.

4237499.title: Becoming a Shochet in the USSR
4237499.description: Rabbi Yitzchak Kogan serves as rabbi of the Bronnaya Synagogue in Moscow. He is a former Refusenik and leading figure in the Soviet Jewish underground. Under the intrusively watchful eye of the Soviet authorities, it was most difficult to obtain Kosher meat. Without any alternative, he decided to become a qualified Kosher slaughterer himself. But it was the Rebbe’s encouragement and blessings from afar that kept his spirit alive. (1980s)
path: Becoming a Shochet in the USSR

4248646.title: Why Did the Levites Care?
4248646.description: While the Egyptians enslaved and persecuted the Jews, the Tribe of Levi was given much more freedom than the rest. They were actually allowed to study Torah and engage in holy pursuits. Moses and Aaron who were Levites as well, could have simply ignored the plight of their Jewish brethren and not been any the worse off. But in the end, it was specifically their concern that helped bring the Jews to redemption.

4248647.title: Dollars: 24 Teves
4248647.description: In honor of the Yahrzeit of the first Rebbe of Chabad, Rabbi Schneur Zalman of Liadi, the Rebbe distributes Dollars after the evening prayers.

4248648.title: Getting Some Sleep
4248648.description: During a Farbrengen marking the 19th of Kislev, Chief Rabbi of Philadelphia, Rabbi Ephraim Yolles, urges the Rebbe to get some more sleep.

4248649.title: Only the Rebbe Knew Her Secret...
4248649.description: Rabbi Yitzchak Wineberg has served as director of Chabad of British Columbia for over four decades. He remembers a particularly interesting story that took place when someone asked him to reach out to the Rebbe for a blessing for his non-Jewish wife. Or so he thought. (1970s)
path: Only the Rebbe Knew Her Secret...

4249617.title: Brick and Mortar
4249617.description: Torah relates that the Egyptian exile involved hard labor of “chomer u’leveinim – mortar and brick.” Of the current exile, however, Torah explains that the refinement of “chomer – mortar” is acquired through “kal vachomer – in-depth Torah study,” and the refinement of “leveina– brick,” through “libun hilchisa – clarification of Jewish law."

4249618.title: Purim Farbrengen
4249618.description: During a Farbrengen celebrating Purim in 1980, the Rebbe leads Chasidim in some lively and spirited Nigunim.

4249619.title: Going Kosher
4249619.description: Make sure you have rabbinical supervision and may G-d Almighty bless you to go from strength to strength, with good supervision. The main thing is to have real livelihood, and to use it for good purposes, also in your private life.

4249620.title: With a Whole Heart
4249620.description: Gila Lilian works in recruitment consultancy in Johannesburg, South Africa, where she lives with her husband and family. She was six months pregnant when the doctor delivered some frightening news about the baby. But as it turned out, it was the doctors who were shocked in the end. (1983)

4259583.title: Restoring the World
4259583.description: Just days before his passing on the tenth of Shevat in 1950, Rabbi Yosef Yitzchak Schneerson, the Rebbe’s father-in-law and predecessor, published a discourse titled “Basi L’gani”. The discourse expounds on many ideas from the Torah that highlight the importance of making this world a dwelling place for the Divine Presence of the Almighty.

4259584.title: Yud Shevat Vintage Footage
4259584.description: Vintage footage from a Farbrengen in 1967 making the Yahrzeit of the Rebbe’s father-in-law and predecessor, Rabbi Yosef Yitzchak Schneerson.

4259585.title: A Growing Influence
4259585.description: Mr. Sami Rohr visits the Rebbe to offer thanks for encouraging him to teach a Torah class to others in his community.

4259586.title: A Real Connection
4259586.description: Rabbi Nosson Gurary is the founder of the Chabad Student Center at the State University of New York, Buffalo. In the 1960s, as a yeshiva student in Brooklyn, New York, he began suffering from chest pain. Upon turning to the Rebbe for advice, he was sent to a doctor who would calm him of his concerns. Years later, the Rebbe still remembered about the incident.

4266752.title: A Branch of G-d’s Planting
4266752.description: The Fifteenth of Shevat marks the New Year for Trees, and the Rebbe encouraged men, women and children to celebrate the day with a Farbrengen, a joyful gathering where people inspire each other in the service of G-d.

4266753.title: Farbrengen
4266753.description: Color footage of a Farbrengen celebrating the New Year for Trees on the Fifteenth of Shevat.

4266754.title: Bearing Fruit
4266754.description: The walnut is covered by a shell, and its fruit, its seed, can produce many more trees. So too, the Jewish people; outwardly they are like all other nations, but their inner purpose, their inner soul, is to produce spiritual fruit which yields even more fruit. (Collage)

4266755.title: Two Kinds of Trees
4266755.description: Rabbi Zev Litenatsky was an accomplished educator from Los Angeles, California. He grew up in Montreal, Canada in the 1940s and 50s, when, before his Bar Mitzvah, he accompanied his father for a private audience with the Rebbe. He recalls the Rebbe asking him a peculiar question. And teaching him a lesson that has remained with him since.

4274101.title: The Right Lifestyle Choice
4274101.description: The Torah portion of Beshalach contains both the song of Moses, as well as the song of Miriam. The chosen Haftarah, however, which discusses the Song of Deborah, is chosen specifically in connection to the Song of Miriam.

4274102.title: Rebbetzin’s Yahrzeit
4274102.description: The Rebbe leads the Evening Services on the fourth Yahrzeit of his wife, Rebbetzin Chaya Mushka Schneerson.

4274103.title: In Honor of
4274103.description: A collage of videos related to the Rebbe’s wife, Rebbetzin Chaya Mushka Schneerson. (Collage)

4274104.title: A Blessing and a Contribution
4274104.description: Mrs. Esther Sternberg is the director of the Shabbos Candle Campaign, a division of the Lubavitch Women's Organization. She was involved in the medical care of the Rebbe’s wife, Rebbetzin Chaya Mushka, until the Rebbetzin’s passing in 1988. While the Rebbe was still sitting Shiva, the Shabbos Candle Campaign announced a new fund in honor of Rebbetzin Chaya Mushka. They didn’t inform the Rebbe of the new campaign, but once the Shiva was over, the Rebbe called her and her father to his home on President Street.

4278573.title: A Witness of G-d
4278573.description: The Torah prohibits speaking falsehood and bearing false witness in court. The codifiers list this as just one of Judaism’s 365 negative commandments. Yet Maimonides singles out the offense as one of the most disgraceful in Torah.

4278574.title: Nigun Simcha
4278574.description: During a lively Purim Farbrengen, Chassidim sing a joyous Niggun from the opening verse of the Megillah.

4278575.title: Having a Good Eye
4278575.description: Looking with a good eye on the entire Jewish people will also affect your physical eyes. When you look at your fellow Jew without judgment, with a “good eye,” it strengthens the health of your physical eyes as well.

4278576.title: Postponed Indefinitely
4278576.description: Rabbi Dovid Golowinski is the director of the Kosher Organics supervision agency. He grew up in Brooklyn New York, and in the summer of 1968 was a student at Lubavitcher Yeshiva in Montreal, Canada. When he went to visit his brother in camp, his eye suddenly began to hurt - badly. Upon examination, specialists insisted that he have an operation. But the Rebbe didn’t agree.

4285610.title: The Inner Light
4285610.description: When Haman drew lots to choose a month to annihilate the Jews, he was thrilled when it fell on the month of Adar, since 7 Adar is the day of Moses’ passing. Little did Haman know that it was also the day of Moses’ birth, and a source of strength for the Jewish people – as a nation, and as individuals.

4285611.title: 7 Adar
4285611.description: The Rebbe addresses the Chasidim on the birthday and Yahrzeit of Moses, the first leader of the Jewish people.

4285612.title: A Cause for Celebration
4285612.description: Some melancholy people take issue with celebrating during the first month of Adar. Why argue with those joyless people? The Rema rules, “A cheerful person always celebrates.” If there was room for doubt, “always celebrate.”

4285613.title: A Personal Interest
4285613.description: Mrs. Chaya Hecht served as an early education teacher in Brooklyn, New York, for over five decades. In the early 1950s, shortly after he had assumed leadership of the Chabad movement, she had an audience with the Rebbe. The Rebbe asked her if she was praying every day. When she answered that she didn’t really have the time to pray, the Rebbe suggested a new approach. And she’s adopted it as a part of her daily life.

4293365.title: Generation Gap
4293365.description: The youth rebellion of the 60s saw an explosion of counterculture movements fighting the status quo across the Western world. As many wrote off the radicalism of their children, the Rebbe embraced their passion, arguing that it all stemmed from a thirst for good.

4293366.title: Children’s Rally
4293366.description: A rally celebrating Purim Katan. On the Hebrew calendar, a leap year means adding a second month of Adar. Purim is celebrated on the second month, and Purim Katan - the mini Purim, is marked during the first month of Adar.

4293367.title: Small, Yet Big
4293367.description: Your father named himself “Klein–small,” and he doesn’t want to change it. May he merit the fulfillment of “Arise Jacob, for he is small.” As for yourself, may you have blessing and success. May you immediately become great.

4293368.title: Self Help
4293368.description: Rabbi Avraham Krishevsky lived in Betar Illit, Israel, where he was involved in the production of Tefillin. In this interview, he remembers a friend that he had in Crown Heights who spiraled into a life of drugs and other bad behavior. Unable to help him on his own, he succeeded in convincing his friend to write to the Rebbe. But the fellow had one condition: it couldn’t go through the Rebbe’s office; his letter could only be read by the Rebbe himself. (1980s)

4298806.title: On Keeping Clean
4298806.description: As committed Jews in an imperfect world, we’re constantly trying to balance our mundane responsibilities with our spiritual aspirations. We’re even encouraged to engage with the world to transform it into a G-dly place.

4298807.title: Nigun Simcha
4298807.description: Chasidim sing a lively Chasidic Nigun during a spirited Farbrengen celebrating Purim.

4298808.title: Supporter of the Arts
4298808.description: You once drew a painting of me; may G-d help you make more pictures of healthy and happy things. Draw a painting depicting the arrival of Moshiach. Don’t fear that it will be a big picture; you are a Jew, and a Jew can accomplish anything. (Collage)

4298809.title: "The Rebbe Told Me to Be Like a Spider"
4298809.description: Yossi Rosenstein is an artist living in Bnei Brak, Israel. In the late 1970s he travelled to New York for an exhibition of his work. It was a most interesting sequence of events that led him to arrange a meeting with the Rebbe. The Rebbe discussed the importance of his art, but encouraged him to teach the skill to others. He had no idea where to begin, but to his great surprise, someone approached him.
path: "The Rebbe Told Me to Be Like a Spider"

4308753.title: Buying Atonement
4308753.description: In the Book of Exodus, the Jewish people are instructed to contribute a half-shekel coin towards the building of the tabernacle as “atonement for their souls,” and the commentaries explain that it atoned for the grievous sin of the golden calf.

4308754.title: Dollars
4308754.description: The Rebbe hands out dollar bills for charity to mark the beginning of the second month of Adar.

4308755.title: Majority Opinion
4308755.description: What to do if you get conflicting medical advice?

4308756.title: A Medical Recommendation
4308756.description: Rabbi Zevulun Charlop is a prominent American rabbi and Dean Emeritus of the Rabbi Isaac Elchanan Theological Seminary, where he served for over thirty-five years. He remembers when his mother suddenly became ill and lost her sight. They quickly discovered that she was suffering from a stroke, and after stabilizing her, the doctor recommended a risky procedure. But first, they had to ask the Rebbe. (1950s)

4316001.title: Foiling the Plot
4316001.description: At the height of danger, with Haman’s decree of annihilation hanging over the heads of the Jewish people, their spiritual leader, Mordechai, sought some all-important counsel. He did not turn to the thought leaders or political pundits of the time; he went to some innocent Jewish children. When he heard their certainty that G-d would save them, he knew all would be well.

4316002.title: Visit from Gur
4316002.description: A video with footage from a visit by Rabbi Yaakov Alter, son of the Rebbe of Gur. The Rebbe and Rabbi Alter spent over an hour in a private meeting.

4316003.title: A Time for Joy
4316003.description: This is for the wedding in an auspicious time. It’s in the month of Adar, so you must be extra joyous. May your wellsprings spread to the outside; with increased joy. (Collage)

4316004.title: The Power of Thought
4316004.description: Mrs. Chana Popack and her husband served as Chabad emissaries in Philadelphia for three decades. She was born in Soviet Russia during Stalinist times, and her father was at a loss about where to send her to school. He couldn’t communicate directly with the Rebbe, for fear of being intercepted by the Soviet authorities. But through various maneuvers, he managed to get advice from the Rebbe, and somehow, the Rebbe’s unlikely idea worked. (1930s)

4323941.title: Purim with the Rebbe: A Unique Presentation
4323941.description: This special presentation highlights scenes of Purim farbrengens with the Rebbe throughout the years.
path: Purim with the Rebbe: A Unique Presentation

4331853.title: A Direct Connection
4331853.description: G-d’s presence didn’t rest in the Tabernacle until they offered atonement for the Golden Calf. Now, the Golden Calf didn’t deny G-d’s existence; it merely rejected the idea that a person could relate to G-d directly.

4331854.title: Post Purim Audience
4331854.description: A special audience for guests who had come to spend the holiday of Purim with the Rebbe.

4331855.title: A Movement’s Success
4331855.description: Thank you for your token of appreciation – but it’s for the movement, not for me. I’m very happy that your wife is also here. Say L’chaim and may G-d Almighty bless you to go from strength to strength.

4331856.title: A Good Role Model
4331856.description: In the early 1970s, Diane Abrams practiced law in New York and taught the nation’s first “Women and the Law” course at NYU. Her husband, Robert Abrams served as New York State Attorney General. The Rebbe, whom she met a number of times, kept bringing up the same thing – she had to write a book.

4336975.title: Living with Moshiach
4336975.description: While discussing the laws of the Red Heifer, Maimonides goes on to detail by whom each of them were ministered. Maimonides writes that the tenth and final Red Heifer will be ministered by Moshiach, “may he be revealed speedily – Amen, so may it be God’s will.”

4336976.title: Nigun Vesamachta
4336976.description: Chassidim sing a lively Chasidic nigun during a Purim farbrengen.

4336977.title: Time for Peace
4336977.description: There should be quiet in Colombia and everything should take place in a peaceful manner, as a good preparation for the peace after the coming of our righteous Moshiach. Have a happy and Kosher Passover.

4336978.title: Our Sages Teach Us
4336978.description: In 1956 Rabbi Eitan Green was a yeshiva student in Beis Medrash Govoha in Lakewood, New Jersey, when he had an audience with the Rebbe. He had a theory about the precise accuracy of some of the statements made by our sages. The Rebbe fundamentally disagreed, and referenced Einstein’s Theory of Relativity to make his point.

4346030.title: Let G-d Do the Rest
4346030.description: Generally, the requirements of the Variable Offering change according to one’s financial ability. Yet, within these laws, Maimonides brings a case of a poor person who pledges to bring the offerings of someone with more means than him. How will he afford it? Doesn’t Jewish law only obligate a person according to his means? Yet, this law emphasizes, that if he pledged to bring the offering, he will be given the means to fulfill his promise. When a Jew commits to doing something positive; if he resolves to disregard his own shortcomings and do a favor for another Jew, we are assured that G-d will help him fulfill his pledge – a lesson illustrated by a story of printing the Tzemach Tzeddek.

4346031.title: Distribution of Matzah
4346031.description: Unique footage from before Passover of the Rebbe distributing Matzah to representatives and dignitaries from around the world.

4346032.title: Matza Therapy
4346032.description: New York City Deputy Commissioner of Corrections Arthur Sinai visits the Rebbe: You used the Matza I sent you in a good place and a good time — Passover. Passover is connected with correction, and to be rid of all worries. May G-d Almighty bless you to be rid of all the worries that you may have had until now.

4346033.title: “Don’t Worry, He’s Coming”
4346033.description: Mr. Freddy Hager lived in London, England. One year, he made an unexpected stop at 770 on his way to the airport to return to England. But it soon became clear that his visit was not entirely unexpected after all. (1980s)

4351327.title: A New Day
4351327.description: Before birth, your soul may have basked in the glory of G-d and the Torah, but only in this world can you utilize your individuality to master Torah with your own abilities. In truth, we must always be mindful of this, and approach each day as a new birth. But on a person’s birthday, this lesson is ever more potent.

4351328.title: Burning the Chametz
4351328.description: The Rebbe burns the Chametz on the eve of the Passover holiday.

4351329.title: For Your Birthday
4351329.description: A collage of well-wishers greeting the Rebbe upon his birthday. (Collage)

4351330.title: Judaism on the Go
4351330.description: Moshe Kagan is a consultant living in Jerusalem, Israel. In the early 1960s, he arrived from England to attend yeshiva in 770. He was one of the few Yeshiva students with a driver’s license, and it worked in his favor. He was one of a group of students who got together to launch a new project – a mobile mitzvah vehicle.

4351373.title: The Pathologies of Exile
4351373.description: The Israelites were exiled in Egypt and forced to engage in slave labor, yet, when their redemption finally came, there were some who didn’t want to leave exile! Life became easy as soon as the slave-labor ceased, so they began complaining, “Why do we need to search for Torah and Judaism in the desert, and follow a wild individual like Moses? We have a competent king, culture and wisdom – let’s remain. But G-d sent a warning through Moses, that Pharaoh will “banish them from his land.” A Jew isn’t given a choice in the matter.

4351374.title: Children’s Passover Rally
4351374.description: The Rebbe participates in a children’s rally celebrating Passover.

4351375.title: Priestly Blessings
4351375.description: People with the family name “Kaplan” are usually Kohens. This Passover, bless all Jews with the priestly blessing, and may we see the fulfillment of “And G-d will bless them.”

4351376.title: Private Admission
4351376.description: Rabbi Hershel Feigelstock served as principal of the Lubavitch Yeshiva in Montreal for some forty years. In the 1940s, as a Yeshiva student at 770, he spent the holiday of Passover in New York. In a fascinating interview, he recalls the Rebbe inviting him to the private Passover meal of his father-in-law and predecessor, Rabbi Yosef Yitzchak Schneerson.

4358957.title: 49 Pages for 49 Days--Is It Just a Coincidence?
4358957.description:
On each day of the 49 days between Passover and Shavuos, it is customary to study a page of the Talmudic tractate Sotah, which consists of 49 pages. But the origins of this custom are immediately called into question: The Talmud existed well before the age of printing, and no two
copies had the same format; the pages are always different. Additionally, the first prints of Talmud didn’t have an identical typeface either. Later, one format became common in which Tractate Sotah happens to have forty nine folios. Why then, do we associate Tractate Sotah with the 49 days between Passover and Shavuot?
path: 49 Pages for 49 Days--Is It Just a Coincidence?

4358958.title: Cup of Blessing
4358958.description: The Rebbe distributes wine from the “Cup of Blessing” immediately after the holiday of Passover.

4358959.title: A Miracle Baby
4358959.description: You have no need for explanations from your daughter’s doctors. May you have a kosher and happy Passover, and channel the joy of your daughter’s health to the entire year.

4358960.title: A Natural Miracle
4358960.description: Rabbi Zvi Hartman is an esteemed Chassidic mentor in Beit Shemesh, Israel. In the 1960s, he served as Principal of Bet Sefer Lemlacha for vocational training in Kfar Chabad, Israel. After being married for some five years without being able to have children, he and his wife decided to ask the Rebbe for a blessing. They carried out the Rebbe’s instructions in New York but seemed to hit a wall. But everything would change after they met a doctor that the Rebbe referred them to in Tel Aviv.

4358993.title: Why the Rebbetzin Pawned Her Pearls
4358993.description: Rabbi Shmuel of Lubavitch would travel extensively to advocate for his fellow Jews. He would often return to a surprise.
path: Why the Rebbetzin Pawned Her Pearls

4358994.title: Nigun "Lechatchilah Ariber”
4358994.description: Chasidim sing “Lechatchilah Ariber” a Nigun attributed to Rabbi Shmuel of Lubavitch, known as the Rebbe Maharash.

4358995.title: Patting on the Back
4358995.description: You lavish so much praise on the volunteers for the charity fund. Add that you demand of them that they do even more – otherwise, they’ll be satisfied with past accomplishments… Good tidings.

4358996.title: Believing in Youth
4358996.description: Shimshon Stock headed the Chevra Simchas Shabbos V’Yom Tov charity fund for thirty years. In the 1940s, he was a rambunctious teenager growing up in the Crown Heights section of Brooklyn. One day, on the way to a ball game with his friend, he met the Rebbe. They didn’t expect it, but they then got a Torah lesson from baseball. (Late 1940s and Early 1950s)

4358998.title: How to Be a "Jewish Lion"
4358998.description:
A talk in honor of the 32nd yahrzeit of the Rebbe’s brother, Reb Yisrael Aryeh Leib.
In Jewish law, if someone has both a Jewish and secular name, the Jewish name comes first in legal documents. Similarly, if parents wish to give their child a Hebrew name together with its Yiddish equivalent, the Hebrew name customarily comes first.

4358999.title: Kaddish
4358999.description: Footage from the afternoon prayers on the yartzeit of Rabbi Yisroel Aryeh Leib, the Rebbe’s brother.

4359000.title: A Play on Words
4359000.description: This special collage shows individuals coming by the Rebbe, and receiving a lesson about the meaning and power of their Jewish names. (Collage)

4359001.title: Three Conditions
4359001.description: Milek Kremer served as deputy chairman of the Regional Council of Kiryat Ono, Israel. In 1963, his work brought him to the United States. With one of his children interested in becoming religious, he decided to ask the Rebbe for help and advice. The Rebbe agreed to help them – on three conditions…

4387265.title: A Career in Torah
4387265.description: We see in human nature that when you decisively resolve that for a particular amount of time, you’re completely dedicated to a specific thing – whatever it may be, you can indeed succeed. The same should be true of Torah study.

4387266.title: Nigun “Hinei Mah Tov”
4387266.description: Song lyrics: “Behold how good and how pleasant it is when brothers dwell together.” (Psalm 133:1)

4387267.title: In the Merit of Rabbi Shimon Bar Yochai
4387267.description: We need G-d’s mercy so that the redemption actually arrives. Then, on the Second Passover, we can discuss whether we need to offer the Passover offering, and how exactly to go about doing so properly.
path: In the Merit of Rabbi Shimon Bar Yochai

4387268.title: A Doctor with Solutions
4387268.description: Rabbi Moshe Weiss serves as director of Chabad of Sherman Oaks, California. He was married in 1983 but struggled to have children. He visited the Rebbe a number of times and merited to receive numerous blessings, but they never seemed to materialize. It was only many years later that something finally changed. (1991)

4391283.title: Counting the Days
4391283.description: The days between Passover and Shavuos correspond to the Israelites’ journey from Egypt in the lead up to receiving the Torah at Sinai. The closer they came to their goal, the more their anticipation grew.

4391284.title: N’shei Chabad
4391284.description: The Rebbe addresses members of the N’shei Chabad women’s movement in the lead up to Shavuos.

4391285.title: Latest Releases
4391285.description: A book needs to be paid for. How many are here? May you have blessing and success, and much thanks for the books. Good tidings. (Collage)

4391286.title: More Than Stories
4391286.description: In the mid-1970s, Rabbi Gershon Burkis was a member of the Religious Council in the city of Lod, Israel. With a number of children in their schools reaching the age for reading books, he decided to do something about the dearth of quality Jewish educational reading. With blessings and direction from the Rebbe, the Machanayim collection was born.

4402069.title: The Illogical Jew
4402069.description: Some parts of Torah cannot be explained. This helps explain the insatiable desire to study more and more Torah.

4402070.title: Nigun - Ata V’chartanu
4402070.description: Chassidim sing “Ata V’chartanu,” a Nigun with words from the holiday liturgy.

4402071.title: A Vessel for Blessings
4402071.description: The main thing: Your daily conduct should follow Jewish law. That will bring G-d’s blessing. The verse says, “If you follow My Laws,” you will receive all the blessings mentioned there. There is always room to grow, whether in scrupulously fulfilling the commandments, or in Torah study. (Collage)

4402072.title: The Simple Answer
4402072.description: Yaakov Abrams is a business appraiser and author on business evaluation living in Los Angeles, California. In the early 1980s, in the midst of exploring his Jewish roots, he began to suffer tremendous pain related to a personal matter. He decided to write to the Rebbe about it and hoped for a response that could make everything clear and easy. But that’s not what he got, at least not right away… (1984)

4404477.title: A True Scholar
4404477.description: The Talmud quotes Rav Yosef who said about Shavuot: “If not for this day, how many Yosefs would wander the market?”

4404478.title: Shavuos Havdalah
4404478.description: Footage of the Havdalah ceremony following the festival of Shavuos.

4404479.title: Use it for the Good
4404479.description: You are the head of the Chassidic Burial Society of Jerusalem. The appropriate wish for a Burial Society is that they should be out of work… “May G-d wipe away tears from every face.” Good tidings, and many good years.

4404480.title: A Good Incentive
4404480.description: Rabbi Chaim Cohen is a Jewish community activist living in Jerusalem. In 1984, he accompanied the Rebbe of Sadigura for an audience with the Rebbe. After informing the Rebbe about a new annual journal that he had begun publishing, the Rebbe encouraged him to do so even more often. Years later, he returned to show the Rebbe the fruits of his suggestion. (1984)

4413088.title: A Temple Made in Heaven
4413088.description: In Temple times, Jews with offerings in hand would make the yearly pilgrimage to Jerusalem for the festival of Shavuos. Those who did not bring an offering on the holiday itself, were able to do so in the six days that followed, known as the Days of Tashlumin. Today, even if we haven’t merited Moshiach before Shavuos, we hope and pray that we’ll still arrive in Jerusalem before the end of Tashlumin so we can still bring our offerings.

4413089.title: Post Shavuos Children’s Rally
4413089.description: A rally for children of Tzivos Hashem in the days following Shavuos.

4413090.title: Ladder to Sinai
4413090.description: Rabbi Simcha Ashlag presents the Rebbe with a volume of the Zohar Im Peirush HaSulam “The word ‘Sulam – Ladder’ is numerically equivalent to ‘Sinai.’ May it form ‘a ladder reaching the heavens for living souls.”

4413091.title: The Common Goal
4413091.description: Shmuel Abramson works in special education and lives in Monsey, New York. As a college student in the mid-1970s, he began to re-connect to his Jewish heritage. After getting engaged to his wife-to-be, he and his fiancé went to the Rebbe to seek a blessing before getting married. During their audience, he took the opportunity to ask two questions of the Rebbe. Their answers have guided him until this day. (1977)

4416527.title: The Beginning or the End?
4416527.description: As the school year ends and people take vacations, many want to leave all responsibility behind them. But when it comes to Torah study, there’s no such thing. Just like when we complete the communal reading of Torah, we immediately begin once again, the same is true of our own lives.

4416528.title: N’shei Chabad Convention
4416528.description: Footage of a summer gathering for the women of the N’shei Chabad organization.

4416529.title: Going Camping
4416529.description: Blessings for campers and staff of Camp Gan Israel in Montreal, Canada.

4416530.title: A Summer to Remember
4416530.description: Tzipporah Edelkopf was born in Kharkov, in the Soviet Republic of Ukraine. As a young girl, she managed to immigrate with her family to Israel. Her parents traveled to the Rebbe but couldn’t afford to bring her along. When the Rebbe heard why she was missing, he arranged for his emissary in Israel to get her a ticket to New York. But once she arrived, the Rebbe had a job for her. (1971)

4425427.title: Bring Moshiach Now!
4425427.description: Maimonides teaches us to imagine the world as hanging in the balance between good and evil. One action may be all that’s needed to tip the scales towards the good and bring salvation to the entire world.

4425428.title: Nigun - Ach Du
4425428.description: Chasidim sing a lively nigun during a farbrengen on the eve of Rosh Hashana.

4425429.title: Visiting the Sick
4425429.description: This is for success of the Bikur Cholim hospitality organization. May you have good news and may God send healing to all those who need it, speedily.

4425430.title: Keep Going
4425430.description: After her arrival in the Crown Heights section of Brooklyn over a decade earlier, Esther Mentz was appointed as a co-president of the N’shei Chabad Women’s Movement in the late 1960s.

4430124.title: A Living Legacy
4430124.description: On the Tenth of Shevat in 1982, the Rebbe delivered an address at a gathering marking thirtytwo years from the passing of this father-in-law and predecessor, Rabbi Yosef Yitzchak Schneersohn.

4430125.title: Visiting the Ohel
4430125.description: Unique footage from the Freidin collection showing the Rebbe visiting the resting place of his father-in-law and predecessor, Rabbi Yosef Yitzchak Schneerson.

4430126.title: Brotherly Love
4430126.description: May the Lelover Rebbe lead for many more years and grow from strength to strength in all matters of Torah and its precepts. You probably know that Lelov always excelled in showing love to fellow Jews and had a name for it. So you must be a living example; however good it was until now, may it increase many times more. Amidst joy and gladness of heart.

4430127.title: Twenty-Four Hours a Day
4430127.description: Rabbi Binyomin Klein served as a longtime secretary of the Rebbe. He joined the Rebbe’s staff in 1963.

4435118.title: One Love for All
4435118.description:
The Twelfth and Thirteenth of Tammuz marks the release of Rabbi Yosef Yitzchak Scheersohn, the sixth Lubavitcher Rebbe, from Soviet imprisonment.
His self-sacrifice on behalf of Jews of all stripes serves as a testament to the true nature of leadership.

4435119.title: Dollars for Charity
4435119.description: At the end of a farbrengen, the Rebbe recites the Grace After Meals and then hands out dollars to be given to charity.

4435120.title: Thank You from Russia
4435120.description: May you be blessed in all you need, as well as all the Jews still there, in Ladispoli, in Moscow, and everywhere else.

4435121.title: Unbroken Spirit
4435121.description: Reb Mottel Lifshitz, a key figure in the Soviet Jewish underground, served as Moscow’s only ritual slaughterer for almost three decades, and performed countless clandestine circumcisions.

4440347.title: The Good in Everything
4440347.description: The Seventeenth of Tammuz is a fast day commemorating the breach of the walls of Jerusalem before the destruction of the Second Temple. When it falls on Shabbos, the fast is postponed until Sunday, the 18th. More than a scheduling difference, this holds a deep lesson for every Jew.

4440348.title: Nigun - Avinu Malkeinu
4440348.description: The Rebbe leads the prayers in his house on the fast of the 17th of Tammuz. Chasidim sing the nigun, Avinu Malkeinu.

4440349.title: Measure for Measure
4440349.description: May the merit of working with the Almighty’s children help you with your own daughter to have good news. And may the merit of the Holy Land assist you to have good news and much success.

4440350.title: My Generals
4440350.description: David Mayer lives with his family in Los Angeles, California, where he was an executive in the toy industry. (Early 1980s)

4446781.title: Uncompromising Love
4446781.description: The Mishnah instructs us to “Be a student of Aaron,” love peace, pursue peace; love G-d’s creations...” Notably, the passage concludes, “and bring them close to Torah.”

4446782.title: Nigun “Ani Amarti”
4446782.description: Nigun composed for the Rebbe’s 81st birthday with words from Psalm 82.

4446783.title: Striving Higher
4446783.description: Good tidings for all of El Al, with much success. Your name Kurtzag means brief, but you should do everything at a steady pace, with abundance... The meaning of “El Al” is that one must always strive for higher.

4446784.title: Safe Skies
4446784.description: Rabbi Dr. Chaim Shine is a professor of law in Israel and a columnist for the Israel Hayom newspaper. In the late 1970s he joined his uncle, David Shine, then director of El Al in North America, for an audience with the Rebbe. Concerned with the flight security on El Al’s planes, Mr. Shine brought up the issue with the Rebbe. The Rebbe’s advice surprised him at first, but taking heed of the Rebbe’s words, he led the effort to implement them at El Al. (Late 1970s)

4451838.title: The Center of Judaism
4451838.description: The verse states: “They shall build me a Temple, and I will dwell within them.” Our sages teach us that “within them” refers to every Jewish heart. Each and every single one of us, and the entire Jewish people, all share the mission of bringing the light of Judaism out to the entire world.

4451839.title: Dollars
4451839.description: Distribution of dollars for charity in the days preceding Tisha B’av

4451840.title: Temple Life
4451840.description: Rashi states that G-d took the two Holy Temples from us as collateral for our sins. By Jewish law, collateral must be returned in one piece; nothing can be missing. May we go from “G-d’s presence filled the Tabernacle” to “G-d called Moses”, with everything that follows.

4451841.title: On the Battlefield
4451841.description: Ronnie Romberg and her husband, Dr. Henry Romberg, met at Case Western University in Cleveland, Ohio and were married in 1968. Having long dreamed of making Aliyah and moving to Israel, they had all their plans set. All until a Chabad friend of theirs convinced them to ask the Rebbe’s advice first. To make a long story short, they didn’t get the answer they were expecting.

4459453.title: Why, Oh Why, Must We Suffer?!
4459453.description: Concerning the future Redemption, the prophet declares, “I will offer thanks to You, G-d, for Your wrath,” for at that time, the good hidden in all mankind’s suffering will be made clear. But why must this be concealed from us until then?
path: Why, Oh Why, Must We Suffer?!

4459454.title: End of the Fast
4459454.description: Havdala following the fast of Tisha B’av

4459455.title: Moshiach, a Reality
4459455.description: You can tell the Zablitover Rov that it is not only a feeling that the “birth pangs” of Moshiach are over, it is reality. G-d Almighty bless you to be the bearer of good news.

4459456.title: Unnecessary Surgery
4459456.description: Eitan Ben-David is a businessman and philanthropist living in Jerusalem, Israel. In the 1970s, with his father suffering from a heart condition, they were unsure whether to operate or not. After writing to the Rebbe, they finally received a response: no surgery was necessary. His doctor wasn’t too confident about the Rebbe’s ability to know the details of the case, but couldn’t override the patient’s wishes.

4462439.title: Life Through the Lens of Kabbalah
4462439.description: The Rebbe’s father saw kabbalistic significance in every event in his life. Was this a humble approach?
path: Life Through the Lens of Kabbalah

4462440.title: Farbrengen – Av 15
4462440.description: Vintage footage taken of a farbrengen held in honor of 15 Av.
