4462441.title: For Soviet Jewry
4462441.description: The Jewish Congress must also have a charity box, put this in the charity box at the Congress, it couldn’t hurt. You can put the computers to use and perhaps calculate when Moshiach will arrive. As long as it doesn’t delay his coming…

4462442.title: A Personal Request
4462442.description: Israel Singer is a Jewish activist, academic and former secretary general of the World Jewish Congress. In the mid-1970s, he taught political science in New York and served on the staff of President Gerald Ford. When he visited the Rebbe in preparation for a trip to the Soviet Union, the Rebbe asked him for a personal favor. The feeling of privilege from carrying out the Rebbe’s wishes at that time, has remained the most special experience of his life to this day. (1974)

4469444.title: Building Security
4469444.description: In June of 1982, war broke out between Israel and terrorist factions in Lebanon. Dubbed Operation Peace for Galilee, it was hoped that it would end years of strife in the region. In an address just one week after the war began, the Rebbe urged Israel’s leaders not to repeat the mistakes of the past.

4469445.title: Scenes From a Farbrengen
4469445.description: Vintage footage taken from a farbrengen marking the passing of the Rebbe’s father, Rabbi Levi Yitzchak Schneerson.

4469446.title: Focus on the Future
4469446.description: There are crucial decisions to be made in the Land of Israel, associated with the “Integrity of the Land,” the “Integrity of the Jewish People,” and the “Integrity of the Torah.” Don’t be concerned if you need miracles; even miracles will occur.

4469447.title: Fighting for Israel
4469447.description: Gedalya Schreiber has served as director-general of Israel’s Religious Affairs Ministry and as director-general of its Chief Rabbinate. In 1980, he joined the entourage of the Sadigura Rebbe for an audience with the Rebbe.

4477456.title: “For My Children? Only the Best!”
4477456.description: How many times does every parent ask him or herself: “Am I giving my child the very best that’s out there?” Here, the Rebbe argues that “the best” is not just wishful thinking, it’s an obligation.

4477457.title: Afternoon Prayers Preceding Rally
4477457.description: Before a special children’s Rally during the month of Elul, the Rebbe joins for the Mincha prayer service.

4477458.title: In the Merit of Jewish Girls
4477458.description: The redemption will come in the merit of the righteous women of that generation, so It depends, to a large extent, on you. God has always helped you, you just need to “cash” in and raise righteous women in Israel. (Collage)
path: In the Merit of Jewish Girls

4477459.title: Higher Education
4477459.description: Rabbi Osher Ehrenreich has served as dean of Bais Yaakov High School for Girls in the Boro Park section of Brooklyn for over six decades. In 1968, he and a group of supporters had an audience with the Rebbe.

4481438.title: On the Doorposts of Your House
4481438.description: As part of his campaign, launched in 1974 to encourage Jews to affix mezuzahs in their homes, the Rebbe also urged checking them in order to ensure that they are indeed kosher.
path: On the Doorposts of Your House

4481439.title: Morning Prayers
4481439.description: The Rebbe partakes in the morning prayers at 770.

4481440.title: Just Checking
4481440.description: A special video collage on the importance of checking tefillin and mezuzahs to make sure that they are Kosher.

4481441.title: A Second Look
4481441.description: Born in the Soviet Union, Rabbi Mottel Chein is now a communal activist living in the Crown Heights section of Brooklyn. In the late 1950s, he was a student at the Tomchei Temimim yeshiva in Lod, Israel.

4487804.title: One Path, Two Ways
4487804.description: One of the earliest Chasidic texts, Tzavoas Harivash, is a manual of insights and guidance culled from the teachings of the Baal Shem Tov and his successor, Rabbi Dovber of Mezritch. Rabbi Shneur Zalman of Liadi, known as the Alter Rebbe, was their foremost student and the founder of Chabad, and is known for his seminal work, the Tanya.

4487805.title: Nigun Aimosay
4487805.description: Meaning of the song: “When will the Master come?” This question was asked of Moshiach by the Baal Shem Tov, founder of Chassidism, during a visit to his chamber On High. “When your Wellsprings (of Chassidism) will spread to the outside,” was Moshiach’s response.

4487806.title: Bastion of Truth
4487806.description: May the Yeshiva building be an edifice of truth, as befitting Tomchei Temimim. May you have much success.

4487807.title: The King in the Field
4487807.description: Yaakov Abrams is a business appraiser and author on business evaluation, living in Los Angeles, California. He was married to his wife Chana in the mid-1980s. (1986)

4497301.title: An Opportune Time
4497301.description: At the commencement of Elul, the month preceding Rosh Hashanah, we begin to reflect on the year that passed, and on improving our relationship with G-d. The Alter Rebbe, the founder of Chabad, compared the Almighty during the month of Elul to a king who goes out to the field to make himself accessible to all. But it’s our responsibility to take full advantage of this time - after all, soon the King will return to his chambers.

4497302.title: Selichos on Erev Rosh Hashanah
4497302.description: Scenes of the Selichos prayers at 770 on the eve of Rosh Hashanah in 1983.

4497303.title: A Worthwhile Discussion
4497303.description: May it be in an auspicious hour and may Chasidim have the upper hand. We have that guaranteed by the Alter Rebbe and the Baal Shem Tov. As in the Haggadah, may they be up all night in Bnei Brak, discussing the era of Moshiach.

4497304.title: Repentance and Healing
4497304.description: Rabbi Ephraim Rosenblum serves as principal of Yeshiva Boys School in Pittsburgh, Pennsylvania. In the 1950s, he was a student at the Central Lubavitch Yeshiva in Brooklyn, New York. The students would go out to different cities and disseminate the books of Chasidism and talk to people. Everything was going smoothly until they were involved in a scary accident. (1954)

4497317.title: What is the Purpose of Life on Earth?
4497317.description: But why does G-d need our efforts? Can He not accomplish His goals without us? A pre-Rosh Hashanah message.
path: What is the Purpose of Life on Earth?

4497318.title: Niggun Yemin Hashem
4497318.description: Chasidim sing a soul stirring nigun, Yemin Hashem, attributed to the third Rebbe of Chabad, the Tzemach Tzedek.

4497319.title: Connecting Generations
4497319.description: Give this to charity in London, and this is for great and increasing success. You probably know that we’re both connected to the Tzemach Tzedek. Being that we carry his name, it’s a sign of our connection. May we be connected with him at the time of the resurrection. (Collage)

4497320.title: Investing in the Future
4497320.description: Professor Shlomo Eckstein is the former president and director of Bar Ilan University in Tel Aviv, Israel. In the 1950s, he was a leader in the B’nei Akiva youth movement and was disappointed by his lack of results. After writing a letter to the Rebbe expressing his feelings, he received a response that changed his entire perspective.

4503398.title: Always Returning
4503398.description: In his work, Iggeres Hateshuvah, the Alter Rebbe explains that there are two levels of repentance. While the first brings about a change in the person’s conduct, it is the second, higher level, which revolutionizes his entire inner world.

4503399.title: Distribution of Lekach
4503399.description: Scenes from the Rebbe’s distribution of honey cake on the eve of Yom Kippur in 1990.

4503400.title: A Mother in Israel
4503400.description: Thank you for the picture of my mother, Rebbetzin Chana. May you have good tidings. (collage)

4503401.title: A Chandelier in Heaven
4503401.description: Rabbi Nochum Stilerman is an accomplished fundraiser for various Jewish charities and institutions. As a teenager in the late 1950s, he ran deliveries for his father’s grocery store in Brooklyn, New York. His customers included Rebbetzin Chana Schneerson, the Rebbes’ mother. The Rebbetzin enjoyed talking to him, and on one occasion, he decided to ask her a question. He didn’t know that she’d tell the Rebbe all about it.

4512035.title: Torah in Motion
4512035.description: During the Holiday of Sukkos, we take a palm branch, citron, and branches of myrtle and willow, and wave them together in every direction. In fact, it was the custom of our Rebbes that when waving the lulav, they would not only extended it forward and bring it back, but would move it out in each of the six directions, give it a shake, and then bring it back towards the chest.

4512036.title: Distribution of the Four Kinds
4512036.description: The Rebbe distributes the Four Kinds to dignitaries on the day before the holiday of Sukkos.

4512037.title: Diligent Study
4512037.description: This will be for a special blessing to be diligent in your studies. May you study Torah and fulfill the commandments. And this you can give as your first Mitzvah, to give this dollar to charity. (collage)

4512038.title: Let’s Make a Deal
4512038.description: Rabbi Mendel Lipskar is the Executive Director of Chabad of South Africa and serves as rabbi of the Shul at Hyde Park in Johannesburg. He grew up in Toronto, Canada, where his father was on the staff of Camp Gan Israel. To his surprise, when he went to visit the Rebbe with his father, the Rebbe made him an offer that he could not refuse. (1960)

4525542.title: A Greater Kind of Joy
4525542.description: The nights of the festival of Sukkos are marked by Simchas Beis Hashoeva, dancing and joyous celebration reminiscent of the festivities in Temple times. The final day of Sukkos, Hoshana Rabbah, is marked in a more solemn way, as it is the day on which the judgement that began on Rosh Hashanah is sealed. But that should not be a reason not to celebrate.

4525543.title: Hoshana Rabbah Prayers
4525543.description: A special video montage of the morning prayers on Hoshana Rabbah, including the Rebbe reciting Hallel and waving the Four Species.

4525544.title: Dance for Joy
4525544.description: The Rebbe advises someone to dance on Simchat Torah to help bring physical healing.

4525545.title: The Doctors Said I Was Going Blind
4525545.description: Yisroel Swimmer is a chief financial officer living in Lawrence, New York. In the 1980s, he was a child growing up in Johannesburg, South Africa. (1983)
path: The Doctors Said I Was Going Blind

4530451.title: The Year-Long Month
4530451.description: In Temple times, the seventh day of the month of Cheshvan meant that the festivals of the month of Tishrei were well and truly behind us. It was the date that the last of the pilgrims would return home from Jerusalem.

4530452.title: Kos Shel Brachah
4530452.description: Following the festival of Simchas Torah, the Rebbe distributes from the wine of Havdalah to the Chasidim gathered.

4530453.title: A Fresh Start
4530453.description: Regarding the annual study of Maimonides’ Mishneh Torah, when study of a part of Torah is completed, it must at once begin anew, as was just done on Simchas Torah. You probably don’t need a reminder, but you can remind your students. (Collage)

4530454.title: Unpack the Merchandise
4530454.description: Rabbi Shimon Bekerman serves on the board of the Chabad Youth Organization in Israel. In 1965 he traveled to New York for the month of Tishrei and had his first audience with the Rebbe.

4536259.title: The Very Last Jew
4536259.description: In Temple times, Jews from far and wide would make the annual pilgrimage to Jerusalem to celebrate the festival of Sukkos. The last of them would return home some two weeks after the festival on the seventh of Cheshvan, and the prayer for rain was delayed until then.

4536260.title: Farewell Audience for Tishrei Guests
4536260.description: Following a month packed with festivals and joy, the Rebbe holds a special farewell audience for the guests who came to spend Tishrei with him.

4536261.title: Jewish Unity
4536261.description: The meaning of the word ‘congress’ is when people gather together – to bring unity among Jews. No easy task, but it can be done. May it be in an auspicious hour.

4536262.title: It’s No Mistake
4536262.description: Rabbi Elchanan Jaacobovez is a veteran educator living in Nachlat Har Chabad, Israel. He was married in 1966. (Mid 1970s)

4547214.title: The Tests of Life
4547214.description: The Kabbalists teach that within every created thing lies a spark of G-dliness. The role of the Jew is to redeem those sparks through his service of G-d, and elevate the world in the process. A task which is not without its challenges.

4547215.title: Nigun Aimosai
4547215.description: During a Farbrengen marking the passing of the founder of Chabad, Rabbi Shneur Zalman of Liadi, Chasidim sing a Chabad classic, Aimosay.

4547216.title: Nothing too Difficult for G-d
4547216.description: May you lead your community for many long years, and speedily lead them to the Land of Israel; when they go with Moshiach, they’ll need their rabbi at their head. There is nothing too difficult for G-d, whether it’s Brazil or other countries.

4547217.title: Do Not be Afraid!
4547217.description: An excerpt from the Jewish Educational Media film, Switch. Shortly after his arrival from Israel in 1963, Rabbi Chaim Benyamini established the Machneh Israel yeshiva in Petropolis, Brazil, which he headed for over three decades.

4552026.title: Behind Every Great Jew Is a Great Mother
4552026.description: Sarah, the first Jewish mother, is a shining example of the great power that every woman has over her family and our entire nation. It was Sarah who insisted that Isaac, not Ishmael, continue Abraham’s progeny. It was she who raised Isaac in his formative years, instilling within him the fortitude to stand up to all tests, and to become the second Patriarch of the Jewish People.
path: Behind Every Great Jew Is a Great Mother

4552027.title: The Rebbe Rashab’s Birthday
4552027.description: On the birthday of the Rebbe Rashab, Rabbi Sholom DovBer of Lubavitch, the Rebbe distributes a special edition of the discourse “Heichaltzu.”

4552028.title: An Occasion for Joy
4552028.description: The twentieth of Cheshvan marks the birthday of the Rebbe Rashab, Rabbi Sholom DovBer of Lubavitch. It’s an auspicious day on the chasidic calendar and provides an opportunity to cultivate joy.

4552030.title: The Best Way to Help
4552030.description: Rabbi Shmarya Katzen was a beloved teacher for close to five decades. After becoming observant in the 1960s and spending several years in yeshivas, he began to think about his life ahead. The Rebbe encouraged him to take an aptitude test to discover how to best use his unique talents, and it was this that led him to his long career as an educator, with the Rebbe’s guidance and blessings.

4556857.title: Keep It Real
4556857.description:
Many observers remain stumped by the unparalleled success that Chabad continues to see in its
efforts in Jewish outreach. How is it, they wonder, that the movement can maintain such a rigid adherence to Jewish law and observance, while still welcoming Jews of every stripe, no matter their background or level of observance? In this fascinating talk, the Rebbe reconciles the apparent paradox and lays out his approach to Jewish outreach, for every time and every place.

4556858.title: Kinus Hashluchim (Mincha) 1987
4556858.description: During the International Conference of Shluchim, and on the day before the books of Chabad’s precious library were returned to 770, the Rebbe is greeted by an excited crowd as he enters the afternoon prayers.

4556859.title: Lighthouse to the Nations
4556859.description: May the city be true to its name, Tel Aviv. “Aviv – spring” is the beginning of growth for the entire year. The Chabad House in Tel–Aviv is the most important thing, as it is a lighthouse for all of its surroundings.

4556860.title: No Place Too Small
4556860.description:
Rabbi Yaakov Reitzes has served as rabbi of Yesod Hama’ala and the Upper Galilee in Israel for
close to forty years. In 1976 he was part of a delegation of students sent by the Rebbe to Israel, where he remained and married. After receiving an offer to move as the Chabad emissary to Yesod Hama’ala, a tiny settlement at the time, he and his wife asked the Rebbe if it was worth their time and effort. By now, they know it was and continues to be.

4566348.title: Keep Up the Good Work
4566348.description: On the occasion of his eightieth birthday, the Rebbe gives spirited advice to those approaching the age of retirement: Since “man was created to toil,” if G–d gives us another year in this world, it is proof positive that we still have something to accomplish.

4566349.title: Nigun “Rosh Chodesh Kislev”
4566349.description: Chasidim sing the “Rosh Chodesh Kislev Nigun” as the Rebbe distributes dollars to those who lead the Mitzvah campaigns on Chabad’s famous Mitzvah Tanks.

4566350.title: Healthy Living
4566350.description: May G–d bless you by healing all your patients. Then you can focus on practicing preventive medicine for healthy people. Instruct your patients about kosher diet and lifestyle, which will bring them G–d Almighty’s blessings.

4566351.title: As Old as You Feel
4566351.description: Dr. Louis Teichholz is a leading cardiologist. In 1977, he was a Head of Cardiology at Mount Sinai Hospital in New York. When, on the holiday of Shmini Atezers in 1977, the Rebbe suffered a massive heart attack, he was asked to join a team of doctors treating the Rebbe at 770. It was there that he merited to converse with the Rebbe about many fascinating topics.

4574469.title: A Whole New Light
4574469.description:
The Mitteler Rebbe’s imprisonment came about after the wellsprings of the Baal Shem Tov had
already swept the Jewish People, nourishing tens of thousands of souls. Despite all this, there descended a darkness so profound that it challenged even such a great light, and resulted in an imprisonment. But when denser darkness is conquered, the resultant light that shines forth out of the darkness is ever the brighter.

4574470.title: The 9th of Kislev
4574470.description: The Rebbe encourages the Chasidim to sing the song “Podoh B’sholom” in honor of the birthday and Yahrzeit of the Mitteler Rebbe, Rabbi Dovber of Lubavitch.

4574471.title: A Good Vision
4574471.description: You should be careful to hear kiddush and havdalah – it helps to keep the eyes healthy. May G-d help you see many good things with both eyes, and in an ever–increasing manner. You’re spreading the light of Torah, so you need healthy eyes. Why lose something that God Almighty has given you? You must hold onto it, and G-d Almighty will help you to be successful. (Collage)

4574472.title: Seeing is Believing
4574472.description: In the 1960s, Moshe Kagan was a student at 770, the Central Lubavitch yeshiva in Brooklyn, New York. It was during this time that his father was in a car accident which caused him to lose his eyesight. His father wanted to avoid bringing any unnecessary pain to his family, and suggested to the Rebbe that he might not participate in his own son’s wedding. The Rebbe did not agree, and gave him a very special blessing.

4582974.title: Where Are You?
4582974.description: The founder of Chabad Chasidism, Rabbi Schneur Zalman of Liadi, known as the Alter Rebbe, was arrested by the Czarist authorities in Russia. He was accused of treason, aiding the Czars enemies in the Ottoman Empire. In reality, he was simply urging his followers to send charity to the poor Jews of Israel. Spiritually speaking, there was another reason that heaven orchestrated the arrest: the Alter Rebbe was spreading the secrets of Chasidism too widely.

4582975.title: Nigun Podoh V’sholom
4582975.description: During a Farbrengen marking the Alter Rebbe’s liberation from Czarist prison on the 19th of Kislev, Chasidim sing a Nigun with words from Psalms that he was reciting at the time of his release.

4582976.title: No Simple Answer
4582976.description: You should decide your particular position after trying your hand at different things. Then you can decide if you should continue the same thing or try something else. In general terms, a Jew’s purpose in life is to study Torah regularly, and observe its commandments meticulously. (Collage)

4582977.title: Two Fateful Letters
4582977.description:
Rabbi Sholom Ber Schapiro is a veteran educator living in Brooklyn, New York. In the early
1980s he was a teacher in the Yeshiva of Brooklyn when he was approached by a student’s parent who had an offer for a business opportunity. After receiving the consent of his boss, he asked the Rebbe for a blessing which he received with a condition. A story about making sure every Jewish child has a letter in a Torah scroll.

4592174.title: Much to Accomplish Together
4592174.description: During Chanukah in 1985, a joint rally was held at 770 for groups of seniors and young children. Addressing the gathering, the Rebbe explained their shared lessons and the rally’s special connection to Chanukah.

4592175.title: Light the Menorah
4592175.description: The full Menorah, with all its lights, being kindled in 770 during a special children’s rally on the eighth night of Chanukah.

4592176.title: Menorahs for Moscow
4592176.description: May you distribute the Chanukah Menorahs to the Jews in Russia in an auspicious time with blessings and success.

4592177.title: A Chanukah Miracle
4592177.description:
In the early 1950s, Shmuel Langsam was a young child growing up in the Crown Heights section
of Brooklyn, New York. It was Chanukah time when his mother received some frightening news from the doctor. In 1952, this cancer wasn’t something that could be cured. In desperation, they pulled all the strings they could, for her to receive the Rebbe’s blessing. When they finally got to the Rebbe, he wasn’t worried at all, much to their relief.

4596790.title: Was the Chanukah Miracle Necessary?
4596790.description: We all know the story of Chanukah: With all the odds against them, the Jews were victorious over their enemies. However, when they returned to the Holy Temple, they found that all the oil for the Menorah was defiled. God made a miracle and the oil lasted for eight days until they could procure new oil that was pure.

4596791.title: Didan Notzach Anniversary (Mincha)
4596791.description: The 5th of Teves marks the day that Chabad won the court case surrounding the ownership of the Chabad library. On this day in 5749, during the year of mourning for his wife, Rebbetzin Chaya Mushkah, the Rebbe leads the afternoon services.

4596792.title: Chanukah Blessings
4596792.description: Like the Chanukah lights that shine outside, education, too, must illuminate the “outside.” May you be blessed with a speedy recovery and have no need of a cane, and be able to dance joyously on Chanukah. (Collage)

4596793.title: Living with the Times
4596793.description:
Rabbi Yisroel Rubin has served as the director of Chabad of the Capital District in Albany, New York, for over forty years.
In the summer of 1970, he was on the staff of Camp Gan Israel of Montreal, Canada. He wanted to do something to encourage the children to study Chitas, a daily portion from the Chumash, Psalms, and Tanya. His project ended up lasting longer than the short summer he had planned, and the Rebbe’s blessings and encouragement motivated him throughout.

4596805.title: The Root of the Problem
4596805.description: The Tenth of Teves commemorates the siege of Jerusalem, the beginning of a series of events that lead to the eventual destruction of the Holy Temple and the Jews’ captivity in Babylonia.

4596806.title: Mincha Prayers on the Tenth of Teves
4596806.description: The Rebbe is called to the Torah and recites the Haftorah during the afternoon prayers on the fast of the Tenth of Teves.
path: Mincha Prayers on the Tenth of Teves

4596807.title: The Right Kind of Clients
4596807.description: You were complaining that you don’t have enough clients; may you soon have many, but peaceful cases. You don’t necessarily need disputes for business, since people also need lawyers for peaceful matters.

4596808.title: Let’s Make a Deal
4596808.description: Rabbi Nachman Sudak was the director of Chabad’s operations in the United Kingdom for over five decades. At one particular point of financial strain, he turned to a supporter asking for help. The amount they had to come up with seemed way beyond their reach, but with faith, perseverance, and many blessings from the Rebbe, the story finally came to a happy end. (mid 1980s)

4612764.title: How Jacob Survived and Thrived in Egypt
4612764.description: As a young child, the Tzemach Tzedek once asked the Alter Rebbe how Jacob’s best years could have been in Egypt, a land of immorality.
path: How Jacob Survived and Thrived in Egypt

4612765.title: Maimonides’ Yahrtzeit
4612765.description: “On the day that a Tzaddik passes away all his life’s work is revealed – “and effects salvation throughout the world.” How much more so in regard to Maimonides, who taught the entire Torah to “young and old alike.”

4612766.title: Extra-Strength Mitzvah
4612766.description: “The Alter Rebbe extols the greatness of charity given to the Holy Land. All charity hastens the Redemption, but in Israel even more so.”

4612767.title: Home Remedy
4612767.description: In the late 1950s, Chana Chanowitz and her Husband, Chaim Chanowitz, were living on the Upper West Side of New York City. At one point, Chaim was plagued by terrible stomach ulcers. The doctors urged an urgent surgery, but when they asked the Rebbe, they received different advice.

4619614.title: Two Luminaries
4619614.description: There are many similarities between Maimonides and the Alter Rebbe, the Founder of Chabad Chasidism. They both issued decisions on Jewish law that guide all later generations.

4619615.title: Nigun of Four Stanzas
4619615.description: On the eve of 24 Teves, the Rebbe conducts a special farbrengen in honor of the 150th year since the passing of Rabbi Schneur Zalman of Liadi, the founder of Chabad Chasidism.

4619616.title: The Merit of Mishnah
4619616.description: “The Alter Rebbe writes that in the merit of the study of Mishnah we will be redeemed from exile. May you bear good tidings in your project to encourage Mishnah study in memory of those who perished in the Holocaust.”

4619617.title: Worth Waiting
4619617.description: Eitan Ben-David is a businessman and philanthropist living in Jerusalem, Israel. In the early ‘70s, his wife had become pregnant, but the doctors deemed the pregnancy unsafe due to a condition that she was suffering from, and advised them to go through with an abortion. Unsure about how to proceed within the parameters of Jewish law, they penned an urgent letter to the Rebbe.

4627178.title: The Inner Moses
4627178.description: The seventh of Adar marks the birth of Moses, which came in the wake of Pharaoh’s decree that all newborn Jewish boys be cast into the Nile. It was not only a decree against the Jews as a whole; it was a decree targeted specifically against Moses himself.

4627180.title: Just Visiting?
4627180.description: When you visit Peru, find the Chabad Shliach there and assist him in the way that only a visitor can. Sometimes a visitor can help more than someone who has been living in a community for many years.

4627181.title: Like a Father
4627181.description:
Rabbi Sholom Ber Gorodetsky was appointed by the Rebbe to serve as the director general of the European and North African Bureau of Chabad-Lubavitch.
The Bureau was established by his father at the request of Rabbi Yosef Yitzchak Schneerson, the Previous Rebbe, shortly after the family's arrival in the United States from Europe.

4634806.title: 70 Years to Bear Fruit
4634806.description: Our sages teach that “Jacob never died. As long as ‘Zaro – his seed’ is alive, he too is alive.” What is the significance of the word “zaro – his seed?” “Zaro” can mean “his children,” but it can also mean “what he has sown.”

4634807.title: The Story of Yud Shevat
4634807.description:
A special presentation highlighting the fascinating events that led up to the Rebbe accepting leadership of the Chabad movement on the 10th of Shevat in
1951. It was a watershed moment in Chabad that ultimately ended up changing the landscape of Judaism all across the world.

4642188.title: In Every Student’s Reach
4642188.description: Throughout the ages, it just wasn't a possibility for most people to publish their own Torah ideas. But today, authentic Torah study must be encouraged. Even if you are uncertain, don't hesitate when it comes to writing and publishing Torah.

4642189.title: An Obligation to Innovate
4642189.description: The Rebbe urged all people to realize their G-d-given potential in whichever possible way, and when it came to Yeshiva students, it was no different. This presentation highlights the Rebbe's efforts and input in encouraging Yeshiva students to publish Torah journals with discussions, questions, and explanations about their studies.

4649071.title: She Speaks with Wisdom
4649071.description: The Sages say: “Who is a worthy wife? One who does the will of her husband.” Chassidism explains that the Hebrew word, ‘Oseh – does’ also means ‘creates.’ Therefore, “Who is a worthy wife? One who creates the will of her husband.”

4649072.title: Vignettes of Royalty
4649072.description:
On the 22nd of Shevat in 1988, the Rebbe's wife, Rebbetzin Chaya Mushka Schneerson, passed away. The Rebbetzin was extremely modest, so not much is known about her life and little footage exists to allow for a comprehensive biography.
This presentation, comprised of the Rebbe's own words following her passing, and first-hand accounts from people who merited to have met her, gives us a peek into the modest loyalty and sacrifice that the Rebbetzin showed. She stood unwavering at her husband's side, and by extension, dedicated her life to the Rebbe's thousands of followers around the world.

4791167.title: The Rebbe on Rocket Science
4791167.description: A fascinating conversation between NASA scientist Professor Velvl Greene and the Rebbe.

4250745.title: Scholarship and Song: A Documentary on the Alter Rebbe
4250745.description: A special video presentation in honor of the 24th of Tevet, the yahrtzeit (anniversary of passing) of Rabbi Schneur Zalman of Liadi, the first Chabad Rebbe, who’s known as the Alter Rebbe.
path: Scholarship and Song: A Documentary on the Alter Rebbe

4429924.title: Four Individuals Forever Affected by the Rebbe
4429924.description: The Baal Shem Tov taught that just as the earth holds the deepest treasures, so does every Jew contain precious stones and gems. Watch as the Rebbe digs deep into four souls, reveals their brilliance, and sets them forth to inspire others.
path: Four Individuals Forever Affected by the Rebbe

4183946.title: On Security and Solidarity
4183946.description: Excerpts from a talk by the Rebbe following the raid on Entebbe to free hostages taken during the hijacking of an Air France flight from Tel Aviv in the summer of 1976.

929769.title: Sensitivity
929769.description: Starting from Moses, their first leader, the Jewish People have been led by individuals exhibiting an essential and unique quality: They were thoughtfully attuned to the distinct and disparate needs of each person in their flock. Throughout history, in times of triumph and adversity, this trait has shown to be distinctively present and in each of our leaders.

132936.title: Challenge
132936.description: The Rebbe's message was as old as the Torah itself, yet his approach was as rousing as dawn. He urged each person, in personal and communal life, to never be satisfied with yesterday's achievements

2776455.title: The Rebbe: Marching Orders
2776455.description: “The Rebbe didn't leave a legacy; he left marching orders”

634110.title: The Jewish Woman
634110.description: The Jewish woman has a unique mission specific to her special qualities and sensitivities. The very future of the Jewish people depends on her success.

1043409.title: The Mission Statement
1043409.description: A powerful tribute to Rabbi Gavriel and Rivky Holtzberg הי"ד and eight thousand of their fellow Shluchim and Shluchos, accompanied by the Rebbe’s talk upon his accepting leadership of the Chabad-Lubavitch movement in 1951.

1038748.title: Faithful and Fortified
1038748.description: The inside story of the Rebbe’s involvement in Israel’s security, as told by its defense and government leaders.

1261262.title: Return of the Souls
1261262.description: A community's visit to the resting place of Rabbi Menachem Mendel Schneerson of Lubavitch on his fifth yahrzeit, Tammuz 3, 5759—June 17, 1999

132979.title: Peace Upon the Land
132979.description: Throughout Jewish history, through times serene and turbulent, the People of Israel looked to the Torah for guidance and stability. Only through steadfast adherence to Torah principles, - the Rebbe insisted - can Israel achieve true peace.

697667.title: From Nikolaev to New York
697667.description: A short video presentation on the life of the Rebbe.

132937.title: Waves
132937.description: Although today's world is a scary place, as evident from the attacks on the World Trade Center on September 11, 2001, one good deed can tip the scales. In Waves, hear the Rebbe explain how each deed, however insignificant it may seem, is universally important.

695828.title: The Rebbe
695828.description: A very brief tribute to the Lubavitcher Rebbe, R’ Menachem Mendel Schneerson of righteous memory. (Narrated by Jon Voight.)

1558408.title: The Rebbe and Rebbetzin Arrive in America
1558408.description: This short documentary includes first hand accounts from those who were actually present at the Rebbe and Rebbetzin's arrival on American soil. Interviewees: Rabbis Yitzchak Groner, Leibel Posner, Dovid Edelman, and Hershel Fogelman.
path: The Rebbe and Rebbetzin Arrive in America

1560685.title: The Rebbe in His Own Words
1560685.description: A compilation of moments with the Rebbe, of righteous memory, highlight some of his key messages and ideas.
path: The Rebbe in His Own Words

1636128.title: The Life of Rebbetzin Chana Schneerson
1636128.description: A look at the remarkable and heroic life of the mother of the Rebbe, Rabbi Menachem Mendel Schneerson, of righteous memory.
path: The Life of Rebbetzin Chana Schneerson

2247427.title: 3 Tammuz Webcast
2247427.description: Presented in honor of the Rebbe’s yahrtzeit, a collection of talks, song and inspiring moments with the Rebbe.

397220.title: The Six-Day War and Tefillin
397220.description: A brief history of the Six-Day War and the Rebbe’s call for all Jewish men, particularly soldiers in the IDF, to don tefillin as a special merit for added security.

2807371.title: A Movement on Trial
2807371.description: Jewish Educational Media pulls back the curtain on the fascinating saga of the violation of Lubavitch’s sacred manuscripts and books—and their ultimate triumph. From the Rebbe’s earliest public references to the theft of Chabad’s treasured library, it was clear that this was a spiritual struggle over the movement’s very soul—as embodied in its holy writings—and even over the very definition of a rebbe. (Excerpt from the complete film)

3374997.title: All About the Rebbe’s Resting Place
3374997.description: The gravesite of the Lubavither Rebbe, of righteous memory, is known as “The Ohel”. Thousands from across the globe stream regularly to visit this sacred place for prayer and blessing.
path: All About the Rebbe’s Resting Place

3113305.title: A Year of Gathering
3113305.description: Today – as in Temple times – men, women, and children unite together at the same place, the same time, and with the same purpose of strengthening our commitment to Torah.

3985041.title: A Moment to Save the World
3985041.description: On multiple occasions in his televised addresses, the Rebbe urgently called for a daily “Moment of Silence” in U.S. public schools, where most American children receive their education. This 20 minute primer summarizes the Rebbe’s approach on this initiative, which is absolutely essential to our country’s future.
path: A Moment to Save the World

4118820.title: Farewell Gathering for the Sixth Rebbe’s First Visit to America
4118820.description: Footage of a farewell dinner in 1930 for the Sixth Lubavitcher Rebbe, who was returning to Latvia following an extended visit to America. The gathering was hosted at the home of Chaim Schneur Zalman (Hyman) Kramer in Brooklyn.
path: Farewell Gathering for the Sixth Rebbe’s First Visit to America

4192713.title: The Story of Rosh Chodesh Kislev 5738 (1977)
4192713.description: The inside story of the horror and pain felt by Chasidim after the Rebbe's heart attack on Shemini Atzeret, and the jubilant joy at his miraculous recovery and finally returning home on Rosh Chodesh Kislev. This presentation lets you experience the timeline of this fascinating story as it took place.
path: The Story of Rosh Chodesh Kislev 5738 (1977)

4205239.title: The Wedding of the Rebbe and Rebbetzin: a Documentary
4205239.description: A special presentation in honor of the anniversary of the wedding of the Rebbe and the Rebbetzin on the 14th of Kislev, 5689 (1928), in Warsaw, Poland.
path: The Wedding of the Rebbe and Rebbetzin: a Documentary

5323408.title: The Moment That Changed My Life
5323408.description: Chief Rabbi Lord Jonathan Sacks describes how meeting the Rebbe as a young university student changed the course of his life.
path: The Moment That Changed My Life

6755617.title: Come With Me to the Ohel
path: Come With Me to the Ohel

1688444.title: One Little Apostrophe
1688444.description:
Dr. Velvel Greene was an original participant in NASA’s Exobiology program searching for life
on Mars. The Rebbe used to ask him for regular reports on his scientific research.

1688443.title: “Un-expert” Advice
1688443.description:
Dr. Velvl Greene is Professor Emeritus of Epidemiology and Public Health at Ben Gurion
University. An original participant in NASA’s Exobiology program, he served as Professor of
Public Health and Microbiology at the University of Minnesota for 27 years.

930198.title: Lone Voice
930198.description:
Dr. David Luchins served on the staff of US Senator Daniel Patrick Moynihan for twenty
years. He reveals the Rebbe’s influence in bringing down the Iron Curtain.

930194.title: Worthy of Respect
930194.description:
Rabbi Sholom Ber Lipskar is executive director of the Aleph Institute, which services the
religious needs of Jewish men and women in prison. In 1985, they brought a group of prisoners
to spend a weekend in Crown Heights, where they attended the Rebbe’s Shabbos Farbrengen.

929639.title: A Parent Feels
929639.description:
In 1973, Rabbi Shmuel Kaplan was called upon by the Rebbe to help a teenager at risk. He
shares a touching letter that the youth received from the Rebbe.

142882.title: Benjamin Netanyahu
142882.description: Former Prime Minister of Israel Benjamin Netanyahu shares some of the personal experiences he had with the Rebbe during his tenure as Israel’s Ambassador to the United Nations.

6197980.title: A Wife’s Nachas
6197980.description:
Mrs. Louise Hager was fourteen years-old when she first met the Rebbe's wife, Rebbetzin
Chaya Mushka. Over the years, she developed a close relationship with the Rebbetzin.

929634.title: Choosing a Thesis
929634.description:
Dr. Susan Handelman is Professor of English Literature at Bar Ilan University in Israel. Trying
to decide on a topic for her doctoral thesis, she decided to ask the Rebbe’s opinion.

929638.title: Department of Military Intelligence
929638.description:
Mr. Aaron Noach Blasbalg was a member of the board of Poalei Agudat Israel for 25 years. He
recalls a fascinating private audience he and his colleagues had with the Rebbe.

6197976.title: Jewish Feminism
6197976.description:
Dr. Susan Handelman is Professor of English Literature at Bar Ilan University in Israel. While
working on her PhD in 1977, she came to study in Crown Heights, with some suspicions as
to what she would find to be the woman’s place in Chassidic life.

929640.title: A Friend's Memory
929640.description: Efraim Steinmetz's father knew the Rebbe in Paris during the 1930s.

929635.title: Consistency
929635.description:
Rabbi Ephraim Sturm served as Executive Vice President and Chief Executive Officer of the
National Council of Young Israel from 1956 to 1992. In the early 1960s, he read an alarming
statistic about the assimilation rate of Jewish Orthodox students in American colleges.

929633.title: “Cookies and Milk”
929633.description: Robert Steingut shares a heartwarming childhood account, of what it was like to be the Rebbe’s neighbor.

929637.title: “You’re Related to the Lubavitcher Rebbe?”
929637.description: David Bezborodko was a businessman from a non-Chassidic family, who directed his family’s glass and mirror factory in Paris.

929636.title: “He'll Find a Way”
929636.description:
With Germany about to invade France, Asher Heber’s father was unsure whether to escape
Paris with his family and leave behind their well-established life. When he consulted the Rebbe
for his opinion, the Rebbe suggested some seemingly impossible advice...

693214.title: A Long-Term Investment
693214.description:
Dr. David Luchins' family joined the Tzemach Tzedek Synagogue in the Brownsville section of
Brooklyn, around 1910. In 1955, when the neighborhood changed, the property was sold for
a large sum. The Rebbe was asked where the money should be spent.

693213.title: Behind the Miracle
693213.description:
After the first El Al plane was hijacked to Algiers, the story began to circulate of the Rebbe’s
advice to Ariel Sharon not to board that flight. Rabbi Zev Segal decided to corroborate the
story with the Rebbe himself.

693216.title: Purim in Berlin
693216.description:
Rabbi Chaim Ciment shares a few stories he heard from Rabbi Joseph Ber Soloveitchik about
his days together with the Rebbe in Berlin.

6195243.title: A Visit with the Rebbetzin - 1987
6195243.description: Mrs. Danièle Gorlin Lassner’s parents and grandparents knew the Rebbe and Rebbetzin from Europe. On this occasion in 1987, she accompanied her parents to visit the Rebbetzin.

693218.title: Chassidism in not Asceticism
693218.description: Dr. Yaacov Hanoka relates how the Rebbe guided him when he first left college and began studying in the Lubavitch Yeshivah

693215.title: No Child Left Behind
693215.description:
As a rabbinic student at 770, Rabbi Aaron Cousin joined his colleagues in working under the
New York State "Released time" program, which allows Public School students to receive
religious instruction.

693211.title: A Tree Grows in Brooklyn
693211.description: Dr. David Luchins served on the staff of US Senator Daniel Patrick Moynihan for twenty years. In 1983, he attended a retirement party for Congresswoman Shirley Chisholm of Crown Heights, where she revealed the identity of a most important mentor.

695939.title: My Job Description
695939.description:
Dr. Yitzchak Block is Emeritus Professor of Philosophy at the University of Western Ontario.
In the mid-1950s, he accompanied a group of college students to a private audience with the
Rebbe.

523700.title: He Meant Business
523700.description: Dov Zlotnik, Professor of Rabbinic Literature at the Conservative Movement’s Jewish Theological Seminary, once delivered a sermon on the importance of Family Purity. As he was to discover, for the Rebbe, a good sermon requires a great ending…

523702.title: A Nation that Dwells Alone
523702.description: Yitzchak Rabin was Prime Minister of Israel, and served as Israel’s ambassador to the United States in the early 1970s. In 1972, he was sent to convey Israel’s blessings to the Rebbe in honor of his 70th birthday.

523699.title: “The Little Lantern”
523699.description: Efraim Steinmetz is a businessman from Caracas, Venezuela. He and his wife came to the Rebbe with concerns about their children’s Jewish education. The Rebbe answered with a story from his own childhood.

523701.title: He Didn’t Change
523701.description: While living in Berlin, the Rebbe made the acquaintance of a Jewish businessman named Yitzchok Meir Ferstenberg. Rabbi Chazkel Besser of Agudas Yisrael of America later heard these recollections from Yitzchok Meir.

523704.title: The King and the Pawn
523704.description: Rabbi Leibel Posner was a student at 770 during the 1940s, and would attend the Rebbe’s monthly Shabbos-Mevorchim Farbrengen. An illuminating lesson in the game of life.

295126.title: Yona Kese,
295126.description: Yona Kese grew up in Dnepropetrovsk at the same time the Rebbe was there. He was a writer, who later became a member in the Israeli Parliament, the Knesset.

295122.title: Shaar Yashuv Cohen
295122.description: In 1927, the Previous Rebbe, Rabbi Yosef Yitzchak Schneersohn, was arrested in Leningrad for counterrevolutionary activity – spreading religion. Shortly thereafter Rabbi Menachem Mendel, his son-in-law to be, was forced into hiding. Shaar Yashuv Cohen is the Chief Rabbi of Haifa, Israel.

295127.title: Chana Shapiro
295127.description:
In 1909, Rabbi Levi Yitzchak, Rebbetzin Chana and their three sons moved to Dnepropetrovsk, a huge military city 520 kilometers from Kiev, where Rabbi Levi Yitzchok became the rabbi of the city’s 25 synagogues and 50,000 Jews.
He turned to Rabbi Zalman Vilenkin, asking him to teach his sons.
Chana Shapiro is Rabbi Vilenkin’s daughter, recalling her parents’ descriptions of the children in their home.

2047034.title: "Deep Down, A Spark"
2047034.description: Rabbi Zalman Posner was a young yeshivah student when the Rebbe arrived in the United States in 1941. He describes an event early in the Rebbe’s presence on these shores, which was truly characteristic of the Rebbe.

295125.title: Rabbi Yisroel Gordon
295125.description: Rabbi Yochanan Gordon traveled from Dokshitz, Russia, to the Rebbe’s wedding in Warsaw. His son, Rabbi Yisroel Gordon, recalls his father’s reports of the wedding.

295124.title: Rabbi Moshe Gerlitzky
295124.description:
Every year, from Berlin, and later from Paris, the Rebbe and the Rebbetzin would visit her father, the Previous Rebbe, for the festive month of Tishrei.
Rabbi Moshe Gerlitzky was a student in the Lubavitch Yeshiva at that time.

1228291.title: This Art is in the Details
1228291.description: Surrounded by original paintings and bas-relief mosaics, long-white-bearded Michoel Muchnik was working on a 3D mosaic of Shabbat and holiday candlesticks when I arrived at his Brooklyn studio.
path: This Art is in the Details

1126916.title: Remembering the Rebbe's Passing
1126916.description: The former chief rabbi of Israel describes the passing of the Rebbe, of righteous memory, and his flight in from Israel for the burial.

1126917.title: The Jewish Embers in the Soviet Union
1126917.description: The former chief rabbi of Israel describes a meeting of Israeli political leftists and how his visit to the Former Soviet Union tens of years later proved their prediction to be correct.
path: The Jewish Embers in the Soviet Union

1126918.title: Where Are the Israeli Revolutionaries?
1126918.description: Rabbi Israel Meir Lau, former chief rabbi of Israel, describes his first audience with the Rebbe, wherein the Rebbe asked him why the citizens of Israel had not moved on from the one political party they had voted in to power for forty-four years, to another party.

1130017.title: Our Generation’s Battle
1130017.description: The Rebbe tells a young rabbi, "We have to enter the enemies battle in order to win the war of assimilation."

1130018.title: American Rabbi Goes to Soviet Russia
1130018.description: The Rebbe sends an American rabbi to open four Jewish religious underground schools and he comes back with a lesson in his mission in life.
path: American Rabbi Goes to Soviet Russia

1130019.title: Modern on the Outside and Chabad on the Inside
1130019.description: The Rebbe encourages a rabbi to open an institution that will create rabbis with the spirit of the chabad warmth
path: Modern on the Outside and Chabad on the Inside

6195204.title: “A Rabbi that Gives”
6195204.description: Dr. Luis Alberto Lacalle, former president of Uruguay, describes his meeting with the Rebbe at Sunday dollars, shortly before his election.

6195205.title: “A Rabbi for Life”
6195205.description: Rabbi Hollander, a well-known rabbinic activist and past president of the Rabbinical Council of America, informs the Rebbe of his plans for retirement.

6195206.title: “The Typewriter”
6195206.description: Rabbi Yosef Goldstein relates a story from his days working in the Rebbe’s office in the 1940s.

6195208.title: “He Created Leaders”
6195208.description: Chief Rabbi of Great Britain and the Commonwealth, Dr. Jonathan Sacks highlights some unique aspects of the Rebbe’s leadership.

6195209.title: “It’s Good to Pray with the Child” – 1950
6195209.description: Rabbi Chaskel Besser tells a story illustrating the Rebbe’s gentle attention to children.
path: “It’s Good to Pray with the Child” – 1950

6195210.title: “On the Way to Washington”
6195210.description: US Senator Joseph Lieberman tells of his first experience at 770 and of his last stop on the way to Washington to take his oath for the Senate.

6195212.title: “Look Up A Professor in Your Field”
6195212.description: Professor Herman Branover, a renowned scientist in the field of Magnetohydrodynamics, left the Soviet Union in 1972. A year later, he received an extraordinary, and perplexing, instruction from the Rebbe.
path: “Look Up A Professor in Your Field”

6195214.title: "It Wasn't Me, It Was Him"
6195214.description: Mr. Robert Abrams served as New York State attorney general from 1978 to 1994. He and his wife, Diane, an attorney herself, would come to the Rebbe for Lekach on Hoshana Rabbah. In 1985, the Rebbe gave them an unexpected blessing for an addition to their family.

6195215.title: “My Son, May He Be Well”
6195215.description: Rabbi Shmuel Lew discovers a Farbrengen of elder Chassidim with the Rebbe’s mother, Rebbetzin Chana Schneerson.

6195216.title: Sukkos with the Rebbe-to-Be
6195216.description: Rabbi Yitzchak Groner is a Shliach of the Rebbe in Melbourne, Australia for over 50 years. He recalls warm anecdotes of the Rebbe’s interaction with the students at 770 during the lifetime of the Previous Rebbe.

6195219.title: A Chassid Is Born
6195219.description: Rabbi Moshe Feller was a non-Lubavitch Yeshiva student from Minneapolis. He speaks here of the first Farbrengen he attended in 1955. Today, he is the Head Shliach of the State of Minnesota.

6195220.title: To Be a Jew
6195220.description: Former Prime Minister of Israel, Ariel Sharon describes part of his first Yechidus with the Rebbe shortly after the Six Day War.

6195221.title: So Serene!
6195221.description: After finding safety on American shores in 1941, the Rebbe helped the war effort, working at the Brooklyn Navy Yard. Mr. Milton Fechter’s desk in the electrical engineering section was not far from the Rebbe’s.

6195224.title: City of Torah Light
6195224.description: Eliyahu Schochetman is a professor of Law at Hebrew University in Jerusalem. His father, Meir, knew the Rebbe while living in Paris in the 1930s.

6195225.title: Hiskashrus
6195225.description: While living in France in the 1930s, the Rebbe and Rebbetzin would often visit the Previous Rebbe in Poland. Rabbis Yitzchak Hakohen Hendel and Menachem Zev Greenglass were students in the Lubavitcher Yeshiva in Warsaw and Otwock.

6195228.title: “I am a Shliach”
6195228.description: Asher Heber’s family moved to Paris in the early 1930s. His father, Leibish, was a businessman who assisted the Rebbe.

6195230.title: “He Saw My Pain”
6195230.description: While on business in Japan, Mr. Ephraim Steinmetz, a businessman from Venezuala, received a mysterious package and note from the Rebbe.

6195233.title: “My Father Belonged to Chassidim”
6195233.description: Attorney Nathan Lewin was one of Chabad’s main lawyers in the federal court case over ownership of the Previous Rebbe’s library. He tells the events which led up to the case, and the vital roles of the Rebbe and Rebbetzin in that court victory (1985 – 1987).

6195234.title: “You’re a Good Salesman, Right?”
6195234.description: Mayer Zeiler is the owner of Flocktex Industries in Israel, one of the world’s leading textile manufacturers.

6195237.title: Build, Build, Build!
6195237.description: Ron Nachman is the mayor of Ariel, Israel.

6195239.title: From Brooklyn to Jerusalem
6195239.description: Rabbi Shaar Yashuv Cohen is the Chief Rabbi of Haifa, Israel. Once, in Yechidus, he asked the Rebbe why he did not move to the Holy Land.

6195240.title: The Jewish Woman’s Courage – 1960s
6195240.description: Rabbi Chaim Yaakov Shlomei was dean of the Bais Rivka Girl’s Seminary in France for over twenty years. He shares a special letter sent by the Rebbe to the seminary students.

6195245.title: The Essence of Things
6195245.description: Former Prime Minister of Israel Benjamin Netanyahu shares some of the personal experiences he had with the Rebbe during his tenure as Israel’s Ambassador to the United Nations.

6195246.title: Loans for Education
6195246.description: Mr. Sam Feiglin’s father, Moshe Zalman, was a founder of the Jewish community in Australia. A glimpse into the Rebbe’s personal involvement for Australian Jewry.

6195247.title: They Will Not See Us” – A Story of the Fifth Rebbe
6195247.description: Asher Heber’s father, Laibish, was present at the last Purim Farbrengen of Rabbi Sholom Dov Ber, the fifth Rebbe of Chabad, several years after the beginning of Communist rule.
path: They Will Not See Us” – A Story of the Fifth Rebbe

6195250.title: If a Jew is Challenged
6195250.description: Rabbi Fabian Shoenfeld had a private audience with the Rebbe along with fellow members of the Rabbinical Council of America. A fascinating exploration by the Rebbe of the biblical story of Elijah on Mount Carmel.

6195251.title: “Only 14 years-old!?”
6195251.description: Nochum Goldschmidt attended the same Cheder in Dnepropetrovsk as the Rebbe and the Rebbe’s brother, Leibel. Nochum’s cousin, Rabbi Mordechia Ashkenazi, heard these memories him.

6195252.title: The Chief Rabbi’s Son
6195252.description: Yona Kesa grew up in Dnepropetrovsk in the early 1900s. He shares his fond memory of the Rebbe and of the Rebbe’s father, Reb Levik.

6195254.title: 11 Hours of Torah
6195254.description: Every year, from Berlin, the Rebbe and Rebbetzin would visit the Rebbetzin’s father, Rabbi Yosef Yitzchok, for the festive month of Tishrei. Rabbi Moshe Eliyahu Gerlitzky was a student at the Lubavitcher Yeshiva in Lodz, Poland. He was present when, upon the Previous Rebbe’s instruction, the Rebbe Farbrenged with the Chassidim for Simchas Beis Hashoevah.

6195255.title: The Lubavitcher Rebbe's View on Zionism
6195255.description: Rabbi Yehudah Leib Posner and his brother were students in 770 during the 1940s. One week, their father came in from Pittsburgh and spent Shabbos with them. Friday night after the prayers, their father asked the Rebbe how he should respond to the controversial topic of the day – the creation of a Jewish State.
path: The Lubavitcher Rebbe's View on Zionism

6195257.title: Brothers
6195257.description: Rabbi Chazkel Besser of Agudas Yisrael of America, befriended the Rebbe’s brother, Leibel, while living in Tel Aviv during the 1940s.

6195258.title: Brothers – Part 2: The Brother in New York
6195258.description: Rabbi Chazkel Besser of Agudas Yisrael of America knew the Rebbe’s brother, Leibel, in Tel Aviv. In 1948, Rabbi Besser moved to New York, and Leibel sent family pictures with him to give to his mother, Rebbetzin Chana.
path: Brothers – Part 2: The Brother in New York

6195260.title: Reporting from 770, Part 1: Encounter at Farbrengen
6195260.description: Herbert Weiner is the author of Nine and a Half Mystics. In 1955, he was sent by Commentary magazine to report on the activities going on at Lubavitch World Headquarters.
path: Reporting from 770, Part 1: Encounter at Farbrengen

6195262.title: Reporting from 770, Part 2: Alone with the Mystic
6195262.description: Herbert Weiner is the author of Nine and a Half Mystics. In the mid-1950s, he scheduled his first private audiences with the Rebbe, intending to interview him for a series of articles.
path: Reporting from 770, Part 2: Alone with the Mystic

6195264.title: It’s 4:00 AM. Do You Know Where the Rebbe Is?
6195264.description: The Rebbe and Rebbetzin arrived to America on the 28th of Sivan – June 23, 1941. Rabbi Mottel Sharfstein was a student in 770 during the 1940s. He recalls the first time he heard from his teacher about the Rebbe.
path: It’s 4:00 AM. Do You Know Where the Rebbe Is?

6195266.title: Handing the Match
6195266.description: Yehuda Avner served on the personal staff of five Israeli Prime Ministers. In 1977, after meeting with President Carter at Camp David, Menachem Begin sent him to report to the Rebbe.

6195267.title: Caring for Soviet Jewry
6195267.description: At the time that the Soviet Union began to open its doors, Shoshana Cardin served as Chairman of NCSJ, the National Conference on Soviet Jewry.

6195268.title: Camp Memories
6195268.description: Meir Lieberman was a camper in Gan Israel, New York in the summer of 1960. He had never heard of the Rebbe before, but apparently, the Rebbe knew of him.

6195269.title: Scientific Analysis
6195269.description: Professor Herman Branover is a renowned physicist, who received not only spiritual guidance from the Rebbe, but scientific guidance, as well.

6195270.title: Astronomically Impossible
6195270.description: Rabbi Yosef Goldstein, an educator and author of the children’s audio-cassette series, Story Time with Uncle Yossi.

6195271.title: Three Millimeters Off
6195271.description: Rabbi Dov Levanoni is the author of The Temple in Jerusalem, and an expert on the Holy Temple. His book is based on the scaled model of the Second Temple which he built, and for which he received “a little help” from the Rebbe.

6195272.title: Children, Be Strong!
6195272.description: In 1939, the Rebbe’s father was exiled by the Soviet government to a remote region of Kazakhstan. At the end of his sentence, he and his wife traveled to the closest large city, Almaty, Kazakhstan. Leibel Raskin and his family were there to greet and assist them upon their arrival.

6195274.title: Sephardic Recordings
6195274.description: Mr. Joseph Cayre is a business leader and a prominent member of the Sephardic community.

6195277.title: A Mission in Australia – Part 1: Torah is Not Overseas
6195277.description: Thirteen year-old Shmuel Gurewicz arrived with his family to Australia in 1949. He was among the first students of the Tomchei Temimim Yeshiva in Shepparton, Australia. But he had “bigger” plans…
path: A Mission in Australia – Part 1: Torah is Not Overseas

6195278.title: A Mission in Australia – Part 2: Go Back Tonight!
6195278.description: Living in Australia during the early 1950s, young Shmuel Gurewicz wished to study abroad in a more established Yeshiva. The Rebbe instructed him to remain in Australia, to spread the light of Torah to others there. Some time passed, and Shmuel decided to try again…
path: A Mission in Australia – Part 2: Go Back Tonight!

6195279.title: Head Held High
6195279.description: Shortly after her engagement, Chana Sharfstein had an audience with the Rebbe. To her surprise, the Rebbe asked if she was planning to wear a Shaitel after her marriage. But that wasn’t the only surprise in store for her.

6195281.title: Yom Kippur in the Air Force - Part 1: Operation Greenland
6195281.description: A few days before Yom Kippur in 1964, a sudden request came to 770 from a Jew who worked on a US Air force base in Greenland, to send a Shliach there to conduct the Yom Kippur services. Rabbi Shmuel Lew was called to duty.
path: Yom Kippur in the Air Force - Part 1: Operation Greenland

6195282.title: Yom Kippur in the Air Force - Part 2: Mission Accomplished
6195282.description:
Rabbi Shmuel Lew continues recounting his Yom Kippur mission. Just one day before he was
to leave for Greenland, the Rebbe’s mother, Rebbetzin Chana Schneerson, suddenly passed
away.
path: Yom Kippur in the Air Force - Part 2: Mission Accomplished

6195283.title: Courage Under Oppression
6195283.description:
In spring of 1944, the Rebbe’s parents were stranded in Kazakhstan, having just completed
five years of Soviet-imposed exile. Mrs. Rochel Lipskar and her family lived a few hours away,

6195285.title: The World's Blueprint
6195285.description:
In 1961, Rivkah Blau was Vice-President of Yavne, one of the first Orthodox student
organizations on American college campuses. In a private audience, the Rebbe asked Rivkah
and her friend numerous questions on the realities of Jewish outreach in university. As it
turned out, her friend came with some questions of his own.

6197974.title: Questions of Faith
6197974.description:
Herbert Weiner is the author of Nine-and-a-Half Mystics. During his private audiences with
the Rebbe in the mid-1950s, he raised some questions about the nature of faith in Judaism.

6197975.title: Questions of Faith
6197975.description:
Herbert Weiner is the author of Nine-and-a-Half Mystics, and served as the leader of a Reform
congregation in New Jersey for forty years. He discussed with the Rebbe Chabad’s unique
approach to reconnecting Jews with their faith.

6197977.title: The Rebbe's Son-in-law
6197977.description:
During the 1930s, the Previous Rebbe would often visit a health clinic in Paris. On Shabbos,
he would stay at the home of Yankel and Baila Lax. Their son, Berel, was about twenty years
old at the time, and recalls the Rebbe visiting his father-in-law at their home quite frequently.

6197978.title: Anatomy of a Miracle
6197978.description:
On Shemini Atzeres, 1977, the Rebbe suffered a massive heart attack during the Hakofos
celebration. Dr. Ira Weiss flew in from Chicago to join the medical team treating the Rebbe at
770. Subsequently, he became the Rebbe's cardiologist.

6197981.title: An Encounter with the Alter Rebbe
6197981.description:
Rabbi Yehuda Leib Schapiro heard Rabbi J.B. Soloveitchik retell the story of the Alter Rebbe’s
attempt to visit the Vilna Gaon, as it had been passed down through his own family, all the
way back to the Gaon’s chief disciple.
path: An Encounter with the Alter Rebbe

6197982.title: In the Halls of the Sorbonne
6197982.description:
In November 1937, the Rebbe enrolled in the University of Paris, known as "the Sorbonne."
A young man named Moshe Zev Reitzer was studying to become a pharmacist at the
Sorbonne, attending some of the same classes as the Rebbe. Yoel Reitzer is Moshe Zev's son.
path: In the Halls of the Sorbonne

6197983.title: A Talmud Class to Remember
6197983.description:
Rivkah Marelus’s father told her a “memorable” story about a Talmud class the Rebbe gave
in Paris during the 1930s.

6197985.title: Head of the Resistance
6197985.description:
As First Secretary in the Israeli embassy in Moscow during the late 1950s, Aryeh Lova Eliav
assisted Chabad's underground network in their mission to preserve Judaism in the Soviet
Union. After completing his post in Russia, he had a private audience with the Rebbe, which
lasted seven hours.

6197986.title: "How Could He Have Known?"
6197986.description:
In April, 1985 the Rebbe instructed Professor Herman Branover to call his contacts in the
Soviet Union and inform them that freedom was closer than they could possibly imagine.

6197987.title: It's Not About You
6197987.description:
As a young man, Rabbi Aharon Serebryansky lived in Australia, and was among the original
students of the Lubavitch Yeshivah there. When he found himself devoting vast amounts of
time to teaching others rather than to his own learning, he turned to the Rebbe for guidance.

6197988.title: To Be A Rebbe
6197988.description:
Freddy Hager comes from a long line of famous rabbis and Chassidic Rebbes. At his first
private audience with the Rebbe, the Rebbe told him how to carry on the family legacy.

6197989.title: Someone had Spoken to Him
6197989.description:
Mr. Bentzion Rader and his wife, Hinda, live in London, England. In 1974, the Rebbe
instructed them to publish a chassidic primer for Jewish women.

6197991.title: Understanding the Shluchim
6197991.description:
Mrs. Leah Kahan shares some of the Rebbetzin’s admiration for the Shluchim, which she
heard first-hand.

6197993.title: Money or Life
6197993.description:
Mr. Peter Kalms lives in London, England. In one of his letters, he explained to the Rebbe the
financial pressures that Chabad institutions were facing there, and that it may compel them
to restrict some of their classes...

6197994.title: Downstairs Neighbors
6197994.description:
In the mid-1950s, Rabbi Yosef Goldstein and his family lived two floors below the Rebbe and
Rebbetzin, at 346 New York Avenue.

6197996.title: The Path of the Heart
6197996.description:
In 1969, Mr. Gordon Zacks was Chairman of the UJA's Young Leadership Cabinet. Shortly
after delivering a keynote address to three thousand communal leaders from across the US
and Canada, he was informed that the Rebbe wished to meet with him - for a “heart to heart”
discussion.

6197997.title: Priorities
6197997.description:
Don't wait so long as since I last spoke with you to report good news in spreading Judaism,
especially in the realm of Jewish education. Your main concern must be: What are you doing
to benefit the community?

6197998.title: A Happy Ending
6197998.description:
Joe Cayre, businessman, philanthropist and co-founder of Good Times Home Video, shares
some personal business advice he received from the Rebbe.

6197999.title: A Mother Recalls
6197999.description:
Mrs. Rochel Lipskar used to visit the Rebbe's mother, Rebbetzin Chana Schneerson of blessed
memory. On occasion, Rebbetzin Chana would recall the Rebbe's childhood.

6198001.title: My Dear Children: An audience with the Previous Rebbe
6198001.description:
In 1941, Yehudah Leib Posner, age 13, and his brother Zalman, age 14, were students at the
Yeshiva in 770.
path: My Dear Children: An audience with the Previous Rebbe

6198002.title: The Flashpoint
6198002.description: In 1972, Yehuda Avner was a senior diplomat at the Israeli Embassy in Washington.

6198004.title: A Contract with G-d
6198004.description:
Rabbi Zev Segal served as Rabbi of the Young Israel of Newark for fifty years, and was
president of the Rabbinical Council of America. Through his work, he visited Jewish
communities across the globe.

6198007.title: Revolutionaries
6198007.description:
Rabbi Yisroel Meir Lau was Chief Rabbi of Israel from 1993 to 2003. He had his first private
audience with the Rebbe in 1974, shortly after the Yom Kippur War.

6198008.title: A Mission to Lithuania
6198008.description:
In 1966, Rabbi Yosef Krupnik was a student at the RJJ Yeshivah on the Lower East Side.
From his teacher, Rabbi Shaya Shimonowitz, he heard a story about the Rebbe in Europe.

6198009.title: “Think Good, and it will be Good”
6198009.description:
In 1979, Mr. Freddy Hager was a diamond dealer in London, England. Business was slow, and
he came to the Rebbe for advice.
path: “Think Good, and it will be Good”

6198010.title: Returning to Torah - Part 1
6198010.description:
In 1962, Dr. Yaacov Hanoka was a physics student at Pennsylvania State University. After a
group of rabbinic students visited his campus for Shabbos, he was intrigued to learn more
about Judaism. His Hillel rabbi arranged a private audience for him with the Rebbe.

6198012.title: Returning to Torah - Part 2
6198012.description: Dr. Yaacov Hanoka continues the account of his first year studies at 770.

6198013.title: Family Memories
6198013.description:
Rabbi Sholom Ber Butman recalls his childhood memories of the Rebbe in Paris, 1947, when
the Rebbe flew there to greet his mother after she escaped Russia.

6198014.title: Family Memories
6198014.description:
Rabbi Sholom Ber Butman concludes his childhood memories of the Rebbe’s stay in Paris in
1947. The Butman family was staying at the same home as the Rebbe’s mother after her
escape from Russia.

6198015.title: Under the Talis
6198015.description:
The Rebbe records in his diary of 1932 that his father-in-law and predecessor, Rabbi Yosef
Yitzchak of Lubavitch, instructed him to don four pairs of Tefillin every day.
Rabbi Yisroel Gordon was a student in 770 when the Rebbe arrived in America in June, 1941.
He recalls how this secret first became known to American Chassidim.

6198017.title: Diplomacy
6198017.description:
Rabbi Avraham Korf is head Shliach of the State of Florida. He shares some instructions he
received from the Rebbe in how to balance groundbreaking Shlichus with respect for existing
institutions.

6198018.title: Seven Hours Straight
6198018.description:
Rabbi Nochum Avraham Yakobovitch was in Paris during the Rebbe’s stay there in 1947. He
was present one Shabbos when the Rebbe was studying alone in the synagogue.

6198019.title: The Stamp Collection
6198019.description:
Mr. Hirsh Katz recalls some of the Rebbe’s personal guidance to him as a youth. His father,
Reb Yankel Katz, was a major supporter of Chabad in America, whom the Rebbe termed, “a
good friend.”

6198020.title: Millions of Hostages
6198020.description:
Mr. Bentzion Rader shares a private audience he and his wife had with the Rebbe, at which
they discussed the Rebbe's views about Aliyah and demonstrations for Soviet Jewry.

6198021.title: Change of Plan
6198021.description:
Rabbi Moshe Herson is Head Shliach of the State of New Jersey. As a student at 770 from
1955 to 1959, he would spend his summers visiting remote Jewish communities.

6198022.title: Jewish Science
6198022.description:
In 1961, Dr. Velvel Greene joined NASA’s Exobiology program. He had his first private
audience with the Rebbe in the mid-1960s.

6198023.title: Jewish Science
6198023.description:
Dr. Velvel Greene worked in NASA’s Exobiology program searching for life on Mars. He
continues the account of his first private audience with the Rebbe in the mid-1960s.

6198024.title: A Guarantee and a Miracle
6198024.description:
Mr. Joe Cayre and his brothers founded Good Times Home Video. He shares an episode
involving himself and one of his brothers.

6198025.title: Rabbi Engineer
6198025.description:
Mr. Yaakov Hardof is an electrical engineer, and founder of Amperon Electronics and
Soundsystems and Interconcept Incorporated. In 1957, he spent close to two hours with the
Rebbe discussing... engineering!

6198026.title: Rabbi Engineer
6198026.description:
Mr. Yaakov Hardof continues the account of his 1957 audience with the Rebbe, when the
Rebbe asked him to explain an engineering breakthrough of the time: the transistor.

6198027.title: Fatherly Concern
6198027.description:
Mrs. Esther Goldman shares a heartwarming story of the Rebbe’s concern for a young
expecting mother.

6198028.title: To Honor His Mother
6198028.description:
In 1960, Rabbi Yosef Wineberg began to deliver Tanya lessons over the radio in New York. The
Rebbe's mother, Rebbetzin Chana Schneerson, was fond of his broadcasts. When she passed
away in 1964, he asked the Rebbe for permission to honor her memory in a special way...

6198030.title: The Story Behind the Story
6198030.description:
Rabbi Yisroel Meir Lau tells the “story behind the story” of the Rebbe’s foresight regarding
his position in Israel’s Chief Rabbinate.

6198031.title: Entry Exam
6198031.description:
Rabbi Chaim Nachman Kovalsky was a student of Rabbi Yechiel Yaakov Weinberg, author of
the Halachic responsa, Sridei Eish. He shares a story he heard from Rabbi Weinberg about the
Rebbe in Berlin.

6198033.title: Science and Faith
6198033.description:
In 1950, Rabbi Yehuda Leib Posner was a student at 770. He received some coaching from the
Rebbe on how to approach the topic of “science and faith.”

6198034.title: Leaving Paris
6198034.description:
Rabbi Sholom Ber Levine shares the account of the Rebbe and Rebbetzin’s departure from Paris,
as told to him by the Rebbetzin herself.

6198035.title: To Save a Life
6198035.description:
Mendel Notik worked in the Rebbe and Rebbetzin’s household during the 1970s. He shares a
story he heard from the Rebbetzin about a “campaign” of the Rebbe to save Jews in Nazioccupied
France.

6198036.title: The Rebbe Insisted on Registering as a Jew
6198036.description: Rabbi Menachem Tiechtel was a refugee in Southern France during the Nazi occupation. He shares a story about the Rebbe that he learned during that time.
path: The Rebbe Insisted on Registering as a Jew

6198037.title: First Farbrengen at 770
6198037.description:
Rabbis Dovid Edelman, Hershel Fogelman and Yehuda Leib Posner were students at 770 in
1941. They describe the first Farbrengen the Rebbe held after arriving safely to America from
war-torn Europe.

6198038.title: Rationalist Acting Above Reason
6198038.description:
Dr. Yitzchak Block is Emeritus Professor of Philosophy at the University of Western Ontario.
Upon the Rebbe’s instructions, he disregarded his desire to avoid academic conferences. One
time, however, the Rebbe seemed to go too far...

6198039.title: The Rebbe Taught a Young Woman the Meaning of Love
6198039.description: Mrs. Chana Sharfstein recalls one of her first private audiences with the Rebbe, as a young woman in her early twenties, when the Rebbe asked her about her prospects for marriage (1954).
path: The Rebbe Taught a Young Woman the Meaning of Love

6198040.title: Not Quite What the Doctor Ordered
6198040.description:
On the night of Shemini Atzeres, 1977, the Rebbe suffered a heart attack during the Hakafos
celebration. Dr. Ira Weiss was part of the medical team that treated the Rebbe at 770 over
the next month and a half. He recalls the Rebbe’s first Farbrengen following the heart attack.
path: Not Quite What the Doctor Ordered

6198041.title: Making Aliyah: a Multifaceted Decision
6198041.description:
In the early 1970s, Mr. Peter Kalms planned to move his family from England to Israel. Before
making the move, he visited the Rebbe to receive his blessing.

6198042.title: A Gentleman and a Scholar
6198042.description:
In 1947, the Rebbe flew to Paris to escort his mother to the United States after her escape
from the Soviet Union. While there, he visited a small Yeshiva outside Paris where Rabbi Yaakov
Holtzman was a student. Later, in New York, he worked in the Rebbe’s household.

6198043.title: The Bottom Line
6198043.description:
Rabbi Shimon Goldman's father-in-law, Rabbi Yochanan Gordon, was head of the Gemillas
Chesed Shomrei Shabbos interest-free loan fund for over twenty years. The Rebbe sets a high
bar for how to measure the fund’s success.

6198044.title: No Questions Asked
6198044.description: Rabbi Mordechai Ashkenazi shares a personal audience with the Rebbe, where an answer was given to a question had, but not asked.

6198045.title: “You’ll be Asking Him Soon…”
6198045.description:
Dr. David Luchins’ father, Dr. Abraham Luchins, was a renowned psychologist and an admirer
of the Previous Rebbe, Rabbi Yosef Yitzchak of Lubavitch. In a private audience, he learned
that the Previous Rebbe was also an “admirer” — of a certain Rebbe-to-be.

6198046.title: Love that Knows No Barriers
6198046.description:
Rabbi Dovid Edelman was a student at 770 during the 1940s. One night, the Rebbe came out
from the study of his father-in-law, the Previous Rebbe, with a fundamental lesson in loving
one’s fellow Jew.

6198047.title: "They're Going to Listen to You…"
6198047.description: Mrs. Rochel Fogelman and her husband have been Shluchim in Worcester, Massachusetts since 1947. As one of her outreach activities, she would give book reviews for Jewish women’s groups. (1967)

6198048.title: Motherly Guidance
6198048.description:
Mrs. Hadassa Carlebach is an extended cousin of the Rebbe and Rebbetzin. When she arrived
in New York in 1947, they were her only family there.

6198051.title: Month of Good Mazel
6198051.description:
Dr. Yaakov Hanoka is a renowned scientist. In 1970, the Rebbe’s advice helped him get “top
dollar” when he had to sell his house.

6198052.title: Directions
6198052.description:
Rabbi Avrohom Pinter’s family moved to Crown Heights in the mid-1950s. When his European
grandparents came to visit, they asked for directions from a “simple Jew” who happened to
be passing by on the sidewalk.

6198053.title: Tax Advice
6198053.description:
Mr. Bentzion Rader was a practicing chartered accountant in London, England for almost
forty years. One time, the Rebbe recommended against the tax advice Mr. Rader had given
to a major philanthropist in England.

6198054.title: “What Do You Mean You’re Stopping?”
6198054.description:
Mr. Shimshon Stock was head of a Crown Heights charity fund, “Chevras Simchas Shabbos
V’Yom Tov” for 30 years. He recalls how it all started...

6198055.title: “Quiet, Please!”
6198055.description:
Rabbi Yisroel Gordon was a student at 770 during the 1940s. One time, the Rebbe came down
from his father-in-law, the Previous Rebbe, with a message “all the way from the top.”

6198056.title: See No Evil
6198056.description:
Rabbi Moshe Feller is the Head Shliach of Minnesota. In 1972, he invited bestselling author
Herman Wouk to speak at his dinner in honor of the Rebbe’s 70th birthday.

6198058.title: “Don’t Worry, He’s Coming”
6198058.description:
Mr. Freddy Hager lives in London, England. One year, he made an unexpected stop at 770 on
his way to the airport to return to England. It soon became clear that his visit was not
entirely unexpected after all.

6198059.title: Proud Father-in-Law, Proud Son-in-Law
6198059.description:
Rabbi Mendel Feldman was a student at 770 during the 1940s. He recalls some of the mutual
admiration he was privy to witness between the Previous Rebbe and the Rebbe.

6198061.title: Faith is Contagious
6198061.description:
Mr. David Chase shares how one little request from the Rebbe changed his entire life — and
the lives of others.

6198062.title: Welcome Home
6198062.description:
In the early 1970s, upon the Rebbe’s instruction, Rabbi Laibl Wolf worked as Hillel Rabbi at
the University of Wisconsin-Madison. After encountering many non-Jewish students who
were curious about Judaism and wished to convert, he approached the Rebbe for advice.

6198063.title: A Life and Death Matter
6198063.description:
On the 13th of Iyar, 1952, the Rebbe’s brother, Reb Yisroel Aryeh Leib, passed away in
England at the age of 42. The Rebbe enlisted Reb Berel Junik in the effort to shield his elderly
mother from the tragic, and potentially devastating, news.

6198065.title: “Don’t Tell”
6198065.description:
After his marriage, Rabbi Shmuel Lew was studying at the Rebbe’s Kolel for newly married
men, adjacent to 770. It was not until decades later that he discovered who offered to fund
his full-time Torah study while he started a family.

6198070.title: To Lift Up
6198070.description: Rabbi Yosef Wineberg shares a penetrating story, revealing the Rebbe’s own view of himself.

6198073.title: “I’ll Give You Half”
6198073.description:
Reb Leibel Zisman has been in the construction and real estate business for almost 50 years.
