In June 1987, he was asked to join a building project that had opportunity for enormous profit.

6198074.title: Private Conversation
6198074.description:
Rabbi Moshe Herson is Head Shliach of the State of New Jersey. He recalls the Rebbe’s visit
to the Ohel on the first Yud-Beis Tammus after the passing of the Previous Rebbe.

6198075.title: Knowing Chicago's Ropes
6198075.description:
Mr. Frank Moscowitz worked in the Chicago public school system for 38 years. In 1969, after
qualifying to become an elementary school principal, he was assigned a school in a high-crime
neighborhood in Chicago’s South Side. He flew to New York to consult with the Rebbe...

6198076.title: Sent Packing
6198076.description:
After four years away in Yeshiva, Rabbi Aaron Cousin was planning to visit his family back in
Leeds, England. The Rebbe showed extraordinary interest in his travel plans.

6198077.title: The ABCs of Love
6198077.description:
Rabbi Yehuda Leib Posner studied at 770 during the 1940s. In March 1948, he was sent out
by Merkos L’inyonei Chinuch to travel through small American towns disseminating Jewish
outreach material.

6198078.title: Your People’s Future
6198078.description:
After graduating High School, Mrs. Bassie Garelik planned to attend college. The Rebbe,
however, offered her a whole new perspective on planning for the future...

6198079.title: Kumatz-Alef — Uh
6198079.description:
Dr. Bunim Weinbaum used to tutor Hebrew reading on the side. Here, he recalls how the Rebbe
led him to turn a “side-job” into nothing short of an educational revolution.

6198080.title: The Schneerson Resolve
6198080.description:
Rabbi Mordechai Ashkenazi’s cousin, Reb Nochum Goldshmidt, was close with the Rebbe’s
family when they lived in Dnepropretrovsk, Ukraine. Rabbi Ashkenazi recounts a story he
heard from Reb Nochum about the Rebbe’s father, Rabbi Levi Yitzchak Schneerson.

6198081.title: The Holy Shabbos
6198081.description:
Mr. Jonathan Nelson recounts some of his father’s encounters with the Rebbe during the
1940s and 50s.

6198082.title: “Check Your Mezuzahs”
6198082.description:
After suffering a debilitating injury to her back, Mrs. Tzirel Weinbaum received an instruction
from the Rebbe to have her Mezuzos checked...

6198083.title: Over the Top
6198083.description:
Rabbis Yosef Goldstein and Mendel Baumgarten recall a memorable Tashlich on Rosh
Hashanah, 1956.

6198085.title: Chivalry on the Upper East Side
6198085.description:
Mr. Jules Lassner shares a private audience he and his father-in-law had with the Rebbe, in
which the Rebbe set a “liberating” agenda.
path: Chivalry on the Upper East Side

6198086.title: “It's Nothing”
6198086.description:
Rabbi Chaim Ciment has been a Shliach in Boston, Massachusetts, since 1954. In the late
1970s, he was diagnosed with Ankylosing Spondylitis, a debilitating condition that until today
has no known cure.

6198087.title: A Father
6198087.description:
Rabbi Dovid Edelman recalls the events of Simchas Torah, 1955, when the Rebbe taught the
Niggun “Darkecha Elokeinu.”

6198088.title: Just What the Rebbe Ordered
6198088.description:
Rabbi Chaim Zev Bomzer is a long-standing member of the Rabbinical Council of America, and
was rabbi of the Young Israel of Ocean Parkway for 40 years. He shares a story about the
Rebbe’s advice to his daughter.

6198091.title: The Patient Knows Best
6198091.description:
On Shemini Atzeres 1977, the Rebbe suffered a massive heart attack during the Hakofos
celebration. Dr. Ira Weiss, a cardiologist, flew in from Chicago to join the team of doctors
treating the Rebbe at 770.

6198092.title: Solidarity
6198092.description:
In 1990, Mr. David Chase opened the Solidarity-Chase Bank in Poland, one of the first private
financial institutions there after communist rule. He received personal instructions from the
Rebbe about rebuilding Jewish life in Poland and improving Polish attitudes towards Jews.

6198096.title: Spare the Rod
6198096.description:
Rabbi Shmuel Lew, a veteran Shliach and educator, shares a lesson he received from the Rebbe
about disciplining children.

6198100.title: “Thousands of Things to Do”
6198100.description: Rabbi Nachman Sudak is Head Shliach of the United Kingdom. He recalls his days as a young rabbinic student at 770, when the Rebbe began to call upon young couples to pick up their lives and move across the globe to reach out to fellow Jews. (Late 1950s)

6198102.title: How Important is it to You?
6198102.description:
In 1975, Mr. Bentzion Rader went on a business trip to Detroit, Michigan. While there, he
met a non-observant Jew whom he convinced to put on Tefillin. After reporting this episode
to the Rebbe, he found himself doing a little soul-searching of his own...
path: How Important is it to You?

6198104.title: Check Again
6198104.description:
Rabbi Hersh Kotlarsky, an elder Chassid, shares a personal story about the Rebbe’s medical
advice to his wife before surgery.

6198105.title: Honoring Groom and Bride
6198105.description: Menachem and Devorah Emanuel were married in Crown Heights in 1983. On the day of their wedding, they received an invitation from the Rebbe to hold their first Sheva Brachos at the Rebbe’s Farbrengen in 770.

6198108.title: Bringing Chanukah Light to Prisoners
6198108.description: The Rebbe instructs Rabbi Shabsi Katz, chief Jewish chaplain for South Africa’s prison system, to brighten the lives of prisoners incarcerated in South Africa.

6198109.title: Student Revolution
6198109.description:
In 1970, Rabbi Laibl Wolf took up the position of Hillel Rabbi at the University of Wisconsin-
Madison upon the Rebbe’s instruction. At his first private audience with the Rebbe he
received special guidance in how to effectively reach Jewish students on campus.

6198110.title: Letters from Youth
6198110.description:
Rabbi Sholom Ber Levine, chief librarian at the Library of Agudas Chassidei Chabad at 770,
recalls the discovery of the earliest known letter of the Rebbe to Rabbi Yosef Rosen, the
Rogatchover Gaon.

6198111.title: Memories of the Rebbe in Paris
6198111.description: Rabbi Moshe Herson shares stories he heard from Alexander Reinin, who was with the Rebbe in France during the 1930s.
path: Memories of the Rebbe in Paris

6198112.title: Understanding the Sacrifice
6198112.description: Moshe Levy was a sergeant in the IDF Special Forces during the Yom Kippur War. The unit he led defended the Budapest Outpost, the only Israeli bunker on the Suez Canal to withstand the Egyptian attack. He is one of only forty people to be awarded the Israel Hero Medal.

6198113.title: Calling the Shots
6198113.description:
Major General Yossi Ben Hanan served as Commander of the IDF Armored Corps and of
Israel’s National Security College. He is a recipient of the IDF’s Medal of Courage.

6198115.title: Laying Down Roots
6198115.description: Reb Shmuel Isaac Popack recalls events after the Previous Rebbe’s arrival in America.

6198117.title: Ten Minutes to Change Worlds
6198117.description:
As a college student in 1970, Mr. Freddy Hager was in New York, when he was unexpectedly
called in for an audience with the Rebbe.

6198118.title: Tearful Departure
6198118.description: Mrs. Fruma Junik’s husband, Rabbi Berel Junik, was a member of the Rebbe and Rebbetzin’s household in New York. In 1953, the Rebbetzin traveled to Europe.

6198120.title: No Doubts
6198120.description: Mrs. Bassie Garelik, one of the Rebbe's emissaries in Milan, Italy since 1958, shares a letter she received from the Rebbe during a time when she was doubting her abilities as the Rebbe's representative

6198121.title: Waiting for Shlichus
6198121.description:
Rabbi Avraham Korf is head Shliach of the State of Florida. He recalls some of the Rebbe’s
instructions to him as a young rabbinic student in Crown Heights during the 1950s waiting to
go on Shlichus.

6198123.title: The Two-Page P.S.
6198123.description:
Reform Rabbi Herbert Weiner maintained a relationship with the Rebbe over the years, after
having interviewed him twice in the 1950s. His interviews with the Rebbe are published in his
book Nine and a Half Mystics.

6198128.title: In-reach
6198128.description:
Mr. Shimshon Stock headed the Chevra Simchas Shabbos V’Yom Tov charity fund for thirty
years. As a teenager in the 1940s, he studied at the Lubavitcher Yeshiva in Crown Heights,
Brooklyn. During that time, he was privileged to study one-on-one with the Rebbe.

6198133.title: End the War Now!
6198133.description: Dr. Elliot Udell, the Rebbe’s podiatrist, relates how he requested of the Rebbe to write a prayer that the Gulf War end in a week’s time, so that the holiday of Purim could be joyously celebrated.

6198135.title: First Impression
6198135.description:
Rabbi Heschel Ryzman, a Torah scholar and author of numerous Torah works, studied at the
Lubavitcher Yeshivas in Warsaw and Otwock, Poland during the 1930s. He recalls the first
time he saw the Rebbe.

6198136.title: “It’ll Be Good for Him”
6198136.description:
Dr. David Luchins is Chair of the Political Science Department at Touro college. He dicusses
the roots of his family’s 4-generation-connection to Chabad.

6198137.title: The Alter Rebbe’s Parade
6198137.description:
Rabbi Yitzchok Dovid Groner was Head Shliach of Australia for 50 years. As a student at
770 during the 1940s, he organized a children’s parade during the Intermediate Days of
Passover.

6198138.title: “Joyful Mother of Children”
6198138.description:
A new couple had moved in next door to the Kazens in Cleveland, Ohio. Little did they know,
miracles were about to happen...

6198139.title: A Very Jewish Enterprise
6198139.description:
In the early 1950s, Mr. Sheldon Rudoff brought a group of teenagers from the Young Israel of
Crown Heights for a private audience with the Rebbe.

6198142.title: Humor and Wit
6198142.description:
On occasion during the 1950s, Rabbi Yisroel Gordon served as the Rebbe’s driver. He recalls
some of the wit and humor that he witnessed.

6198143.title: Birthday Quiz
6198143.description:
Rabbi Mordechai Ashkenazi is rabbi of Kfar Chabad, Israel. In the Spring of 1958, around the
time of his 15th birthday, he had his first private audience with the Rebbe.

6198144.title: Term Paper: The Chassidic Society
6198144.description:
In 1972, Mrs. Chana Sharfstein wrote a term paper about the Lubavitch movement for her
sociology class at Brooklyn College. After receiving an A, she gave it to the Rebbe, who
returned it to her with two pages of corrections in his own handwriting.

6198145.title: The Term Paper: Autobiographical Notes
6198145.description:
In 1972, Mrs. Chana Sharfstein wrote a term paper about the Lubavitch movement for her
sociology class at Brooklyn College. After receiving an A, she gave it to the Rebbe, who
returned it to her with two pages of corrections in his own handwriting.

6198147.title: From Brooklyn to Cairo
6198147.description:
Mr. Yisroel Katzover is a senior journalist who covered the IDF for several decades for
numerous Israeli newspapers and media channels. Through the years, he consulted and
received much advice and guidance from the Rebbe.

6198148.title: A Sun Sets, A Sun Rises
6198148.description:
For 42 years, Rabbi Yoel Kahan led the team of scholars who memorized and transcribed the
Rebbe’s addresses. He arrived in New York from Israel to study at 770, right after the
passing of the Previous Rebbe.
path: A Sun Sets, A Sun Rises

6198149.title: Turning the Wheels
6198149.description:
Mr. Efraim Ilin was born in Kharkov, Ukraine in 1912. In 1951, he built Israel’s first automobile
assembly plant, Kaiser-Frazer of Israel.

6198150.title: 16 Years
6198150.description:
A special film in honor of the Rebbe’s 16th Yahrzeit, and highlighting his instruction that all
Jews record and publish their memoirs about the Rebbes and the Chassidim of generations
past.

6198175.title: Torah Education in Israel
6198175.description:
Rabbi Menachem Porush was born in Jerusalem in 1916. A seventh-generation Jerusalemite,
he devoted his life to championing Torah values and Torah education in Israel.
A story about the Previous Rebbe, Rabbi Yosef Yitzchak of Lubavitch.

6198176.title: The Kollel Student, Part 1
6198176.description: Rabbi Chaim Brovender was founder and Rosh Yeshiva of Yeshivat Hamivtar in Efrat, Israel. As a young, non-Chassidic, Kollel student in Jerusalem during the late 1960s, he and his wife had a private audience with the Rebbe.

6198177.title: The Kollel Student, Part 2
6198177.description: Rabbi Chaim Brovender is founder and Rosh Yeshiva of Yeshivat Hamivtar in Efrat, Israel. As a young, non-Chassidic, Kollel student in Jerusalem during the late 1960s, he and his wife had a private audience with the Rebbe.

6198179.title: The “Art” of Jewish Outreach
6198179.description:
Mr. Rafael Nouril is an acclaimed Jewish artist. The Rebbe encouraged him on numerous
occasions to spread Judaism through his art.

6198180.title: When G-d Sends a Curveball
6198180.description: When Mr. Bentzion Rader came to the Rebbe seeking advice concerning a serious and complex business problem he was facing, he got down-to-earth counsel as well as spiritual advice.

6198181.title: The 4:00 AM Jew
6198181.description:
Rabbi Mendel Baumgarten was a student at 770 during the 1940s. He was 17 years old in
1944 when the Rebbe’s father, Rabbi Levi Yitzchak, passed away in Soviet-imposed exile.

6198184.title: The Man with the Information
6198184.description:
In 1956, Rabbi David Hollander became one of the first American rabbis to visit the Soviet
Union. On that visit, and on each of his many subsequent visits, he would come to be briefed
by the Rebbe before leaving, and would report back to him upon his return.

6198188.title: Rabbinic Ordination
6198188.description:
Rabbi Yechiel Yaakov Weinberg, author of the Halachic work Sridei Eish, served as director of
the Hildesheimer Rabbinical Seminary in Berlin from 1924 to 1938.
After the war, he opened a Yeshiva in Montreux, Switzerland. Rabbi Gershon Mendel Garelik,
the Rebbe’s Shliach to Milan, Italy was invited to speak at the Yeshiva's opening ceremony.
Before travelling to the ceremony, the Rebbe gave Rabbi Garelik specific guidance.

6198189.title: Two Lions
6198189.description:
Rabbi Avrohom Pinter’s father, Rabbi Pinchas Pinter, was a recognized Torah scholar who
studied at the same time as the Rebbe with the famous Torah Sage, Rabbi Chaim Heller.

6198191.title: “I Think His Name is Schneerson”
6198191.description:
In 1940, along with thousands of other Jewish refugees fleeing the Nazi advance into
Belgium, Reb Aharon Noach Blasbalg and his family escaped to Southern France.

6198193.title: My Chassid, the Lawyer
6198193.description:
After earning his law degree, Mr. Bentzion Bernstein decided to change his career plans and
go into Jewish education instead. But the Rebbe had other plans for him… (1961)

6198194.title: It’s in G-d’s Hands
6198194.description:
Dr. Avraham Lorber was training at Guy’s Hospital in London, England, when a young baby
was brought in with a severe congenital heart defect. After the medical team recommended
immediate surgery, the family flew to New York to see the Rebbe for a second opinion (mid-1980's).

6198196.title: “He Thinks I Don’t Know”
6198196.description:
Reb Hirshel Chitrik used to visit the Rebbe’s mother, Rebbetzin Chana, after she moved to
New York. On one occasion, Rebbetzin Chana let Reb Hirshel in on a little family secret (early 1960s).

6198197.title: To Israel’s Labor Party, With Love
6198197.description:
Rabbi Menachem Hacohen served as a member in Israel’s Knesset for 15 years. At the time
of his first private audience with the Rebbe in 1959, he was serving as Rabbi of Israel’s
Moshav settlement movement, Rabbi and executive member of the Israeli Trade Union, and
Chief Editor of Machanayim, the official publication of the IDF Rabbinate.
path: To Israel’s Labor Party, With Love

6198198.title: New Blood
6198198.description:
Rabbi Dovid Edelman is the Rebbe’s Shliach in Springfield, Massachusetts since 1950. During
Hakafos at 770 on Simchas Torah 1973, he was standing right beside the Rebbe and was
privy to a converation between the Rebbe and an Israeli military representative.

6198199.title: Faith and Reason: Evolution
6198199.description:
Rabbi Dr. Moshe Tendler is a senior Rosh Yeshiva and a professor of biology and of medical
ethics at Yeshiva University in New York. He shares from his encounter with the Rebbe in 1970.

6198202.title: Who Knows Who
6198202.description:
Dr. Yitzchak Block is Emeritus Professor of Philosophy at the University of Western Ontario.
He earned his PhD in Greek Philosophy at Harvard University in 1958.
In his book, however, it was the Rebbe who made him a “great philosopher.”

6198203.title: Incognito
6198203.description:
Rabbi Mottel Zajac studied at 770 from 1950 to 1956. He recalls some fascinating anecdotes
about some of the Rebbe’s attempts to ‘hide himself’ from the public eye.

6198204.title: The Chicken Race
6198204.description:
In 1945, the Previous Rebbe appointed Rabbi Hershel Fogelman to head Chabad’s Hebrew Day
School in Worcester, Massachusetts. A few years later, when adversaries challenged
Chabad’s presence there, he turned to the Rebbe for advice.

6198205.title: Heart to Heart
6198205.description:
In 1961, Rabbi Shmuel Lew spent a Shabbos with the university students at Penn State. One
of the students had plans to marry a non-Jewish girl. A few weeks later, the student had a
heart-to-heart talk with the Rebbe.

6198208.title: Condensed Matter
6198208.description: Rabbi Adin Even-Yisrael Steinsaltz is a world-renowned Jewish scholar. Here, he shares some of the Rebbe’s guidance to him in his own life’s work.

6198212.title: Turn Up the Light
6198212.description:
Len Weksler was a 22 year-old college student when he had a private audience with the
Rebbe in 1952. His career aspirations — and the Rebbe’s — were the topic of discussion.

6198213.title: Texas Minds
6198213.description:
In 1972, the Rebbe sent Rabbi Shimon Lazaroff on Shlichus to Houston, Texas. A year later,
he brought his first group of Jewish-Texan college students to the Rebbe — in cowboy hats!

6198215.title: The Rebbe on Extremism Among Arab Youth
6198215.description:
Motti Eden is director of Israel’s Channel One television. In 1980, while working as a
broadcast journalist for Kol Yisrael Israeli radio, he had a private audience with the Rebbe,
which he recorded and later broadcast on Kol Yisrael.
path: The Rebbe on Extremism Among Arab Youth

6198216.title: If I Forget Thee, Oh Jerusalem…
6198216.description:
Geulah Cohen is a renowned journalist for the Israeli newspaper Maariv, who also served on
its editorial board from 1961 through 1973. In 1974, she was elected as a member of the
Knesset, where she served for five terms until 1992.
path: If I Forget Thee, Oh Jerusalem…

6198217.title: Journalism – A G-dly Mission
6198217.description:
Moshe Ishon served as a representative for Israel’s Jewish Agency in New York from 1977 to
1980. In 1981, he became the chief editor of the Israeli newspaper HaTzofe, a position which
he held until 1997.

6198223.title: “In All Your Ways, Know Him”
6198223.description:
During the 1940s, the Rebbe was instructed by his father-in-law, the Previous Rebbe, to Farbreng
every Shabbos Mevarchim. Rabbi Leibel Posner recalls two “out of the box” talks from that time.

6198224.title: Jewish Boys at the Front - Tour in Korea
6198224.description:
Mr. Bernard Cytryn arrived in the United States in 1946. Having been liberated from the
concentration camps by US soldiers, he wished to repay the kindness, and enlisted in the US
Army. Before shipping off to Korea in 1950, he had a private audience with the Rebbe (1950-1951.
path: Jewish Boys at the Front - Tour in Korea

6198225.title: Jewish Boys at the Front - Safe and Secure
6198225.description:
After meeting with the Rebbe in 1950, Private Bernard Cytryn shipped off to the Korean
warfront with his US Battalion. From there, he continued to correspond with the Rebbe.
path: Jewish Boys at the Front - Safe and Secure

6198226.title: The Physician’s Prayer
6198226.description: Dr. Ira Weiss served as the Rebbe’s chief cardiologist from 1977 to 1994.

6198230.title: Shlichus Dimensions - Part 1
6198230.description:
Mrs. Reba Sharfstein and her husband were sent by the Rebbe on Shlichus to Cincinnati, Ohio,
in 1954. Here, she discusses various instructions they received from the Rebbe.

6198231.title: Shlichus Dimensions - Part 2
6198231.description:
Mrs. Reba Sharfstein and her husband were sent by the Rebbe on Shlichus to Cincinnati,
Ohio, in 1954. Here, she discusses some advice the Rebbe gave her on being a mother.

6198233.title: On the Mark
6198233.description: Rabbi Raphael Pelcovitz shares a personal discussion he had with the Rebbe in the late 1950s.

6198235.title: Security from a Higher Source
6198235.description: Rabbi Binyomin Klein, a member of the Rebbe’s secretariat, tells the story behind an improptu talk of the Rebbe in 1990 on a global terrorist threat.

6198236.title: Drug War
6198236.description: The late 1970s saw the rise of drugs in Israel’s school system. Dr. Eliezer Shmueli served as Director General of Israel’s Ministry of Education at that time.

6198237.title: Something Is Funny Here
6198237.description:
Rabbi Pinchas Weberman, President of the Orthodox Rabbinical Council of South Florida, and
founder of congregation Ohev Shalom in Miami Beach, relates a “Baal Shemske Maaseh” (1967).

6198238.title: Love of Torah
6198238.description:
Rabbi Chaim Ciment studied at 770 in the late 1940s. He recalls some of his impressions of
the Rebbe from that time.

6198239.title: Mamish Geshmak!
6198239.description: Reb Ben Zion Shenker is a world-renowned composer of Jewish music. He first heard about the Rebbe during the 1940s, while studying in Beis Medrash at Yeshiva Torah Vodaas.

6198244.title: Matters of Principle - Part 1
6198244.description:
Rabbi Hershel Feigelstock served as principal of the Lubavitch Yeshiva in Montreal for forty
years. He recalls a time when he was on the verge of calling it quits...

6198246.title: Matters of Principle: Through Children’s Eyes
6198246.description:
Rabbi Hershel Feigelstock served as principal of the Lubavitch Yeshiva in Montreal for forty
years. In 1960, he began to take the High School students to New York once a year for a
private audience with the Rebbe.
path: Matters of Principle: Through Children’s Eyes

6198247.title: What a Rebbe Is
6198247.description: For many years, Rabbi Tzvi Greenwald worked at the “Chasam Sofer Home for Boys,” under its Director, Rabbi Akiva Sofer. Rabbi Sofer once shared a story with the boys about an encounter he had with the fifth Lubavitcher Rebbe, Rabbi Sholom Dovber.

6198249.title: Birthday Observance
6198249.description: As a student, Rabbi Sholom Chaskind was present at the Rebbe’s first “birthday Maamar” (1952).

6198250.title: The Four Answers
6198250.description: On Passover night, before conducting his own Seder, the Rebbe would visit the Seders at a number of educational institutions in Crown Heights. Rabbi Moshe and Mindy Feller, Shluchim to Minnesota, would lead the Seder at the Machon Chana Yeshiva for Women (circa 1978).

6198252.title: No-Brainer
6198252.description:
Reb Chaim Meir Minkowitz of Montreal recalls some surprising business advice he and his
wife received from the Rebbe, and how it helped spell their success (1958).

6198256.title: We Need Justice!
6198256.description: Renowned Nazi-hunter Tuvia Friedman reveals the Rebbe’s role in his life’s work (circa 1970).

6198258.title: The Real Maimonides
6198258.description: Rabbi Marvin Tokayer is a prolific writer and speaker. As a young college student in 1960, he came to the Rebbe to discuss some of his theological questions (1960).

6198261.title: Scholar in Residence: Exchanging Kabbalah for Alef-Beis
6198261.description: Over the course of the Rebbe’s three-month stay in Paris, he was asked to speak publicly on numerous occasions. Rabbi Nachum Avraham Yakobovitch was 20 years old at the time, and was present at a number of these events (1947).
path: Scholar in Residence: Exchanging Kabbalah for Alef-Beis

6198263.title: Scholar in Residence: “A Waterfall of Torah!”
6198263.description: Rabbi Nachum Avraham Yakobovitch continues his account of the the Rebbe’s public addresses in Paris in 1947.
path: Scholar in Residence: “A Waterfall of Torah!”

6198264.title: Drawing with the Rebbe
6198264.description: In 1959, Mrs. Esther Mentz brought her toddler to a private audience she had with the Rebbe. When the child could not be made to sit quietly, the Rebbe took matters into his own hands.

6198268.title: Speechless
6198268.description: Around 1970, a young teenage girl who had inexplicably lost her voice emerged from the Rebbe’s room speaking again! Now a healthy mother of eleven, she tells “the rest of the story.”

6198270.title: If You Could Have Anything in the Whole World…
6198270.description: Rabbi Yitzchok Meir Gurary is Mashpiya of the Lubavitcher Yeshiva in Montreal. His father, Rabbi Zalman Gurary, a devoted Chassid and financial supporter of the Rebbe’s work, once made a deal with the Rebbe that he could ask for a blessing in anything he wanted...(circa 1959)
path: If You Could Have Anything in the Whole World…

6198275.title: Sweet Deal
6198275.description: Mr. David Mintz is founder and Chief Executive Officer of Toffuti. He shares one of many occasions when the Rebbe literally saved his business (circa 1987).

6198278.title: Be a Man
6198278.description: In the summer of 1968, Rabbi Moshe Feller was invited to be a visiting scholar at Bnai Brith’s Youth Leadership camp in Pennsylvania. When some of the teenagers asked him to Farbreng with them in honor of Yud Beis Tammuz, he reluctantly agreed, giving up his chance to enjoy the Rebbe’s Farbrengen in New York. Or so he thought...

6198279.title: Kostroma
6198279.description: In 1927, the communist authorities sentenced Rabbi Yosef Yitzchak of Lubavitch to exile in Kostroma, a small city over 400 miles away from his headquarters in Leningrad. During his time there, he stayed with the family of the local Shochet, Reb Yerachmiel Kugel.

6198280.title: Religion and Politics
6198280.description: Dr. David Luchins is Chair of Political Science at Touro College. For 20 years he served on the staff of US Senator Daniel Patrick Moynihan, during which the Senator visited the Rebbe on several occasions.

6198281.title: Completely Unwarranted Love
6198281.description: The Sages teach that the Holy Temple was destroyed on account of unwarranted hatred, and will be rebuilt through unwarranted love. Rabbi Pinchas Weberman recalls a private audience in 1973 where the Rebbe explained just how literal this teaching is.

6198282.title: All for the Cause
6198282.description: In 1968, Mr. Moshe Salzberg founded a new Jewish elementary school in Montreal, Canada, despite the existence of a local Chabad school. What did the Rebbe think of that?

6198283.title: Don’t Worry, the Money will Come
6198283.description: In 1979, Mr. Chaim Bialik-Chacham was appointed senior aide to Israel’s Minister of Finance. While on assignment in New York, he got an out-of-the-blue phone call that the Rebbe wished to see him.
path: Don’t Worry, the Money will Come

6198284.title: Light at the End of the Tunnel
6198284.description: Mr. Murray Dalfen recalls how the Rebbe’s words got him through some of the darkest financial moments of his career (1989).
path: Light at the End of the Tunnel

6198285.title: Reb Yitzchok the Schochet
6198285.description: Rabbi Mordechai Goldschmid’s father, Reb Nochum, grew up with the Rebbe in Dniepropetrovsk, Ukraine. His grandfather, Reb Yitzchok, was the local Shochet.

6198286.title: “Where were you?!”
6198286.description: After giving birth to triplets prematurely, Mrs. Esther Glauberson and her parents waited helplessly while the newborns’ lives hung in the balance. In the middle of it all, her mother suddenly vanished into thin air…

6198288.title: The Logic of Joy
6198288.description: The importance of joy in one’s life and in one’s G-dly service is central to Chassidic teaching. In one of his private meetings with the Rebbe (in 1961), Mr. Bentzion Bernstein asked how such joy was humanly possible.

6198289.title: Testing the Waters
6198289.description: In 1956, Rabbi Eitan Greene had a two hour audience with the Rebbe, in which he asked many questions on Talmud and Jewish philosophy.

6198291.title: Baba Sali Stories
6198291.description: Rabbi Machluf Krispin is married to the granddaughter of the Moroccan Torah sage, Rabbi Yisrael Abuchatzeira, famously known as “Baba Sali.” At his first private audience with the Rebbe, he related a fascinating story of his grandfather.

6198293.title: A Higher Network
6198293.description: In 1987, Mr. Jerry Levine was working as an anchorman for Miami’s Channel 10 News when he was asked to get involved in Chabad’s outreach activities. When he wrote the Rebbe to ask his guidance on the matter, the response he got back seemed somewhat . . . silly.

6198295.title: “Someone’s Praying for Him”
6198295.description: Rabbi Shabsi Alpern is a senior Shliach in Brazil. In 1976, a member of his community funded the building of a new synagogue and Mikveh, after which he suffered a serious accident...

6198296.title: Picking the Rebbe’s Lulav
6198296.description: For many years, Rabbi Yitzchak Maier Gurary and his father-in-law, Rabbi Mordechai Altein, would provide the Four Species to the Rebbe for Sukkos.

6198299.title: G-d-Given Talents
6198299.description: At the time Avraham Zigman was starting out on the path of Teshuva, he was working as a music radio host. He consulted the Rebbe as to what his next step on the path should be (1979).

6198312.title: What Did They Teach You?!
6198312.description: Rabbi Mottel Zajac grew up in Brazil. In 1947, he was sent to New York to study at the Lubavitcher Yeshiva in Crown Heights, and later at 770 (from an encounter with the Rebbe in 1960).

6198313.title: Vote of Confidence
6198313.description: Born into a secular Jewish family, Rabbi Michoel Kanterovitz returned to Judaism on his own at the age of 7. Over the course of his rabbinic career, he served Jewish communities in Canada, England and Australia. But it was the Rebbe who got him his first rabbinic post (1967).

6198314.title: Healing Light
6198314.description: A miraculous account of the power of the Shabbos lights (1957).

6198315.title: “There Are No Jews in Madagascar”
6198315.description: Rabbi Yosef Wineberg worked for the central Lubavitcher Yeshiva, and traveled on numerous missions for the Previous Rebbe and the Rebbe over his 60 years of service. In 1955, the Rebbe asked him to visit Madagascar in search of fellow Jews.

6198316.title: Tools of the Trade
6198316.description: Before setting out to their post as the Rebbe’s Shluchim to the state of Minnesota in 1962, Rabbi Moshe Feller and his wife, Mindy, had a private audience with the Rebbe.

6198317.title: Chasidus for Kids
6198317.description: Rabbi Mordechai Goldschmid’s father, Reb Nochum, grew up with the Rebbe and his brothers in Dnepropetrovsk, Ukraine (circa 1917).

6198318.title: Perceiving the Roots
6198318.description: Rabbi Binyomin Klein was a member of the Rebbe’s secretariat for 30 years. He shares two stories of the Rebbe’s unique ability to see to the root of things.

6198319.title: On the Borderline
6198319.description:
Rabbi Meir Schlesinger is the founder of Yeshivat Sha’alvim in Israel, where he served as Rosh
Yeshiva for over 30 years (reflections from the 1960s).

6198322.title: Look for the Unifying Force
6198322.description: Rabbi Shmuel Lew recalls a simple, yet powerful, formula for Jewish unity, taught to him by the Rebbe (in the year 1974).

6198323.title: Torah to the People
6198323.description: Rabbi Meir Wunder was a senior librarian at Hebrew University’s National Library. During the 1960s, he managed the extensive Torah library at the Ponevezh Yeshiva in Bnei Brak, which inspired him to help found a central organization for Torah libraries (from a 1970 encounter).

6198324.title: The Rebbe Discusses Israeli Aviation
6198324.description: In 1977, while training in the United States together with a group of fellow IAF pilots, Mr. Herzl Makov visited the Rebbe.

6198327.title: Once a Leader, Always a Leader
6198327.description: Israeli Major-General Yehoshua Sagi served as director of AMAN, Israel’s Military Intelligence, from 1979 to 1983. His first audience with the Rebbe took place in the early 1980s.
path: Once a Leader, Always a Leader

6198328.title: Rabbeinu Tam Tefillin
6198328.description: Rabbi Leibel Schapiro is Rosh Yeshiva of the Yeshiva Gedolah of Miami. He recalls some of the Rebbe’s special instructions to him when he first started to don Rabbeinu Tam Tefillin (in 1965).

6198330.title: Never Give Up On a G-dly Spark
6198330.description: Professor Reuven Feuerstein, a world-renowned Israeli clinical and developmental cognitive psychologist, discusses some of the Rebbe’s influence on his life’s work.
path: Never Give Up On a G-dly Spark

6198331.title: Plant Your Vineyard
6198331.description: Rabbi Nachman Bernhard served the largest Jewish congregation in South Africa for over three decades. Before taking the job, he had actually planned to leave the rabbinate. That was when he had his first private audience with the Rebbe…(in the year 1964)

6198333.title: The Jewish Performing Arts
6198333.description: Mrs. Leah Gniwisch lives in Montreal, Canada. Each year from 1963 to 1974, she directed a Jewish musical for the women and girls of the community.

6198403.title: Secret Weapon
6198403.description: Rabbi David Bouskila translated the Tanya into Arabic thinking that he would enable Jews from Arabic-speaking countries to learn about G-d. Little did he know, he was stepping into the middle of an age-old cosmic battle and turning the tides of the war... (1980)

6198404.title: To Be Connected
6198404.description: In the early 1970s, Rabbi Meir Tzvi Gruzman sought the Rebbe’s advice on motivating the students of his Tomchei Temimim Yeshiva in their study of Talmud.

6198405.title: So Far, Yet So Close
6198405.description: Rabbi Shmuel Chefer, director of the Beis Rivkah Teachers’ Seminary in Kfar Chabad, Israel, recounts a heartwarming story about what it truly means to be “close” to the Rebbe (1968).

6198406.title: Returning a Lost Art
6198406.description:
In 1964, Baruch Nachshon had his first private audience with the Rebbe. An aspiring artist
who had recently returned to his Jewish roots, the Rebbe commissioned him with the historic
task of reviving an ancient “art form.”

6198407.title: Hiding and Seeking
6198407.description:
Reb Chonye Morosow served as a personal secretary to the fifth and sixth Lubavitcher Rebbes
in Russia. His son, Reb Mendel, was born in 1916, and recalls two episodes in the Rebbes’
homes.

6198409.title: Working Through Others
6198409.description: Rabbi Don Yoel Levy is director of the OK Kosher Certification. During the early 1960s, his father, Rabbi Berel Levy, was privy to the Rebbe’s methods of working with other Jewish movements.

6198410.title: How the Rebbe Bought Us Passover Dishes
6198410.description: Where is a young couple to turn when they can’t afford their Passover expenses? Mrs. Esther Mentz tells a heartwarming story of kindness and sensitivity (in the year 1957).
path: How the Rebbe Bought Us Passover Dishes

6198411.title: Balanced Rebuke
6198411.description: Rabbi Yisroel Gordon’s father, Reb Yochanan Gordon, studied at the Tomchei Temimim Yeshiva in Lubavitch, Russia, in the early 1910s. His father would recall an insightful lesson he was taught by the Yeshiva’s director, the future Sixth Rebbe, Rabbi Yosef Yitzchak (circa 1912).

6198426.title: We Checked Already!
6198426.description: What does it mean when the Rebbe gives you the same advice three times in a row? And how many times must you check your Mezuzos anyway? (1992)

6198427.title: The Highest Calling
6198427.description: Rabbi Avraham Leizerson is chairman of Chinuch Atzmai, the independent religious education system in Israel (1992).

6198432.title: The Joy of Children, Part 1
6198432.description: Just three days before her wedding, a bride declares her wishes to call off the marriage... (circa 1957)

6198433.title: The Joy of Children, Part 2
6198433.description: The doctors promised her she would never have a single child. The Rebbe promised her she would have many! (circa 1957)

6198434.title: Judaism in Color
6198434.description: In 1973, Mr. David Stauber accompanied his wife and father-in-law to an audience with the Rebbe. Although he thought he had no personal interest in the meeting, he came out a new Jew.

6198435.title: Healthy Soul, Healthy Body
6198435.description: Rabbi Yekusiel Farkash is a prominent halachic authority living in Jerusalem, Israel. An amazing story of how the Rebbe’s advice saved his doctor-friend’s wife from fatal illness, through a change of diet (circa 1975).

6198436.title: Healthy Soul, Healthy Body
6198436.description: Rabbi Yekusiel Farkash relates a sequel to the story of his friend’s wife’s miraculous healing (circa late-1970s).

6198437.title: Ten Hour Flight, One Hour Mission
6198437.description: Rabbi Israel Haber, a decorated former U.S. Air Force chaplain, was stationed in Alaska during the 1970s. In 1980, two years after making aliyah with his family, the Rebbe asked him to visit Alaska again, “at least for one hour.” (circa 1980)
path: Ten Hour Flight, One Hour Mission

6198438.title: The Shlichus Will Find You
6198438.description: Rabbi Yitzchok Sufrin is an administrator of the Lubavitch Foundation in the United Kingdom. His dream, however, was to be a Shliach, battling on the front lines for Yiddishkeit...

6198439.title: A Shabbos Afternoon in Mexico
6198439.description: Professor Shlomo Eckstein is the former President and Rector of Bar Ilan University in Tel Aviv. He shares an insight the Rebbe gave him in his youth, which he has carried with him throughout his lifelong career in education (circa 1953).

6198440.title: The Basics
6198440.description: With all the complex challenges of life, it’s easy to search for complex solutions, overlooking the basics of success. Reb Aaron Dalfin shares two illuminating interactions with the Rebbe (the early 1960's)

6198441.title: Leningrad On the Line
6198441.description:
Professor Herman Branover is a world-renowned physicist. Living as a refusnik in Leningrad in
1972, he found the phone number to 770 in the inside page of a Jewish prayer book...(circa 1972)

6198442.title: A Visit to the Sick
6198442.description: Rabbi Nissen Mangel recalls a story about his father-in-law, to whom the Rebbe paid a personal visit in the hospital (circa early-1970's)

6198443.title: Jewish Nationalism
6198443.description: An excerpt from a recently discovered 1969 recording of Prime Minister Ariel Sharon describing his second private audience with the Rebbe.

6198444.title: Mezuzah Delivery
6198444.description: Reb Chaim Meir and Faige Minkowitz recall the tribulations of her four-day labor, and the Rebbe’s unorthodox “medical” advice (circa 1952).

6198445.title: A Symbiotic People
6198445.description: Yitzchak Rabin served as Israel’s ambassador to the United States from 1968 to 1973. In 1972, Ambassador Yehuda Avner accompanied Rabin to pay Israel’s respects to the Rebbe in honor of his 70th birthday.

6198446.title: You Will Survive
6198446.description: Mr. Israel Adamski grew up in Dniepropetrovsk, Ukraine, and attended underground Torah classes taught by the Rebbe’s father, Rabbi Levi Yitzchok Schneerson. Here, he recalls Reb Levik’s prophetic words to him shortly before the outbreak of World War II.

6198448.title: The Place Where All Worries Melt
6198448.description: Mrs. Rochel Pinson, head Shlucha of Tunisia since 1960, recalls how the Rebbe was sometimes the lone source of calm amidst the challenges.
path: The Place Where All Worries Melt

6198449.title: Quantity is Quality
6198449.description: Rabbi Shmuel Chefer, director of the Beis Rivkah Teachers’ Seminary in Kfar Chabad, Israel, shares a fundamental perspective of the Rebbe on building a successful educational institution (circa 1960).

6198452.title: The Soul Hears
6198452.description:
uring the 1980s, renowned podiatrist Dr. Elliot Udell would treat the Rebbe and Rebbetzin at
their home on President Street. One time, he shared with the Rebbe an experience he had of
a Chabad Shliach’s outreach efforts, which he expected would displease the Rebbe...(late 1980s)

6198455.title: 200 Years of Hindsight
6198455.description: Detractors to chasidism still point to the Vilna Gaon’s opposition as the basis upon which they rely. But would the Vilna Gaon count himself among them today? (from a 1963 encounter)

6198456.title: L’chaim, To a Healthy Birth!
6198456.description: When the doctors keep threatening that the baby will be born with a defect, it’s hard not to be terrified, even with the Rebbe’s assurances again, and again, and again, and again... Miriam Haber shares her personal story.

6198457.title: By the Grace of G-d
6198457.description: The importance of two little letters at the top of every page (circa 1967).

6198458.title: Rosh Hashanah Heirloom
6198458.description: Rabbi Leibel Raskin shares several heartwarming anecdotes from his family’s interactions with the Rebbe’s mother, Rebbetzin Chana Schneerson, of blessed memory.

6198459.title: Why the Rebbe Snuck Over the Wartime Border
6198459.description: Rabbi Menachem Teichtel was a refugee student in Vichy France during the war. He recounts just how far the Rebbe was willing to go to uphold a Jewish custom during wartime (circa 1940).
path: Why the Rebbe Snuck Over the Wartime Border

6198460.title: At the Rebbe’s Table
6198460.description: Rabbi Tuvia Blau is a renowned author and educator. In 1967, he managed to work his way into the Previous Rebbe’s apartment upstairs at 770, and observe the Rebbe’s Simchas Torah meal with the elder Chasidim.

6198461.title: Extended Family
6198461.description: Rabbi Dr. Israel Drazin served for over three decades as Assistant Chief of Chaplains of the US Army. The Rebbe taught him that being a Jewish chaplain is not only about ministering to Jews (circa 1986).

6198462.title: Of Love and Marriage
6198462.description: Reb Sholom Goldshmid was a student at 770 during the late 1940s and early 1950s. When it came time to start thinking about dating and marriage, it was the Rebbe who gave him the most important advice of all (c. 1951).

6198463.title: Prognosis: Positive
6198463.description: When it’s three doctors against one rabbi, who would you believe? (1973)

6198464.title: Be Sensitive to the Other
6198464.description: When Mrs. Sarah Karmely chose to return to Jewish observance, her husband was resistant. She turned to the Rebbe for guidance (Mid 1980s).

6198465.title: The Missing Farewell
6198465.description: Rabbi Shabsi Alpern and his wife were among the first to answer the Rebbe’s call to leave Crown Heights for lifelong Shlichus in far-off lands. But when they stopped at 770 on their way to the airport, the Rebbe didn’t show up to say good-bye... (1961)

6198466.title: Source of Healing
6198466.description: During Shemini Atzeres hakafos in 1977, the Rebbe suffered a massive heart attack. Dr. Moshe Feldman was a member of the medical team that treated the Rebbe at 770.

6198467.title: On a Tight Schedule
6198467.description: “Knock, knock.” “Who’s there?” “Tefillin delivery from the Lubavitcher Rebbe.” (1961)

6198468.title: The Answer with No Question
6198468.description:
Rabbi Tuvia Blau, a prominent Chabad Chasid, was born into a family of distinguished nonchasidic
origins. After discovering Chabad Chasidism as a student in yeshiva, he wrote to the Rebbe asking for clarification on a number of theological questions. In his response, the Rebbe added the answer to a question Tuvia hadn’t even asked – which turned out to be perhaps the most important answer of all.

6198469.title: Chanukah in July 1979
6198469.description: During the first summer of the Iranian Hostage Crisis, Chief Rabbi of Mexico Abraham Hershberg was selected by the United Nations to visit the Jewish hostages. Before leaving, the Rebbe gave him an important instruction: “Be sure to light the Chanukah menorah with them.”

6198471.title: The Decree is Over, Part I
6198471.description: After a horrific car accident, three-and-a-half year old Yaacov Orimland was left in a coma, with doctors giving him just hours to live. His father, Reb Gimpel, turned to the Rebbe for advice and a blessing (1963).
path: The Decree is Over, Part I

6198472.title: The Decree is Over, Part II
6198472.description: Part two of last week’s incredible story...
path: The Decree is Over, Part II

6198473.title: On the Front Line
6198473.description: During the 1982 Lebanon War, Rabbi Aharon Eliezer Ceitlin was part of a group of Chasidim instructed by the Rebbe to print the Tanya in various Lebanese cities — including the capital, Beirut, itself.

6198474.title: Chasid in Camouflage
6198474.description:
Rabbi Benjamin Blech is a world-renowned Modern Orthodox author and lecturer, and a professor of Talmud at Yeshiva University in New York.
One day, he received a surprising phone call from Chabad world headquarters...

6198782.title: A Few Blocks Away
6198782.description: Rabbi Herschel Feigelstock, an elder Chasid of the Montreal Lubavitcher community, recalls details of the Previous Rebbe’s funeral in the winter of 1950 and instructions he received from the Rebbe concerning the mourning and the visitation to the Previous Rebbe’s resting place.

6198783.title: Seeing is Believing
6198783.description: Rabbi Yitzchak Dovid Grossman is a recipient of the Israel Prize, his country’s highest honor. In 1985, his daughter developed a severe eye condition that confounded all the experts... The Rebbe’s diagnosis: “Check the mezuzahs.”

6198784.title: How Are You?
6198784.description: As an Israeli college student studying in London, England, Mrs. Orah Jurawel befriended a local Chabad family. When she subsequently traveled to visit New York, they asked her for a small favor: to deliver a gift to the Rebbe’s wife, Rebbetzin Chaya Mushka. (1974)

6198785.title: Gas Mask in the Yom Kippur War
6198785.description: During the Yom Kippur War, Reb Efraim Mol was stationed at Israel’s southern border with Sinai, when intelligence came in about a possible imminent chemical attack by the Egyptians. Ordered to shave his beard in preparation to don a gask mask, Efraim convinced his superiors to allow him to consult the Rebbe first.
path: Gas Mask in the Yom Kippur War

6198786.title: Risky Business
6198786.description: In 1962, the Rebbe’s warning to Meyer Zajac to stay away from stock market investing saved him from enormous losses. A decade later, after buying $100,000 worth of shares as a favor to a friend, his portfolio fell by 95% to $5,000! Meyer flew to New York to see the Rebbe...

6198787.title: Keep It Simple
6198787.description: Expecting for the first time, Dr. and Mrs. David Lazerson requested a blessing from the Rebbe to raise their child to be a “G-d-fearing, righteous, scholarly, Chasid.” The Rebbe’s response on how to achieve this was a little simpler than they’d expected (1973).

6198789.title: Our Friend, the Grand Rebbe
6198789.description: New York City councilman James E. Davis, rest in peace, founded the non-profit organization, Love Yourself, Stop the Violence, dedicated to halting inner city gun crime and drug abuse. His brother, Geoffrey Davis, retells the original inspiration behind his brother’s life work. (late-1970’s)

6198790.title: “They will be Successful”
6198790.description: Mr. Nash Kestenbaum, president of the National Council of Young Israel at the time of the Yom Kippur War, was instrumental in securing the Nixon Administration’s weapons airlift to Israel. His son, Dovid Kestenbaum, recalls his father’s interactions with the Rebbe at the time.

6198791.title: Special Delivery
6198791.description: Dr. Abraham Luchins was a world-renowned Orthodox Jewish psychologist who was close to both the Previous Rebbe and the Rebbe. When he was appointed by Washington to lead the American delegation to the World Psychology Convention in Moscow, the Rebbe tasked him with a secret mission.

6198794.title: A Timely Message
6198794.description: Reb Nochum Partzovitz, the beloved head of the Mirer Yeshivah in Jerusalem, had a private audience with the Rebbe in the early 1970s. His student, Rabbi Yosef Yitzchak Havlin, recounts the details of that meeting as related to him by Reb Nochum (1972).

6198795.title: Engine Trouble
6198795.description: For over sixty years, Rabbi Yosef Wineberg traveled the globe fundraising on behalf of the central Lubavitcher Yeshiva. The Rebbe would often entrust him with personal missions during these travels. A story out of the Jewish heart of Africa (1950s).

6198796.title: The Right Diagnosis
6198796.description: Shortly after becoming pregnant with their first child, Reb Meshulom Weiss’s wife was diagnosed with the rare Weber-Christian Disease. But even after the diagnosis was confirmed by a top expert in the field, the Rebbe insisted on his own ‘third opinion.’ (Late 1950s)

6198797.title: Bird’s Eye View
6198797.description: During the Yom Kippur War, Israeli fighter jets from 1967 faced cutting-edge Russian-made surface-to-air missiles. Shortly after the war, Israeli Air Force engineer Mr. Yitzchak Rappaport was sent to America on a mission to update the IDF’s technology for the future.

6198798.title: Keep Looking
6198798.description: Rabbi Mordechai Einbinder is a Chabad emissary in Tarzana, California. When one of his congregants was facing financial ruin, they wrote to the Rebbe in hope of a miracle. Following the Rebbe’s advice, the man discovered the solution to his problem in his own backyard... (Late-1980's)

6198799.title: Showing Appreciation
6198799.description: Rabbi Shneur Zalman Vilenkin served as the Rebbe’s childhood teacher in Yekaterinoslav (Dnepropetrovsk), Ukraine. Vilenkin’s grandson, Rabbi Yehudah Leib Schapiro, describes the extraordinary honor the Rebbe accorded his grandfather years later in New York.

6198800.title: Stories of Tzadikim
6198800.description: Mrs. Chana Arnold is a veteran educator. She recalls a simple instruction she received from the Rebbe, advising her how to instill love and respect of G-d in the hearts of children. (1977)

6198801.title: First Fruits in Brooklyn
6198801.description: Mr. Amram Malka served for a time as an assistant in the Rebbe’s household. One time, he was asked to assist in organizing the Rebbe’s office, and he came across a drawer with family pictures of Chasidim sent to the Rebbe from around the world. This gave Malka an idea...

6198802.title: The Bar Lev Line
6198802.description: Mr. Yisroel Katzover is senior military correspondent who covered the IDF for numerous Israeli newspapers and media channels. (year 1970)

6198806.title: A Practical Gift
6198806.description: Rabbi Zalman Aaron Grossbaum is executive director of Chabad Lubavitch of Ontario, Canada. He recalls the Rebbe’s advice for the “perfect gift” to present to Canada’s Prime Minister. (Early-1980s)

6198807.title: A 365-Day Jew
6198807.description: Mr. Dennis Eckstein grew up as what he calls a “three-day-a-year-Jew.” But twenty five years ago that changed, thanks to one thoughtful act of the Rebbe. (year: 1989)

6198808.title: Think of Me, and I’ll Think of You
6198808.description: Reb Mendel Futerfas, imprisoned in a Soviet gulag and unable to communicate with the outside world, composed a unique letter in his mind and “sent” it off to the Previous Rebbe. Reb Mendel’s wife was shocked to receive a letter from the Previous Rebbe in reply to her husband’s “telegram.”
path: Think of Me, and I’ll Think of You

6198810.title: For The Sake of Torah
6198810.description:
Rabbi Mayer Plotkin was a student in Yeshiva Torah Vodaas, when he heard a former faculty
member recount that the Previous Rebbe boldly kept the doors of the Yeshiva open during a
financial crisis in the late-1940s.

6198811.title: Don’t Give Up!
6198811.description: Rabbi Yaakov Biderman, director of Chabad-Lubavitch in Austria, discovered that he was not the first shliach to Vienna. Over two decades before his arrival, the Rebbe sent Mrs. Marguerite Chajes to pay a visit to Doctor Viktor Frankl, the founder of logo-therapy and author of Man’s Search for Meaning.

6198812.title: Sweet Medicine
6198812.description: Mrs. Rochel Fogelman led a group of women from Worcester, Massachusetts, on a visit to New York and to an audience with the Rebbe that went down in history. (year 1953)

6198813.title: Does the Rebbe Know You?
6198813.description: Rabbi Shimon Lazaroff, director of Chabad-Lubavitch of Texas, traveled to New York to resolve a personal issue. While there, he was astonished by the special attention he received from the Rebbe during a farbrengen, especially in light of preceding events. (1980s)

6198814.title: The Facts of Life
6198814.description: Mr. Yaakov Schiffman joined his family in an audience with the Rebbe when his father was terminally ill. The Rebbe proceeded to teach him a page of Talmud, and a lesson that changed his life. (1975)

6198815.title: Presidential Visit
6198815.description: Mr. Dan Patir served as advisor to several Israeli leaders. He accompanied President Shazar on a historic visit to the Rebbe in 1966.

6198817.title: A Jew Just Like You
6198817.description: Mr. Israel Adamski lived in Dnepropetrovsk, Ukraine, where Rabbi Levi Yitzchok Schneerson, the Rebbe’s father, served as rabbi. He recalls Rabbi Levi Yitzchok performing an underground wedding, and inviting a communist informant to be the tenth man. (Late 1930’s)

6198818.title: Lasting Impressions
6198818.description: Rabbi Norbert Weinberg was becoming despondent when all of his hard work as a Hebrew school principal was becoming undone by his students’ parents. Fortunately, the Rebbe cast a new light on the situation. (Late 1950s)

6198819.title: On Keeping Resolutions
6198819.description: As a student in yeshiva, Rabbi Yitzchok Meir Gurary received important guidance from the Rebbe. (Early 1950s)

6198820.title: "But Where Is G-d?"
6198820.description: Mr. Elliot Lasky had returned from a concert tour with a famous band when he experienced an unexpected spiritual awakening and began to reexamine his lost faith. (1973)

6198824.title: Letters to Camp Pickett
6198824.description: When Mr. Mendel Greenbaum was conscripted into the U.S. Armed Forces after the outbreak of the Korean War, he sought the Rebbe’s advice and began a correspondence. (1952)

6198829.title: Lost in Translation
6198829.description: After Mr. Naftali Deutsch financed the construction of a Jewish school, the Rebbe used the High Holiday prayer book to reassure Mr. Deutsch that he had made the best investment possible. (Late 1970s)

6198830.title: Urgent Message
6198830.description: A year after visiting an isolated group of Jews in Sweden, Rabbi Dovid Weitman discovered that the Rebbe did his own outreach, sending one of them an urgent telegram just a few days before Rosh Hashana. (1974)

6198832.title: A Promise Fulfilled, Part 1
6198832.description: Reb Gimpel Orimland took the Rebbe’s advice to move to Florida and take on a new business venture. When he later made a commitment to charity which he couldn’t afford, the Rebbe assured him he’d be able to give many times that amount the following year. (Late 1960s)

6198833.title: A Promise Fulfilled, Part 2
6198833.description: Almost a year had passed since the Rebbe had assured Reb Gimpel Orimland that he’d return to 770 and be able to give many times more than his previous pledge to charity. Several weeks before his return to 770, however, the fulfillment of the Rebbe’s blessing was yet to be seen. (Late 1960s)

6198836.title: Never Too Small
6198836.description: Rabbi Immanuel Schochet was a prominent scholar and author. On two occasions, he was surprised to discover just how much the Rebbe paid attention to the needs of his chasidim. The Rebbe seemed to keep track of even the very small ones.

6198837.title: Exceptional Soldiers
6198837.description: Mr. Yosef Lautenberg was injured in the battle for Jerusalem in 1948, and among the founders of the IDF Disabled Veterans Organization. In 1976 he led the Israeli delegation, made up in large part of injured IDF veterans, to the Paralympics in Toronto, and decided to bring the group to New York to visit with the Rebbe.

6198840.title: Waiting for an Answer
6198840.description:
Rabbi Boruch Zaichyk was serving as a rabbi in Johannesburg, South Africa, when a
congregant fell critically ill and called the Rebbe’s office for a blessing and advice. When an answer did not arrive, Rabbi Zaichyk decided to take matters into his own hands. (1970s)

6198841.title: Time for Ice Cream
6198841.description: When Rabbi Mordechai Gutnick was told by the Rebbe to enter the rabbinate, he sought to prepare himself through study and a rabbinic apprenticeship. Yet his greatest lesson lay in the Rebbe’s attitude to a request from a young girl. (1974)

6198844.title: All Shall Come to Know God
6198844.description:
Rabbi Chaim Druckman was a young man involved in the Bnei Akiva Youth Movement when the Rebbe told him that the main focus of the curriculum, even in formal schools, should be the fear of Heaven.
Many years later, the Rebbe added that the imperative to bring people closer to G-d applies not only to Jews, but to all mankind.
path: All Shall Come to Know God

6198846.title: What Happens When You Help Others
6198846.description: Rabbi Shlomo Riskin, rabbi of Efrat, Israel, comes to the Rebbe with a concern about one of his children and ends up with a life-lesson from the super-rational commandment of the red heifer. (1991)
path: What Happens When You Help Others

6198847.title: Tuned In
6198847.description: Standing amongst the crowd in 770, Mr. Michoel Hazan discovers the extent to which the Rebbe understands his personal situation – a yeshiva student from Gibraltar who wants to adopt Chabad customs. (Late 1970s)

6198848.title: Mandate for a Woman
6198848.description: Rabbi Yekusiel Farkash and his wife arrive for an audience with the Rebbe, but receive a private talk on the requirement for women to study chasidic teachings, with a special directive for Mrs. Farkash.

6198849.title: The Soul of Torah
6198849.description: Rabbi Nissen Mangel, a prominent author and scholar, was a yeshiva student in Montreal, Canada, when he brought a friend from a non-Chabad background to spend Shabbos in Crown Heights and have an audience with the Rebbe. (Late-1950s)

6198850.title: A Sure Cure
6198850.description: As a young child, Rabbi Psachya Korf arrived in an emergency room after a terrible house fire. Doctors scrambled to airlift him to a special treatment center and warned his parents that his prognosis was not too optimistic. That’s when his father, Rabbi Pinchas Korf, rushed to the Rebbe for a blessing. (1989)

6198851.title: A Sign of Things to Come
6198851.description: When Rabbi Moshe Weiss’ father would not give him the prayer book the Rebbe had sent him as a gift, he asked his teacher for paper and decided to write his own. The Rebbe saw this as a sign of things to come. (Late 1960’s)
path: A Sign of Things to Come

6198852.title: A Message from Tashkent
6198852.description: Rabbi Bentzion Vishedsky relates that when his sister was in the former USSR, her father in law, Reb Simcha Gorodetzky, was overjoyed to receive word from the Rebbe that she and her husband would soon be allowed to leave the Soviet Union. (1966)

6198853.title: Sensitivity in Code
6198853.description: When Mrs. Shulamis Saxon wrote a letter to the Rebbe just days before her bat mitzvah, instead of simply asking for a blessing, she decided that she would bless the Rebbe as well.

6198854.title: Name Him Yosef Yitzchak
6198854.description:
Dr. Yechiel Lasri is the mayor of Asdod, Israel, and a former member of the Knesset. After
his mother lost her first three children within hours of their being born, the family sought the
advice and blessing of the Rebbe.

6198855.title: How to Inspire a Generation
6198855.description: Upon accepting his first pulpit, Rabbi Sholom Ber Gordon consulted Rabbi Yosef Yitzchak Schneersohn, the sixth Lubavitcher Rebbe, on how to bring his new congregation to deepen their Jewish observance.

6198856.title: Feeling the Connection
6198856.description:
After having made numerous trips to New York to see the Rebbe, Rabbi Avrohom Michoel
Halpern, the rabbi of Givat Tzarfatit in Jerusalem, tells the Rebbe that he still feels no change
in their connection.

6198857.title: Making a Mess
6198857.description: On two separate occasions when their shlichus seemed in trouble, Rabbi Yossi Groner’s wife wrote to the Rebbe. When she received the Rebbe’s encouragement and experienced unanticipated outcomes, one of her congregants noticed and decided to try the same.

6198858.title: A Class of Their Own
6198858.description: When Mrs. Alice Zlotnick’s husband, Professor Dov Zlotnick, told the Rebbe about the success of his Talmud class in Riverdale, New York, he received an unexpected challenge, which he duly passed on to his wife.

6198859.title: The Chancellor of the Exchequer
6198859.description: Mr. Bentzion Rader, a registered accountant for almost forty years, was surprised to learn that the financial advice he gave to an acquaintance who wanted to increase his contributions to charity was vetoed by the Rebbe. As events unfolded, he realized that the Rebbe must have his own sources.

6198861.title: A Covert Operation
6198861.description: Shortly after Mrs. Ella Skoblo arrived in New York, she had an audience with the Rebbe. While she knew that her grandfather, Rabbi Yehuda Leib Levin, the Chief Rabbi of Moscow during the Soviet era, had met with the Rebbe during his visit in 1968, she was surprised to discover that he was also part of a covert operation orchestrated by the Rebbe.

6198862.title: The Rebbe’s Response on Sepharadim and Ashkenazim
6198862.description: Rabbi Hillel Zaltzman was active in the Soviet Jewish underground. When faced with hard times and tough decisions, he recalls secretly consulting his “zeide” in America. The word may simply mean “grandfather” in Yiddish, but to Rabbi Zaltzman and his comrades, it was the code name for “Rebbe.” (1960s)
path: The Rebbe’s Response on Sepharadim and Ashkenazim

6198864.title: A Needle in a Haystack, Part 1
6198864.description: Rabbi Pinchas Woolstone, who served as rabbi of the Jewish House Crisis Center in Sydney, Australia, was on a trip to New York when he was approached for assistance in finding a girl from Brooklyn who had run away to Australia. Not knowing where to start, Rabbi Woolstone decided on his first step: to consult the Rebbe. (1980s)
path: A Needle in a Haystack, Part 1

6198867.title: A Needle in a Haystack, Part 2
6198867.description: When the Rebbe instructed Rabbi Pinchas Woolstone to take a trip to Brisbane, Australia, he was unsure of what he was expected to do there. He set out on his mission anyway, and by the time he arrived, he knew exactly what had to be done. (1980s)
path: A Needle in a Haystack, Part 2

6198868.title: Seeing the Connection
6198868.description: Rabbi Zalman Sudakevitch was living in Paris when the Rebbe traveled to France to escort his mother to the United States, three years before he assumed leadership. He recalls meeting the Rebbe for the first time in the Rebbe’s hotel room, and learning a lesson about the connection of a chosid to his Rebbe. (1947)

6198870.title: Downfall of a Modern-Day Haman
6198870.description: Rabbi Yoel Kahn, a leading authority on Chabad Chasidic thought, recalls being present at a Purim farbrengen in 770 when the Rebbe told a very unusual story. But even more unusual, were the events which unfolded soon after. (1953)

6198871.title: Getting Out of Debt
6198871.description:
When the rand suddenly collapsed, Rabbi Nachman Bernhard recalls that Lubavitch Foundation of South Africa stood to lose the property which housed its growing school. After receiving an unsolicited message from the Rebbe, Rabbi Bernhard wasted no time in
putting the advice to use. (1980s)

6198872.title: A Mikvah for Whom?
6198872.description: Rabbi Moishe Engel was among the shluchim in Long Beach, California, who dreamt of opening a kosher store or starting a Hebrew school to help boost the community’s Jewish infrastructure. They were astonished when a call arrived from the Rebbe’s office with a blessing for a new mikvah. (1971)

6198873.title: Birthday Blessings
6198873.description: Rabbi Aron Eliezer Ceitlin would write monthly reports to the Rebbe when he was a senior yeshiva student in Tzefat, Israel. Approaching the month of Nissan, he decided to include a birthday blessing for the Rebbe in the name of the entire administration. Not knowing how his superiors would react, he sent off the report and hoped for the best. (1980)

6198874.title: Sensitivity at Midnight
6198874.description: Rabbi Yisroel Shmotkin, as a yeshiva student had the good fortune to attend the Rebbe’s seder for a number of years in the 1960s.

6198884.title: Permission Granted
6198884.description: While Professor Evsey Nemoytin served as dean of Kazakh State University, his parents ran an underground mikvah. In the 1970s, the Rebbe arranged their eventual exit from the Soviet Union. Professor Nemoytin recalls the Rebbe’s valuable advice, as well as his delight at learning that the Rebbe understood his field of research. (Includes footage filmed by Rabbi Berel Levy to be smuggled out to the Rebbe.)

6198888.title: A Special Year
6198888.description: Rabbi Shlomo Zarchi shares some recollections of 770, where he was a student in the mid- 1960s. He recalls the Rebbe’s mother’s passing in 1965, as well as one particular morning prayer that became seared into his memory.

6198889.title: Desperate Measures
6198889.description:
After Mrs. Leah Englander’s three year old son was rushed to the hospital, the doctors
informed her that the boy would be at least partially paralyzed for life.
When she contacted her brother, Dr. Levi Reiter for help, he was left with only one option to help his nephew: To ring the bell at the Rebbe’s home on President Street, in the middle of the night.

6198894.title: I Did My Part
6198894.description: Before her marriage, Mrs. Chana Arnold received a letter from the Rebbe outlining the rewards a woman receives for covering her hair with a wig. Six years later, Mrs. Arnold kept the Rebbe to his word.

6198895.title: Inscribed in a Book
6198895.description: When Rabbi Yosef Minkowitz suggested that a certain verse might have a connection to the Rebbe’s “Letter in the Torah Scroll” Campaign, he never expected the Rebbe’s reaction. At a subsequent rally for children, some heavenly force seems to have altered the weather forecast.

6198899.title: A Change of Heart
6198899.description: When Israel’s future President, Zalman Shazar, requested that Chabad send someone to assist the Israeli author Eliezer Steinman in writing about the movement, Rabbi Chanoch Glitzenstein approached the mission cautiously. Given the writer’s sacrilegious bent, Rabbi Glitzenstein decided to request the Rebbe’s advice.

6198900.title: A Timely Letter
6198900.description: When Rabbi Chanoch Glitzenstein discovered that his acquaintance, the Israeli author Eliezer Steinman, had fallen seriously ill, he sent an urgent telegram to the Rebbe requesting a blessing. To his surprise, no response was forthcoming.

6198905.title: A Triple Blessing
6198905.description: After five years of marriage and numerous visits to doctors, Yocheved and Yehuda Daphna were yet to have children. At the urging of a friend, they sought the Rebbe’s blessing..

6198906.title: Just the Person to Talk To
6198906.description: After Rabbi Dr. Tzvi Hersh Weinreb had earned his Ph.D. from the University of Maryland, he was faced with a variety of decisions that would shape the course of his life. Not knowing where to turn, he decided to place a call to the Rebbe. In the end, he received his counsel from a different person entirely.
path: Just the Person to Talk To

6198910.title: The Unforgotten Jew
6198910.description: When Mr. Yitzchok Nemes was about to travel to Guyana, the Rebbe gave him an extra dollar for charity “to pass on to a Jew living there.” Although he could not find any Jews in Guyana, Mr. Nemes took his mission very seriously, and did not give up until he delivered the dollar to its intended recipient. (Late 1980s)

6198911.title: Quiet Activism
6198911.description: When Irina Markish became active in the protests and demonstrations calling for the release of Soviet Jewry and on behalf of her husband, David Markish, in particular, her advocacy led her to a surprising and fruitful meeting with the Rebbe. (1972)

6198912.title: Worth the Risk
6198912.description: Rabbi Mordechai Dubinsky readily agreed to host a young couple from Israel who came to the United States seeking treatment for the wife’s heart condition. What he didn’t expect was to also be involved in the birth of their first child. (1970s)

6198913.title: Where is Moshiach?
6198913.description: Rabbi Moshiach Chudaitov and his family were active in the Jewish underground in Samarkand, Uzbekistan during Soviet times. When they succeeded in leaving the Soviet Union, they received some unexpected attention from the Rebbe, together with a very special blessing. (Early 1970s)

6198914.title: On My Shoulders
6198914.description: Shortly after his Bar Mitzvah, the Rebbe assured Rabbi Mordechai Einbinder’s parents that he would see to the well-being of their son in a yeshiva far away from home. Decades later, Rabbi Einbinder discovered just how serious the Rebbe was about his word.

6198915.title: What Makes a Marriage Endure?
6198915.description: After becoming observant in college, Rabbi Meilech Leib DuBrow asked the Rebbe about marrying someone whom he had known during his student years. In an unusually long audience, he received the answer to his question, as well as advice on the basics of a Jewish marriage. (1971)

6198916.title: Saying Thank You
6198916.description: Mr. Evsey Neymotin recalls his father’s efforts in assisting Rabbi Levi Yitzchak and Rebbetzin Chana Schneerson, the Rebbe’s parents, when they arrived in Almaty, Kazakhstan, as well as the Rebbe’s expressions of gratitude when the Neymotins arrived in the United States many decades later.

6198919.title: A Spiritual Business
6198919.description: Mr. Meir Zeiler, the proprietor of a textile factory in Israel, was encouraged by the Rebbe to take part in European trade shows. His reports that the shows were not profitable did not deter the Rebbe, and Mr. Zeiler began to suspect that the tefillin booth he would set up as part of his display had something to do with it.

6198920.title: The Essence of Things
6198920.description: Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu of Israel shares the enduring message which he received in his first meeting with the Rebbe during his tenure as Israel’s Ambassador to the United Nations. (1984)

6198923.title: The Nation That Dwells Alone
6198923.description: Yitzchak Rabin was prime minister of Israel, and served as Israel’s ambassador to the United States in the early 1970s. In 1972 he was sent to convey Israel’s blessings to the Rebbe in honor of his 70th birthday, and left with a challenging message. (1972)

6198924.title: Wake Up Call
6198924.description: Motti Eden is Director of Israel’s Channel One television. In 1980, while working as a broadcast journalist for Kol Yisrael Israeli radio, he had a private audience with the Rebbe, which he recorded and later broadcast on Kol Yisrael. (1980)

6198926.title: Exceptional Soldiers
6198926.description:
Mr. Yosef Lautenberg was injured in the battle for Jerusalem in 1948, and was one of the founders of the IDF Disabled Veterans Organization.
In 1976, he led the Israeli delegation, made up in large part of injured IDF veterans, to the Paralympics in Toronto, and decided to bring the group to New York to visit with the Rebbe. (1976)

6198927.title: Are There 'Secular' Soldiers in the IDF?
6198927.description: When Shmuel Blizinsky served in the Israel Defense Forces in the early 1950s, he was only able to find twelve religious soldiers on his entire base. As it turned out, the Rebbe was able to find three thousand. (1951)
path: Are There 'Secular' Soldiers in the IDF?

6198932.title: Secret Mission
6198932.description: Elimelech Leiman relates that when the Rebbe heard about his father’s upcoming trip to the Soviet Union to visit family, he requested to see him. Handing him a bag of esrogim and a secret code, the Rebbe stated, “This mission will be good for them and good for you.”

6198934.title: A Helping Hand
6198934.description: When things became tough financially, Rabbi Yossi Groner decided to travel to the Rebbe for a blessing before Simchas Torah. Before he could say anything, the Rebbe blessed him with improvement in his finances, and even secured a donation. (1991)

6198935.title: Practically Speaking
6198935.description: Rabbi Mordechai Gutnick relates that his father, known as a powerful orator, once confided in the Rebbe that he wonders how much he is actually accomplishing with his speeches. The Rebbe’s advice to his father is something Rabbi Gutnick still uses today.

6198938.title: Isaac Herzog, President-Elect of Israel
6198938.description: Firsthand recollections of his visit to 770 one Simchat Torah with his father, Chaim Herzog, who was then Israel’s Ambassador to the United Nations. (1977)

6198939.title: The Rebbe’s Prescription for a Paralyzed Arm
6198939.description: Soon after Dr. Levi Reiter purchased his own pair of tefillin, he found himself in a doctor’s office with a paralyzed arm. Neurologists gave him three possible prognoses, but the Rebbe reduced it to one.
path: The Rebbe’s Prescription for a Paralyzed Arm

6198940.title: The Rebbe’s Word
6198940.description: Reb Velvel Konikov relates that when his father, Reb Chaim Tzvi Hersh, was drafted into the Russian army, he sought the blessing of the Rebbe Rashab.

6198942.title: Construction and Destruction
6198942.description: Professor Aaron Ciechanover, a Nobel Prize winning scientist, relates the conversation he shared with the Rebbe when his research was in its early stages, as well as the lesson he learned. (1977)

6198944.title: A Wedding and a Mission
6198944.description: As a student in yeshiva in his early twenties, Rabbi Yossi Baumgarten asked the Rebbe for a blessing on route to a friend’s wedding in Italy, and ended up with a mission. (Early 1970s)

6198946.title: Saving Three Lives
6198946.description: Dr. Harold Serebro was surprised when the rabbi of his synagogue walked into his practice holding a file of x-rays belonging to a fellow congregant. The rabbi’s dilemma: doctors were insisting on immediate surgery, but the Rebbe was of an entirely different opinion. (Early 1980s)

6198949.title: Everybody Counts
6198949.description: Mrs. Dena Horn, who lost her father at a young age, recalls the special attention the Rebbe showed her family when they moved to the neighborhood. (1950s)

6198950.title: Celebrating Study of Rambam
6198950.description:
Rabbi Shmuel Butman recalls the day the Rebbe called him to his house, requesting that he publish a book commemorating the worldwide celebrations of the annual completion of the Mishneh Torah.
His due date? Three weeks. (1980s)

6198954.title: Stay the Course
6198954.description: When Avraham Infeld agreed to accompany an Israeli dignitary to a meeting with the Rebbe, he had no intention of meeting the Rebbe himself. Little did he know that the trip would not only change his life, but the lives of thousands. (Late 1960s)

6198955.title: The Educator’s Secret
6198955.description: Rabbi Moshe Naparstek, who serves on the faculty of Yeshiva Tomchei Temimim in Kfar Chabad, Isreal, was surprised when during an audience, the Rebbe volunteered advice on the correct approach to education. More than just sound advice, it was a solution to his dilemma. (1960's)

6198958.title: Transformative Vision
6198958.description: When academic and artist, Mel Alexenberg, was considering giving up his position at New York’s Columbia University and relocating to Israel, he and his wife were looking to do something out of the box. As it turned out, the Rebbe had just the idea. (1977)

6198959.title: Medical Referral
6198959.description: Rabbi Hershel Slansky recalls that when his mother-in-law was diagnosed with a painful condition, and doctors were recommending disfiguring surgery, he encouraged her to go to 770 to see the Rebbe. Expecting a blessing, she returned with a referral instead.

6198960.title: Keep the Land
6198960.description: Moshe Ishon, chief editor of the newspaper Hatzofeh in Israel, recalls an audience he had with the Rebbe in the wake of the Six Day War. (1971)

6198964.title: The Right Question
6198964.description:
Rabbi Joseph Telushkin recalls that when his father, who served as the accountant for Chabad Lubavitch, was hospitalized after a stroke, he received daily phone calls from the Rebbe’s office, inquiring about his progress. Shortly after his father came out of his coma, he received another
call from the Rebbe’s office. This time, it was an accounting query. (1986)

6198966.title: In the Beginning
6198966.description: Reb Moshe Chaim Sapochkinsky recalls traveling to New York in honor of the first yahrzeit of Rabbi Yosef Yitzchak Schneerson, the Previous Rebbe. He was present at the historic event when a group of elder chasidim petitioned the Rebbe to accept the leadership of ChabadLubavitch, which the Rebbe had previously declined to do. (1951)

6198967.title: She Taught Us to Appreciate the Mainstay of the Home
6198967.description: Louise Hager, who developed a close relationship with the Rebbe’s wife, Rebbetzin Chaya Mushka, recalls speaking about her for the first time in public, and relates some important lessons the Rebbetzin taught her. (1991)
path: She Taught Us to Appreciate the Mainstay of the Home

6198969.title: We are Together
6198969.description: Rabbi Noson Gurary shares two unique and candid audiences he had with the Rebbe after he and his wife set out on shlichus and established the Chabad Student Center near the campus of New York State University, Buffalo. (1970s)

6198970.title: Old Traditions in a New Land
6198970.description: Rabbi Avraham Alashvili relates that when his father, Rabbi Rafael Alashvili, emigrated from his native Georgia to Israel, he travelled to New York to seek the Rebbe’s guidance on adjusting to his new life in the Holy Land, and returned to Israel a changed man. (1973)
path: Old Traditions in a New Land

6198971.title: Bringing it Together
6198971.description: When Rabbi Michael Paley was a physics student at Brandeis University and found himself surrounded by many doubts, a friend and a mentor advised him to see the Rebbe. The short encounter left its impression on the remainder of his life. (1951)

6198972.title: We Tried Everything to Have a Child
