6198972.description: Dr. Shelli Menachemson and her husband had tried everything they could to have a child, including infertility treatment and a blessing from the Rebbe, but there seemed to be no success. After another failed pregnancy, they reluctantly turned to the Rebbe again. (1989)
path: We Tried Everything to Have a Child

6198973.title: Remembering the Law
6198973.description: Jacob Abramczyk recalls being present at a Purim farbrengen when the Rebbe suddenly turned to the distinguished rabbis seated behind him and asked a question in Jewish law, the answer to which almost no one seemed to remember. (Early 1960s)

6198975.title: No, There is Hope! - Part One
6198975.description: When one year old Amina Schochet was badly burned, doctors were in doubt whether she would survive the day. When her father turned to the Rebbe, he offered a more positive prognosis and instructed the family to make a kiddush that Shabbos. (1951)
path: No, There is Hope! - Part One

6198976.title: No, There is Hope! - Part Two
6198976.description: When one year old Amina Schochet sustained critical burns, her family followed the Rebbe’s advice and, with heavy hearts, prepared a kiddush on Shabbos. Later, when little Amina suffered another setback, the family again turned to the Rebbe. (1951)
path: No, There is Hope! - Part Two

6198977.title: At the Rebbe’s Seder
6198977.description: Rabbi Yosef Yitzchak Offen recalls being present at the Rebbe’s Passover seder, and describes how the Rebbe recited the Haggadah. (Late 1960s)

6198979.title: A Double Portion of Blessing
6198979.description: When Shraga Jameson and his wife experienced a personal tragedy, they decided to travel to the Rebbe in search of some solace. After a seemingly uneventful first encounter, they decided to write the Rebbe about their troubles. (1990)

6198981.title: Trouble in Tanzania
6198981.description: Ephraim Katz recalls a hapless business trip he took to Tanzania to purchase gemstones. Luckily, it turned out to be very lucrative – but only thanks to the Rebbe’s blessing and guidance along the way. (1980's)

6198990.title: A Joint Effort
6198990.description: Stanley Abramowitz frequently traveled to North Africa on behalf of the Joint Distribution Committee, where he found himself working side by side with Chabad. Impressed, he decided to meet the man behind the operation. (1950s)

6198991.title: The Start of a Career
6198991.description: When Rabbi Immanuel Schochet became engaged to be married, he decided to drop college to pursue a business opportunity. “If there is no livelihood, there is no Torah,” he reasoned. The Rebbe had a different plan. (1960's)

6198993.title: Thirteen Channels of Blessing
6198993.description: When Reb Berel Wiess, a successful businessman, asked the Rebbe for a blessing to have both wealth and Torah knowledge, the Rebbe told him that this particular blessing requires a special vessel which Reb Berel was yet to acquire. (1980's)

6198995.title: Missing in Action
6198995.description: During his year as a student in 770, Amram Malka was often enlisted to help in the Rebbe’s secretariat, and assisted at the Rebbe’s table during all festival meals – except for the second night of Shavous. (1966)

6198996.title: Sing Your Way to Success, Part 1
6198996.description: When Cantor Berel Zaltzman first arrived from the Soviet Union, the Rebbe asked him to sing numerous times during his distribution of wine at the conclusion of Rosh Hashanah. At his first audience, Rabbi Zaltzman finally understood the Rebbe’s intentions. (1970's)
path: Sing Your Way to Success, Part 1

6198997.title: Sing Your Way to Success, Part 2
6198997.description: Cantor Berel Zaltzman was too busy adjusting to his new life in Israel and struggling to make a living to realize that the Rebbe had already given him the key to his success. (1970's)
path: Sing Your Way to Success, Part 2

6199001.title: The Power of a Letter – Part I
6199001.description: Rabbi Shmuel Greisman recalls some of the special instructions he received from the Rebbe as he began to direct the new campaign for Jewish children to own a letter in a Torah scroll. (1981)
path: The Power of a Letter – Part I

6199002.title: The Power of a Letter – Part II
6199002.description: Rabbi Shmuel Greisman relates that after initiating the campaign for the children’s Torah scroll, the Rebbe urged all Jews to participate in signing up as many children as possible. Speaking about the campaign on numerous occasions, the Rebbe and stressed that a display of unity would help avert a threat over the Jewish people. (1981)
path: The Power of a Letter – Part II

6199013.title: Together in Thought
6199013.description: Rabbi Pinchos Baumgarten relates that the Rebbe asked his father to visit Jews scattered in rural Argentina and Brazil. Finding himself alone on the anniversary of the Previous Rebbe’s release from Soviet imprisonment, a day celebrated by chasidim, he decided to send the Rebbe a telegram. (1950's)

6199014.title: On the Straight and Narrow
6199014.description: Mrs. Mariashi Groner, now the co-director of Lubavitch of North Carolina and director of the Charlotte Jewish Day School, recalls turning to the Rebbe during a difficult time in her teens. (1976)

6199015.title: The Beginning of Camp
6199015.description: When Rabbi Moshe Lazar was a yeshiva student in his late teens, he wrote to the Rebbe with the idea of opening a Chabad summer camp for Jewish children – an initiative the Rebbe embraced. (Mid 1950's)

6199016.title: A Niche Market
6199016.description: When Mr. Bernard Perrin was having trouble with his fur business, he followed the advice of a friend and wrote to the Rebbe, only to receive a most unexpected response.

6199017.title: The Full Picture
6199017.description: When Rabbi Shlomo Jakobovits was a student at Yeshiva University, he asked the Rebbe a series of questions in an audience which lasted over two hours. (1953)

6199018.title: Unbroken Spirit
6199018.description: Reb Gedaliah Mazal shares his memories of the arrival of Rabbi Levi Yitzchak Schneerson, the Rebbe’s father, in Alamty, Kazakhstan. Reb Gedaliah’s father became close to Rabbi Levi Yitzchak, and was present at his passing. (1940's)

6199022.title: Closing Shop
6199022.description: Ami Pykovski, the proprietor of a large clothing store in downtown Los Angeles, found himself grappling with the idea of closing his store on Shabbos. Torn between his business and a growing commitment to Judaism, he decided to write to the Rebbe. (1980s)

6199024.title: Atomic Energy
6199024.description: Overwhelmed by mounting questions about his work in the rabbinate and Jewish outreach, as well as in his business, Rabbi David Lapin sought advice from the Rebbe.

6199026.title: Fomenting Revolution
6199026.description:
After calling for revolution at an anti- Vietnam War rally, Larry Caroline lost his position as a philosophy professor at the University of Texas, and his academic career. After making his journey to Judaism and reporting the events to the Rebbe almost a decade later, he was encouraged to
remain a radical.

6199028.title: Time for Prayer
6199028.description: Rabbi Meir Tzvi Gruzman taught a class of adolescent yeshiva boys. When he noticed that his encouragement of “chasidic prayer” was not always having the desired results, he decided to bring the issue up in an audience with the Rebbe.(1960's)

6199029.title: A Vote of Confidence, Part I
6199029.description: Rabbi Simon Jacobson recalls the visit of the controversial Israeli writer, Natan Yellin-Mor, to his home one Rosh Hashanah, and the fateful exchange the writer shared with the Rebbe at the conclusion of the festival.(1977)
path: A Vote of Confidence, Part I

6199030.title: A Vote of Confidence, Part II
6199030.description: Rabbi Simon Jacobson relates that a few years after his father introduced the writer Natan Yellin-Mor to the Rebbe, he received an envelope from the ailing writer. Inside was a request that its contents be published after the writer’s death.(Early 1980s)
path: A Vote of Confidence, Part II

6199031.title: A Heartfelt Prayer
6199031.description: Rabbi Yossi Baumgarten would often seek out the company of a newcomer to 770, a basketball coach by the name of Abe Sacks. As it turns out, the Rebbe shared his affinity for this Jew.(1970's)

6199032.title: When the Time Comes
6199032.description: Sam Friedland recalls that when he suggested making changes in the family business to his father, he was instructed to ask the Rebbe for his opinion. Aware of the Rebbe’s saintliness and scholarship, he could not help but wonder what the Rebbe could possibly know about his father’s small company. (1980's)

6199033.title: Where Everything seems Right
6199033.description: Leah Aizenman arrived in New York from Tel Aviv to discover that her sister’s home served as a stop for guests coming from all over the world to spend the High Holidays with the Rebbe. On Hoshana Raba, after feeding an endless flow of people, she ran to 770 toward the end of the Rebbe’s distribution of honey cake for a sweet new year. Fortunately, she was too late. (1976)

6199034.title: Speaking the Truth
6199034.description: Rabbi Mordechai Piron recalls that when he served as chief rabbi of the Israel Defense Forces, he faced a moral dilemma and sought the Rebbe’s advice. He knew in his heart that the guidance he was hearing seemed right on the mark, but to what extent, he would only realize when he returned to Israel. (Early 1970's)

6199036.title: Focus on Healing
6199036.description: When Arnold Dalfen was told by his doctor that he would not be able to have children, the Rebbe referred him to another specialist. When that doctor arrived at the same conclusion, the Rebbe asked him to simply focus on the healing. (1950's)

6199037.title: A Sign Upon Your Arm, Part I
6199037.description: When Rabbi Shimon Lazaroff discovered that Dr. Milton Nirken, the pediatrician that treated his children, had suffered a sudden paralysis of his left arm, he assured the doctor that he would seek a blessing from the Rebbe on his behalf. (1970s)
path: A Sign Upon Your Arm, Part I

6199038.title: A Sign Upon Your Arm, Part II
6199038.description: When neurologists could do nothing about his paralysis, Dr. Milton Nirken turned to Rabbi Shimon Lazaroff, who then turned to the Rebbe for a blessing. After receiving a phone call from the Rebbe’s office late one night, he called Dr. Nirken to relay the Rebbe’s words. Dr. Nirken, however, had news of his own. (1970s)
path: A Sign Upon Your Arm, Part II

6199039.title: Encouraging Words
6199039.description: Rabbi Yehoshua Gordon relates that when he and his family were facing a difficult challenge in their work as Chabad emissaries, his wife wrote to the Rebbe for advice and blessing. To this day, the words of the Rebbe’s response hang framed in Rabbi Gordon’s office.

6199040.title: Assembling the Nation
6199040.description: When Rabbi Tuvia Blau told the Rebbe that he hoped that his wife and children would have the experience of meeting him, the Rebbe suggested that he bring his family in for hakhel. This was not an easy feat for a family of seven from Israel, in the 1970s

6199041.title: You are with Us
6199041.description: Israel Adamski grew up in Dnepropetrovsk, Ukraine, where the Rebbe’s father served as Rabbi. Although the Rebbe was married in faraway Warsaw, Mr. Adamski remembers the celebration that took place the night of the wedding in the Rebbe’s parent’s home. (1928)

6199042.title: A Chapter a Day
6199042.description: Rabbi Nissen Mangel recalls that shortly after the Rebbe sent him to Lakewood, New Jersey, to teach chasidic philosophy in a non-chasidic yeshiva, he was approached by an impatient student eager to study Tanya – at one o’clock in the morning. (Late 1950s)

6199043.title: At Just the Right Time
6199043.description: Rabbi Yechezkel Sofer relates that when he tried convincing his father to write a letter to the Rebbe, his father was skeptical that he would receive a response. When Rabbi Sofer finally succeeded but no reply was forthcoming, he couldn’t help but wonder whether his father was right. (Mid 1960s)

6199044.title: Positive Thinking
6199044.description: Rabbi Avraham Rottenberg recalls that when he received word from Israel that his father had suffered a heart attack, the Rebbe insisted that he take the oldest medicine in the book, and to good effect. (Late 1950s)

6199045.title: A Bright Future
6199045.description: During a polio outbreak in the United States in the 1950s, Rabbi Yechiel Ziskind contracted the dreaded disease and found himself paralyzed in an iron lung. While doctors were losing hope, the Rebbe had bright plans for the future. (Mid 1950s)

6199046.title: A Global Responsibility
6199046.description: When Ovadia Eli met the Rebbe shortly after his appointment as the Deputy Defense Minister of Israel, he was surprised to hear the Rebbe say that all of the world’s Jews are under his watch, not just those living in the Holy Land. As it turns out, the Rebbe’s words had far reaching effects. (1991)

6199047.title: An Unexpected Letter
6199047.description: Rabbi Avraham Chaputa recalls a fateful audience he had with Rebbe when he was the dean of a fledgling yeshiva in Tel Aviv. The consequences of that audience only became clear to him many decades later. (1973)

6199048.title: The Rebbe's Plan to Calm the Streets of New York
6199048.description: Jacob Worenklein, who was an intern at the office of the president of the New York City Council, recalls arranging a meeting between City Council President Francis X. Smith and the Rebbe at a time when New York City was facing a surge in crime. (1969)
path: The Rebbe's Plan to Calm the Streets of New York

6199049.title: Twice Blessed
6199049.description: Rhoda Friedland recalls receiving a blessing for children from Rabbi Yosef Yitzchak Schneersohn, the Previous Rebbe. After the Previous Rebbe’s passing, with the blessing yet to materialize, she turned to the Rebbe for help. (Early 1950's)

6199050.title: The Heart of the Matter
6199050.description: As a young serviceman in the Israeli Air Force, Moshe Tzur was moved by Chabad’s outreach work. Almost a decade later, when he had a chance to give back to the movement that changed his life, he was even more moved by what he heard from the Rebbe in a private audience. (1970's)

6199052.title: Words of Encouragement
6199052.description: As a young woman, Sarah Rifkah Sassonkin was sent by the Rebbe to be a teacher in Milan, Italy, where her sister and brother-in-law served as shluchim. Overwhelmed by her new responsibilities, she wrote an emotional letter to the Rebbe. (1960)

6199053.title: Hakhel State of Mind
6199053.description: Rabbi Chaim Benyamini established and headed the Yeshiva in Petropolis, Brazil, for over 30 years. He shares a perplexing encounter with the Rebbe that left him with a penetrating lesson about just how “hakhel-conscious” a Jew can be. (1987)

6199055.title: Your Action Is What Counts
6199055.description: Rabbi Chaim Shneor Nisenbaum is a Chabad representative in Paris, France. As a young Rabbi, he approached the Rebbe with a sincere concern; while he felt productive in his work, he was concerned about it inflating his ego. The Rebbe’s clear and direct response shaped the remainder of Rabbi Nisenbaum’s life. (1970s)

6199056.title: Hear O Israel
6199056.description: Soon after they moved to Alabama, Rabbi Stern’s young daughter suffered damage to her ear which resulted in loss of hearing. After going through two surgeries which failed, the Sterns decided to ask the Rebbe for his advice and blessing. (1969)

6199057.title: A Mission Accomplished
6199057.description:
Rabbi Yoseph Itzhak Gurewitz was part of a delegation sent by the Rebbe sent to study in Israel.When Purim arrived, the Rebbe requested that they bring the joy of the festival to soldiers stationed on bases across Israel.
As the group neared their destination, they came to a makeshift roadblock where they were confronted by a mob of Arab youths. Motivated by their mission and the Rebbe’s words, they forged on with their assignment. (1976)

6199058.title: A Mission Accomplished Part II
6199058.description: Part of a special group charged with visiting soldiers serving in the IDF on the festival of Purim, Rabbi Yosef Yitzchak Gurewitz recalls risking involvement in a dangerous situation in order to carry out his mission. An event the Rebbe used as a lesson in life. (1976)

6199059.title: On the Other Hand
6199059.description: Rabbi Yisroel Shusterman is left handed. Since mitzvos are usually to be done with the right hand, as a young man, he asked the Rebbe for direction in this matter and about the ramifications of being a lefty. At the time, the Rebbe sent him to the local Rabbinic authority and Rabbi Shusterman all but forgot about the story. Imagine his surprise when the Rebbe made reference to this so many years later. (Early 1970s)

6199060.title: To Every Single Child
6199060.description: Rabbi Yaakov Roth is an educator and teacher Miami, Florida. From time to time, he would have his young students send letters to the Rebbe. The Rebbe’s thoughtful responses were touching and inspiring. (Early 1970s)

6199061.title: Preventive Psychology
6199061.description: Mr. Mordechai Reich is a psychologist practicing in Efrat, Israel, where he lives with his wife and their five children. In the summer of 1974, during a visit with the Rebbe, he asked for advice on what career path he should pursue. The Rebbe’s answer gave him new insight into both psychology and education, and their effect on our society at large. (1974)

6199062.title: House Visits
6199062.description: Dr. Alan Newmark merited to attend to Rebbetzin Chaya Mushkah, the wife of the Rebbe. In this clip, he recalls and shares some of the most memorable conversations that he had with the Rebbetzin, illustrating her sensitivity and care. (1980s)

6199064.title: Soviet Exodus Part I
6199064.description: Rabbi Gershon Ber Schiff was active in the Jewish underground in the Soviet Union. When he heard that his relative was visiting Moscow from beyond the Iron Curtain, he was torn about whether to put himself and his activities in danger in order to meet - until he heard a message from the Rebbe. (1969)

6199066.title: Soviet Exodus Part II
6199066.description: When Gershon Ber Schiff finally emigrated from Russia, he was excited to be spending Passover with the Rebbe. When the Rebbe called an unscheduled farbrengen on the first day of the festival, he realized just how much it meant to the Rebbe, too. (1971)

6199067.title: Passover in Wartime
6199067.description:
Rabbi Fabian Schonfeld describes the Rebbe’s efforts to obtain matzo of the highest kosher
standard during the Second World War, for his own use and for others.

6199068.title: With Conviction and with Love
6199068.description: Rabbi Sidney Katz was a chaplain and Rabbi in South Africa. His son, Rabbi Michoel Katz, recalls the Rebbe’s answer to his parents when like many, they were thinking of leaving the country. (1972)

6199069.title: When the Nurse Blinded Our Newborn
6199069.description: Like all parents, the Landbergs were very excited by the birth of their son. Their joy, however, was short lived when their child was blinded by a nurse’s negligence. Given the frightening prognosis, their doctor offered a surprising referral.(1973)
path: When the Nurse Blinded Our Newborn

6199070.title: Patient Empowerment
6199070.description: Dr. Mordechai Shani is an Israeli physician and medical Professor. Intrigued by the Rebbe’s words to him one Simchas Torah, he decided to follow up with a private audience. The meeting, which discussed developments in healthcare, continues to impact him today. (1976)

6199071.title: Research Results
6199071.description: Hans Morgenthau was a major twentieth-century figure in the study of international politics. In 1991, while researching his life for a dissertation, Dr. Benjamin Mollov came to 770 to interview Rabbi Yehuda Krinsky about his subject’s relationship with the Rebbe. As it turned out, Dr. Mollov, developed a relationship of his own. (1991)

6199072.title: Darkness to Light
6199072.description: Mrs. Riva Ceitlin runs Chabad programs for women in Montreal, Canada. When her son, Rabbi Aaron Eliezer Ceitlin, heard his mother speaking about the pressures of her position, he decided to ask the Rebbe for some encouragement. (1980's)

6199073.title: Crossing the Line
6199073.description: When Rabbi Yoel Kahn discovered that his Shabbos guest had crossed the International Date Line during the Omer Count, he realized that for him, that Shabbos was already the fiftieth day of the Omer, and the festival of Shavuos. Uncertain of what his guest should do, he advised him to consult the Rebbe. (1961)

6199074.title: Musical Interlude
6199074.description: When Shmuel Katan came to spend Simchas Torah with the Rebbe, he didn’t expect to becomethe center of attention. But hearing of his musical talent, chasidim urged him to play his violin while the Rebbe distributed wine after the conclusion of the festival. To his surprise, the Rebbe offered three pointers on his technique. (1968)

6199075.title: Slowly, But Surely
6199075.description: Rabbi Joseph Karasick was president of the Orthodox Union from 1966 till 1972. One day during his tenure, he received an unexpected call from the Rebbe’s office inviting him for a meeting with the Rebbe. In the course of their conversation about his organization, Rabbi Karasick asked the Rebbe an unrelated question. The Rebbe’s answer has been with him, and shared with others, to this day.(1967)

6199077.title: Match Made in Heaven
6199077.description: On the advice of her father, Chaya Cohen would often turn to the Rebbe for advice and guidance in her life. When the Rebbe advised her to start visiting friends for Shabbos meals, she knew something good would follow. (1970)

6199078.title: Praying for His People
6199078.description: Rabbi Chaim Yehuda Krinsky served in various positions of Chabad's administrative staff since 1954, and as a personal secretary and press director for the Rebbe. In this presentation, he recalls some of the most memorable moments and details of when the Rebbe would visit the gravesite of his father-in-law and Rebbe, Rabbi Yosef Yitzchok Schneerson.

6199079.title: Matters of the Heart
6199079.description: In 1991, Naftoli Feldman was confined to the hospital suffering from cardiovascular issues. As each treatment that he tried failed to bring positive results, he asked his wife to go to the Rebbe to seek a blessing. The Rebbe’s advice, and his subsequent care and attention, is something that left an indelible impression. (1991)

6199080.title: Opening the Doors to the Soviet Union
6199080.description: After promising to maintain secrecy and informing the Rebbe of his plans, he was given some contacts by the Rebbe. (1960's)
path: Opening the Doors to the Soviet Union

6199081.title: Seeing Potential
6199081.description: As a young man, Rabbi Fishel Jacobs came with his mother for a private audience with the Rebbe. In his innocence, he brought along a tape recorder to record the meeting. Listening to the recording brings back powerful memories of the Rebbe’s care and concern for his personal life - both spiritually and materially. (1981)

6199082.title: Not a Scratch!
6199082.description: Rabbi Yisroel Shemtov was a sixteen year old student in 1956. He recalls the Rebbe’s visit to Camp Gan Israel that summer, and the farbrengen the Rebbe held there. During the gathering, news arrived of a terrible accident that had involved a busload of people on their way to the camp. The Rebbe’s reaction to the news was wholly unexpected, and seemingly miraculous. (1956)

6199083.title: A Healer’s Job
6199083.description: Uriel Ash was riding his bike one day when he was hit by a car and knocked unconscious. After putting him through various tests in the hospital, the doctors despaired and gave up on trying to save his life. In their desperation, the Ashes asked the Rebbe for advice and blessing. While seemingly unremarkable, it was a few words from the Rebbe, which guided the young boy to a miraculous recovery. (1987)

6199084.title: Summer in the Caribbean
6199084.description: In 1959, the Rebbe sent Rabbi Shmuel Pesach Bogomilsky to the caribbean Islands, to help strengthen the local Jewish community. Upon landing at the airport in Barbados, he met an estranged Jew who sought to develop a relationship with the Rebbe. Little did he know, that this one small connection would lead to some very big achievements.

6199085.title: The Greatest Custom
6199085.description: While visiting from France, Rabbi Yaakov Spitetzky was confused as to why the Rebbe seemed to ignore him during one of their meetings. It was some information that he later received from the Rebbe’s secretary that touches and inspires him till this day. (1968)

6199087.title: West Meets East – Part 1
6199087.description: Rabbi Marvin Tokayer recalls the life changing audience in which the Rebbe brought the plight of the Jewish community in Japan to his attention, along with the suggestion that he might hold the solution to their problem. (1960's)

6199088.title: West Meets East – Part 2
6199088.description: After agreeing to serve as rabbi in Japan for a period of two years, Rabbi Marvin Tokayer was thinking of backing out when his father suddenly passed away. The Rebbe’s guidance and advice turned his challenge into the most rewarding experience of his life.(1960's)

6199090.title: Attention to Detail
6199090.description: Rabbi Yitzchok Wolf, who serves as director of Chicago's Cheder Lubavitch Hebrew day School, recalls the Rebbe’s request that schools test students and send the results to his office. After sending in a box of notebooks, he was surprised to receive a telephone call from 770. (1987)

6199091.title: No Time to Quit
6199091.description: After some difficult first years as a shliach in New York City, Rabbi Shlomo Kugel was ready to throw in the towel, and sent a letter of resignation to the Rebbe’s secretariat just before Rosh Hashana. The Rebbe’s refusal to accept his resignation continues to drive him further each day. (1980's)

6199093.title: A Touching Apology
6199093.description: Mrs. Asya New remembers the care that the Rebbe showed her family when her father, Rabbi Isser Kluwgant, took ill. Not only did the Rebbe provide indispensable advice, he requested a daily report on Rabbi Kluwgant’s progress. (1981)

6199094.title: Path to Success
6199094.description: As a young boy, Baruch Wilhelm suffered an accident causing damage to his ears, and requested the Rebbe’s blessing to regain his hearing. While he may not have received what he was hoping for, he received was a deep and impactful lesson to apply throughout his life. (1980)

6199095.title: My Spiritual Compass
6199095.description: Elie Wiesel, an author, Nobel Prize laureate, and Holocaust survivor, recalls seeing the Rebbe for the first time, and the profound impact it had on the rest of his life. (1960's)

6199096.title: When It Rains on Sukkot
6199096.description: Rabbi Binyomin Silberstrom recalls asking the Rebbe, “How can we spread joy during the festival Sukkos when it won’t stop raining? The Talmud clearly states that rain is a sign of God’s displeasure.” The quick reply to his question was was a revealing example of the Rebbe’s unique perspective. (1975)

6199099.title: A Fateful Blessing
6199099.description: Hanan Caspi recalls attending Simchas Torah celebrations in 770, as well as a private audience he had as a child, when his father served as the Consul General of Israel in New York. It was then that he heard the words that would give him the strength he so much needed many years later in life. (Early 1970s)

6199100.title: Seizing the Moment
6199100.description: Rabbi Mayer Plotkin recalls the unusual scene that unfolded as he approached the Rebbe to request a blessing for an ailing acquaintance the night after Simchas Torah, as the Rebbe was distributing wine. (1971)

6199101.title: Message for the World
6199101.description: Ari Goldman, then a reporter for The New York Times, recalls several encounters that he shared with the Rebbe, as well as an unexpected telephone call shortly after one particular visit. (Late 1980s)

6199102.title: Preventative Medication
6199102.description: As a young man, Mottel Feiglin suffered from painful migraines. On the advice of friends, he decided to ask the Rebbe for a blessing. He expected the blessing, and even advice, but not the prescription. (1971)

6199103.title: Nothing Wrong
6199103.description: In 1981, Dr. Leslie Rosenthal was suddenly struck by a severe headache during the Rosh Hashanah services. Further tests indicated that he was suffering from an aneurysm behind his eye. Running out of options, his rabbi convinced him to write to the Rebbe detailing his ailments. The Rebbe’s answer startled him, as well as his doctors. (1981)

6199104.title: On the Rebbe’s Mind
6199104.description: Rabbi Shlomo Matusof was one of the first Chabad shluchim and a pioneer of Jewish education in Morocco. His son, Rabbi Yosef Yitzchak Matusof recalls an episode highlighting the Rebbe’s care and concern for his emissaries around the world. (1957)

6199105.title: No Shortcuts
6199105.description: Rabbi Shlomo Majeski recalls an audience that he had with the Rebbe on the occasion of his Bar Mitzvah. After asking him to share the words of Torah that he would speak at his Bar Mitzvah, the Rebbe offered some words of his own. (1963)

6199106.title: Late Notice
6199106.description: Rabbi Shmuel Lew recalls that his father-in-law, Zalman Jaffe, tried every angle he could in an effort to convince the Rebbe to officiate at his daughter’s wedding, a practice that the Rebbe had ceased several years earlier. (1963)

6199107.title: The Bilingual Tanya
6199107.description: Mr. Bernard Perrin lives in Manchester, England. In the 1970’s the Rebbe commissioned him for an important project in the dissemination of Chassidism to the wider world. (1970's)

6199108.title: Family Time
6199108.description: In 1976, Rabbi Shmuel Gurewicz brought his family with him for an audience with the Rebbe. Relating to each child in a unique and personal manner, the Rebbe’s special interaction with the children was a beautiful expression of his love for every Jew. (1976)

6199109.title: An Exhibition in Brooklyn
6199109.description: Baruch Nachshon is a famed artist from Chevron, Israel. In 1979, he brought some of his art with him when he came to visit the Rebbe. After suggesting to him to make an art exhibit, the Rebbe came and gave comments which were subtle, yet very profound. (1979)

6199110.title: A Place in the Sun
6199110.description: Rabbi Avraham Shalem hailed from a long line of Sephardic rabbis. In the 1960’s, after being offered two different rabbinic posts, he was conflicted as to what to do. Seeing no way to solve his dilemma on his own, he turned to the Rebbe for advice. (1960's)

6199111.title: The Work Must Go On
6199111.description: Rabbi Eliezer Nisilevitch recalls the dangers his family faced in the Soviet Union as members of the Jewish underground, and the strength and direction they received from the Rebbe even after they had succeeded in emigrating to Israel. (1971)

6199112.title: A Weight off His Shoulders
6199112.description: When Meir Moss returned to his Jewish roots and decided to attend a yeshiva in his teens, his father, a holocaust survivor who had become alienated from Judaism, decided to take it up with the Rebbe. He travelled to all the way to New York from Melbourne, Australia but forgot to lodge his complaint with the Rebbe. (1970's)

6199113.title: The Stray Kitten
6199113.description: Shavi Slodowitz grew up in Brooklyn, New York, where she attended Bais Rivkah High School. Being a somewhat difficult student, she lacked the motivation she needed to grow. In the most unusual way, the Rebbe channeled her passions into personal growth and academic success.

6199114.title: What the Rebbe Was Thinking About
6199114.description: Rabbi Asher Zeilingold recalls spending 10 Shevat, the anniversary of the passing of Rabbi Yosef Yitzchak Schneersohn, the sixth Lubavitcher Rebbe, in 770. After observing the Rebbe during evening services, he could not help but wonder how the Rebbe would spend the remainder of such an auspicious day. To his surprise, an answer was short to follow. (1958)
path: What the Rebbe Was Thinking About

6199115.title: Memories of 15 Shevat, 1941, in Marseille
6199115.description:
In 1941, the Rebbe travelled to Marseilles, France, to obtain entry visas to the United States for himself and his wife, Rebbetzin Chaya Mushka. While there, the Rebbe maintained his characteristic low profile, but at a gathering in honor of the New Year for Trees, he gave those
present a taste of things to come. (1941)

6199118.title: Family Medicine
6199118.description: A relative of the Rebbe’s family, Shem Rokeach describes the warm friendship his mother and grandmother enjoyed with Rebbetzin Chaya Mushka, and recalls a time when the friendship helped save his mother’s life. (1970's)

6199119.title: On Taking Charge
6199119.description: Rabbi Yaakov Lieder recalls making the decision to become an emissary of the Rebbe in Sydney Australia. In what he thought was a noble sense of dedication to the Rebbe’s vision, he asked the Rebbe to send him wherever he saw fit. The Rebbe’s answer – or the lack of it – contained a powerful lesson. (1970's)

6199120.title: The Second Blessing
6199120.description: Rabbi Fabian Schonfeld, former president of the Rabbinical Council of America, recalls receiving a blessing from the Rebbe for his daughter to find a suitable match. After waiting a year for the blessing to materialize, he returned to 770 to take the issue up with the Rebbe. (1990's)

6199123.title: That’s Nothing?
6199123.description: Rabbi Sholom Geisinsky recalls that when his father moved from New York to Cleveland, Ohio, the Rebbe personally assisted him in securing a new rabbinic position. While he was very grateful to the Rebbe for his help, he was especially touched when the Rebbe’s persistent questioning reminded him of a personal matter. (1951)

6199124.title: The Power of Charity
6199124.description:
Rabbi Dovid Shochet recalls a most amazing story that took place following a lecture he had
given to students in Buffalo, New York. During his talk, he related a story which took place with a miser who was later revealed to be the secret benefactor of his entire town. After concluding his speech, Rabbi Shochet was approached by a young priest in the audience. Little did he know the impact of the story he had told. (1960's)

6199126.title: Billing the Rebbe
6199126.description: Rivkah Zakutinsky recalls the inspiration she gained from traveling with her class to visit the Rebbe. Motivated by the Rebbe to be proactive in spreading Judaism, she decided to begin a Shabbos group for the local Jewish children. She had everything in place to begin, except the necessary funds, until she reached out to the Rebbe.

6199127.title: Keeping the Focus
6199127.description:
Rabbi Laibl Wolf recalls being sent by the Rebbe to run a Chabad House at the University of
Madison, Wisconsin. In the weeks before Passover, wanting to grab the attention of the students, he put an advertisement in the local student newspaper. As with all of his work, he sent it to the Rebbe for review. The Rebbe’s feedback wasn’t just to the point; it has continued to guide him in
all his projects since. (1970)

6199128.title: Faith is Contagious
6199128.description: David Chase, a prominent businessman and philanthropist, recalls how one little request from the Rebbe had far-reaching effects on his life and the lives of others. (1983)

6199129.title: Tithes to Riches
6199129.description: Ami Pykovski recalls introducing designer Maurice Sasson to the Rebbe. Despite a successful career in the clothing business, Sasson was not seeing the returns from his work and turned to the Rebbe for help. (1990)

6199131.title: Ask Again
6199131.description: Winnie Gourarie remembers the story of when her husband got sick with appendicitis. Their uncle, Zalman Gurarie went to the Rebbe to ask for some urgent counsel. It took lots of faith to carry through with the Rebbe’s advice before they found out the real diagnosis. (1950's)

6199132.title: Three More Lights
6199132.description: Yehudah Clapman recalls arranging a private audience with the Rebbe for his cousins. After asking the girls in the family to light their own Shabbos candle, the Rebbe offered them a special gift to help them get started. When they tried to thank the Rebbe as they left, it was the Rebbe who thanked them instead.

6199135.title: The Teacher from Tekumah
6199135.description: Henny Karniel is a veteran educator living in Kfar Chabad, Israel. In 1975, as she was about to return to work after taking time off on maternity leave, she was approached with a particularly challenging job offer. After the Rebbe encouraged her to go ahead, she accepted the position. She saw immediate results, but it was only many years later that she found out what a big difference her efforts had made.

6199136.title: Lag B’omer Mint
6199136.description: Rabbi Chaim Yehuda Krinsky served in various positions of Chabad’s administrative staff and as a personal secretary to the Rebbe. In 1990, just days before the grand Lag B’Omer parade, the Rebbe asked him about the possibility of minting a batch of special coins commemorating the event. A seemingly impossible task to pull off in such short time, Rabbi Krinsky all but gave up. But after hearing how the Rebbe blamed himself for the last minute notice, he concluded that failure wasn’t an option. The coins were ready in time…

6199138.title: One Short Telegram
6199138.description: In 1967, Rabbi Shlomo Schwartz was part of a delegation of students sent by the Rebbe to revitalize the Toras Emes Yeshiva in Jerusalem. The group was in Israel on the cusp of the Six Day War. As the war drums were being beaten across the Arab world, many American Yeshiva students were leaving Israel in fear. After asking the Rebbe whether to stay or leave, the response that they got would make headlines in the Israeli Press and boost the morale of the country ahead of the war.

6199142.title: Restaurant Status
6199142.description:
In 1988, as a restaurant owner living in the Flatbush section of Brooklyn, Naftali Feldman was on
the dinner committee of Colel Chabad, the oldest operating charity in Israel. When the invitation for the dinner was sent to the Rebbe, it was his name – and restaurant – which the Rebbe inquired about. Wanting to only give the Rebbe positive news, he committed to bringing his establishment
up to standard.

6199143.title: Try to Remember
6199143.description: When Mr. Shaul Schiff handed his note to the Rebbe during a private audience in 1971, the Rebbe recognized his handwriting, but Mr. Schiff had no recollection of ever writing to the Rebbe before.

6199144.title: The Full Picture
6199144.description: Not long after the Rebbe launched the tefillin campaign, Mr. Bentzion Rader asked the Rebbe, “Why tefillin?”. The answer the Rebbe gave him, was only understood seven years later (1967).

6199145.title: Early Impressions
6199145.description: Yitzchak Popack recalls his memories from when the Rebbe and Rebbetzin arrived to the United States in 1941.

6199147.title: A Few Realistic Words
6199147.description:
As a young teenager, Charles Ramat would sometimes chauffer his teacher from time to time. Once, when his teacher had an audience with the Rebbe, Charles took the opportunity to ask the Rebbe’s advice in regards to his mother’s terminal illnes. The Rebbe’s realistic prognosis helped
him deal with the eventual outcome. (1968)

6199148.title: A Message for the President
6199148.description: Rabbi Shimon Lazaroff is the regional director of Chabad-Lubavitch of Texas. In 1973, when President Zalman Shazar of Israel was in Houston, Rabbi Lazaroff was among the local Jewish leaders invited to meet him at the airport. On the Rebbe’s advice, Rabbi Lazaroff took up the invitation and reminded President Shazar of his roots in Chabad.

6199149.title: It’s Who You Are
6199149.description: Rabbi Tzvi Grunblatt is the regional director of Chabad-Lubavitch in Argentina. In this account from 1976, he recalls his first shot at promoting the teachings of Judaism and Chassidism. After complaining to the Rebbe about what he felt was his lack of success, the Rebbe rejected this notion. The Rebbe’s answer, beyond inspiring him, is sure to remind of our own privileges and responsibilities.

6199150.title: A Painful Solution
6199150.description:
Eliezer Shefer serves as chairman of the World Organization of Orthodox Communities and Synagogues in Israel and the Diaspora. In 1971, he and two of his colleagues had an audience with the Rebbe.
At the time, Jerusalem was dealing with friction between segments of its community. Pained about the goings-on on both sides of the fighting, the Rebbe suggested a practical solution to try to tamp down the hostilities.

6199151.title: Yours Faithfully
6199151.description:
Esther Solomon is a veteran educator living in Israel. In 1969, she was diagnosed with an inability to give birth. Desperate for her own children, she and her husband flew to New York and arranged an audience with the Rebbe. After reprimanding them for not placing more faith in G-d, the Rebbe
gave the couple a blessing. But the story only reached its conclusion many years later.

6199154.title: Help from Above
6199154.description: Moshe Mandelbaum is a professor of economics and former Governor of the Bank of Israel. In 1967, while working to defend his thesis explaining the nature of Israel’s economy, he had an audience with the Rebbe. The Rebbe’s suggestion to him was eventually passed into law, and the cryptic statement the Rebbe left him with, helped him succeed in completing his thesis. (1989)

6199155.title: Music for the Mind
6199155.description: Michael Tabor is an educator and musician. In 1970, as a student at the London School of Economics, he had an audience with the Rebbe. After a conversation with the Rebbe about music and the arts, he learned an important lesson that has remained with him ever since.

6199157.title: A Son’s Obligation
6199157.description: In 1970, Mordechai Gorelik was granted permission to leave the Soviet Union. His parents and brother, Rabbi Elozor Gorelik, remained there, trapped behind the Iron Curtain. During his first audience with the Rebbe, he presented the Rebbe with a photograph of the resting place of the Rebbe’s father in Almaty, Kazakhstan.

6199158.title: A Wish Granted
6199158.description: Rabbi Yosef Mendelevitch is a Rabbi and teacher living in Jerusalem, Israel. He is famous for his struggles in Soviet Russia where he was imprisoned for almost a decade for his public attempts to immigrate to Israel from the Soviet Union. It is the Rebbe’s care and direction, however, which led him down the path on which he finds himself until this day.(year 1980)

6199159.title: The Rebbe’s Care
6199159.description: Rabbi Yitzchak Kogan serves as the director of the Bronnaya Synagogue in Moscow. He is a former refusenik and leading figure in the Soviet Jewish underground. Although he later had numerous encounters with the Rebbe, as a young child, all he knew was what he heard from his mother. (1981)

6199160.title: Give and Take
6199160.description: Zlata Hertzel is a veteran educator living in Israel. In the early 1970s, she had an audience with the Rebbe. Being both a young mother and a committed teacher meant that she found most of her earnings going towards childcare for her young children. Asking the Rebbe if she should quit her job evoked a response that has inspired her since.

6199161.title: Double Tipping
6199161.description: Rabbi Avraham Yitzchak Kiss is a restaurant manager and caterer living in Brooklyn, New York. As a young boy in the early 1960s, he had had an after-school job delivering groceries. As one of his customers, he merited to to deliver to the home of the Rebbe’s mother, Rebbetzin Chana Schneerson. Once, when he knocked at her door, he was surprised to see who opened.

6199162.title: A Special Invitation
6199162.description: Rabbi Ezra Schochet serves as dean of Yeshiva Ohr Elchonon Chabad in Los Angeles, California. In 1976, he was on a visit to New York with his wife and two children. When they arrived, he never thought he’d have a chance to meet with the Rebbe privately. But then he got an exciting message from the Rebbe’s secretary.

6199164.title: Common Bond
6199164.description: After spending a month at his ill father’s bedside, Dr. Stuart Ditchek had the unique privilege of meeting privately with the Rebbe. The Rebbe brought to light a common connection the two of them shared, and gave him an open invitation to visit. (1986)

6199165.title: Esrogim in Kfar Chabad
6199165.description: In the late 1950s, When Rabbi Nachman Elbaum raised the issue of using an esrog from a tree that had been grafted, the Rebbe gave him a solution and a mission. The result was a new orchard in the village of Kfar Chabad, Israel.

6199166.title: Spreading the Joy
6199166.description: Mendel Greenbaum recalls how the Rebbe waited to begin the Simchas Torah celebrations until the last of the Chasidim who had gone out on the Rebbe’s directive to spread the joy of the festival, had returned to 770. (1954)

6199167.title: A French Revolution
6199167.description: Rabbi Chaim Shneur Nisenbaum recalls his visit from France to Brooklyn to spend the High Holidays with the Rebbe, and the surprise that awaited him and his entire group. (1973)

6199168.title: Think for Yourself
6199168.description: In the late 1960s, Rabbi Mottel Krasnjasnki was a child growing up in the Crown Heights section of Brooklyn. (circa 1975)

6199169.title: Four Miracles
6199169.description: After six years of unsuccessfully trying to start a family, Fay Flood and her late husband, Vic, turned to the Rebbe for help and advice. (1978)

6199171.title: Peaceful Solution
6199171.description: Kasriel Oliver lives in Melbourne, Australia. In 1975 after becoming acquainted with Lubavitch, he came to spend the summer in 770. While there he had an audience with the Rebbe.

6199172.title: The One Mitzvah That Kept My Kids Jewish
6199172.description: In the 1970s, Charles Ramat had a number of audiences with the Rebbe. During one of these meetings, he asked the Rebbe about something he was struggling with.
path: The One Mitzvah That Kept My Kids Jewish

6199174.title: A Life’s Mission
6199174.description: Rabbi Yossi Gordon is a teacher in Yeshiva College in Melbourne Australia, and the director of Chabad of Tasmania. After hearing from the Rebbe about the greatness of serving Jews in remote places, he volunteered to assist in the Rebbe’s efforts to bring Judaism as far as Tasmania. A paper the Rebbe gave him before leaving keeps him inspired until this day.

6199175.title: Musical Harmony
6199175.description: Jeanne Zaidel-Rudolph is a composer, conductor, and professor of music at University of the Witwatersrand in Johannesburg, South Africa. As she and her husband became more observant, they travelled to New York for an audience with the Rebbe. Throughout their discussions, personal and professional, it was the Rebbe’s care that struck them most. (1981)

6199176.title: Two Halves of a Whole
6199176.description: In 1950, Rabbi Leibel and Thirza Posner became engaged to be married. The Rebbe, who was yet to officially accept leadership of Chabad after the passing of Rabbi Yosef Yitzchak Schneerson, granted them a private audience. During the meeting, the Rebbe shared with them the secret of what makes a marriage so special.

6199177.title: From Tennis to Tefillin
6199177.description: In 1970, Rabbi Sholom Ber Lipskar was sent as a Chabad emissary to Florida, where he serves as rabbi and director of The Shul in Bal Harbor. A member of his community, a champion tennis player, invited him to meet his wealthy friend. Bringing his Tefillin to the tennis courts began a relationship that lasted well beyond that first encounter. In fact, the impact of that meeting is still felt by hundreds of children today.

6199178.title: Doctor and Chasid
6199178.description: On Shmini Atzeres in 1977, the Rebbe suffered a massive heart attack during the dancing. For the next five weeks, Jews around the world prayed for the Rebbe’s health and wellbeing. Rabbi Mendel Groner, whose father was a personal secretary of the Rebbe, was a student at 770 at the time. Here, he recalls the joy that Chassidim felt when the Rebbe finally returned home

6199179.title: Bringing the Rebbe Joy
6199179.description: In 1985, important books and manuscripts were discovered missing from the Previous Rebbe’s Library. Following a surveillance operation, the culprit was found, leading to a long court battle over the ownership of the library itself. Throughout the battle, the Rebbe frequented and prayed at the resting place of his father-in-law and predecessor, the Previous Rebbe. Rabbi Mendel Azimov was a yeshiva student at the time, whose father, Rabbi Shmuel Azimov, was the Rebbe’s emissary to France. At one point, Rabbi Shmuel Azimov led an initiative in the Rebbe’s merit.

6199181.title: A Risky Business
6199181.description: In the late 1980s, Rabbi Shlomo Schwartz was a Chabad emissary in Los Angeles, California. He recalls having a great idea to pitch to producers in Hollywood. It was just after Rabbi Yitzchak Kogan got out of the Soviet Union, and writing a script about his story would be a great way to draw attention to the plight of the Jews that were stuck there. But after he asked the Rebbe for his blessing, all his plans were changed.

6199182.title: Fulfilling an Obligation
6199182.description: Rabbi Henry Isaacs served as rabbi on Bangor, Maine, for close to forty years. In 1958, he was a rabbinical student at Yeshiva University, and was engaged to be married. He had plans to enter the Armed Forces and join the Air Force. His father wouldn’t agree and unsure how to proceed, he turned to the Rebbe. The Rebbe’s advice on that night was more far-reaching than he could have ever imagined at the time.

6199183.title: A Change in Career
6199183.description: Meir Bastomski wasn’t raised in a Lubavitch family, so as he began to look and dress more like a Chabad Chassid, he also began to worry about any upset it might bring to his parents. It became so uncomfortable, that he was reluctant to return home for fear of causing friction in his relationship with them. Unsure of the best way to proceed, he asked the Rebbe for advice. (1967)

6199184.title: Everything in Its Time
6199184.description: Michael Allouche is an aerospace engineer from France. He asked the Rebbe numerous times about the prospect of making Aliya with his family and moving to Israel, yet he was always somewhat disappointed when the Rebbe discouraged them from doing so. When the Israeli Air Force embarked on a project to build their own fighter jet, it seemed like a most opportune time for him to relocate with his family. Yet for some reason, the Rebbe wouldn’t give them his blessing for the move. (1982)

6199186.title: A Community of Individuals
6199186.description: Nochum Stilerman grew up in the Crown Heights area of Brooklyn in the years following World War ll. It was in this immigrant community that his father decided to open a Kosher grocery store. Challenging all the naysayers, they managed to keep the store afloat and served many prominent customers in the process. Nochum would help his father with the deliveries, but was embarrassed by his menial work when he became of marriageable age. On one of his delivery stops, he asked the Rebbe for some advice. (1960s)

6199187.title: Sharing the Experience
6199187.description: Eliot Sovronsky is a videographer who was commissioned to film the Rebbe’s farbrengens in the 1970s. He was very pleased to hear that the Rebbe appreciated his concern for the Rebbetzin, the Rebbe’s wife, to be able to view the farbrengens on video.

6199188.title: Getting to Work
6199188.description: Shortly after getting married, Gittel Eidelman moved with her husband to Morocco as emissaries of the Rebbe. Having grown up in England, Morocco wasn’t exactly a natural place for her to end up living. It was an interesting place for them to have ended up, but with the Rebbe’s guidance, they succeeded in having a real impact on the community there. (1959)

6199189.title: A Picture Tells a Thousand Words
6199189.description: Rabbi Shimon Elituv is a rabbi in Mevaseret Zion and a member of the Chief Rabbinate Council. As a young boy, he sent his first letter to the Rebbe, beginning a relationship that has lasted since. Here, he remembers the help that the Rebbe provided to him and his family during difficult times. And it was the Rebbe’s guidance and inspiration that set him on his career path until this day. (1957)
path: A Picture Tells a Thousand Words

6199197.title: Seeking in Bangladesh
6199197.description: Max Cohen is a businessman from Manchester, England who was scheduled to make a trip to Bangladesh in April of 1991. Shortly before his trip, a powerful cyclone had struck the Chittagong district of southeastern Bangladesh, killing 138,000 people and leaving over ten million homeless. He was very worried about the safety of travelling there as more cyclone warnings were still in effect in that area. But a message he received from the Rebbe made him reconsider cancelling.

6199198.title: Any Further Questions?
6199198.description: Yehudis Fishman had an audience scheduled with the Rebbe late in the evening. The long wait outside the Rebbe’s room gave her time to think about some different questions that we wished the Rebbe would answer, and she was pleasantly surprised when the Rebbe afforded her that opportunity. Here, she remembers some of the questions that she asked. (1960s)

6199199.title: When Three Girls Left a Letter for the Rebbetzin
6199199.description: Devora Caytak heads the Jewish Youth Library in Ottawa, Canada. In 1978, after making her way back to Judaism, she was a seminary student at Machon Chana in the Crown Heights section of Brooklyn. Feeling alone, she and her friends decided to write a letter to the Rebbe’s wife, Rebbetzin Chaya Mushka. The Rebbetzin’s surprising response is a lesson that Devorah has implemented in her own life until this day.
path: When Three Girls Left a Letter for the Rebbetzin

6199200.title: No Appointment Necessary
6199200.description: Rabbi Yaakov Shpitzer was director of the Sanz-Klausenberg institutions in Israel before becoming the chief gabbai of the Imrei Shefer community in Jerusalem. In the early 1980s, his niece was suffering from a particularly aggressive cancer that doctors said left her with slim chances for survival. During an audience with the Rebbe, he raised her plight and left the meeting with specific instructions of what to do.

6199201.title: Closed for Business
6199201.description: Today, Harvey Milstein is a businessman living in Israel. As a child, however, he grew up in the Crown Heights section of Brooklyn where his father owned a pharmacy. While his father was a respected member of the religious community, he still struggled with the idea of closing his business on Shabbos and Jewish holidays. But a letter from the Rebbe finally convinced him to change his mind. (1960)

6199202.title: Straight to the Top
6199202.description: Rabbi Efraim Schmuckler has served as rabbi of the Geriatric Center in Montreal, Canada for over thirty years. In 1970, during an audience with the Rebbe, he asked for a blessing that his uncle succeed in leaving Soviet Russia. The Rebbe gave him a blessing, but made it conditional on him keeping it secret. He was elated to have received assurances from the Rebbe, but was dismayed when he failed to live up to the condition the Rebbe had set.

6199204.title: A Gift for Your Father
6199204.description: Menasheh Janashvilli lives in Lud, Israel. As a teenager in the 1970s, he travelled to the United States to study at the United Lubavitcher Yeshiva in Brooklyn, New York. The Rebbe’s words to him after Pesach made him wonder if everything was okay with his father back in Israel. It was only after he finally reached his father on the telephone that he began to appreciate the full story.

6199205.title: A Torah of Truth
6199205.description: Rabbi Sholom Rephune is an educator and community activist. In the early 1970s, while serving as principal of Manhattan Day School, he made an appointment to see the Rebbe. It was an important meeting for him, as he had a long list of questions that he wished to ask the Rebbe about reconciling science with the Torah.

6199207.title: A Teenager’s Dream
6199207.description: Golda Jacobs is a career counselor and consultant. As a teenager growing up in Chicago in the 1960s, she had a strong desire to travel on Zim Lines, a shipping company that offered rides to Israel. After her father heard her plans to travel alone with another female friend, he raised concerns about their safety. Golda wasn’t willing to let go of her dream so easily, and decided to ask the Rebbe what to do.

6199208.title: Different Strokes for Different Folks
6199208.description: Rabbi Raphael Aron is the director of the Gateway family Counseling Centre in Melbourne, Australia. In 1974, while running the Lubavitch Youth Organization in Melbourne, he had an audience with the Rebbe. At the time, he was looking for a way to deal with the opposition they were receiving for the rambunctious nature of their Mitzvah campaigns. The Rebbe’s response was somewhat surprising, and has remained with him since.

6199209.title: More Than a Donation
6199209.description: In 1975, Rabbi Yekusiel Yehudah Halberstam, the Sanz-Klausenburger Rebbe, opened a not-for-profit hospital in Netanya, Israel. He appointed Rabbi Gershon Lieder to oversee the project while it was still in the early stages of development, and as the eventual director of the hospital. As part of their effort, the fundraising committee decided to visit the Lubavitcher Rebbe in Brooklyn, to ask for his assistance and advice.

6199210.title: The Start of a Campaign
6199210.description: Rabbi Chaim Jacobs and his wife Sora, have been the co-directors of Lubavitch of Scotland for more than four decades. In 1967, the Rebbe launched the now famous Tefillin campaign. A Yeshiva student at the time, Rabbi Jacobs began an initiative for students to visit the local Jews and help them don Tefillin. He remembers the Rebbe’s warm responses to the work they were doing.

6199211.title: A Rising Threat
6199211.description: Shlomo Shamir is a journalist and political analyst. He was the New York correspondent for the Israeli daily, Haaretz, for over thirty-five years, and a long time columnist for the Algemeiner Journal. He met and corresponded with the Rebbe on numerous occasions over the years, but it was an indirect message that he received from the Rebbe that led him to send the Rebbe an apology. (1979)

6199212.title: Help Your Friend First
6199212.description: Mrs. Rochel Fogelman and her husband, Rabbi Hershel Fogelman, of blessed memory, have been Chabad emissaries in Worcester, Massachusetts since 1947. She remembers asking the Rebbe repeatedly for a blessing for her sister to find her match. Her sister seemed so choosy, it almost looked like there wouldn’t be anyone who’d meet her qualifications. The matter was on her mind again when she brought a group with her to the Rebbe from Worcester, Massachusetts in the 1950s. Thankfully, she finally received the blessing she was seeking when the Rebbe asked her to help someone else.

6199213.title: This is for Your Child
6199213.description: Rabbi Simcha Krakovsky is a community activist and served as a secretary of the Lelover Rebbe in Bnei Brak, Israel. When he and his wife struggled to have children, a friend of his, Mordechai Werdiger, invited Rabbi Krakovsky to visit the Rebbe and ask for a blessing. (1989)

6199214.title: A Rebbe, A Mentch
6199214.description: Rabbi Chaim Zev Bomzer was a longstanding member of the Rabbinical Council of America, and Rabbi of Young Israel of Ocean Parkway for more than forty years. It was during the sixties that over the course of his travels to Israel, he developed a relationship with the chief chaplain of the Israeli Army, Rabbi Shlomo Goren. Once, when Rabbi Goren was in New York, he asked Rabbi Bomzer to take him to see the Rebbe.

6199215.title: They Need to Spread Outside
6199215.description: Rabbi Tzvi Greenwald was an educator living in Kfar Chabad. In the 1960s, he was involved in the “Evening with Chabad” outreach program, visiting kibbutzim across Israel. After receiving criticism for his approach toward the attendees and the atmosphere at the events, he decided to ask the Rebbe how to continue his activities.

6199216.title: Spiritual Extravagance
6199216.description: Rabbi Sholom Spalter is on the faculty of the Rabbinical College of America in Morristown, New Jersey. Before his Bar Mitzvah, his father wrote to the Rebbe. The Rebbe’s memorable response changed his Bar Mitzvah, as well as those of his children. (1967)

6199218.title: Living to See Nachas
6199218.description: In 1974, Rabbi Shimon and Goldie Feld became engaged. But while they were making plans for their wedding celebration, they were also receiving worrying news from the doctors who were treating Goldie’s father for a cancer that he was battling. When some Chassidim suggested that they ask the Rebbe for a blessing for him to be able to attend the wedding, they grabbed the opportunity.

6199219.title: A Healthy Diet
6199219.description: Rabbi Yosef Yitzchak Gurewitz serves on the faculty of Yeshiva Tomchei Temimim in Migdal Haemek, Israel. He remembers how when his wife was expecting, she started feeling severe pains which impacted her breathing. After receiving a diagnosis, they were strongly urged by her doctor to go ahead with surgery. After asking the Rebbe a number of times about how to proceed, they finally received an answer - albeit not one that they or their doctor were expecting. (1979)

6199220.title: If at First You Don’t Succeed
6199220.description: David Mintz is the founder and CEO of Tofutti Brands. In the early 1980s he was the proprietor of Mintz’s Buffet, a kosher catering business in New York. With an eye on expanding his catering business, he asked the Rebbe for a blessing. The answer he received was unequivocal: he should not pursue this opportunity. Instead, the Rebbe encouraged him to continue his experimentations with creating frozen tofu desserts. Looking back, it almost seems obvious. But at the time, it took a great level of trust to heed the Rebbe’s advice.
path: If at First You Don’t Succeed

6199221.title: Surgeon Without Surgery
6199221.description: Dr. Leonard Lovitch is a general surgeon in Whittier, California. Originally members of a Conservative temple in North Hollywood, he and his wife were first introduced to Chabad in the mid-1970s. At one point, still in the beginning of his career, he was stepping on an unstable stool when he slipped and injured his eye. The prognosis wasn’t good, and he decided to ask the Rebbe for advice. He did, in fact, get an answer from the Rebbe, but it had no apparent connection to the injury of his eye. (1982)

6199222.title: Documenting History
6199222.description: Rabbi Naftali Tzvi Gottlieb was an author and biographer living in Betar Illit, Israel. Bothered by the fact that so little was known about the Rebbes’ father, he decided to write a book about him. (1960s)

6199223.title: Never Stuck
6199223.description: Stranded in an airport away from their families, Miryam Swerdlov recalls the phone call made to the Rebbe. The Rebbe’s response was a life lesson for all Jews. (1967)

6199224.title: To Each in His Way
6199224.description: Rabbi Nochum Cohen is an educator and rabbi serving the needs of diverse Jewish communities across Israel. During a trip to the United States in the 1970s, he had an audience with the Rebbe.

6199225.title: Like a Father
6199225.description: Rabbi Tzvi Abba Lerman recalls the special attention the Rebbe gave him in the early 1950s, in connection to his wedding.

6199226.title: Gaining Approval
6199226.description: Rabbi Gad Bouskila has served as rabbi of Congregation Netivot Israel in Brooklyn, New York, for over three decades. Originally from Morocco, he was a yeshiva student in Lakewood, New Jersey, in 1980.

6199227.title: An Effort to Innovate
6199227.description: Rabbi Yitzchok Sufrin is an administrator of the Lubavitch Foundation in the United Kingdom. In 1962 he was a student at the Central Lubavitch Yeshiva in Brooklyn, New York, and engaged to be married.

6199228.title: Sounding the Shofar
6199228.description: Rabbi Sholom Tenenbaumis an educator living in Brooklyn New York. Beginning in the early 1950s his father, Rabbi Yosef Menachem Tenenbaum, would sound the Shofar on Rosh Hashanah in 770.

6199229.title: Sound Advice
6199229.description: Rabbi Avraham Tanzer has served as head of Yeshiva College and spiritual leader of the Glenhazel Hebrew Congregation in Johannesburg, South Africa, for over five decades. In 1966, he had an audience with the Rebbe.

6199230.title: Matters of Faith
6199230.description: Yosef Shandling reconnected to his Jewish roots as a senior in college. In 1970, as a student in Yeshiva Hadar Hatorah in Brooklyn, New York, he had an audience with the Rebbe.

6199231.title: Waiting for an answer
6199231.description: Rabbi Shmuel Rodal has served as a Chabad emissary, educator, and rabbi of the Beth Shlomo Synagogue in Milan, Italy, for close to fifty years. In the mid-1960s he was a student in Yeshiva Tomchei Temimim in Kfar Chabad, Israel.

6199232.title: Mystery Solved
6199232.description: Rabbi Yechiel Michel Stern is a prolific author and rabbi of the Ezrat Torah neighborhood in Jerusalem. In the early 1980s, he served on Israel’s ministry of religious services, supervising numerous mikvahs in Jerusalem and across Israel.

6199233.title: A Grounding Experience
6199233.description: Michoel Muchnik is a foremost Jewish artist living in Brooklyn, New York. In the early 1970s, he was a student at the Rabbinical College of America, in Morristown, New Jersey, when he had an audience with the Rebbe.

6199234.title: The Right Balance
6199234.description: Rabbi Chaim Moshe Bergstein serves as the director of Chabad of Farmington Hills, Michigan. As a student in Yeshiva in Israel, he internalized the lessons of his rabbis in Yeshiva about refraining from materialism and physical desires. But he couldn’t reconcile this idea with living a happy life. With this seeming contradiction in mind, he resolved to write to the Rebbe. (1969)

6199235.title: All in the Right Time
6199235.description: Rabbi Menachem Mendel Gluckowsky serves as rabbi of the Chabad community in Rechovot, Israel. He was part of a special delegation of emissaries sent by the Rebbe to Israel, where he married and raised a family. When his newborn son had jaundice, he feared that he would not be able to have the Bris on time. He asked for a blessing from the Rebbe, but only later discovered the care and attention the Rebbe had given him. (1989)

6199236.title: Ask the Rabbi
6199236.description: Rabbi Moshe Havlin serves as the Ashkenazi Chief Rabbi of Kiryat Gat in Israel, where he lives with his family. After his wife gave birth to two sons and a daughter, she suffered a number of miscarriages. When doctors recommended an operation, they decided to ask the Rebbe for advice and blessing. (1981)

6199237.title: In the Moment
6199237.description: Dovber Klein lives in Manchester, England, where he teaches in a boy’s school. As a student who was reconnecting to his Jewish roots he asked the Rebbe a wide range of questions, ranging from black magic to how much one should sleep at night. (1970s)

6199238.title: A Time for Everything
6199238.description: Rabbi Zalman Gopin is a mentor at the yeshiva in Kfar Chabad, Israel. As a student, he once asked the Rebbe about how to best deal with the mood swings a person experiences. He would have expected the Rebbe to say that sadness is a bad thing, unequivocally. To his surprise, the Rebbe’s answer was much more unpredictable. (1960s)

6199240.title: Who Is a Chasid?
6199240.description: Professor David Weiss was issued a special passport by the Soviet Union that allowed him to reach Jews that others couldn’t. At one point, the Rebbe asked him to come for a meeting to discuss the state of Jewish affairs in the USSR. in this interview, he recalls some of the points that were addressed at that meeting. (1965)

6199241.title: Living in the Present
6199241.description: Rabbi Avraham Glick was a shliach in Worcester, Massachusetts when he was asked to join the Chabad Representatives in Melbourne, Australia. The Rebbe approved of his move but advised him not to move right away but to wait a while. Feeling like he was in limbo, he wasn’t sure about how to proceed with his Chabad activities. But upon mentioning his feelings to the Rebbe, he was given an entirely new perspective. (1970)

6199242.title: Success in All You Need
6199242.description: Daniel Finkelman is a producer and filmmaker living in Brooklyn, New York. In the late 1980s he was a young child growing up in Jerusalem when he contracted a severe eye condition that made it very difficult for him to see. When his family moved to the United States, a family friend urged his father to seek the Rebbe’s blessing - a blessing that has since been fulfilled in more than one way.

6199243.title: Becoming a Shochet in the USSR
6199243.description: Rabbi Yitzchak Kogan serves as rabbi of the Bronnaya Synagogue in Moscow. He is a former Refusenik and leading figure in the Soviet Jewish underground. Under the intrusively watchful eye of the Soviet authorities, it was most difficult to obtain Kosher meat. Without any alternative, he decided to become a qualified Kosher slaughterer himself. But it was the Rebbe’s encouragement and blessings from afar that kept his spirit alive. (1980s)
path: Becoming a Shochet in the USSR

6199244.title: Only the Rebbe Knew Her Secret...
6199244.description: Rabbi Yitzchak Wineberg has served as director of Chabad of British Columbia for over four decades. He remembers a particularly interesting story that took place when someone asked him to reach out to the Rebbe for a blessing for his non-Jewish wife. Or so he thought. (1970s)
path: Only the Rebbe Knew Her Secret...

6199246.title: With a Whole Heart
6199246.description: Gila Lilian works in recruitment consultancy in Johannesburg, South Africa, where she lives with her husband and family. She was six months pregnant when the doctor delivered some frightening news about the baby. But as it turned out, it was the doctors who were shocked in the end. (1983)

6199248.title: A Real Connection
6199248.description: Rabbi Nosson Gurary is the founder of the Chabad Student Center at the State University of New York, Buffalo. In the 1960s, as a yeshiva student in Brooklyn, New York, he began suffering from chest pain. Upon turning to the Rebbe for advice, he was sent to a doctor who would calm him of his concerns. Years later, the Rebbe still remembered about the incident.

6199249.title: Two Kinds of Trees
6199249.description: Rabbi Zev Litenatsky was an accomplished educator from Los Angeles, California. He grew up in Montreal, Canada in the 1940s and 50s, when, before his Bar Mitzvah, he accompanied his father for a private audience with the Rebbe. He recalls the Rebbe asking him a peculiar question. And teaching him a lesson that has remained with him since.

6199250.title: A Blessing and a Contribution
6199250.description: Mrs. Esther Sternberg is the director of the Shabbos Candle Campaign, a division of the Lubavitch Women's Organization. She was involved in the medical care of the Rebbe’s wife, Rebbetzin Chaya Mushka, until the Rebbetzin’s passing in 1988. While the Rebbe was still sitting Shiva, the Shabbos Candle Campaign announced a new fund in honor of Rebbetzin Chaya Mushka. They didn’t inform the Rebbe of the new campaign, but once the Shiva was over, the Rebbe called her and her father to his home on President Street.

6199251.title: Postponed Indefinitely
6199251.description: Rabbi Dovid Golowinski is the director of the Kosher Organics supervision agency. He grew up in Brooklyn New York, and in the summer of 1968 was a student at Lubavitcher Yeshiva in Montreal, Canada. When he went to visit his brother in camp, his eye suddenly began to hurt - badly. Upon examination, specialists insisted that he have an operation. But the Rebbe didn’t agree.

6199253.title: A Personal Interest
6199253.description: Mrs. Chaya Hecht served as an early education teacher in Brooklyn, New York, for over five decades. In the early 1950s, shortly after he had assumed leadership of the Chabad movement, she had an audience with the Rebbe. The Rebbe asked her if she was praying every day. When she answered that she didn’t really have the time to pray, the Rebbe suggested a new approach. And she’s adopted it as a part of her daily life.

6199254.title: Self Help
6199254.description: Rabbi Avraham Krishevsky lived in Betar Illit, Israel, where he was involved in the production of Tefillin. In this interview, he remembers a friend that he had in Crown Heights who spiraled into a life of drugs and other bad behavior. Unable to help him on his own, he succeeded in convincing his friend to write to the Rebbe. But the fellow had one condition: it couldn’t go through the Rebbe’s office; his letter could only be read by the Rebbe himself. (1980s)

6199256.title: "The Rebbe Told Me to Be Like a Spider"
6199256.description: Yossi Rosenstein is an artist living in Bnei Brak, Israel. In the late 1970s he travelled to New York for an exhibition of his work. It was a most interesting sequence of events that led him to arrange a meeting with the Rebbe. The Rebbe discussed the importance of his art, but encouraged him to teach the skill to others. He had no idea where to begin, but to his great surprise, someone approached him.
path: "The Rebbe Told Me to Be Like a Spider"

6199257.title: A Medical Recommendation
6199257.description: Rabbi Zevulun Charlop is a prominent American rabbi and Dean Emeritus of the Rabbi Isaac Elchanan Theological Seminary, where he served for over thirty-five years. He remembers when his mother suddenly became ill and lost her sight. They quickly discovered that she was suffering from a stroke, and after stabilizing her, the doctor recommended a risky procedure. But first, they had to ask the Rebbe. (1950s)

6199258.title: The Power of Thought
6199258.description: Mrs. Chana Popack and her husband served as Chabad emissaries in Philadelphia for three decades. She was born in Soviet Russia during Stalinist times, and her father was at a loss about where to send her to school. He couldn’t communicate directly with the Rebbe, for fear of being intercepted by the Soviet authorities. But through various maneuvers, he managed to get advice from the Rebbe, and somehow, the Rebbe’s unlikely idea worked. (1930s)

6199259.title: A Good Role Model
6199259.description: In the early 1970s, Diane Abrams practiced law in New York and taught the nation’s first “Women and the Law” course at NYU. Her husband, Robert Abrams served as New York State Attorney General. The Rebbe, whom she met a number of times, kept bringing up the same thing – she had to write a book.

6199260.title: Our Sages Teach Us
6199260.description: In 1956 Rabbi Eitan Green was a yeshiva student in Beis Medrash Govoha in Lakewood, New Jersey, when he had an audience with the Rebbe. He had a theory about the precise accuracy of some of the statements made by our sages. The Rebbe fundamentally disagreed, and referenced Einstein’s Theory of Relativity to make his point.

6199261.title: “Don’t Worry, He’s Coming”
6199261.description: Mr. Freddy Hager lived in London, England. One year, he made an unexpected stop at 770 on his way to the airport to return to England. But it soon became clear that his visit was not entirely unexpected after all. (1980s)

6199263.title: Judaism on the Go
6199263.description: Moshe Kagan is a consultant living in Jerusalem, Israel. In the early 1960s, he arrived from England to attend yeshiva in 770. He was one of the few Yeshiva students with a driver’s license, and it worked in his favor. He was one of a group of students who got together to launch a new project – a mobile mitzvah vehicle.

6199265.title: Private Admission
6199265.description: Rabbi Hershel Feigelstock served as principal of the Lubavitch Yeshiva in Montreal for some forty years. In the 1940s, as a Yeshiva student at 770, he spent the holiday of Passover in New York. In a fascinating interview, he recalls the Rebbe inviting him to the private Passover meal of his father-in-law and predecessor, Rabbi Yosef Yitzchak Schneerson.

6199266.title: A Natural Miracle
6199266.description: Rabbi Zvi Hartman is an esteemed Chassidic mentor in Beit Shemesh, Israel. In the 1960s, he served as Principal of Bet Sefer Lemlacha for vocational training in Kfar Chabad, Israel. After being married for some five years without being able to have children, he and his wife decided to ask the Rebbe for a blessing. They carried out the Rebbe’s instructions in New York but seemed to hit a wall. But everything would change after they met a doctor that the Rebbe referred them to in Tel Aviv.

6199267.title: Believing in Youth
6199267.description: Shimshon Stock headed the Chevra Simchas Shabbos V’Yom Tov charity fund for thirty years. In the 1940s, he was a rambunctious teenager growing up in the Crown Heights section of Brooklyn. One day, on the way to a ball game with his friend, he met the Rebbe. They didn’t expect it, but they then got a Torah lesson from baseball. (Late 1940s and Early 1950s)

6199268.title: Three Conditions
6199268.description: Milek Kremer served as deputy chairman of the Regional Council of Kiryat Ono, Israel. In 1963, his work brought him to the United States. With one of his children interested in becoming religious, he decided to ask the Rebbe for help and advice. The Rebbe agreed to help them – on three conditions…

6199269.title: A Doctor with Solutions
6199269.description: Rabbi Moshe Weiss serves as director of Chabad of Sherman Oaks, California. He was married in 1983 but struggled to have children. He visited the Rebbe a number of times and merited to receive numerous blessings, but they never seemed to materialize. It was only many years later that something finally changed. (1991)

6199270.title: More Than Stories
6199270.description: In the mid-1970s, Rabbi Gershon Burkis was a member of the Religious Council in the city of Lod, Israel. With a number of children in their schools reaching the age for reading books, he decided to do something about the dearth of quality Jewish educational reading. With blessings and direction from the Rebbe, the Machanayim collection was born.

6199272.title: The Simple Answer
6199272.description: Yaakov Abrams is a business appraiser and author on business evaluation living in Los Angeles, California. In the early 1980s, in the midst of exploring his Jewish roots, he began to suffer tremendous pain related to a personal matter.
