He decided to write to the Rebbe about it and hoped for a response that could make everything clear and easy. But that’s not what he got, at least not right away… (1984)

6199275.title: A Good Incentive
6199275.description: Rabbi Chaim Cohen is a Jewish community activist living in Jerusalem. In 1984, he accompanied the Rebbe of Sadigura for an audience with the Rebbe. After informing the Rebbe about a new annual journal that he had begun publishing, the Rebbe encouraged him to do so even more often. Years later, he returned to show the Rebbe the fruits of his suggestion. (1984)

6199276.title: The Common Goal
6199276.description: Shmuel Abramson works in special education and lives in Monsey, New York. As a college student in the mid-1970s, he began to re-connect to his Jewish heritage. After getting engaged to his wife-to-be, he and his fiancé went to the Rebbe to seek a blessing before getting married. During their audience, he took the opportunity to ask two questions of the Rebbe. Their answers have guided him until this day. (1977)

6199277.title: A Summer to Remember
6199277.description: Tzipporah Edelkopf was born in Kharkov, in the Soviet Republic of Ukraine. As a young girl, she managed to immigrate with her family to Israel. Her parents traveled to the Rebbe but couldn’t afford to bring her along. When the Rebbe heard why she was missing, he arranged for his emissary in Israel to get her a ticket to New York. But once she arrived, the Rebbe had a job for her. (1971)

6199278.title: Keep Going
6199278.description: After her arrival in the Crown Heights section of Brooklyn over a decade earlier, Esther Mentz was appointed as a co-president of the N’shei Chabad Women’s Movement in the late 1960s.

6199279.title: Twenty-Four Hours a Day
6199279.description: Rabbi Binyomin Klein served as a longtime secretary of the Rebbe. He joined the Rebbe’s staff in 1963.

6199281.title: Unbroken Spirit
6199281.description: Reb Mottel Lifshitz, a key figure in the Soviet Jewish underground, served as Moscow’s only ritual slaughterer for almost three decades, and performed countless clandestine circumcisions.

6199282.title: My Generals
6199282.description: David Mayer lives with his family in Los Angeles, California, where he was an executive in the toy industry. (Early 1980s)

6199283.title: Safe Skies
6199283.description: Rabbi Dr. Chaim Shine is a professor of law in Israel and a columnist for the Israel Hayom newspaper. In the late 1970s he joined his uncle, David Shine, then director of El Al in North America, for an audience with the Rebbe. Concerned with the flight security on El Al’s planes, Mr. Shine brought up the issue with the Rebbe. The Rebbe’s advice surprised him at first, but taking heed of the Rebbe’s words, he led the effort to implement them at El Al. (Late 1970s)

6199284.title: On the Battlefield
6199284.description: Ronnie Romberg and her husband, Dr. Henry Romberg, met at Case Western University in Cleveland, Ohio and were married in 1968. Having long dreamed of making Aliyah and moving to Israel, they had all their plans set. All until a Chabad friend of theirs convinced them to ask the Rebbe’s advice first. To make a long story short, they didn’t get the answer they were expecting.

6199286.title: Unnecessary Surgery
6199286.description: Eitan Ben-David is a businessman and philanthropist living in Jerusalem, Israel. In the 1970s, with his father suffering from a heart condition, they were unsure whether to operate or not. After writing to the Rebbe, they finally received a response: no surgery was necessary. His doctor wasn’t too confident about the Rebbe’s ability to know the details of the case, but couldn’t override the patient’s wishes.

6199287.title: A Personal Request
6199287.description: Israel Singer is a Jewish activist, academic and former secretary general of the World Jewish Congress. In the mid-1970s, he taught political science in New York and served on the staff of President Gerald Ford. When he visited the Rebbe in preparation for a trip to the Soviet Union, the Rebbe asked him for a personal favor. The feeling of privilege from carrying out the Rebbe’s wishes at that time, has remained the most special experience of his life to this day. (1974)

6199291.title: Fighting for Israel
6199291.description: Gedalya Schreiber has served as director-general of Israel’s Religious Affairs Ministry and as director-general of its Chief Rabbinate. In 1980, he joined the entourage of the Sadigura Rebbe for an audience with the Rebbe.

6199292.title: Higher Education
6199292.description: Rabbi Osher Ehrenreich has served as dean of Bais Yaakov High School for Girls in the Boro Park section of Brooklyn for over six decades. In 1968, he and a group of supporters had an audience with the Rebbe.

6199293.title: A Second Look
6199293.description: Born in the Soviet Union, Rabbi Mottel Chein is now a communal activist living in the Crown Heights section of Brooklyn. In the late 1950s, he was a student at the Tomchei Temimim yeshiva in Lod, Israel.

6199295.title: The King in the Field
6199295.description: Yaakov Abrams is a business appraiser and author on business evaluation, living in Los Angeles, California. He was married to his wife Chana in the mid-1980s. (1986)

6199297.title: Repentance and Healing
6199297.description: Rabbi Ephraim Rosenblum serves as principal of Yeshiva Boys School in Pittsburgh, Pennsylvania. In the 1950s, he was a student at the Central Lubavitch Yeshiva in Brooklyn, New York. The students would go out to different cities and disseminate the books of Chasidism and talk to people. Everything was going smoothly until they were involved in a scary accident. (1954)

6199298.title: Investing in the Future
6199298.description: Professor Shlomo Eckstein is the former president and director of Bar Ilan University in Tel Aviv, Israel. In the 1950s, he was a leader in the B’nei Akiva youth movement and was disappointed by his lack of results. After writing a letter to the Rebbe expressing his feelings, he received a response that changed his entire perspective.

6199299.title: A Chandelier in Heaven
6199299.description: Rabbi Nochum Stilerman is an accomplished fundraiser for various Jewish charities and institutions. As a teenager in the late 1950s, he ran deliveries for his father’s grocery store in Brooklyn, New York. His customers included Rebbetzin Chana Schneerson, the Rebbes’ mother. The Rebbetzin enjoyed talking to him, and on one occasion, he decided to ask her a question. He didn’t know that she’d tell the Rebbe all about it.

6199301.title: Let’s Make a Deal
6199301.description: Rabbi Mendel Lipskar is the Executive Director of Chabad of South Africa and serves as rabbi of the Shul at Hyde Park in Johannesburg. He grew up in Toronto, Canada, where his father was on the staff of Camp Gan Israel. To his surprise, when he went to visit the Rebbe with his father, the Rebbe made him an offer that he could not refuse. (1960)

6199304.title: The Doctors Said I Was Going Blind
6199304.description: Yisroel Swimmer is a chief financial officer living in Lawrence, New York. In the 1980s, he was a child growing up in Johannesburg, South Africa. (1983)
path: The Doctors Said I Was Going Blind

6199306.title: Unpack the Merchandise
6199306.description: Rabbi Shimon Bekerman serves on the board of the Chabad Youth Organization in Israel. In 1965 he traveled to New York for the month of Tishrei and had his first audience with the Rebbe.

6199308.title: It’s No Mistake
6199308.description: Rabbi Elchanan Jaacobovez is a veteran educator living in Nachlat Har Chabad, Israel. He was married in 1966. (Mid 1970s)

6199309.title: Do Not be Afraid!
6199309.description: An excerpt from the Jewish Educational Media film, Switch. Shortly after his arrival from Israel in 1963, Rabbi Chaim Benyamini established the Machneh Israel yeshiva in Petropolis, Brazil, which he headed for over three decades.

6199311.title: The Best Way to Help
6199311.description: Rabbi Shmarya Katzen was a beloved teacher for close to five decades. After becoming observant in the 1960s and spending several years in yeshivas, he began to think about his life ahead. The Rebbe encouraged him to take an aptitude test to discover how to best use his unique talents, and it was this that led him to his long career as an educator, with the Rebbe’s guidance and blessings.

6199313.title: No Place Too Small
6199313.description:
Rabbi Yaakov Reitzes has served as rabbi of Yesod Hama’ala and the Upper Galilee in Israel for
close to forty years. In 1976 he was part of a delegation of students sent by the Rebbe to Israel, where he remained and married. After receiving an offer to move as the Chabad emissary to Yesod Hama’ala, a tiny settlement at the time, he and his wife asked the Rebbe if it was worth their time and effort. By now, they know it was and continues to be.

6199315.title: As Old as You Feel
6199315.description: Dr. Louis Teichholz is a leading cardiologist. In 1977, he was a Head of Cardiology at Mount Sinai Hospital in New York. When, on the holiday of Shmini Atezers in 1977, the Rebbe suffered a massive heart attack, he was asked to join a team of doctors treating the Rebbe at 770. It was there that he merited to converse with the Rebbe about many fascinating topics.

6199316.title: Seeing is Believing
6199316.description: In the 1960s, Moshe Kagan was a student at 770, the Central Lubavitch yeshiva in Brooklyn, New York. It was during this time that his father was in a car accident which caused him to lose his eyesight. His father wanted to avoid bringing any unnecessary pain to his family, and suggested to the Rebbe that he might not participate in his own son’s wedding. The Rebbe did not agree, and gave him a very special blessing.

6199318.title: Two Fateful Letters
6199318.description:
Rabbi Sholom Ber Schapiro is a veteran educator living in Brooklyn, New York. In the early
1980s he was a teacher in the Yeshiva of Brooklyn when he was approached by a student’s parent who had an offer for a business opportunity. After receiving the consent of his boss, he asked the Rebbe for a blessing which he received with a condition. A story about making sure every Jewish child has a letter in a Torah scroll.

6199319.title: A Chanukah Miracle
6199319.description:
In the early 1950s, Shmuel Langsam was a young child growing up in the Crown Heights section
of Brooklyn, New York. It was Chanukah time when his mother received some frightening news from the doctor. In 1952, this cancer wasn’t something that could be cured. In desperation, they pulled all the strings they could, for her to receive the Rebbe’s blessing. When they finally got to the Rebbe, he wasn’t worried at all, much to their relief.

6199320.title: Living with the Times
6199320.description:
Rabbi Yisroel Rubin has served as the director of Chabad of the Capital District in Albany, New York, for over forty years.
In the summer of 1970, he was on the staff of Camp Gan Israel of Montreal, Canada. He wanted to do something to encourage the children to study Chitas, a daily portion from the Chumash, Psalms, and Tanya. His project ended up lasting longer than the short summer he had planned, and the Rebbe’s blessings and encouragement motivated him throughout.

6199321.title: Let’s Make a Deal
6199321.description: Rabbi Nachman Sudak was the director of Chabad’s operations in the United Kingdom for over five decades. At one particular point of financial strain, he turned to a supporter asking for help. The amount they had to come up with seemed way beyond their reach, but with faith, perseverance, and many blessings from the Rebbe, the story finally came to a happy end. (mid 1980s)

6199323.title: Home Remedy
6199323.description: In the late 1950s, Chana Chanowitz and her Husband, Chaim Chanowitz, were living on the Upper West Side of New York City. At one point, Chaim was plagued by terrible stomach ulcers. The doctors urged an urgent surgery, but when they asked the Rebbe, they received different advice.

6199325.title: Worth Waiting
6199325.description: Eitan Ben-David is a businessman and philanthropist living in Jerusalem, Israel. In the early ‘70s, his wife had become pregnant, but the doctors deemed the pregnancy unsafe due to a condition that she was suffering from, and advised them to go through with an abortion. Unsure about how to proceed within the parameters of Jewish law, they penned an urgent letter to the Rebbe.

6199326.title: Like a Father
6199326.description:
Rabbi Sholom Ber Gorodetsky was appointed by the Rebbe to serve as the director general of the European and North African Bureau of Chabad-Lubavitch.
The Bureau was established by his father at the request of Rabbi Yosef Yitzchak Schneerson, the Previous Rebbe, shortly after the family's arrival in the United States from Europe.

142953.title: "It wasn't me; thank Him!"
142953.description: Mr. Robert Abrams served as New York State attorney general from 1978 to 1994. He and his wife, Diane, an attorney herself, would come to the Rebbe for Lekach on Hoshana Rabbah. In 1985, the Rebbe gave them an unexpected blessing for an addition to their family.

527752.title: In Berlin
527752.description: Studying in Berlin at the same time with the Rebbe was Rabbi Joseph B. Soloveichik, his students heard from him about the encounters with the Rebbe in Berlin. Three of his students tell of these encounters.

527033.title: Coffee in Berlin
527033.description: Rabbi Sholom Kovalski continues his account of taking Rabbi Joseph Ber Soloveitchik to visit the Rebbe in 1964. During the drive home, Rav Soloveitchik shared some personal recollections of the Rebbe, from their time together in Berlin.

527032.title: A Visit in New York
527032.description: Rabbi Sholom Kovalski shared a close relationship with Rabbi Joseph Ber Soloveitchik. Here, he recalls taking Rav Soloveitchik to visit the Rebbe upon the passing of the Rebbe’s mother, Rebbetzin Chana Schneerson, of blessed memory.

527750.title: The Rav Attends a Farbrengen
527750.description: Rabbi Herschel Schacter, former president of the Rabbinical Council of America, tells of coming along with the Rav, Rabbi Yosef Ber Soloveitchik, to visit the Rebbe in 1980.

586344.title: Rabbi Asher Heber
586344.description: The Heber family moved to Paris in the 1930’s. Rabbi Asher Heber recalls some of his father’s memories of the Rebbe in Paris then.

586338.title: Reb Yankel and Baila Lax
586338.description: When visiting Paris, France, the Previous Rebbe stayed at the home of Reb Yankel and Baila Lax in the 1930’s. The Rebbe used to visit the Previous Rebbe there. Berel Lax, their twenty years old son, recalls some of his memories of the Previous Rebbe and his son-in-law, the Rebbe, there.

586339.title: Rivkah Marelus
586339.description: Rabbi Avrohom Yehuda Jaloginsky was a young boy of about thirteen years when he lived in Paris in the 1930’s. His daughter, Rivkah Marelus, recalls some of his father’s fondest memories of the Rebbe there.

586340.title: Rabbi Yoel Reitzer
586340.description: Rabbi Yoel Reitzer lives in Antwerp, Belgium. His father, Moshe Zev Reitzer was studying to become a pharmacist at “the Sorbonne,” attending some of the same classes as the Rebbe in the late 1930’s.

586341.title: Efraim Steimetz
586341.description: The Steinmetz family moved to Paris in 1938. Their oldest son, Efraim, was ten years old at the time and he remembers their visits to the Rebbe & Rebbetzin’s apartment in Paris.

586342.title: Volume III: Trailer
586342.description: The Early Years Volume III sheds unprecedented light on Rebbe and Rebbetzin’s last years in Paris, from 1938 through 1940

1489503.title: The Importance of Speed
1489503.description: The Torah uses the metaphor that the Jewish people left Egypt "on eagles' wings" to emphasize the speed in which G-d took them out of Egypt. How important is a sense of urgency in our service of G-d? Guest Expert: Rabbi Mendel Kaplan. (From “Messages”—Season 4, Episode 2)

1489504.title: The Evolution of Judaism
1489504.description: The sun and the moon as symbols for innovation and tradition. Should Judaism adapt with the times or resist the changes of modernity? Guest Expert: Rabbi Manis Friedman. (From “Messages”—Season 4, Episode 3)

1489505.title: The Gift of Motherhood
1489505.description: The Torah reading for Rosh HaShanah describes two great women -- Sarah and Hannah -- and their intense determination to become mothers. Guest Expert: Rivkah Slonim. (From "Messages" -- Season 4, Episode 4)

1489509.title: Moving Back to Move Forward
1489509.description: King Solomon says that a righteous person will "fall seven times and get back up." Why must we suffer a setback before we forge ahead? Guest Expert: Rabbi Mendel Kaplan. (From "Messages" -- Season 4, Episode 5)

1489511.title: Sincere Effort
1489511.description: The story of a sage assisted by angels in lifting a boulder leads to a discussion of how much can really be accomplished if one only makes a sincere effort. Guest Expert: Rabbi Manis Friedman. (From "Messages" -- Season 4, Episode 6)

1489513.title: Respectful Disagreement
1489513.description: True peace is apparent only between people who have opposite perspectives and still manage to live in harmony with each other. Guest Expert: Chana Weisberg. (From “Messages”—Season 4, Episode 7)

1489516.title: Physical Judaism
1489516.description: The purpose of creation is fulfilled by our making use of our bodies and the physical world around us to do G‑d’s will. Guest Expert: Rivkah Slonim. (From “Messages”—Season 4, Episode 8)

1489540.title: Leaving Noah's Ark
1489540.description: On the ark, Noah lived in a utopian state of harmony with his family and all the animals on board—so much so that G‑d had to force him to leave after the Flood was over. What is the parallel in our own lives? Guest Expert: Rabbi Manis Friedman. (From “Messages”—Season 4, Episode 9)

1489557.title: Freedom of Religion
1489557.description: What is the proper interpretation of the U.S. Constitution's Establishment Clause of the First Amendment? Did the founding fathers intend on creating a strict "separation of church and state"? Guest Expert: Rabbi Mendel Kaplan. (From “Messages”—Season 4, Episode 11)

1489555.title: Exile and Your "Inner Jewish Child"
1489555.description: The first stage of the Jewish people's Exile was when the rabbis were sent away, but the "final straw" was when the children stopped studying. Guest Expert: Rabbi Manis Friedman. (From “Messages”—Season 4, Episode 12)

1489562.title: Torah Study as an Occupation, Part 1
1489562.description: The Talmud says that R' Shimon ben Yochai's "Torah study was his profession"? What does it mean to make Torah study your main occupation. Guest Expert: Rabbi Manis Friedman. (From “Messages”—Season 4, Episode 14)
path: Torah Study as an Occupation, Part 1

1489573.title: Torah Study as an Occupation, Part 2
1489573.description: The Talmud says that R' Shimon ben Yochai's "Torah study was his profession"? What does it mean to make Torah study your main occupation. Guest Expert: Rabbi Mendel Kaplan. (From “Messages”—Season 4, Episode 15)
path: Torah Study as an Occupation, Part 2

1489564.title: Jewish Mothers and Children
1489564.description: What is the role of the Jewish mother in raising and educating her children? How does this differ from the role of the father? Guest Expert: Chana Weisberg. (From “Messages”—Season 4, Episode 16)

1489599.title: Can You See G-d?
1489599.description: Upon completing the building of the Sanctuary in the desert, everyone was able to behold G-d's presence with their physical eyes. When Moshiach comes, G-d will be seen everywhere by everyone. What does it mean to see G-d and why can't we see him all the time? Guest Expert: Manis Friedman. (From “Messages”—Season 4, Episode 18)

1489602.title: Activism or Self-Improvement
1489602.description: How does one find the perfect balance between perfecting oneself and perfecting the world? Guest Expert: Rabbi Tzvi Freeman. (From “Messages”—Season 4, Episode 19)

1489603.title: Israeli Inferiority Complex
1489603.description: In the wake of the 1982 Lebanon War, the Rebbe speaks about the foolish and dangerous stance of making concessions in the hopes of winning favor in the eyes of other nations. Guest Expert: Rabbi Moshe Spalter. (From “Messages”—Season 4, Episode 20)

1489610.title: After a Tzaddik's Passing
1489610.description: The greatness of a perfectly righteous tzaddik is not fully evident while he is still alive and his students can behold his physical presence. It is only after the passing of such a leader that we can know what effect he had on those who follow his ways. Guest Expert: Rabbi Manis Friedman. (From “Messages”—Season 4, Episode 21)

1489674.title: Jewish Unity
1489674.description: When there is discord between Jews, it is only because they fail to understand the true nature of their relationship with one another. When Jews understand that they are truly one, then all problems will automatically become resolved on their own. Guest Expert: Rivka Slonim. (From “Messages”—Season 4, Episode 23)

1489675.title: Why Does G-d Give Us Obstacles?
1489675.description: If G-d wants us to serve him, why does he present us with obstacles that make it difficult to do so? Guest Expert: Rabbi Mendel Kaplan. (From “Messages”—Season 4, Episode 24)
path: Why Does G-d Give Us Obstacles?

1489677.title: Ten Days of Repentance
1489677.description: What is the purpose of the Ten Days of Repentance? Is it a time of solemn introspection or a time of rejoicing? Guest Expert: Rabbi Manis Friedman. (From “Messages”—Season 4, Episode 25)

1489678.title: Egypt, Exile and the Body
1489678.description: How is it possible that the best year's of our forefather Jacob's life were spent in Egypt and not in the Holy Land? What does this teach us about the purpose of the soul's descent into the body? Guest Expert: Rabbi Tzvi Freeman. (From “Messages”—Season 4, Episode 26)

630431.title: The Rebbetzin
630431.description: A brief biography of Rebbetzin Chaya Mushka Schneerson, of righteous memory, wife of the Lubavitcher Rebbe, Rabbi Menachem Mendel Schneerson, of righteous memory.

629828.title: Mrs. Hadassa Carlebach
629828.description: Mrs. Hadassa Carlebach is a relative of the Rebbetzin. Here she recalls some memories of her visits to the Rebbetzin.

629829.title: Mrs. Leah Kahan
629829.description: Mrs. Leah Kahan is a relative of the Rebbetzin. Here she recalls some memories of her visits to the Rebbetzin.

629830.title: Rabbi Shmuel Lew
629830.description: Rabbi Shmuel Lew’s father-in-law, Zalmon Jaffe, would visit the Rebbe and Rebbetzin’s home in Brooklyn, New York. As a result, Rabbi Lew had the privilege of visiting the home as well.

629831.title: Dr. Ira Weiss
629831.description: On Shemini Atzeres 1977, after the Rebbe suffered a massive heart attack, Dr. Ira Weiss flew in from Chicago to join the medical team treating the Rebbe. Subsequently, he became the Rebbe and Rebbetzin’s cardiologist.

3566045.title: Tending G-d’s Garden
3566045.description: The last discourse that Rabbi Yosef Yitzchok Schneersohn, the Previous Lubavitcher Rebbe, published before his passing commences with the verse “I have come into My garden.” The Previous Rebbe explains that this refers to our world, the innermost dwelling place of G-d.

3566033.title: It’s a Beautiful World
3566033.description:
The Previous Rebbe wrote a discourse that served as his last teaching. Its title quotes the verse where G-d says, “I have come to My garden, My abode.”
By choosing those powerful words, the Rebbe taught his generation and future generations, that beneath all its outer appearances, this world is G-d’s own garden and dwelling place. No matter how strong the urge to give in to cynicism or despair, no matter how bad things may appear, this teaching shows and empowers us to search out and reveal the essential goodness and G-dliness of the entire creation.

3566027.title: A World of Pain, or of Pleasure?
3566027.description: In a letter to one of his disciples, Maimonides describes the taxing daily schedule he endured as court physician to the sultan of Egypt. It not only drained him to the point of exhaustion, it also left him nearly no time to pursue the true joy of his life: Torah study.
path: A World of Pain, or of Pleasure?

2843808.title: The Divine Orchard
2843808.description: “Bosi L’Gani – I have come to My garden.” G-d created this world to be a glorious Divine orchard for His presence. Man is charged with planting and tending this orchard by creating a “fruit-bearing tree” out of his own portion of the world.

2843807.title: "This is My G-d"
2843807.description:
At the crossing of the Red Sea, the Jews proclaimed, "This is my G-d, and I will exalt Him!"
But the first to recognize G-d's hand were those children born in Egypt during the harsh
decrees. G-d Himself had hidden them away in the fields and sustained them.

2843806.title: Protector of Her People
2843806.description:
At the time of the Song of Moses, the Jews were in the midst of a great journey through an
awesome desert. They had yet to reach, conquer and establish a Jewish homeland. By
contrast, at the time of the Song of Deborah, the Jews were already settled in the Land of
Israel. Deborah was called upon to organize a campaign against Canaanite invaders.

2843791.title: L'chaim for Distribution by Russian and Georgian Guests
2843791.description: The Rebbe distributes bottles of L’chaim at a Farbrengen at 770.
path: L'chaim for Distribution by Russian and Georgian Guests

2843797.title: A Song in Georgian
2843797.description: The Rebbe asks a recent émigré from Georgia to sing a traditional song of the Georgian Jews.

2843798.title: E Vadye (Russian)
2843798.description: A lively niggun sung during the times of the Soviet Jewish resistance. “Water will not drown us and fire will not burn us”.

2843800.title: Farbrengen Highlights: 10 Shevat 5732
2843800.description: A vintage clip of this lively Chabad Niggun.

3566070.title: Niggun Yosisu
3566070.description: “Let all those seek You rejoice and delight in You, and let those who love your deliverance say always, ‘May G-d be exalted!’” (Psalms 70:5) Although the tune of the Niggun is much older, the words were added in honor of the Rebbe’s sixty-ninth birthday.

3566064.title: Much Nachas
3566064.description:
Between talks at the Yud Shevat Farbrengen in 1972, the Rebbe gives special blessings to a
grandfather on the birth of his granddaughter, and to a father on the Bar Mitzvah of his son.

133341.title: 10 Shevat 5732 - Niggun
133341.description: Sacred Chassidic nuggunim sung at the conclusion of major farbrengens.

929717.title: Part 1
929717.description: Civilized society depends on proper education built on a healthy foundation. But the only true foundation for education is the same as that of all of creation: “In the beginning, G-d created the Heavens and the Earth.”
path: A Moment to Save the World

929718.title: Part 2
929718.description: Parents rely on the Public School System to rear their children into mature, responsible adults. Their children are imbued with the values of this country’s sense of pride: That “My own power and the strength of my hand have brought me my success.” But with this approach unchecked, they will grow up to use their education to achieve their own selfish desires.
path: A Moment to Save the World

929716.title: Part 3
929716.description: Those who oppose silent prayer in public schools, cite the separation of religion and state as the basis to eliminate religion from the public arena. However, this ignores the reason the law was established in the first place: to protect the freedom of religious expression of the original settlers in this country. This modern-day repression of democracy goes against the intention of the authors of the Constitution.
path: A Moment to Save the World

695899.title: Clarity of Purpose: Moral Leadership
695899.description:
An address on the Rebbe's birthday, shortly after the assassination attempt on US President
Ronald Reagan's life.

695900.title: Reflections on an Assassination Attempt
695900.description: On March 30, 1981, crazed gunman, John Hinckley attempted to kill President Ronald Reagan. Shortly there-after the Rebbe, of righteous memory, spoke of the shocking nature of the crime, and the root cause of such evil.

695901.title: Clarity of Purpose: Inner Unity, World Peace
695901.description:
The best way to heal illness is through preventive measures. The disease of crime is a reality,
but recognizing that it is real should bring about real change. The education system must
reorient itself to stop this disease before it manifests. We are not calling for a "new" resolution,
but rather a return to the values accepted by the citizens of this country and by all nations.
path: Clarity of Purpose: Inner Unity, World Peace

929715.title: Energy Independence – Part 1
929715.description: “Evil will come from the north.” The Soviet Union is a clear manifestation of this prophecy. At the same time, G-d bestowed the United States with the mission and the moral and material might to counter this evil. To succeed, however, America must be free of economic pressure from immoral dictatorships. If we rely on them for oil, this nation’s strength and influence is compromised.

929714.title: Energy Independence – Part 2
929714.description:
There is a solution to America’s energy crisis: Solar Energy. Solar technology requires far less time to develop than other energy sources.
What can a small group of Jews accomplish by discussing this issue amongst themselves? Maimonides rules that even a single statement based on Torah, has the power to tip the scales for salvation. Past experiences have shown that issues discussed here, have reached Washington.

132924.title: Foundations In Education
132924.description: The Rebbe speaks on the foundations of education (September 13, 1983)

133363.title: Memories of My Mother
133363.description: The Rebbe recalls his mother's activities during World War I.

132927.title: Leadership
132927.description: Every person is expected to become a ‘ruler’ over his surroundings – to make it a proper dwelling place for G-d. At first, a person is ruler only over himself. Later, he becomes ‘ruler’ and leader of his family. Then he goes on to become a leader in his community and so on. At each stage he must accustom himself to place the new majority’s needs before the previous “individual’s” needs.

132923.title: True Charity
132923.description:
The Talmud explains that the verse, “He redeemed my soul in peace from battles against me, because of the many who were with me,” refers to, “One who works in Torah and charity…”
A business owner isn’t satisfied with the clientele who find him; he publicizes his goods and services. His work also has no end; it is constantly on his mind. To work in Torah and charity means going beyond the realm of ‘obligation’ – developing self-motivation for personal growth, and exerting relentless effort to improve the spiritual and physical welfare of others.

133365.title: Marriage Ceremonies
133365.description: Until 1963, the Rebbe would officiate at weddings of Chassidim. A collection of vintage films from weddings at which the Rebbe officiated./

132928.title: 70 Years, 71 New Institutions
132928.description: 70 New institutions: The Rebbe addresses his 70th birthday (March 26, 1972)

132929.title: The Tefillin Campaign
132929.description: The Rebbe explains the idea of approaching somebody on the street to perform a Mitzva

132930.title: Light Unto the Nations: Part 2
132930.description: The Rebbe speaks on the Seven Universal Laws for all mankind.

133361.title: A Tribute to the Rebbetzin
133361.description: The Rebbe speaks on the Rebbetzin's passing (January 27, 1992)

133369.title: G-d is With Us in Exile
133369.description: The Rebbe speaks on how God shares the pain of exile with his People (May 20, 1984)
path: G-d is With Us in Exile

132931.title: CNN With the Rebbe
132931.description: Join CNN as the Rebbe receives visitors, hear his remarks about the Messiah

132932.title: Tzama Lecha Nafshi
132932.description: Hear this moving, age-old chasidic melody sung by the Rebbe (August 9, 1982).

132926.title: The Rebbe on the The Six-Day War
132926.description: A passionate talk by the Rebbe several days before the outbreak of the Six-Day War (May 28, 1967).
path: The Rebbe on the The Six-Day War

133364.title: A Message of Hope for Russian Jewry
133364.description: Addressing Jews who had recently arrived from the Soviet Union at a Lag B’omer parade, the Rebbe explains that they demonstrate, for all to see, the steadfast commitment to Torah and Judaism that the Jewish people have, despite adversity.
path: A Message of Hope for Russian Jewry

133072.title: Martyrs of Auschwitz
133072.description: The Rebbe speaks about the martyrs at Auschwitz (April 13, 1973)

133359.title: To Benefit a Third Jew
133359.description: The Rebbe speaks on what happens when two Jews get together

133360.title: Morning Prayers
133360.description: The Rebbe takes part in morning prayers during the intermediate days of Passover. (Chol Moed Pesach, 5736 - Passover, 1976)

132925.title: Utilizing Children's Energy
132925.description: The Rebbe speaks on utilizing the energy of children (August 7, 1985)

427555.title: High Holidays with the Rebbe
427555.description: Join us as we spend the "head" and nerve center of the Jewish year with the Rebbe

427556.title: Selichot with the Rebbe
427556.description: The post-midnight “supplication” prayers are a unique blend of solemnity and joy.

427557.title: At the Ohel
427557.description: The Rebbe visits resting place of his predecessor, Rabbi Yosef Yitzchak Schneersohn

427558.title: Kaparot
427558.description: The somber "kaparot" rite reminds us of the fragility of life

427559.title: Lekach: A Piece of Honey Cake
427559.description: The Rebbe distributes the traditional lekach - sweet honey cake for a sweet year
path: Lekach: A Piece of Honey Cake

2451287.title: Prime Minister Ariel Sharon and the Rebbe
2451287.description: Video highlighting the relationship between the Lubavitcher Rebbe and Israeli Prime Minister Ariel Sharon.
path: Prime Minister Ariel Sharon and the Rebbe

132951.title: Yitzchak Rabin
132951.description: Yitzchak Rabin was Prime Minister of Israel, and served as Israel’s ambassador to the United States in the early 1970s. In 1972, he was sent to convey Israel’s blessings to the Rebbe in honor of his 70th birthday.

1897999.title: "The Rebbe Told Me Not to Fear"
1897999.description: A series of clips highlight the relationship between the Rebbe and Israeli Prime Minister Yitzhak Shamir.
path: "The Rebbe Told Me Not to Fear"

132942.title: Menachem Begin and the Rebbe
132942.description: Israeli Prime Minister Menachem Begin talks on the Rebbe's standing in Israel (1977)

2818231.title: Governor Mario Cuomo on the Rebbe
2818231.description: Former New York Governor Mario Cuomo speaks of the Rebbe’s abilities to communicate so well with adult and child alike, and his way of explaining even the most difficult subject matter and making it sound lucid to all. (Special thanks to the Friendship Circle of NJ)
path: Governor Mario Cuomo on the Rebbe

132947.title: Margaret Thatcher on the Rebbe's Leadership
132947.description: Reflections on the Rebbe -- British Prime Minister Margaret Thatcher
path: Margaret Thatcher on the Rebbe's Leadership

3514851.title: Brigadier General Ran Ronen Pecker and the Rebbe
3514851.description: The legendary Brigadier General Ran Ronen-Pecker, one of Israel’s most decorated “ace” fighter pilots, reflects on his encounters with the Rebbe.
path: Brigadier General Ran Ronen Pecker and the Rebbe

4909572.title: The Light of the Rebbe
4909572.description: Warm remarks by Joe Lieberman in honor of the Rebbe’s yarhtzeit. This talk is from the virtual event “Transform and Transcend” by Merkos 302.

2133156.title: Rabbi Abraham D. Hecht and the Rebbe
2133156.description: Rabbi Abraham Dov Hecht served for over 40 years as the Rabbi of Congregation Shaarei Tziyon of the Syrian community in Brooklyn. He was 90 years old upon his passing in 2013. This video highlights his relationship with the Lubavitcher Rebbe, of righteous memory.
path: Rabbi Abraham D. Hecht and the Rebbe

132941.title: Elie Wiesel
132941.description: Nobel Laureate Elie Wiesel at the award ceremony of the Rebbe's Congressional Gold Medal

132938.title: “He Created Leaders”
132938.description: Chief Rabbi of Great Britain and the Commonwealth, Dr. Jonathan Sacks highlights some unique aspects of the Rebbe’s leadership.

132946.title: Rabbi Adin Even-Israel (Steinsaltz) - Part 1
132946.description: Talmudic Scholar Rabbi Adin Even-Israel (Steinsaltz) on the Rebbe's scholarship

132939.title: Professor Lawrence Schiffman (Part 1)
132939.description: The Rebbe and gentiles, NYU Professor Lawrence Schiffman

132963.title: Professor Lawrence Schiffman (Part 2)
132963.description: The Rebbe's Torah Scholarship, NYU Professor Lawrence Schiffman

132964.title: Professor Lawrence Schiffman (Part 3)
132964.description: Lubavitch's openess, with NYU Professor Lawrence Schiffman

132965.title: Rabbi Israel Meir Lau - Reflections on the Rebbe
path: Rabbi Israel Meir Lau - Reflections on the Rebbe

132943.title: Rabbi Israel Meir Lau - U.S. House of Representatives
132943.description: Opens the US House of Representatives before the Gold Medal resolution is passed
path: Rabbi Israel Meir Lau - U.S. House of Representatives

132948.title: Joseph Lieberman
132948.description: Reflections on the Rebbe by U.S. Senator Joseph Lieberman

132966.title: “On the Way to Washington”
132966.description: US Senator Joseph Lieberman tells of his first experience at 770 and of his last stop on the way to Washington to take his oath for the Senate.

132949.title: Congressman John Lewis Speaks About the Rebbe
132949.description: Reflections on the Congressional Gold Medal from civil rights activist US Congressman John Lewis (1995)
path: Congressman John Lewis Speaks About the Rebbe

3161851.title: Jack and Miriam Shenkman's 75th Wedding Anniversary
3161851.description: Philanthropists Jack and Miriam Shenkman of Detroit and their meetings with the Rebbe, in a video prepared for their 75th wedding anniversary.
path: Jack and Miriam Shenkman's 75th Wedding Anniversary

2143150.title: A Story in Three Acts
2143150.description: Chief Rabbi of the British Commonwealth, Rabbi Jonathan Sacks, tells how the Rebbe's guidance affected him at three critical junctures in his life. Rabbi Sacks suggests that we can all live the Rebbe's vision by a) increasing in love for all Jews, b) empowering individuals to discover their true potential, and c) sharing our Jewish commitment and observance with others.

937503.title: Reflection on the Rebbe by Senator Joseph Lieberman
937503.description: An address by Senator Joe Lieberman at an evening commemorating the Lubavitcher Rebbes’s fifteenth yahrtzeit—anniversary of passing (June 29, 2009 - Philadelphia, PA).
path: Reflection on the Rebbe by Senator Joseph Lieberman

1055244.title: The Rebbe as Statesman
1055244.description: Israeli diplomat Yehuda Avner speaks at the concluding banquet of the International Conference of Chabad-Lubavitch Emissaries in New York, addressing a series of encounters he had with the Rebbe, Rabbi Menachem M. Schneerson, of righteous memory.

1560632.title: Rabbi to the World
1560632.description: Rabbi Levi Shemtov, Chabad emissary in Washington, D.C., and rabbi to ambassadors, presidents and potentates, shares firsthand accounts of how the Rebbe’s teachings have influenced the world’s most powerful men and women. (Recorded on the occasion of the 17th anniversary of the Rebbe’s passing.)

1220320.title: The Rebbe Trained me to be a “Shliach”
1220320.description: The Chief Rabbi of Efrat, Israel, describes what it means to be a “Shliach,” a Chabad-Lubavitch emissary.
path: The Rebbe Trained me to be a “Shliach”

2143147.title: My Rebbe
2143147.description: Rabbi Simon Jacobson shares his personal reflections on the teachings of the Rebbe, Rabbi Menachem M. Schneerson, on the occasion of the anniversary of his passing. (filmed at Chabad of Brooklyn Heights, 6/20/2012)

1220318.title: A Leader, An Activist, A Man
1220318.description: Rabbi Lau describes the Rebbe not just as a leader who revolutionized world Jewry, but also as one who cared about a widow in Israel who wanted to commit suicide...
path: A Leader, An Activist, A Man

2250624.title: The Faithful Shepherd
2250624.description: On the occasion of the Lubavitcher Rebbe’s yahrtzeit, Rabbi Yossy Goldman shares the Rebbe’s unique vision of hope.

2632828.title: A Visionary in Our Time
2632828.description: The past century has been fraught with unprecedented challenges facing our people, and it was precisely at this juncture that called for extraordinary leadership. Rabbi Yosef Y. Jacobson explores three central themes in the Rebbe’s visionary leadership. (Recorded at a tribute commemorating the Rebbe’s twentieth yahrtzeit at Park East Synagogue)

2143140.title: The Rebbe and Soviet Jewry
2143140.description: An extraordinary address by Professor David Luchins, chair of Touro College’s department of political science and a longtime advisor to the late New York Sen. Daniel Patrick Moynihan, at the gala banquet of the International Conference of Chabad-Lubavitch Emissaries (Nov. 15, 2009).

2143142.title: The Rebbe's Example
2143142.description: Joseph Telushkin reflects on what we can all learn and apply in our own lives from various stories about the Rebbe’s unique approach to leadership.

2633026.title: Marching Orders from the Rebbe for Each of Us
path: Marching Orders from the Rebbe for Each of Us

2632823.title: The Rebbe as a Role Model
2632823.description: There is an abundance to learn from the Rebbe’s example, even in the everyday seemingly small things, in the details of both his sensitivity to others to his devotion to Torah and truth, which remain inspiring, vibrant and relevant as ever.
path: The Rebbe as a Role Model

2143145.title: The Rebbe's Revolution
2143145.description: Rabbi and author Benjamin Blech shares personal stories of his relationship with the Lubavitcher Rebbe, of righteous memory, and speaks about what he believes was the main component of the Rebbe's influence -- the ability to see the fullest potential of each Jew. (filmed at Chabad of Brooklyn Heights on the occasion of the Rebbe’s 17th Yahrtzeit, 2011)

2676615.title: The Rebbe’s Personal Cardiologist Speaks
2676615.description: Following the Rebbe’s severe heart attack in 1977, Dr. Ira Weiss was entrusted to treat the Rebbe, which led to a special personal relationship for many years. (Recorded at a tribute for the Rebbe’s 20th yahrtzeit at the Eastside Torah Center in Bellevue, Washington)

2143144.title: The Rabbi of the Far East
2143144.description: Rabbi Marvin Tokayer who served as the Rabbi to the Far East from 1968-1981 reveals how several personal encounters with the Lubavitcher Rebbe, of righteous memory, influenced his path in life.
path: The Rabbi of the Far East

2635880.title: Timeless Leadership
2635880.description: Join the Jewish community of greater Houston for an evening of inspiration and reflection, marking the twentieth yahrtzeit of the Lubavitcher Rebbe, of righteous memory. Presenting a panel discussion exploring the Rebbe’s leadership, led by Dennis Prager in conversation with Rabbi Simon Jacobson, Rabbi Yosef Kantor and Mrs. Miriam Lipskier.

2635894.title: An Evening of Vision, Music and Inspiration
2635894.description: Join the greater Detroit Jewish community for an evening of inspiration and tribute, marking the twentieth yahrtzeit of the Lubavitcher Rebbe, of righteous memory. Featured guest speaker: Joe Lieberman.
path: An Evening of Vision, Music and Inspiration

2718589.title: Rabbi Yehuda Krinsky on Rebbetzin Chana
2718589.description: Rabbi Yehuda Krinsky shares his personal memories of Rebbetzin Chana (the Rebbe’s mother) in honor of the 6th of Tishrei marking her yahrtzeit.
path: Rabbi Yehuda Krinsky on Rebbetzin Chana

2719523.title: Rabbi Shmuel Lew Reflects on Rebbetzin Chana
2719523.description: Rabbi Shmuel Lew shares his personal memories of Rebbetzin Chana (the Rebbe’s mother) in a webcast on the 6th of Tishrei marking her yahrtzeit.
path: Rabbi Shmuel Lew Reflects on Rebbetzin Chana

4429627.title: The Rebbe Was Like My Grandfather
4429627.description: Mrs. Chani Levitin shares the story of her family becoming affiliated with Chabad and their warm connection with the Rebbe, and her personal encounters; until she ultimately became a shlucha together with her husband in in Seatle, Washington (This talk is from an evening of tribute to the Rebbe by Chabad of Washington State)..
path: The Rebbe Was Like My Grandfather

4429707.title: A Leader with Heart
4429707.description: Rabbi Yisrael Meir Lau, the former Chief Rabbi of Israel, shares his memories and reflections at an evening of unity and inspiration celebrating the leadership and inspiration of the Lubavitcher Rebbe of righteous memory, on the occasion of the 25th yahrtzeit, in Seatle Washington.

4475034.title: The Most Influential Rabbi in Modern History
4475034.description: Joseph Telushkin, author of the bestselling book “Rebbe”, shares insights and lessons from the life and teachings of the Lubavitcher Rebbe. (A lecture at Congregation Kehilath Jeshurun in Manhattan, NY at the book launch)
path: The Most Influential Rabbi in Modern History

4790102.title: Israel's President on the Anniversary of the Rebbe's Passing
path: Israel's President on the Anniversary of the Rebbe's Passing

4791363.title: Israel’s Minister of Diaspora Affairs Speaks About the Rebbe
4791363.description: Omer Yankelevitch, Minister of Diaspora Affairs, shares her warm sentiments to the Rebbe and to Chabad’s emissaries.
path: Israel’s Minister of Diaspora Affairs Speaks About the Rebbe

5580524.title: The Rebbe’s Impact on My Life and His Unique Approach to Torah Study
5580524.description: Rabbi Dr. Tzvi Hersh Weinreb shares a personal experience with the Rebbe, and endeavors to give a sense of the Rebbe’s innovative contribution to the world of Torah study and scholarship.
path: The Rebbe’s Impact on My Life and His Unique Approach to Torah Study

5580526.title: Discovering Our True Self
5580526.description: Rabbi Efraim Mintz, using story and anecdote, shares key messages we learn from the Rebbe. From an evening of inspiration called a Meeting of Souls in honor of the Rebbe’s yahrtzeit, hosted by Tzach, Lubavitch Youth Organization.

5580528.title: The Rebbe Gave Us a Voice
5580528.description: Rabbi Manis Friedman shares a glimpse into the Rebbe’s vision and historic impact as portrayed in how the Rebbe unmuted the Jewish world and gave us back our voice. A talk on the Rebbe’s yahrtzeit at an evening of tribute near the Rebbe’s Ohel (resting place) in Queens, NY (hosted by Tzach, Lubavitch Youth Organization).
path: The Rebbe Gave Us a Voice

5580529.title: The Gift We Were Given
5580529.description: A keynote address at an event in Miami celebrating the Rebbe’s life, vision and leadership in honor of the 120th birthday anniversary.

2634200.title: Commemorating the Rebbe’s 20th Yahrtzeit
2634200.description: The Rebbe’s monumental lifework and inspiration continues to guide us. Join Chabad-Lubavitch of the state of New Jersey in paying tribute to the Rebbe on the occasion of the twentieth yahrtzeit. Keynote address by Richard Joel, president of Yeshiva University.
path: Chabad-Lubavitch of New Jersey Marks the Rebbe’s 20th Yahrtzeit

2634352.title: A Glimpse of the Rebbe
path: Chabad-Lubavitch of New Jersey Marks the Rebbe’s 20th Yahrtzeit

2634407.title: I Want to Express My Personal Appreciation
path: Chabad-Lubavitch of New Jersey Marks the Rebbe’s 20th Yahrtzeit
I Want to Express My Personal Appreciation

2634428.title: The Vitality of the Rebbe’s Values
2634428.description: The vitality of the Rebbe’s values and the timeliness of his mission continue to illuminate the world. Richard Joel shares some thoughts on the Rebbe’s legacy and our destiny.
path: Chabad-Lubavitch of New Jersey Marks the Rebbe’s 20th Yahrtzeit
The Vitality of the Rebbe’s Values

2627361.title: Reflections on the Rebbe by Rabbi Arthur Schneier
2627361.description: Rabbi Shneier shares some personal recollection and experiences at a tribute to the Rebbe commemorating the twentieth yahrtzeit, initiated by Chabad in Manhattan and hosted at Park East Synagogue.
path: Chabad Centers of Manhattan Mark the Rebbe’s 20th Yahrtzeit
Reflections on the Rebbe by Rabbi Arthur Schneier

2627353.title: My Journey from the Fast Life Back to My Jewish Roots
2627353.description: Eliot Lasky shares the moving story of his return to Jewish tradition after pursuing a path alien to our faith. (This talk was given at a tribute commemorating the Rebbe’s twentieth yahrtzeit at Park East Synagogue in Manhattan)
path: Chabad Centers of Manhattan Mark the Rebbe’s 20th Yahrtzeit
My Journey from the Fast Life Back to My Jewish Roots

2627343.title: A Visionary in Our Time
2627343.description: The past century has been fraught with unprecedented challenges facing our people, and it was precisely at this juncture that called for extraordinary leadership. Rabbi Yosef Y. Jacobson explores three central themes in the Rebbe’s visionary leadership. (Recorded at a tribute commemorating the Rebbe’s twentieth yahrtzeit at Park East Synagogue)
path: Chabad Centers of Manhattan Mark the Rebbe’s 20th Yahrtzeit

3785733.title: Pre-Rosh Hashanah Farbrengen
3785733.description: An hour excerpt of the Rebbe’s Farbrengen on the evening before Rosh Hashanah in 1980, which also marks the birthday of the Tzemach Tzedek, the third Chabad Rebbe. The Rebbe addresses the Jew’s purpose to illuminate the entire world around him and teaches the “tools for illumination.”

2716843.title: 6 Tishrei Farbrengen with the Rebbe
2716843.description: Footage from the Rebbe’s 1981 gathering (Tishrei 6, 5742) commemorating the yahrtzeit (anniversary of passing) of Rebbetzen Chana Schneerson, the Rebbe’s mother.

1962723.title: Pre-Sukkot Gathering
1962723.description: An hour-long excerpt from a 1980 recording of the Rebbe’s pre-Sukkot gathering on the 13th day of the month of Tishrei, the yahrzeit of the fourth Chabad-Lubavitch Rebbe, Rabbi Shmuel Schneerson (1834–1882).

1973458.title: Gathering in Honor of the Fourth Rebbe
1973458.description: The 13th day of Tishrei is the yahrzeit (anniversary of the passing) of the fourth Rebbe of Chabad-Lubavitch, Rabbi Shmuel Schneerson (1834-1882). His successor, Rabbi Menachem Mendel Schneerson, would convene a special gathering (known as a farbrengen) to commemorate this date each year.
path: Gathering in Honor of the Fourth Rebbe

3869114.title: Farbrengen with the Rebbe: 19 Kislev, 5744
3869114.description: An hour-long excerpt from the Rebbe’s 1983 farbrengen on the 19th of Kislev. This Chasidic holiday celebrates the liberation of the first Chabad Rebbe, R' Shneur Zalman, from czarist imprisonment in 1798, due to trumped up charges of treason by opponents to the Chassidic movement.

2088507.title: Gathering in Honor of the Alter Rebbe
2088507.description: The 24th day of the month Tevet is the yahrzeit (anniversary of the passing) of the first Rebbe of Chabad-Lubavitch, Rabbi Shneur Zalman (1745-1812). His successor, the seventh Rebbe, Rabbi Menachem Mendel Schneerson, would often convene a special gathering (known as a farbrengen) to commemorate this date. This video is from the gathering held in the year 5741 (1981).
path: Gathering in Honor of the Alter Rebbe

3201685.title: 10 Shevat Farbrengen with the Rebbe
3201685.description: An hour-long excerpt from the Rebbe’s 1983 gathering on the occasion of the yahrtzeit (anniversary of passing) of the Sixth Rebbe, Rabbi Yosef Yitzchak Schneersohn.

1753681.title: 10 Shevat Gathering with the Rebbe
1753681.description: An hour-long excerpt from a 1972 recording of the Rebbe’s annual gathering on the occasion of the yahrtzeit (anniversary of passing) of his father-in-law, the Previous Rebbe.

3585468.title: The New Year for Trees Farbrengen
3585468.description: A ninety-minute excerpt of the Rebbe’s Farbrengen celebrating the 15th of Shevat in 5741 (1981).
path: The New Year for Trees Farbrengen

2517303.title: Purim Farbrengen 5732 (1972)
2517303.description: An hour-long excerpt from a 1972 recording of the Rebbe’s Purim farbrengen. The Rebbe tackles the enigmatic essence of the Purim story, and explains the real and primary miracle the Sages say we are celebrating. Drawing life lessons from how in those dark times, a generation of assimilating Jews were found worthy in G-d’s eyes.

1451460.title: Purim Farbrengen 5733 (1973)
1451460.description: An hour-long excerpt of an original archival recording of the Rebbe's farbrengen (gathering) on Purim 1973.

1171545.title: Is It Human to Retire?
1171545.description: Revealing a glimpse of the wisdom that moves himself, the Rebbe addresses questions that go to the very core of the human experience: Why am I here? Why do I struggle? And more importantly—what am I capable of becoming?

1809252.title: Pre-Passover Farbrengen
1809252.description: An hour-long excerpt from a 1981 satellite broadcast of the Rebbe’s pre-Passover gathering on the occasion of his 79th birthday (Nissan 11, 5741).

1480910.title: Pre-Passover Farbrengen
1480910.description: An hour-long excerpt from a 1982 satellite broadcast of the Rebbe’s pre-Passover gathering on the occasion of his 80th birthday (11 Nissan, 5742).

3643242.title: Farbrengen with the Rebbe - Nissan 11, 5743 (1983)
3643242.description: In this excerpt from a televised farbrengen in 1983 celebrating his eighty-first birthday, the Rebbe zeroes in on the vital need for moral education for our children, genuine pride in our Jewish ways, and how these simple and straightforward measures will impact the world at large.

903318.title: Farbrengen: 11 Nissan 5745
903318.description: This farbrengen was held on the Rebbe’s birthday in 1985 and also marked the first Siyum Harambam, the closure of the yearly cycle of studying the Mishneh Torah, the magnum opus of Maimonides.

2201583.title: Lag B'Omer Gathering
2201583.description: Excerpts from a 1983 recording of the Lag B’Omer parade at Lubavitch World Headquarters, Brooklyn, New York.

2201603.title: Lag B’Omer Parade Highlights
2201603.description: Children gather to celebrate the holiday of Lag B’Omer. Excerpts from a 1983 recording of the grand parade with the Rebbe at Lubatvitch World Headquarters, Brooklyn, New York.

1517359.title: Lag B’Omer Parade and Rally
1517359.description: Children gather to celebrate the holiday of Lag B’Omer. Excerpts from a 1984 satellite feed from Lubatvitch World Headquarters, Brooklyn, New York.

1517337.title: Lag B'Omer Gathering
1517337.description: Excerpts from a 1984 satellite feed from Lubavitch World Headquarters, Brooklyn, New York.

4032955.title: Pre-Shavuot Farbrengen with the Rebbe
4032955.description: Each year, the Rebbe would hold a Farbrengen the night before Shavuot, often touching on topics from Tractate Sotah in the Talmud, which is customarily studied during the Counting of the Omer period, as well as discussing the lessons of the approaching holiday.

1556596.title: 12 Tammuz Gathering with the Rebbe
1556596.description: Footage from the Rebbe’s 1985 gathering in celebration of the birthdate (in 1880) of his father-in-law, the Sixth Lubavitcher Rebbe, R. Yosef Yitzchak Schneersohn, and the Sixth Rebbe’s release from Soviet incarceration (1927). The Sixth Rebbe was imprisoned for spreading Judaism in the Soviet Union.

2974977.title: Farbrengen with the Rebbe - Tammuz 12, 5741 (1981)
2974977.description: An hour-long excerpt from a televised gathering with the Rebbe’s in 1981. In this talk the Rebbe focuses on the topic of education and the urgent need for children to be raised with the knowledge of a Higher Being, an “eye that sees and ear that hears” everything they do.

4094677.title: Farbrengen with the Rebbe: Chof Av, 5732
4094677.description: During this Chassidic gathering, the Rebbe focuses on an enigmatic statement of Rashi: “The passing of the righteous is difficult for G-d like the breaking of the Tablets.” What connection is there between the two? Is there anything positive in the breaking of the Tablets? And what lesson can we derive from those situations?
path: Farbrengen with the Rebbe: Chof Av, 5732

2838514.title: Maamar Basi LeGani 5735
2838514.description: Footage of the Rebbe saying a maamar or Chassidic discourse (as customary in Yiddish), preceded and followed by a niggun. From the Yud Shevat farbrengen of the year 5735, marking the 25th yahrtzeit of the Previous Rebbe (the sixth Lubavitcher Rebbe).

2843972.title: A Nation Under G-d – Farbrengen
2843972.description: One of the Patriarch Avraham’s great first deeds was not only the promotion of monotheism, but the credo that G-d is “Master of the World.” G-d is the Master of the World in the occupational sense; this is what he does constantly. He fills the entire world with His presence and guidance.

2843973.title: Leadership
2843973.description: Every person is expected to become a ‘ruler’ over his surroundings – to make it a proper dwelling place for G-d. At first, a person is ruler only over himself. Later, he becomes ‘ruler’ and leader of his family. Then he goes on to become a leader in his community and so on. At each stage he must accustom himself to place the new majority’s needs before the previous “individual’s” needs.

2843975.title: "He, Too, Is Alive"
2843975.description:
Torah expects a tzaddik to not be satisfied with his own righteousness; his mission is to
influence his fellow Jews to follow G‑d’s path, and to help them become in turn sources of
inspiration to others as well.

2843978.title: Mission of Kings
2843978.description: Torah states: “Every Jew is a king.” The Mitzvah campaigns especially express this kingship.

2843979.title: Weapons of Peace
2843979.description: Addressing members of Israel’s Defense Mission in the audience, the Rebbe explains the importance of Israel maintaining a large defense arsenal.

2843981.title: Opening the Doors to Goodness
2843981.description: The recipient of a key takes possession of the entire property. Therefore everything in the properties must follow the Code of Jewish Law. These keys will be used to lock out all negative things and lock in Judaism, Torah and Mitzvos.

2843983.title: There’s a Great Thirst
2843983.description: I am happy that your book, This is My G-d has been translated into Hebrew. Jews brought up in Israel have a great thirst to know more about Judaism.

2843984.title: Not an Only Child
2843984.description: It is not good to be the only religious Jewish politician. You must cause there to be others.

2843987.title: An Independent Mind
2843987.description: The Rebbe tells Professor Paul Rosenbloom: “I had a younger brother who passed away many years ago. He left this unfinished mathematical paper. If you will supervise someone to prepare it for publication, I will be very happy to pay for it.”

2843989.title: A Candle for One, A Light for All
2843989.description:
There is an expression: "A candle for one, is a candle for one hundred." If you light one
candle, it provides the needs, of light, for all the people in the room. Go from strength to
strength in all matters of Judaism in general, and especially in something that will influence
a crowd. Then with the same amount of effort you can influence a greater number of people.
path: A Candle for One, A Light for All

2843996.title: What Comes First: The Money or the Pledge?
2843996.description:
Although you only pledged a quarter million dollars to charity, don’t be afraid to commit to half
a million. G-d can make you wealthier. “Toil, and you will succeed.”
path: What Comes First: The Money or the Pledge?

2843998.title: Farbrengen Interlude
2843998.description: Yosef Ciechanover, head of Israel’s Defense mission to the United States, shares an exchange with the Rebbe at a farbrengen.

2844005.title: Niggun Hisvaadus
2844005.description: The Chasidim sing one of many inspirational niggunim commonly sung at Chasidic gatherings.

2844006.title: Uforatzta
2844006.description: “And you shall spread out westward and eastward and northward and southward.” (Genesis 28:14) This lively Niggun was composed to honor the Rebbe’s campaign to spread Torah Judaism to all four corners of the globe.

2844008.title: Tune of “Zol Shoin Zein Di Geulah”
path: Tune of “Zol Shoin Zein Di Geulah”

5306946.title: What My Life in Russia Is (Not) Like
5306946.description: "Thirteen years ago, my parents made two big announcements..." Yakov Danzinger shares what life is like in Rostov, Russia – offering an inside view as the son of the Chabad emissaries there. This video was produced in honor of Yakov’s Bar Mitzvah.
path: What My Life in Russia Is (Not) Like

5098418.title: The Story of My Kidney Donation
5098418.description: This short video presents the journey of how Mr. Jack Hananya obtained a lifesaving organ donation from Rabbi Zalman Sandhaus. Let's make the world a brighter place with acts of goodness and kindness. A project of Kidney Assist; video production: Yuvla Media.
path: The Story of My Kidney Donation

4072778.title: Chabad’s Expanding Activities in Nigeria
4072778.description: “When I meet people and tell them I’m a Chabad emissary in Nigeria,” says Rabbi Uzan, “they ask me: there are Jews in Nigeria?!” This video offers a peek into Chabad’s great work over the past five years in Nigeria.

3503119.title: Inside the Biggest Gathering of Rabbis
3503119.description: Get a glimpse of the behind the scenes inner-workings at the International Conference of Chabad-Lubavitch Emissaries.
path: Inside the Biggest Gathering of Rabbis

3183989.title: How It Feels to Take a Picture with Thousands of Rabbis
3183989.description: A glimpse into the making of the group picture of the thousands of Chabad-Lubavitch emissaries from around the world, which captures their united focus of mission and shared sense of pride and confidence in their life work.
path: How It Feels to Take a Picture with Thousands of Rabbis

1349194.title: How I Met Chabad
1349194.description: Ukrainian businessman and philanthropist Gennady Bogoliubov discusses his upbringing that led him to become one of today’s most well-known and generous supporters of shluchim in the world (International Conference of Chabad-Lubavitch Emissaries 2010).

1349185.title: The Son of Shluchim Speaks
1349185.description: Young Moshe Cohen – the son of shluchim to Manchester, England Rabbi Mendel Cohen and his late wife Esti of blessed memory, who tragically passed away just a month before this event – addresses the International Conference of Chabad-Lubavitch Emissaries with words of Torah (Nov. 7, 2010).

1416685.title: The Secret of Chabad
1416685.description: Dennis Prager shares his thoughts on happiness and Chabad at the 18th Anniversary Dinner of the Chai Center of Dix Hills, NY.

1926673.title: Sami Rohr and the Shluchim
1926673.description: The late philanthropist Sami Rohr, who was a pillar of generosity throughout the Jewish world, addresses thousands of emissaries and their guests at the movement’s 2006 convention.

1386618.title: Rabbi Levi's Smile
1386618.description: Members of the Tyson's Corner, VA Jewish community reflect on their friend, Rabbi Levi Deitsch, and the warmth, passion and dedication which he showed each one of them.

1242484.title: Chabad Wins World Cup
1242484.description: Chabad of Cape Town, South Africa demonstrates how to play the spiritual game of soccer as the goal being to better the world around us.

1057926.title: Embers
1057926.description: Defying rogue regimes, the Rebbes of Chabad-Lubavitch and their emissaries risked their lives to keep Judaism alive across the Soviet Union. Their efforts enabled the embers of Judaism to spark the transformation of Jewish life thriving there today.

1060520.title: Sam’s Elmo Muppet
1060520.description: In 1953, the late Rabbi Jacob J. Hecht founded Toys for Hospitalized Children with the dream of bringing joy and comfort to children everywhere.

534334.title: Matti's Story
534334.description: Matti finds warmth, confidence, and hope after enduring tragedy, with the help and care of Colel Chabad.

534332.title: A Home Away From Home in Thailand
534332.description: Jewish life continues to flourish and grow in Bangkok for Jews from all over the globe.
path: A Home Away From Home in Thailand

1005775.title: Onward and Upward...
1005775.description: Join us on a journey as we explore the growth of Chabad of Port Washington over the past seventeen years.

534335.title: The Art of the Child
534335.description: Preschool of the Arts is a center for early childhood education located in the Chelsea neighborhood of Manhattan, NY.

1151148.title: Mindsets
1151148.description: The Friendship Circle brings together teenage volunteers and children with special needs for hours of fun and friendship. These shared experiences empower these special children, while enriching the lives of everyone involved.

1020815.title: Released Time Program
1020815.description: The Released Time program reaches out to Jewish students in public school and exposes them to their Jewish heritage and religion. Since 1941 Chabad-Lubavitch has been acting on this federal law, which allows children to be excused from class for religious instruction.

1084396.title: 108 Bar Mitzvahs
1084396.description: One hundred eight tragedies, 108 orphans, and 108 victories. Here is the story of one of the boys who was part of Colel Chabad’s annual bar mitzvah celebration at the Kotel.

779312.title: Mission of Love
779312.description: A glimpse into the life of Rabbi Gabi and Rivky Hotzberg—the Chabad emissaries to Mumbai, India.

600780.title: Copenhagen's Torah Teacher
600780.description: Meet the man whose mission is to teach Torah and Judaism to every Jew living in Copenhagen, Denmark.

1122304.title: Challenge to Life
1122304.description: Challenge to Life brings injured Israeli solders to Aspen, Colorado to ski its magnificent snow-covered slopes. This program builds tremendous confidence and shows how these special people can achieve more than anyone can ever imagine.

1120026.title: Chabad Opens Jewish Center in Cambodia
1120026.description: Mashie Butman tells of her family’s recent move to Phnom Penh, Cambodia as Chabad emissaries to establish a new Jewish center.
path: Chabad Opens Jewish Center in Cambodia

1070697.title: Washington D.C.
1070697.description: Giant menorah lighting by White House Chief of Staff Rahm Emanuel on the ellipse at the White House. Also featuring the United States Air Force Band and "The Three Cantors".

867608.title: Canadian PM Stephen Harper Addresses Chabad Emissaries
867608.description: Canadian Prime Minister Stephen Harper joined members of the House of Commons in saluting the Canadian Federation of Chabad-Lubavitch as 100 emissaries gathered for a national conference on Parliament Hill.
path: Canadian PM Stephen Harper Addresses Chabad Emissaries

866104.title: Canadian Prime Minister Participates in Dedication of Synagogue
866104.description: Prime Minister Stephen Harper addresses the congregation at Chabad of Flamingo on the occasion of the grand opening of the newly expanded Ernest Manson Lubavitch Center.
path: Canadian Prime Minister Participates in Dedication of Synagogue

1081055.title: Shabbat at Chabad on Campus
1081055.description: A first time video experience of a Shabbat meal at Chabad House on Campus and what it takes to make it (this video was not filmed on Shabbat).

641543.title: Aussie PM Salutes Sydney Yeshiva
641543.description: Newly elected Australian Prime Minister Kevin Rudd toasted Sydney’s Yeshiva Centre at the Chabad-Lubavitch school’s annual gala dinner on Thursday, which was attended by some 1,350 people.

133353.title: Cornerstones - USA
133353.description: A glimpse at Lubavitch building projects in the United States. (excerpt)

1764563.title: Oprah's Visit to Hasidic Brooklyn
1764563.description: Oprah Winfrey spent a day visiting Hasidic communities in Brooklyn, NY. At the end of the day, Chabad.org's own Rabbi Motti Seligson interviewed Winfrey about her experiences.

133354.title: Cornerstones - Russia
133354.description: A glimpse at Lubavitch building projects in the former Soviet Union (Excerpt)

133355.title: Cornerstones - Israel
133355.description: A glimpse at Lubavitch building projects in Israel. (excerpt)

1488228.title: Delivering Matzah
1488228.description: The students of Yeshiva Gedola in London, UK prepare for the holiday of Pesach by delivering packages of hand-baked shmura matzah to 2000 homes throughout the city.

1792126.title: The Chabad House Serving NYU
1792126.description: The Chabad House Serving NYU, directed by Rabbi Dov Yona and Sarah Korn, held an inaugural event at its new 8,000-square-foot space in a building in the Bowery. Featured speakers: Vice-Chairman of Merkos L'Inyonei Chinuch Rabbi Moshe Kotlarsky, NYU Chaplain Rabbi Yehuda Sarna, philanthropist George Rohr, and Rabbi Dov Yona and Sarah Korn.

1834334.title: Influence in the White House
1834334.description: Rabbi Abraham Shemtov, the Rebbe's Shliach to the White House, recounts firsthand how the Rebbe influenced the U.S. government to push for the release of Soviet Jews in the 1980s.

1844369.title: Basel's New Synagogue
1844369.description: This video gives the background behind the historic dedication of the first synagogue to open in Basel, Switzerland since 1929. Philanthropist Sami Rohr who funded the project, was able to honor the memory of Shlomo Zalman and Recha Feldinger, who at the height of World War II provided a loving home to the young refugee. (April, 2012)

1890283.title: 770 Through Yossi's Lens
1890283.description: The late Yossi Melamed spent hundreds of hours photographing the Rebbe between the years 1975-1992 and his collection contains tens of thousands of photographs of the Rebbe. This video highlights the extensive preservation efforts by Jewish Educational Media (JEM) to bring Yossi's work to the public.

1891355.title: Connecticut Honors Life's Work of the Rebbe
1891355.description: Dignitaries and community leaders gather at Connecticut’s State Capitol to honor the life of the Rebbe, Rabbi Menachem M. Schneerson on the occasion of the 18th anniversary of his passing. Speakers include Gov. Dannel P. Malloy, Rabbi Yosef Gopin, Rabbi Yisrael Deren.
path: Connecticut Honors Life's Work of the Rebbe

1898671.title: One Nation Under G-d
1898671.description: Rabbi Yisroel Deren, regional director of the Chabad Lubavitch of Western and Southern New England, shares his thoughts on what the Rebbe, of righteous memory, taught us about maximizing our contribution to our country, our people and our world. (Recorded at the Connecticut State Capital at an event honoring the Rebbe on the occasion of the 18th anniversary of his passing.)

2044460.title: Chabad and Hurricane Sandy
2044460.description: October 2012. In the aftermath of superstorm Sandy, we visit Chabad-Lubavitch emissaries in some of the areas that were hardest hit by the storm.

2117968.title: House of Healing
2117968.description: Beit Chanoch House of Healing at Duke Medical Center provides visiting families a place of comfort in their time of need.

2235211.title: My First Year As a Chabad Rabbi
2235211.description: When the Landa family moved to Novato, Calif., as Chabad emissaries, they got a welcome they never expected . . . from their mail carrier. Rabbi Menachem Landa shares some inspiring stories from his first year as a Chabad shliach (emissary).
path: My First Year As a Chabad Rabbi

2257188.title: The Friendship Circle of San Diego
2257188.description: The Friendship Circle of San Diego, a Chabad-Lubavitch organization that serves individuals with special needs by pairing them with volunteer teenagers and adults from the local community, has been recognized as one of the most innovative programs in the country for enriching the lives of individuals with autism.
path: The Friendship Circle of San Diego

2312125.title: Hurricane Sandy: Kindness in the Storm
2312125.description: After the horrific devastation of Hurricane Sandy, Chabad at the Shore swung into action providing relief, comfort and help.
path: Hurricane Sandy: Kindness in the Storm

2436239.title: The Early Days of Chabad.org
2436239.description: Charles Rawls, co-founder of the Dorsai Embassy, talks about the early days of the World Wide Web, his involvement in the launching of Chabad.org, and some of his personal experiences with Rabbi Yosef Y. Kazen and his work with Chabad.org some twenty years ago.

2797172.title: The Exciting World of Tzivos Hashem
path: The Exciting World of Tzivos Hashem

2932727.title: Israeli President Rivlin Hosting Lifshitz Kids from Nepal
path: Israeli President Rivlin Hosting Lifshitz Kids from Nepal

2799728.title: Lighting of the National Chanukah Menorah, Washington DC
2799728.description: Highlights of the 2014 National Menorah Lighting ceremony in Washington, D.C., including an address by U.S. Vice President Joe Biden.
path: Lighting of the National Chanukah Menorah, Washington DC

3222616.title: Honoring Rabbi Gordon
3222616.description: A video tribute celebrating the outstanding leadership of Rabbi Yehoshua B. and Rebbetzin Deborah Gordon, emissaries of the Lubavitcher Rebbe to the San Fernando Valley in California. (Produced by Mayer Greene in association with Ari Greene Productions. Edited by Ari Greene)

3290817.title: Inspiring a Generation of Leaders at Princeton
3290817.description: In November 2002, Rabbi Eitan and Gitty Webb began their work to build a more vibrant Judaism at Princeton University with the continuing success at the Scharf Family Chabad House.
path: Inspiring a Generation of Leaders at Princeton

3332224.title: Children of Chernobyl Airlift Campaign
3332224.description: Following the radioactive contamination from the nuclear disaster in Ukraine, Chabad-Lubavitch launched an extensive rescue mission of airlifting vulnerable children to safety in Israel.

3871830.title: A Tribute to Rabbi Moshe and Mrs. Mindy Feller
3871830.description: The Fellers were pioneers in Jewish outreach and established Chabad of Minnestoa in 1961. This short tribute video presents a small glimpse into their work and outstanding accomplishments in strengthening Judaism with love and dedication in the upper Midwest of the United States. This video was shown at the Annual Gala Dinner of Lubavitch Cheder of Minnesota in 2016.
path: A Tribute to Rabbi Moshe and Mrs. Mindy Feller

path: Meet Chabad's New Emissaries to the Ivory Coast

5603072.description: Rabbi Chaim and Menuchy Birnhack will be starting a new Chabad House on an alluring North Atlantic island.

221818.description: Join 6,500 Chabad-Lubavitch emissaries and lay leaders from across the globe as they renew, recharge and reinvigorate each other at the closing ceremony of the annual Conference of Chabad-Lubavitch emissaries.

7610599.title: From Moscow to Miami
7610599.description: Sasha Kaller grew up without Judaism. A few months after joining the recently founded Jewish school, he volunteered to kindle the menorah for an international satellite broadcast. More than 30 years later, he’d discover a photo of that lighting at a critical juncture in his life.

7610608.title: The Boy From Bondi
7610608.description: Rabbi Eli Schlanger was murdered at the Chanukah celebration he hosted. His son, just 14 years old, shares how he is living out his father’s mission.

7610615.title: A Flame Rekindled in Rome’s Jewish Ghetto
7610615.description: As the Holocaust raged in Rome, a non-Jewish milkman saved two Jewish children. Decades later, one of those children would rediscover his Jewish identity in that same spot.
path: A Flame Rekindled in Rome’s Jewish Ghetto

path: Shluchim Kids Sing From Around the World

Chaya Dadon, Priva Schlanger, and Mina Levitan, survivors of the Bondi massacre, share what inspired them to stand up to darkness and make the world a better, brighter 
place.

2471043.title: Keynote Address: Chanie Lipskar
2471043.description: Mrs. Chanie Lipskar, emissary to Bal Harbour, Florida, addresses the Conference of Chabad-Lubavitch Women Emissaries on January 26, 2014.

2471046.title: Shluchos Roll Call
2471046.description: Rochel Gordon - Tasmania, Australia; Bat Sheva Cohen - Chevron, Israel; Chana Lieblich - Wilmington, North Carolina; Sara Steifel - Lipetsk, Russia

2376576.title: Jewish Pride in the Limelight
2376576.description: Senator Joseph I. Lieberman was the Democratic Party nominee for Vice President in the 2000 election, but his deeply personal relationship with Chabad began in the 1960s, before he started a political career. The Rebbe's vision and emissaries, he says, continue to empower him to openly embrace his faith wherever he finds himself, and they will continue to empower the Jewish people and all humanity for eternity.

2376579.title: Shepherds of Israel
2376579.description: Rabbi Dov Greenberg offers a deeply personal account of the Rebbe’s take on Song of Songs’ imagery of a maiden and shepherd who cycle from intense love to outright rejection before the shepherd reignites her passion. This embodies the turbulent relationship between the Jewish people and G‑d. It is our mission to be shepherds of Israel, reaching deep to reignite the passionate soul of Judaism.
