2124284.description: Mrs. Chanchy Kaplan emissary to Milan, Italy welcomes the shluchos and their guests to the International Convention of Chabad Women Emissaries.

2124280.title: Opening Remarks
2124280.description: Vice-Chairman of Merkos L’lnyonei Chinuch, Rabbi Moshe Kotlarsky, delivers a message of inspiration and encouragement to the International Convention of Chabad Women Emissaries.

2124299.title: Personal Memories of the Rebbetzin
2124299.description: Louise Hager shares personal memories of her unique relationship with Rebbetzin Chaya Mushka on the occasion of the 25th anniversary of her passing.

2124300.title: Message to the Shluchos
2124300.description: Rabbi Yehuda Krinsky, Chairman of Merkos L'Inyonei Chinuch, delivers a message of inspiration and encouragement to the International Convention of Chabad Women Emissaries.

2128051.title: When the "Shlucha" Came to Town
2128051.description: Chana Gittle Deray recalls the series of events set in motion when Chabad emissarie Chani Baron and her husband arrived in Columbia, MD in 1986.

2124303.title: Implementing the Rebbe's Vision
2124303.description: Rabbetzin Chani Baron of Columbia, MD delivers the keynote address at the International Conference of Chabad Women Emissaries and tells about how she and her husband have been privileged to implement the Rebbe's vision.

2124304.title: International Roll-Call
2124304.description: One of the highlights of the yearly International Conference of Chabad Emissaries is the roll call of nations.

2032143.title: Opening Remarks
2032143.description: Rabbi Moshe Kotlarsky, Vice-Chairman of Merkos L'Inyonei Chinuch, greets the crowd at the 2012 International Conference of Chabad-Lubavitch Emissaries.

2032149.title: Why Jacob Left Home
2032149.description: Rabbi Eli Rosenfeld of Lisbon, Portugal asks why our forefather Jacob had to go so far from home in order to start his life

2035589.title: The Rebbe's Blessings in My Life
2035589.description: Mr. Steven Solarsh, a prominent entrepreneur and founding member and supporter of Chabad of Strathavon, South Africa, addresses the banquet at the 5773 Conference of Shluchim.
path: The Rebbe's Blessings in My Life

2032150.title: Living Day to Day
2032150.description:
Rabbi Ari Shishler, Director of Chabad of Strathavon, South Africa, represents his fellow Shluchim and delivers the keynote address at the Kinus Hashluchim Gala Banquet. He speaks on the theme of this years's
convention: the 200th anniversary of the Alter Rebbe's passing and the 70th anniversary of the publication of the Rebbe's book Hayom Yom.

2032152.title: My Relationship with the Rebbe
2032152.description: Chief Rabbi Yisroel Meir Lau shares inspirational moments of his longtime and special relationship with the Rebbe during his decades-long service in the Israeli Rabbinate.

2032147.title: Shluchim Roll Call
2032147.description: The shluchim roll call, a yearly institution at the International Conference of Chabad-Lubavitch Emissaries, has been named to honor the illustrious philanthropist, Mr. Sami Rohr, who passed on early this year.

1776342.title: Greetings from the Chairperson
1776342.description: Mrs. Shterni Gruzman, emissary to Vienna, Austria, welcomes the shluchos and their guests to the International Convention of Chabad Women Emissaries.

1776343.title: Global Update
1776343.description: Vice-Chairman of Merkos L’lnyonei Chinuch, Rabbi Moshe Kotlarsky, reviews some of the accomplishments in the world of shlichus over the past year.

1776418.title: Message to the Shluchos
1776418.description: Rabbi Yehuda Krinsky, Chairman of Merkos L'Inyonei Chinuch, delivers a message of inspiration and encouragement to the International Convention of Chabad Women Emissaries.

1776344.title: A Jewish Woman's Journey
1776344.description: Mrs. Ilana Skolnik of Capetown, South Africa shares the amazing story of her personal journey as a Jewish woman. While married to Israeli businessman and chairman of Friends of Lubavitch of Tel Aviv, the late Naaman Skolnik, she developed a special connection to the Rebbe.

1776345.title: Being a Chasid in Every Aspect of Our Lives
1776345.description: Keynote Speaker Mrs. Fruma Schapiro of Sydney, Australia addresses the theme of this year's Convention.
path: Being a Chasid in Every Aspect of Our Lives

1776346.title: International Roll-Call
1776346.description: Introducing Shluchos from all over the world are: Mrs. Simcha Abergel, Singapore, Singapore; Mrs. Shaindel Raskin, Larnaca, Cyprus; Mrs. Nechama Dina Segal, Poltava, Ukraine; Mrs. Shaindel Samama, Strassbourg, France; Mrs. Chaya Tawil, Salta Argentina; Mrs. Sara Weinstein, Pittsburgh, PA.

1490392.title: I Have Come to My Garden
1490392.description: Basi L’gani, the title of the last Chassidic discourse from the sixth Chabad Rebbe, is customarily studied on the tenth of Shevat, the day of his passing. (From “Messages”—Season 2, Episode 1)
path: I Have Come to My Garden

1490414.title: Love Others as Yourself?
1490414.description: The Torah’s axiom to love your friend as yourself, in essence means to love the other in accordance with their needs and wants—not merely what you want for yourself. (From “Messages”—Season 2, Episode 2)

1490420.title: G-d's Choice of Home
1490420.description: Maimonides in his code refers to the section of laws related to the Holy Temple as the laws of the ‘Chosen Home’. What is the message hidden therein? (From “Messages”—Season 2, Episode 3)

1490423.title: Torah and Egypt
1490423.description: The opening statement in the Ten Commandments is “I am the L-rd your G-d who took you out of Egypt.” Why does G-d introduce himself at Sinai as being the liberator from Egypt, instead of as the creator of heaven and earth? (From “Messages”—Season 2, Episode 4)

1490425.title: What is the Battle Plan?
1490425.description: What provides us the fortitude and confidence to always overcome the evil inclination (yetzer hara) in our internal battles? (From “Messages”—Season 2, Episode 5)

1490434.title: Mission: U.S.A.
1490434.description: Why the Rebbe didn’t go to the holy land of Israel even for just a visit. (From “Messages”—Season 2, Episode 7)

1490443.title: True Humility
1490443.description: A prerequisite to truly perceive Torah is humility. Most humble before all was Moses, who received the Torah from G-d Himself (From “Messages”—Season 2, Episode 8)

1490457.title: Trees & Kids
1490457.description: On Tuesday, the third day of creation, trees sprouted forth and produced fruit. This can serve as a metaphor that applies to children too. (From “Messages”—Season 2, Episode 9)

1490459.title: A Letter in Torah for Each Jew
1490459.description: The Rebbe initiated a campaign encouraging each and every Jew to acquire a letter in a Torah Scroll. (From “Messages”—Season 2, Episode 10)
path: A Letter in Torah for Each Jew

1490469.title: Summer Camp
1490469.description: During summer, schools and yeshivahs may close for vacation, but Judaism and Torah study must never cease, as they are our very source of life and vitality. (From “Messages”—Season 2, Episode 11)

1490471.title: The Crown Jewel
1490471.description: A parable of an ill prince is given to explain the need to reveal the inner dimension of Torah, known as the Kabbalah, to make it accessible to the masses. (From “Messages”—Season 2, Episode 12)

1490503.title: The Moshiach Decision
1490503.description: The Rebbe asks a leading halachic authority to ‘rule’ that Moshiach should come. What purpose is this ruling meant to serve? (From “Messages”—Season 2, Episode 15)

1490569.title: Concluding Mishneh Torah
1490569.description: Upon concluding the study of Mishneh Torah, Maimonides’ code of Jewish law, we immediately start again from the very beginning, which implies a strong connection between the two bookends. (From “Messages”—Season 2, Episode 23)

1490606.title: A Mother's Child
1490606.description: Jewish identity is determined exclusively through being born to a Jewish mother. What is the rationale to this Torah law? (From “Messages”—Season 2, Episode 25)

1490607.title: Israel's True Defense
1490607.description: The Torah provides guidance on how to increase security in Israel. (From “Messages”—Season 2, Episode 26)

4503345.title: High Holidays with the Rebbe
4503345.description: Join us as we spend the "head" and nerve center of the Jewish year with the Rebbe

1635549.title: The Rebbe’s Yizkor Speech
1635549.description: The unity of all Jews derives from the fact that every Jewish soul is “an actual part of G-d Above.” Therefore, “Jewish unity” is not limited to Jews who are alive, but includes those who have passed on, as well.

994325.title: A Piece of Honey Cake
994325.description: The Rebbe distributes the traditional lekach - sweet honey cake for a sweet year

1635546.title: Return
1635546.description: Our Sages extol the virtue of “Teshuva and good deeds.” But why do they praise the path of repentance before the path of purity? Shouldn’t repentance for misdeeds be enumerated after we speak of doing good deeds?

995863.title: An Extra Sweet Year
995863.description: In case it has been decreed upon a person to turn to others for help this coming year, it should already be fulfilled now, by receiving this sweet cake.

986088.title: Individual Teshuvah, With the Community
986088.description: Teshuva requires that a person make an honest assessment of his spiritual standing. To do this, it would seem ideal to isolate oneself from all distractions, to focus on one’s past deeds. Why do we see, that on Yom Kippur – the main day for Teshuvah of the whole year – we spend the entire day in a public place, in synagogue, together with so many others?

4893509.title: A Heartfelt Cry
4893509.description: There are many details and rituals connected to the various obligations of a Jew. Even when it comes to matters of the heart, such as prayer and repentance, there are many laws and requirements.

4893511.title: One Day, One People
4893511.description:
At the very beginning of Yom Kippur, before Kol Nidrei, we declare: “With the sanction of the
Omnipresent, and with the sanction of the congregation, by authority of the Heavenly Court, and by authority of the earthly court, we hereby grant permission to pray with those who have transgressed.” All agree that on this day, there are no differences between Jews; they all stand united as one in the presence of G-d.

4512197.title: Yom Kippur in the Air Force - Part 1: Operation Greenland
4512197.description: A few days before Yom Kippur in 1964, a sudden request came to 770 from a Jew who worked on a US Air force base in Greenland, to send a Shliach there to conduct the Yom Kippur services. Rabbi Shmuel Lew was called to duty.
path: Yom Kippur in the Air Force - Part 1: Operation Greenland

4894970.title: Yom Kippur in the Air Force - Part 2: Mission Accomplished
4894970.description:
Rabbi Shmuel Lew continues recounting his Yom Kippur mission. Just one day before he was
to leave for Greenland, the Rebbe’s mother, Rebbetzin Chana Schneerson, suddenly passed
away.
path: Yom Kippur in the Air Force - Part 2: Mission Accomplished

4894965.title: Erev Yom Kippur
4894965.description: On his way to Afternoon Prayers on Yom Kippur Eve, the Rebbe places coins in all the charity boxes set out in 770. On his way to Kol Nidrei, the Rebbe blesses the students of Tomchei Temimim. (Collage)

4894967.title: Lekach
4894967.description: The Rebbe distributes “Lekach,” honey cake, on the eve of Yom Kippur.

4902779.title: The Specialty of the Willow
4902779.description: During the festival of Sukkos, the Torah commands us to take a citron, a date palm frond, a myrtle branch, and a willow twig and bring them all together. The Midrash adds that each of these represents a different kind of Jew.

746740.title: One Sukkah, One Lulav, One People
746740.description: The two central mitzvos of Sukkos, the sukkah and the Four Kinds, have at their core the theme of Jewish unity.
path: One Sukkah, One Lulav, One People

1645627.title: Swords into Palm Branches
1645627.description: An address to children on Sukkos: Unlike other nations, who parade with a rifle, a Jew parades with a lulav. And instead of bullets, a Jew arms himself with an esrog. Instead of brandishing daggers or swords, a Jew carries hadassim (myrtles) and aravos (willows).

1645640.title: Four of a Kind
1645640.description: The Midrash teaches that each of the Four Species on Sukkos represents one kind of Jew and concludes: “On Sukkos, all four Jews must join together, for each one completes the others.”

3462173.title: Let the World Know
3462173.description: The sukkah is a testament to G‑d’s protection over the Jewish people. Like the clouds of glory in the desert, which it represents, the sukkah brings the nations of the world to respect the Jewish people and to recognize that this world has one true Master, G‑d Almighty. Thus, the coronation of G‑d which the Jewish people initiated on Rosh Hashana also reaches its apex on Sukkos, as all the nations of the world recognize G‑d’s dominion.

4521954.title: Torah in Motion
4521954.description: During the Holiday of Sukkos, we take a palm branch, citron, and branches of myrtle and willow, and wave them together in every direction. In fact, it was the custom of our Rebbes that when waving the lulav, they would not only extended it forward and bring it back, but would move it out in each of the six directions, give it a shake, and then bring it back towards the chest.

4902301.title: The Properties of Water
4902301.description: When the Holy Temple stood in Jerusalem, wine was poured on the altar daily, but on the festival of Sukkos there was an additional water libation after the morning service.

4902302.title: Why the Willow Need Not Grow Near Water
4902302.description: The Four Species taken on Sukkos represent four types of Jews, from the citron which has both flavor and fragrance, and represents the Jew who studies Torah and fulfills its commandments, to the willow which is neither tasty nor fragrant, represents the simplest of Jews, who lacks both Torah and good deeds.
path: Why the Willow Need Not Grow Near Water

4902303.title: Move Into G-d’s Barracks
4902303.description: During their sojourn in the desert, G-d protected the Jewish people against danger and the elements with the Clouds of Glory, which the Torah refers to as “sukkahs.” To commemorate this, He commanded us to observe the holiday of Sukkos, when we spend a week in temporary huts.

4902792.title: The Humble Willow
4902792.description: The seventh day of Sukkos is known as Hoshana Raba, during which we fulfill the custom of making seven circuits around the bima while holding the Four Species and reciting prayers for blessing and prosperity in the coming year.

4902304.title: Rabbi Shmuel and Spreading Sukkot Joy
4902304.description: The yahrzeit of the Rebbe Maharash, the fourth Chabad Rebbe, falls just before Sukkos, a time when Jews busily prepare for the upcoming festival. In recalling his life’s work, we see how the Rebbe Maharash gave up personal comforts, working tirelessly to improve the spiritual and physical lives of Russian Jewry.
path: Rabbi Shmuel and Spreading Sukkot Joy

4902306.title: Open Invitation
4902306.description: The Talmud relates that the entire Jewish people could dwell in one sukkah.

4902307.title: Choosing the Four Kinds
4902307.description: A group of Chassidim representing Chabad communities around the world, along with members of the Rebbe’s secretariat, are invited into the Rebbe’s study, to choose for themselves the Four Species for the upcoming Festival. (Late 1970s)

4902310.title: Distributing the Four Kinds
4902310.description: The Rebbe inspects lulavim and distributes them to a number of distinguished individuals, concluding with a blessing for good and joyful tidings throughout the year.

4902311.title: The Four Species
4902311.description: During Chol Hamoed Sukkos, the Rebbe shares his Four Species with the Chasidim.

4902318.title: Intermediate Days of Sukkos
4902318.description: A vintage scene from morning services in 770 during the festival of Sukkos. (5720s - 1960s)

4902314.title: Choosing the Four Species
4902314.description: The Rebbe chooses palm branch, willows and myrtles for his set of Four Species for Sukkos.

1306949.title: The Rebbe’s Sukkah
1306949.description: Distribution of Lekach, honeycake, with wishes for a sweet New Year. This is an age-old tradition on Hosha’ana Rabah. The Rebbe hands Lekach to men, women and children of all walks of life.

4902794.title: Distribution of Lekach
4902794.description: A special collage featuring scenes of the Rebbe distributing lekach, or honey cake, for a sweet new year.

4902320.title: Hallel – Chol Hamoed Sukkos
4902320.description: Reciting Hallel with the Four Kinds during the intermediate days of Sukkos. (October, 1978)

4903032.title: Hallel, Hoshanos
4903032.description:
During the Morning Prayers on Hoshana Rabba, the Rebbe waves the Four Species during
Hallel and circles the Bimah for Hoshanos.

4903029.title: Hoshanos
4903029.description: The Rebbe takes part in the services of Hoshana Rabbah.

4903031.title: Hoshana Rabbah Prayers
4903031.description: A special video montage of the morning prayers on Hoshana Rabbah, including the Rebbe reciting Hallel and waving the Four Species.

4903033.title: Hoshana Rabba
4903033.description: Reciting the Book of Psalms on the Eve of Hoshana Rabba.

4902786.title: V’samachta
4902786.description: “And you shall rejoice in your Festival… and you will be only happy.” (Deuteronomy 16:14, 15)

4902789.title: Al Hasela
4902789.description: “He struck the rock and water flowed.” The verse tells how, in the desert, G-d commanded Moses to hit the rock with his staff. Water flowed forth from it to satisfy the thirst of the Jewish people. From the Prayer for Rain.

4902313.title: Picking the Rebbe’s Lulav
4902313.description: For many years, Rabbi Yitzchak Maier Gurary and his father-in-law, Rabbi Mordechai Altein, would provide the Four Species to the Rebbe for Sukkos.

4902804.title: Why the Rebbe Snuck Over the Wartime Border
4902804.description: Rabbi Menachem Teichtel was a refugee student in Vichy France during the war. He recounts just how far the Rebbe was willing to go to uphold a Jewish custom during wartime (circa 1940).
path: Why the Rebbe Snuck Over the Wartime Border

4902805.title: Esrogim in Kfar Chabad
4902805.description: In the late 1950s, When Rabbi Nachman Elbaum raised the issue of using an esrog from a tree that had been grafted, the Rebbe gave him a solution and a mission. The result was a new orchard in the village of Kfar Chabad, Israel.

4902788.title: When It Rains on Sukkot
4902788.description: Rabbi Binyomin Silberstrom recalls asking the Rebbe, “How can we spread joy during the festival Sukkos when it won’t stop raining? The Talmud clearly states that rain is a sign of God’s displeasure.” The quick reply to his question was was a revealing example of the Rebbe’s unique perspective. (1975)

603067.title: A Brilliant Victory
603067.description: Chanukah celebrates the Jews’ battle for G‑d’s Torah to prevail. But the mitzvah which they established to immortalize their triumph—the kindling of the Chanukah menorah—sheds light on the true nature of “Jewish victory.”

603066.title: The Chanukah Battle Continues
603066.description: The Chanukah candles evoke the memory of the small group of Jews who fought those who had opposed the Torah. Today, we each battle our own evil inclination as well. Our current mission and battle is for the coming of Moshiach, as we request three times a day during prayer.

792105.title: Minority Rules
792105.description:
When a Jew celebrates Chanukah, he may be confronted: “You Jews are so few compared to
the nations of the world. Yet you hold fast to your customs and commandments, ignoring what
the billions of non-Jews around you think and do… Wherein lies your strength to stand in the
face of such odds?”

792129.title: One Small Candle; One Giant Light for Mankind
792129.description: On Chanukah, Jewish children increase in spiritual light, adding an additional candle in the menorah, and inspiring their neighbors to join in illuminating the world.
path: One Small Candle; One Giant Light for Mankind

4215650.title: You Can Be a “Hillel” Menorah
4215650.description: There are two approaches to Judaism, increasing the good or decreasing the bad. On Chanukah, and particularly on the fifth night of Chanukah, we emphasize the former by adding an extra light on each new day.

606594.title: Lights, Camera, Action!
606594.description: An address at the Chanukah Live worldwide satellite hookup at 770: The ultimate purpose of science is to discover new ways to facilitate and increase our ability to serve G-d. This we see clearly here at this gathering: Jews in every corner of the globe were able to tune in, via satellite, and watch as a little child kindled the Chanukah flames.

1377713.title: A Chanukah Message for All Ages
1377713.description:
Chanukah reminds every Jew that it is G-d’s eternal mandate to carry the torch of His
“Mitzvah-candle and Torah-light.” With most Mitzvos, the “candle” and “light” are not
physically visible. But with the Chanukah candles we see how fulfilling the Mitzvah creates
actual physical light that illuminates all one’s surroundings.
path: A Chanukah Message for All Ages

4215648.title: Chanukah and Chasidism
4215648.description: Chasidism is often challenged based on the fact that it’s a relatively new path in the service of the Almighty. But the laws of Chanukah actually provide an important answer for this question. The Torah and Mitzvos are our best weapon against the darkness of the world around us. As we get closer to the end of this exile and the darkness increases, it’s also necessary to add more light as a counterbalance. Jewish observance has minimums set by Jewish Law. Then there’s going beyond these minimums, to “beautify” it, which can be done in various ways. The lesson of the Chanukah lights for the year ahead is to strive to be the best Jews we can possibly be.

1714722.title: Chanukah Fun and Games
1714722.description: It is customary on Chanukah to organize special gatherings for children. It is also the custom to make family gatherings which include activities such as playing dreidel, staging plays and distributing Chanukah gelt.

1714734.title: Chanukah Money for the Children
1714734.description: Why we give children money, known as Chanukah gelt, to spend as they wish.

792113.title: Chanukah for Children
792113.description: At a children’s rally the Menorah is lit, the children sing the prayer after the lighting and recite the 12 Torah passages. The Rebbe tells the children to “listen to what the candles have to tell us.”

792120.title: Chanukah Rally
792120.description: Children’s rally at 770 on the last night of Chanukah, 1987.

792130.title: Haneiros Hallalu
792130.description: At a Farbrengen on the last night of Chanukah, Chassidim sing Haneiros Hallalu.

792124.title: Chanukah Rally
792124.description: The Rebbe joins in a Chanukah rally at 770 for public school children.

792128.title: Haneirot Hallalu
792128.description: The words of this Niggun recount the miracles of G-d, which are evoked by the Chanukah lights. It is sung each night of Chanukah, after lighting the Menorah.

792132.title: Menorah Lighting in the Rebbe’s House
792132.description: Afternoon Prayers and Menorah lighting in the Rebbe’s house on President Street.
path: Menorah Lighting in the Rebbe’s House

792131.title: Shabbos-Chanukah Light
792131.description: There is a special lesson when both the first and last days of Chanukah fall out on Shabbos. It teaches us that every aspect of a Jew’s life must be completely permeated and saturated with “the Shabbos spirit,” with extra holiness and transcendence over the mundane.

2060816.title: Shining Examples
2060816.description: The festival is called, “Chanukah – dedication” for it recalls the rededication of the Holy Temple after the Macabees’ victory over the Greeks. The Temple was purified and made holy, and the Jewish people renewed its service with greater love and passion than before.

4598418.title: Much to Accomplish Together
4598418.description: During Chanukah in 1985, a joint rally was held at 770 for groups of seniors and young children. Addressing the gathering, the Rebbe explained their shared lessons and the rally’s special connection to Chanukah.

4599487.title: Was the Chanukah Miracle Necessary?
4599487.description: We all know the story of Chanukah: With all the odds against them, the Jews were victorious over their enemies. However, when they returned to the Holy Temple, they found that all the oil for the Menorah was defiled. God made a miracle and the oil lasted for eight days until they could procure new oil that was pure.

2871111.title: When G-d Is Hidden
2871111.description: A deeper look at the heroine of the Purim story, whose very name means “hidden” in Hebrew.

641144.title: What Can King Achashverosh Teach You?
641144.description: Why does the Megillah describe the extravagance of Achashveirosh’s feast in such great detail, which is irrelevant to the miracles or themes of Purim?
path: What Can King Achashverosh Teach You?

641149.title: Victory in Our Times
641149.description:
An address to children:
Thousands of years ago there lived the wicked Haman, who wanted to do bad to the Jewish
People. But they were not afraid, and they remained loyal to Judaism, to Mordechai and
Esther, and to their teachers who showed them how a Jew should live his daily life.
What connection does Haman have to a Jewish child today?

641150.title: Awakening
641150.description:
Haman, bitter enemy of the Jews, said of their misdeeds, “the Jewish nation is slumbering.”
Even their worst enemy perceived that a Jew’s heart is inseparable from G-d. The Jew is merely asleep sometimes, and his heart’s true desire cannot be expressed through our sleeping body.

3953171.title: Stop Living in the Past
3953171.description: The Baal Shem Tov explains the Talmudic statement, “One who reads the Megilah backwards, does not fulfill his obligation.” He interprets “backwards” to mean that one can read the Megilah following all the laws, with all the proper intentions, but at the same time, he might think “This is ‘backwards,’ it’s irrelevant.

641151.title: Esther, Model for Jewish Women
641151.description: Mordechai and Esther are the heroes of Purim, yet the Megillah is named only after Esther. And the initiative that the Megillah be included among the books of the Bible came specifically from Esther. Why is Esther given the spotlight, when her success depended on Mordechai’s plan?

641352.title: The Night the King Woke Up…
641352.description:
"On that night the king's sleep was disturbed…" Taken literally this verse refers to King
Achashverosh. But the Midrash explains a deeper dimension: "The sleep of the King of the
universe was disturbed" - G-d Himself "woke up."
path: The Night the King Woke Up…

2871142.title: Torah Light
2871142.description: How Purim emphasizes the feminine aspect of Torah, which was missing until then.

4325453.title: Purim with the Rebbe: A Unique Presentation
4325453.description: This special presentation highlights scenes of Purim farbrengens with the Rebbe throughout the years.
path: Purim with the Rebbe: A Unique Presentation

851040.title: The Power of Children
851040.description:
Mordechai gathered thousands of Jewish children to study Torah and pray to G-d to save the
Jews from annihilation. Only when the innocent voices of the children ascended On High, did
the Almighty annul the decree and replace it with the opposite — boundless joy.

1131778.title: Who Should Teach the Children?
1131778.description:
The Midrash relates that when Mordechai learned of Haman’s wicked plot, he immediately
gathered 22,000 Jewish children to study Torah with them. This caused a commotion on
High, eliciting Divine mercy.

1791753.title: A Jew is a Jew
1791753.description: There are some who believe that by hiding their Jewishness they will be protected from anti-Semitism. The Megillah teaches us a lesson: When Haman persuaded King Achashverosh to issue the decree against the Jewish people, he argued that...

2871108.title: Why Does Purim Have a Persian Name?
2871108.description: The names of the Jewish festivals and other dates on the Jewish calendar are all in Hebrew, the Holy Tongue. There is, however, one exception: The festival of Purim.
path: Why Does Purim Have a Persian Name?

2871173.title: Be Your True Self
2871173.description: The Megillah recounts how Haman’s evil decree was reversed. Here is how it happened.

2871164.title: The Silly Bird and the Wily Fox: Two Purim Parables
2871164.description: The Midrash gives a parable for the story of Haman’s plot against the Jews...
path: The Silly Bird and the Wily Fox: Two Purim Parables

2527418.title: Dare to Be Different
2527418.description: The Book of Esther relates that when King Achashverosh made a great feast, he provided every guest with whatever food and drink they desired.

2149988.title: What Makes Purim Unique
2149988.description: What makes Purim unique from all other Jewish holidays?

2871185.title: Free to Serve
2871185.description: In modern times, G-d has blessed the Jewish People, and the majority of Jews live in countries where they are not persecuted or segregated. But with this comes a new challenge

2149993.title: Purim Farbrengen 5732 (1972)
2149993.description: An hour-long excerpt from a 1972 recording of the Rebbe’s Purim farbrengen. The Rebbe tackles the enigmatic essence of the Purim story, and explains the real and primary miracle the Sages say we are celebrating. Drawing life lessons from how in those dark times, a generation of assimilating Jews were found worthy in G-d’s eyes.

3266315.title: Two Days of Purim
3266315.description: When king Achashverosh gave permission to the Jews fight off their enemies, he allowed an extra day for those in Shushan. The day after Purim, called Shushan Purim, is celebrated to mark this special phenomenon. In a sense this is more than just an historical commemoration; it celebrates the ability in general, to add to good in a meaningful way.

3287562.title: Children of Redemption
3287562.description: The festival of Purim has a special connection to young children.

6368851.title: Foiling the Plot
6368851.description: At the height of danger, with Haman’s decree of annihilation hanging over the heads of the Jewish people, their spiritual leader, Mordechai, sought some all-important counsel. He did not turn to the thought leaders or political pundits of the time; he went to some innocent Jewish children. When he heard their certainty that G-d would save them, he knew all would be well.

657028.title: The Fifth Son
657028.description: The Haggadah speaks of the “Four Sons” at the Seder table, demonstrating that every Jewish child needs to be given the full experience of Passover; if need be, search him out, find him, and invite him together with his family to your Seder table, to celebrate the freedom of our People.

2900678.title: War on Ignorance
2900678.description: The Haggadah lists four sons at the Passover Seder table. The child ‘who doesn’t know to ask’ is listed last amongst the four sons, following not only the ‘wise son’, but also the ‘wicked’ one. This offers insight and an important lesson in our calling to action in these times.

2900692.title: "Why Am I Different?"
2900692.description: The Passover Seder begins with the child’s question: “Why is this night different from all other nights?” Fundamentally, the question bothering the child is: “Why am I different from children of all other nations?”

3298526.title: All Are Welcome
3298526.description: The Haggadah relates that “Torah speaks to four sons”. Although they are all different they are placed one beside the other to emphasize the innate value of each.

3638532.title: Passover Preparations
3638532.description:
All important things need preparation, and education is certainly no exception. We need not wait to respond to our children; by being proactive, we can be sure that they’re properly engaged. This is especially true by the Passover Seder. Much of the ritual that surrounds the Passover Seder
involves the participation of our children. By properly preparing, all our children, no matter their personalities, can feel welcome and involved.

657023.title: From Darkness to Light
657023.description: The Torah does not tell us the exact times when many important events occurred. Nevertheless, we are told that Pharoah commanded the Jews to leave Egypt exactly at midnight on the 15th of Nissan. Further, the Torah narrates the exact moment they actually left: The next day, precisely at noon – not delaying even for the “blink of an eye”.

3298572.title: Lasting Freedom
3298572.description: Although Passover is called the Season of Our Freedom, when the Jewish people were redeemed from Egypt there was no mention of the matter. Instead, they were told by Moses that they are leaving Egypt to serve G-d.

2900690.title: The Jewish Woman – Royal Benefactor
2900690.description:
We begin the Seder by announcing, “Whoever is hungry come and eat; whoever needs come celebrate Passover.”
It is admirable to give money to someone who hungers, but even greater to provide prepared food so he need not exert any effort before quieting his hunger. Although we give money to the needy so they may acquire their Passover needs, we go further to invite them to our prepared Seder meal; all they must do is come in and they will immediately be able to eat!

858901.title: Why is this Nation Different from All Other Nations?
858901.description:
Every Jew descends from those Jews who were enslaved in Egypt. When G-d freed them, He
freed all Jews of all future generations, including each and every one of us.
path: Why is this Nation Different from All Other Nations?

2900688.title: The Season of Freedom--Preaching and Practicing
2900688.description: Education comes in many forms: First and foremost is to provide a living example. The best way to influence someone is by practicing what you preach. As we approach Passover, the call of the hour is to seek out those who cannot afford the holiday expenses and provide all that they need.
path: The Season of Freedom--Preaching and Practicing

657024.title: Lessons From the Exodus
657024.description: Two essential lessons from the Exodus for every Jew: Pharaoh, the mightiest king in the world, ruthlessly oppressed the Jewish People. Yet his behavior completely reversed, and, instead of afflicting the Jews, “Pharaoh sent the people away...

1176035.title: Passover – Calling All Citizens!
1176035.description:
Passover is ‘The Festival of Our Freedom.’ The Festival itself calls out: “Listen, Jews – we
must be free!” The verse states: “There shall be one law for the Passover sacrifice – for you,
the convert and the native-born.” Allegorically speaking, ‘native-born’ refers to the ‘true
citizen’ of a country – one who thinks that his country is the greatest. A Jew must recognize,
however, that he is “Jerusalem-born” – no matter where in the world he is.

657031.title: Asking the Four Questions
657031.description: May your entire family have good preparations for a wonderful Passover. All the children who are old enough should prepare the four questions for the Seder.

657046.title: The Rebbe’s Matzos
657046.description: The Rebbe distributes Matzah before Passover, at his home on President Street.

657045.title: This Year in Jerusalem
657045.description: Our Seder eve wish, “Next year in Jerusalem,” doesn’t mean that we wish to wait a year before Moshiach comes. Rather, we anticipate the Redemption today, and then certainly by “next year” we will be “in Jerusalem!”

657048.title: Selling the Chametz – Erev Pesach
657048.description: In his home, the Rebbe sells the chametz before Passover.

657049.title: Biur Chametz
657049.description: On the eve of Passover, the Rebbe burns the Chametz and recites Kol Chamira.

6496739.title: “I Prefer to Illuminate Souls”
6496739.description: “My field was electrical engineering," the Rebbe told me. "But I prefer to turn on the lights in people’s souls.”

6518711.title: “There Is No Small Jew”
6518711.description: A short story with the Rebbe.

6525936.title: Who Is Considered My Chassid?
6525936.description: A question asked by Dr. David Weiss, a professor at Berkeley in California, during his visit to the Rebbe.

6530647.title: Turning Disappointment into Possibility
6530647.description: How a conversation Shirley Chisholm, the first African American woman elected to Congress, had with the Rebbe, turned disappointment into opportunity and helped feed hungry children across America.

6539721.title: You Are Never Alone
6539721.description: When a widow shared how lonely she felt with the Rebbe, he shared a powerful message of hope and the essential truth: We're never alone, because G-d is always with us.

6547877.title: A Lesson From Chess
6547877.description: When the Rebbe explained the deeper meaning of the game to chess champion Sammy Reshevsky.

6555062.title: What Is True Love?
6555062.description: The Rebbe enlightens a young lady who was dating for marriage on the true meaning of love.

6559352.title: Get to Know Yourself
6559352.description: In 1974, Rabbi Moshe Yitzchak Hecht, a Chabad rabbi in New Haven, Connecticut, wrote to the Rebbe after 33 years of tremendous work, begging the Rebbe to help him.

6566309.title: Speak to Yourself
6566309.description: When Rabbi Tzvi Hirsch Weinreb was a young psychologist in Silver Spring, Maryland, he faced a personal crisis and sought out sage advice.

6579808.title: What Is the Rebbe’s Favorite Prayer?
6579808.description: When a curious boy posed a question to the Rebbe’s mother.
path: What Is the Rebbe’s Favorite Prayer?

6584332.title: Love Your Brother, Love Yourself
6584332.description: Two boys playing outside their home in Brooklyn had no idea that the friendly Jewish man who'd stop to say hi was none other than the Rebbe.

6591301.title: I’m Here to Uplift Others
6591301.description: The secretariat office was already closed for the day, so Rabbi Yosef Wineberg slipped the urgent letter through the Rebbe’s door. Then the unexpected happened.

6606641.title: Tashlich in the Rain
6606641.description: The locked gates to Brooklyn’s Botanical Gardens didn’t stop the Rebbe from doing Tashlich on Rosh Hashana that year.

6622786.title: Holiday Joy During War
6622786.description: Why was the Rebbe calling for joy and celebration during a time of war?

6623007.title: From Disabled to Exceptional
6623007.description: A group of Israelis wounded whilst serving in the IDF came to Brooklyn for an exclusive visit with the Rebbe. The Rebbe insisted on changing and reframing their disability to positive empowerment.

6629859.title: Players and Fans
6629859.description: The Rebbe asked the Bar Mitzvah boy, who was a baseball fan, what is the difference between a player and a fan?

6638959.title: The Original High-Tech
6638959.description: What is the connection between tefillin and computers?

6655400.title: Dancing Away Depression
6655400.description: Taibel Lipskier was a refugee from the Soviet Union. Turning to the Rebbe about her fears and worries, he gave her advice that changed her life.

6657812.title: The Rebbe and the Troubled Teen
6657812.description: When a teen questioned whether the Rebbe really felt her pain, he replied with an analogy.
path: The Rebbe and the Troubled Teen

6666163.title: The Rebbe, the Artist and the Phoenix
6666163.description: When Jacques Lipchitz, a world-renowned sculptor, left an unfinished work, his wife was unsure of how to proceed. The Rebbe's wisdom empowered her.
path: The Rebbe, the Artist and the Phoenix

6673268.title: "Do You Make Miracles?"
6673268.description: The Rebbe showed a group of college students that making a miracle is easier than they thought.

6674525.title: Are You Too Busy?
6674525.description: Chances are you are not as busy as Rabbi Adin Even-Israel (Steinsaltz); feeling overwhelmed, he turned to the Rebbe for advice.

6693588.title: Why Are Weddings Not Sad?
6693588.description: The Rebbe shared with a bride and groom the kabbalistic reason why weddings are joyous occasions.

6701038.title: Can We Communicate With Departed Loved Ones?
6701038.description: When a bereaved mother was inconsolable after the loss of her young son, she came to the Rebbe desperate for comfort and left with an entirely new perspective.
path: Can We Communicate With Departed Loved Ones?

6721180.title: Don’t Forget Your Anniversary!
6721180.description: Did you ever forget an anniversary or birthday of a loved one? Here's what the Rebbe told one husband who forgot…

6724913.title: Why Light Menorahs in Public?
6724913.description: The Rebbe's reply has proven itself right again and again.

6739213.title: More Faith, More Livelihood
6739213.description: Zalmon Jaffe, a prominent businessman from Manchester, UK, had a close connection with the Rebbe. When he shared concern about his business fortunes, the Rebbe’s reply rings true in many areas of life.

6745205.title: Can My Thoughts Really Change the Situation?
6745205.description: Avraham Rottenberg was distraught and worried after finding out that his father suffered a heart attack. The Rebbe showed him the power of positive thinking.
path: Can My Thoughts Really Change the Situation?

6748533.title: Is Weeping a Sign of Weakness?
6748533.description: A young trauma survivor shared his struggles with the Rebbe and finally allowed himself to grieve.
path: Is Weeping a Sign of Weakness?

6764604.title: The Job of a Chassidic Artist
6764604.description: The Rebbe conveyed a life lesson to the famed Chassidic artist Hendel Lieberman: the primary talent of an artist is to see past the externalities of something and capture its inner life—exposing the essence of the thing being portrayed.
path: The Job of a Chassidic Artist
